For $x \in O_1$ the fixed-point condition reads $Dr(x)h = h$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.mem_tangent_iff_of_mem⟧, and the second component of $Tr \circ Tr = Tr$ at $(x, h)$ gives $Dr(x) \circ Dr(x) = Dr(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.scDeriv_comp_self⟧ — the remark after Definition 2.1.3 (preprint 2.3) that $Dr(x)$ is a projection. So for $x \in O_1$, $(x, h) \in Tr(TU)$ iff $h$ is in the range of $Dr(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.mem_tangent_iff_mem_range⟧, and $Tr(TU) = \{(r(x), Dr(x)h) : x \in U_1, h \in E_0\}$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.mem_tangent_iff_exists⟧.

**Proposition 2.1.11 (preprint 2.4).** *If $r(U) \subseteq r'(U')$ then $r' \circ r = r$ on $U$*: for $y \in U$, $r(y) \in r'(U')$ is a fixed point of $r'$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.comp_eq_self_of_retract_subset⟧. *And then $Tr(TU) \subseteq Tr'(TU')$*: let $p \in Tr(TU)$, so $p \in TU$ and $Tr(p) = p$. Its base point lies in $O_1 \subseteq U'_1$, so $p \in TU'$. The map $r$ sends $U$ into $U'$ (into $O \subseteq U'$), so the chain rule applies to $r' \circ r$ on $U$: $T(r' \circ r)(p) = Tr'(Tr(p)) = Tr'(p)$; and $T(r' \circ r) = Tr$ on $TU$ because $r' \circ r = r$ on $U$ (tangent maps depend only on the values on $U$). So $Tr'(p) = Tr(p) = p$, which is the fixed-point condition for $r'$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.tangent_subset_of_retract_subset⟧. Applied in both directions, two retractions with the same retract have the same tangent image ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · proposition_2_1_11⟧. This is the text's proof, with its step "$Tr'(x, h) = (x, h)$" made the definition of membership.

**Definition 2.1.12 (preprint 2.5).** $TO$ is $Tr(TU)$ for a retraction chosen (by choice) among those onto $O$, and the empty set if $O$ is not a retract ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · retractTangent⟧; by Proposition 2.1.11 (preprint 2.4) it equals $Tr(TU)$ for *every* retraction onto $O$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · retractTangent_eq⟧. The tangent space at $x \in O_1$ is the fibre $T_xO = \{h : (x, h) \in TO\}$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · tangentSpace⟧, the range of $Dr(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · tangentSpace_eq_range⟧, a linear subspace ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · tangentSpace_eq_coe_submodule⟧ (closed, as the range of a continuous projection).

### II.3 Sc-smooth maps between retracts (Proposition 2.1.13 (preprint 2.6), Definition 2.1.14 (preprint 2.7), Theorem 2.1.15 (preprint 2.8), Proposition 2.3.1 (preprint 2.10))

**Proposition 2.1.13 (preprint 2.6).** Let $r$ on $U$ and $s$ on $V$ be retractions onto the same $O$. Since $s$ takes values in $O$, which $r$ fixes, $(f \circ r) \circ s = f \circ s$ on $V$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.comp_comp_eqOn⟧. (1) If $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth on $U$, then $f \circ r \circ s$ is sc-smooth on $V$ by the chain rule ($s$ maps $V$ into $O \subseteq U$), hence so is $f \circ s$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · proposition_2_1_13_one⟧ ⟦Chapter1/ChainRule · IsScSmooth.comp⟧. (2) For $p \in TO$: $p \in TV$ and $Ts(p) = p$ (fixed-point description for $s$, after Proposition 2.1.11 (preprint 2.4)); so $T(f \circ r)(p) = T(f \circ r)(Ts(p)) = T((f \circ r) \circ s)(p) = T(f \circ s)(p)$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · proposition_2_1_13_two⟧. (3) If $f$ maps $O$ into $O' = r'(U')$, then $r' \circ f \circ r = f \circ r$ on $U$; the chain rule gives $Tr'(T(f \circ r)(p)) = T(f \circ r)(p)$ for $p \in TU$, and $T(f \circ r)(p) \in TU'$, so $T(f \circ r)(p) \in TO'$ by the fixed-point description ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · proposition_2_1_13_three⟧.

**Definition 2.1.14 (preprint 2.7).** $f$ is *sc-smooth from $(O, C, E)$ to $(O', C', E')$* if $f(O) \subseteq O'$ and $f \circ r$ is sc-smooth on $U$ for every retraction $r$ onto $O$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · IsScSmoothRetractMap⟧. For a retract $O$ this is equivalent to "$f(O) \subseteq O'$ and $f \circ r$ sc-smooth for one $r$", by Proposition 2.1.13 (1) (preprint 2.6) ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · isScSmoothRetractMap_iff_exists⟧. Quantifying over all retractions makes the definition independent of choices without further argument; the target triple enters only through $f(O) \subseteq O'$. The *tangent map* $Tf$ is $T(f \circ r)$ for the chosen retraction ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · retractTangentMap⟧; on $TO$ it equals $T(f \circ r)$ for every $r$ onto $O$, by Proposition 2.1.13 (2) (preprint 2.6) ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · retractTangentMap_eqOn⟧, it maps $TO$ into $TO'$ by (3) ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · IsScSmoothRetractMap.tangentMap_mapsTo⟧, and $Tf(x, h) = (f(x), D(f \circ r)(x)h)$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · retractTangentMap_apply⟧. An sc-smooth map between retracts is continuous on $O$ (level $0$ of the $\mathrm{sc}^0$ property of $f \circ r$, and $f = f \circ r$ on $O$) ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · IsScSmoothRetractMap.continuousOn⟧ and maps points of $O$ on level $m$ to points on level $m$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · IsScSmoothRetractMap.mem_range_toBase⟧.

**Theorem 2.1.15 (preprint 2.8).** Let $O = r(U)$, $O' = r'(U')$ be retracts, $f$ sc-smooth from $O$ to $O'$ and $g$ from $O'$ to $O''$. Since $f \circ r$ takes values in $O'$, which $r'$ fixes, $(g \circ r') \circ (f \circ r) = (g \circ f) \circ r$ on $U$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.comp_comp_comp_eqOn⟧. The left side is sc-smooth by the chain rule ($f \circ r$ maps $U$ into $O' \subseteq U'$, and $g \circ r'$ is sc-smooth on $U'$), so $g \circ f$ is sc-smooth from $O$ to $O''$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · IsScSmoothRetractMap.comp⟧. For the tangent maps, at $p \in TO$: $T(g \circ f)(p) = T((g \circ f) \circ r)(p) = T(g \circ r')(T(f \circ r)(p)) = Tg(Tf(p))$, the last step because $Tf(p) \in TO'$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · retractTangentMap_comp⟧. Together ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · theorem_2_1_15⟧. The text gives no proof ("follows from Theorem 1.21"); this is the one it has in mind, with $r' \circ f \circ r = f \circ r$ made explicit. Further: the identity is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · isScSmoothRetractMap_id⟧, a retraction is sc-smooth as a map $(U, C, E) \to (O, C, E)$ and the inclusion $O \to U$ as a map $(O, C, E) \to (U, C, E)$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.isScSmoothRetractMap⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.isScSmoothRetractMap_inclusion⟧, and sc-smoothness depends only on $f|_O$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · IsScSmoothRetractMap.congr⟧.

**Proposition 2.3.1 (preprint 2.10).** (1) For $W \subseteq E_0$ open, $U \cap r^{-1}(W)$ is relatively open in $C$ because $r$ is continuous on $U$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.relOpen_inter_preimage⟧; the restriction of $r$ to it is a retraction ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.restrict⟧ (sc-smooth by §II.1) with retract $O \cap W$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.restrict_retract⟧. So $(O \cap W, C, E)$ is a retract ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · proposition_2_3_1_one⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · LocalModel.restrict⟧; "an open subset $O'$ of $O$" is $O \cap W$ in the subspace topology. (2) If $V = r(U)$ and $s$ is sc-smooth from $(V, C, E)$ to itself with $s \circ s = s$ on $V$, then $\rho = s \circ r$ is sc-smooth on $U$ (that is what sc-smoothness of $s$ on the retract $V$ means), maps $U$ into $s(V) \subseteq V \subseteq U$, and is idempotent: $\rho(\rho(x)) = s(r(s(r(x)))) = s(s(r(x))) = s(r(x))$ because $r$ fixes $s(r(x)) \in V$. Its retract is $s(V)$ ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · proposition_2_3_1_two⟧. As the text's proof.

*Restriction and locality between retracts.* An sc-smooth map between retracts restricts to $O \cap W$: a retraction onto $O \cap W$ composed with $r$ is handled by the chain rule ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · IsScSmoothRetractMap.restrict⟧; the target may be shrunk to any set containing the image ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · IsScSmoothRetractMap.mono_target⟧. Conversely, if every point of $O$ has an open $W$ with $f$ sc-smooth on $(O \cap W, C, E)$, then $f$ is sc-smooth on $(O, C, E)$: for a retraction $r$ onto $O$ and $y \in U$, the set $W$ around $r(y)$ pulls back under the continuous $r$ to an open $u \ni y$; on $U \cap u$ the map $f \circ r$ equals $(f \circ r') \circ r$ with $r'$ the restriction of $r$ onto $O \cap W$, which is sc-smooth, and the locality of §II.1 concludes ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · IsScSmoothRetractMap.of_locally⟧. The text uses this silently every time it says "the definition does not depend on the choice of charts".

### II.4 The tangent functor on retracts

*The tangent of a partial quadrant.* If $C = T_0^{-1}(\text{quadrant})$ for $T : E \cong \mathbb R^n \oplus W$, then $TC = C_1 \times E_0$ is a partial quadrant in $TE = E^1 \oplus E$: compose the tangent of $T$, an sc-isomorphism $TE \cong T(\mathbb R^n \oplus W)$, with the re-association $((a, w), (b, v)) \mapsto (a, (w, (b, v)))$ onto $\mathbb R^n \oplus (W^1 \oplus (\mathbb R^n \oplus W))$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · tangentQuadrantIso⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · IsPartialQuadrant.tangentSet⟧. $TU$ is relatively open in $TC$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.tangentSet⟧ (this is Lemma 3.B of the exposition of Chapter 1; Part I, V1.36). Sc-operators are sc-smooth on every sc-domain ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · ScOperator.isScSmooth⟧.

*$Tr$ is a retraction.* $Tr$ is sc-smooth on $TU$ (Part I: the tangent map of an sc-smooth map is sc-smooth) ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · LocalModel.tangent_isScSmooth⟧, maps $TU$ into itself and is idempotent; so it is an sc-smooth retraction on $TC$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · ScRetraction.tangentRetraction⟧ with retract $TO$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · ScRetraction.tangentRetraction_retract⟧. Hence $(TO, TC, TE)$ is a retract ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · IsScRetract.tangentSet⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · LocalModel.tangent⟧, base points of $TO$ lie in $O_1$ and $(x, 0) \in TO$ for $x \in O_1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · retractTangent_fst_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · mk_zero_mem_retractTangent⟧.

*$Tf$ is sc-smooth.* If $f$ is sc-smooth from $O$ to $O'$ then $Tf$ is sc-smooth from $(TO, TC, TE)$ to $(TO', TC', TE')$: with the retraction $Tr$ onto $TO$, $Tf \circ Tr = T(f \circ r) \circ Tr = T(f \circ r \circ r) = T(f \circ r)$ on $TU$, which is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · IsScSmoothRetractMap.tangent⟧. $Tf$ depends only on $f|_O$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · retractTangentMap_congr⟧, and a map equal to the identity on $O$ has tangent map the identity on $TO$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · retractTangentMap_id⟧. With Theorem 2.1.15 (preprint 2.8) this is the tangent functor $T : \mathcal R \to \mathcal R$ of the text; the bundle structure of Definition 2.1.16 (preprint 2.9) is §II.32 ($Tr$ a bundle retraction, $Tf$ a bundle map), the category $\mathcal{BR}$ is not formalized.

*Locality of the tangent.* For $W$ open, $T(O \cap W) = TO \cap (W_1 \times E_0)$: with the restricted retraction, a fixed point of $Tr$ over a base point in $W_1$ is a fixed point of the restricted $Tr$, the two tangent maps agreeing on the smaller domain (§II.1) ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · retractTangent_inter_isOpen⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · retractTangent_mono_inter⟧. And $Tf$ computed on $(O \cap W, C, E)$ agrees with $Tf$ computed on $(O, C, E)$ on $T(O \cap W)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · retractTangentMap_inter_isOpen⟧. These two facts are what Definitions 2.3.12–2.3.14 (preprint 2.17–2.18) use silently when the chain rule is applied on a triple overlap.

### II.5 Charts, atlases and M-polyfolds (Definitions 2.3.2–2.3.8 (preprint 2.11–2.14))

**Definition 2.3.2 (preprint 2.11).** A *chart* on $X$ is a local model $(O, C, E)$ and a partial equivalence $\varphi$ between $X$ and $E_0$ with open source $V$ and target $O$, continuous on $V$, with inverse continuous on $O$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart⟧. Images of open subsets of $V$ are open subsets $O \cap W$ of $O$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.exists_isOpen_image_eq⟧, hence retracts (Proposition 2.3.1 (1) (preprint 2.10)) ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.isScRetract_image⟧, and charts restrict to open subsets of their sources ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.restrict⟧. The overlap $\varphi(V \cap V')$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.overlap⟧ is a retract ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.isScRetract_overlap⟧, the transition map is $\psi \circ \varphi^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.transition⟧, mapping $\varphi(V \cap V')$ into $\psi(V \cap V')$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.transition_mapsTo⟧, and two charts are *compatible* if both transition maps are sc-smooth between the overlap retracts ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.Compatible⟧. Compatibility is symmetric, reflexive, and passes to restrictions ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.Compatible.symm⟧ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.compatible_self⟧ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.Compatible.restrict⟧.

*Compatibility is local.* Let $\varphi$, $\psi$ be charts and $S$ a family of charts each compatible with $\varphi$ and with $\psi$, whose sources cover $V \cap V'$. Then $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are compatible ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.compatible_of_locally⟧. By the locality between retracts (§II.3) it suffices to show that $\psi \circ \varphi^{-1}$ is sc-smooth near every point $\varphi(x)$ of the overlap. Take $\chi \in S$ around $x$ and the triple overlap $s = V \cap V' \cap V''$, with $\varphi(s) = \varphi(V \cap V') \cap W$ for an open $W$. On $\varphi(s)$, $\psi \circ \varphi^{-1} = (\psi \circ \chi^{-1}) \circ (\chi \circ \varphi^{-1})$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MChart.transition_eq_comp_on⟧; the two factors are sc-smooth on the restricted retracts $\varphi(s)$ and $\chi(s)$, and Theorem 2.1.15 (preprint 2.8) composes them. The reverse transition is the same argument with the roles exchanged. This is the step that makes "the equivalence class of atlases" a usable notion; the text does not discuss it.

**Definition 2.3.3 (preprint 2.12).** An *atlas* is a set of pairwise compatible charts covering $X$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MAtlas⟧; two atlases are *equivalent* if their union is an atlas ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MAtlas.Equiv⟧, i.e. if every chart of one is compatible with every chart of the other ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MAtlas.equiv_iff⟧. The relation is reflexive and symmetric ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MAtlas.Equiv.refl⟧ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MAtlas.Equiv.symm⟧, and transitive by the locality of compatibility (§II.45) ⟦Chapter2/StrongBundleRestrict · MAtlas.Equiv.trans⟧.

**Definition 2.3.4 (preprint 2.13).** An *M-polyfold* structure on a Hausdorff paracompact space is an atlas ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold⟧. Its *charts* are all charts compatible with every chart of the atlas ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsChart⟧ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.isChart_of_mem⟧. By locality of compatibility (with $S$ the atlas), any two of them are compatible ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsChart.compatible⟧; restrictions of charts are charts ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsChart.restrict⟧; every point lies in one ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.exists_isChart_mem_source⟧; and equivalent atlases have the same charts, again by locality ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.isChart_congr⟧. So the maximal atlas represents the equivalence class, and every later definition (levels, index, tangent bundle) quantifies over it.

**Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14).** $f : X \to Y$ is *sc-smooth on the open set $U$* if it is continuous on $U$ and for all charts $\varphi$ of $X$, $\psi$ of $Y$ and every open $V \subseteq U \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi$ with $f(V) \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\psi$, the representation $\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1}$ is sc-smooth from $(\varphi(V), C, E)$ into $(O', C', E')$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothOn⟧; *sc-smooth* means sc-smooth on $X$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap⟧. Continuity is a field: the text's pairs of charts with $f(V) \subseteq V'$ exist around every point only for continuous $f$. The notion passes to open subsets and to maps agreeing on $U$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothOn.mono⟧ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothOn.congr⟧. *One pair of charts suffices*: if every $x \in U$ has charts $\varphi$, $\psi$ and an open $V \ni x$ with $\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1}$ sc-smooth on $\varphi(V)$, then $f$ is sc-smooth on $U$ ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothOn.of_exists_charts⟧. For arbitrary charts $\varphi'$, $\psi'$ and $V'$, locality reduces to a neighbourhood $\varphi'(V \cap V')$ of each point, where $\psi' \circ f \circ \varphi'^{-1} = (\psi' \circ \psi^{-1}) \circ (\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1}) \circ (\varphi \circ \varphi'^{-1})$, three sc-smooth maps between retracts composed by Theorem 2.1.15 (preprint 2.8). This is the text's "the definition does not depend on the choice of charts". The identity is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_id⟧, and compositions are sc-smooth by the same three-factor argument with a chart of the middle space ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothOn.comp⟧ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.comp⟧.

### II.6 The filtration $X_m$ and the M-polyfold $X^1$ (Lemma 2.3.9 (preprint 2.15))

*Levels.* $x$ is on level $m$ if $\varphi(x) \in \iota_m(E_m)$ for some chart $\varphi$ around $x$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.levelSet⟧. *Independence of the chart*: if $\psi$ is another chart around $x$, the transition map $\varphi \circ \psi^{-1}$ is sc-smooth between the overlap retracts, hence maps points on level $m$ to points on level $m$ (§II.3), and $\varphi(x) = (\varphi \circ \psi^{-1})(\psi(x))$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.mem_levelSet_iff⟧. $X_0 = X$, $X_{m+1} \subseteq X_m$, and $X_\infty = \bigcap_m X_m$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.levelSet_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.levelSet_succ_subset⟧ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.smoothSet⟧. For $x \in V_m$ the lift of $\varphi(x)$ to $E_m$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.levelLift⟧ satisfies $\iota_m(\text{lift}) = \varphi(x)$ and is compatible with the inclusions ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.toBase_levelLift⟧ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.levelLift_eq_incl⟧. $X_m$ carries the topology generated by the sets $\{x \in V : \text{lift}(x) \in W\}$, $W$ open in $E_m$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.levelBasis⟧ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.levelTopology⟧; that this family is a basis is not needed.

**Lemma 2.3.9 (preprint 2.15).** The preimage under $X_{m+1} \to X_m$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.levelIncl⟧ of a generating set $\{\text{lift}_m \in W\}$ is the generating set $\{\text{lift}_{m+1} \in \mathrm{incl}_m^{-1}(W)\}$, by the compatibility of lifts with inclusions; so the inclusion is continuous ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · lemma_2_3_9⟧. This is the text's proof.

*The space $X_m$.* As a type, $X_m$ is the subtype of points on level $m$ with this topology ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · MPolyfold.Level⟧. The inclusion $X_m \to X$ is continuous: for $V$ open in $X$ and $x \in X_m$, a chart $\varphi$ around $x$ gives $\varphi(V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi) = O \cap W$, and the generating set $\{\text{lift}_m \in W_m\}$ is a neighbourhood of $x$ inside the preimage of $V$ ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · MPolyfold.continuous_levelVal⟧ ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · MPolyfold.isOpen_level_basic⟧. Since this inclusion is injective and continuous into the Hausdorff $X$, $X_m$ is Hausdorff (an instance in `LevelPolyfold`, the text's argument with disjoint neighbourhoods).

*The level shift of the local data.* An sc-isomorphism shifts to $E^1 \to F^1$ ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · ScIso.shift⟧, so $C_1$ is a partial quadrant in $E^1$ and $U_1$ relatively open in it ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · IsPartialQuadrant.shift⟧ ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.shift⟧. A retraction $r$ induces the retraction $r_1$ on $U_1$ — sc-smooth by Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) (Part I, §I.15), idempotent by the injectivity of $\iota_1$ ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · ScRetraction.shift⟧ — with retract $O_1$ ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · ScRetraction.shift_retract⟧ ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · IsScRetract.shift⟧ ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · LocalModel.shift⟧. An sc-smooth map between retracts is $\mathrm{sc}^0$ on $O$, maps $O_m$ into $O'_m$ and is continuous there ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · IsScSmoothRetractMap.isSc0⟧ ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · IsScSmoothRetractMap.mapsTo_levelMap⟧ ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · IsScSmoothRetractMap.continuousOn_levelMap⟧, and its level-$1$ map is sc-smooth from $O_1$ to $O'_1$: with the retraction $r_1$, $f_1 \circ r_1 = (f \circ r)_1$, sc-smooth by Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · IsScSmoothRetractMap.shift⟧.

*The M-polyfold $X^1$.* For a chart $\varphi$ of $X$, $x \mapsto \text{lift}_1(x)$ on $V_1$ with model $(O_1, C_1, E^1)$ is a chart of $X_1$ ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · MPolyfold.levelChart⟧ (with a junk value for the inverse off $O_1$, since $X_1$ might be empty ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · MPolyfold.levelChartInv⟧); its overlap with another level chart is the level-$1$ part of the overlap ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · MPolyfold.levelChart_overlap⟧, its transition map the level-$1$ map of the transition map ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · MPolyfold.levelChart_transition⟧, and so any two level charts are compatible by the level shift of sc-smooth maps ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · MPolyfold.levelChart_compatible⟧. They form an atlas ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · MPolyfold.levelAtlas⟧, and $X_1$ with it is the M-polyfold $X^1$ ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · MPolyfold.shift⟧ ⟦Chapter2/LevelPolyfold · MPolyfold.shift_isChart⟧. Its paracompactness, an instance argument, is supplied by Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) (§II.7). Only $m = 1$ is constructed; the levels of $X^1$ are those of $X$ with their topology and charts, so the iterates are the $X_m$ (§II.32; gap G.6, closed).

### II.7 Metrizability: Smirnov's theorem and Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) (Theorem 2.7.1 (preprint 2.55))

The text proves Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) with Smirnov's theorem (2.55), Michael's characterization of paracompactness (Lemma 2.7.3 (preprint 2.56)) and Proposition 2.7.4 (preprint 2.57) (a regular space with a locally finite closed cover by paracompact subspaces is paracompact). Proposition 2.7.4 (preprint 2.57) needs $X_m$ to be regular, which the text does not check. The formal proof needs neither 2.56 nor 2.57.

*The metrization lemma.* Let $Y$ have open subspaces $V_i$, each metrizable with a metric $d_i$, and continuous $\rho_i : Y \to [0, \infty)$ with $\operatorname{supp}\rho_i \subseteq V_i$, the supports locally finite and $\rho_i(y) > 0$ for some $i$ at every $y$ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · metrizableSpace_of_partition⟧. Put $\delta_i(x, y) := \min(d_i(x, y), 1)$ for $x, y \in V_i$ and $1$ otherwise ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · truncDist⟧ — nonnegative, at most $1$, symmetric, zero only on the diagonal, and satisfying the triangle inequality inside $V_i$ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · truncDist_nonneg⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · truncDist_le_one⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · truncDist_triangle⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · truncDist_eq_zero⟧ — and the *cone metric*
$$e_i(x, y) := |\rho_i(x) - \rho_i(y)| + \min(\rho_i(x), \rho_i(y))\,\delta_i(x, y),\qquad D(x, y) := \sum_i e_i(x, y).$$
The sum is finite (only the $i$ with $x$ or $y$ in $\operatorname{supp}\rho_i$ contribute). $D(x, x) = 0$ and $D$ is symmetric. *Triangle inequality:* termwise, by an elementary inequality for $a, b, c \ge 0$ and $\delta$'s bounded by $1$, which needs the triangle inequality for $\delta_i$ only when $\min(\rho_i(x), \rho_i(z)) > 0$ and $\rho_i(y) > 0$, i.e. when all three points lie in $V_i$ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · cone_triangle⟧. *Separation:* if $D(x, y) = 0$, take $i$ with $\rho_i(x) > 0$; then $\rho_i(y) = \rho_i(x)$ and $\delta_i(x, y) = 0$, so $x = y$. *Topology:* $y \mapsto D(x, y)$ is continuous (locally a finite sum of continuous functions; the term $\min(\rho_i(x), \rho_i(y))\delta_i(x, y)$ is continuous where $y \in V_i$ and vanishes near points outside $\operatorname{supp}\rho_i$), so $D$-balls are open; conversely, if $s$ is open and $x \in s$, take $i$ with $\rho_i(x) > 0$ and a $d_i$-ball of radius $r \le 1$ around $x$ inside $s$; then $D(x, y) < \frac12\rho_i(x) r$ forces $\rho_i(y) > \frac12\rho_i(x)$ (so $y \in V_i$) and $\frac12\rho_i(x)\delta_i(x, y) < \frac12\rho_i(x) r$, so $d_i(x, y) < r$ and $y \in s$. Mathlib then builds a metric space structure with this distance and the given topology ⟦Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Defs · MetricSpace.ofDistTopology⟧.

*Pulled back, and Smirnov.* If $\pi : Y \to X$ is continuous into a paracompact Hausdorff $X$ and every point of $X$ has an open $U$ with $\pi^{-1}(U)$ metrizable, then $Y$ is metrizable: a partition of unity of $X$ subordinate to these $U$ ⟦Mathlib/Topology/PartitionOfUnity · PartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate⟧, composed with $\pi$, satisfies the hypotheses of the lemma with $V_i = \pi^{-1}(U_i)$ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · metrizableSpace_of_pullback⟧. With $\pi = \mathrm{id}$ this is **Smirnov's theorem** (Theorem 2.7.1 (preprint 2.55)) ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · metrizableSpace_of_locally⟧. Metrizable spaces are paracompact (Stone; in Mathlib through the instance for pseudo-emetric spaces) ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · paracompactSpace_of_metrizableSpace⟧.

**Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16).** *$X$ is metrizable*: chart domains are homeomorphic to subsets $O$ of the Banach space $E_0$ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MChart.sourceHomeomorph⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MChart.metrizableSpace_source⟧, and Smirnov applies ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.metrizableSpace⟧. *$V_m \cong O_m$*: the lift $x \mapsto \text{lift}_m(x)$ is a topological embedding of $V \cap X_m$ into $E_m$ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.isEmbedding_levelLift⟧. Its injectivity is that of $\varphi$; the induced topology is finer than that of $X_m$ because generating sets of $X_m$ inside $V$ are preimages of open sets; it is coarser because a generating set $\{\text{lift}^\psi_m \in W\}$ of another chart, intersected with $V$, is the preimage under $\text{lift}^\varphi_m$ of the open set $\{z \in \varphi(V \cap V')_m : (\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})_m(z) \in W\}$, open since the level-$m$ map of the transition is continuous on the level-$m$ part of the overlap retract. *$X_m$ is metrizable*: apply the pulled-back Smirnov to the continuous inclusion $X_m \to X$ and the chart domains $V$, whose preimages $V \cap X_m$ embed in $E_m$ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.metrizableSpace_level⟧; hence paracompact ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_level⟧. *$X_\infty$*: the text does not define its topology; it is taken to be the initial topology of the inclusions $X_\infty \to X_m$ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.SmoothLevel⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.smoothIncl⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.smoothLevel_topology_eq⟧. It embeds in the countable product $\prod_m X_m$, which is metrizable ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · metrizableSpace_pi_nat⟧, so $X_\infty$ is metrizable ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.metrizableSpace_smoothLevel⟧. Together ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · theorem_2_3_10⟧. *No hypothesis is added.* As a by-product every subset of an M-polyfold is metrizable, hence paracompact ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_subtype⟧, which discharges the paracompactness of sub-M-polyfolds (§II.10).

### II.8 The tangent bundle $TX$ (Definitions 2.3.12–2.3.14 (preprint 2.17–2.18), Proposition 2.3.15 (preprint 2.19))

*Tuples and transport.* A tangent tuple is $(x, \varphi, h)$ with $x \in X_1$, $\varphi$ a chart of the structure around $x$ and $(\text{lift}_1 x, h) \in TO$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre⟧; its vector is $(\text{lift}_1 x, h)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.vec⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.vec_mem⟧. For a vector of $TO$ over a point of an open $\varphi(s)$, membership in $TO$ and in $T(\varphi(s))$ agree (locality of the tangent, §II.4) ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.mem_retractTangent_image_iff⟧. The transport of the tuple to a chart $\psi$ around $x$ is $T(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})(\text{vec})$, the tangent map computed on the overlap retract ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.transport⟧. Transport to $\varphi$ itself does nothing, by $T(\mathrm{id}) = \mathrm{id}$ on the overlap $\varphi(V)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.transport_self⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MChart.transition_self_eqOn⟧; the transported vector lies in $TO'$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.transport_mem⟧ and has base point $\text{lift}^\psi_1(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.transport_fst⟧.

*The chain rule for transports.* Transporting to $\psi$ and then by $T(\chi \circ \psi^{-1})$ is transporting to $\chi$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.transport_transport⟧. On the triple overlap $s = V \cap V' \cap V''$ the transition maps are sc-smooth from $\varphi(s)$ to $\psi(s)$ and from $\psi(s)$ to $\chi(s)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MChart.Compatible.transition_image⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MChart.image_eq_overlap_inter⟧, $\chi \circ \varphi^{-1} = (\chi \circ \psi^{-1}) \circ (\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})$ there, and Theorem 2.1.15 (preprint 2.8) gives $T(\chi \circ \varphi^{-1}) = T(\chi \circ \psi^{-1}) \circ T(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})$ on $T(\varphi(s))$. The three tangent maps here are computed on $\varphi(s)$ and $\psi(s)$, the transports on the full overlaps; the locality of $Tf$ (§II.4) identifies them. The text never checks this.

**Definition 2.3.12 (preprint 2.17).** Two tuples are *equivalent* if their points agree and the transport of the first to the chart of the second is the second ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.Rel⟧. Equivalent tuples transport to the same vector in every chart (chain rule for transports) ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.Rel.transport⟧; hence the relation is reflexive, symmetric and transitive ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.Rel.refl⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.Rel.symm⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.Rel.trans⟧, an equivalence relation ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.setoid⟧.

**Definition 2.3.14 (preprint 2.18).** $TX$ is the quotient ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentSpace⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentSpace.mk⟧, with $p : TX \to X^1$, $[(x, \varphi, h)] \mapsto x$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentProj⟧, and $T_xX = p^{-1}(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentFiber⟧. For a chart $\varphi$: $TV = p^{-1}(V_1)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChartSet⟧ and $T\varphi : TV \to TO$ sends a class to the transport of a representative to $\varphi$, well defined by the previous paragraph ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChartMap⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_mk⟧; $T\varphi[(x, \varphi, h)] = (\varphi(x), h)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_mk_self⟧, $T\varphi$ lands in $TO$ over the lift of the base point ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_fst⟧, and it is injective on $TV$: equal images have equal base points (injectivity of $\varphi$ and $\iota_1$) and then the representatives are equivalent ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_injOn⟧. Its inverse on $TO$ is $a \mapsto [(\varphi^{-1}(\iota_1 a_1), \varphi, a_2)]$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentPre.ofVec⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_mk_ofVec⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.mk_ofVec_tangentChartMap⟧, and in another chart $T\psi \circ (T\varphi)^{-1} = T(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})$ on $T(\varphi(V \cap V'))$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_mk_ofVec_of_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.mk_ofVec_mem_tangentChartSet_iff⟧. The topology is generated by the sets $\{\alpha \in TV : T\varphi(\alpha) \in W\}$, $W$ open ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentBasis⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.isOpen_tangent_basic⟧; $TV$ itself is open ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.isOpen_tangentChartSet⟧. Here $T_xX$ is identified with $T_{\varphi(x)}O$ by $T\varphi$; its own vector space structure, for which $T\varphi$ is a linear isomorphism in every chart, is §II.39 ⟦Chapter2/TangentSpaceLinear · MPolyfold.tangentFiberLinearEquiv⟧.

**Proposition 2.3.15 (preprint 2.19).** (2) *$p$ is continuous*: the preimage of a generating set $\{\text{lift}^\psi_1 \in W\}$ of $X_1$ is the generating set of $TX$ given by $\psi$ and $W \times E_0$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.continuous_tangentProj⟧; so is $TX \to X$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.continuous_levelVal_tangentProj⟧. Openness of $p$ is §II.40 ⟦Chapter2/TangentProjOpen · MPolyfold.isOpenMap_tangentProj⟧. (1) *$TX$ is Hausdorff* (the instance `T2Space` in `TangentBundle`): two classes over the same point lie in one $TV$ and have distinct images under the injective $T\varphi$, separated by open sets of $E_1 \times E_0$ whose preimages are basic; classes over distinct points are separated by preimages of disjoint open sets of $X$ under the continuous $TX \to X$. (3) *$TX$ is metrizable*: apply the pulled-back Smirnov theorem to $TX \to X$ and the chart domains $V$, whose preimages $TV$ are homeomorphic to subsets of $E_1 \times E_0$ through the charts of §II.8's next paragraph ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.metrizableSpace_tangentSpace⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MChart.metrizableSpace_source⟧; hence paracompact ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_tangentSpace⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · proposition_2_3_15_three⟧.

*$TX$ as an M-polyfold.* For a chart $\varphi$ of $X$, $(TV, T\varphi, (TO, TC, TE))$ is a chart of $TX$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChart⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChartInv⟧; its overlap with another is $T(\varphi(V \cap V'))$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChart_overlap⟧ and its transition map is $T(\psi \circ \varphi^{-1})$ — formula (5) ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChart_transition⟧ — which is sc-smooth between the tangent retracts by the tangent functor (§II.4); so the charts are compatible ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentChart_compatible⟧, form an atlas ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentAtlas⟧ and make $TX$ an M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentPolyfold_isChart⟧. *$p : TX \to X^1$ is sc-smooth*: in the charts $T\varphi$ and the level chart of $\varphi$ it is the projection $TO \to O_1$, $(a, h) \mapsto a$, which is sc-smooth between the retracts $(TO, TC, TE)$ and $(O_1, C_1, E^1)$ because, with the retraction $Tr$ onto $TO$, $\mathrm{pr}_1 \circ Tr = r_1 \circ \mathrm{pr}_1$ on $TU$, a composite of the sc-operator $\mathrm{pr}_1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · ScBanach.tangentFst⟧ and the sc-smooth $r_1$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.isScSmoothRetractMap_tangent_fst⟧; one pair of charts per point suffices (§II.5) ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentProj_isScSmooth⟧.

### II.9 The tangent map of an sc-smooth map between M-polyfolds

The text uses $Tf$ for maps between M-polyfolds from §2.4 (preprint §2.3) on without defining it. *The chain rule on chart images, with locality*: for $F$ sc-smooth on $\varphi(s_1)$ into a retract $O_1$ mapping $\varphi(t)$ into $O'_1$, $G$ sc-smooth on $O'_1$ and $H$ sc-smooth on $\varphi(s_2)$ with $H = G \circ F$ on $\varphi(t)$ ($t \subseteq s_1 \cap s_2$ open), $TH = TG \circ TF$ on $T(\varphi(t))$, the three tangent maps computed on their own domains ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MChart.retractTangentMap_comp_image⟧ — Theorem 2.1.15 (preprint 2.8) on $\varphi(t)$ plus the locality of $Tf$. *Levels*: an sc-smooth map maps $X_m$ into $Y_m$, because its coordinate representations do ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothOn.mapsTo_levelSet⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.mapsTo_levelSet⟧. *The image vector*: for a tuple $(x, \varphi, h)$ and a chart $\psi$ around $f(x)$, $T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1})(\text{vec})$, computed on $\varphi(V \cap f^{-1}(V'))$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.fdom⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.ftransport⟧, lies in $TO'$ over $\psi(f(x))$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.ftransport_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.ftransport_fst⟧; changing $\psi$ changes it by $T$ of the transition map ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.ftransport_transport⟧, changing $\varphi$ by transport ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.ftransport_eq_of_transport⟧, and equivalent tuples give the same image ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.Rel.ftransport⟧ — all by the chain rule with locality. The image tuple $(f(x), \psi, \cdot)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.fimageWith⟧ therefore has a class independent of $\psi$ and of the representative ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.mk_fimageWith_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.TangentPre.mk_fimageWith_eq_of_rel⟧.

*$Tf$.* With a chosen $\psi$, $Tf[(x, \varphi, h)]$ is the class of the image tuple ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentMap⟧, computable in any chart around $f(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentMap_mk⟧. It covers $f$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.levelVal_tangentProj_tangentMap⟧, maps $T_xX$ into $T_{f(x)}Y$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentMap_mapsTo_fiber⟧, and in charts $T\psi \circ Tf = T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1}) \circ T\varphi$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentChartMap_tangentMap⟧. $T(\mathrm{id}) = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentMap_id⟧, and **the chain rule** $T(g \circ f) = Tg \circ Tf$ holds: with charts $\psi$ around $f(x)$ and $\chi$ around $g(f(x))$ and the open set $t = \operatorname{fdom}(\varphi, f, \psi) \cap f^{-1}(\operatorname{fdom}(\psi, g, \chi))$, the chain rule with locality gives $T(\chi \circ g \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1}) = T(\chi \circ g \circ \psi^{-1}) \circ T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1})$ on $T(\varphi(t))$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentMap_comp⟧. $Tf$ is continuous: near a class in $TV$, the preimage of a generating set of $TY$ contains the generating set of $TX$ given by $\varphi$ and the preimage under the continuous $T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1})$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.continuous_tangentMap⟧; and $Tf$ is sc-smooth $TX \to TY$, its representation in the charts $T\varphi$, $T\psi$ being $T(\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1})$, sc-smooth by the tangent functor ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentMap_isScSmooth⟧.

### II.10 Sub-M-polyfolds (Definition 2.3.18 (preprint 2.20), Proposition 2.3.19 (preprint 2.21))

**Definition 2.3.18 (preprint 2.20).** $A \subseteq X$ is a *sub-M-polyfold* if every $a \in A$ has an open $V \ni a$ and a map $r$ with $r(V) \subseteq V$, sc-smooth on $V$, idempotent on $V$, with $r(V) = A \cap V$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsSubMPolyfold⟧; $X$ is one ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_univ⟧. The data at a point are packaged ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.IsSubMPolyfold.data⟧: $r$ maps $V$ into $A$, fixes $A \cap V$, and is continuous on $V$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.apply_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.apply_eq_self⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.continuousOn⟧.

**Proposition 2.3.19 (preprint 2.21), the structure.** *Shrinking.* For a chart $\varphi$, put $W := (V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi) \cap r^{-1}(V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi)$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.shrink⟧: open (continuity of $r$) ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.isOpen_shrink⟧, containing every $a \in A \cap V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.mem_shrink⟧, with $r(W) \subseteq W$ and $r(W) = W \cap A$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.mapsTo_shrink⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.image_shrink⟧. *The retract.* $\rho := \varphi \circ r \circ \varphi^{-1}$ is sc-smooth from $\varphi(W)$ to itself — Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14) for $r$ in the charts $\varphi$, $\varphi$ — idempotent, and $\rho(\varphi(W)) = \varphi(W \cap A)$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.rho_isScSmooth⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.rho_idem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.rho_image⟧; so $\varphi(W \cap A)$ is a retract by Proposition 2.3.1 (2) (preprint 2.10) ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.isScRetract_image⟧. *The chart.* With the subspace topology on $A$, $\varphi$ restricted to $W \cap A$ is a chart of $A$ with model $(\varphi(W \cap A), C, E)$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subChart⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subChartInv⟧. *Compatibility.* The overlap of two such charts is $\varphi((W \cap W') \cap A)$, a subset of $\varphi(V \cap V')$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subChart_overlap⟧. An sc-smooth map between retracts is sc-smooth on every sub-retract $O_1 \subseteq O$: for a retraction $s$ onto $O_1$, $f \circ s = (f \circ r) \circ s$, sc-smooth by the chain rule ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · IsScSmoothRetractMap.mono_source⟧ — this is the text's "$(\psi' \circ \psi^{-1}) \circ s'' = (\varphi' \circ \varphi^{-1}) \circ s''$". The transition maps of the sub-charts are restrictions of those of $X$, hence sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subChart_compatible⟧. They form an atlas ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subAtlas⟧, and $A$ is an M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subPolyfold_isChart⟧. The structure requires $A$ to be paracompact (an instance argument); it is, as a subset of the metrizable $X$ (§II.7), and for closed $A$ also elementarily ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_of_isClosed⟧.

*(1) and (2).* The inclusion $A \to X$ is sc-smooth: in the sub-chart and $\varphi$ it is the identity of $\varphi(W \cap A)$ into $O$; one pair of charts per point suffices ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subPolyfold_inclusion_isScSmooth⟧; it is a homeomorphism onto its image by the choice of topology. For any data $(V, r)$, the map $i^{-1} \circ r$ (a total map with a junk value off $V$) ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.retractInto⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.SubData.retractInto_val⟧ is sc-smooth on $V$: near $x \in V$ take a chart $\varphi'$ around $x$, a chart $\varphi$ around $r(x)$ and $V_0 = V \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi' \cap r^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\varphi)$; on $\varphi'(V_0)$ the representation in $\varphi'$ and the sub-chart on $\varphi$ is $\varphi \circ r \circ \varphi'^{-1}$, sc-smooth by Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14) for $r$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · MPolyfold.subPolyfold_retraction_isScSmooth⟧.

**Proposition 2.3.19 (3), (4) (preprint 2.21), in a chart.** Let $r$ be a retraction onto $O$, $s$ sc-smooth from $(O, C, E)$ to itself with $s \circ s = s$, and $t := s \circ r$, a retraction onto $s(O)$ (Proposition 2.3.1 (2) (preprint 2.10)) ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · ScRetraction.compRetraction⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · ScRetraction.compRetraction_retract⟧. For $a \in s(O)_1$ put $P := Dr(a)$, $Q := Dt(a) = D(s \circ r)(a)$ — the text's "$Ds(a)$". Both are idempotent (§II.2). From $r \circ t = t$ and $t \circ r = t$ on $U$ ($s$ takes values in $O$, which $r$ fixes; and $r \circ r = r$), the chain rule at the point $a$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · scDeriv_comp_apply⟧ gives $PQ = Q$ and $QP = Q$. If $a$ is smooth, $P$ and $Q$ are sc-operators (Part I, Proposition 1.2.1 (preprint 1.16)), and so is $P - Q$; identities between base maps of sc-operators hold on every level ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · ScOperator.lvl_comp_of_base⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · ScOperator.lvl_comp_eq_zero_of_base⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · ScOperator.lvl_eq_add_of_base⟧. Then $Q$ and $P - Q$ are commuting idempotent sc-operators with $Q(P - Q) = 0$, their ranges are sc-subspaces (Part I, §I.3: sc-splittings and sc-projections ⟦Chapter1/ExpositionLemmas · ScBanach.isScSplitting_of_idem⟧), and on every level the level parts of $QE$ and $(P - Q)E$ are disjoint with sum the level part of $PE$. Since $T_aO = PE$ and $T_a s(O) = QE$ (§II.2), this is the sc-splitting $T_aO = T_aA \oplus (Dr(a) - Dt(a))E$ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · proposition_2_3_19_three⟧. For (4), $s$ is sc-smooth from $O$ onto $s(O)$ (shrinking the target), and $Ts(a, h) = (a, Q h)$ for $h \in T_aO$ because $Q h = Q P h$; as $Q$ maps $PE$ onto $QE = Q(PE)$, $Ts(a)$ maps $T_aO$ onto $T_a s(O)$ ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · proposition_2_3_19_four⟧. The transport to $T_aX$ is §II.39 ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldTangent · MPolyfold.proposition_2_3_19_3_linear⟧ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldTangent · MPolyfold.proposition_2_3_19_4⟧.

### II.11 The degeneracy index of an M-polyfold (Definitions 2.4.1, 2.4.5 (preprint 2.22, 2.25); Lemmas 2.4.3, 2.4.6 (preprint 2.23, 2.26); Proposition 2.4.4 (preprint 2.24))

A retract is contained in its quadrant, and chart values lie in $C$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · LocalModel.O_subset_C⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MChart.apply_mem_C⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · LocalModel.isPartialQuadrant⟧. **Definition 2.4.1 (preprint 2.22).** $d(x, \varphi) := d_C(\varphi(x))$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.chartDegIndex⟧, and $d_X(x)$ is the least $d(x, \varphi)$ over the charts of the structure around $x$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.degIndex⟧; $d_X(x) \le d(x, \varphi)$ for every such chart and the minimum is attained ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.degIndex_le⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.exists_isChart_degIndex_eq⟧. **Lemma 2.4.3 (preprint 2.23).** $d_C$ is upper semicontinuous: coordinates positive at $x$ stay positive nearby, so the vanishing set can only shrink ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · eventually_degIndexWith_le⟧; composed with the continuous chart, $d(\cdot, \varphi)$ is upper semicontinuous on $V$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.eventually_chartDegIndex_le⟧, and with a chart realizing $d_X(x)$, $d_X(y) \le d(y, \varphi) \le d(x, \varphi) = d_X(x)$ near $x$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · lemma_2_4_3⟧. Hence $\{d_X < k\}$ is open and $\{d_X \ge k\}$ closed ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.isOpen_setOf_degIndex_lt⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.isClosed_setOf_le_degIndex⟧.

**Proposition 2.4.4 (preprint 2.24).** An sc-diffeomorphism of open sets is $f$ sc-smooth on $U$, $g$ sc-smooth on $V$, mapping into each other and mutually inverse ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.symm⟧. For a chart $\psi$ of $Y$, $\psi \circ f$ on $U \cap f^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}\psi)$, with inverse $g \circ \psi^{-1}$, is a chart of $X$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.transportChart⟧; it is compatible with every chart $\varphi$ of the atlas of $X$, because its transition maps with $\varphi$ are $\psi \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1}$ and $\varphi \circ g \circ \psi^{-1}$, sc-smooth by Definition 2.3.8 (preprint 2.14) for $f$ and for $g$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.transportChart_isChart⟧. Its index at $x$ is $d(f(x), \psi)$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.chartDegIndex_transportChart⟧. With $\psi$ realizing $d_Y(f(x))$: $d_X(x) \le d_Y(f(x))$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.degIndex_le_of_isScDiffeoOn⟧, and with $g$ the reverse ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · proposition_2_4_4⟧. The text's "from the definitions one deduces immediately" is this construction.

**Definition 2.4.5 (preprint 2.25).** $\partial X = \{d_X \ge 1\}$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.boundary⟧; without boundary means $d_X \equiv 0$, equivalently $\partial X = \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.IsWithoutBoundary⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · MPolyfold.isWithoutBoundary_iff⟧. $\partial X$ and the corners $\{d_X \ge 2\}$ are closed, the interior $\{d_X = 0\}$ is open ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.isClosed_boundary⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.corners⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.isClosed_corners⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.isOpen_interior⟧, and sc-diffeomorphisms preserve $\partial X$ by Proposition 2.4.4 (preprint 2.24) ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.mem_boundary_iff⟧.

**Lemma 2.4.6 (preprint 2.26).** For a sub-M-polyfold $A$ and $a \in A$: take a chart $\varphi$ of $X$ realizing $d_X(a)$ and the data at $a$; the sub-chart built on $\varphi$ has the same quadrant $C$ and the same value $\varphi(a)$, so $d_A(a) \le d_C(\varphi(a)) = d_X(a)$ ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfold · lemma_2_4_6⟧.

*A retract as an M-polyfold.* A nonempty retract $O$, as a subtype, has the single chart $\mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · LocalModel.selfChart⟧, compatible with itself, and is an M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · LocalModel.toMPolyfold⟧ (Hausdorff and paracompact as a subspace of $E_0$); so is a nonempty relatively open $U \subseteq C$ ⟦Chapter2/MPolyfold · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.toMPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.selfChart_isChart⟧ — the text's $X_C$.

### II.12 The subspaces $E_x$, the cones $C_x$ and the sign arguments

*Coordinates.* For a presentation $T$ of $C$ and $x \in E_0$, the coordinates vanishing at $x$ form a continuous linear surjection $E_0 \to \mathbb R^{I(x)}$, $v \mapsto ((Tv)_i)_{i \in I(x)}$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · coordProj⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · coordMapL⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · coordMapL_surjective⟧. Its kernel is $E_x$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · minimalSubspaceWith⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · mem_minimalSubspaceWith⟧, closed ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · isClosed_minimalSubspaceWith⟧, and by the first isomorphism theorem $E_0/E_x \cong \mathbb R^{I(x)}$, so $\dim(E_0/E_x) = d_C(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · finrank_quotient_minimalSubspaceWith⟧. The cone $C_x = \{v : (Tv)_i \ge 0 \text{ for } i \in I(x)\}$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · partialQuadrantAtWith⟧ is convex and closed and contains $E_x$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · convex_partialQuadrantAtWith⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · isClosed_partialQuadrantAtWith⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · minimalSubspaceWith_subset_partialQuadrantAtWith⟧. *Approximation*: if $Tx = (a, w)$, the points $T^{-1}(a, w')$ with $w' \in W_1$ (resp. $W_\infty$) converge to $x$ as $w' \to w$ and have the same vanishing coordinates, so $x$ is a limit of points on level $1$ (resp. smooth points) of the same index, in $C$ iff $x$ is ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · exists_tendsto_lvl1_degIndexWith⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · exists_tendsto_smooth_degIndexWith⟧.

*Density on level $1$.* For a continuous linear $L : E_0 \to V$, $V$ finite-dimensional, the level-$1$ points of $\ker L$ are dense in $\ker L$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · ScBanach.subset_closure_ker_inter_range_toBase⟧. The image $S$ of $E_1$ is dense in $E_0$; $L$ maps $S$ onto the finite-dimensional $L(S)$, which has a linear, hence continuous, right inverse $g$ with values in $S$. For $v \in \ker L$ take $u_k \in S$ with $u_k \to v$; then $L(u_k) \to 0$, $g(L(u_k)) \to 0$, and $u_k - g(L(u_k)) \in S \cap \ker L$ converges to $v$. This is the text's "the closure of $(T^R_xO)_\infty$ is $T^R_xO$" in the form the proofs need; the level-$1$ points of $C_x$ are dense in $C_x$ likewise ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · partialQuadrantAtWith_subset_closure⟧.

*The two-sided sign argument.* Let $f$ be sc¹ on $U$ relatively open in $C$, with values in $C'$, $x \in U_1$ and $v \in E_1$ with $\iota_1 v \in E_x$. Then $x + tv \in U_1$ for $|t|$ small: the coordinates in $I(x)$ stay $0$, the others stay positive, and $U_1$ is relatively open ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · eventually_add_smul_mem_lvlSet⟧. For $j$ with $(T'f(x))_j = 0$ the real function $g(t) = (T'f(\iota_1(x + tv)))_j$ is $\ge 0$ near $0$ (values in $C'$), vanishes at $0$, and has derivative $(T' Df(x)v)_j$ at $0$ (Definition 1.1.15's (preprint 1.14) derivative along $E_1$, composed with the path); a local minimum has zero derivative ⟦Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/LocalExtr/Basic · IsLocalMin.hasDerivAt_eq_zero⟧. So $Df(x)v \in E'_{f(x)}$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · IsSc1With.deriv_mem_minimalSubspace_of_lvl1⟧, and by density and continuity of $Df(x)$ on $E_0$, $Df(x)$ maps $E_x$ into $E'_{f(x)}$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · IsSc1With.mapsTo_minimalSubspace⟧.

*The one-sided sign argument.* For $v \in E_1$ with $\iota_1 v \in C_x$, $x + tv \in U_1$ for small $t \ge 0$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · eventually_add_smul_mem_lvlSet_of_cone⟧, the same $g$ is $\ge 0$ on $[0, \varepsilon)$ with $g(0) = 0$, so its one-sided derivative is $\ge 0$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · nonneg_of_hasDerivWithinAt_Ici⟧; hence $Df(x)v \in C'_{f(x)}$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · IsSc1With.deriv_mem_partialQuadrant_of_lvl1⟧, and $Df(x)$ maps $C_x$ into $C'_{f(x)}$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · IsSc1With.mapsTo_partialQuadrant⟧. These are the derivative-level content of Lemma 2.4.9 (1) and (2) (preprint 2.29); the lemma itself, about sc-smooth paths, is proved from them in §II.42 ⟦Chapter2/GapP1_Lemma249 · GapP1Lemma249.lemma_2_4_9_cone⟧.

*The chain rule at a point.* For sc¹ maps $f$, $g$ on relatively open sets with $f(U) \subseteq U'$, $Dg(f(x)) Df(x) = D(g \circ f)(x)$ at $x \in U_1$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · scDeriv_comp_apply⟧; if $g \circ f = \mathrm{id}$ on $U$ then $g_1(f_1(x)) = x$ and $Dg(f(x)) Df(x) = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · levelMap_comp_eq_self⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · scDeriv_comp_eq_self⟧.

### II.13 Proposition 2.4.10 (preprint 2.30), Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31), Corollary 2.4.13 (preprint 2.32)

**Definition 2.4.7 (preprint 2.27), Remark 2.4.8 (preprint 2.28).** For a retraction $r$, a presentation $T$ and $x \in O_1$: $T^R_xO := Dr(x)E_0 \cap E_x$ and $C_xO := Dr(x)E_0 \cap C_x$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · reducedTangentSpaceWith⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · partialConeWith⟧, defined at every point on level $1$; $T^R_xO \subseteq C_xO$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · reducedTangentSpaceWith_subset_partialConeWith⟧. The remark's further claim, that $C_xO$ is in general not a partial quadrant in $T_xO$, does not hold as we read it: at a smooth point it always is one (§II.41). The number $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO)$ is $\dim(A/(A \cap B))$ for $A = T_xO$, $B = E_x$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · quotDim⟧; since $A \to E_0/E_x$ has kernel $A \cap E_x$, it is at most $d_C(x)$ and finite ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · quotDim_inf_minimalSubspace_le⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · quotDim_reducedTangentSpaceWith_le⟧.

*Germs between retracts.* A germ of sc-diffeomorphisms between $O = r(U)$ and $O' = r'(U')$ is a pair $F$, $G$ with $F \circ r$, $G \circ r'$ sc¹ (sc¹ suffices here; the text has sc-smooth), $F(O) \subseteq O'$, $G(O') \subseteq O$, inverse to each other on $O$, $O'$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm⟧; an sc-smooth map between retracts with an sc-smooth inverse is one ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · IsScSmoothRetractMap.isDiffeoGerm⟧, and two compatible charts give one between the overlap retracts, with the restricted retractions ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MChart.Compatible.isDiffeoGerm⟧. Since $(G \circ r') \circ (F \circ r) = r$ on $U$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.comp_eq⟧, the chain rule at $x \in O_1$, $y = (F \circ r)_1(x) \in O'_1$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.image_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.image_image⟧, gives
$$D(G \circ r')(y)\,D(F \circ r)(x) = Dr(x),\qquad D(F \circ r)(x)\,D(G \circ r')(y) = Dr'(y)$$
⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.deriv_inv_deriv⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.deriv_deriv_inv⟧. So $D := D(F \circ r)(x)$ maps $T_xO$ into $T_yO'$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.deriv_mem_range⟧, and by the sign arguments for $F \circ r$ (with values in $O' \subseteq C'$) it maps $E_x$ into $E'_y$ and $C_x$ into $C'_y$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.deriv_mapsTo_minimalSubspace⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.deriv_mapsTo_partialQuadrant⟧.

**Proposition 2.4.10 (preprint 2.30).** $D(T^R_xO) = T^R_yO'$ and $D(C_xO) = C_yO'$, with $Tf(x) = D$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · proposition_2_4_10_reduced⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · proposition_2_4_10_cone⟧. "$\subseteq$": $D$ maps $T_xO$ into $T_yO'$ and $E_x$ (resp. $C_x$) into $E'_y$ (resp. $C'_y$). "$\supseteq$": for $w \in T^R_yO'$, the vector $D' w$, $D' = D(G \circ r')(y)$, lies in $T_xO$ and in $E_x$ by the same facts for the inverse germ, and $D(D' w) = Dr'(y) w = w$ because $w$ is in the range of the projection $Dr'(y)$. This proof does not pass through Lemma 2.4.9 (preprint 2.29).

*The core of Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31).* Along a germ $F$, $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) \le d_{C'}(F(x))$ for $x \in O_1$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.IsDiffeoGerm.quotDim_le⟧. With $P = Dr(x)$, $P' = Dr'(y)$: $D$ maps $T_x = PE$ into $T_y = P'E'$ and $D'$ maps back, $D'D = P$ is the identity on $T_x$ and $DD' = P'$ the identity on $T_y$. The map $\Phi : T_x \to T_y/(T_y \cap E'_y)$, $v \mapsto [Dv]$, is onto ($[w] = \Phi(D'w)$) with kernel $T_x \cap E_x$ ($Dv \in E'_y$ implies $v = D'Dv \in E_x$). Hence $T_x/T^R_x \cong T_y/T^R_y$, which embeds in $E'_0/E'_y$, of dimension $d_{C'}(y)$. The same argument with $U_0$ relatively open in $C$ in place of the retract $O$ is the form used for Corollary 2.4.13 (preprint 2.32) and Theorem 1.3.5 (preprint 1.25) ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · degIndexWith_le_of_germ⟧: there $D'D = \mathrm{id}$, so $E_0/E_x \cong T_y/T^R_y \hookrightarrow E'_0/E'_y$ and $d_C(x) \le d_{C'}(F(x))$.

**Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31).** Let $\varphi$ be a chart of an M-polyfold around $x$ with $\varphi(x) = \iota_1 z$, $r$ a retraction onto its model and $T$ a presentation. For every other chart $\psi$ around $x$, the overlaps are $O \cap W$ and $O' \cap W'$, the transition maps form a germ between the restricted retractions, and the restricted retraction has the same derivative at $z$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · ScRetraction.scDeriv_restrict⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · reducedTangentSpaceWith_restrict⟧; so the core gives $\dim(T_zO/T^R_zO) \le d(x, \psi)$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.quotDim_le_chartDegIndex⟧. Taking $\psi$ realizing $d_X(x)$: $\dim(T_zO/T^R_zO) \le d_X(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · theorem_2_4_12⟧. For a retract $O$ as an M-polyfold with the chart $\mathrm{id}$ this is the text's statement $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) \le d_O(x)$, at points on level $1$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · theorem_2_4_12_retract⟧. The text instead reduces to a chart realizing $d_O(x)$ and counts linearly independent $\mathbb R^d$-components; the quotient isomorphism makes the reduction unnecessary. The second statement (equality makes $C_xO$ a partial quadrant) is §II.41, proved without the hypothesis: at every smooth point of every retract, $C_xO$ is a partial quadrant of dimension $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO)$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialConeQuadrant · remark_2_4_8_isPartialQuadrant⟧.

**Corollary 2.4.13 (preprint 2.32).** Let $U$ be nonempty and relatively open in $C$, and $X_U$ its M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · corollary_2_4_13⟧. The chart $\mathrm{id}$ gives $d_{X_U} \le d_C$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.degIndex_le⟧. At a point $x$ on level $1$, a chart $\psi$ realizing $d_{X_U}(x)$ is compatible with $\mathrm{id}$, so $F = \psi$ (on $U_0 = \operatorname{dom}\psi$, relatively open in $C$) and $G = \psi^{-1}$ form a germ from $U_0$ to the retract $\psi(V)$, and the core gives $d_C(x) \le d_{C'}(\psi(x)) = d_{X_U}(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · IsRelOpenInQuadrant.degIndex_le_degIndex_of_lvl1⟧. For a general $x$, approximate by level-$1$ points $\sigma_i \in U$ with $d_C(\sigma_i) = d_C(x)$ (§II.12); by Lemma 2.4.3 (preprint 2.23), $d_{X_U}(\sigma_i) \le d_{X_U}(x)$ eventually, so $d_C(x) = d_C(\sigma_i) \le d_{X_U}(\sigma_i) \le d_{X_U}(x)$. The text approximates by smooth points; level $1$ suffices. **Theorem 1.3.5 (preprint 1.25)** (Part I, §I.19) is proved in the same file by the same argument for a germ between relatively open subsets of two quadrants ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · theorem_1_3_5_lvl1⟧ ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · theorem_1_3_5⟧.

### II.14 Tame retractions; Propositions 2.5.3 and 2.5.6 (preprint 2.35 and 2.36)

**Definition 2.5.1 (preprint 2.33).** $C_e$ and $E_e$ are the cone and subspace of §II.12 for the presentation $T$. They do not depend on it: for two presentations $T$, $T'$ of $C$ and $e \in C$, $v \in E_e$ (for $T$) gives $e + tv \in C$ for $|t|$ small ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · eventually_add_smul_mem_of_minimalSubspace⟧; for $j$ with $(T'e)_j = 0$, $(T'(e + tv))_j = t(T'v)_j \ge 0$ for $t = \pm\delta/2$, so $(T'v)_j = 0$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · minimalSubspaceWith_le⟧; by symmetry the two subspaces agree ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · minimalSubspaceWith_eq⟧. This is the argument of Lemma 1.3.4 (preprint 1.24).

**Definition 2.5.2 (preprint 2.34).** $r$ is *tame for $T$* if (1) $d_C(r(x)) = d_C(x)$ on $U$ and (2) at every smooth $x \in O_1$ some $A \le E_x$ makes $E = Dr(x)E_0 \oplus A$ an sc-splitting ⟦Chapter2/Tame · ScRetraction.IsTameWith⟧; *tame* if tame for every presentation ⟦Chapter2/Tame · ScRetraction.IsTame⟧, and by the independence of $E_x$ tameness for one presentation suffices ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · ScRetraction.IsTameWith.isTame⟧. A *tame retract* is the retract of a tame retraction ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsTameRetract⟧ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · IsTameRetract.isScRetract⟧. Identities of relatively open sets are tame ($T_xU = E$, $A = 0$) ⟦Chapter2/Tame · ScRetraction.id_isTame⟧, and restrictions of tame retractions to $U \cap r^{-1}(V)$ are tame (same derivatives) ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · ScRetraction.IsTameWith.restrict⟧.

**Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35).** *$Dr(x)E_x \subseteq E_x$ for every retraction at every $x \in O_1$*: the two-sided sign argument for $r$, with $r(x) = x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.scDeriv_mapsTo_minimalSubspace⟧. At a smooth $x$, $Dr(x)$ is an sc-operator ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.isScOperator_scDeriv⟧, so $E = Dr(x)E \oplus (1 - Dr(x))E$ is an sc-splitting ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.isScSplitting_range_scDeriv⟧. *The proposition* ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · proposition_2_5_3⟧: with $A \le E_x$ from tameness (2), $E_0 = Dr(x)E_0 \oplus A$ algebraically (the level-$0$ part of the sc-splitting); write $v = t + a$; then $(1 - Dr(x))v = (1 - Dr(x))a = a - Dr(x)a \in E_x$, because $a \in E_x$ and $Dr(x)a \in E_x$. Only condition (2) is used; the text uses condition (1) for $Dr(x)E_x \subseteq E_x$. In coordinates: $\lambda_j(Dr(x)v) = \lambda_j(v)$ for $j \in I(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coord_scDeriv_eq⟧.

**Proposition 2.5.6 (preprint 2.36).** *(13) at smooth points.* If $V = A' \oplus B$ and $B \le K$, then $A'/(A' \cap K) \cong V/K$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · quotDim_eq_finrank_quotient_of_isCompl⟧; with $A' = T_xO$, $B = A$ and $K = E_x$ this gives $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) = \dim(E_0/E_x) = d_C(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · quotDim_reducedTangentSpaceWith_eq⟧ — the text's equations (15)–(16). *A tame chart realizes the index* ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.degIndex_eq_chartDegIndex_of_isTameWith⟧: let $\varphi$ be a chart of any M-polyfold whose model has a tame retraction $r$. At $y$ with $\varphi(y)$ smooth, $d(y, \varphi) = \dim(T/T^R) \le d_X(y)$ by Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31), and $d_X(y) \le d(y, \varphi)$ by definition. At a general $y$, with $\varphi(y) = o$, approximate $o$ by smooth points $\sigma_i$ of $C$ with the same vanishing coordinates; then $r(\sigma_i)$ are smooth points of $O$ (an $\mathrm{sc}^0$ map preserves smoothness ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · IsSc0.mem_smooth⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · exists_smoothLvl_one_of_mem_smooth⟧) converging to $r(o) = o$, with $d_C(r(\sigma_i)) = d_C(\sigma_i) = d_C(o)$ by tameness (1); so the points $\varphi^{-1}(r(\sigma_i))$ converge to $y$ and have $d_X = d(\cdot, \varphi) = d_C(o)$, and Lemma 2.4.3 (preprint 2.23) gives $d_C(o) \le d_X(y)$. For charts of the structure modelled on a tame retract ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.degIndex_eq_chartDegIndex_of_isTameRetract⟧. Applied to the retract itself as an M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.toLocalModel⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · LocalModel.degIndex_toMPolyfold_of_isTameWith⟧: (14) $d_O = d_C$ on $O$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · proposition_2_5_6_degIndex⟧ and (13) $\dim(T_xO/T^R_xO) = d_O(x) = d_C(x)$ at smooth points ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · proposition_2_5_6⟧. This is the text's proof, generalized from the retract to any chart; Proposition 2.5.14 (preprint 2.42) needs the general form.

*Splitting off finitely many coordinates.* Let $B \le A$ be sc-subspaces of $E$, $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_d$ continuous functionals on $E_0$ with $B = A \cap \bigcap_j \ker \ell_j$, and $e_1, \dots, e_d \in A$ smooth with $\ell_i(e_j) = \delta_{ij}$. Each $e_j$ has a lift to every level $m$, compatible with the inclusions ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · smoothLift⟧ ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · incl_smoothLift⟧. On level $m$ the maps $v \mapsto ((\ell_j v)_j,\ v - \sum_j \ell_j(v) e_j)$ and $(a, u) \mapsto u + \sum_j a_j e_j$ are continuous linear $A_m \to \mathbb R^d \times B_m$ and back ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · splitFwd⟧ ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · splitBwd⟧ — the bracket lies in $B$ because every $\ell_i$ kills it ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · sub_sum_mem⟧ — and mutually inverse ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · splitBwd_splitFwd⟧ ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · splitFwd_splitBwd⟧; they commute with the inclusions, so they form an sc-isomorphism $A \cong \mathbb R^d \oplus B$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · splitIso⟧, $A$ and $B$ with the sc-structures induced from $E$ ⟦Chapter1/ScBanach · ScBanach.ofSubspace⟧. It carries $\{v \in A : \ell_j(v) \ge 0\ \forall j\}$ onto $[0, \infty)^d \oplus B$, so that set is a partial quadrant in $A$ ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · isPartialQuadrant_ofSubspace⟧. This is the map $S$ of the proof of Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31), with the $e_j$ smooth as the exposition requires.

**Proposition 2.5.6 (preprint 2.36), the remaining statements** ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · proposition_2_5_6_partialCone⟧. Let $r$ be tame for $T$, $x \in O_1$ smooth, $P = Dr(x)$ and $I(x) = \{i_1, \dots, i_d\}$. $T_xO = PE$ is an sc-subspace, the range of the sc-projection $P$ (Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35) above) ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.isScSplitting_range_scDeriv⟧. The vectors $\hat e_j := P(T^{-1}(e_{i_j}, 0))$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coordVec⟧ lie in $T_xO$; they are smooth, because $T^{-1}(e_{i_j}, 0)$ is smooth ⟦Chapter2/PartialCone · coordVec_mem_smooth⟧ and $P$ is an sc-operator at the smooth point $x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.isScOperator_scDeriv⟧ ⟦Chapter1/ScBanach · ScOperator.mapsTo_smoothLvl⟧; and $\lambda_{i_k}(\hat e_j) = \lambda_{i_k}(T^{-1}(e_{i_j}, 0)) = \delta_{jk}$ by Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35) in coordinates ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coord_scDeriv_eq⟧. By definition $T^R_xO = T_xO \cap \bigcap_k \ker \lambda_{i_k}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coordL⟧. *$T^R_xO$ is an sc-subspace.* It is closed, as an intersection of closed subspaces ⟦Chapter2/DegeneracyIndex · isClosed_minimalSubspaceWith⟧. For the density of smooth points, let $u \in T^R_xO \cap E_m$ with $Tu = (a, w)$ on level $m$, and put $\phi(w') := P(T^{-1}(a, w'))$, a continuous map $W_m \to E_m$. For smooth $w'$ the point $\phi(w')$ is smooth, lies in $T_xO$, and lies in $E_x$, because $T^{-1}(a, w')$ has the same vanishing coordinates in $I(x)$ as $u$ and $P E_x \subseteq E_x$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.scDeriv_mapsTo_minimalSubspace⟧. And $\phi(w) = Pu = u$, since $u \in T_xO$ and $P$ is a projection ⟦Chapter2/Retracts · ScRetraction.scDeriv_comp_self⟧. As $W_\infty$ is dense in $W_m$, $u$ lies in the closure of $\phi(W_\infty) \subseteq T^R_xO \cap E_\infty$ (this is the exposition's Lemma 3.A (1) in the case at hand). *The quadrant.* The splitting with $A = T_xO$, $B = T^R_xO$, $\ell_j = \lambda_{i_j}$ and $e_j = \hat e_j$ makes $\{v \in T_xO : \lambda_{i_j}(v) \ge 0\ \forall j\}$ a partial quadrant in $T_xO$, and this set is $C_xO = T_xO \cap C_x$. The text deduces the claim from the equality case of Theorem 2.4.12 (preprint 2.31), which needs smooth lifts $\hat v^j$ of a basis of $T_xO/T^R_xO$ (the exposition chooses them by a density argument); for a tame retraction they are the explicit $\hat e_j$, and the general equality case, proved in §II.41, is not needed here.

### II.15 Faces: local geometry, Lemma 2.5.12 (preprint 2.40), Corollary 2.5.13 (preprint 2.41), Proposition 2.5.14 (preprint 2.42)

**Definitions 2.5.7, 2.5.10 (preprint 2.37, 2.39).** $X$ is *tame* if an atlas equivalent to its atlas has only tame models ⟦Chapter2/Tame · MPolyfold.IsTame⟧; charts of an equivalent atlas are charts of the structure ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.isChart_of_mem_equiv⟧, so every point lies in a chart of the structure with a tame model ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.IsTame.exists_chart⟧. A *face* is the closure of the connected component in $\{d_X = 1\}$ of a point with $d_X = 1$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · MPolyfold.IsFace⟧, closed ⟦Chapter2/Tame · MPolyfold.IsFace.isClosed⟧ and inside $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter2/Boundary · MPolyfold.IsFace.subset_boundary⟧; $X$ is *face-structured* if every $x$ lies in exactly $d_X(x)$ faces ⟦Chapter2/Tame · MPolyfold.IsFaceStructured⟧.

*Coordinates of faces.* $I(z) = \{i : \lambda_i(z) = 0\}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · zeroSet⟧ with $d_C = \#I$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · degIndexWith_eq_card_zeroSet⟧; the extended face $f_i$ is the hyperplane $\{\lambda_i = 0\}$, closed ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coordHyper⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · isClosed_coordHyper⟧; $I(z) \subseteq I(e)$ for $z$ near $e$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · eventually_zeroSet_subset⟧. *A connected piece of $\{d_C = 1\}$ lies in one face* (exposition Lemma 4.A): if $S \subseteq C$ is preconnected with $d_C = 1$ on $S$ and $\lambda_i(p) = 0$ at some $p \in S$, then $S \subseteq f_i$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · subset_coordHyper_of_isPreconnected⟧. Points of $S$ have $I = \{i\}$ or $\lambda_i > 0$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · zeroSet_eq_singleton⟧, so $S$ is covered by the open sets $u = \{\lambda_l > 0 \text{ for } l \ne i\}$ and $v = \{\lambda_i > 0\}$, which are disjoint on $S$ (a point in both would have $d_C = 0$); preconnectedness puts $S$ in one of them ⟦Mathlib/Topology/Connected/Clopen · isPreconnected_iff_subset_of_disjoint⟧, and $p \in u$.

*Rays stay in their face* (exposition Lemma 4.B). If $f$ is sc¹, $x + tv \in U_1$ for small $t \ge 0$ and a functional $L$ vanishes on $f(x + tv)$ for $t \in [0, \varepsilon)$, then $L(Df(x)v) = 0$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · IsSc1With.apply_deriv_eq_zero_of_ray⟧. Now let $r$ be tame, $x \in O_1$ smooth, $i \in I(x)$, $\lambda_i(y) = 0$ and $\lambda_l(y) > 0$ for the other $l \in I(x)$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ray_zeroSet⟧. For small $\tau > 0$, $x + \tau y \in U$ and $I(x + \tau y) = \{i\}$, so $d_C(r(x + \tau y)) = 1$ by tameness (1), and $I(r(x + \tau y)) \subseteq I(x)$ by continuity of $r$ at $x = r(x)$. The image of $(0, \tau_0]$ under $\tau \mapsto r(x + \tau y)$ is preconnected with $d_C = 1$, so it lies in one $f_j$ with $j \in I(x)$. Differentiating $\lambda_j(r(x + \tau y)) = 0$ at $\tau = 0$ gives $\lambda_j(Dr(x)y) = 0$, and $\lambda_j(Dr(x)y) = \lambda_j(y)$ by Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35) ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coordL⟧; as $\lambda_l(y) > 0$ for $l \in I(x) \setminus \{i\}$, $j = i$. This is the step of Lemma 2.5.12 (preprint 2.40) that the text omits, and it needs tameness (2).

*The local structure of a face* (exposition Lemma 4.C) ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · local_face_structure⟧. Let $S = \{z \in O : d_C(z) = 1\}$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.faceStratum⟧ and $e \in O$ with $\lambda_i(e) = 0$. (a) Choose $\varepsilon$ so that $B = B_\varepsilon(e) \cap C \subseteq U$ and $I(z), I(r(z)) \subseteq I(e)$ on $B$. (b) $A_i \cap B = \{z \in B : I(z) = \{i\}\}$ is convex ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · convex_ball_inter_zeroSet_eq⟧, hence connected, and $r$ maps it into $S$; a smooth $u = r(T^{-1}(a, w')) \in O \cap B$ with $I(u) = I(e)$ and the ray of Lemma 4.B from $u$ in the direction $T^{-1}(b, 0)$, $b = 1$ on $I(e) \setminus \{i\}$ and $0$ elsewhere ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · coordVec⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · rayDir⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · exists_lvl1_coordVec⟧, produces a point $p \in S$ with $\lambda_i(p) = 0$ in $r(A_i \cap B)$; so $r(A_i \cap B)$ lies in the component of $S$ through $p$. (c) A point $e' \in f_i \cap B$ is the limit of points of $A_i \cap B$ (perturb the coordinates of $I(e') \setminus \{i\}$ upward), so $r(e')$ lies in the closure of that component.

**Lemma 2.5.12 (preprint 2.40).** A *face of the retract* is $\overline{\hat F} \cap O$ for a component $\hat F$ of $S$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · ScRetraction.IsRetractFace⟧. A component of $S$ through a point with $\lambda_i = 0$ lies in $f_i$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · faceStratum_degIndexWith⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · connectedComponentIn_faceStratum_subset⟧, and a component of $S$ in $f_i$ whose closure contains $e$ is the component of Lemma 4.C at $e$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · connectedComponentIn_eq_of_mem_closure⟧. *The face through $x \in S$, $\lambda_i(x) = 0$, is the component of $f_i \cap O$ through $x$* ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · closure_connectedComponentIn_faceStratum⟧: it is connected, lies in $f_i \cap O$, is closed in it, and is relatively open in it by Lemma 4.C(c); a preconnected subset meeting a relatively clopen set lies in it ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · subset_of_relClopen_of_isPreconnected⟧. Conversely, the component of $f_i \cap O$ through any $e \in O$ with $\lambda_i(e) = 0$ is the face through the point $p$ of Lemma 4.C at $e$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · connectedComponentIn_coordHyper_eq⟧. Together: the faces of the retract are the components of the sets $f_i \cap O$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · lemma_2_5_12⟧. If the components of $f_i \cap O$ and $f_j \cap O$ through $x$ coincide, a point $z$ of the face in $S$ has $I(z) = \{i\}$ and is a limit of points with $I = \{j\}$, which near $z$ forces $j = i$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · lemma_2_5_12_injective⟧. The faces of the M-polyfold $O$ (Definition 2.5.10 (preprint 2.39), with $d_O = d_C$ by Proposition 2.5.6 (preprint 2.36)) are exactly the faces of the retract, transferred along the subtype inclusion ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · image_val_connectedComponentIn⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · image_val_closure⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · LocalModel.isFace_toMPolyfold_iff⟧.

**Corollary 2.5.13 (preprint 2.41).** The map $i \mapsto$ (component of $f_i \cap O$ through $x$) sends $I(x)$ onto the faces through $x$ (Lemma 2.5.12 (preprint 2.40)) and is injective (its second statement), so $x$ lies in exactly $\#I(x) = d_C(x)$ faces of the retract ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · corollary_2_5_13_retract⟧, and the M-polyfold $O$ is face-structured ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · LocalModel.isFaceStructured_toMPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · corollary_2_5_13⟧.

**Proposition 2.5.14 (preprint 2.42).** Let $X$ be tame. *The global bound* ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · MPolyfold.faces_encard_le⟧: in a tame chart $\varphi$ around $x$, $o = \varphi(x)$, Lemma 4.C gives for each $i \in I(o)$ a component $\hat F_i$ of $S$ containing all points of $O$ near $o$ with $I = \{i\}$. A face $F = \overline G$ through $x$ has points $y \in G$ near $x$; $d_C(\varphi(y)) = d_X(y) = 1$ (the tame chart realizes $d_X$) and $I(\varphi y) \subseteq I(o)$, so $I(\varphi y) = \{i\}$ for some $i \in I(o)$, and the preconnected set $\varphi^{-1}(\hat F_i) \subseteq \{d_X = 1\}$ meets $G$, hence lies in $G$. Distinct faces give distinct $i$; so at most $d_X(x)$ faces pass through $x$. *The local statement*: the tame chart realizes $d_X$ on its domain, the M-polyfold $O$ has $d_O = d_C$ (Proposition 2.5.6 (preprint 2.36)), and $O$ is face-structured (Corollary 2.5.13 (preprint 2.41)) ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · proposition_2_5_14⟧. The neighbourhood $V$ of the text is represented by $O$.

### II.16 Faces are tame sub-M-polyfolds: Propositions 2.5.15, 2.5.16 (preprint 2.43, 2.44) and Theorem 2.5.17 (preprint 2.45)

*The projection onto a face.* $P_i := T^{-1} \circ (a \mapsto a \text{ with } a_i = 0) \circ T$ is an sc-operator ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · killCoordL⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · killCoordModel⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · killCoord⟧ which kills the $i$-th coordinate and keeps the others ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · killCoord_coord⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · killCoord_coord_self⟧, fixes $f_i$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · killCoord_eq_self⟧ and maps $C$ into $C$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · killCoord_mem⟧.

**Proposition 2.5.15 (preprint 2.43), the retraction.** Let $F$ be a face of the retract, through $x \in S$ with $I(x) = \{i\}$, so $F \subseteq f_i$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · proposition_2_5_15⟧. For each $e \in F$, Lemma 4.C gives $\varepsilon_e$ with $B_e = B_{\varepsilon_e}(e) \cap C \subseteq U$ and $r(z) \in F$ for $z \in B_e \cap f_i$ (the component of Lemma 4.C at $e$ is the one of $F$). Put $U^* := \bigcup_{e \in F} (B_{\varepsilon_e}(e) \cap P_i^{-1}(B_{\varepsilon_e}(e))) \cap C$: relatively open in $C$, contains $F$ (as $P_i e = e$), and for $z \in U^*$ the point $P_i z$ lies in some $B_e \cap f_i$, so $r(P_i z) \in F$. Then $s := r \circ P_i$ is sc-smooth on $U^*$ (chain rule), maps $U^*$ into $F \subseteq U^*$, and fixes $F$; so it is a retraction onto $F$, and $U^* \subseteq U$. The preimages under $P_i$ are needed because $P_i$ need not be norm-decreasing for the norm of $E_0$; the exposition's "$|P_1 z - e|_0 \le |z - e|_0$" holds only for special norms. *$F$ is a sub-M-polyfold of $O$*: in the chart $\mathrm{id}$ of $O$, $s$ restricted to $O \cap U^*$ is an sc-smooth retraction onto $F$ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · LocalModel.selfChart_symm_apply⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameRetracts · LocalModel.isSubMPolyfold_of_isFace⟧.

*The face as a model space.* Insert and delete a coordinate: $\mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^{k+1}$, $b \mapsto (b_1, \dots, 0_i, \dots, b_k)$, and back ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · insertCoordL⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · removeCoordL⟧, as sc-operators on $\mathbb R^k \oplus W$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · insertCoordModel⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · removeCoordModel⟧; composed with $T$ they give $\iota : \mathbb R^k \oplus W \to E$ onto $f_i$ and $\pi : E \to \mathbb R^k \oplus W$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · faceIncl⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · faceProj⟧, with $\pi\iota = 1$, $\iota\pi = 1$ on $f_i$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · faceProj_faceIncl⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · faceIncl_faceProj⟧, $\iota(C') \subseteq C$ and $\pi(C) \subseteq C'$ for $C' = [0, \infty)^k \oplus W$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · faceIncl_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · faceProj_mem⟧, and $d_C(y) = d_{C'}(\pi y) + 1$ on $f_i$ ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · degIndexWith_eq_quadrantDeg_faceProj_add_one⟧. The derivative of an sc-operator is itself ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · ScOperator.scDeriv_eq⟧, and the chain rule at a point holds between arbitrary sc-domains ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · scDeriv_comp_apply_of_isScDomain⟧.

**Proposition 2.5.15 (preprint 2.43), the tame model** ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · proposition_2_5_15_tameModel⟧. With $U^*$ and $s$ as above, put $U' := \iota^{-1}(U^*)$ (relatively open in $C'$) and $r' := \pi \circ r \circ \iota$ on $U'$. Since $r \circ \iota$ maps $U'$ into $F \subseteq f_i$, where $\iota\pi = 1$, $r'$ is an sc-smooth retraction with retract $\pi(F)$, and $\iota$ maps it back into $F$. *Tameness (1)*: for $z \in U'$, $d_{C'}(r'z) + 1 = d_C(r(\iota z)) = d_C(\iota z) = d_{C'}(z) + 1$. *Tameness (2)*: at a smooth $x \in \pi(F)$, $\iota x$ is a smooth point of $O$ and $Dr'(x)v = \pi(Dr(\iota x)(\iota v))$ by the chain rule; for $j$ with $x_j = 0$ the coordinate $j' = i.\mathrm{succAbove}(j)$ vanishes at $\iota x$, and Proposition 2.5.3 (preprint 2.35) for $r$ gives $\lambda_{j'}(Dr(\iota x)\iota v) = \lambda_{j'}(\iota v) = v_j$; so $\lambda'_j \circ Dr'(x) = \lambda'_j$, and $(1 - Dr'(x))E'$ is an sc-complement of $T_x\pi(F)$ inside $E'_x$. The exposition instead intersects the complement $A$ of $T_xO$ with $f_1$; that is not needed. And $d_{C'}(\pi y) + 1 = d_C(y)$ on $F$.

**Proposition 2.5.15 (preprint 2.43), faces are tame** ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · LocalModel.proposition_2_5_15_isTame⟧.
