Each $k_i$ is $\Phi(e_i)_2$ for a smooth point $e_i$ of the fibre over $y$ ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · mem_smoothSet_toMPolyfold0_of_chart⟧; Lemma 5.3.3 (preprint 5.11) gives $s_i$ with $s_i(y) = e_i$, support in $U$ and $N(s_i) < N(e_i) + 1$, and $s_i/(N(e_i) + 1)$ is allowable, with support unchanged ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · sectionSupport_sectionSmul_const_subset⟧, $N$ scaled ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · StrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.oneMk_sectionSmul_const⟧ and principal part scaled ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · principal_sectionSmul_const⟧. The density of the smooth vectors is the point the text omits: Lemma 5.3.3 (preprint 5.11) only reaches smooth points of the fibre.

### V.13 Theorem 5.3.5 (preprint 5.13): openness, and the omitted compactness step

**No boundary on $\mathbb R^m \times X$.** "The interior case, Theorem 3.19" is applied to $F$ on $\mathbb R^m \times X$, so $\partial(\mathbb R^m \times X) = \emptyset$ is needed: $d_{\mathbb R^m} \equiv 0$ ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · rnPolyfold_degIndex⟧ and $d_{\mathbb R^m \times X} \le d_{\mathbb R^m} + d_X$ ⟦Chapter2/FibredProduct · MPolyfold.degIndex_prod_le⟧ ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · isWithoutBoundary_prod_rn⟧. At a point with $d = 0$ good position is surjectivity ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexG · StrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_isLinSurjAt⟧.

**Transversality spreads.** If $g$ has tame germ data and $F$ is transversal at $(0, x)$, $x$ a zero of $g$, then $(F, (0, x))$ is in good position, and Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54) gives an open $V \ni (0, x)$ all of whose zeros are in good position, hence transversal; $U(x) = \{y \mid (0, y) \in V\}$ is the text's neighbourhood ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoG · theorem_3_6_8_one'⟧ ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · exists_isOpen_isLinSurjAt_zero_near⟧. Likewise, if $F$ is transversal at every $(0, y)$, $y \in S_g$, the union of these sets is an open $V \supseteq \{0\} \times S_g$ all of whose zeros of $F$ are in good position in a tame chart ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · exists_isOpen_goodPosition_of_isLinSurjAt⟧.

**The omitted step.** The text passes from the neighbourhood $U$ of $\{0\} \times S_{f+s_0}$ to "$U \subset \{|\lambda| < \delta_0\} \oplus X$" without argument; what is needed is that *every* zero of $F$ with $|\lambda|$ small lies in $V$. The topological core: if $Z \subseteq \mathbb R^m \times X$ is compact and the open $V$ contains $Z \cap \{\lambda = 0\}$, then $Z \setminus V$ is compact, its projection to $\mathbb R^m$ is compact and misses $0$, and any $\delta$ below its distance to $0$ works ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · exists_pos_forall_mem_of_isCompact⟧. The compact $Z$ is the set of zeros of $F$ with $|\lambda| \le \delta_1$: for such $\lambda$ the perturbation $s_0 + \sum\lambda_it_i$ is allowable (§V.11), so by Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12) its zeros lie in the compact $\operatorname{cl}\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le 1\}$ of Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5) — $Z$ is a closed subset of $\bar B(\delta_1) \times$ (that compact set), closed because $F$ is continuous.

### V.14 Theorem 5.3.5 (preprint 5.13): the Sard step

"$\tilde S := F^{-1}(0)$ is a smooth manifold"; "taking a regular value $\lambda_0$ for the projection $\tilde S \to \mathbb R^m$, it is easily verified that $f + s_0 + s(\lambda_0, \cdot)$ is transversal". The formalization does not build $\tilde S$; it proves the needed statement near each zero ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · exists_null_isLinSurjAt_paramSlice_near⟧.

*Claim.* Let $g$ have tame germ data, $t_i$ be sc⁺, and $z_0$ a zero of $F$ in good position in a tame chart. There are an open $W \ni z_0$ and a null set $CV \subseteq \mathbb R^m$ such that for every zero $(\lambda, y) \in W$ with $\lambda \notin CV$ the slice $g_\lambda$ is transversal at $y$.

1. *The chart of $\tilde S$.* Theorem 3.6.8 (2) (preprint 3.54) gives at $z_0$ a regular tangent germ chart $D$ of the solution set of $F$ (Definition 3.2.1 (2) (preprint 3.25)): a chart $D.\varphi$ of $\mathbb R^m \times X$ with domain $W$, a finite-dimensional $N$, a relatively open $V \subseteq N \cap C$ and an sc-smooth graph map $\Gamma$ with $D.\varphi^{-1} \circ \Gamma$ parametrizing $\tilde S \cap W$ ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTTheoremsG · theorem_3_6_8_two⟧.
2. *The projection.* $q = p \circ D.\varphi^{-1} \circ \Gamma : V \to \mathbb R^m$, $p$ the projection to the parameter, is sc-smooth on a finite-dimensional space with the constant structure, hence $C^\infty$ ⟦Chapter1/ExpositionLemmas · isScSmooth_iff_contDiffOn_const⟧.
3. *Sard on the strata.* $V$ is relatively open in a partial quadrant of $N$; Sard's theorem on each stratum of the quadrant (Part IV) makes the set $CV$ of stratified critical values of $q$ null ⟦Chapter4/FamiliesLocal · measure_image_stratCritSet⟧. Since $\partial X = \emptyset$ the points over the zeros are interior and classical Sard would do, but proving that needs the degeneracy index of the induced structure; the stratified form makes the question unnecessary.
4. *The point.* A zero $(\lambda, y) \in W$ is $D.\varphi^{-1}(\Gamma(v))$ for some $v \in V$ with $q(v) = \lambda$. Let $\Phi$ be a chart centred at $y$ and $\psi = (r \mapsto r - \lambda) \times \varphi$ the product chart. On a relatively open $V' \subseteq V$ around $v$, $\mathrm{gmap} = \psi \circ D.\varphi^{-1} \circ \Gamma$ is sc-smooth (the transition between the two charts of $\mathbb R^m \times X$ restricted to the overlap), and $q = \mathrm{pr}_1 \circ \mathrm{gmap} + \lambda$ there.
5. *Kernel vectors.* If $\lambda \notin CV$, $Dq(v)$ maps the stratum through $v$ onto $\mathbb R^m$. The values of $D\,\mathrm{gmap}(v)$ lie in the tangent space $T_0O$ of the product chart, and in $\ker\mathrm{Lin}_F(0)$: the principal part of $F$ vanishes along $r \circ \mathrm{gmap}$, and the chain rule gives $\mathrm{Lin}_F(0) \circ D\,\mathrm{gmap}(v) = 0$. So for every $a \in \mathbb R^m$ there is a kernel vector with first component $a$.
6. *Conclusion.* $F$ is transversal at $(\lambda, y)$ (good position near $z_0$), and §V.11 gives the transversality of the slice at $y$.

Only $\operatorname{range}D\,\mathrm{gmap}(v) \subseteq \ker\mathrm{Lin}_F$ is used, not "$T\tilde S = \ker F'$".

### V.15 Theorem 5.3.5 (preprint 5.13): the assembly

**The generic form** ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · theorem_5_3_5_generic⟧. Let $\partial X = \emptyset$, $X$ admit bump functions, $f$ have tame germ data and compact solution set, $N$ be an auxiliary norm.

1. *$U$ and part (1).* Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5) gives $U \supseteq S_f$ with $\operatorname{cl}\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le 1\}$ compact ⟦Chapter5/Compactness · theorem_5_2_2_preprint⟧; for allowable $s$, Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12) and closedness give $S_{f+s}$ compact (§V.10).
2. *The section $g = f + s_0$.* For $s_0$ sc⁺ with $\operatorname{supp}s_0 \subseteq U$ and $N(s_0) \le 1 - \varepsilon$, $g$ has tame germ data ⟦Chapter3/TameGermsAddG · theorem_3_1_18_tame⟧, a compact solution set (part (1)), and $S_g \subseteq U$ (Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12)).
3. *Local families.* At every zero $x$ of $g$, spanning sections $s^x_1, \dots, s^x_{k_x}$ supported in $U$ (§V.12) make $F_x$ transversal at $(0, x)$, and at $(0, y)$ for the zeros $y$ in an open $U(x)$ (§V.13).
4. *One family.* Finitely many $U(x_j)$ cover the compact $S_g$; the families are united through an equivalence $\Sigma_j\mathrm{Fin}(k_{x_j}) \simeq \mathrm{Fin}(m)$ into $t_1, \dots, t_m$, allowable and supported in $U$; adding sections keeps transversality (§V.11), so $F$, whose slice at $\lambda = 0$ is $g$ ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · paramSlice_zero⟧, is transversal at every $(0, y)$, $y \in S_g$.
5. *Good position near the zero slice.* An open $V \supseteq \{0\} \times S_g$ of zeros of $F$ in good position (§V.13).
6. *Allowability and compactness.* For $|\lambda| \le \delta_1 = \varepsilon/(m + 1)$ the slices $s_0 + \sum\lambda_it_i$ are allowable, and the zeros of $F$ over $|\lambda| \le \delta_1$ form a compact $Z$ (§V.13).
7. *The omitted step.* $Z \cap \{|\lambda| < \delta_0\} \subseteq V$ for some $\delta_0 > 0$.
8. *Sard.* With $\delta = \min(\delta_0, \delta_1)$, the zeros $Z_0$ of $F$ over $|\lambda| \le \delta/2$ are compact and lie in $V$; the Sard step (§V.14) at each point of $Z_0$ gives an open $W_z$ and a null $CV_z$; finitely many $W_z$ cover $Z_0$, and $CV = \bigcup CV_z$ is null.
9. *The conclusions.* For $|\lambda| < \delta/2$, $\lambda \notin CV$: $s_\lambda = s_0 + \sum\lambda_it_i$ is allowable; every zero $y$ of $f + s_\lambda$ gives a zero $(\lambda, y) \in Z_0$, inside some $W_z$, so $f + s_\lambda$ is transversal at $y$; $S_{f+s_\lambda}$ is compact by part (1); and if it is non-empty, Theorem 3.6.10 (preprint 3.56) for a transversal section over $X$ without boundary, applied to $f + s_\lambda$ with tame germ data, makes it a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame, a manifold without boundary of locally constant dimension, with regular tangent germ data of dimension the Fredholm index at every zero ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexG · theorem_3_6_10_of_surjective⟧ ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · StrongBundle.SolutionSetIsManifold⟧.

**The dense form** ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · theorem_5_3_5_preprint⟧. Given an allowable $s'$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, let $\varepsilon' = \min(\varepsilon, 1)$ and $s_0 = (1 - \varepsilon'/2)s'$, so $N(s_0) \le 1 - \varepsilon'/2$. The generic form gives $t$, $\delta$, $CV$; since $CV$ is null and the ball $\{|\lambda| < \min(\delta, \varepsilon'/(2m + 2))\}$ has positive measure, some $\lambda$ in it avoids $CV$. Then $s = s_0 + \sum\lambda_it_i$ has $N(s(x) - s'(x)) \le (\varepsilon'/2)N(s'(x)) + \sum|\lambda_i|N(t_i(x)) \le \varepsilon'$. The text's "$N(s_0(y) + s(\lambda_0, y)) \le 1 - \varepsilon/2$" is presumably meant as $\le 1$, its "$N(f(x)) \le 1$" in the statement is $N(s(x)) \le 1$, and its "the germ $(f, x)$ is in good position" is $(f + s, x)$.

### V.16 Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17) and Lemma 5.26 (preprint)

**Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17), in a tame chart** ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · StrongBundle.IsGeneralPositionGerm⟧. $(f, y)$, $f(y) = 0$, is in general position if in some tame strong bundle chart around $y$ (Definition 3.6.3 (preprint 3.50)) ⟦Chapter3/TameGerms · StrongBundle.IsTameChart⟧, at the level-$1$ point $z$ over $\varphi(y)$, $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is onto $K_z$, and for every presentation $T$ of the partial quadrant the kernel has an sc-complement $B$ in $T_zO$ inside the reduced tangent space $T^R_zO = T_zO \cap E_z$ ⟦Chapter2/Tame · reducedTangentSpaceWith⟧, on every level: $(T_zO)_m = (\ker\mathrm{Lin}(z))_m \oplus B_m$. The chart is tame because $T^R_xX$ is the reduced tangent space of a tame M-polyfold and the dimension count below needs it. General position includes transversality ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · StrongBundle.IsGeneralPositionGerm.isLinSurjAt⟧.

**The linear algebra of Lemma 5.26 (preprint)** ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · isInGoodPositionIn_of_scComplement_le_reduced⟧. Let $r$ be a tame retraction, $z$ a smooth point of the retract, and $N, B \subseteq T_zO$ with $T_zO = N \oplus B$ and $B \subseteq T^R_zO$. Then $N$ is in good position to the cone $C_z$ inside $T_zO$ (Definition 3.1.24 (preprint 3.21)): $B$ is a good complement, because adding a vector of $E_z$ does not change membership in $C_z$ (the coordinates $\lambda_i$, $i \in I(z)$, vanish on $E_z$); and $N \cap C_z$ has non-empty interior in $N$, because the coordinates $\lambda_i$, $i \in I(z)$, map $T_zO$ onto $\mathbb R^{I(z)}$ — $\dim T_zO/T^R_zO = d_C(z)$ in a tame retract (Proposition 2.5.6 (preprint 2.36)) — and vanish on $B$, so they map $N$ onto $\mathbb R^{I(z)}$, and a vector of $N$ with all these coordinates equal to $1$ is interior. The text omits the interior condition; this is the argument of Part IV for tangent spaces ⟦Chapter4/LocalStructure · IsGeneralPositionRetractAt.isGoodPositionRetractAt⟧, for a subspace not given as one.

**Lemma 5.26 (preprint)** ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · StrongBundle.IsGeneralPositionGerm.isGoodPositionGerm⟧. For $f$ sc-Fredholm and $(f, y)$ in general position: in the chart of Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17) $\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ is onto and its kernel is in good position by the linear algebra; Definition 3.6.6 (preprint 3.53) then follows ⟦Chapter3/LinearizationChartsG · StrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_linAt_surj⟧. For $f$ with tame germ data, good position holds in the tame chart of the germ data ⟦Chapter3/TameGermsAddG · StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGerm.toTame⟧ ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · StrongBundle.IsGeneralPositionGerm.isGoodPositionGermTame⟧ — the form the §3.6 theorems take. $X$ itself need not be tame. (The text places the lemma after Theorem 5.25 (preprint) and calls it "clear" after Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18); it is used in Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) and Theorem 5.25 (preprint) here.)

### V.17 The bridge lemma, and $T_yS = \ker f'(y)$

Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) applies Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23) to the parametrized solution set $\tilde S$, which needs $\tilde S$ to be a smooth submanifold in the sense of Definition 4.2.1 (preprint 4.13) — locally the image of an sc⁺-retraction. The implicit function theorem gives tangent germ data (Definition 3.2.1 (preprint 3.25)), and the text never connects the two.

**sc⁺ on a finite-dimensional domain** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · isScPlus_of_isScSmooth_const⟧. On a finite-dimensional space with the constant structure all levels of the domain coincide, so an sc-smooth $f$ is $C^\infty$ into every $F_m$, and its lift into $F^1$ is sc-smooth: $f$ is sc⁺.

**The bridge lemma.** Let $D$ be regular tangent germ data for $M$ at $x$ (Definition 3.2.1 (2) (preprint 3.25)), with graph map $\Gamma : V \to E$ over the finite-dimensional $N$, projection $\pi$ onto $N$, and $r$ a retraction onto the chart model. Then $\Gamma$ is sc⁺ on $V$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · MPolyfold.TangentGermChart.Γ_isScPlus⟧, so $\tau = \Gamma \circ \pi \circ r$, on the set of points whose image under $\pi \circ r$ lies in $V$, is an sc-smooth retraction (as in the proof of Theorem 3.2.3 (preprint 3.27)) ⟦Chapter3/TangentGerm · theorem_3_2_3_of_isRegular⟧ which is sc⁺ (sc⁺ ∘ sc-smooth), with $\tau \circ \Gamma = \Gamma$ on $V$ and retract the chart image of $M$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · MPolyfold.TangentGermChart.exists_scPlusRetraction⟧. Transported to $X$ it is an sc⁺-retraction on an open set with image $M \cap V$ ⟦Chapter4/LocalStructure · MPolyfold.isScPlusRetractionOn_of_chart⟧ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · MPolyfold.TangentGermChart.exists_isScPlusRetractionOn⟧. Hence a set with regular tangent germ data at each point is a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · MPolyfold.isSmoothSubmanifold_of_isRegular⟧. For solution sets: if all zeros of $f$ in an open $W$ are in good position in a tame chart, Theorem 3.6.8 (2) (preprint 3.54) gives regular data at each, on charts inside $W$, and $S_f \cap W$ is a smooth submanifold ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · StrongBundle.isSmoothSubmanifold_solutionSet_inter⟧.

**$T_yS \subseteq \ker f'(y)$** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · tangentSpace_subset_linKer⟧. In a chart, let $Q \subseteq O$ be a retract on which the principal part $\hat f$ vanishes, $S$ a retraction onto $Q$, $z$ a level-$1$ point of $Q$. Then $T_zQ = \operatorname{range}DS(z) \subseteq T_zO$, and $\hat f \circ r \circ S = 0$ gives $D(\hat f \circ r)(z) \circ DS(z) = 0$ by the chain rule, i.e. $T_zQ \subseteq \ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · StrongBundleChart.mem_linKer_iff⟧.

**Equality, by counting** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · exists_tangentSpace_eq_linKer⟧. Let $f$ have tame germ data and $(f, x_0)$ be a zero in good position in a tame chart. The index form of Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) gives an open $V \ni x_0$ whose zeros are in good position, and regular data $D$ of a fixed dimension $d$ at each zero, with $\dim\ker\mathrm{Lin}(z) = d$ in *every* chart ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexG · theorem_3_6_8_index⟧ ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndex · StrongBundle.IsSurjLinOfIndex⟧. On the other side, the tangent space of the bridge retraction $\tau$ at the point over $\Gamma(v)$ contains the $d$ vectors $D\Gamma(v)b_i$, $b_i$ a basis of $N$: $D\tau \circ D\Gamma(v) = D(\tau \circ \Gamma)(v) = D\Gamma(v)$, and $\pi \circ D\Gamma(v) = 1$ makes them independent ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · MPolyfold.TangentGermChart.exists_linearIndependent_tangentSpace⟧. "Having $d$ independent tangent vectors" ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · HasIndepTangent⟧ is carried by germs of sc-diffeomorphisms, since $D(F \circ r)(z)$ maps $T_zQ$ into $T_{F(z)}Q'$ and is injective on $T_zO$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · HasIndepTangent.transport⟧, so it passes from the chart of $D$ to any chart $\Phi$ through the transition maps ⟦Chapter4/Submanifolds · MPolyfold.chart_change_of_transport⟧. A $d$-dimensional subspace of the $d$-dimensional $\ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ — tangent spaces of retracts are germs, so the retract $\varphi(G \cap S_f \cap V)$ of any small open $G$ has the same tangent space — is all of it.

### V.18 General position: chart independence and openness

**Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17) is Definition 4.2.10 (preprint 4.21)** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · exists_isGeneralPositionGerm_iff⟧. Near a zero $x_0$ in good position (with $f$ of tame germ data) there is an open $V$ such that every zero in $V$ is in good position, $S = S_f \cap V$ is a smooth submanifold (§V.17), and at every zero $y \in V$: $(f, y)$ is in general position iff $S$ is in general position at $y$ (Definition 4.2.10 (preprint 4.21), Part IV). Since $T_zS = \ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ in every chart, an sc-complement of $\ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ inside $T^R_zO$ *is* an sc-complement of $T_zS$ inside $T^R_zO$. Definition 4.2.10 (preprint 4.21) is chart independent (Part IV) ⟦Chapter4/Submanifolds · MPolyfold.IsGeneralPositionAt.isGeneralPositionChart⟧, so Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17) is too, at these zeros.

**From submanifold general position to good position** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · isGoodPositionGermTame_of_isGeneralPositionAt⟧. If $f'(y)$ is onto and a smooth submanifold $A \subseteq S_f$ is in general position at $y$, then in the tame chart of the germ data $T_zA \subseteq \ker\mathrm{Lin}(z)$ (§V.17) ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · StrongBundleChart.linKer_le⟧ and $T_zA + T^R_zO = T_zO$; so $\ker\mathrm{Lin}(z) + T^R_zO = T_zO$, the kernel has an algebraic complement inside $T^R_zO$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · exists_compl_le_of_sup_eq⟧, and §V.16 gives good position.

**Openness** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · exists_isOpen_isGeneralPositionGerm⟧. Let $X$ be tame, $f$ with tame germ data, $(f, x_0)$ in general position. By Lemma 5.26 (preprint) it is in good position; the previous paragraph turns its general position into general position of the submanifold $S_f \cap V$ at $x_0$; Theorem 4.2.11 (3) (preprint 4.22) for tame $X$ (Part IV) makes that open along the submanifold ⟦Chapter4/LocalStructure · MPolyfold.theorem_4_2_11_preprint⟧; Definition 4.2.10 (preprint 4.21) depends only on the germ of the submanifold, since tangent spaces of chart models agree on open sets ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · MPolyfold.IsGeneralPositionAt.congr_nhds⟧; and the equivalence turns it back into general position of $(f, y)$ at the nearby zeros. The text uses this without proof ("they will also hold at $(0, y)$ for $y \in S_f$ close to $x$"; "the properties (i)–(ii) hold for all $(\lambda, y) \in \tilde S$").

### V.19 Properties (i)–(ii)

In a chart centred at $y$, with a presentation $T$, the properties of the proof of Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) are ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · StrongBundleChart.IsParamGP⟧: (i) $\mathrm{Lin}_g(0)(T_0O) + \operatorname{span}\{\hat t_i(0)\} = K_0$ — $F'(0, y)$ onto; (ii) every $w \in T_0O$ is $u + e$ with $e \in E_0$ and $\mathrm{Lin}_g(0)u + \sum a_i\hat t_i(0) = 0$ for some $a$ — $\ker F'(0, y)$ transversal to $\mathbb R^m \oplus T^R$. Adding sections keeps both, by linear algebra ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · StrongBundleChart.IsParamGP.comp⟧.

**(i)–(ii) give general position** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · isGeneralPositionGerm_paramSection_of_isParamGP⟧. In the tame product chart $(r \mapsto r) \times \Phi$ of a tame chart centred at $y$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · pc0⟧, whose tangent space at the centre is $\mathbb R^m \times T_0O$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · ofProd_mem_rangeS⟧ and whose reduced tangent space is $\mathbb R^m \times T^R_0O$, the minimal subspace of $\mathbb R^m$ being everything ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · minimalSubspaceWith_rnPres⟧: (i) is the surjectivity of $F'(0, y)$; (ii) says $\ker F'(0, y) + T^R = T(\mathbb R^m \times O)$ on level $0$, so the kernel has an algebraic complement inside $T^R$, and §V.16 gives good position of $(F, (0, y))$. *Then* $\ker F'(0, y) = T_{(0, y)}\tilde S$ (§V.17), which is finite-dimensional and smooth; a finite-dimensional smooth subspace has an sc-complement inside any sc-subspace it complements algebraically ⟦Chapter4/LocalStructure · exists_scComplement_le⟧, which gives Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17) for $F$. The text's "at this point the combined system of sections already satisfies (i) and (ii)" compresses these two steps.

**General position gives (i)–(ii)** in every tame chart centred at $y$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · isParamGP_of_isGeneralPositionGerm⟧: (i) is surjectivity read in the product chart; for (ii), $\tilde S$ is in general position at $(0, y)$ (§V.18), and in the product chart its tangent space is $\ker F'(0, y)$, which therefore has a complement inside $\mathbb R^m \times T^R$.

**Achieving (i)–(ii)** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · exists_sections_isParamGP⟧. Spanning sections give (i) (§V.12) ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · spanning_of_isLinSurjAt⟧. For (ii), "take a linear subspace $L$ complementing $T^R_xX$ in $T_xX$ and add sections which at $x$ span $f'(x)L$": the sections must come from Lemma 5.3.3 (preprint 5.11), which needs *smooth* points of the fibre, so $L$ must consist of smooth vectors. The coordinates $\lambda_{I(0)}$ map $T_0O$ onto $\mathbb R^{I(0)}$ with kernel $T^R_0O$ (Proposition 2.5.6 (preprint 2.36)), and already map the dense smooth vectors of $T_0O$ onto it (a dense subspace of a finite-dimensional image is all of it); so there are smooth $l_i \in T_0O$ with $\lambda(l_i) = e_i$. $\mathrm{Lin}_g(0)l_i$ is smooth ($\mathrm{Lin}$ is an sc-operator at the smooth point), Lemma 5.3.3 (preprint 5.11) gives allowable sections through $\Phi^{-1}(0, \mathrm{Lin}_g(0)l_i)$ supported in $U$, and with these added every $w \in T_0O$ is $u + e$: subtract $\sum\lambda_i(w)l_i$, whose image under $\mathrm{Lin}_g(0)$ is cancelled by the new sections.

### V.20 Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18)

**From a family** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · theorem_5_3_10_of_family⟧. Let $X$ be tame, $f$ with tame germ data and compact solution set, $N$ auxiliary, $U$ from Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5). Fix $s_0$ with $\operatorname{supp}s_0 \subseteq U$, $N(s_0) \le 1 - \varepsilon$, and allowable $t_1, \dots, t_m$ with $F$ in general position at every $(0, x)$, $x \in S_g$, $g = f + s_0$.

1. *General position near the zero slice.* $\mathbb R^m \times X$ is tame ⟦Chapter3/ParamPerturbation · prod_rn_isTame⟧ and $F$ has tame germ data ⟦Chapter3/ParamPerturbationG · theorem_3_1_21_tame⟧, so openness (§V.18) gives, around each $(0, x)$, an open set on which the zeros of $F$ are in good and general position; their union $W \supseteq \{0\} \times S_g$.
2. *Compactness and the omitted step* as in §V.13: the zeros $Z$ of $F$ over $|\lambda| \le \delta_1$ are compact, and $Z \cap \{|\lambda| < \delta_0\} \subseteq W$.
3. *The submanifold.* $A = \tilde S \cap W \cap \{|\lambda| < \delta\}$ is a smooth finite-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb R^m \times X$ (the bridge lemma, §V.17), in general position at each of its points (Definition 4.2.10 (preprint 4.21), by §V.18 and locality), with compact closure (inside $Z$).
4. *Theorem 4.3.1 (preprint 4.23).* In its countable-cover form (Part IV) ⟦Chapter4/Families · theorem_4_3_1_of_subset⟧, it gives a set $\Sigma$ of parameters with null complement over which the fibre $A_\lambda$ is a smooth submanifold of $X$ in general position.
5. *Transversality.* The Sard step of §V.14 on the compact zeros over $|\lambda| \le \delta/2$ gives a further null set off which the slices are transversal at their zeros.
6. *The conclusions for $\lambda$.* For $|\lambda| < \delta/2$ off both null sets, with $h = f + s_\lambda$: the fibre of $A$ over $\lambda$ is $S_h$; $h$ is transversal; $S_h$ is a submanifold in general position, so $(h, y)$ is in good position (§V.18), and then in general position by the equivalence of §V.18 applied at $y$ together with the locality of Definition 4.2.10 (preprint 4.21); Theorem 4.2.7 (preprint 4.18) gives the corner structure and tameness of $S_h$ ⟦Chapter4/Submanifolds · MPolyfold.theorem_4_2_7⟧, and Theorem 4.2.11 (2) (preprint 4.22) gives $d_{S_h} = d_X$ on $S_h$ ⟦Chapter4/LocalStructure · MPolyfold.theorem_4_2_11_preprint⟧. These are the conclusions collected in ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · StrongBundle.SolutionSetInGeneralPosition⟧.

**The generic form** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · theorem_5_3_10_param⟧. At every zero $x$ of $g$ choose a tame chart centred at $x$ with a presentation; sections with (i)–(ii) there (§V.19) make $F_x$ general at $(0, x)$, hence (openness, §V.18) at $(0, y)$ for the zeros $y$ in an open $U(x)$. Finitely many $U(x_j)$ cover $S_g$; the united family $t$ keeps (i)–(ii) at every $(0, y)$ — read (i)–(ii) off general position in the chart of $x_j$, add sections, go back — so $F$ is in general position at every $(0, y)$, and the previous theorem applies. "Replacing $f + s_0$ by $f$ and $N$ by $cN$" is not needed; the proof keeps $s_0$.

**The dense form** ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · theorem_5_3_10_dense⟧ is derived exactly as for Theorem 5.3.5 (preprint 5.13) (§V.15).

The text's $\tilde S$ omits the equation $F = 0$, and its "$p^{-1}(\{|\lambda| \le \varepsilon\})$ is compact" is the omitted step of §V.13.

### V.21 Theorem 5.25 (preprint)

⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · theorem_5_25_preprint⟧. Let $X$ be tame with bump functions, $f$ proper with tame germ data. Properness gives a compact solution set; Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) with $s_0 = 0$ gives $U$, $t$, $\delta$ and a null $CV$ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · StrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.fiberZero_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · sectionAdd_fiberZero⟧; the ball $\{|\lambda| < \delta\}$ has positive measure, so some $\lambda$ avoids $CV$, and $s = \sum\lambda_it_i$ is allowable with $f + s$ in general position at every zero and all the conclusions of Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18); Lemma 5.26 (preprint) turns general into good position in the tame chart of the germ data (§V.16). The text's proof says "in view of Theorem 3.54 ... in general position", which is the openness of §V.18 (Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) is about good position), and writes $x \in S_f$ for $x \in S_{f+s_0}$. Here $U$ is the neighbourhood Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) produces; the text lets the reader choose "an associated" one.

### V.22 Theorem 5.3.12 (preprint 5.19)

⟦Chapter5/GeneralPosition · theorem_5_3_12_param⟧. Let $X$ admit bump functions, $f$ have tame germ data and compact solution set, and $(f, x)$ be in good position at the zeros $x \in \partial X$. The text's "as before" applies the implicit function theorem to $F$ at the boundary zeros $(0, x)$, where all $t_i$ vanish and $\ker F'(0, x) = \mathbb R^m \times \ker f'(x)$; this is in good position to $\mathbb R^m \times C_x$ only if $\ker f'(x) + E_x \supseteq T_xX$, a general position condition that good position does not imply (Finding 88, below). The formal proof avoids those points:

1. *Near the boundary zeros.* Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54) at each zero of $f$ on $\partial X$ gives an open set of zeros in good position ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoG · theorem_3_6_8_one'⟧; their union $V_{bd}$, and an open $V_1$ with $S_f \cap \partial X \subseteq V_1$ and $\operatorname{cl}V_1 \subseteq V_{bd}$.
2. *Away from them.* The zeros of $f$ outside $V_1$ are not on $\partial X$, so interior ($d = 0$). Spanning sections at these zeros are taken with supports in $U \setminus (\partial X \cup \operatorname{cl}V_1)$, an open set containing them; finitely many families cover the compact $S_f \setminus V_1$, and $F$ is onto at every $(0, y)$, $y \in S_f$ outside $V_1$.
3. *Good position of $F$ off the boundary.* At the interior points good position is surjectivity ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTIndexG · StrongBundle.isGoodPositionGerm_of_isLinSurjAt⟧; Theorem 3.6.8 (1) (preprint 3.54) for $F$ gives an open $W \supseteq \{0\} \times (S_f \setminus V_1)$ of zeros in good position, off $\mathbb R^m \times \partial X$.
4. *Compactness and Sard* as in §V.15 for the zeros of $F$ over small $\lambda$ outside $\mathbb R^m \times V_1$.
5. *The conclusions.* For small $\lambda$ off the null set, $h = f + s_\lambda$. On $V_1$ all $t_i$ vanish, so $h = f$ there, and the good position of $(f, y)$ at the zeros in $V_1$ passes to $(h, y)$ because good position depends only on the germ of the section ⟦Chapter3/Chapter5BridgeG · StrongBundle.IsGoodPositionGermTame.congr_nhds⟧. Off $V_1$ the zeros of $h$ are interior, $h$ is transversal there by the Sard step, hence in good position. Theorem 3.6.11 (preprint 3.57) makes $S_h$, if non-empty, a sub-M-polyfold whose induced structure is tame and a manifold with boundary with corners ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTTheoremsG · theorem_3_6_11⟧.

$s_\lambda = \sum\lambda_it_i$ has support disjoint from $\partial X$, so it vanishes on the open neighbourhood $X \setminus \operatorname{supp}s_\lambda$ of $\partial X$, and it is "arbitrarily small" as $\lambda \to 0$. The text's tameness of $X$ is not used, and its "$(f, x)$ in good position for every $x \in S_{f+s}$" is $(f + s, x)$. The dense form is §V.34.

**Finding 88 in Lean** (gap G.46). The smallest instance ⟦Chapter3/Counterexamples2021 · Counterexamples2021.theorem_5_3_12_goodPosition_not_stable⟧: the line $\mathbb R(1, 1)$ is in good position to the corner $[0, \infty)^2$, with good complement $\mathbb R(1, -1)$ ⟦Chapter3/Counterexamples2021 · Counterexamples2021.isGoodComplement_diag_antidiag⟧ ⟦Chapter3/Counterexamples2021 · Counterexamples2021.isInGoodPosition_diag⟧, also with the sc-complement of the definition as written ⟦Chapter3/Counterexamples2021 · Counterexamples2021.isInGoodPositionSc_diag⟧; but $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R(1, 1)$ is not in good position to $\mathbb R \times [0, \infty)^2$, not even with an algebraic complement ⟦Chapter3/Counterexamples2021 · Counterexamples2021.not_isInGoodPosition_prod_diag⟧. A good complement $Y$ would have $(a, 0) + y \in \mathbb R \times [0, \infty)^2$ for $y \in Y$ and $|a|$ large, so the second components of $Y$ lie in $[0, \infty)^2 \cap -[0, \infty)^2 = 0$, $Y \subseteq \mathbb R \times 0$, and $(0, (1, 0))$ is not in $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R(1, 1) + Y$. So the step "as before" — the implicit function theorem for good position applied to $F$ at the boundary zeros — does not hold as we read it; the theorem does, by the route above.

### V.23 Definition 5.3.13 (preprint 5.20), and Lemmas 5.3.16 and 5.3.17 (preprint 5.23 and 5.24)

**Definition 5.3.13 (preprint 5.20)** ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · StrongBundle.IsGenCompactHomotopy⟧. $X$ tame, $f$ with tame germ data and compact solution set, $t : X \to \mathbb R$ sc-smooth with $t(X) = [0, 1]$, and for every $\tau \in [0, 1]$: $X_\tau = t^{-1}(\tau)$ a sub-M-polyfold (Definition 2.5.7 (2017: 2.19)) with tame induced structure, on which the restriction $f|X_\tau$ — the section $a \mapsto (a, f(a))$ of the pull-back of $P$ along the inclusion ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · restrictSection⟧ ⟦Chapter3/ParamPerturbation · StrongBundle.pullback⟧, the inclusion being sc-smooth (Proposition 2.3.19 (preprint 2.21)) — has tame germ data. The text never says what $Y|X_t$ is; the pull-back of Proposition 2.6.8 (preprint 2.54) is the strong bundle structure available. The end problems are the restrictions to $t^{-1}(0)$ and $t^{-1}(1)$ (or problems isomorphic to them, Remark 5.3.14 (preprint 5.21), §V.35); their solution sets are $S_f \cap X_\tau$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · isZeroAt_restrictSection_iff⟧, closed in the compact $S_f$, hence compact ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · StrongBundle.IsGenCompactHomotopy.isCompact_solutionSet_restrict⟧.

**Lemma 5.3.16 (preprint 5.23) and the hidden hypothesis.** The proof of Theorem 5.3.15 (preprint 5.22) fixes a critical point $x$ of $t|S$ and says "since $x$ is a smooth point, we find a one-dimensional smooth linear sc-subspace $Z \subset T_xX$ such that $T_xX = Z \oplus \ker(dt(x))$". For $dt(x) = 0$, $\ker dt(x) = T_xX$ and the only complement is $0$: a non-zero complement exists only if $\ell \ne 0$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · ne_zero_of_isCompl_ker⟧. Theorem 5.3.15 (preprint 5.22) does not assume that $t$ is a submersion at the critical points of $t|S$, so this is a hidden hypothesis of the preprint. The 2021 condition (3) supplies it (§V.32), and Theorem 5.3.15 is proved in §§V.36–V.41. When $\ell \ne 0$, some vector $e$ of any spanning set (e.g. the dense smooth vectors) has $\ell(e) \ne 0$, and $\mathbb Re$ complements $\ker\ell$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · exists_isCompl_ker_of_ne_zero⟧. Lemma 5.3.16 (preprint 5.23) is then linear algebra: $\ell|_Z$ is an isomorphism onto $\mathbb R$, so $b = (\ell|_Z)^{-1} \circ \tau$ is the unique $b : S \to Z$ with $\ell \circ b = \tau$, and adding $a$ with values in $\ker\ell$ does not change $\ell \circ b$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · lemma_5_3_16_preprint⟧.

**The calculus.** At a level-$1$ point $z$, $D(a \cdot w)(z)v = Da(z)v \cdot w(z) + a(z)Dw(z)v$ for sc-smooth $a : U \to \mathbb R$, $w : U \to F$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · scDeriv_smul_apply⟧, and $D(\ell(\rho(\cdot) - p))(z) = \ell \circ D\rho(z)$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · scDeriv_clm_sub_apply⟧. The function $g = \beta \cdot \ell(\varphi(\cdot) - \varphi(x))$ on $\operatorname{dom}\varphi$, $0$ outside ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · chartLinCutoff⟧, is sc-smooth when $\beta$ is with $\operatorname{supp}\beta \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\varphi$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · isScSmoothMap_chartLinCutoff⟧.

**Lemma 5.3.17 (preprint 5.24).** *The construction* ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · exists_scPlusSection_linAt⟧: for a chart $\Phi$ around the smooth point $x$, a smooth point $e$ over $x$, a continuous linear $\ell$ on the model space and $U \ni x$, let $s_e$ be the sc⁺-section through $e$ of Lemma 5.3.3 (preprint 5.11), supported in $U \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi$, $\beta$ a bump with $\beta \equiv 1$ near $x$ and support in the chart domain, and $s = g \cdot s_e$ with $g$ as above. Then $s$ is sc⁺ (§V.9), $s(x) = g(x)e = 0$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · principal_sectionSmul⟧, $\operatorname{supp}s \subseteq U$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · sectionSupport_sectionSmul_subset⟧, and in the chart, by the product rule, $\mathrm{Lin}_s(z)v = D(g \circ \varphi^{-1} \circ r)(z)v \cdot \hat s_e(\varphi(x)) + g(x)\mathrm{Lin}_{s_e}(z)v = \ell(Dr(z)v)\Phi(e)_2 = \ell(v)\Phi(e)_2$ for $v \in T_zO$, since $g \circ \varphi^{-1} = \ell(\cdot - \varphi(x))$ near $\varphi(x)$ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · chartLinCutoff_of_mem⟧ and $Dr(z) = 1$ on $T_zO$. *The lemma* ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · lemma_5_3_17⟧: for a finite-dimensional $K \subseteq T_zO$ (the text's $T_xS = \ker f'(x)$) and a linear $b : K \to T_zO$ with $\mathrm{Lin}_f(z)(bv) = \lambda(v)\Phi(e)_2$, extend $-\lambda$ (linear on the finite-dimensional $K$) to a continuous linear functional $\ell$ on the model space (Hahn–Banach) and apply the construction: $\mathrm{Lin}_f(z)(bv) + \mathrm{Lin}_s(z)v = \lambda(v)\Phi(e)_2 - \lambda(v)\Phi(e)_2 = 0$. The text's graph of $S$ over $T_xS$, its complement $L$ with $j : L \to \mathbb R$, and its case "if this operator is the zero operator we can take $s = 0$" are not needed. That $f'(x) \circ b_\tau$ has its image in the line of a *smooth* point is a hypothesis; the text's justification ("the image of any vector in $T_xS$ belongs to $Y_\infty$") is not formalized; the proof of Theorem 5.3.15 in §V.41 does not need it, because it takes the vector of the section's value at a smooth point directly.

### V.24 Bump functions in local models: Theorem 5.5.7 (preprint 5.34) and Proposition 5.5.8 (preprint 5.35)

**Definition 5.5.6 (preprint 5.33)** ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · LocalModel.HasBumpProperty⟧. For $x \in O$ and $W$ open in $E_0$ with $\operatorname{cl}(O \cap W) \subseteq O$, an sc-smooth $f$ on $O$ with $f(x) \ne 0$ (as in Definition 5.3.1 (preprint 5.9)) and support in $O$ inside $W$.

**A retract is closed near its points** ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · closure_inter_ball_subset⟧. If $B(z, r) \subseteq W'$ and $U = C \cap W'$ is the domain of a retraction $\rho$ onto $O$, then $O \cap \operatorname{cl}B(z, r/2) \subseteq O$: a limit of points of $O$ in the closed half ball lies in $C$ ($C$ closed) and in $B(z, r)$, hence in $U$, where $\rho$ is continuous, and it is a fixed point of $\rho$.

**Theorem 5.5.7 (preprint 5.34)** ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · theorem_5_5_7⟧. "⇒": every chart's model has the property — given $x$, $W$, a bump of $X$ at $\varphi^{-1}(x)$ supported in $\varphi^{-1}(O \cap W)$, read in the chart. "⇐", "clearly" in the text, hides a support condition: a local bump $f_0$ with support in $U(x)$, $\operatorname{cl}_E(U(x)) \subseteq O$, gives $f = f_0 \circ \varphi$ on the chart domain, but $\operatorname{cl}_X\{f \ne 0\}$ may leave the domain. For $X = E$ a Hilbert space, the chart $\varphi(u) = u/(1 - |u|_0^2)$ from the open unit ball onto $O = E$, $U(x) = O$ and $f_0 \equiv 1$, the extension by $0$ is the indicator of the ball. The proof chooses $U_1 \ni x$ with $\operatorname{cl}_XU_1 \subseteq U \cap \operatorname{dom}\varphi$ (regularity of $X$) and $r$ with $B(\varphi(x), r) \cap O \subseteq \varphi(U_1)$, takes the local bump in $W = B(\varphi(x), r/2)$ — admissible by the previous paragraph — and extends $f_0 \circ \varphi$ by $0$: its support lies in $\operatorname{cl}_XU_1 \subseteq U$, and it is sc-smooth because it vanishes on the open complement of its support and is sc-smooth in the chart (§V.8).

**Proposition 5.5.8 (preprint 5.35).** If $\kappa\|v\|^2 \le b(v, v)$ for a continuous bilinear $b$ on $E_0$, then $f(v) = \tau(1 - b(v - x, v - x)/\rho)$ is $C^\infty$ on $E_0$, equal to $1$ at $x$ and supported in a small ball; it is sc-smooth on $E$ by Corollary 1.2.5 (preprint 1.20) from the base level ⟦Chapter1/Levels · IsScSmooth.of_contDiffOn_finiteDimensional⟧, and so is its composition with any retraction onto $O$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · LocalModel.hasBumpProperty_of_quadratic⟧. "$E_0$ is a Hilbert space" is stated as $\|v\|^2 = b(v, v)$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · proposition_5_5_8⟧: an inner product structure on $E_0$ would be a second normed structure next to that of the sc-scale. Translating by a non-smooth $x$ is legitimate here because $f$ is $C^\infty$ on $E_0$ itself; for a merely sc-smooth function it would not be. With Theorem 5.5.7 (preprint 5.34): an M-polyfold covered by charts on sc-Hilbert spaces admits sc-smooth bump functions, the remark before Definition 5.3.1 (preprint 5.9) ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert⟧.

### V.25 Partitions of unity: Theorem 5.5.10 (preprint 5.37) and Proposition 5.5.11 (preprint 5.38)

**The algebra of sc-smooth functions.** Sums, differences and products of sc-smooth functions are sc-smooth, on retracts ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · IsScSmoothRetractMap.real_add⟧ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · IsScSmoothRetractMap.real_mul⟧ and on $X$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.real_add⟧ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.real_sub⟧ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.real_mul⟧, and so are finite sums and products ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · isScSmoothMap_real_finsetSum⟧ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · isScSmoothMap_real_finsetProd⟧. Sc-smoothness is local ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · isScSmoothMap_real_of_eventuallyEq⟧, so a locally finite sum, which near each point is a finite sum, is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · isScSmoothMap_real_finsum⟧; and a function supported in a chart domain with sc-smooth representative is sc-smooth on $X$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · isScSmoothMap_real_of_chart⟧.

**Definitions 5.5.1 and 5.5.9 (preprint 5.28 and 5.36).** A partition of unity is Mathlib's (continuous $\rho_i \ge 0$, locally finite supports, $\sum\rho_i = 1$), sc-smooth if every $\rho_i$ is ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothPartitionOfUnity⟧; $X$ admits sc-smooth partitions of unity if every open cover has a subordinate one ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.AdmitsScPartitionsOfUnity⟧. The approximation property: for $V = O \cap W$ with $\operatorname{cl}V \subseteq O$, continuous $f : O \to [0, 1]$ supported in $V$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, an sc-smooth $g : O \to [0, 1]$ supported in $V$ with $|f - g| \le \varepsilon$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · LocalModel.HasApproxProperty⟧. Partitions of unity give bump functions: the function attached to $U$ of a partition subordinate to $\{U, X \setminus \{x\}\}$ is $1$ at $x$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.AdmitsScPartitionsOfUnity.admitsBumpFunctions⟧ — the easy half of the open problem the text states after Definition 5.5.2 (preprint 5.29).

**"(i) ⇒ (ii)"** ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · hasApproxProperty_restrict⟧. The text calls $f \circ \varphi$ "sc-smooth" ($f$ is only continuous) and asserts $\operatorname{cl}_X(\varphi^{-1}(V)) \subseteq U$; with the chart of the unit ball above, $V = O$ and $f \equiv 1$, the extension by $0$ is not continuous. Since (ii) asks only for *some* atlas, the proof restricts each chart to an open $s$ with $\operatorname{cl}_X(s) \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\varphi$. Then for closed $A \subseteq \varphi(s)$ the set $\varphi^{-1}(A)$ is closed in $X$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MChart.isClosed_inter_preimage⟧, so $F = f \circ \varphi$ extended by $0$ is continuous. Cover $X$ by $\{F < \varepsilon/2\}$ and the sets $U_x = \{|F - F(x)| < \varepsilon/2\} \cap \varphi^{-1}(V)$, take a subordinate sc-smooth partition of unity $(\beta_0, \beta_x)$, and let $\hat g = \sum_x\beta_xF(x)$: a locally finite sum of sc-smooth functions with values in $[0, 1]$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · PartitionOfUnity.finsum_mul_mem_Icc⟧, supported in $\varphi^{-1}(V)$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · PartitionOfUnity.tsupport_finsum_mul_subset⟧, and within $\varepsilon/2$ of $F$, since every $F(x)$ with $\beta_x(y) \ne 0$ is ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · PartitionOfUnity.abs_sub_finsum_mul_le⟧. Every chart has the property, by a different route (§V.42).

**"(ii) ⇒ (i)".** Every point of a chart domain has small open neighbourhoods $N$ with $\operatorname{cl}_XN \subseteq \operatorname{dom}\varphi$ and $\operatorname{cl}\varphi(N) \subseteq O$ — half a ball inside the domain of a retraction, closed by §V.24 ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MChart.exists_small_nhds⟧ — and the approximation property transports to continuous functions on $X$ supported in such $N$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · LocalModel.HasApproxProperty.exists_approx⟧. *Sc-smooth Urysohn functions* ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · exists_isScSmoothMap_urysohn⟧: for disjoint closed $s, t$, cover $t$ by small neighbourhoods $W_x$ inside $X \setminus s$, take continuous $f_x = 1$ near $x$ supported in $W_x$, a locally finite refinement, approximations $\hat g_x$ within $1/2$ — so $\hat g_x \ge 1/2$ where $f_x = 1$ — and $F = \tau(4\sum\hat g_x - 1)$, sc-smooth, $0$ on $s$ and $1$ on $t$. Then Mathlib's bump coverings produce a covering indexed by the given cover with sc-smooth functions ⟦Mathlib/Topology/PartitionOfUnity · BumpCovering.exists_isSubordinate_of_prop⟧, and $\rho_i = f_i\prod_{j < i}(1 - f_j)$, locally a finite product, is the partition of unity ⟦Mathlib/Topology/PartitionOfUnity · BumpCovering.toPartitionOfUnity⟧ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_approx⟧. This replaces the text's refinement "with the same index set", which does not exist in general (the cover $\{X\}$); metrizability is not needed.

**Theorem 5.5.10 (preprint 5.37)** ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · theorem_5_5_10⟧ combines the two directions, "atlas" read as a family of charts covering $X$.

**Proposition 5.5.11 (preprint 5.38)** ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · proposition_5_5_11⟧ is not "an immediate consequence of Theorem 5.37": that theorem produces some atlas, not the given model, and applied to $O$ would need partitions of unity on an open subset of $C$. The proof repeats "(i) ⇒ (ii)" in $E_0$: $A = \{x \in O \mid f(x) \ge \varepsilon/2\}$ is closed in $E_0$ because $\operatorname{cl}V \subseteq O$; $E_0 \setminus A$ and balls $B(x, r_x) \subseteq W$, $x \in V$, on which $f$ varies by less than $\varepsilon/2$, cover $E_0$; a $C^\infty$ partition of unity of $E_0$ gives $g = \sum\beta_xf(x)$, $C^\infty$ on $E_0$, hence sc-smooth (Corollary 1.2.5 (preprint 1.20)), composed with a retraction onto $O$.

### V.26 Banach space geometry: Definitions 5.5.4, 5.5.12, 5.5.14 (preprint 5.31, 5.39, 5.41), Proposition 5.5.15 (preprint 5.42), Corollary 5.5.17 (preprint 5.44)

A Banach space admits a $C^k$-bump function if some $C^k$ function, not identically zero, has bounded support ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · HasContDiffBump⟧, and $C^k$ partitions of unity if every open cover has a subordinate $C^k$ one ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · AdmitsContDiffPartitionsOfUnity⟧. $c_0(\Gamma)$ is the subspace of $\ell^\infty(\Gamma)$ of functions tending to $0$ along the cofinite filter ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · cZero⟧, equivalently with $\{|f(\gamma)| > \varepsilon\}$ finite for every $\varepsilon$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · mem_cZero_iff⟧, normed by the supremum ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · norm_cZero⟧; coordinate-wise $C^k$ embeddings are as in the text ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · IsCoordinatewiseContDiffEmbedding⟧, and Toruńczyk's Theorem 5.5.13 (preprint 5.40) is recorded as a statement ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · TorunczykStatement⟧, proved in §V.45. WCG means a weakly compact set with dense span ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · IsWCG⟧; reflexive, used in Proposition 5.5.15 (preprint 5.42) and not defined in the text, means $V \to V''$ onto ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · IsReflexive⟧.

**Proposition 5.5.15 (preprint 5.42).** (i) For reflexive $V$ the weak closure of the closed unit ball is weakly compact — Kakutani's theorem, in Mathlib as Banach–Alaoglu in $V''$ through the embedding of $(V, \text{weak})$ into $(V'', \text{weak-*})$ ⟦Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Module/DoubleDual · NormedSpace.isCompact_closure_of_isBounded⟧ — and its span contains the ball, hence is $V$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · span_closedBall_eq_top⟧ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · proposition_5_5_15_reflexive⟧. (ii) For separable $V$, a dense sequence $(y_n)$ scaled by $1/((n + 1)(|y_n| + 1))$ is a null sequence; with $0$ it is norm compact, hence weakly compact, and its span contains every $y_n$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · proposition_5_5_15_separable⟧. The text's "$\{0\} \cup \{x_n/n\}$" has its index range missing.

**Corollary 5.5.17 (preprint 5.44)** ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · corollary_5_5_17⟧. Let $\|v\|^2 = b(v, v)$ on $E_0$, and assume Theorem 5.5.16 (preprint 5.43) for $E_0$ and $k = \infty$, recorded as a statement ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · GodefroyTroyanskiWhitfieldZizlerStatement⟧. A Hilbert space is reflexive: the parallelogram law holds, so the norm comes from an inner product ⟦Mathlib/Analysis/InnerProductSpace/OfNorm · InnerProductSpace.ofNorm⟧, and every $\phi \in V''$ is evaluation at the Riesz representative of $x \mapsto \phi(\langle x, \cdot\rangle)$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · isReflexive_of_hilbert⟧; hence WCG by Proposition 5.5.15 (i) (preprint 5.42). It has the $C^\infty$-bump $\tau(1 - b(v, v))$ ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · hasContDiffBump_of_hilbert⟧. Theorem 5.5.16 (preprint 5.43) gives $C^\infty$ partitions of unity of $E_0$, and Proposition 5.5.11 (preprint 5.38) — not Theorem 5.5.10 (preprint 5.37), as the text says — the approximation property. With Theorem 5.5.10 (preprint 5.37), an M-polyfold on such charts admits sc-smooth partitions of unity ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_hilbert⟧. The hypothesis is removed in §V.46: $E_0$ is separable, and Theorem 5.5.16 (preprint 5.43) is proved for separable spaces there and for every WCG space in §V.47.

### V.27 What is not formalized

Of the chapter's gaps, G.41, G.42, G.44–G.48 and G.50–G.53 are closed, G.41 for each fixed $i$ and G.42 with a correction; G.43 and G.49 have nothing to formalize. What remains:

- **Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8) as one statement for all $i$.** It is proved for each fixed $i$ (§V.29; gap G.41 closed in the fourth addendum). Not formalized: a family $P^i$ indexed by $i$, and the tame form of the conclusion, which needs the tameness of the index raises of tame charts. The identification of the iterated base $(X^1)^1$ with $X_2$ as a topological space is proved since (§II.32; gap G.6, closed). Condition (3) of a filling on level $1$ does not follow from level $0$ alone — on $E_m = \{x \mid \sum e^{2mk}x_k^2 < \infty\}$ the right shift $T$ makes $1 - T/2$ invertible on $E_0$ while $(1 - T/2)^{-1}e_0 = \sum2^{-n}e_n \notin E_1$ — so the corollary's proof needs the regularity argument of §V.29, through Lemma 3.1.20 (preprint 3.17) ⟦Chapter3/Filler · lemma_3_1_20⟧.
- **The non-completeness of $(\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P), \rho)$ in the text's setting**, beyond the trivial bundle, and the identification of the completion with the sections of Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12) (§V.30; gap G.42).
- **Weak against pointwise bump functions at a non-smooth point** (§V.31).
- **Theorem 5.3.15 (preprint 5.22)**, proved (§§V.36–V.41; gap G.48), leaves the comparison of the smooth parametrizations through which "Morse-type" is read with the charts of the Mathlib manifold structure on the solution set. That the complement $Z$ of Lemma 5.3.16 (preprint 5.23) can be chosen smooth is not formalized; the formal proof does not use Lemmas 5.3.16 and 5.3.17 (preprint 5.23 and 5.24), proved in §§V.23 and V.32.
- **Remark 5.3.8 (preprint 5.16)** is formalized on $\mathbb R^1 \times X$ with the time window $[0, 1]$, not on $[0, 1] \times X$, which would need a tame structure on the product with an interval (§V.33).
- **Theorem 5.27 (preprint; not in the 2021 edition)** (gap G.49, nothing to formalize in the 2021 edition; the preprint leaves the proof to the reader). Its general-position analogue is §V.33. A good-position form at the corner points $\{i\} \times \partial X$ would need the step that Finding 88 shows not to hold as we read it ⟦Chapter3/Counterexamples2021 · Counterexamples2021.not_isInGoodPosition_prod_diag⟧; no counterexample to the theorem itself is built (Findings, Chapter 5, items 104, 186).
- **The Sobolev sc-structure on other domains** (row V5.76, narrower): compactness of the inclusions $W^{k+1,p}(\Omega) \to W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ and density of $E_\infty$ are proved for $\Omega = (0, 1)$ and every $p > 1$; for cubes in $\mathbb R^n$, $n \ge 2$, and other domains they are hypotheses (§V.44). The bump claims hold for every $\Omega$.
- **The 2021 remark that the notions of Definition 5.2.1 differ for general sc-smooth sections** (§V.32).
- **Remark 5.3.6 (preprint 5.14)** (gap G.43): nothing to formalize; the formalization assumes neither separable sc-Hilbert fibres nor further properties of auxiliary norms.

### V.28 What the formalization taught us

**The tameness hypothesis.** The first formal versions of Theorem 5.3.5 (preprint 5.13) and Lemma 5.26 (preprint) assumed, as the §3.6 theorems then did, that the base retraction of *every* compatible strong bundle chart — and of every chart of the pull-backs to $\mathbb R^k \times X$ — is tame. No strong bundle over a nonempty base satisfies this (a compatible chart $(1, \varphi)$ with base retraction $(a, u) \mapsto (1, r(u))$ on $[0, \infty) \times U$ is never tame), so those statements were vacuous. The repair is the text's own Definitions 3.6.3, 3.6.4, 3.6.6 (preprint 3.50, 3.51, 3.53) in a tame chart: the perturbation theorems take $f$ with tame germ data, the parametrized sections inherit them through the tame product chart, and Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17) lives in a tame chart, where Lemma 5.26's (preprint) count $\dim T_zO/T^R_zO = d_C(z)$ holds.

**What "it is easily verified" costs.** The perturbation theorems of §5.3 are sketches. Their formal proofs needed the density of smooth vectors (§V.12), the compactness of the zeros over a small parameter ball (§V.13), a local, stratified Sard step (§V.14), the bridge from tangent germ data to Definition 4.2.1 (preprint 4.13) (§V.17), $T_yS = \ker f'(y)$ by a dimension count, which gives the chart independence of Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17) and the openness of general position (§§V.17–V.18), and, in Theorem 5.3.12 (preprint 5.19), a route around the implicit function theorem at boundary points where its hypothesis fails (§V.22).

**Theorem 5.3.15 without a trivialization.** The text's proof moves the solution set $S$ along a trivialization $\Phi_\lambda : S \to S_\lambda$ and differentiates the equation twice. The formal proof takes the perturbations of the form $a_i\sigma_{g(i)}$, so that every $S_\lambda$ is a level set inside one fixed solution manifold of $f + \sum\mu_j\sigma_j$, and replaces the trivialization by Lagrange multipliers and the bordered Hessian (§§V.38–V.39). The "parameterized version of Sard's theorem" is the inverse function theorem plus Sard's lemma in equal dimensions (§V.38). When the families of several critical points are united, the transversality obtained at one of them must survive the others; the bounded coordinates $\arctan(q_i)/2$ and the constant $1$ make it do so, because a multiplier of the larger family restricts to a non-zero multiplier of the smaller one (§V.39; Findings, Chapter 5, item 183).

**The corner case is no case.** The boundary of the solution set might have corners where $t|S$ is not regular. It cannot: at a zero on $\partial X$, $t$ takes the value $0$ or $1$ and is an extremum, so $dt(x)$ vanishes on the two-sided directions $E_x \supseteq T^R_xX$; general position and $dt(x) \ne 0$ then make $dt(x)$ non-zero on $\ker f'(x)$, at every degeneracy index (§V.41).

**The hidden hypothesis is the 2021 condition.** The hypothesis $dt(x) \ne 0$ that §V.23 found missing from the preprint is Definition 5.3.13 (3) of the 2021 edition, and with it Theorem 5.3.15 needs nothing beyond the text (§§V.32, V.36).

**Finding 88 is machine-checked.** Good position is not stable under $\mathbb R \times \cdot$ (§V.22), so the implicit function theorem cannot be applied "as before" at the boundary zeros of the parametrized section; Theorem 5.3.12, its dense form and the cobordisms of §V.33 are proved on routes that avoid those points.

**$E_0$ is always separable.** The inclusion $E_1 \to E_0$ of an sc-Banach space is compact with dense range, so $E_0$ is separable (§V.46). In the sc-calculus, Theorem 5.5.16 (preprint 5.43) is needed only for separable spaces, where it is elementary, and Corollary 5.5.17 (preprint 5.44) holds without it. The general WCG case was proved anyway, without Krein's theorem, the Eberlein–Šmulian theorem or a transfinite recursion: Mazur's theorem and finite character of a closure operator suffice (§V.47).

**Every chart, by shells.** The text's derivation of the approximation property in a chart uses $\operatorname{cl}_X(W) \subseteq U$, which does not follow from $\operatorname{cl}_C(V) \subseteq O$ (§V.25; Findings, Chapter 5, item 111). Exhausting the chart domain by shells $\{1/(n + 2) \le d \le 1/(n + 1)\}$ and summing local approximations gives the property for every chart (§V.42).

**The Sobolev remark lives on level $0$.** Its bump claims use only $E_0 = W^{1,4}(\Omega)$ or $W^{1,3/2}(\Omega)$: a $C^k$ bump on $E_0$ is sc$^k$ on any sc-structure. The sc-structure $E_m = W^{1+m,p}(\Omega)$ itself — Rellich compactness and density of smooth functions — is a separate matter, proved here for $(0, 1)$ (§V.44).

### V.29 Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8) on the shifted strong bundle

Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8) says that, for an sc-Fredholm section $f$ with compact solution set, $f^i$ is an sc-Fredholm section of $P^i : Y^i \to X^i$ with compact solution set, and that "it is a priori clear that $f^i$ is sc-Fredholm". The text defines $Y[i]$ for $i = 0, 1$ only, never $Y^i$, and "a priori clear" hides the filler condition on level $1$ (§V.7). Both are supplied here (Findings, Chapter 5, items 140–146).

**The reading of $Y^1$.** $Y^1 = Y_{1,1}$ with $(Y^1)_{m,k} = Y_{m+1,k+1}$ — the convention of $E^1$ and of $(U \triangleleft F)^1 = U^1 \triangleleft F^1$ — not $Y[1] = Y_{0,1}$ and not $Y_{1,2}$. It is forced by "$f^i$ is obtained by raising the index": an sc-smooth section maps $X_1$ into $Y_{1,1}$, and in general not into $Y_{1,2}$.

**Fibres of a strong bundle.** Through a chart, $P^{-1}(x)$ is linearly homeomorphic to $K_{\varphi(x)} = \{h \mid \Gamma(\varphi(x), h) = h\}$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.fiberK⟧ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.fiberCLE⟧, the fixed points of a continuous projection, a closed subspace of the fibre model ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.isClosed_fiberK⟧; so every fibre is a Banach space ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.isBanachable_fiber⟧, which Definition 2.6.5 (preprint 2.51) asks of a strong bundle.

**The levels of $X^1$, and raising the index of maps.** $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ and $(X^1)_\infty = X_\infty$ as sets ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · MPolyfold.mem_shift_levelSet_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · MPolyfold.mem_shift_smoothSet_iff⟧ (their topologies agree too, §II.32; gap G.6, closed). An sc-smooth map $f : X \to Z$ between M-polyfolds induces an sc-smooth $f_1 : X^1 \to Z^1$: continuity, and in the level charts the local representatives are the level-$1$ maps of those of $f$, sc-smooth by Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) for retracts ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · MPolyfold.levelChart_apply_levelOne⟧ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.levelOne⟧.

**The shifted strong bundle** ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.shift⟧. Its total space is $Y_{1,1}$, the level $1$ of the M-polyfold $Y[0]$ with its level topology, Hausdorff and paracompact by Theorem 2.3.10 (preprint 2.16) ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.ShiftSpace⟧; the projection is $P^1 = P|_{Y_{1,1}}$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.shiftProj⟧, continuous and onto ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.continuous_shiftProj⟧ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.surjective_shiftProj⟧; the fibre $P^{-1}(x) \cap Y_{1,1}$ is a linear subspace — in a chart it is the preimage of $F_1$ under the linear fibre map ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.shiftFiberSubmodule⟧ — carries the topology of $F_1$, not that of $P^{-1}(x)$, and is a Banach space, a closed subspace of $F_1$ through a chart ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.banachable_shift⟧. The atlas consists of the *index raises* of the strong bundle charts ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.shift⟧ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.shiftAtlas⟧: base chart the level chart $\varphi^1 : V_1 \to O_1$, fibre model $F^1$, retraction $R$ on $U^1 \triangleleft F^1$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · IsStrongBundleRetraction.shift⟧, bundle chart the level chart of $\Phi$ in $Y[0]$. Compatible charts have compatible index raises ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.Compatible.shift⟧: on $[0]$ the transitions are level charts of compatible charts, on $[1]$ the transition $(\Phi'^1 \circ (\Phi^1)^{-1})[1]$ is the level-$1$ map of $(\Phi' \circ \Phi^{-1})[1]$ (Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) for retracts) ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.shift_transition_one⟧, and the $F_1$-condition of Definition 2.6.4 (preprint 2.50) holds because the $[1]$-transition is sc⁰ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundleChart.shift_compatible_range⟧. Checks: $(Y^1)_{m,k} = Y_{m+1,k+1}$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.mem_shift_doubleLevel_iff⟧, the M-polyfold $Y^1[0]$ is $Y[0]^1$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.isChart_shift_toMPolyfold0_iff⟧, and the index raise of every chart of $P$ is a chart of $P^1$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.isChart_shift⟧.

**The section $f^1$.** $f^1 = f|_{X_1}$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.sectionShift⟧ is a section of $P^1$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.isSection_sectionShift⟧, sc-smooth by the raising of the index of maps ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.IsScSmoothSection.shift⟧, with the zeros of $f$ in $X_1$ as its zeros ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.solutionSet_sectionShift⟧, and regularizing, from $(X^1)_m = X_{m+1}$ and $(Y^1)_{m,m+1} = Y_{m+1,m+2}$ ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · StrongBundle.regularizing_sectionShift⟧. In the index raise of a chart the principal part of $f^1$ is the level-$1$ map of that of $f$ ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · StrongBundleChart.principal_sectionShift⟧, and the raised chart is centred where the chart is ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · StrongBundleChart.shift_φ_eq_zero⟧.

**Condition (3) on every level, at every centre** ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · IsFillingGerm.mem_range_toBase_of_fillDefect⟧. *Let $(g, s)$ be a datum of Definition 3.1.11 (preprint 3.11) in a chart — $g$ a filling germ of $\hat f$ with fill defect $k = [1 - \rho(r)]g$ and derivative family $Dk$, $s$ an sc⁺-germ with $s(0) = g(0)$, $g - s$ conjugated to a basic germ. If $v \in \ker Dr(0)$ and $Dk(0)v \in F_m$, then $v \in E_m$* — at the centre of the datum, which need not be a zero. At a zero this is the regularity of §III.45 ⟦Chapter3/LinearizationChartsScG · IsFillingGerm.mem_range_toBase_of_scDeriv_r_eq_zero⟧. The reduction to a zero needs neither a global sc⁺-section nor a bump function: $g(0) = \iota s(0)$ is a smooth point of $F$ ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · IsScSmoothGerm.toBase_zero_mem_smooth⟧; $\hat s(z) = \Gamma(z, -g(0))$ is sc-smooth on $U$ ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoXi · isScSmooth_const_of_smooth⟧ and a section of $K \to O$, so by Lemma 3.1.20 (preprint 3.17) $g' = g + \hat s \circ r$ fills $\hat f + \hat s$ with the *same* fill defect ⟦Chapter3/GermCalculus · IsFillingGerm.add_section⟧, and $g'(0) = g(0) - \Gamma(0, g(0)) = 0$. With the sc⁺-germ $s' = s + \Gamma^1(r(\cdot), -s(0))$, $g' - s' = g - s$ on $U$, so Proposition 3.6.5 (preprint 3.52) in sc form makes $Dg'(0)$ sc-Fredholm ⟦Chapter3/FredholmGermLinearizationScG · proposition_3_6_5_local_sc⟧; and $Dk(0) = (1 - \rho(0))Dg'(0)$ ⟦Chapter3/GermFillerLinearization · fillDefect_deriv_zero_eq_rho⟧, so the case of a zero applies to $g'$.

**The filling on level $1$** ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · IsFillingGerm.germ_shift⟧. The fill defect of $g^1$ is the level-$1$ map of $k$, an sc¹-germ with derivative family $(Dk)_1$ by Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) for germs ⟦Chapter3/GermLevels · IsSc1GermWith.shift⟧; $\iota\,Dr^1(0) = Dr(0)\,\iota$, by the uniqueness of the derivative of $r^1 = r_1$ on the shifted germ ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · toBase_scDeriv_r_shift⟧, and $\iota\,\rho^1(0) = \rho(0)\,\iota$ ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · toBase_ρCLM_shift⟧. So $Dk^1(0) = Dk(0)|_{E_1}$ maps $\ker Dr^1(0)$ to $\ker\rho^1(0)$; it is injective by condition (3) on level $0$, onto by the regularity just proved with $m = 1$, and a topological isomorphism by the open mapping theorem. Conditions (1) and (2) of the filling shift directly ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · StrongBundleChart.shift_filling_eq_on⟧ ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · StrongBundleChart.shift_filling_mem_of_fixed⟧, and $g^1$ is a filling germ of the principal part of $f^1$ in $\Phi^1$ ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · StrongBundleChart.shift_isFillingGerm⟧.

**Corollary 5.2.5 (preprint 5.8).** At every smooth point of $X^1$, the datum $(g, s)$ of $f$ in a chart $\Phi$ gives the datum $(g^1, s^1)$ of $f^1$ in $\Phi^1$: $g^1$ fills, $s^1$ is an sc⁺-germ on the shifted germ, $s^1(0) = g^1(0)$, and $g^1 - s^1 = (g - s)_1$ near $0$ is conjugated to a basic germ by the index raise of the conjugation (§V.7) ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · isScFredholmGerm_sectionShift⟧. *For an sc-Fredholm section $f$, $f^1$ is an sc-Fredholm section of $P^1$* ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · corollary_5_2_5_isScFredholmSection⟧; *if $f$ has compact solution set, so has $f^1$*, by the compactness on level $1$ (§V.7) ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · corollary_5_2_5⟧. Since this holds for every strong bundle, it applies to $P^1$ and $f^1$: $f^2 = (f^1)^1$ is an sc-Fredholm section of $P^2 = (P^1)^1$ with compact solution set ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · corollary_5_2_5_two⟧, and so on for every fixed $i$. The unpacked data in the shifted chart are kept for reference ⟦Chapter5/Corollary58 · corollary_5_2_5_data⟧. No hypothesis beyond the text's is added, and tameness is not used. *Not done*: a family $P^i$ indexed by $i$ (a dependent type of strong bundles) and the tame form of the conclusion — germ data of $f^1$ in tame charts of $P^1$ — which needs the presentation independence of the degeneracy index for $C^1$ and that $A \cap E_1$ is an sc-complement of $T_xO^1$ when $A$ is one of $T_xO$; there is no counterexample either.

### V.30 The metric $\rho$ on $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$

The text: $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$ "becomes a metric space" for $\rho(s, s') = \sup_xN(s(x) - s'(x))$, and "is not complete" (p. 217 (preprint p. 174)). The first is proved here; the second turns out to need a hypothesis (Findings, Chapter 5, items 150–153).

**The metric.** $\rho(s, s')$ is the supremum of the pointwise distances of §V.10 ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.allowableDist⟧. For an auxiliary norm the fibre norm is symmetric and subadditive (Definition 5.1.1 (1) (preprint 5.1)) ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.neg⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.sub_le⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.sub_triangle⟧, so for allowable sections $N(s(x) - s'(x)) \le N(s(x)) + N(s'(x)) \le 2$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.sectionDistAt_le_two⟧: the supremum is finite and $\rho \le 2$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.allowableDist_le_two⟧. $\rho(s, s) = 0$, symmetry and the triangle inequality come from the fibre norms ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.allowableDist_self⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.allowableDist_comm⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.allowableDist_triangle⟧, and $\rho(s, s') = 0$ forces $s = s'$ because $N$ vanishes only at $0_x$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.eq_of_allowableDist_eq_zero⟧. So $\rho$ is a metric ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.allowableMetric⟧, carried by a type synonym of $\Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$, since the sections $X \to Y$ carry the product topology ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.AllowableSpace⟧. Only Definition 5.1.1 (1) (preprint 5.1) is used. The density statements of Theorems 5.3.5 and 5.3.10 (preprint 5.13 and 5.18) (§§V.15, V.20) are $\rho(s, s') \le \varepsilon$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.allowableDist_le_iff⟧.

**Not complete, by an example** ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.not_completeSpace_allowableSections⟧. Take the trivial bundle $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R \to \mathbb R$ of the non-vacuity witnesses of Chapter 3, the fibre norm $N(x, v) = |v|$ — an auxiliary norm, including the condition on the topology of $Y[1]$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.fibNorm⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.isAuxNorm_fibNorm⟧ — and $U = \mathbb R$. Graphs of $C^\infty$ maps are sc⁺-sections ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.isScPlusSection_graphSection⟧, so $s_j(x) = (x, \sqrt{x^2 + 1/(j+1)^2}/(2\sqrt{1 + x^2}))$ is allowable, with $N \le 1/2$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.approx⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.graphSection_approx_mem⟧, and $\rho(s_i, s_j) \le (\varepsilon_i + \varepsilon_j)/2$ with $\varepsilon_j = 1/(j+1)$, by $|\sqrt{x^2 + a^2} - |x|| \le a$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.abs_sqrt_sub_abs_le⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.abs_approx_sub_limitFn⟧. A $\rho$-limit $s$ would have, by pointwise convergence, the fibre part $|x|/(2\sqrt{1 + x^2})$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.limitFn⟧, which is not differentiable at $0$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.not_differentiableAt_limit⟧; but the fibre part of an sc⁺-section of the trivial bundle is $C^1$, by Proposition 1.2.3 (preprint 1.18) in the chart $\Phi = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.differentiable_snd_of_isScPlusSection⟧.

**Complete, in two cases.** For $U = \emptyset$ every allowable section is the zero section, so the space is a point, for every bundle and auxiliary norm ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.subsingleton_allowableSections_empty⟧ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · StrongBundle.completeSpace_allowableSections_empty⟧. Over the point $\mathbb R^0$ with fibre $\mathbb R^k$ every section is the graph of a constant, hence sc⁺ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.isScPlusSection_of_isSection_point⟧, and the space is the closed unit ball of $\mathbb R^k$ (or $\{0\}$), complete for every $U$ ⟦Chapter5/AllowableSectionsMetric · TrivialBundle.completeSpace_allowableSections_point⟧. So the text's "not complete" does not hold as we read it without a hypothesis and is read as "not complete in general". In the text's setting — $U$ a neighbourhood of the solution set of an sc-Fredholm section on an M-polyfold with bump functions — one expects non-completeness as soon as $U$ contains a non-isolated point over which $Y_{0,1}$ is nonzero, by the same mechanism (bump functions times a non-smooth uniform limit); this is not formalized, and neither is the identification of the metric completion with the sections of Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12) (§V.10).

### V.31 Weak and pointwise bump functions

§V.8 reads Definition 5.3.1 (preprint 5.9) pointwise, $f(x) \ne 0$, because Proposition 5.5.3 (preprint 5.30) needs it, and keeps Definition 5.5.2's (preprint 5.29) "not identically zero" as the weak reading. How far apart are they? (Findings, Chapter 5, items 160–163.)

**Bump points.** $x$ is a *bump point* if every open $U \ni x$ carries an sc-smooth $f$ with $f(x) \ne 0$ and $\operatorname{supp} f \subseteq U$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · MPolyfold.HasBumpAt⟧. The pointwise reading says that every point is a bump point ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_iff_forall_hasBumpAt⟧, and the weak reading holds as soon as the bump points are dense: a bump at a bump point inside $U$ is not identically zero and is supported in $U$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctionsWeak_of_dense⟧. (The converse, weak ⟹ dense bump points, is a nested-neighbourhoods argument with Cantor's theorem in a chart; not formalized.)

**On an sc-Banach space.** An sc-Banach space $E$ is an M-polyfold with the identity chart and model $(E, E, E)$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · scChart⟧ ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · scPolyfold⟧, whose sc-smooth functions are the sc-smooth maps $E \to \mathbb R$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · isScSmoothMap_scPolyfold_iff⟧. *There the weak reading gives a bump point at every smooth point* ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak.hasBumpAt_of_mem_smooth⟧: given $x \in E_\infty$ and $B(x, \varepsilon) \subseteq U$, a weak bump supported in $B(x, \varepsilon/2)$ is non-zero on a non-empty open set, which contains a smooth point $y$ because $E_\infty$ is dense; $a = y - x$ is smooth, so $v \mapsto f(v + a)$ is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter4/Recentre · isScSmooth_add_const⟧, non-zero at $x$, with support in $B(x, \varepsilon) \subseteq U$. The argument stops at $E_\infty$: translation by a vector $a \notin E_m$ is not even sc⁰, since it sends $0 \in E_m$ out of $E_m$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpWeakPointwise · not_isSc0_add_const⟧. On M-polyfolds built on sc-Hilbert spaces both readings hold at every point ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert⟧. *Open*: whether the weak reading gives a bump function non-zero at a non-smooth point, on an sc-Banach space or an M-polyfold; a counterexample would need an $E_0$ without $C^1$ bump functions.

### V.32 The Springer 2021 edition: Definition 5.2.1, Theorems 5.2.2 and 5.3.5, Definition 5.3.13

The 2021 edition adds two compactness properties to Definition 5.2.1 (preprint 5.4) and extends Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5) to them, concludes in Theorem 5.3.5 (preprint 5.13) that the perturbed solution sets are compact sub-M-polyfolds, and changes Definition 5.3.13 (preprint 5.20): $t$ need not be onto, the fibres $X_\tau$ are no longer asked to be Fredholm problems, and $dt(x)$ is asked onto at every smooth point. Chapter 5 has no item that is new in the 2021 edition. The file is `Chapter5/Book2021.lean` (Findings, Chapter 5, items 170–179).

**Definition 5.2.1, 2021 form** ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.IsWeaklyProperOnU⟧ ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.IsWeaklyProperLtInfty⟧ ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.IsProperLtInfty⟧. *Statement.* (2) weakly proper: compact solution set, and for every auxiliary norm $N$ an open $U \supseteq f^{-1}(0)$ such that $\{f = s\}$ is compact for every sc⁺-section $s$ supported in $U$ with $N(s(y)) \le 1$ for $y \in U$; (4) weakly proper$_{<\infty}$: the same for every such $s$ with $N(s) \le C$ on $U$ for some constant $C$; (5) proper$_{<\infty}$: compact solution set, and for every $N$ an open $U \supseteq f^{-1}(0)$ with $\operatorname{cl}_X\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le C\}$ compact for every $C > 0$, where $N(f(x)) \le C$ includes $f(x) \in Y_{0,1}$ ⟦Chapter5/Compactness · StrongBundle.AuxLe⟧. *The bound on $U$ is the old bound everywhere* ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.isWeaklyProperOnU_iff⟧: a section supported in $U$ vanishes off $U$ ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.isZeroAt_of_not_mem_of_support_subset⟧, and the zero of a fibre has $N \le r$ for every $r \ge 0$ ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.auxLe_fiberZero⟧; so (2) is the `IsWeaklyProper` of §V.4 ⟦Chapter5/Compactness · StrongBundle.IsWeaklyProper⟧, and (1), (3) are unchanged ⟦Chapter5/Compactness · StrongBundle.IsProper⟧.

**The a priori dependencies (p. 209).** Proper$_{<\infty}$ gives proper with $C = 1$ ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.IsProperLtInfty.isProper⟧; weakly proper$_{<\infty}$ gives weakly proper, since the bound $1$ is a constant ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.IsWeaklyProperLtInfty.isWeaklyProperOnU⟧; weakly proper includes a compact solution set ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.IsWeaklyProperOnU.isCompact_solutionSet⟧. For a continuous $f$, proper gives weakly proper by §V.4 ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.IsProper.isWeaklyProperOnU⟧, and proper$_{<\infty}$ gives weakly proper$_{<\infty}$ ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.IsProperLtInfty.isWeaklyProperLtInfty⟧: let $N(s) \le C$ on $U$. A solution $x$ of $f = s$ lies in $U$ — otherwise $s(x) = 0$, so $x \in f^{-1}(0) \subseteq U$ — and there $N(f(x)) = N(s(x)) \le \max(C, 1)$; so $\{f = s\}$, closed because $f$ and $s$ are continuous, lies in the compact $\operatorname{cl}\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le \max(C, 1)\}$ ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.AuxLe.mono⟧. The text's remark that the notions differ for general sc-smooth sections is not formalized.

**Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5), 2021 form** ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · theorem_5_2_2⟧. *Statement.* An sc-Fredholm section with compact solution set is proper$_{<\infty}$. *Proof.* As for §V.6 ⟦Chapter5/Compactness · theorem_5_2_2_preprint⟧. At a zero $x$, the local step gives a chart $c$, an open $V \ni x$ and for every bound $b$ a compact set containing the closure of the points of $V$ whose fibre part has level-$1$ norm $\le b$ ⟦Chapter5/Compactness · exists_nbhd_isCompact_closure_bdd⟧; near $x$ the chart norm is at most $A \cdot N$ ⟦Chapter5/AuxNorm · StrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.exists_norm_liftOne_le⟧. So on a smaller $V$ the closure of $\{N(f) \le C\}$ lies in the compact set for $b = A \cdot C$, and $V$ does not depend on $C$. Finitely many such $V$ cover $f^{-1}(0)$, and the closure of the finite union lies in the finite union of the compact closures. $\square$ The text's first display writes $N(f(x)) \le d$ for the points $z$ of the set, presumably meant as $N(f(z)) \le d$; the later display has $y$ throughout. *The five properties are equivalent* for sc-Fredholm sections ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · theorem_5_2_2_tfae⟧: the cycle (5) ⇒ (3) ⇒ (2) ⇒ (1) ⇒ (5) and (5) ⇒ (4) ⇒ (2), with $f$ continuous because it is sc-smooth.

**Theorem 5.3.5 (preprint 5.13), 2021 form** ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · theorem_5_3_5⟧. *Statement.* The conclusions of §V.15 ⟦Chapter5/Transversality · theorem_5_3_5_preprint⟧, and moreover $S_{f+s}$ is a compact sub-M-polyfold for the transversal perturbations $s$. *Proof.* `theorem_5_3_5_preprint` gives $S_{f+s}$ compact and, if non-empty, a manifold, a sub-M-polyfold in particular; the empty set is a sub-M-polyfold ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · isSubMPolyfold_solutionSet_of_manifold⟧. $\square$ The perturbations are the allowable sections, bounded by $N(s) \le 1$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · StrongBundle.allowableSections⟧; the printed "$N(f(x)) \le 1$ for all $x$" is read as $N(s(x)) \le 1$, presumably what is meant, as in §V.15.

**Definition 5.3.13 (preprint 5.20), 2021 form** ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.IsSubmersiveGenCompactHomotopy⟧. *Statement.* $X$ tame; $f$ an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data and compact solution set; $t : X \to \mathbb R$ sc-smooth with values in $[0, 1]$; for $i = 0, 1$ the end $t^{-1}(i)$ a sub-M-polyfold with tame induced structure over which the restriction of $f$ to the pull-back bundle has tame germ data ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.IsCompactFredholmRestriction⟧ ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · restrictSection⟧; and (3) $dt(x)$ onto at every smooth $x$. Since $T_xX$ has no linear structure in the project, (3) is read in a chart $\varphi$ around $x$ with a retraction $R$ onto its model and the level-$1$ point $z$ over $\varphi(x)$: every $a \in \mathbb R$ is the derivative of $t \circ \varphi^{-1} \circ R$ at $z$ on some $DR(z)v \in T_zO$ ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · MPolyfold.HasSurjDerivAt⟧. *Relation to §V.23.* The data of the earlier reading ⟦Chapter5/Homotopy · StrongBundle.IsGenCompactHomotopy⟧ together with (3) give the new data ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.IsGenCompactHomotopy.isSubmersiveGenCompactHomotopy⟧ ($t$ onto $[0, 1]$ gives values in $[0, 1]$, and the fibre conditions at $\tau = 0, 1$ are the end conditions). Every fibre $t^{-1}(\tau)$ still has a compact solution set: it is closed, and the solution set of the restriction is the trace of $f^{-1}(0)$ ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.IsSubmersiveGenCompactHomotopy.isCompact_solutionSet_restrict⟧.

**A witness, and the converse.** Over an empty end the end conditions hold: $\emptyset$ is a tame sub-M-polyfold whose atlas has no charts, and every section over it is tame sc-Fredholm ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · StrongBundle.isCompactFredholmRestriction_of_eq_empty⟧ ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · isScSmoothRetractMap_of_domain_empty⟧.
