**Lemma 6.6.8 (preprint 6.33)** (V6.45) ⟦Chapter6/Propagation · IsStabKernels.push_append⟧. *Appending sc⁺-sections $\bar s_1, \dots, \bar s_d$ after $s_1, \dots, s_k$ does not change the push-forward.* The text proves it with a homotopy $\tilde F(\tau, \cdot)$ and "one verifies by a simple computation". The computation is this. For $\ell_1, \dots, \ell_d \in \ker(T \oplus (\varphi, \psi))$ whose $\psi$-coordinates are the standard basis of $\mathbb R^d$, the map $w \mapsto (w, 0) \wedge \ell_1 \wedge \dots \wedge \ell_d$ ⟦Chapter6/AddSections · wedgeExt⟧ ⟦Chapter6/AddSections · wedgeExt_wedge⟧ does not depend on the $\ell_j$ — two choices differ by vectors of the image of $\ker(T \oplus \varphi)$, the span of the first block ⟦Chapter6/AddSections · wedgeExt_congr⟧ — and is bijective ⟦Chapter6/AddSections · wedgeExt_bijective⟧. With the appended stabilization ⟦Chapter6/AddSections · appendStab⟧ and the kernel inclusion $(v, \lambda) \mapsto (v, \lambda, 0)$ ⟦Chapter6/AddSections · kerAppend⟧, *the stabilization isomorphism of $(\varphi, \psi)$ is that of $\varphi$ followed by $w \mapsto (w, 0) \wedge \ell_1 \wedge \dots \wedge \ell_d$, exactly, with no sign* ⟦Chapter6/AddSections · detEquiv_stabIota_append⟧: a choice of Proposition 6.4.15 (preprint 6.15) for $(\varphi, \psi)$ is one for $\varphi$ with the $\ell_j$ appended to the kernel basis and the standard basis vectors to the $r_i$, and with the appended sections last the matrix $(\bar c, r)$ becomes block triangular with an identity block, so the determinant in (94) is unchanged. Along a family the $\ell_j$ are chosen continuously ⟦Chapter6/AddSections · SubspaceFamily.exists_continuous_lifts⟧ — the larger kernels project onto $\mathbb R^d$ because $T \oplus \varphi$ is already onto — and the wedge extension carries continuous orientations along ⟦Chapter6/AddSections · isLineOrientation_wedgeExt⟧, through the kernel inclusion ⟦Chapter6/AddSections · kerEquivMap⟧. So the stabilized rays ⟦Chapter6/AddSections · stabRayEquiv_append⟧ and the propagations ⟦Chapter6/AddSections · propagate_append⟧ agree, and with them the push-forwards. The homotopy of the text's proof is not needed (Findings, Chapter 6, item 51) (pp. 266–271 (preprint pp. 224–225)).

**Sections over families** (V6.46). For $g$ affine, $(q, y) \mapsto S(g(q), y)$ ⟦Chapter6/FamilySections · reparamSection⟧ is again an sc⁺-section of the pull-back ⟦Chapter6/FamilySections · StrongBundle.IsScPlusSection.reparam⟧, through the sc-smooth product map $g \times 1$ ⟦Chapter6/FamilySections · rnProdMapOp⟧, with the expected slices ⟦Chapter6/FamilySections · pullbackSlice_reparamSection⟧. Sc⁺-sections may be checked in one chart around each point ⟦Chapter6/FamilySections · StrongBundle.isScPlusSection_of_local⟧. Adding sections keeps the general position of $F$ at $(0, y)$ ⟦Chapter6/FamilySections · StrongBundle.isGeneralPositionGerm_paramSection_of_comp⟧: the linearization only gains columns, and the properties of Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17) survive. These are the sections $s(y, \tau, t)$ over a square and the text's "adding more sections, the properties will still hold" (pp. 266–272 (preprint pp. 224–226)).

### VI.17 Lemma 6.6.10 (preprint 6.34) and Proposition 6.6.7 (preprint 6.32)

**Lemma 6.6.10 (preprint 6.34)** (V6.47) ⟦Chapter6/Propagation · IsStabKernels.push_square⟧. *For a family of stabilized kernels over the square $[0, 1]^2$ with the end points $x_0$, $x_1$ fixed and the end-point operators varying continuously, the push-forwards along the edges $\tau = 0$ and $\tau = 1$ agree.* The edges are the restrictions to affine segments of the square ⟦Chapter6/PropagationWellDefined · sqEdge⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PropagationWellDefined · sqPath⟧. On the edge $t = 0$ the point is $x_0$ and the operators vary continuously, so by §VI.14 continuation along it carries $\mathrm{orRay}_{(0,0)}(o)$ to $\mathrm{orRay}_{(1,0)}(o)$; the same on $t = 1$. The square is simply connected, so continuation from $(0, 0)$ to $(1, 1)$ is the same through $(0, 1)$ and through $(1, 0)$. Writing both push-forwards as $\mathrm{orRay}^{-1} \circ \mathrm{cont} \circ \mathrm{orRay}$ gives the claim. The text's convex homotopy $s^\tau$ is part of the square of Proposition 6.6.7 (preprint 6.32) below, and the continuity of the end-point orientations along $\tau$ is that of §VI.14, with the sign (preprint p. 226).

**Proposition 6.6.7 (preprint 6.32)** (V6.44) ⟦Chapter6/PropagationWellDefined · proposition_6_6_7⟧. *Two push-forwards along the same sc-smooth path in the domain of a chart agree.* Let the data be $(S^0; s^0_1, \dots, s^0_{k^0})$ and $(S^1; s^1_1, \dots, s^1_{k^1})$. The text combines Lemma 6.6.8 (preprint 6.33) (more sections) and Lemma 6.6.10 (preprint 6.34) (a homotopy of the data); the formalization does both over one square (Findings, Chapter 6, item 52). *Step 1, the square.* $\Phi(\tau, t) = \gamma(t)$, constant in $\tau$, and $S^\tau = (1 - \tau)S^0 + \tau S^1$, a section of the pull-back over $\mathbb R^2 \times X$ by §VI.16; $f + S^\tau$ vanishes along $\Phi$ since both $f + S^0$ and $f + S^1$ do and the fibres are linear ⟦Chapter6/PropagationWellDefined · isZeroAt_sectionAdd_combo⟧. *Step 2, the sections.* With $\hat s^i_j = s^i_j$ for $j < k^i$ and $0$ otherwise, the sections $(1 - \tau)\hat s^0_j + \tau\hat s^1_j$, followed by the sections that Lemma 6.6.4 (preprint 6.29) gives on the square. The parametrized section is in general position along the square — adding sections keeps it (§VI.16) — so the stabilized kernels exist over $[0, 1]^2$ (§VI.15). *Step 3, the edges $\tau = 0, 1$.* At $\tau = 0$ the sections $s^0$ are the first $k^0$ of the family and at $\tau = 1$ the sections $s^1$ are the first $k^1$, so Lemma 6.6.8 (preprint 6.33) compares each datum with the edge of the square without reordering ⟦Chapter6/PropagationWellDefined · IsStabKernels.push_eq_of_prefix⟧, the edges being data of the same kind ⟦Chapter6/PropagationWellDefined · IsStabKernels.congr_data⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PropagationWellDefined · IsStabKernels.push_congr_data⟧. *Step 4, the edges $t = 0, 1$.* There the point is fixed and the operators are affine in $\tau$ ⟦Chapter6/PropagationWellDefined · linAt_principal_combo⟧, hence continuous ⟦Chapter6/PropagationWellDefined · continuous_principal_pullbackSlice⟧. *Step 5.* Lemma 6.6.10 (preprint 6.34) equates the push-forwards along the edges $\tau = 0$ and $\tau = 1$, and Step 3 identifies them with the two given ones. *Hidden hypotheses:* the standing ones of §6.6 (preprint §6.5) ($X$ tame, bump functions, tame germ data). "Does not depend on the choices" is read as the agreement of any two data (pp. 266–272 (preprint pp. 224–226)).

### VI.18 Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35), and paths in a chart

**Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35)** (V6.48). $U$ has the *local propagation property* in a chart $c$ ⟦Chapter6/PropagationWellDefined · HasLocalPropagation⟧ if $U$ lies in the domain of $c$, along every sc-smooth path in $U$ there is a push-forward, and any two push-forwards along paths in $U$ with the same end points agree. ⟦Chapter6/PropagationWellDefined · theorem_6_6_11⟧: *over a tame $X$ with bump functions, for $f$ with tame germ data, every smooth point $x$ has an open $U \ni x$ and a chart $c$ with the local propagation property.* The statement names the bundle and the point but not the section (possible omission); it is read for an sc-Fredholm section with tame germ data (Findings, Chapter 6, item 53). *Step 1.* $U \subseteq W$ and $c$ from Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28); push-forwards exist along paths in $W$, a fortiori in $U$, by (3) (§VI.15). *Step 2, homotopy invariance* ⟦Chapter6/PropagationWellDefined · push_eq_of_homotopy⟧. For an sc-smooth $\Phi : \mathbb R^2 \to X$ with $\Phi([0, 1]^2) \subseteq W$ and the end points fixed, (3) for $n = 2$ gives $S$, Lemma 6.6.4 (preprint 6.29) gives sections, and the stabilized kernels exist over the square. The edge $t \mapsto (\tau, t)$ is an affine map, so the restriction to it is a push-forward datum along $\Phi(\tau, \cdot)$ (§§VI.14–VI.15). Along $t = 0, 1$ the point is constant and so is the section $S(q, \cdot)$, because it depends on $q$ only through $\Phi(q)$; the end-point operators are then constant, and Lemma 6.6.10 (preprint 6.34) applies. With Proposition 6.6.7 (preprint 6.32), any push-forward along $\Phi(0, \cdot)$ equals any along $\Phi(1, \cdot)$. *Step 3, the reparametrization.* The homotopy of (1′) is $\gamma_0$ and $\gamma_1$ at its edges only for $t \in [0, 1]$, while a push-forward datum asks for zeros of $f + S$ for $t$ near $[0, 1]$. The proof therefore passes through $\gamma_i \circ \kappa$, which maps all of $\mathbb R$ into $\gamma_i([0, 1])$, with three homotopies whose edges are exact for all $t$: $H(\sigma, t) = \gamma_0((1 - \sigma)t + \sigma\kappa(t))$ from $\gamma_0$ to $\gamma_0 \circ \kappa$; the homotopy $(\tau, t) \mapsto \Phi(\tau, \kappa(t))$ from $\gamma_0 \circ \kappa$ to $\gamma_1 \circ \kappa$; and the analogue of $H$ for $\gamma_1$. Step 2 applied three times gives the agreement. $U$ is not shown to be sc-smoothly contractible (gap G.61); what the proof uses is (1′) (pp. 271–273 (preprint pp. 226–227)). For paths on the M-polyfold $[0, 1]$ the theorem is §VI.37.

**Paths in a chart** (V6.49). Sc-smooth maps that agree near every point of a set are sc-smooth together ⟦Chapter6/ScPaths · MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_of_eventuallyEq⟧; $C^\infty$ maps of the parameter compose ⟦Chapter6/ScPaths · pt1_apply⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ScPaths · contDiff_pt1_comp⟧. *For an open $U$ in the domain of a chart and $x \in U$ there is an open $V \ni x$ in $U$ whose smooth points are pairwise joined by sc-smooth paths in $U$* ⟦Chapter6/ScPaths · exists_nhds_scPath⟧: in the chart, $t \mapsto \varphi^{-1}(r(u_1 + \kappa(t)(u_2 - u_1)))$, for $u_1, u_2$ in a small ball around $\varphi(x)$, as in (1′). The concatenation ⟦Chapter6/ScPaths · concatPath⟧ is $\gamma_1(\kappa(3s))$ for $s \le 1/2$ and $\gamma_2(\kappa(3s - 2))$ for $s > 1/2$ ⟦Chapter6/ScPaths · concatPath_of_le⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ScPaths · concatPath_of_gt⟧. It is constant on $[1/3, 2/3]$, with value $\gamma_1(1) = \gamma_2(0)$, so the two pieces glue sc-smoothly ⟦Chapter6/ScPaths · isScSmoothMap_concatPath⟧; it has the right end points ⟦Chapter6/ScPaths · concatPath_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ScPaths · concatPath_one⟧ and halves ⟦Chapter6/ScPaths · concatPath_half₁⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ScPaths · concatPath_half₂⟧. Reparametrizing by a $C^\infty$ map keeps sc-smoothness ⟦Chapter6/ScPaths · isScSmoothMap_reparam⟧, and push-forwards compose along concatenations ⟦Chapter6/ContinuousOrientation · HasLocalPropagation.eq_trans⟧. Paths are joined here locally, inside a chart; the global facts recalled on preprint p. 201 are §VI.37 (gap G.56 closed) (pp. 272–274 (preprint pp. 227–228)).

### VI.19 Definition 6.6.12 (preprint 6.36): orientable neighbourhoods and continuous orientations

**Definition 6.6.12 (preprint 6.36)** (V6.50). The text: an orientable neighbourhood of $(f, x)$ is an open, sc-smoothly contractible $U$ with the local propagation property, and a continuous orientation over it is a choice $y \mapsto o_y$ carried into itself by the propagation. Since Proposition 6.6.3 (preprint 6.28) gives (1′), an orientable neighbourhood is a pair $V \subseteq U$ ⟦Chapter6/SectionOrientation · IsOrientableNbhd⟧: $U$ open with the local propagation property in a chart, $V \ni x$ open with any two smooth points joined by an sc-smooth path in $U$. A *continuous orientation* is a choice $y \mapsto o_y$ on $V_\infty$, read in the chart, carried into itself by the push-forwards along the paths in $U$ ⟦Chapter6/ContinuousOrientation · IsContinuousOrientation⟧. *There are exactly two* ⟦Chapter6/ContinuousOrientation · exists_two_isContinuousOrientation⟧: given $o_x$, set $o_y$ to be the push-forward of $o_x$ along any path in $U$ from $x$ to $y$, well defined by the local propagation property; push-forwards compose along concatenations, so this is a continuous orientation; the two values of $o_x$ give two different ones; and a continuous orientation is determined by its value at $x$. *Every smooth point has an orientable neighbourhood* ⟦Chapter6/ContinuousOrientation · exists_orientableNbhd⟧ ⟦Chapter6/SectionOrientation · exists_isOrientableNbhd⟧, by Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35) and §VI.18. *Hidden hypotheses:* the standing ones of §6.6 (preprint §6.5) (Findings, Chapter 6, item 54) (preprint p. 227).

### VI.20 The path category $PX$

**Reparametrization homotopies** (V6.51). The values of an sc-smooth path at parameters are smooth points ⟦Chapter6/ScHomotopy · mem_smoothSet_of_isScSmoothMap⟧, and $C^\infty$ maps of $\mathbb R^2$ compose ⟦Chapter6/ScHomotopy · contDiff_pt2_comp⟧. *For a $C^\infty$ $\theta$ with $\theta(0) = 0$, $\theta(1) = 1$, $\gamma \circ \theta$ is sc-smoothly homotopic to $\gamma$ with the end points fixed* ⟦Chapter6/ScHomotopy · isScHomotopyRel_reparam⟧, by $H(\tau, t) = \gamma((1 - \tau)t + \tau\theta(t))$, and inside every set containing $\gamma([0, 1])$ when $\theta([0, 1]) \subseteq [0, 1]$ ⟦Chapter6/ScHomotopy · reparam_mem⟧. With the halves of a path ⟦Chapter6/ScHomotopy · leftHalf⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ScHomotopy · rightHalf⟧, the concatenation of the two halves of $\gamma$ is such a reparametrization ⟦Chapter6/ScHomotopy · halvesReparam⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ScHomotopy · concatPath_halves⟧ (preprint p. 228).

**The category** (V6.52). The tools are the value $\kappa(1/2)$ ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · smoothTransition_half⟧, constant maps at smooth points ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · isScSmoothMap_const_of_mem_smoothSet⟧, maps defined by cases on closed pieces that agree near the seams ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · isScSmoothMap_ite⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · isScSmoothMap_ite₃⟧ and the middle third of a concatenation ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · concatPath_of_le_two_thirds⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · concatPath_of_one_third_le⟧. Sc-smooth homotopy with the end points fixed ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScHomotopic⟧ is an equivalence relation on the sc-smooth paths from $x$ to $y$ ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScHomotopic.refl⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScHomotopic.symm⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScHomotopic.trans⟧. Transitivity needs care: a homotopy meets its edge conditions only on $[0, 1]$ (decision D2), and two homotopies glued in $\tau$ need not agree off $[0, 1]$, so all paths and homotopies are first reparametrized by $\kappa$ in $t$ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 71). The paths with smooth end points ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScPath⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScPath.source_mem_smoothSet⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScPath.target_mem_smoothSet⟧ have the constant paths ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScPath.const⟧, concatenation ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScPath.concat⟧ and reversal ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScPath.reverse⟧. Concatenation is well defined on classes ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScPath.concat_congr⟧, has the constant paths as units ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScPath.const_concat⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScPath.concat_const⟧, is associative ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScPath.concat_assoc⟧ — the two bracketings differ by an explicit reparametrization ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · assocReparam⟧, joined by a three-piece homotopy ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · isScHomotopyRel_triHomotopy⟧ — and the reversed paths are inverses ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScPath.concat_reverse⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScPath.reverse_concat⟧. The classes ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScPathClass⟧ with their composition ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · ScPathClass.comp⟧ make the smooth points a category $PX$ ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · PathCat⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · PathCat.category⟧, indeed a groupoid ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · PathCat.groupoid⟧, with the morphism of a path ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · PathCat.homMk⟧, composition and identities on representatives ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · PathCat.comp_mk⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · PathCat.id_eq_mk⟧, equality of morphisms as homotopy ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · PathCat.mk_eq_mk_iff⟧, every morphism represented ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · PathCat.exists_eq_mk⟧ and inverses by reversal ⟦Chapter6/PathCategory · PathCat.inv_mk⟧. The text does not name the identities; they are the classes of the constant paths. The second piece $\psi(\beta(s))$ of the composition on preprint p. 228 leaves $[0, 1]$, since $\beta([1/2, 1]) = [1, 2]$; it is read as $\psi(\beta(s) - 1)$ (possible misprint; Findings, Chapter 6, item 55). Mathlib's $[\varphi] \gg [\psi]$ is the text's $[\psi] * [\varphi]$ (pp. 272–274 (preprint pp. 227–228)). The category with paths on $[0, 1]$, as printed, is equivalent to this one (§VI.37).

### VI.21 Comparing charts: the transfer, and $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ in a chosen chart

The proof of Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37) carries an orientation along orientable neighbourhoods of different points of a path, which may lie in different charts. The text takes $T_xX$, $Y_x$, $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ and $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ to be the same whichever chart is used (preprint p. 219); here they are made at chart points (§VI.1), so the charts have to be compared (Findings, Chapter 6, item 70).

**Conjugation of determinants** (V6.53). For isomorphisms $A$, $\Gamma$ with $S'A = \Gamma S$, $A$ maps $\ker S$ onto $\ker S'$ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · conjKerEquiv⟧ and $\Gamma$ induces $\operatorname{coker}S \cong \operatorname{coker}S'$ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · conjCokerEquiv⟧; together they give $\det(S) \cong \det(S')$ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · conjDet⟧, on wedges $(a \wedge \dots) \otimes (d \wedge \dots)^* \mapsto (Aa \wedge \dots) \otimes ([\Gamma d] \wedge \dots)^*$ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · conjDet_wedge_tmul⟧, compatible with composition, equal data and the identity ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · conjDet_trans⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · conjDet_congr⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · conjDet_refl⟧. Good left-projections are conjugated, $\Gamma P\Gamma^{-1} \in \Pi_{S'}$ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · IsGoodLeftProj.conj⟧, and the $\gamma^P$ commute with the conjugation ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · gammaProj_conjDet⟧; read in local determinant charts the conjugation has a continuous nowhere-zero coordinate ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · coord_conjDet_coordInv⟧, so continuous orientations of $\mathrm{DET}$ are carried along ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · isLineOrientation_conj⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · LineOrientation.conj⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · LineOrientation.conj_apply⟧, with the same rules ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · LineOrientation.conj_refl⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · LineOrientation.conj_trans⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · LineOrientation.conj_congr⟧.

**The transfer between two chart points** (V6.53). For chart points $p$, $p'$ of $x$, $A$ is the derivative at $z$ of the transition of the base charts ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.baseDeriv⟧, with the cocycle rules ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.baseDeriv_self⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.baseDeriv_trans⟧, an sc-operator ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.isScOperator_baseDeriv⟧; $\Gamma$ is the fibre part of the transition of the strong bundle charts ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.fiberMap⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.fiberMap_self⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.fiberMap_trans⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.isScOperator_fiberMap⟧. They restrict to isomorphisms $T_zO \cong T_{z'}O'$ and $K_z \cong K_{z'}$ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.transferT⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.transferK⟧, again with the cocycle rules ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.transferT_self_apply⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.transferT_trans_apply⟧. At a zero the linearizations in the two charts are related by them, the chain rule applied to the principal parts ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.scDeriv_principal_baseDeriv⟧, and sc⁺-operators conjugate to sc⁺-operators ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.IsScPlusOp.conj⟧; so $L \in \mathrm{Lin}_p(f, x)$ iff $\Gamma LA^{-1} \in \mathrm{Lin}_{p'}(f, x)$ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.mem_linSet_transfer_iff⟧. Conjugation of orientations over this bijection of the bases is the transfer $\mathrm{Or}^f_x(p) \cong \mathrm{Or}^f_x(p')$ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.orTransfer⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.orTransfer_apply⟧, with the cocycle rules ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.orTransfer_self⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ChartTransfer · ChartPoint.orTransfer_trans⟧.

**The push-forward does not depend on the chart** (V6.54). The sign is invariant, conjugation preserving $\dim\operatorname{coker}$ ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · stabSign_conj⟧; the stabilization is natural — $(\Gamma S A^{-1}) \oplus \Gamma\varphi$ is the conjugate of $S \oplus \varphi$, with the conjugated kernel, onto iff $S \oplus \varphi$ is ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · coprod_conj⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · ker_coprod_conj⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · surjective_coprod_conj⟧ — and so is its isomorphism on rays ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · conj_stab_key⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · stabRayEquiv_conjDet⟧; continuation is natural under jointly continuous families of injective linear maps ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · SubspaceFamily.cont_map⟧. The principal parts of the sections transform by $\Gamma$ ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · ChartPoint.fiberMap_principal⟧, so the operators $T$ and $\varphi$ of a datum in one chart are the conjugates of those in the other ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · ChartPoint.conj_of_linAt⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · ChartPoint.conj_of_principal⟧, and $A$ varies continuously along a path ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · continuous_baseDeriv⟧. A family of stabilized kernels in one chart is therefore carried by $A \times 1$ to one in the second chart, with the same sections ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · IsStabKernels.exists_transfer⟧, the rays read from an orientation corresponding under the transfer ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · IsStabKernels.orRay_transfer⟧; a push-forward in one chart, conjugated by the transfers at the end points, is a push-forward in the other ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · IsPush.transfer⟧, and the local propagations of two charts agree ⟦Chapter6/PushTransfer · HasLocalPropagation.push_compat⟧. The text does not compare charts (pp. 264–274 (preprint pp. 222–228)).

**$\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ in a chosen chart** (V6.55). A chart of the atlas at $x$ is chosen for every $x$ ⟦Chapter6/SectionOrientation · orChart⟧ ⟦Chapter6/SectionOrientation · isChart_orChart⟧ ⟦Chapter6/SectionOrientation · mem_orChart⟧, and $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ is the set of the orientations read there ⟦Chapter6/SectionOrientation · Orx⟧, with two elements ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · exists_two_orx⟧. It is identified with the orientations read in any other chart at $x$ by the transfer ⟦Chapter6/SectionOrientation · toChartOr⟧ ⟦Chapter6/SectionOrientation · toChartOr_orChart⟧, compatibly with composition ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · toChartOr_trans⟧, and a map $y \mapsto o_y$ is read in the chart of an orientable neighbourhood through it ⟦Chapter6/SectionOrientation · restrictOr⟧. A chosen chart stands for the text's chart-free $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ (preprint pp. 220, 228).

### VI.22 Transport along paths from local push-forwards

The proof of Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37) (p. 273 (preprint p. 228)): for a path $\varphi$, "using the compactness of $[0, 1]$ and a finite covering" by orientable neighbourhoods, $\varphi_*$ is the composite of the local propagations; "by a covering argument" it depends only on $[\varphi]$; and "it is obvious that $\Gamma_f$ is unique". The formalization separates this argument from orientations: it is proved for any family of types over $X_\infty$ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 72).

**Local transport data** (V6.56) ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport⟧: a family of *good* open sets covering $X_\infty$, all fibres in bijection, and for every good set $U$ a push-forward along every sc-smooth path in $U$, such that push-forwards in one good set compose and do not depend on the good set containing the path. Then the push-forward along a loop in a good set is the identity ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.push_eq_refl⟧, in a good set it depends only on the end points ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.push_eq_push⟧, and only on the path on $[0, 1]$ ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.push_congr⟧.

**The dyadic transport.** At level $0$ it is the push-forward in a chosen good set containing $\gamma([0, 1])$ (an arbitrary bijection if there is none); at level $n + 1$ it is the composite of the transports at level $n$ along the two halves ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.transportN⟧. On a path in a good set every level gives the push-forward ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.transportN_eq_push⟧, by the composition rule. The pieces of level $N$ lie in good sets ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.IsFine⟧ for some $N$: the preimages of the good sets cover the compact $[0, 1]$, so there is a Lebesgue number $\delta$ ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.IsLebesgueNumber⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.exists_isLebesgueNumber⟧, and $2^N\delta > 1$ suffices ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.isFine_of_isLebesgueNumber⟧. From such an $N$ on the levels agree ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.transportN_eq_of_isFine⟧, since at the next level each piece is split inside its good set. The *transport* is the value at such a level ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.transport⟧.

**Its properties.** It is the push-forward on a path in a good set ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.transport_eq_push⟧ — property (∗) — depends only on the path on $[0, 1]$ ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.transport_congr⟧, is the identity on paths constant on $[0, 1]$ ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.transport_const⟧, and is the composite along the two halves ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.transport_halves⟧. *Homotopy invariance* ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.transport_eq_of_isScHomotopyRel⟧ is the covering argument. For a homotopy $\Phi : \mathbb R^2 \to X$ the preimages of the good sets cover $[0, 1]^2$, with a Lebesgue number $\delta$ ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.exists_isSqLebesgueNumber⟧. *The square lemma* ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.transportN_square⟧: for a rectangle of $[0, 1]^2$ with sides $< 2^n\delta$, the transports at level $n$ along its vertical, horizontal and diagonal segments ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · vSeg⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · hSeg⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · dSeg⟧ commute around its boundary — left side then top equals bottom then right side. By induction on $n$: for $n = 0$ the rectangle lies in one good set, and both composites are the push-forward along the diagonal; for $n + 1$ the rectangle is cut into four quadrants and the four commutative squares are pasted, the interior edges cancelling ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · equiv_paste_squares⟧. Applied to $[0, 1]^2$ at a level with $2^n\delta > 1$, with the sides $\tau \mapsto \Phi(\tau, 0)$, $\tau \mapsto \Phi(\tau, 1)$ constant on $[0, 1]$ and of trivial transport, it gives the invariance. The transport is invariant under reparametrization ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.transport_reparam⟧ (§VI.20) and takes concatenations to composites ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.transport_concatPath⟧, the halves of a concatenation being reparametrizations of the two paths. *Uniqueness* ⟦Chapter6/PathTransport · LocalTransport.transport_unique⟧: a family of bijections along the sc-smooth paths that is homotopy invariant, takes concatenations to composites and is the push-forward on paths in good sets, is the transport — $G(\gamma) = G(\text{left half}) \circ G(\text{right half})$ through the reparametrization, and induction on the dyadic level. Dyadic subdivisions of $[0, 1]$ and of $[0, 1]^2$ stand in place of arbitrary finite coverings (preprint p. 228).

### VI.23 Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37): the functor $\Gamma_f$

The text: *for a strong bundle over a tame M-polyfold and an sc-Fredholm section $f$ there is a uniquely determined functor $\Gamma_f : PX \to \mathcal O_f$, $x \mapsto \mathrm{Or}^f_x$, with (∗): for every smooth $x$, every sc-smoothly contractible open $U \ni x$ on which $f$ has the local propagation property, and every sc-smooth path $\varphi : [0, 1] \to U$, the propagation $\varphi_*$ and $\Gamma_f([\varphi])$ coincide.*

**The local data of $f$** (V6.57). $U$ is a propagation neighbourhood if it is open with the local propagation property in some chart ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · IsPropagationNbhd⟧. Along a path in such a $U$ the push-forward, read in the chosen charts of the end points through the transfer (§VI.21), is $\mathrm{orPush}$ ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · orPush⟧; it equals every push-forward along the path in every chart in which the path lies in a set with the local propagation property ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · orPush_eq⟧ — by the chart independence of §VI.21 and the cocycle rule of the transfer — it does not depend on the neighbourhood ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · orPush_compat⟧, and it composes ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · orPush_trans⟧. With Theorem 6.6.11 (preprint 6.35), which makes the propagation neighbourhoods cover $X_\infty$, and §VI.9, which puts every $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ in bijection with every other, these are local transport data ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · orLocalTransport⟧, and their transport satisfies (∗) ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · orLocalTransport_transport_eq⟧.

**The functor.** $\Gamma_f([\varphi])$ is the transport along $\varphi$, well defined on classes by homotopy invariance ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · orFunctorMap⟧ ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · orFunctorMap_mk⟧; it takes identities to identities ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · orFunctorMap_id⟧ and compositions to composites ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · orFunctorMap_comp⟧, by the constancy and concatenation rules of §VI.22; and it is a functor $PX \to \mathrm{Type}$ ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · orFunctor⟧. Property (∗) for a family $G$ on the morphisms of $PX$, on the members of a family of open sets ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · IsStarPropertyOn⟧ and on all of them ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · IsStarProperty⟧, reads $G([\varphi]) = \mathrm{toChartOr}^{-1}_{\varphi(1)} \circ e \circ \mathrm{toChartOr}_{\varphi(0)}$ for every chart $c$, every open $U$ with the local propagation property in $c$, every sc-smooth path $\varphi$ in $U$ with smooth end points and every push-forward $e$ along $\varphi$ in $c$. $\Gamma_f$ has it ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · orFunctorMap_isStarProperty⟧, so the property is satisfiable. *Uniqueness*: a family with the rules for identities and composites and with (∗) on the members of a family of such open sets covering $X_\infty$ is $\Gamma_f$ ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · orFunctorMap_unique_of_cover⟧ — restrict the local data to the cover ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · LocalTransport.restrict⟧ and apply the uniqueness of the transport — in particular with (∗) everywhere ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · orFunctorMap_unique⟧.

**Theorem 6.6.13 (preprint 6.37)** ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · theorem_6_6_13_hyp⟧. *Over a tame $X$ with bump functions, for $f$ with tame germ data and $P$ with sc⁺-sections through the smooth fibre points, there is exactly one family of bijections $\Gamma_f([\varphi]) : \mathrm{Or}^f_x \to \mathrm{Or}^f_y$ on the morphisms of $PX$ taking identities to identities and compositions to composites, with property (∗).* *Hidden hypotheses:* the standing ones of §6.6 (preprint §6.5), and sc⁺-sections through every smooth fibre point, so that every $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ has two elements (bump functions give them). (∗) is asked for every open set with the local propagation property, not only for sc-smoothly contractible ones (the preprint's (1), §VI.10), and the uniqueness needs it only on a covering family — for instance on the sc-smoothly contractible ones, wherever they cover $X_\infty$. $\mathcal O_f$ is read as types and bijections, and "uniquely determined" for the maps on morphisms: on objects there is no choice (preprint p. 228). With the text's hypotheses only — $X$ tame with bump functions, $f$ with tame germ data — the sc⁺-sections through the smooth fibre points come from the bump functions (§VI.1) and the paracompactness of $\mathbb R^n \times X$ and of the pull-backs is proved, so the theorem holds without the further hypothesis ⟦Chapter6/OrientationMainClean · theorem_6_6_13⟧ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 122).

### VI.24 Definitions 6.6.14–6.6.16 (preprint 6.38–6.40): orientability and orientations

**Definition 6.6.14 (preprint 6.38)** (V6.58). *$f$ is orientable if for every pair of smooth points $x$, $y$ in the same path component, $\Gamma_f([\varphi])$ does not depend on the class $[\varphi] : x \to y$* ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · IsOrientableSection⟧. "In the same path component" is read as "joined by an sc-smooth path" ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · scPathSetoid⟧; for points not so joined there is nothing to check (Findings, Chapter 6, item 73). The reading is justified in §VI.37: for smooth points, one connected component, one path component and one sc-smooth path component are the same. *Equivalently there is $y \mapsto o_y$ with $\Gamma_f([\varphi])o_x = o_y$ for every $[\varphi] : x \to y$* ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · isOrientableSection_iff_exists⟧: from left to right, choose a base point in each class of points joined by sc-smooth paths and set $o_y = \Gamma_f([\varphi])o_{\text{base}}$ for any $[\varphi]$, which does not depend on $[\varphi]$; from right to left, $\Gamma_f([\varphi])$ and $\Gamma_f([\psi])$ are bijections between two-element sets with the same value at $o_x$, hence equal (§VI.9) (preprint p. 229).

**Definition 6.6.15 (preprint 6.39)** (V6.59). *$f$ is orientable if there is $y \mapsto o_y$ on $X_\infty$ such that every smooth point has an orientable neighbourhood over which it is one of the two continuous orientations* ⟦Chapter6/SectionOrientation · IsOrientableSection'⟧. The definition writes "$y \in U_\infty$" before any $U$ is introduced; it is read as $y \in X_\infty$ (possible misprint; Findings, Chapter 6, item 74). *This holds iff there is $y \mapsto o_y$ with $\Gamma_f([\varphi])o_x = o_y$ for all $[\varphi]$* ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · isOrientableSection'_iff_exists⟧. From right to left: on an orientable neighbourhood $V \subseteq U$ the push-forwards along paths in $U$ are values of $\Gamma_f$, by (∗), so the restriction is a continuous orientation. From left to right: elements carried into each other by the transport along the paths in the members of an open covering are carried into each other along every path ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · LocalTransport.transport_apply_eq_of_local⟧ — the transport is computed on dyadic pieces inside orientable neighbourhoods. *So Definitions 6.6.14 and 6.6.15 (preprint 6.38 and 6.39) are equivalent* ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · isOrientableSection_iff⟧. The text calls them equivalent without proof (Findings, Chapter 6, item 73) (preprint p. 229).

**Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40)** (V6.60). *An orientation of $f$ is a map $y \mapsto o_y$ on $X_\infty$ whose restriction to every orientable neighbourhood of every smooth point is a continuous orientation* ⟦Chapter6/SectionOrientation · IsSectionOrientation⟧. Equivalently $\Gamma_f([\varphi])o_x = o_y$ for all $[\varphi] : x \to y$ ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · isSectionOrientation_iff⟧, by the argument of Definition 6.6.15 (preprint 6.39); so $f$ has an orientation iff it is orientable ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · exists_isSectionOrientation_iff⟧, two orientations that agree at a point agree on the smooth points joined to it by sc-smooth paths ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · IsSectionOrientation.apply_eq_iff⟧, and there are exactly two on each such class ⟦Chapter6/OrientationFunctor · IsSectionOrientation.exists_two⟧. An orientable neighbourhood is the pair of §VI.19 (Findings, Chapter 6, item 75) (preprint p. 229).

### VI.25 Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41): the natural orientation of the solution set

The text: *over a tame $X$, let $f$ be a proper sc-Fredholm section in general position to the boundary at every zero, and $o^f$ an orientation of $f$; then $S = f^{-1}(0)$ is a smooth compact manifold with boundary with corners with a natural orientation.* The proof: $S$ is such a manifold "from the transversality discussion"; $\ker f'(x) = T_xS$ and, $f'(x)$ being onto, $T_xS$ is oriented by $o^f_x$; and "one verifies that the differential geometric local prolongation of the orientation on $S$ is the same as the Fredholm one".

**The first assertion** (V6.61) ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · theorem_6_6_18_solutionSet⟧. *For $X$ tame and a proper $f$ with tame germ data in general position (Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17)) at every zero, $S$ is compact, a smooth submanifold in general position with the induced structure of a tame manifold with boundary with corners* — the conclusions of Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) (§V.20), with good position from general position by Lemma 4.2.8 (preprint 4.19) (§IV.14) ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · MPolyfold.IsGeneralPositionAt.isGoodPositionAt⟧. In a chart, $T_xS = \ker f'(x)$ ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · tangentSpace_solutionSet_eq_linKer⟧ (§V.17). "Proper" is the text's hypothesis; the proof uses only the compactness of $S$, which for sc-Fredholm sections is equivalent to it (Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5), §V.6), so nothing of the hypothesis is lost (Findings, Chapter 6, item 90).

**The tangent orientation.** At a zero, $f'(x)$ — the linearization of $f + s$ with $s = 0$ ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · ChartPoint.linZero⟧ — lies in $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · ChartPoint.linZero_mem_linSet⟧ and is onto ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · ChartPoint.linZero_surjective⟧, with kernel $T_xS$ in the chart ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · ChartPoint.map_ker_linZero⟧. So an element $o_x$ of $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ gives a ray of $\det f'(x) \cong \lambda(\ker f'(x)) = \lambda(T_xS)$, the *tangent orientation* ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · ChartPoint.tangentOr⟧, read in a chart at a zero ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · tangentOrAt⟧. The sign of a surjective operator is $1$ ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · stabSign_of_surjective⟧, and the stabilization by $\mathbb R^0$ of a surjective operator is $\det(T) \cong \lambda(\ker T)$ on rays ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · stabRayEquiv_zero⟧, so the tangent orientation is the stabilized ray of §VI.14 for the empty family of sections ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · ChartPoint.stabRayEquiv_eq_tangentOr⟧.

**"The local prolongation is the Fredholm one."** Along an sc-smooth path $\gamma$ of zeros in the domain of a chart, the datum $S = 0$, $k = 0$ is a family of stabilized kernels ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · isStabKernels_zero⟧, its kernels being those of $f'(\gamma_q)$ ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · SubspaceFamily.congrL⟧; they form a continuous family of subspaces, by Lemma 6.6.5 (preprint 6.30) (§VI.12) ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · exists_tangentFamily⟧ ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · tangentFamily⟧ ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · tangentFamily_L⟧, and the rays read from an orientation are the tangent orientations ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · IsStabKernels.orRay_eq_tangentOr⟧. So along a path of zeros the push-forward is continuation between tangent orientations ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · cont_tangentOr⟧, and *the tangent orientations given by an orientation of $\mathrm{DET}$ along the path form an orientation of the line bundle $\lambda(\Lambda)$* ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · isLineOrientation_tangentOr⟧. Intermediate parameters are reached by the paths $s \mapsto \gamma(t\kappa(s))$, which stay in $\gamma([0, t])$ for all $s \in \mathbb R$. For an orientation $o$ of $f$ and an sc-smooth path of zeros in an orientable neighbourhood $V \subseteq U$, the tangent orientations of $o$ along it form an orientation of $\lambda(\Lambda)$ ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · isLineOrientation_tangentOr_of_isSectionOrientation⟧, and together this is the theorem ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientation · theorem_6_6_18_hyp⟧ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 91).

**Two charts** (V6.61). The tangent orientations are read at chart points, so the text's "natural" needs that they do not depend on the chart. *For $o \in \mathrm{Or}^f_x$ at a zero with $f'(x)$ onto and two charts $c$, $c'$ at $x$, the orientation of $\ker f'(x)$ read in $c'$ is the image of the one read in $c$ under the tangent map $D(\tau \circ r)(z)$ of the transition* ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientationCharts · tangentOrAt_toChartOr⟧. The tangent map restricts to an isomorphism of the two kernels ⟦Chapter6/SolutionOrientationCharts · ChartPoint.tangentKerEquiv⟧, it conjugates the two linearizations, and the transfer of §VI.21, which is the conjugation of determinants, maps the stabilized ray for the empty family to the stabilized ray; on a surjective operator the determinant is $\lambda(\ker)$ and the conjugation is $\lambda$ of the tangent map. (Gap G.68 closed.)

**Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41) in the book's shape** ⟦Chapter6/OrientationMainClean · theorem_6_6_18⟧. *Over a tame $X$, for a proper $f$ with tame germ data in general position at every zero and an orientation $o$ of $f$ (Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40)), $S$ is a compact manifold with boundary with corners in general position with the natural orientation given by $o$* ⟦Chapter6/OrientationMainClean · IsNaturalSolutionOrientation⟧: at every zero $o_x$ orients $T_xS = \ker f'(x)$; the orientations read in two charts correspond under the tangent map of the transition; and along every sc-smooth path of zeros in an orientable neighbourhood they form an orientation of the kernel line bundle. The three clauses are the three paragraphs above.

**$S$ as an oriented manifold** (V6.61). Mathlib has manifolds with corners but no orientations of them. A *tangent orientation* of a Mathlib manifold $M$ is an orientation of every tangent space, and it is *continuous* if, read in the charts of the maximal atlas, it is locally constant ⟦Chapter6/ManifoldOrientation · TangentOrientation.IsContinuous⟧; the tangent maps of chart changes ⟦Chapter6/ManifoldOrientation · chartChangeDeriv⟧ have continuous, nowhere-zero Jacobian determinant, so this is well posed. An *oriented atlas* is a covering family of charts whose changes have positive Jacobian determinant ⟦Chapter6/ManifoldOrientation · IsOrientedAtlas⟧; a continuous tangent orientation gives one whenever the positive charts cover $M$ ⟦Chapter6/ManifoldOrientation · isOrientedAtlas_positiveCharts⟧. The solution set is a compact Mathlib manifold with corners, modelled on the quadrant of $\mathbb R^d$, $d$ the index ⟦Chapter9/MathlibSolutionSets · theorem_6_6_18_isManifold⟧, from the corner structure of Theorem 3.1.26 (Part III). *Theorem* ⟦Chapter6/SolutionSetOrientation · theorem_6_6_18_oriented⟧: *with the bump functions of §6.6 (preprint §6.5), $S$ carries a continuous tangent orientation $o_S$ which at every zero $x$, in every chart $c$ of $X$ at $x$, is $o_x$: the tangent map $\iota$ of $S \hookrightarrow X$ at $x$ is an isomorphism $T_xS \cong \ker f'(x)$, and a basis $b$ of $T_xS$ is positive for $o_S$ iff $\iota b_1 \wedge \dots \wedge \iota b_d$ is positive for the tangent orientation of $o_x$.* *Step 1, the isomorphism.* The tangent map read in the corner coordinates $\kappa$ of $S$ and the chart $c$ is injective with values in $\ker f'(x)$, and both have dimension $d$ ⟦Chapter6/SolutionSetOrientation · solKerEquiv⟧. *Step 2, the orientation at a point.* $o_S(x)$ is the pull-back of the tangent orientation along it, read in the corner chart of $S$ at $x$ and the chosen chart of $X$ at $x$ ⟦Chapter6/SolutionSetOrientation · solOr⟧ ⟦Chapter6/SolutionSetOrientation · solOr_spec⟧. *Step 3, the chart of $X$ plays no role*: two charts of $X$ change the isomorphism by the tangent map of the transition (chain rule), which also relates the two tangent orientations (two charts, above) ⟦Chapter6/SolutionSetOrientation · solReadOr_chartChange⟧. *Step 4, continuity.* Along a path of $S$ in corner coordinates the wedges $\iota_q b_1 \wedge \dots \wedge \iota_q b_d$ of a fixed basis are a continuous section of the kernel line bundle — the derivative of the inverse corner chart is continuous ⟦Chapter6/SolutionSetOrientation · isLineOrientation_solKer⟧ — and the tangent orientations of $o$ along the path are an orientation of the same bundle (the prolongation paragraph); two orientations of a line bundle over an interval that agree at one point agree everywhere, so $o_S$ is locally constant in the corner charts ⟦Chapter6/SolutionSetOrientation · isContinuous_solOr⟧. (Gap G.67 closed.) *Hidden hypothesis:* the bump functions, which give the orientable neighbourhoods on which $o$ is continuous; the text assumes partitions of unity from §6.3 (preprint §6.2) on, which give them, and they hold on Hilbert models ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · MPolyfold.admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert⟧. "A natural orientation" of the manifold is read as a continuous tangent orientation, not as an oriented atlas: for the quadrant model the two differ — $[0, 1]$ has no atlas of quadrant charts with positive changes, since a chart at $0$ increases and one at $1$ decreases, and in dimension $0$ every atlas is oriented while a tangent orientation is a sign at every point (Findings, Chapter 6, item 127). The same holds for an open part of the solution set, without properness: if every zero in an open $V$ is in general position with index $d$, $S \cap V$ is a Hausdorff manifold with corners with the continuous tangent orientation of $o$ ⟦Chapter6/SolutionSetOpen2021 · theorem_6_6_18_oriented_open⟧; Theorem 6.7.1 (preprint 6.43) uses it for the index parts of $S_{f+s}$ and for the cobordism $S_F$ (§VI.27).

**The paragraph after the theorem** (V6.61). For $f$ not in general position the text perturbs by an sc⁺-section $s$ supported near $S$ and orients $S_{f+s}$ from $o^f$, using $\mathrm{Lin}(f + s, x) = \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$. This identity holds at every chart point ⟦Chapter6/PerturbedOrientation · ChartPoint.linSet_eq_of_sectionAdd⟧: $(f + s) + t$ ranges over the same sections as $f + (s + t)$, and the sc⁺-sections form a group. So $\mathrm{DET}(f + s, x) = \mathrm{DET}(f, x)$, the push-forwards of $f + s$ are those of $f$ (the sections $S$ of the push-forward data absorb $s$), and an orientation of $f$ is one of $f + s$ ⟦Chapter6/PerturbedOrientation · isSectionOrientation_sectionAdd⟧ ⟦Chapter6/PerturbedOrientation · SectionOrientation.sectionAdd⟧; for $f + s$ proper and in general position, $S_{f+s}$ has the natural orientation coming from $o^f$ ⟦Chapter6/PerturbedOrientation · theorem_6_6_18_sectionAdd⟧, and this applies to the perturbations of Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) in its pointwise reading ⟦Chapter6/PerturbedOrientation · theorem_6_6_18_perturbation⟧. (Gap G.69 closed.) *Readings:* tame germ data, the standing hypothesis of Chapter 5; the orientation $o$ exists iff $f$ is orientable (§VI.24) (Findings, Chapter 6, items 92, 93, 123, 127) (pp. 274–276 (preprint pp. 229–230)).

### VI.26 Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42): the orientation of $\hat f$

The text: for an oriented $(f, o)$ and an sc⁺-section $s$ of $Y \to X \times [0, 1]$, $\hat f(x, t) = f(x) + s(x, t)$ has a natural orientation from $o$ and the standard orientation of $[0, 1]$: for $L = (f - t)'(x)$ oriented by $h = (a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n) \otimes (b_1 \wedge \dots \wedge b_l)^*$, orient $\tilde L(a, b) = La$ by $\tilde h = (a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n \wedge e) \otimes (b_1 \wedge \dots \wedge b_l)^*$, $e$ the standard orientation of $[0, 1]$ (the preprint's order; the 2021 edition puts $e$ first); $\tilde L$ lies in the linearization space of $\hat f$ at $(x, t)$ (p. 276 (preprint p. 230)).

**The linear algebra** (V6.62). For Fredholm $L$, $\tilde L = L \oplus 0 : E \times \mathbb R \to F$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · extOp⟧ is Fredholm ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · isFredholm_extOp⟧ with $\ker\tilde L = \ker L \times \mathbb R$ — one dimension more ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · finrank_ker_extOp⟧, the new direction $e = (0, 1)$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · extE⟧ — and the same range ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · range_extOp⟧ and cokernel ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · extCoker⟧. The map $h \mapsto \tilde h$, $(a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n) \otimes d^* \mapsto ((a_1, 0) \wedge \dots \wedge (a_n, 0) \wedge e) \otimes d^*$, is an isomorphism $\det(L) \cong \det(\tilde L)$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · extDet⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · extDet_wedge_tmul⟧, the wedge extension of §VI.16 with one vector. In local determinant charts its coordinate is $(-1)^{\dim F/R(P) + \dim\operatorname{coker}L}$ times a continuous nowhere-zero function ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · coord_extDet⟧. Over the convex $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$, where $\dim\operatorname{coker}L$ can change parity, the orientation defined by $\tilde h$ at one $L$ could therefore differ from the one defined at another, as we read it. With the sign of §VI.14, $(-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}L}\,h \mapsto \tilde h$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · extDetN⟧ has a coordinate continuous up to a sign constant on a chart ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · coord_extDetN⟧, agrees with the text's map when $L$ is onto ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · extDetN_eq_of_surjective⟧, and pulls continuous orientations back along $L \mapsto \tilde L$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · isLineOrientation_extPull⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · LineOrientation.extPull⟧ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 95). Transported along isomorphisms $A$, $\Gamma$, $\hat L = \Gamma^{-1}(L \oplus 0)A$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · extConjOp⟧ gets the isomorphism $h \mapsto \tilde h$ followed by the conjugation of §VI.21 ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · extConjDet⟧; and for a preconnected $C$ and a simply connected, locally path-connected $\hat C$ containing the $\hat L$, an orientation $o$ of $\mathrm{DET}$ over a nonempty $C$ gives exactly one orientation $\hat o$ over $\hat C$ with $\hat o(\hat L)$ the image of $o(L)$ for every $L \in C$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · existsUnique_extConjOr⟧.

**In charts.** $X \times [0, 1]$ is read as $\mathbb R \times X$ (decision D2), with the parameter first; $s$ is an sc⁺-section $S$ of $\pi^*P$, and $\hat f = \tilde f + S$ with $\tilde f(t, y) = f(y)$. At the product chart point $(t, z)$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · ChartPoint.prodPt⟧ the tangent space is $\mathbb R \times T_zO$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · ChartPoint.mem_prodPt_T_iff⟧ and the fibre $K_z$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · ChartPoint.mem_prodPt_K_iff⟧. The text's $\tilde L(a, b) = La$ puts the $\mathbb R$-factor second, so $\hat L = \Gamma^{-1}(L \oplus 0)A$ with $A$ the swap of the factors and $\Gamma = 1$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · ChartPoint.prodT⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · ChartPoint.prodK⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · ChartPoint.prodLin⟧. Sc⁺-operators lift to the product ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · ChartPoint.IsScPlusOp.prodPt⟧, sections of $P$ lift to $t$-constant sections of $\pi^*P$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · constLift⟧, and so $\hat L \in \mathrm{Lin}(\hat f, (t, x))$ for every $L \in \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · ChartPoint.prodLin_mem_linSet⟧ — the derivative in $t$ of a $t$-constant lift vanishes, and $S$ only contributes an sc⁺-operator. *An orientation $o$ of $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$ gives exactly one orientation $\hat o$ of $\mathrm{DET}(\hat f, (t, x))$ with $\hat o(\hat L)$ the image of $o(L)$ for every $L$* ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · ChartPoint.existsUnique_prodOr⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · ChartPoint.prodOr⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · ChartPoint.prodOr_apply⟧, and $o \mapsto \hat o$ is injective ⟦Chapter6/ProductOrientation · ChartPoint.prodOr_injective⟧ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 96). *Hidden hypotheses:* $x$ smooth and $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ nonempty (bump functions give it, §VI.1); only the orientation of $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$ at the one point is used, not an orientation of $f$. That these pointwise orientations, in the 2021 convention, form an orientation of $\hat f$ in the sense of Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40) is the last paragraph below.

**The 2021 convention, $e$ first** (V6.62). The 2021 edition prints $\tilde h = (e \wedge a_1 \wedge \dots \wedge a_n) \otimes (b_1 \wedge \dots \wedge b_l)^*$, with $e$ first; the preprint puts it last. Moving $e$ across $n$ vectors costs $(-1)^n$ ⟦Chapter6/OrientationConvention2021 · wedge_snoc_eq_smul_wedge_cons⟧. The 2021 map $h \mapsto \tilde h$ ⟦Chapter6/OrientationConvention2021 · extDetFirst⟧ ⟦Chapter6/OrientationConvention2021 · extDetFirst_wedge_tmul⟧ is $(-1)^{\mathrm{ind}L}$ times the sign-normalized map of the previous paragraph ⟦Chapter6/OrientationConvention2021 · extDetFirst_eq_indSign_smul_extDetN⟧, because $(-1)^{\dim\ker L} = (-1)^{\mathrm{ind}L}(-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}L}$ ⟦Chapter6/OrientationConvention2021 · kerSign_eq_indSign_mul_stabSign⟧. The index is locally constant on the Fredholm operators ⟦Chapter6/OrientationConvention2021 · eventually_fredholmIndex_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter6/OrientationConvention2021 · eventually_indSign_eq⟧, and a line orientation times a locally constant sign is a line orientation, so *the text's own map pulls continuous orientations back, over any set of Fredholm operators* ⟦Chapter6/OrientationConvention2021 · isLineOrientation_extPullFirst⟧. With the 2021 convention no sign has to be changed: the factor $(-1)^{\dim\operatorname{coker}L}$ of the preprint's map and the $(-1)^{\dim\ker L}$ of moving $e$ to the front combine to a locally constant sign. In charts, *an orientation $o$ of $\mathrm{DET}(f, x)$ gives exactly one orientation $\hat o$ of $\mathrm{DET}(\hat f, (t, x))$ with $\hat o(\hat L) = e \wedge o(L)$ for every $L \in \mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$* ⟦Chapter6/OrientationConvention2021 · ChartPoint.existsUnique_prodOrFirst⟧ ⟦Chapter6/OrientationConvention2021 · ChartPoint.prodOrFirst⟧, and on $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ the 2021 map is the preprint's times the one constant sign $(-1)^{\mathrm{ind}(f, x)}$ ⟦Chapter6/OrientationConvention2021 · ChartPoint.exists_extConjDetFirst_eq_sign_smul⟧ (Findings, Chapter 6, item 122).

**The orientation of $\hat f$** (V6.62) ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021f · SectionOrientation.prodFirst⟧. *Over a tame $X$ with bump functions, for $f$ with tame germ data, an orientation $o$ of $f$ (Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40)) and an sc⁺-section $S$ of $\pi^*P \to \mathbb R^1 \times X$, the map $(t, x) \mapsto e \wedge o_x$ is an orientation of $\hat f = \tilde f + S$ in the sense of Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40).* The text's "natural orientation", with its remark that the choices made in the construction are compatible, is this statement. *Step 1, the map.* $(t, x) \mapsto e \wedge o_x$ is defined in the product chart point over any chart point of $x$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021f · prodFirstFun⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021e · prodOrOf⟧, and its reading in any chart of $\mathbb R^1 \times X$ is computed through the product chart ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021f · toChartOr_prodFirstFun⟧; the chart of $X$ plays no role, since the transfer of §VI.21 between two product chart points is the transfer between the chart points of $X$ with $e$ put in front ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021b · ChartPoint.orTransfer_prodPt_prodOrFirst⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021f · prodOrOf_orTransfer⟧. *Step 2, the lifted data.* A push-forward datum of $f$ along a path $\gamma$ — sections $S$, $s_1, \dots, s_k$ and stabilized kernels $\Lambda$ (§§VI.14–VI.15) — lifts to one of $\tilde f$ along $q \mapsto (\tau(q), \gamma(q))$: the sections are lifted constant in $t$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021c · liftProd⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021c · isScPlusSection_liftProd⟧, the linearization of a $t$-constant lift is $(\sigma, v) \mapsto g'(x)v$, and the stabilized kernels become $\mathbb R \times \Lambda$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021c · SubspaceFamily.prodLine⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021c · IsStabKernels.prodLift⟧. *Step 3, no sign.* The stabilization isomorphism of $\hat L$ maps $e \wedge h$ to $\hat e \wedge J(\cdot)$ of the stabilization of $h$, $J$ the inclusion $v \mapsto (0, v)$ of the old kernel ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021c · stabRayEquiv_extConjDetFirst⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021 · detEquiv_stabIota_extDetFirst⟧: in adapted bases, the appended vector $e$ is first on both sides of formula (91), so the computation is that of Proposition 6.4.15 (preprint 6.15) with one more kernel vector. Continuation commutes with $\hat e \wedge J(\cdot)$, proved directly in frames ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021c · SubspaceFamily.cont_prodLine⟧, and the rays read from the product orientation in $\lambda((\mathbb R \times \Lambda)_q)$ are $\hat e \wedge J$ of those read from $o$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021d · ChartPoint.prodOrFirst₀⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021e · IsStabKernels.orRay_prodLift⟧. Hence *the lifted push-forward maps $e \wedge o$ to $e \wedge$ (the push-forward of $o$)* ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021e · IsPush.prodLift⟧. *Step 4.* An orientation of $f$ is carried by every push-forward along paths in orientable neighbourhoods (§VI.24); by Step 3 so is $e \wedge o$ along the lifted paths, and every path of $\mathbb R^1 \times X$ in a product chart is such a lift, so $e \wedge o$ is an orientation of $\tilde f$ ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021f · isSectionOrientation_prodFirstFun⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProductSectionOrientation2021f · SectionOrientation.prodFirst₀⟧, and of $\tilde f + S$ by the paragraph after Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41) (§VI.25). (Gap G.66 closed; Findings, Chapter 6, items 96, 97, 122.) *Readings:* $X \times [0, 1]$ is read as $\mathbb R^1 \times X$ with the parameter first (decision D2; gap G.65 in part), and the hypotheses — $X$ tame with sc-smooth bump functions, tame germ data — are those of Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41) in §VI.25. On a product end of the solution set of $\hat f$ this orientation is the product orientation, the time vector first (§VI.27).

### VI.27 §6.7 (preprint §6.6) and Theorem 6.7.1 (preprint 6.43): the invariant $\Psi_{(f,o)}$

§6.7 (preprint §6.6) (p. 276 (preprint p. 230)) recalls, for a proper oriented $(f, o)$ over a tame $X$ with sc-smooth bump functions and an auxiliary norm $N$, the neighbourhood $U$ of $S_f$ of Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) and the sc⁺-perturbations $s$ supported in $U$ with $N(s) \le 1$ for which $f + s$ is in general position at its zeros; it calls them *admissible for the pair $(N, U)$*. Theorem 6.7.1 (preprint 6.43) (p. 277 (preprint p. 231)): *there is a well-defined map assigning to a proper oriented $(f, o)$ a linear map $\Psi_{(f,o)} : H^*_{dR}(X, \partial X) \to \mathbb R$ such that* (1) *for every auxiliary norm $N$ and every $s$ admissible for $(N, U)$, $S_{f+s}$ is an oriented compact manifold with boundary with corners and $\Psi_{(f,o)}([\omega, \tau]) = \int_{S_{f+s}}\omega - \int_{\partial S_{f+s}}\tau$, the integrals being zero when the dimensions do not agree;* (2) *$\Psi_{(f_0,o_0)} = \Psi_{(f_1,o_1)}$ for a proper oriented homotopy between $(f_0, o_0)$ and $(f_1, o_1)$.* The proof (pp. 277–279 (preprint pp. 231–233)) defines $\Psi$ from one admissible $s_0$, joins two admissible sections by a homotopy $s_t$ whose solution set $S_F$ over $X \times [0, 1]$ is an oriented compact manifold with boundary with corners, decomposes $\partial S_F = S_0 \cup S_1 \cup \tilde S$, and compares the two sides by Stokes' theorem applied to an extension $\bar\omega$ of $\omega$ and to $\tau$; part (2) is "the same homotopy argument". For $\partial X = \emptyset$ (p. 279 (preprint p. 233)), $\Psi([\omega]) = \int_{S_{f+s}}\omega$ for $[\omega] \in H^n_{dR}(X)$, $n$ the index, and zero in the other degrees.

**The theorem formalized** (V6.76) ⟦Chapter6/Theorem671Final2021 · theorem_6_7_1⟧. *Let $P : Y \to X$ be a strong bundle over a tame M-polyfold with sc-smooth bump functions. There is $\Psi$ assigning to every proper sc-Fredholm section $f$ with tame germ data and orientation $o$ (Definition 6.6.16 (preprint 6.40)) linear maps $\Psi_{(f,o)} : H^k_{dR}(X, \partial X) \to \mathbb R$, $k \ge 0$, such that* (1) *for every auxiliary norm $N$ there are open $U \supseteq S_f$ with $\mathrm{cl}\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le C\}$ compact for every $C > 0$; for every such $U$, $S_{f+s}$ is compact for every allowable $s$, admissible sections exist, and for every admissible $s$, $S_{f+s}$ is compact and the union of its index parts $S_k$, each $S_k$ a compact manifold with boundary and corners of dimension $k$ oriented by $o$, and $\Psi_{(f,o)}([\omega, \tau]) = \int_{S_k}\omega - \int_{\partial S_k}\tau$ in degree $k$;* (2) *$\Psi_{(f_0,o_0)} = \Psi_{(f_1,o_1)}$ in every degree for a proper oriented homotopy.* No hypothesis beyond the text's is used: the proof below assumes nothing of its own steps. The readings (Findings, Chapter 6, items 128–133, 136):

- *R-a, the cohomology.* $H^k_{dR}(X, \partial X)$ is the relative cohomology of Part IV: pairs $(\omega, \tau)$ of an sc-form on $X$ and a form on the faces of $X$, with $d(\alpha, \beta) = (d\alpha, j^*\alpha - d\beta)$ ⟦Chapter4/BoundaryForms2021 · MPolyfold.RelForms⟧ ⟦Chapter4/BoundaryForms2021 · MPolyfold.relD⟧. The integrals are integrals of Mathlib forms over the Mathlib manifolds $S_k$ and their faces (Part IX).
- *R-b, the neighbourhood $U$ with a margin.* The text takes $U$ from Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18), for one $N$. It is read existentially and for every $N$, with the margin "$\mathrm{cl}\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le C\}$ compact for every $C > 0$", which the cobordism below needs for $C = 2$ (item 128).
- *R-c, "zero if the dimensions do not agree".* The index of $f$ need not be constant. Degree $k$ is paired with the part $S_k$ of $S_{f+s}$ where the index is $k$ (item 129).
- *R-d, the proper oriented homotopy*, which the text does not define. It is read through Remark 6.6.19 (preprint 6.42): an sc⁺-section $S$ of $\pi^*P \to \mathbb R^1 \times X$ with $S(0, \cdot) = 0$, $f_1 = f_0 + S(1, \cdot)$ and $o_1$ the orientation $o_0$ carried to $f_1$, compact zeros of $\tilde f_0 + S$ over $t \in [0, 1]$, and the properness clause of Definition 5.2.1 (3) on that slab ⟦Chapter6/ProperHomotopy2021 · IsProperOrientedHomotopy⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProperHomotopy2021 · IsProperOrientedHomotopyBetween⟧; then $f_0$, $f_1$ are proper ⟦Chapter6/ProperHomotopy2021 · IsProperOrientedHomotopy.isProper_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter6/ProperHomotopy2021 · IsProperOrientedHomotopy.isProper_one⟧, and $S = 0$ is one ⟦Chapter6/ProperHomotopy2021 · witness_isProperOrientedHomotopyBetween⟧ (item 130).
- *R-e, the extension of $\omega$.* The proof's $\bar\omega = p_1^*\omega \wedge p_2^*dt$ has degree $k + 1$, one more than the dimension $k$ of $\partial S_F$, while the comparison needs $\int_{S_0}\omega$ and $\int_{S_1}\omega$; as we read it, the argument goes through with $p_1^*\omega$ and $p_1^*\tau$ in their place, and that is what is formalized (item 131).
- *R-f, signs.* The boundary orientation is outward vector first, which gives Stokes' theorem with the sign $+$, as the text uses it; $S_F$ is oriented by $e \wedge o$, time first (item 132). The cut-off route below does not need the signs of the pieces of $\partial S_F$.

**Step 1: the neighbourhood and the admissible sections** (V6.76). A proper $f$ has compact $S_f$ (Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5), §V.6). *For an auxiliary norm $N$ and every open $V \supseteq S_f$ there is an open $S_f \subseteq U \subseteq V$ with $\mathrm{cl}\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le C\}$ compact for every $C > 0$* ⟦Chapter5/CylinderPerturbation2021 · exists_adapted_margin⟧: for compact $S_f$, Theorem 5.2.2 (preprint 5.5) gives an open $U_0 \supseteq S_f$ with this property for every $C > 0$ (§V.6), and $U = U_0 \cap V$ keeps it. With such a $U$, *$S_{f+s}$ is compact for every $s$ allowable for $(N, U)$* ⟦Chapter6/Theorem671_2021 · isCompact_solutionSet_sectionAdd_of_margin⟧: off $U$ the zeros of $f + s$ are zeros of $f$, which lie in $U$; in $U$, $f(x) = -s(x)$ gives $N(f(x)) \le 1$; so $S_{f+s}$ is a closed part of a compact set (Remark 5.3.4 (preprint 5.12)). *Admissible* is the text's notion: $s$ is allowable for $(N, U)$ — supported in $U$, $N(s) \le 1$ — and $f + s$ is in general position (Definition 5.3.9 (preprint 5.17)) at every zero ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · StrongBundle.IsAdmissible⟧ (gap G.55 closed). They exist by a relative form of Theorem 5.3.10 (preprint 5.18) ⟦Chapter5/CylinderPerturbation2021 · theorem_5_3_10_relative_hyp⟧: *for $G$ with tame germ data, $N$ an auxiliary norm, $K \subseteq W$ with $K$ compact and $W$ open, $G$ in general position at every zero outside $K$ and $\mathrm{cl}\{x \in W \mid N(G(x)) \le 1\}$ compact, there is for every $\varepsilon > 0$ an sc⁺-section $p$ supported in $W$ with $N(p) \le \varepsilon$ and $G + p$ in general position at every zero.* Its proof is that of §V.20: finitely many sections make $G(x) + \sum\lambda_is_i(x)$ general at the points $(0, y)$ near the compact $K \cap S_G$ ⟦Chapter5/CylinderPerturbation2021 · exists_sections_isGeneralPositionGerm_near⟧, and at the other zeros, where $G$ is already general ⟦Chapter5/CylinderPerturbation2021 · isGeneralPositionGerm_paramSection_of_isGeneralPositionGerm⟧; Sard's theorem and Theorem 4.3.1 give a regular value $\lambda$ of norm as small as needed ⟦Chapter5/CylinderPerturbation2021 · exists_null_isGeneralPositionGerm_paramSlice⟧; off $W$ the perturbation vanishes near the zero, and general position there is that of $G$ ⟦Chapter5/CylinderPerturbation2021 · isGeneralPositionGerm_congr_nhds⟧. The text's theorem is the case $K = S_G$, $W = U$; here $S_G$ need not be compact, which the cobordisms need. With $K = S_f$ it gives an admissible section for $(N, V)$ inside any $V$ ⟦Chapter5/CylinderPerturbation2021 · exists_admissible⟧ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · StrongBundle.exists_isAdmissible_nbhd⟧, and, applied to the maximum of finitely many norms ⟦Chapter5/CylinderPerturbation2021 · IsAuxNorm.max⟧ ⟦Chapter5/CylinderPerturbation2021 · allowableSections_max_subset⟧, one section admissible for two pairs $(N_0, U_0)$, $(N_1, U_1)$ at once ⟦Chapter5/CylinderPerturbation2021 · exists_admissible_subset⟧ ⟦Chapter5/CylinderPerturbation2021 · exists_admissible_two⟧ — the step that compares two norms.

**Step 2: the index parts as oriented manifolds** (V6.76). For admissible $s$, $S_k$ is the set of zeros of $f + s$ at which $f$ has index $k$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · StrongBundle.solPart⟧. The index is locally constant (Proposition 6.2.2 (preprint 6.2), §III.49), so $S_k$ is open and closed in $S_{f+s}$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · StrongBundle.isClosed_solPart⟧, compact ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · StrongBundle.isCompact_solPart⟧, and $S_{f+s} = \bigcup_k S_k$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · StrongBundle.solutionSet_eq_iUnion_solPart⟧. Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41) for an open part (§VI.25), applied to $f + s$ with the orientation $o$ carried to it (§VI.25, the paragraph after the theorem), makes $S_k$ a compact Mathlib manifold of dimension $k$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · isManifold_solPart⟧ with a continuous tangent orientation which is the Fredholm one at every point ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · solPartOr⟧ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · solPartIsOrientedManifold⟧. For a constant index $n$, $S_n = S_{f+s}$ and $S_k = \emptyset$ for $k \ne n$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · StrongBundle.solPart_eq_solutionSet⟧ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · StrongBundle.solPart_eq_empty_of_ne⟧: the text's clause "zero if the dimensions do not agree".

**Step 3: $\Psi_s$ for one admissible section** (V6.76). On relative forms of degree $k$, $\Psi_s(\omega, \tau) = \int_{S_k}\omega - \int_{\partial S_k}\tau$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · solIntegral⟧ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · solBoundaryIntegral⟧ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · psiForms⟧: $\omega$ restricted to $S_k$ is a Mathlib form ⟦Chapter9/MathlibFormsBridge2021 · MPolyfold.formsInftyRestrict⟧, and $\tau$ is read on the faces of $S_k$, which lie in faces of $X$ (Theorem 4.2.11, §IV) ⟦Chapter9/SolutionFaceForms2021 · MPolyfold.solFaceForm⟧. *$\Psi_s$ vanishes on exact relative forms* ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · psiForms_relD⟧: for $d(\alpha, \beta) = (d\alpha, j^*\alpha - d\beta)$,
$$\int_{S}d\alpha - \int_{\partial S}j^*\alpha + \int_{\partial S}d\beta = 0,$$
by Stokes' theorem on the compact manifold with corners $S_{k}$ ⟦Chapter9/MathlibFormsBridge2021 · MPolyfold.stokes_formsInftyRestrict⟧, the face form of $j^*\alpha$ being $\alpha$ restricted to the faces ⟦Chapter9/SolutionFaceForms2021 · MPolyfold.solFaceForm_jStar_integral⟧, and $\int_{\partial S}d\beta = 0$ since the face form of $d\beta$ is $d$ of the face form ⟦Chapter9/SolutionFaceForms2021 · MPolyfold.solFaceForm_d⟧ and exact forms on the compact faces integrate to zero ⟦Chapter4/ManifoldFaceForms2021 · ChartFaceForm.integral_d_eq_zero_of_compactSpace⟧. So $\Psi_s$ descends to $H^k_{dR}(X, \partial X)$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · psiAt⟧ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · psiAt_mk⟧. It depends on $s$ only, not on $(N, U)$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · psiAt_congr_admissible⟧. In degree $0$ it is a signed count, $\Psi_s([\omega]) = \sum_{x \in S_0}\varepsilon(x)\,\omega(x)$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · psiAt_mk_zero_eq_sum⟧ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · ManifoldForm.integral_eq_sum_of_dim_zero⟧, and it is $0$ when $S_{f+s} = \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantSingle2021 · psiAt_of_eq_empty⟧. *An integrand.* A form $a$ on $S_k$ with $a = \omega|_{S_k} + d\gamma$, $\gamma$ a compactly supported $C^\infty$ form extending $-\tau|_{\partial S}$ ($a = \omega|_{S_0}$ in degree $0$), is an *integrand* of $(\omega, \tau)$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantCobordism2021 · IsPsiIntegrand⟧; integrands exist, by extension of face data on the compact $S_k$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantCobordism2021 · exists_isPsiIntegrand⟧, and $\Psi_s([\omega, \tau]) = \int_{S_k}a$, since $\int_{S}d\gamma = \int_{\partial S}j^*\gamma = -\int_{\partial S}\tau$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantCobordism2021 · IsPsiIntegrand.psiAt_eq⟧. This is the form $\omega - d\beta$ with $j^*\beta = \tau$ of the text's computation, written on $S_k$.

Let $K$ be the zeros of $G$ over $[3/16, 13/16]$, compact because they lie in $[3/16, 13/16] \times \mathrm{cl}\{x \in U \mid N(f(x)) \le 1\}$, and $W = (1/8, 7/8) \times U$. **Step 6: the cobordism and its ends** (V6.76). Let $F = \tilde f_0 + \hat S$ for cobordism data. The index-$(k + 1)$ part $S_F^{k+1}$ of its solution set ⟦Chapter6/InvariantCobordism2021 · cobPart⟧ is, by Theorem 6.6.18 (preprint 6.41) for an open part over the tame $\mathbb R^1 \times X$, a $(k + 1)$-dimensional submanifold with a corner structure ⟦Chapter6/InvariantCobordism2021 · isSubmanifoldOfDim_cobPart⟧ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantCobordism2021 · hasCornerStructureOfDim_cobPart⟧, σ-compact ⟦Chapter6/InvariantCobordism2021 · sigmaCompactSpace_cobPart⟧, with the smooth time function $t$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantCobordism2021 · cobTime⟧ whose slabs $\{t \in [c, d]\}$ are compact ⟦Chapter6/InvariantCobordism2021 · isCompact_cobSlab⟧. *The ends.* Over $t \le 1/8$ the solution set of $F$ is $\{t \le 1/8\} \times S_{f+\sigma_0}$, and over $t \ge 7/8$ it is $\{t \ge 7/8\} \times S_{f+\sigma_1}$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantProductEnds2021 · solutionSet_left_eq_prod⟧ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantProductEnds2021 · solutionSet_right_eq_prod⟧, since $F$ is the $t$-constant lift there. *The index on the ends*: at a zero $(t, x)$ where $F$ is the lift of $g = f + \sigma_i$ and in general position, $F'(t, x)$ has index $k + 1$ exactly when $g'(x)$ has index $k$ ⟦Chapter6/InvariantProductEnds2021b · isLinOfIndex_end_iff⟧: the lifted linearization is $(\sigma, v) \mapsto g'(x)v$, with one more kernel dimension, and the index of $F'$ is unique.
