### VII.20 Michael's theorem: Part I's Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7) and Proposition 2.7.4 (2017: 2.17)

(V7.50.) Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2) needs that a finite union of closed paracompact subsets of the regular $|X|$ is paracompact, and the text's route to Proposition 7.5.3 (2017: 7.12) uses Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7). Part I's Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7) (Michael: a regular Hausdorff space is paracompact iff every open cover has a locally finite closed refinement) and Proposition 2.7.4 (2017: 2.17) (a regular Hausdorff space that is the union of a locally finite family of closed paracompact subspaces is paracompact), 2017 p. 51, were gap G.15 of Part I; they are formalized here, for regular spaces and without Hausdorff. Michael's Lemma 1 has four conditions on a regular space: (a) paracompact; (b) every open cover has a σ-locally finite open refinement; (c) every open cover has a locally finite refinement by arbitrary sets; (d) every open cover has a locally finite closed refinement ⟦Chapter7/Michael · michael_tfae⟧. *(d) ⇒ (a), in every topological space* ⟦Chapter7/Michael · paracompactSpace_of_closed_refinement⟧. Let $(A_b)$ be a closed locally finite refinement of the cover $(U_i)$, with $A_b \subseteq U_{f(b)}$; cover the space by open sets each meeting finitely many $A_b$ and take a closed locally finite refinement $(B_c)$ of that cover; then $V_b = (\bigcup\{B_c \mid B_c \cap A_b = \emptyset\})^c \cap U_{f(b)}$ is open (a locally finite union of closed sets is closed), contains $A_b$, and each $B_c$ meets only the finitely many $V_b$ with $B_c \cap A_b \ne \emptyset$; so $(V_b)$ is a locally finite open refinement. *(c) ⇒ (d) in a regular space* ⟦Chapter7/Michael · closed_refinement_of_refinement⟧: refine first a cover by open sets whose closures lie in the cover, and take closures. *(b) ⇒ (c), in every space* ⟦Chapter7/Michael · refinement_of_sigma_refinement⟧: $t_{n,b} \setminus \bigcup_{k<n}\bigcup_{b'}t_{k,b'}$. Hence (c) ⇒ (a) and (b) ⇒ (a) in a regular space ⟦Chapter7/Michael · paracompactSpace_of_refinement⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Michael · paracompactSpace_of_sigma_refinement⟧, and (a) ⇒ (d) by Mathlib's shrinking lemma, with the same index and $v_i \subseteq u_i$ ⟦Chapter7/Michael · exists_closed_precise_refinement⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Michael · exists_closed_precise_refinement_set⟧. **Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7)** is the equivalence of (a) and (d) ⟦Chapter7/Michael · lemma_2_7_3⟧. **Proposition 2.7.4 (2017: 2.17)** ⟦Chapter7/Michael · proposition_2_7_4⟧ follows the text: closed locally finite refinements $(C^i_j)_j$ of the traces $(Y_i \cap U_j)_j$ by Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7) in each $Y_i$, which is regular because $Y$ is; $C_j = \bigcup_iC^i_j$ is locally finite in $Y$ because $(Y_i)$ is and a locally finite family in a closed subspace is locally finite in the space ⟦Chapter7/Michael · locallyFinite_image_val⟧; and (d) ⇒ (a) in $Y$. The subspace forms are what Chapter 7 uses: a locally finite family of closed paracompact subsets has a paracompact union ⟦Chapter7/Michael · paracompactSpace_iUnion⟧, so do finite families and pairs ⟦Chapter7/Michael · paracompactSpace_iUnion_of_finite⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Michael · paracompactSpace_biUnion_of_finite⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Michael · paracompactSpace_union⟧, and a closed subset of a paracompact subspace is paracompact ⟦Chapter7/Michael · paracompactSpace_of_isClosed_subset⟧. *The Hausdorff property is never used*; regularity enters through (c) ⇒ (d) and (a) ⇒ (d). Part I's 2017 p. 51 says "subcovering" in the definition of paracompactness, read as "refinement", as on 2017 p. 249 (Findings, Chapter 7, items 75, 114).

### VII.21 Definition 7.3.7 (2017: 7.14) and Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2)

**Definition 7.3.7 (2017: 7.14)** (V7.49). $K \subseteq |X|$ is component compact if it meets every connected component of $|X|$ in a compact set ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.IsComponentCompact⟧ (2017 p. 247).

**Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2)** (V7.51) ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_3_8⟧. *A component compact $K$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with $\mathrm{cl}_{|X|}U$ paracompact; then $\mathrm{cl}U$ and $U$ are metrizable.* **The text's proof**: work in a connected component of $K$, so that $K$ may be assumed compact; every $z \in K$ has an open $U(z)$ with metrizable, hence paracompact, closure; finitely many $U(z_i)$ cover $K$; $U = \bigcup\mathrm{cl}U(z_i)$ is paracompact, Hausdorff, regular and locally metrizable, hence metrizable, and so is $U = \bigcup U(z_i)$. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1, the compact case, inside a given open $W \supseteq K$* ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_3_8_of_isCompact⟧. Every $z$ has an open $U(z)$ with $\mathrm{cl}U(z) \subseteq W$ metrizable, by Lemma 7.3.2 (2017: 7.4) and the regularity of $|X|$ ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · EpGroupoid.exists_isOpen_metrizableSpace_closure⟧; finitely many cover $K$; $U = \bigcup U(z_i)$ has $\mathrm{cl}U = \bigcup\mathrm{cl}U(z_i)$, paracompact by Michael (§VII.20), which the text does not cite, and metrizable by §VII.19. *Step 2, the components are open.* "We work in a connected component of $K$" is read in a component $C$ of $|X|$, where $K \cap C$ is compact. This needs the components of $|X|$ to be open, which the text does not state: $|X|$ is a quotient of the locally path connected $X$ (§VII.7), hence locally connected ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · EpGroupoid.locallyPathConnectedSpace_orbitSpace⟧. *Step 3, back to $K$, not in the text.* Step 1 in each component $C$, with $W = C$, gives $U_C \supseteq K \cap C$ with $\mathrm{cl}U_C \subseteq C$ paracompact. The components are open and pairwise disjoint, so $(\mathrm{cl}U_C)_C$ is locally finite, $\mathrm{cl}(\bigcup U_C) = \bigcup\mathrm{cl}U_C$, and this locally finite union of closed paracompact sets is paracompact (Proposition 2.7.4 (2017: 2.17), §VII.20) ⟦Chapter7/Michael · paracompactSpace_iUnion⟧. The text's $U$ names both $\bigcup\mathrm{cl}U(z_i)$ and $\bigcup U(z_i)$ (possible misprint); here $U$ is the open one (Findings, Chapter 7, item 74) (2017 p. 247).

### VII.22 Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11): index lifting

**Proposition 7.3.9 (2017: 7.11)** (V7.52) ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_3_9⟧. *If $X = (X, \mathbf X)$ is an ep-groupoid, so is $X^1 = (X^1, \mathbf X^1)$; if $X$ is tame, so is $X^1$.* $X^1$ is the M-polyfold of Part I with the levels shifted by one (§II.6). **The structure maps of $X^1$.** The text restricts $s, t, u, \iota, m$ to level $1$ without comment. Sc-smooth maps preserve the levels, so $s, t, u, \iota$ restrict ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · MPolyfold.levelOneMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.liftSrc⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.liftTgt⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.liftUnit⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.liftInv⟧; a composite of composable morphisms on level $1$ is on level $1$, since $ml(t(\varphi \circ \psi)) = ml(t\varphi) = ml(\varphi)$ (§VII.3) ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.comp_mem_levelSet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.liftComp⟧; the groupoid is ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.liftGroupoidStr⟧. **The text's proof** says that (1), (2) and (4) hold trivially, and proves (3) by sequences: for $x \in X_1$ and $V(x)$ with $t$ proper over $s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_XV(x))$, $W(x) = V(x) \cap X_1$ is open in $X_1$ and $\mathrm{cl}_{X_1}W(x) \subseteq \mathrm{cl}_XV(x)$; for $(\varphi_k)$ with $(t\varphi_k)$ in a compact subset of $X_1$, after a subsequence (a) $\varphi_k \to \varphi$ in $\mathbf X_0$, (b) $s, t$ converge in $X_0$, (c) $t(\varphi_k) \to t(\varphi)$ in $X_1$, so (d) $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$, and $\varphi_k = (t|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1}(t\varphi_k) \to \varphi$ in $\mathbf X^1$. **The formalized proof.** *(1).* The level-$1$ lift of a local sc-diffeomorphism is one: an sc-diffeomorphism on an open set lifts with its inverse ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.levelOne⟧ ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.levelOne⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_liftSrc⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_liftTgt⟧. *(2).* Part I's lifting of the index for sc-smooth maps, Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17) in charts (§I.15) ⟦Chapter5/StrongBundleShift · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothMap.levelOne⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_liftUnit⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_liftInv⟧. *(4).* The text's "trivially", as we read it, uses $(\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X)^1 = \mathbf X^1\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X^1$ as M-polyfolds, which is not proved here; it is avoided through the sheet form (§VII.2). A local inverse $\sigma_1$ of $s$ on level $1$ agrees near each point with the level-$1$ lift of a local inverse $\sigma$ of $s$, both inverting $s$ near that point, and $\psi \mapsto m(\sigma(t\psi), \psi)$ lifts by the lifting of sc-smooth maps on open sets ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothOn.levelOne⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet_lift⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothComp_lift⟧. *(3), the text's argument* ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.exists_isProperMap_lift⟧. "$(t\varphi_k)$ in a compact subset of $X_1$" is replaced by "$t\varphi_k$ converges in $X_1$", the sequential criterion for a closed set (§VII.2) ⟦Chapter7/ProperMaps · isProperMap_domRestrict_iff_of_isClosed⟧, $X^1$ and $\mathbf X^1$ being metrizable (Theorem 2.3.10 (2017: 2.2)) ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.metrizableSpace_level⟧; $\mathrm{cl}_{X_1}W(x) \subseteq \mathrm{cl}_XV(x)$ is the continuity of $X_1 \to X$; (a) is properness on level $0$, (c) the hypothesis, (d) that $t$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism and preserves levels; step (b) is not needed; and "$(t|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1}$ is sc$^0$" is used as the continuity on level $1$ of its level-$1$ lift. So $X^1$ is an ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.liftOne⟧, paracompact on both levels ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · MPolyfold.paracompactSpace_level⟧. The display (7.5), "$s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_{X_1}(W(x)) \to X_1$", has an unbalanced parenthesis (possible misprint; Findings, Chapter 7, items 80, 96).

**Tameness of $X^1$** ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.isTame_liftOne⟧. The text calls it trivial. As we read it, it needs that the index lift of a tame retraction is tame, which Part I left open (Findings, Chapter 5, item 145); it is proved ⟦Chapter7/Lift · MPolyfold.IsTame.levelOne⟧. *Step 1, the shifted presentation.* For a tame $r$ with a presentation $T : E \cong \mathbb R^n \oplus W$ of the partial quadrant $C$, the presentation $T^1 : E^1 \cong \mathbb R^n \oplus W^1$ of $C^1$ has the same $\mathbb R^n$-coordinates ⟦Chapter7/Lift · shiftPres⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · shift_presentation⟧, so $d_{C^1} = d_C$ on $C^1$ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · degIndex_shift⟧ and the subspace $E_x$ for $T^1$ is $E_x \cap E_1$ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · mem_minimalSubspaceWith_shift⟧. *Step 2, the tangent.* $Dr^1(x) = Dr(x)|_{E_1}$ (Proposition 1.2.2 (preprint 1.17)), whose range is $T_xO \cap E_1$ since $Dr(x)$ is a projection. *Step 3, the complement.* An sc-complement $A$ of $T_xO$ gives the sc-complement $A \cap E_1$ of $T_xO^1$, an sc-splitting shifting to one ⟦Chapter7/Lift · isScSplitting_levelSub_one⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · isScSubspace_levelSub_one⟧. *Step 4.* So $r^1$ is tame for $T^1$ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · isTameWith_shift⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · isTameRetract_shift⟧, hence tame by Part I's independence of the presentation ⟦Chapter2/TameFaces · ScRetraction.IsTameWith.isTame⟧, and the level charts of tame charts form a tame atlas of $X^1$ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 81) (pp. 326–328 (2017 pp. 247–248)).

### VII.23 Definition 7.5.1 (2017: 7.15), Remark 7.5.2 (2017: 7.1), and Proposition 7.5.3 (2017: 7.12)

**Definition 7.5.1 (2017: 7.15)** (V7.53). An ep-groupoid has paracompact orbit space if in addition (5) $|X|$ is paracompact ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.HasParacompactOrbitSpace⟧; the text stipulates that paracompact does not include Hausdorff, and Mathlib's notion does not. Since $|X|$ is Hausdorff and locally metrizable (Theorem 7.3.1 (2017: 7.2)), (5) is equivalent to the metrizability of $|X|$ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_iff_metrizableSpace⟧, and it holds when $|X|$ is second countable (Corollary 7.3.6 (2017: 7.1)) ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_of_secondCountableTopology⟧. *The sentence before Remark 7.5.2 (2017: 7.1)*, "in case $X$ has a second countable topology, (1)–(4) imply (5)", is read with $X$ the object space ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.remark_7_5_2⟧: $|X|$ is then second countable, $\pi$ being open and onto (Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1)), hence metrizable by Corollary 7.3.6 (2017: 7.1), hence paracompact. Remark 7.5.2 (2017: 7.1) itself, on the second countability required in [38], has no formal content. The open question the text states here, whether (5) is a consequence of (1)–(4), is settled negatively in §VII.49: the Čech groupoid of a Prüfer-type surface is an ep-groupoid with Hausdorff, non-paracompact orbit space ⟦Chapter7/PropertyFiveResearch · EpGroupoid.Examples.Pruefer.exists_epGroupoid_not_hasParacompactOrbitSpace⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, items 82, 113, 152) (p. 340 (2017 p. 249)).

**The map $|X^1| \to |X|$.** The text writes $|X_1|$ for the orbit space of $X^1$ and treats it as a subset of $|X|$ ("$A_x \cap |X_1|$", 2017 p. 250). Here $|X^1|$ keeps its own quotient topology: the inclusion $X^1 \to X$ is a functor ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.liftIncl⟧ and induces $|X^1| \to |X|$ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.orbitIncl⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.orbitIncl_π⟧, continuous ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.continuous_orbitIncl⟧ and injective, because a morphism between points of $X_1$ lies in $\mathbf X_1$ ($ml(s\varphi) = ml(t\varphi)$, §VII.3) ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.orbitIncl_injective⟧, with range $|X_1| = \pi(X_1)$ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.range_orbitIncl⟧; the preimage of $\pi(U)$ is $\pi_1(U \cap X_1)$ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.preimage_orbitIncl_image⟧.

**Proposition 7.5.3 (2017: 7.12)** (V7.54) ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_5_3⟧. *If $X$ has paracompact orbit space, so has $X^1$.* **The text's proof**: by Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7) the cover $(|U(x)|)$ of $|X|$ has a locally finite closed refinement $(A_x)$, $A_x \subseteq |U(x)|$; $A_{x,1} = A_x \cap |X_1|$ is a locally finite closed cover of $|X_1|$; $G_x$ acts on $U(x)_1$ and, as in Lemma 7.3.2 (2017: 7.4), an invariant metric passes to $|U(x)|_1 = |U(x)_1|$, so $A_{x,1}$ is metrizable, hence paracompact, and $|X_1|$ is a locally finite union of closed paracompact sets (Proposition 2.7.4 (2017: 2.17)). **The formalized proof** proves more, that $|X^1|$ is metrizable ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.metrizableSpace_liftOne_orbitSpace⟧, by Smirnov's theorem pulled back along $|X^1| \to |X|$ (Part I): a continuous injection into a paracompact Hausdorff space whose points have open neighbourhoods with metrizable preimages has a metrizable source ⟦Chapter2/Metrizable · metrizableSpace_of_pullback⟧. *Step 1, the restricted action.* For a natural representation at $x$, $G_x$ acts on $U(x)_1 = U(x) \cap X_1$ by the level-$1$ lifts of the $\Phi(g)$, homeomorphisms of $U(x)_1$ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.liftU⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.liftΦ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.liftMulAction⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.continuous_liftSmul⟧. "$U(x)_1$ has the natural $G_x$-action" is read as this restricted action only: $U(x)_1$ need not be connected in $X^1$, so it is not a natural representation of $X^1$. *Step 2, the fibres.* Points of $U(x)_1$ have the same image in $|X^1|$ iff they are in one $G_x$-orbit, by Theorem 7.1.13 (3) (2017: 7.1) and §VII.3 ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.liftOne_π_eq_iff⟧. *Step 3, the metric.* $G_x\backslash U(x)_1$ is metrizable by the text's $\hat\rho$, the argument of Lemma 7.3.2 (2017: 7.4) repeated for a finite group acting by homeomorphisms on a metrizable space ⟦Chapter7/Lift · lvMaxDist⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · lvQuotDist⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · metrizableSpace_orbitRel_quotient_of_finite⟧. *Step 4, Proposition 7.1.19 (2017: 7.6) on level $1$.* $G_x\backslash U(x)_1 \to |X^1|$ is an open embedding ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.liftOrbitQuotientMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isOpenEmbedding_liftOrbitQuotientMap⟧ onto the preimage of $|U(x)|$ ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.range_liftOrbitQuotientMap⟧, so that preimage is metrizable ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.metrizableSpace_preimage_orbitIncl⟧. *Step 5.* $|X|$ is paracompact by hypothesis and Hausdorff by Lemma 7.3.4 (2017: 7.6), and every point has the open neighbourhood $|U(x)|$; the pulled-back Smirnov theorem gives $|X^1|$ metrizable, hence paracompact (Stone). The regularity of $|X^1|$ and Michael's theorem are not needed on this route, though both are available (§§VII.19, VII.20) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 83) (pp. 340–342 (2017 pp. 249–250)).

### VII.24 Theorem 7.5.4 (2017: 7.3), Definition 7.5.5 (2017: 7.16), Remark 7.5.6 (2017: 7.2), and the statement of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4)

**Theorem 7.5.4 (2017: 7.3)** (V7.55) ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_5_4⟧. *If $|X|$ is paracompact, every open cover $(O_\lambda)$ of $|X|$ has a subordinate partition of unity $(\sigma_\lambda)$, and every cover $(U_\lambda)$ of $X$ by saturated open sets has a subordinate continuous partition of unity $(\beta_\lambda)$ taking equal values on isomorphic objects.* *Step 1.* The first statement is Mathlib's existence of subordinate partitions of unity on a paracompact normal space ⟦Mathlib/Topology/PartitionOfUnity · PartitionOfUnity.exists_isSubordinate⟧. *Hidden hypothesis:* normality, which needs $|X|$ Hausdorff — Lemma 7.3.4 (2017: 7.6) — besides paracompact. *Step 2.* For the second, $O_\lambda = \pi(U_\lambda)$ is open (Proposition 7.1.8 (2017: 7.1)), and $\beta_\lambda = \sigma_\lambda \circ \pi$ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.orbitPullback⟧ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.orbitPullback_apply⟧ has $\beta_\lambda(s\varphi) = \beta_\lambda(t\varphi)$ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.orbitPullback_src⟧. *Step 3, supports.* $\mathrm{supp}(\sigma_\lambda \circ \pi) \subseteq \pi^{-1}(\mathrm{supp}\,\sigma_\lambda) \subseteq \pi^{-1}(\pi(U_\lambda)) = U_\lambda$, since $U_\lambda$ is saturated ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.tsupport_orbitPullback_subset⟧ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.orbitPullback_isSubordinate⟧. *Step 4, local finiteness.* If an open $V \ni \pi(x)$ meets finitely many supports of the $\sigma_\lambda$, the saturated open $\pi^{-1}(V)$ meets finitely many supports of the $\beta_\lambda$ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.exists_isSaturated_nhds_finite_orbitPullback⟧. "Subordinate" is Mathlib's, $\mathrm{supp}\,\sigma_\lambda \subseteq O_\lambda$; "some of the $\sigma_\lambda \equiv 0$" says only that the index set is $\Lambda$ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 90) (2017 p. 250).

**Definition 7.5.5 (2017: 7.16)** (V7.56). $X$ has sc-smooth partitions of unity if every cover of $X$ by saturated open sets has a subordinate sc-smooth partition of unity $(\beta_\lambda)$ with (1) every point having a saturated open neighbourhood meeting finitely many supports and (2) $\beta_\lambda(s\varphi) = \beta_\lambda(t\varphi)$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.HasScPartitionsOfUnity⟧, the partitions being Part I's ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.IsScSmoothPartitionOfUnity⟧ with supports the closed supports and index types in the universe of $X$. The hypothesis is satisfiable: for the trivial ep-groupoid it reduces to Part I's sc-smooth partitions of unity ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.hasScPartitionsOfUnity_trivial⟧, which $\mathbb R^n$ has ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · rnPolyfold_admitsScPartitionsOfUnity⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 91) (pp. 341–343 (2017 pp. 250–251)).

**Remark 7.5.6 (2017: 7.2)** (V7.57). Apart from sc-Hilbert spaces, the existence of sc-smooth partitions of unity is "a zoo"; the remark is an assessment, with nothing to formalize, and the sc-Hilbert case is Corollary 7.6.6, now as printed (§§VII.29, VII.48) (2017 p. 251).

**Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4)** (V7.58) ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_5_7⟧. *If $|X|$ is paracompact and the object M-polyfold admits sc-smooth partitions of unity, $X$ has sc-smooth partitions of unity.* The proof is the text's Theorem 7.6.4 (2017: 7.6) (§§VII.27–VII.28). The hypotheses are satisfiable, by the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^n$ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_5_7_hypotheses_rn⟧ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.hasScPartitionsOfUnity_trivial_rn_of_theorem_7_5_7⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, items 94, 105) (2017 p. 251).

### VII.25 Definition 7.5.8 (2017: 7.17), Propositions 7.5.9 and 7.5.10 (2017: 7.13 and 7.14)

**Definition 7.5.8 (2017: 7.17)** (V7.59). $Q \subseteq X$ is *proper* if $t : s^{-1}(Q) \to X$ is proper ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.IsProperSubset⟧, and an open $U$ has the *properness property* if $\mathrm{cl}_XU$ is proper ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.HasPropernessProperty⟧; every $x$ has such a $U$, by Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3) ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.exists_hasPropernessProperty⟧. In metrizable spaces $Q$ is proper iff $s^{-1}(Q) \cap t^{-1}(K)$ is compact for every compact $K$ ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.isProperSubset_iff_isCompact⟧, and for closed $Q$ iff the sequential criterion holds ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.isProperSubset_iff_exists_tendsto_subseq⟧. Basic facts: a closed subset of a proper set is proper ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.IsProperSubset.of_subset⟧; $\emptyset$, finite unions and compact sets are proper ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.isProperSubset_empty⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.IsProperSubset.union⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.isProperSubset_biUnion⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.isProperSubset_iUnion⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.isProperSubset_of_isCompact⟧; an open set inside one with the properness property has it ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.HasPropernessProperty.isProperSubset⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.HasPropernessProperty.mono⟧, and every neighbourhood of $x$ contains an open, also an open connected, neighbourhood of $x$ with the properness property ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.exists_hasPropernessProperty_subset⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.exists_hasPropernessProperty_isConnected_subset⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 92) (2017 p. 251).

**Proposition 7.5.9 (2017: 7.13)** (V7.60) ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_5_9⟧. *A proper subset is closed.* The text: for $x_n \to x$ in $Q$, the units $1_{x_n}$ lie in the compact $(t|s^{-1}(Q))^{-1}(\{x_n\} \cup \{x\})$, a subsequence converges to some $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) \in Q$, and $s(\varphi) = x$. The formalization is this argument with the compact preimage (§VII.2) ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.IsProperSubset.isClosed⟧ (2017 p. 251).

**Proposition 7.5.10 (2017: 7.14)** (V7.61). *(1) If $Q$ is proper, $\pi(Q)$ is closed. (2) If $|X|$ is paracompact, $A \subseteq |X|$ is closed iff $A = \pi(Q)$ for a proper $Q$.* **(1)** ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_5_10_one⟧. The text uses sequences $\varphi_k : x_k \to y_k$ with $x_k \in Q$, $y_k \to y$. The formalization uses the closed-map property: a set of $|X|$ is closed iff its preimage is ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.isClosed_iff_preimage_π⟧, and $\pi^{-1}(\pi(Q)) = t(s^{-1}(Q))$ is the image of the closed $s^{-1}(Q)$ (Proposition 7.5.9 (2017: 7.13)) under the proper, hence closed, $t$ ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.isClosed_saturation_of_isProperSubset⟧. The proof's "$x = s(\varphi) \in Q$" reuses the name $x$ (possible misprint).

**(2)** ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_5_10_two⟧. One direction is (1). **The text's proof** of the other chooses for $z \in A$ a representative $x_z$ and a neighbourhood $U(x_z)$ with the natural action whose closure $Q_z$ is proper; by Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7) the closed, hence paracompact, $A$ has a locally finite cover by closed $A_i \subseteq \pi(Q_{z_i})$; $P_i = (\pi|\mathrm{cl}_XU(x_{z_i}))^{-1}(A_i)$ and $Q = \bigcup P_i$ has $\pi(Q) = A$; it is proper because only finitely many $A_i$ meet a neighbourhood of $\pi(y)$, so the sources lie in finitely many $P_i$. Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7) assumes a regular Hausdorff space. **The formalized proof** needs only the paracompactness of $|X|$. *Step 1.* Representatives $x_z$ are chosen by the quotient, and $V(x_z)$ is any open neighbourhood with the properness property; the natural action is not used. *Step 2, an open refinement.* The open sets $\pi(V(x_z))$ cover the closed $A$; Mathlib gives an open locally finite precise refinement $(v_z)$ of this cover of $A$, from paracompactness alone ⟦Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Paracompact · precise_refinement_set⟧. *Step 3, closures.* $P_z = \mathrm{cl}_XV(x_z) \cap \pi^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}(v_z) \cap A)$ is a closed subset of the proper $\mathrm{cl}_XV(x_z)$, hence proper, with $\pi(P_z) \subseteq \mathrm{cl}(v_z) \cap A$; and $\pi(P_z) \supseteq v_z \cap A$, since $v_z \subseteq \pi(V(x_z))$. As the $v_z$ cover $A$, $\pi(\bigcup P_z) = A$. *Step 4, properness of $Q = \bigcup P_z$.* The closures $\mathrm{cl}(v_z)$ of a locally finite family are locally finite, and a union of proper sets whose images form a locally finite family is proper: a compact $K$ has compact $\pi(K)$, which meets only finitely many $\mathrm{cl}(v_z)$ ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.isProperSubset_iUnion_of_locallyFinite⟧. Neither Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7) nor the regularity of $|X|$ is used, and no version under a regularity hypothesis is needed; the closed refinement of Michael's theorem would give the text's route as well (§VII.20). The text writes $\mathrm{cl}_X(U_{x_{z_i}})$ for $\mathrm{cl}_X(U(x_{z_i}))$ (possible misprint; Findings, Chapter 7, item 92) (pp. 342–344 (2017 pp. 251–252)).

### VII.26 Appendix §7.6.1 (2017 §7.5.1): the proof of Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1) (Theorem 7.6.1 (2017: 7.5), Lemmas 7.6.2 and 7.6.3 (2017: 7.8 and 7.9))

**Theorem 7.6.1 (2017: 7.5)** (V7.62) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_6_1⟧ is Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1) with $\Phi(g) = t_g \circ s_g^{-1}$; it is stated as the same theorem. **The text's proof** (pp. 344–346 (2017 pp. 253–254)): for every $g \in G_{x_0}$ choose contractible open $N^t_g$, $N^s_g$ on which $t$ and $s$ are sc-diffeomorphisms onto an open $U_0 \ni x_0$, disjoint for distinct $g$ since $G_{x_0}$ is finite; $N_g = N^t_g \cap N^s_g$, $s_g = s|N_g$, $t_g = t|N_g$; Lemmas 7.6.2 and 7.6.3 (2017: 7.8 and 7.9) give $U$; $\Phi(g) = t_g \circ s_g^{-1}$, a homomorphism "since the neighborhoods $N_g$ are disjoint and since the structure maps are continuous"; $\Gamma(g, y) = s_g^{-1}(y)$. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1, the sheets* ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.exists_sheets⟧. $G_{x_0}$ is finite (Proposition 7.1.12 (2017: 7.4)) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.finite_isotropy⟧; Hausdorff separation of the finite set $G_{x_0} \subseteq \mathbf X$ gives pairwise disjoint open $N_g \ni g$, shrunk so that $s$ is an sc-diffeomorphism from $N_g$ onto its open image with inverse $\sigma_g = s_g^{-1}$; $t$ is one too, which is recorded but not used. Only connectedness will be needed, not contractibility. *Step 2, $U \subseteq V$.* The proof does not mention $V$; it starts at $U_0 = V \cap \bigcap_g s(N_g)$. *Step 3, Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8), then Lemma 7.6.3 (2017: 7.9)* (below). *Step 4, the homomorphism* ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.hat⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.isScSmoothOn_hat⟧. On the connected $U$, $y \mapsto \sigma_{gh}(y)$ and $y \mapsto \sigma_g(\Phi(h)y) \circ \sigma_h(y)$ are continuous sections of $s$ — the second by (4) in the sheet form — agreeing at $x_0$, so they agree on $U$ (§VII.7) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.eqOn_σ_mul⟧ and $\Phi(gh) = \Phi(g)\Phi(h)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.hat_mul⟧. In the same way $\sigma_1$ is the unit section $u$ on $U$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.eqOn_σ_one⟧ and $\Phi(1) = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.hat_one⟧, which the text does not mention and which makes $\Phi(g)$ an sc-diffeomorphism with inverse $\Phi(g^{-1})$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.isScDiffeoOn_hat⟧. As we read it, "since the $N_g$ are disjoint and the structure maps are continuous" shows only that the sheet index is locally constant; connectedness of $U$ makes it constant. *Step 5, (3).* A morphism $h$ between points of $U$ lies in some $N_{g'}$ by Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8), and $s$ is injective there, so $h = \sigma_{g'}(sh)$; disjointness of the $N_g$ gives uniqueness ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.eq_of_mem_N⟧. *Step 6.* The natural representation is built on every open connected invariant $U \subseteq \bigcap_g s(N_g)$ with the conclusion of Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.mkRep⟧, and Lemmas 7.6.2, 7.6.3 (2017: 7.8, 7.9) provide one ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.exists_naturalRep_sheets⟧. "$\Phi : G_x \to \mathrm{Diff}_{sc}(U)$" is read with $G_{x_0}$ (possible misprint; Findings, Chapter 7, item 29).

**Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8)** (V7.63) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_6_2⟧. *There is an open $U_1 \subseteq U_0$ of $x_0$ such that every morphism with source and target in $U_1$ lies in some $N_g$* — for any open $N_g \ni g$ and any neighbourhood $U_0$; the sheet property is not used. **The text's proof**: otherwise there are $h_k \notin \bigcup N_g$ with $s(h_k), t(h_k) \to x_0$; by properness $h_{k_l} \to h$, necessarily $h \in G_{x_0}$, so $h \in N_g$ for some $g$, a contradiction. **The formalized proof** follows it. *Step 1.* The sequence is taken along a countable decreasing basis of $x_0$, $X$ being metrizable. *Step 2.* "By the properness assumption" is Definition 7.1.3 (3) (2017: 7.3) at $x_0$, which applies to the $h_k$ with $s(h_k) \in \mathrm{cl}V(x_0)$, i.e. to all large $k$ (§VII.2). *Step 3.* "Necessarily $h \in G_{x_0}$": $t(h) = x_0$ comes with the properness, $s(h) = x_0$ from the continuity of $s$ and the uniqueness of limits. *Step 4.* $N_g$ is an open neighbourhood of the limit, so eventually $h_{k_l} \in N_g$. "The properness assumption of ep-polyfolds" is read as that of ep-groupoids (possible misprint; Findings, Chapter 7, item 30) (pp. 344–346 (2017 pp. 253–254)).

**Lemma 7.6.3 (2017: 7.9)** (V7.64) ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_6_3⟧. *There is an open $U_2 \subseteq U_1$ of $x_0$ such that $U = \bigcup_g t_gs_g^{-1}(U_2)$ lies in $U_1$ and is invariant under all $t_gs_g^{-1}$.* **The text's proof**: choose $U_2$ so small that $U$ and $t_gs_g^{-1}(U)$ lie in $U_1$; for $x = t_hs_h^{-1}(u)$, the point $v = t_gs_g^{-1}t_hs_h^{-1}(u) \in U_1$ is the target of a morphism $u \to v$, which by Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8) is $s_{g'}^{-1}(u)$, so $v = t_{g'}s_{g'}^{-1}(u) \in U$. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1.* Each $t_gs_g^{-1}$ is continuous at its fixed point $x_0$ and $G_{x_0}$ is finite, so a $U_2$ with $t_hs_h^{-1}(U_2) \subseteq U_1$ and $t_gs_g^{-1}t_hs_h^{-1}(U_2) \subseteq U_1$ for all $g, h$ exists; it is taken *connected* (§VII.7). *Step 2.* $U$ is open, $t$ being open and $s_g^{-1}(U_2) = N_g \cap s^{-1}(U_2)$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.unionHat⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.isOpen_image_hat⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.isOpen_unionHat⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.mem_unionHat_iff⟧, and connected, a union of connected sets through $x_0 = t_gs_g^{-1}(x_0)$, so no passage to a component is needed ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.isConnected_unionHat⟧. *Step 3, invariance.* The morphism $u \to v$ is $\sigma_g(x) \circ \sigma_h(u)$, composable because $x \in U_1 \subseteq s(N_g)$; it lies in some $N_{g'}$ by Lemma 7.6.2 (2017: 7.8), and "it has necessarily the form $v = t_{g'}s_{g'}^{-1}(u)$" uses that $s$ is injective on $N_{g'}$ ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · EpGroupoid.NatRepConstruction.Sheets.image_σ⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 31) (2017 p. 254).

### VII.27 Appendix §7.6.2 (2017 §7.5.2): Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10)

**Theorem 7.6.4 (2017: 7.6)** (V7.65) ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_6_4⟧ is Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4), stated again (Findings, Chapter 7, item 95) (2017 p. 255).

**Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10)** (V7.66) ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_6_5⟧. *Let $|X|$ be paracompact and $X$ admit sc-smooth partitions of unity; let $U(x) \subseteq \mathrm{cl}_XU(x) \subseteq V(x)$ be open, $V(x)$ with the natural $G_x$-action and $U(x)$ invariant. A continuous $\beta : X \to [0, 1]$ supported in $U(x)$ and invariant on $V(x)$ lies below an sc-smooth $f \ge 0$ supported in $V(x)$ and invariant on $V(x)$.* The formalization adds the conclusion $\mathrm{supp}f \subseteq \mathrm{cl}_XU(x)$, which the proof gives and Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4) needs, and omits the hypothesis $x \in U(x)$, which the proof does not use and Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4) cannot supply; the paracompactness of $|X|$ and the continuity of $\beta$ are kept, unused. **The text's proof**: open $W(z)$, $z \in V(x)$, with numbers $a_z$ — $\mathrm{cl}W(z) \subseteq U(x)$ and $\beta < a_z$ on $W(z)$ for $z \in U(x)$, otherwise $W(z) \subseteq V(x)$, $\beta|W(z) = 0$, $a_z = 0$; an sc-smooth partition of unity $(\sigma_z)$ of $V(x)$ subordinate to them; $\gamma = \sum\sigma_za_z \ge \beta$, supported in $\mathrm{cl}U(x)$; and $f(y) = |G_x|^{-1}\sum_g\gamma(g \ast y)$. **The formalized proof.** *Step 1, a cover of $X$.* The hypothesis is that $X$, not the open subset $V(x)$, admits sc-smooth partitions of unity, so the cover is completed by $X \setminus \mathrm{cl}U(x)$, where $\beta = 0$ and $a = 0$; and it is coarsened to two sets, $U(x)$ with $a = 1$ (as $\beta \le 1$) and $X \setminus \mathrm{supp}\,\beta$ with $a = 0$. The text's $\mathrm{cl}W(z) \subseteq U(x)$ and $\beta < a_z$ are not needed. *Step 2, $\gamma$.* $\gamma$ is the function attached to $U(x)$ of a partition of unity subordinate to $\{U(x), X \setminus \mathrm{supp}\,\beta\}$: sc-smooth, $\ge 0$, supported in $U(x)$, and $\gamma = 1 \ge \beta$ on $\mathrm{supp}\,\beta$, where the other function vanishes. *Step 3, the average.* $f = |G_x|^{-1}\sum_g\gamma \circ \Phi(g)$ on $V(x)$ and $0$ elsewhere. Each $\gamma \circ \Phi(g)$, extended by $0$, is supported in $\Phi(g)^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}U(x)) = \mathrm{cl}U(x) \subseteq V(x)$ by the invariance of $U(x)$, hence sc-smooth on $X$ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · isScSmoothMap_real_of_tsupport_subset⟧ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · isScSmoothMap_real_of_isScSmoothOn_nhds⟧. *Step 4.* $\beta \le f$ by the invariance of $\beta$: $\beta(y) = \beta(g \ast y) \le \gamma(g \ast y)$ for every $g$. $f$ is invariant by the reindexing $g \mapsto gh$, and $\mathrm{supp}f \subseteq \mathrm{cl}U(x)$ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 93) (2017 p. 255).

### VII.28 Appendix §7.6.2 (2017 §7.5.2): the proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4)

**The text's proof** (pp. 346–347 (2017 pp. 255–256)). For every $x$ choose an open $V(x)$ with (1) an open $W(x)$ with the natural $G_x$-action, $V(x) \subseteq \mathrm{cl}V(x) \subseteq W(x)$ and $V(x)$ invariant; (2) $t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}V(x)) \to X$ proper; (3) $V(x) \subseteq U_\lambda$ for some $\lambda$; (4) $(\pi^{-1}(|V(x)|) \setminus V(x)) \cap W(x) = \emptyset$. Take a locally finite refinement $(V'_i)$ of $(|V(x)|)$ with $V'_i \subseteq |V(x_i)|$, open $V''_i \subseteq \mathrm{cl}V''_i \subseteq V'_i$ covering $|X|$, $U''_i = V(x_i) \cap \pi^{-1}(V''_i)$ and a partition of unity $(\beta_i)$ subordinate to $(V''_i)$. "Approximate $(\beta_i \circ \pi)|V(x_i)$ using Lemma 7.10" gives $f_i$ supported in $V(x_i)$; averaging, extending to the saturation and by $0$ gives $h_i$; $h = \sum h_i > 0$ is locally finite and $(h_i/h)$ is the partition of unity.

**The formalized proof** (V7.67) builds the same functions $h_i$, but for a Urysohn lemma, and normalizes with Mathlib's bump coverings, as Part I's Theorem 5.5.10 (2017: 5.12) does (§V.25) ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_approx⟧. The four points where the text needed more than a reading are marked (a)–(d).

*Step 1, properties (1)–(3)* ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.exists_invariant_nhds_of_isOpen⟧. Given $x$ and an open $O \ni x$, take $V_0 \subseteq O$ with the properness property (§VII.25), $W(x) = U$ of a natural representation inside $V_0$ (Theorem 7.1.13 (2017: 7.1)), an open $N \ni x$ with $\mathrm{cl}N \subseteq W(x)$, $X$ being regular, and $V(x) = \bigcap_g\Phi(g)^{-1}(N)$: open, invariant, $x \in V(x)$, $\mathrm{cl}V(x) \subseteq \mathrm{cl}N \subseteq W(x)$, and proper over its closure by §VII.25. Elements of one orbit have one image in $|X|$ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.π_Φ_eq⟧.

*Step 2, (4) follows from (1)* and is not a further choice. The morphisms between points of $W(x)$ are the $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$ (Theorem 7.1.13 (3) (2017: 7.1)), so a point of $W(x)$ isomorphic to a point of the invariant $V(x)$ is $g \ast v$ for some $v \in V(x)$, hence lies in $V(x)$ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.mem_of_π_mem_image_of_invariant⟧ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.saturation_diff_inter_eq_empty⟧.

*Step 3, extension to the saturation.* A $G_x$-invariant $f$ on $W(x)$ defines $F$ on $|X|$ by $F(|y|) = f(y)$ for $y \in W(x)$ and $0$ elsewhere, well defined because points of $W(x)$ in one orbit differ by the natural action (§VII.11) ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.orbitExtension⟧ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.orbitExtension_π⟧ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.orbitExtension_nonneg⟧ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.support_orbitExtension_subset⟧. (d) *$F \circ \pi$ is sc-smooth* when $f$ is sc-smooth with $\mathrm{supp}f \subseteq \mathrm{cl}V(x)$ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_orbitExtension⟧: $F \circ \pi$ vanishes off the saturation of $\mathrm{supp}f$, which is closed because $\mathrm{supp}f \subseteq \mathrm{cl}V(x)$ is proper by (2) ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · EpGroupoid.isClosed_saturation_of_isProperSubset⟧; near a point $y \cong z$ of that saturation, with $\varphi : z \to y$, $F \circ \pi = f \circ s \circ (t|\mathbf U(\varphi))^{-1}$ (Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4)). The text does not mention the closedness.

*Step 4, the invariant Urysohn lemma* ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.exists_isScSmoothMap_orbit_urysohn⟧: *for disjoint closed $s', t' \subseteq |X|$ there is a continuous $F : |X| \to [0, 1]$ with $F \circ \pi$ sc-smooth, $F = 0$ on $s'$ and $F = 1$ on $t'$.* For every $x \in \pi^{-1}(t')$ Step 1 gives $V(x) \subseteq \mathrm{cl}V(x) \subseteq W(x) \subseteq \pi^{-1}(|X| \setminus s')$. The open sets $|V(x)|$ cover the closed $t'$; take an open locally finite precise refinement $(V'_x)$ of this cover of $t'$ ⟦Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Paracompact · precise_refinement_set⟧ and a bump covering $(b_x)$ of $t'$ subordinate to it ⟦Mathlib/Topology/PartitionOfUnity · BumpCovering.exists_isSubordinate⟧, whose $\mathrm{supp}\,b_x \subseteq V'_x$ takes the place of the text's $V''_x$; put $U''_x = V(x) \cap \pi^{-1}(V'_x)$. (b) *The cut-off.* $c_x = b_x \circ \pi$ on $V(x)$, $0$ elsewhere, is continuous and supported in $U''_x$: a point of $\mathrm{cl}V(x) \cap \pi^{-1}(\mathrm{supp}\,b_x)$ lies in $W(x)$ and is isomorphic to a point of $V(x)$, as $\mathrm{supp}\,b_x \subseteq |V(x)|$, hence lies in $V(x)$ by (4). (a) *Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10)* is applied with $W(x)$ in the role of $V(x)$ and $U''_x$ in the role of $U(x)$: its hypothesis $\mathrm{cl}U''_x \subseteq W(x)$, with the natural action on $W(x)$, holds by (1), and $U''_x$ is invariant. The text's "approximate $(\beta_i \circ \pi)|V(x_i)$ using Lemma 7.10" reads as $V(x_i)$ in the role of $V(x)$ (possible misprint). It gives an invariant sc-smooth $f_x \ge c_x$ with $\mathrm{supp}f_x \subseteq \mathrm{cl}U''_x$, and $F_x$ its extension (Step 3), using $\mathrm{cl}U''_x \subseteq \mathrm{cl}V(x)$. (c) *Local finiteness.* $\mathrm{supp}(F_x \circ \pi) \subseteq \pi^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}V'_x)$ by the support bound of Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10), and $(\mathrm{cl}V'_x)$ is locally finite, so $G = \sum_xF_x$ is a locally finite sum. The text does not state this bound: Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10) as stated gives only $\mathrm{supp}f_x \subseteq W(x)$, and the saturations of the $W(x)$ need not be locally finite. *The function.* $G \circ \pi$ is sc-smooth, $G = 0$ on $s'$ since every $W(x)$ misses $\pi^{-1}(s')$, and $G \ge 1$ on $t'$, since at every point of $t'$ some $b_x$ equals $1$, and then $f_x \ge c_x = 1$ over it; $F = \tau \circ G$ with Mathlib's smooth transition function $\tau$ ⟦Mathlib/Analysis/SpecialFunctions/SmoothTransition · Real.smoothTransition⟧, $0$ on $(-\infty, 0]$ and $1$ on $[1, \infty)$.

*Step 5, the normalization* ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_5_7⟧. Given a saturated open cover $(U_\lambda)$, the $\pi(U_\lambda)$ cover $|X|$ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.iUnion_image_π_eq_univ⟧. Mathlib's existence of bump coverings subordinate to an open cover with all functions satisfying a predicate for which Urysohn's lemma holds ⟦Mathlib/Topology/PartitionOfUnity · BumpCovering.exists_isSubordinate_of_prop⟧, for the class of the $g$ with $g \circ \pi$ sc-smooth and Step 4 as its input, gives $(b_\lambda)$ on the paracompact normal $|X|$, subordinate to $(\pi(U_\lambda))$, each $b_\lambda \circ \pi$ sc-smooth. The partition $\rho_\lambda = b_\lambda\prod_{\mu<\lambda}(1 - b_\mu)$ ⟦Mathlib/Topology/PartitionOfUnity · BumpCovering.toPartitionOfUnity⟧ is locally a finite product of such functions, so $\rho_\lambda \circ \pi$ is sc-smooth, and $\beta_\lambda = \rho_\lambda \circ \pi$, Theorem 7.5.4's (2017: 7.3) pull-back (§VII.24), has the properties (1), (2) of Definition 7.5.5 (2017: 7.16). This replaces the text's $(h_i/h)$ and the passage from the index set of the refinement back to $\Lambda$, which the text leaves implicit. "We average using the $G_{x_i}$-action": $f_x$ is already invariant by Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10), and no second average is taken. "$t : s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}_X(V(x)) \to X$" has an unbalanced parenthesis (possible misprint; Findings, Chapter 7, items 94, 96) (pp. 346–347 (2017 pp. 255–256)).

### VII.29 Corollary 7.6.6 (2017: 7.3)

**Corollary 7.6.6 (2017: 7.3)** (V7.68) ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_6_6⟧. *If $|X|$ is paracompact and the object M-polyfold has an atlas whose local models have Hilbert spaces $E_0$, every saturated open cover of $X$ has a subordinate sc-smooth partition of unity of $X$.* The text cites Part I's Proposition 5.5.8 (2017: 5.6), Theorem 5.5.10 (2017: 5.12) and Corollary 5.5.17 (2017: 5.2), the ingredients of Part I's theorem that such an M-polyfold admits sc-smooth partitions of unity (§§V.25–V.26) ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · MPolyfold.admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_hilbert⟧, and Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4) applies. "An atlas consisting of charts whose local models have Hilbert spaces" is existential, one chart per point; "every compatible chart has a Hilbert $E_0$" would be unsatisfiable. In the first reading, as in Part I, the theorem of Godefroy–Troyanski–Whitfield–Zizler (Part I's Theorem 5.5.16 (2017: 5.14)) was an explicit hypothesis ⟦Chapter5/PartitionsOfUnity · GodefroyTroyanskiWhitfieldZizlerStatement⟧ (gap G.53), which holds for finite-dimensional spaces ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · godefroyTroyanskiWhitfieldZizlerStatement_of_finiteDimensional⟧ ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · admitsContDiffPartitionsOfUnity_of_finiteDimensional⟧. The hypotheses are satisfiable on $\mathbb R^1$ ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · rnPolyfold_one_hilbert_hypothesis⟧ ⟦Chapter7/LocalDiffeo · rnPolyfold_one_admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_hilbert⟧ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_6_6_hypotheses_rn⟧. *The corollary as printed.* Part I now proves Theorem 5.5.16 ⟦Chapter5/GapP1_GTWZ · theorem_5_5_16⟧; the case used here is that of a separable space ⟦Chapter5/GapP1_SeparablePOU · godefroyTroyanskiWhitfieldZizlerStatement_of_separable⟧, $E_0$ being separable for every sc-Banach space, so an M-polyfold with Hilbert $E_0$ admits sc-smooth partitions of unity with no hypothesis ⟦Chapter5/GapP1_SeparablePOU · MPolyfold.admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_hilbert_unconditional⟧, and Corollary 7.6.6 holds as printed ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ACor766 · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_6_6_unconditional⟧, with the same witness on $\mathbb R^1$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ACor766 · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_6_6_hypotheses_rn_unconditional⟧ (gap G.53, closed; §VII.48) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 95, 106) (p. 347 (2017 p. 256)).

### VII.30 Witnesses and counterexamples

Every hypothesis of the chapter that is a predicate on ep-groupoids or on their data is shown satisfiable, and for the readings that do not hold a counterexample is given (Findings, Chapter 7, items 100–107, 152, 156).

**The trivial ep-groupoid** of an M-polyfold $Z$, with only units, exists on every M-polyfold ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.trivial⟧. It is tame for tame $Z$ and for $\mathbb R^n$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isTame_trivial⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isTame_trivial_rn⟧, effective with $X_{reg} = Z$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isEffective_trivial⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.regularSet_trivial⟧, every closed set is proper and every open set has the properness property ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isProperSubset_trivial⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.hasPropernessProperty_trivial⟧, $|X| \cong Z$ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.trivialOrbitHomeomorph⟧ is paracompact ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_trivial⟧, and it has natural representations on every connected open neighbourhood ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.trivialNaturalRep⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.trivialNaturalRepFinite⟧. Its witnesses are vacuous for the isotropy, which the next ones are not.

**The translation groupoid $K \ltimes U$** of a finite discrete group acting on an M-polyfold by sc-smooth maps, with morphisms the product with the discrete M-polyfold ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.actionMorPolyfold⟧, is an ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.actionEpGroupoid⟧: $s$ is a projection, $t$ a projection after the shear ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.actionShear⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.action_isLocalScDiffeo_src⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.action_isLocalScDiffeo_tgt⟧, (4) holds in the sheet form ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.action_isScSmoothCompSheet⟧ and $t$ is proper on all of $\mathbf X$ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.action_isProperMap_tgt⟧. Its isotropy is the stabilizer ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.isotropyEquivStabilizer⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.isRegular_action_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.regularSet_action⟧, its orbit space $U/K$ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.action_π_eq_π_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.actionOrbitHomeomorph⟧, its proper sets the closed sets ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.isProperSubset_action⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.isProperSubset_action_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.hasPropernessProperty_action⟧, and its orbit space is paracompact for second countable $U$ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_action⟧.

**$\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ by reflection** ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.isScSmoothMap_units_smul⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.reflectionEpGroupoid⟧ is effective ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.isEffective_reflection⟧ with a non-trivial isotropy element $(-1, 0)$ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.reflectionIsotropyNegOne⟧, so Definition 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11) is met non-vacuously ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.isEffective_reflection_nonvacuous⟧; $X_{reg} = \mathbb R \setminus \{0\}$ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.regularSet_reflection⟧, $G_0 \cong \mathbb Z/2$ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.reflectionIsotropyZeroEquiv⟧, $T_x = 1$ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.trivialSubgroup_reflection⟧; it is tame and has paracompact orbit space ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.isTame_reflection⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_reflection⟧.

**The trivial action of $\mathbb Z/3$ on $\mathbb R$** ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.trivialZ3EpGroupoid⟧ has $G_x \cong \mathbb Z/3$ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.trivialZ3IsotropyEquiv⟧, $T_x = G_x$ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.trivialSubgroup_trivialZ3⟧ ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.trivialZ3TrivialSubgroupEquiv⟧, is not effective ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.not_isEffective_trivialZ3⟧, and its regular set is empty ⟦Chapter7/NonVacuity · Examples.regularSet_trivialZ3⟧: the text's "examples show that the regular set can be empty" (p. 308 (2017 p. 239)). **Zhou's retract** ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.X⟧, $\mathbb Z/2$ acting by $(t, f) \mapsto (t, -f)$ on the sc-smooth retract of $\mathbb R \oplus L^2(\mathbb R)$ of Appendix 7.6.3, for every choice of the data ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.Data⟧, of which one exists ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.Data.std⟧: an ep-groupoid in which $T_R$ is not Hausdorff and LUC and (ZHOU) fail (§VII.47; Findings, Chapter 7, item 156).

**The Čech groupoid of a Prüfer-type surface** ⟦Chapter7/PropertyFiveResearch · EpGroupoid.Examples.Pruefer.epGroupoid⟧: an ep-groupoid whose orbit space is Hausdorff and not paracompact, so property (5) of Definition 7.5.1 (2017: 7.15) is not a consequence of (1)–(4) (§VII.49; Findings, Chapter 7, item 152).

### VII.31 What is not formalized

Nothing of the chapter: every gap is closed, and the one narrower row is a reading (§VII.50). In detail:

- **Closed since the first reading.** $T\varphi$ as a bounded linear isomorphism and an sc-isomorphism (gap G.70), with the tangent facts (3), (4) on $A$ (§VII.44); $|X_\infty|$ and $|X_\infty| = \bigcap_k|X_k|$ (gap G.72) and the density of $X_\infty$ in $X_k$ (gap G.73) (§VII.44); the M-polyfold $\mathbf X^R$ (gap G.71): paracompact for every ep-groupoid, Hausdorff exactly under LUC, which is the 2021 text's hypothesis (§§VII.34, VII.35, VII.48); Corollary 7.6.6 (2017: 7.3) as printed, Part I's gap G.53 being closed (§§VII.29, VII.48).
- **The 2017 statements that do not hold as we read them.** The remark after Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7) for functors that are only sc-smooth on objects (§VII.4; the 2021 remark holds), and Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017) for every ep-groupoid (§VII.16; the 2021 forms hold). Each has a counterexample in Lean.
- **The open question of p. 340 (2017 p. 249)**, whether (5) follows from (1)–(4): settled negatively (§VII.49). Remark 7.5.2 (2017: 7.1) has no formal content, and Remark 7.5.6 (2017: 7.2) is an assessment, with nothing to formalize (§§VII.23, VII.24; Findings, Chapter 7, items 82, 113, 152).
- **Not needed.** The contractibility of $N^t_g$, $N^s_g$ in the proof of Theorem 7.6.1 (2017: 7.5) (p. 344 (2017 p. 253)): connectedness suffices (§VII.26; Findings, Chapter 7, item 29). The identification $(\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X)^1 = \mathbf X^1\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X^1$, which the sheet form avoids (§VII.22). The comparison with the classical properness of $(s, t)$ on 2017 p. 227 has no formal content.
- **Gaps of Part I taken up**: G.15 (Lemma 2.7.3 (2017: 2.7), Proposition 2.7.4 (2017: 2.17)) is formalized (§VII.20); the local path connectedness of M-polyfolds (§VII.7) and, now, the path connectedness of $U \cap X_\infty$ (§VII.45); the tameness of $X^1$, left open in Part I, is proved (§VII.22) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 114).

### VII.32 What the formalization taught us

**Continuity is the content of the remark after Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7).** The formula $f(\gamma) = (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}(f(s\gamma))$ is right wherever it applies; what it needs is a neighbourhood of $\varphi$ mapped into the sheet at $f(\varphi)$, and for that the functor must be continuous on morphisms. A functor of the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action that swaps two isotropy elements on one side of $0$ shows that sc-smoothness on objects alone does not give it, as we read the remark (§VII.4).

**Connectedness is the hidden hypothesis of the natural representation.** Every proof that $\Phi$ is a homomorphism, that $\Gamma$ is a functor, that $\Gamma(1, a) = 1_a$ (Lemma 7.2.2 (2017: 7.2)), and that two natural representations agree compares two continuous sections of $s$ that agree at $x$; without connectedness they agree only near $x$. The text chooses a connected $U(x)$ on 2017 p. 231 and never states it again. Making $U$ connected a field of the datum, and proving that M-polyfolds are locally path connected, settles all of these at once (§§VII.7–VII.9, VII.26).

**"Small" neighbourhoods and the kernel of $\Phi$.** Since sc-smooth maps are not analytic, the kernel of $\Phi$ can depend on $U(x)$, and the text's "for $U(x)$ small, $\ker\Phi = T_x$" needs a precise form: a neighbourhood $N$ of $x$ such that every natural representation inside $N$ has kernel $T_x$, and the intrinsic description $g \in T_x$ iff $s = t$ near $g$. That description turns Definition 7.2.1 (2017: 7.11) into $T_x = \{1_x\}$, proves the effectiveness of $X_R$ in one line, and gives the conjugation $\varphi T_x\varphi^{-1} = T_y$ that the composition of $X_R$ needs and the text does not state (§§VII.15, VII.17).

**The reduced charts do not give Hausdorffness.** The proof of Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) builds charts and sc-smooth transitions for $\mathbf X^R$ without any hypothesis; an M-polyfold also has to be Hausdorff and paracompact, and these do not follow from the charts as we read it. The formalization separates what is proved unconditionally from the two hypotheses, and shows them satisfiable (§VII.16).

**A star instead of an induction.** Proposition 7.1.15 (2017: 7.5) becomes a construction transported from one object along chosen morphisms, with nothing shrunk afterwards; the text's inductive adjustment of components, and most of its possible misprints, have no counterpart (§VII.10).

**Properness does more than sequences.** Where the text extracts convergent subsequences, the formalization mostly uses that a proper map is closed or that preimages of compact sets are compact: Proposition 7.1.10 (2017: 7.3), Proposition 7.5.10 (1) (2017: 7.14), the closedness of points behind Lemma 7.3.4 (2017: 7.6), and the closed saturations behind the sc-smoothness in Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4). With compact sets in place of sequences, Proposition 7.5.10 (2) (2017: 7.14) needs only paracompactness, no regularity (§§VII.5, VII.19, VII.25, VII.28).

**Paracompact without Hausdorff.** Definition 7.5.1 (2017: 7.15) stipulates that paracompact does not include Hausdorff, and Michael's theorem, which the text quotes for regular Hausdorff spaces, holds for regular spaces; one direction holds in every space. This closes gap G.15 of Part I and gives Corollary 7.3.8 (2017: 7.2) its finite and locally finite unions (§§VII.20, VII.21). For Proposition 7.5.3 (2017: 7.12) a shorter route proves more: $|X^1|$ is metrizable (§VII.23).

**Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10) needs its support bound.** As stated, Lemma 7.6.5 (2017: 7.10) bounds the support of $f$ by $V(x)$; the proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4) needs the bound $\mathrm{cl}\,U(x)$, which the lemma's own proof gives, for the sum $\sum h_i$ to be locally finite, and it applies the lemma to sets $U''_i$ that need not contain $x_i$. Stating the lemma with the stronger conclusion and the weaker hypothesis makes the proof of Theorem 7.5.7 (2017: 7.4) go through as written, with $W(x_i)$ in the role of $V(x)$ (§§VII.27–VII.28).

**Paracompactness of the orbit space is a genuine condition.** The text leaves open whether (5) follows from (1)–(4). It does not: the orbit space of an ep-groupoid is locally a finite quotient of an M-polyfold, so every Hausdorff, locally Euclidean space whose atlas has a Čech groupoid with proper target maps is one, and a Prüfer-type surface is such a space without being paracompact. The object space of the example is not second countable, as it must be by Remark 7.5.2 (2017: 7.1) (§VII.49).

**What the tangent of a morphism needs is the linear structure of $T_xX$.** Once Part I gives $T_xX$ its linear structure through charts, Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4) is the chain rule and the fact that the derivative at a smooth point is an sc-operator; nothing in Chapter 7 itself was missing (§VII.44).

### VII.33 The 2021 additions to §7.1: the remark after Definition 7.1.7, Propositions 7.1.14, 7.1.15, Lemma 7.1.16, Corollary 7.1.17

The Springer edition (2021) changes the remark after Definition 7.1.7 and Proposition 7.1.15 and adds Proposition 7.1.14, Lemma 7.1.16 and Corollary 7.1.17; Sections VII.33–VII.41 retell the additions of the 2021 edition, with its numbers and pages (V7.69–V7.98).

**The remark after Definition 7.1.7, 2021 form** (V7.69) ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.remark_definition_7_1_7⟧. *A functor sc-smooth on objects and continuous on morphisms is sc-smooth on morphisms, through $f(\gamma) = (s|U(\psi))^{-1}(f(s(\gamma)))$ on a neighbourhood $U(\varphi)$ mapped into a sheet $U(\psi)$ at $\psi = f(\varphi)$.* The 2021 text adds the continuity on morphisms, the hypothesis under which §VII.4 proved the 2017 remark; the continuity gives the neighbourhood $U(\varphi)$, the sheets give the formula, and sc-smoothness follows as in §VII.4. The functor of the counterexample of §VII.4 is sc-smooth on objects and not continuous on morphisms, so the 2021 hypothesis excludes it ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.remark_definition_7_1_7_remarkFunctor⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 117) (p. 291).

**The data (7.3) and Proposition 7.1.14** (V7.70) ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_14⟧. *For data (7.3) — an open $W(x)$ and sheets $U^s(g)$, $U^t(g)$ of $s$ and $t$ at each $g \in G_x$ onto $W(x)$ — and a representation $(\Phi, \Gamma)$ with the properties of Theorem 7.1.13, there is a $\Phi$-invariant open $V(x) \subseteq W(x) \cap U(x)$ on which $\Gamma(g, v) = s_g^{-1}(v)$ and $\Phi(g)(v) = t(s_g^{-1}(v))$.* The data are a structure ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.IsotropySheetData⟧ and exist at every object ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.exists_isotropySheetData⟧; "neighbourhoods $U^s(g)$, $U^t(g)$ for $g$" is read as neighbourhoods of $g$, without which $\Gamma(g, x) = g = s_g^{-1}(x)$ fails. *The proof.* On the open set $N$ of the $v \in W(x) \cap U(x)$ with $\Gamma(g, v) \in U^s(g) \cap U^t(g)$ for all $g$, $\Gamma(g, v) = s_g^{-1}(s(\Gamma(g, v))) = s_g^{-1}(v)$; applying $t$ gives the formula for $\Phi(g)$, and $\Gamma(g, v) = t_g^{-1}(\Phi(g)(v))$, the identity (7.4) of the proof, is part of the conclusion. $V(x) = \bigcap_g \Phi(g)^{-1}(N)$, a finite intersection, is open and invariant. Property (3) of Theorem 7.1.13 is a hypothesis as printed and is not used. The same holds for every natural representation ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_14_of_naturalRep⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 118) (p. 296).

**Proposition 7.1.15, 2021 form** (V7.71) ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_1_15⟧. *For a finite set $Y$ of mutually isomorphic objects and $V \in \mathcal N(Y)$ there is a natural representation of $Y$ in $V$ whose sheets $\mathbf U(\psi) \ni \psi$ are the components of the morphisms between points of $\bigcup_y U(y)$, with $s : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(s(\psi))$, $t : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(t(\psi))$ sc-diffeomorphisms, $f(\psi) = t \circ (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}$ and $t(\psi') = f(\psi)(s(\psi'))$ on $\mathbf U(\psi)$.* This is the star construction of §VII.10, whose structure already had the 2021 form of (2). *The 2017 form of (2).* As printed in 2017, $s, t : \mathbf U(\psi) \to U(y)$ with one $y$ for both maps; with $y \in U(y)$, disjoint $U(y)$ and $\psi \in \mathbf U(\psi)$ this forces $s(\psi) = t(\psi)$ ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.src_eq_tgt_of_printed_2017⟧, and for $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ by reflection with $Y = \{1, -1\}$ the hypotheses hold, a natural representation of the 2021 form exists, and no data of the printed 2017 form exist ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.not_printed_2017_reflection⟧. So the 2017 form does not hold as we read it, and the 2021 form is the one proved (Findings, Chapter 7, items 25, 119) (p. 297).

**Lemma 7.1.16** (V7.72) ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_1_16⟧. *If $\psi'_k \in \mathbf U(\psi)$ converge to $\psi'$ and $s(\psi'_k)$ or $t(\psi'_k)$ converges to a point of $U(s(\psi)) \cup U(t(\psi))$, then $\psi' \in \mathbf U(\psi)$ and the sources and targets converge inside $U(s(\psi))$, $U(t(\psi))$.* The four cases reduce to two, since a limit lying in $U(b)$ of points of $U(a)$ lies in $U(a)$, the $U(y)$ being open and disjoint ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.mem_U_of_tendsto⟧; then $s$ on $\mathbf U(\psi)$ is a homeomorphism onto $U(s(\psi))$ and the limits agree (Findings, Chapter 7, item 120) (p. 300).

**Corollary 7.1.17 (4)–(7)** (V7.73). *(4) For $x \in Y$, the natural representation of $G_x$ on $U(x)$ has $\Gamma(g, z) = (s|\mathbf U(g))^{-1}(z)$ and $f(g) = \Phi(g)$* ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_1_17_4⟧ — by a topological argument, the image of the connected $U(x)$ under $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$ lying in one component, since $f(\psi) = f(\psi')$ does not force $\psi = \psi'$ in a non-effective ep-groupoid. *(5)* $f(\varphi)$ is equivariant along the conjugation $g \mapsto \varphi \circ g \circ \varphi^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_1_17_5⟧. *(6)* The multiplication is an sc-diffeomorphism from $\mathbf U(\psi)\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf U(\varphi)$, an open subset of the fibred-product sub-M-polyfold of Part I's Proposition 2.5.20 (2017: 2.15), onto $\mathbf U(\psi \circ \varphi)$ ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_1_17_6⟧: it is $(s|\mathbf U(\psi \circ \varphi))^{-1} \circ s \circ \mathrm{pr}_2$ once its image is known to lie in $\mathbf U(\psi \circ \varphi)$, which follows, as in the text, from the connectedness of the domain and the continuity of the multiplication, without sequences. *(7)* The $U(y)$ can be taken with the properness property ⟦Chapter7/Book2021Basic · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_1_17_7⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 120) (p. 301).

### VII.34 The 2021 §7.2: $T_x$, the topology $T_R$, Lemma 7.2.11, Propositions 7.2.12, 7.2.13 and Theorem 7.2.14

**Definition 7.2.5 and Lemma 7.2.6** (V7.74) ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.definition_7_2_5⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_2_6⟧. *$T_x$ is the maximal subgroup of $G_x$ acting trivially on some small $W(x)$; conjugation by $\varphi : x \to y$ maps $T_x$ onto $T_y$.* For a natural representation, $T_x^V$ is the group of the $g$ with $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ on $V \cap U(x)$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerOn⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mem_kerOn⟧; it grows as $V$ shrinks ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerOn_anti⟧, is normal for invariant $V$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerOn_normal⟧ and lies in the intrinsic $T_x$ of §VII.15 ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerOn_le_trivialSubgroup⟧. "Maximal" is read as two statements: $T_x \supseteq T_x^W$ for every open $W \ni x$, with equality for every small $W$, by §VII.15 Step 3. Lemma 7.2.6 is the conjugation $\varphi T_x \varphi^{-1} = T_y$ that §VII.15 had proved for the composition of $X_R$, now an isomorphism ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.trivialSubgroupEquiv⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.trivialSubgroupEquiv_apply⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 121) (p. 310).

**Remark 7.2.8 and Lemma 7.2.9** (V7.75) ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.remark_7_2_8⟧. *$T_R$ is the finest topology on $\mathbf X^R$ for which $\pi$ is continuous; in general $(X, \mathbf X^R)$ cannot be made an ep-groupoid, but it can when $T_R$ is Hausdorff.* The finest such topology is the quotient topology of §VII.16, and $\pi$ is an open quotient map ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.isOpenQuotientMap_reducedπ⟧; Lemma 7.2.9 is §VII.16 Steps 2 and 3 ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isOpenMap_reducedπ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isOpenEmbedding_domRestrict_reducedπ⟧. In Definition 7.2.7 the target map is printed "$s([\varphi]) = t_X(\varphi)$", a possible misprint for $t([\varphi])$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedTgt⟧. The remark's "in general not" is what the counterexample of §VII.16 shows (Findings, Chapter 7, items 122, 123) (p. 311).

**Lemma 7.2.11** (V7.76). *If $\varphi_1, \dots, \varphi_k$ are the other members of the class of $\varphi_0$, there are neighbourhoods $U(\varphi_i)$ with disjoint closures, each mapped by $\pi$ homeomorphically onto one $U([\varphi_0])$, which contain every $\psi$ with $[\psi] \in U([\varphi_0])$.* The class is finite ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.finite_reducedπ_preimage⟧, by properness. The conclusion is a predicate ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.IsReducedEvenlyCovered⟧, with "homeomorphism onto $U([\varphi_0])$" read as: $\pi(U(\varphi_i)) = U([\varphi_0])$ and $\pi$ an open embedding on $U(\varphi_i)$. *As we read it, the lemma needs $T_R$ Hausdorff.* The text's proof of (3) takes a sequence $\psi_k$ with $[\psi_k] \to [\varphi_0]$ and uses that the limit of $[\psi_k]$ is unique. Without that, (1)–(3) at every unit already make $\mathbf X^T$ closed ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.isClosed_nonEffectivePart_of_isReducedEvenlyCovered⟧, and (1)–(3) at every morphism are equivalent to $T_R$ Hausdorff ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.isReducedEvenlyCovered_iff_t2Space⟧; in the ep-groupoid of §VII.16 they fail at $(1, o_0)$, whose class contains only $(1, o_0)$ while the morphisms $(-1, (-1/(n+1), 0))$ have classes converging to it ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.reducedπ_preimage_one⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.not_isReducedEvenlyCovered⟧. *Under $T_R$ Hausdorff*, the setting of Theorem 7.2.14 where the lemma is used, every open $N \supseteq \pi^{-1}([\varphi_0])$ contains $\pi^{-1}(O)$ for an open $O \ni [\varphi_0]$, which gives (3) for sheets at the finitely many members of the class, chosen with disjoint closures ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.exists_preimage_reducedπ_subset_of_t2Space⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.isReducedEvenlyCovered_of_t2Space⟧, and the lemma holds ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_2_11⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 124) (p. 315).

**Proposition 7.2.12** (V7.77) ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_12⟧. *$(\mathbf X^R, T_R)$ is paracompact, for every ep-groupoid.* **The text's proof** refines an open cover through the neighbourhoods of Lemma 7.2.11, which as we read it need $T_R$ Hausdorff. **The formalized proof** needs no hypothesis. *Step 1, descent.* Paracompactness descends along an open continuous surjection $p$ if every point $q$ has a compact $K$ such that every open $N \supseteq K$ contains $p^{-1}(O)$ for some open $O \ni q$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_of_isOpenMap⟧: the images of a locally finite precise refinement upstairs form one downstairs, with no separation axiom. *Step 2, the compact set.* For $q = [\varphi]$ and $V$ the open set of Definition 7.1.3 (3) at $s(\varphi)$, $K = \{\psi \in s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,V) \mid (s, t)(\psi) = (s, t)(\varphi)\}$ is compact by properness and contains the class of $\varphi$; $(s, t)$ is proper, hence closed, on $s^{-1}(\mathrm{cl}\,V)$, so an open $N \supseteq K$ contains $\pi^{-1}(O)$ for an open $O \ni q$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.exists_isCompact_preimage_reducedπ_subset⟧. So `ParacompactSpace X.ReducedMor` is an instance ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_reducedMor⟧, and of the two hypotheses of §VII.16 only the Hausdorff one remains, the 2021 text's own (gap G.71, closed) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 111, 125) (p. 317).

**Proposition 7.2.13 and Theorem 7.2.14** (V7.78) ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_13⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_2_14⟧. *The natural charts make $(\mathbf X^R, T_R)$ an M-polyfold iff $T_R$ is Hausdorff; if $T_R$ is Hausdorff, $(X, \mathbf X^R)$ is naturally an ep-groupoid.* An M-polyfold is Hausdorff and paracompact by definition, so Proposition 7.2.13 is read as the equivalence of "an M-polyfold structure with the atlas of §VII.16 exists" and $T_R$ Hausdorff; one direction is the definition, the other is §VII.16 with Proposition 7.2.12. Theorem 7.2.14 is Proposition 7.10 (2017) of §VII.17 under exactly the hypothesis the formalization had taken: $X_R$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedEpGroupoid⟧, with the M-polyfold $\mathbf X^R$ ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedPolyfold⟧, the groupoid structure of §VII.17 and the ep-functor $X \to X_R$; it is effective (Proposition 7.2.16) ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.isEffective_reducedEpGroupoid⟧. The 2021 text thus agrees with the reading of §§VII.16–VII.17 (gap G.71, closed in the 2021 form); the 2021 statements, with the Hausdorff hypothesis alone, are §VII.48 ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_AReduced · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_16⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, items 56, 107, 111, 126, 143) (p. 318).

### VII.35 Proposition 7.2.17, the local unique continuation property, and Theorem 7.2.22

**Proposition 7.2.17** (V7.79) ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_17⟧. *$T_R$ is Hausdorff iff $\mathbf X^T$ is closed in $\mathbf X$.* *Step 1, the relation.* $[\varphi] = [\psi]$ iff $t\varphi = t\psi$ and $\psi^{-1} \circ \varphi \in \mathbf X^T$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.reducedπ_eq_iff_comp_inv⟧; in particular $\varphi \in \mathbf X^T$ iff $[\varphi]$ is the class of a unit ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.mem_nonEffectivePart_iff_reducedπ⟧. *Step 2, closed relation.* $(\varphi, \psi) \mapsto \psi^{-1} \circ \varphi$ is continuous on $\{s\varphi = s\psi\}$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.continuous_comp_fibredProduct⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.continuousOn_comp_inv⟧, so the relation is closed when $\mathbf X^T$ is ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.isClosed_reducedπ_eq_of_isClosed⟧, and a quotient by an open quotient map is Hausdorff iff its relation is closed (Mathlib). *Step 3, conversely,* if $T_R$ is Hausdorff, $\mathbf X^T = \{\varphi \mid [\varphi] = [1_{s(\varphi)}]\}$ is closed, the set where two continuous maps into a Hausdorff space agree ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.isClosed_nonEffectivePart_of_t2Space⟧. Properness is not needed. Always, $\mathrm{cl}\,\mathbf X^T \subseteq \{s = t\}$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.isClosed_src_eq_tgt⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.closure_nonEffectivePart_subset⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 127) (p. 320).

**Definition 7.2.18 (= 7.4.1), Remarks 7.2.19 and 7.2.20** (V7.80). *(LUC): every object has a natural representation on which $\hat g = \mathrm{id}$ on a nonempty open subset forces $\hat g = \mathrm{id}$.* ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.HasLUC⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.IsLUC⟧. The choice of $U(x)$ does not matter: if $\mathbf X^T$ is closed, every natural representation has the property ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.hasLUC_of_isClosed⟧, so LUC holds iff it holds for all of them ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.isLUC_iff_forall_naturalRep⟧, and Remark 7.2.20 (inside every $O(x)$) follows ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.remark_7_2_20⟧. Remark 7.2.19, some ep-groupoid is not LUC, is §VII.36 ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_7_2_19⟧. Effective ep-groupoids are LUC, $\mathbf X^T$ being the closed set of units ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.isClosed_range_unit⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.nonEffectivePart_eq_range_unit_of_isEffective⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.isLUC_of_isEffective⟧, and so are the trivial ep-groupoid, the reflection and the non-effective trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.isLUC_trivial⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.Examples.isLUC_reflection⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.Examples.isLUC_trivialZ3⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, items 128, 144) (p. 321).

**Proposition 7.2.21, Theorem 7.2.22 and Proposition 7.2.23** (V7.81) ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_2_22⟧. *$T_R$ Hausdorff, LUC and $\mathbf X^T$ closed are equivalent; under LUC, $X_R$ is an ep-groupoid.* *Proposition 7.2.21, by connectedness.* In a natural representation, $\Gamma(g, y) \in \mathbf X^T$ iff $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ near $y$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eventually_Φ_eq_of_Γ_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Γ_mem_of_eventually⟧. So the set of $y \in U(x)$ near which $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ is open, and closed in $U(x)$ when $\mathbf X^T$ is closed, hence empty or all of the connected $U(x)$: LUC. Conversely, under LUC, a morphism $\varphi \in \mathrm{cl}\,\mathbf X^T$ has $s\varphi = t\varphi = x$, so $g = \varphi \in G_x$; the open sheet $\Gamma(g, U(x)) \ni \varphi$ meets $\mathbf X^T$ in some $\Gamma(g, y)$, so $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ near $y$, LUC gives $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ on $U(x)$, and $\varphi \in T_x$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.isClosed_nonEffectivePart_of_isLUC⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_21⟧. With Proposition 7.2.17 this is Theorem 7.2.22, and Proposition 7.2.23 is Theorem 7.2.14 under LUC ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.t2Space_reducedMor_of_isLUC⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_23⟧. For the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action, $\mathbf X^T = \mathbf X$ is closed and $T_R$ is Hausdorff ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.Examples.nonEffectivePart_trivialZ3⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.Examples.t2Space_reducedMor_trivialZ3⟧, the case the first reading had left open (Findings, Chapter 7, items 60, 128, 129) (pp. 321–323).

### VII.36 Appendices 7.6.3 and 7.6.4: Zhou's example, and the reduced groupoid of $X^1$

**Appendix 7.6.3** (V7.82) ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_7_2_19⟧. *Zhou's example: $\mathbb Z/2$ acting on the retract of Part I's Subsection 1.4.4 by $(s, f) \mapsto (s, -f)$; $\mathrm{cl}(\mathbf X^T) \setminus \mathbf X^T$ is one point, so $T_R$ is not Hausdorff and LUC fails.* The formalization uses its own example of §VII.16, $\mathbb Z/2$ acting by $(t, z) \mapsto (t, \pm z)$ on the retract of Part I's Remark 4.2.2 (2017: 4.3), which has the same features: the action is trivial over $t < 0$ and moves points arbitrarily close to the origin over $t > 0$. The point $(-1, o_0)$ is a limit of $(-1, (t, 0))$, $t < 0$, which lie in $\mathbf X^T$, and is not in $\mathbf X^T$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.mem_closure_nonEffectivePart⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.not_isClosed_nonEffectivePart⟧, so by Theorem 7.2.22 LUC fails ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.not_isLUC⟧ and $T_R$ is not Hausdorff, as §VII.16 had shown directly ⟦Chapter7/ReducedNotHausdorff · EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.not_t2Space_reducedMor⟧. *$\mathbf X^T$ exactly.* Since then the non-effective part of the analogue is computed: $\mathbf X^T = (\{1\} \times O) \cup (\{-1\} \times \{(t, z) \in O \mid t < 0\})$ — the element $1$ acts trivially everywhere, $-1$ near exactly the points over $t < 0$, since near a point over $t \ge 0$ there are points of $O$ with $z \ne 0$ — and $\mathrm{cl}(\mathbf X^T) \setminus \mathbf X^T = \{(-1, o_0)\}$, one point, as the text says of its example ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_AZhouRetract · EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.nonEffectivePart_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_AZhouRetract · EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.closure_nonEffectivePart_diff⟧ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_AZhouRetract · EpGroupoid.Examples.JumpingRetract.appendix_7_6_3⟧. Zhou's example itself is §VII.47 ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.appendix_7_6_3⟧ (gap G.83, closed). The counterexample found in the first reading is thus consistent with the 2021 text: it is of the kind Remark 7.2.8 announces and Appendix 7.6.3 gives, and it fails LUC as Theorem 7.2.22 requires (Findings, Chapter 7, items 107, 129, 130, 156) (p. 348).

**Appendix 7.6.4, Theorem 7.6.7 and Corollary 7.6.8** (V7.83) ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_6_7⟧. *Under (SLUC), $(\mathbf X^T)^1 = (\mathbf X^1)^T$, and the identification of $(X^1)_R$ with $(X_R)^1$ is an sc-diffeomorphism; likewise for every $i$.* *(7.24).* A morphism of level $1$ in $\mathbf X^T$ lies in $(\mathbf X^1)^T$, since $s = t$ near it in $\mathbf X$ gives $s = t$ near it in $\mathbf X^1$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.mem_nonEffectivePart_liftOne_of_levelVal⟧. *The converse* follows the text: for $g$ acting trivially near $x$ in $X^1$, $\hat g = \mathrm{id}$ on $U(x) \cap X_1$ by LUC for $X^1$, through the level-one form of $\Gamma$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.levelOneΓ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.continuousOn_levelOneΓ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eventually_of_levelOneΓ_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.levelOneΓ_mem_of_eventually⟧, and on $U(x)$ by density ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.levelVal_mem_nonEffectivePart_of_liftOne⟧. Then $(\mathbf X^1)^T = (\mathbf X^T)^1$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.nonEffectivePart_liftOne_eq⟧, the two relations agree on level $1$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.liftOne_reducedπ_eq_iff⟧, and $[\varphi]_1 \mapsto [\varphi]$ ⟦Chapter7/ReducedCriterion · EpGroupoid.reducedLevelOneMap⟧ is well defined, injective and continuous with range $\pi(\mathbf X_1)$.
