### VII.37 §7.4 (new in the 2021 edition): index lifts, Lemma 7.4.4, the Part I facts, and $Tg$

§7.4 has no 2017 counterpart. It introduces the Zhou condition and the unique continuation and regularity properties that the reduced groupoid and the index lifts need.

**Index lifts, Proposition 7.4.2 and Remark 7.4.3** (V7.84). The lifts $X^i$ are bundled ep-groupoids ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EP.liftOne⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EP.lift⟧, with $X^0 = X$, $X^{i+1} = (X^i)^1 = (X^1)^i$ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EP.lift_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EP.lift_succ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EP.lift_succ'⟧. *Under LUC, the property passes from a connected invariant $U(x)$ to a larger $W(x)$, so $U(x)$ may be taken small or large.* By §VII.35 every natural representation has the property under LUC, so the hypotheses on $U(x)$ are not used ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_4_2⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.remark_7_4_3⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 132) (pp. 328–329).

**Lemma 7.4.4** (V7.85) ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_4_4⟧. *If $X^i$ has LUC, so has every $X^k$, $k \le i$.* For $i = 1$ the text shows that the points of $U(x) \cap X_1$ near which $\hat g = \mathrm{id}$ in $X^1$ form an open, closed and nonempty subset of the connected $U(x) \cap X_1$, and concludes by density ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eqOn_of_isClosed_liftOne⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.isLUC_of_isLUC_liftOne⟧. The connectedness of $U(x) \cap X_1$ in $X^1$ is used without proof, and the density is that of $X_1$ in $X$ (gap G.73); both are a hypothesis on each $X^k$, $k < i$ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.HasLevelOneConnectedDenseReps⟧ (gap G.85, closed: the hypothesis holds for every ep-groupoid, §VII.45; the lemma is not restated without it), satisfied on subsingletons and by every lift of the point ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.hasLevelOneConnectedDenseReps_of_subsingleton⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.Examples.hasLevelOneConnectedDenseReps_lift_pointEP⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.Examples.lemma_7_4_4_pointEP⟧. In the proof, "$s : W(g) \to W(y)$" for $W(h)$ (possible misprint) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 133) (p. 329).

**The Part I facts** (V7.86). The proofs of §7.4 use, without stating them, facts about an M-polyfold that Part I did not state; in the first reading they were hypotheses, and §VII.45 proves them for every M-polyfold (gap G.85, closed): $X_\infty$ dense in every $X_m$ (gap G.73) ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · MPolyfold.DenseSmooth⟧, $U \cap X_\infty$ connected for connected open $U$ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · MPolyfold.SmoothConnected⟧, maps agreeing near a smooth point in $X_\infty$ have the same tangent there ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · MPolyfold.TangentDeterminedSmooth⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · MPolyfold.TangentDeterminedSmooth.eq_self⟧, and tangent vectors are approximated by tangent vectors at nearby smooth points, which follows from the openness of $p : TX \to X^1$ (gap G.8) ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · MPolyfold.eqOn_tangentFiber_of_mem_closure⟧. They are bundled as one hypothesis ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · MPolyfold.SmoothRegular⟧, with the density of $(T_xX)_\infty$ in $T_xX$ separate ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · MPolyfold.DenseSmoothTangent⟧, and consequences ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · MPolyfold.DenseSmooth.dense⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · MPolyfold.DenseSmooth.subset_closure_inter⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · MPolyfold.DenseSmooth.exists_smooth⟧. They hold on subsingletons with all points smooth and on the discrete M-polyfold of a point ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · MPolyfold.smoothRegular_of_subsingleton⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · MPolyfold.smoothRegular_discrete_unit⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · MPolyfold.denseSmoothTangent_discrete_unit⟧ (gap G.85) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 134) (pp. 331–340).

**The tangent $Tg$** (V7.87). For a smooth $x$ and $g \in G_x$, Chapter 7's tangent of a morphism (Definition 7.1.4, $Tt \circ (Ts|T_g\mathbf X)^{-1}$, without charts, §VII.3) is, on $T_xX$, the tangent $T\Phi(g)$ of $\hat g$, for every natural representation ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tangentMor_Γ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tangentMor_eq_tΦ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tΦ_eq_tΦ⟧: $t = \Phi(g) \circ s$ on the sheet $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$. At a fixed point $z$ of $\Phi(g)$, $\Gamma(g, z) \in G_z$ acts near $z$ as $g$ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isoΓ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isoΓ_val⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eventually_Φ_eq_Γ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.tangentMor_isoΓ⟧, and lies in $T_z$ iff $\Phi(g) = \mathrm{id}$ near $z$ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isoΓ_mem_trivialSubgroup_iff⟧. $Tg$ is a set map on the fibre; (ZHOU) asks only that it be the identity, so the linear structure of $T_xX$ (gap G.7) is not needed (Findings, Chapter 7, item 135) (p. 331).

### VII.38 §7.4: (ZHOU), (ZHOU'), unique continuation, (SLUC) and (VSLUC)

The forms below take the Part I facts of §VII.37 as hypotheses; since these hold for every M-polyfold, every result also holds without them, and the restatements are listed in §VII.45.

As in §VII.38, the Part I facts taken as hypotheses below are theorems (§VII.45).

**Definitions 7.4.19, 7.4.21 and Lemma 7.4.20** (V7.93). *(LR): inside every neighbourhood of $x$ a natural representation such that every sc-diffeomorphism $\beta$ of $U(x)$ with $|\beta(y)| = |y|$ equals some $\hat g$* ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.IsLR⟧; *(LR'): the same for $\beta$ onto an open image with $\beta(x) = x$* ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.IsLR'⟧. "Arbitrarily small" is "inside every open $O \ni x$", and $|\beta(y)| = |y|$ is $\pi(\beta(y)) = \pi(y)$. *Lemma 7.4.20: such a $\beta$ maps $U(x)$ onto $U(x)$* ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_4_20⟧. Two points of $U(x)$ in one orbit are related by the natural action, so where $\beta(y) \in U(x)$, $\beta(y) = \hat g(y)$ for some $g$ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.exists_Φ_eq_of_π_eq⟧; so $U(x) \cap \beta^{-1}(U(x))$ is covered by the finitely many closed sets $\{\beta = \hat g\}$, and connectedness of $U(x)$, instead of the text's paths, gives $\beta(U(x)) \subseteq U(x)$ and then equality; the only point of $U(x)$ in the orbit of $x$ is $x$ ⟦Chapter7/Zhou · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eq_self_of_π_eq⟧. ### VII.41 The 2021 additions: what is not formalized, and what they taught us

Every gap of the 2021 additions is closed:

- **Theorem 7.6.7 for every $i$** (gap G.82, closed): the identification $(X^1)_R \cong (X_R)^1$ is an sc-diffeomorphism and an isomorphism of ep-groupoids, and $(X^i)_R \cong (X_R)^i$ for every $i$ under (SLUC) (§VII.46; Findings, Chapter 7, item 131).
- **Zhou's retract** (gap G.83, closed): the example itself, with the sc-smoothness the text cites from [60], and its non-effective part computed as printed; the analogue's non-effective part is computed exactly as well (§§VII.36, VII.47; Findings, Chapter 7, items 130, 139, 156).
- **$X^i$, $i \ge 2$, in §7.4** (gap G.84, closed): Propositions 7.4.9 and 7.4.16–7.4.18 and the results for every $X^i$ are §VII.43; of "(ZHOU') is the same for $X$ and $X^i$" only the direction from $X$ to $X^i$, the one the proof uses, is formalized (Findings, Chapter 7, items 137, 148–150).
- **The Part I facts** (gap G.85, closed): they hold for every M-polyfold, and every natural representation has $U(x) \cap X_m$ connected and $U(x) \cap X_1$ dense, so §7.4 and Appendix 7.6.4 hold with no added hypothesis (§VII.45; Findings, Chapter 7, item 153). Lemma 7.4.4 is not restated without its hypothesis, which now holds.
- **Theorem 7.6.9** (row V7.98, narrower): "$\Phi$ is a homeomorphism onto $\theta$" holds as we read it only for $V$ centred at $x$; the image is $\theta \cap V^x$ in general, and the theorem is proved for every representative in that form (§VII.50; Findings, Chapter 7, items 141, 151, 155).

**The counterexample and the 2021 text agree.** The first reading found that $\mathbf X^R$ need not be Hausdorff, on a dimension-jumping retract, and took Hausdorffness and paracompactness as hypotheses of Proposition 7.2.10 (2017: 7.9) and Proposition 7.10 (2017). The 2021 text rewrites §7.2 to the same effect: Remark 7.2.8 says the structure fails in general, Theorem 7.2.14 assumes $T_R$ Hausdorff, Theorem 7.2.22 characterizes it by LUC and the closedness of $\mathbf X^T$, and Appendix 7.6.3 gives Zhou's example of the same kind. Paracompactness, which the formalization had left open, holds always (§§VII.34–VII.36; gap G.71, closed).

**Hausdorffness sits inside Lemma 7.2.11.** Its conclusion at every morphism is equivalent to $T_R$ Hausdorff, so it cannot serve, as we read it, as a step towards Hausdorffness; the paracompactness of Proposition 7.2.12 is proved instead from the openness of $\pi$ and the properness of $(s, t)$ (§VII.34).

**Connectedness replaces sequences.** Propositions 7.2.21, 7.4.8, 7.4.10, 7.4.22, Lemmas 7.4.4, 7.4.15 and 7.4.20 are proved by showing a set open and closed in a connected $U(x)$, $U(x)_\infty$ or $U(x) \cap X_1$; what this needs of Part I — density and connectedness of the smooth points, locality of tangents, the openness of $p : TX \to X^1$ — becomes visible as explicit hypotheses (§§VII.35–VII.39).

**$Tg$ needs no linear structure.** (ZHOU) asks that a map be the identity; Chapter 7's chart-free tangent of a morphism suffices (§VII.37).

### VII.42 Appendix 7.6.5: Theorem 7.6.9 in full (the boundary ep-groupoid)

Theorem 7.6.9 (2)–(5) rest on Part I's Theorem 2.7.13 (2)–(4): for a tame M-polyfold $A$, the tame boundary $bA$ carries a tame M-polyfold structure ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold_isTame⟧ whose charts are $p \mapsto \pi(\varphi(Bp))$, $\pi$ a coordinate projection of a tame chart $\varphi$ and the face read off the triple; $B : bA \to A$ is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.tameBoundaryMap_isScSmooth⟧ and $d_A(Bp) = d_{bA}(p) + 1$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.degIndex_tameBoundaryMap⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.degIndex_tameBoundaryMap_sub_one⟧; the structure is characterized by the charts $\Phi$ of centred triples, and unique with that property ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.tameBoundaryPolyfold_unique⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryStructure · MPolyfold.theorem_2_7_13_structure⟧. The text leaves the verification of Theorem 7.6.9 to the reader, with a sketch: for $[\varphi, \mathbf V, \theta]$ choose $\mathbf V$ with $s : \mathbf V \to V$ an sc-diffeomorphism; in the charts $\Phi_{(\varphi, \mathbf V, \theta)}$ and $\Phi_{(x, V, s(\theta))}$ the map $s$ becomes $s : \theta \to s(\theta)$, an sc-diffeomorphism of faces. The formalization replaces this sc-diffeomorphism by a computation in the charts of $bA$, which needs only that the map below is sc-smooth (Findings, Chapter 7, items 145–147).

**Maps of tame boundaries** (V7.99) ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · MPolyfold.isScSmoothOn_of_bMap⟧. *Let $f : A \to B$ be sc-smooth on an open $U$ and $g : bA \to bB$ continuous on an open $O \subseteq B^{-1}(U)$ with $B \circ g = f \circ B$ on $O$. Then $g$ is sc-smooth on $O$.* *Proof.* Sc-smoothness is local. Near $p \in O$ take the chart $\chi = \pi \circ \varphi \circ B$ of $bA$ at $p$ and $\chi' = \pi' \circ \varphi' \circ B$ of $bB$ at $g(p)$, with $\varphi$, $\varphi'$ tame charts at $Bp$ and $f(Bp)$. On a neighbourhood of $\chi(p)$ in the face, $\chi' \circ g \circ \chi^{-1} = \pi' \circ (\varphi' \circ f \circ \varphi^{-1}) \circ \iota$, with $\iota$ the inclusion of the face into the model of $\varphi$: indeed $B \circ \chi^{-1} = \varphi^{-1} \circ \iota$ near $\chi(p)$ and $B \circ g = f \circ B$. The right side is a composition of sc-smooth maps, $\pi'$ and $\iota$ being linear. *The lifts.* The lift $bf$ of an sc-smooth index-preserving local homeomorphism (§VII.40) covers $f$ and is continuous, so it is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · MPolyfold.isScSmoothMap_bLift⟧. For a local sc-diffeomorphism $f$ and a sheet $f : W \to V$ with inverse $\sigma$, a lift of $\sigma$ takes $bf(c)$ back to $c$ for $Bc \in W$, by the uniqueness of lifts ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · MPolyfold.isLiftOf_bLift_sheet⟧; so $bf$ is injective on $B^{-1}(W)$, maps it onto $B^{-1}(V)$, and its inverse, covering $\sigma$ and continuous, is sc-smooth by the same statement: $bf$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · MPolyfold.isLocalScDiffeo_bLift⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 146).

**The boundary ep-groupoid** (V7.100) ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.boundaryEpGroupoid⟧. For a tame ep-groupoid, $bX$ and $b\mathbf X$ are paracompact ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_bObj⟧ ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_bMor⟧ and carry the structures of Theorem 2.7.13 (2) for the object and the morphism M-polyfold ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.bPObj⟧ ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.bPMor⟧ ($\mathbf X$ is tame, §VII.40). Since $s$, $t$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms of $(X, \mathbf X)$, their lifts (7.25) are local sc-diffeomorphisms ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_bSrc⟧ ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_bTgt⟧; $u$ and $\iota$ are sc-smooth index-preserving local homeomorphisms, so their lifts (7.28), (7.27) are sc-smooth ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_bUnit⟧ ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_bInv⟧. *The multiplication (7.29).* Condition (4) of Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3) is proved in its sheet form (§VII.1, V7.3): for every sheet $\sigma$ of $s : b\mathbf X \to bX$ over $V$, $b \mapsto m(\sigma(tb), b)$ is sc-smooth on $t^{-1}(V)$ ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet_bComp⟧. Near $b$ take a sheet $\sigma_1$ of $s : \mathbf X \to X$ through $B(\sigma(tb))$; then $b' \mapsto m(\sigma(tb'), b')$ is continuous and covers $\gamma \mapsto m(\sigma_1(t\gamma), \gamma)$, which is sc-smooth by (4) for $(X, \mathbf X)$ in sheet form ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothCompSheet⟧, so the statement on maps of tame boundaries applies; the sheet form gives (4) ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · isScSmoothComp_iff_sheet⟧ ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothComp_bComp⟧. With the groupoid and the properness of §VII.40 this is an ep-groupoid, tame by Theorem 2.7.13 (2) ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.isTame_boundaryEpGroupoid⟧. *$B$ is an ep-functor* ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.boundaryEpFunctor⟧: a functor (§VII.40), sc-smooth on objects and morphisms, so a morphism of $\mathcal{EP}$ (Definition 7.1.7 (2017: 7.7)) ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpFunctor⟧. *The diagram of the sketch* ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.phiTot_bSrc⟧: for $(\varphi, \mathbf V, \theta)$ with $\mathbf V$ in a sheet of $s$, $s$ maps $U(\varphi, \mathbf V, \theta)$ into $U(x, s(\mathbf V), s(\theta))$ and $\Phi_{(x, s(\mathbf V), s(\theta))} \circ s = s \circ \Phi_{(\varphi, \mathbf V, \theta)}$ there (Findings, Chapter 7, items 145, 146) (p. 355).

**Theorem 7.6.9** (V7.101) ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_6_9_full⟧. *For a tame ep-groupoid: (1) $bX$, $b\mathbf X$ are metrizable; (2) they carry the tame M-polyfold structures above, characterized as in Theorem 2.7.13 — for a triple with $V$ centred at $x$, $U(x, V, \theta)$ is open and $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is an sc-diffeomorphism onto the face $\theta$, inverse to the homeomorphism of §VII.40 — and every structure with this property is equivalent to it; (3) both maps $B$ are sc-smooth; (4) $d_X(B(p)) - 1 = d_{bX}(p)$ and $d_{\mathbf X}(B(a)) - 1 = d_{b\mathbf X}(a)$; (5) the boundary ep-groupoid is tame, with the structure maps (7.25)–(7.29), $s$, $t$ local sc-diffeomorphisms, $u$, $\iota$ sc-smooth, $m$ sc-smooth on the fibred product; and $B$ is an ep-functor.* *Proof.* (1) is §VII.40; (2)–(4) are Theorem 2.7.13 (2)–(4) for the object and the morphism M-polyfold; (5) and the ep-functor are the previous paragraph. *Readings.* "Natural" in (2) is read through the characterization and its uniqueness, for representatives with $V$ centred at $x$ (in Part I every representative is covered since, with image $\theta \cap V^x$, §II.37; gap G.78, closed; for the boundary ep-groupoid, §VII.50); the hypotheses of the two uniqueness statements are satisfied by the structures of (2) themselves. (4) is stated as printed, with the subtraction of natural numbers ($B$ takes values in $\partial X$, where $d_X \ge 1$); the additive form is Part I's. *Witness* ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEpStructure · EpGroupoid.trivial_quadrant_boundaryEp_witness⟧: the trivial ep-groupoid of the tame quadrant $[0, \infty)^n \oplus W$, $n \ge 1$, is tame, its boundary ep-groupoid is tame with nonempty $bX$, $b\mathbf X$, and the classes over the corner have $d_{bX} = n - 1$ (Findings, Chapter 7, items 145, 147) (p. 355).

### VII.43 §7.4 on every lift $X^i$: Propositions 7.4.9, 7.4.16–7.4.18

The per-level hypotheses below — the Part I facts on every $X^i$, the density of $X_\infty$ and level-connected natural representations — hold for every ep-groupoid (§VII.45), where the forms without them are listed.

**The smooth points of $X^1$** (V7.102) ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · MPolyfold.continuous_levelDown⟧. The inclusion $X_{m+1} \to X_m$ is continuous; so the identity $(X^1)_\infty \to X_\infty$ and its inverse are continuous ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · MPolyfold.shiftSmoothMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · MPolyfold.shiftSmoothInv⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · MPolyfold.continuous_shiftSmoothMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · MPolyfold.continuous_shiftSmoothInv⟧, a homeomorphism ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · MPolyfold.shiftSmoothHomeomorph⟧. This is the text's "$X_\infty = X^i_\infty$" in Propositions 7.4.9 and 7.4.16, as topological spaces.

**Proposition 7.4.9** (V7.102) ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EP.proposition_7_4_9⟧. *If $X$ satisfies (ZHOU), so does every $X^i$.* The text says (ZHOU') is the same for $X$ and $X^i$, by $X_\infty = X^i_\infty$ and Proposition 7.4.8. *(ZHOU') passes from $X$ to $X^1$.* An isotropy element of $x \in X_1$ in $X^1$ is one in $X$ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.isotropyLevelVal⟧; a natural representation of $X^1$ at $x$ with $U'(x) \subseteq U(x) \cap X_1$ acts, on $U'(x)$, by the natural action of $X$ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.levelVal_Φ_liftOne⟧, and the tangent of a smooth morphism of $\mathbf X^1$ is, under $T(X^1) \to TX$ (Part I's Proposition 2.3.17 for $i = 1$), that of $\mathbf X$ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.tangentLower_tangentMor_liftOne⟧. So $Tg = \mathrm{id}$ on $(T_xX^1)_\infty$ gives $Tg = \mathrm{id}$ on $(T_xX)_\infty$, (ZHOU') for $X$ gives $\hat g = \mathrm{id}$ near $x$ in $X_\infty$, hence near $x$ in $(X^1)_\infty$ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.isZhou'_liftOne⟧, and by induction on $i$ for every $X^i$ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EP.isZhou'_lift⟧. The converse, from $X^i$ to $X$, is not used and not formalized. *The proposition.* (ZHOU) for $X$ gives (ZHOU') for $X$ by Lemma 7.4.6, which uses $(T_xX)_\infty$ dense in $T_xX$; then (ZHOU') for $X^i$, and (ZHOU) for $X^i$ by Proposition 7.4.8 on $X^i$, which uses the Part I facts on $X^i$ (§VII.37). Witness ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.Examples.proposition_7_4_9_pointEP⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 148) (p. 333).

**Corollary 7.4.11, Theorems 7.4.13 and 7.4.24 for every $X^i$** (V7.102). With Proposition 7.4.9, the forms of §§VII.38–VII.39 that took (ZHOU) for every $X^i$ hold for (ZHOU) on $X$ only: every $X^i$ has LUC ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EP.corollary_7_4_11_all⟧, $X$ has (SLUC) ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EP.theorem_7_4_13_all⟧ and (SLR) ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EP.theorem_7_4_24_all⟧. Witnesses ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.Examples.theorem_7_4_13_all_pointEP⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.Examples.theorem_7_4_24_all_pointEP⟧ (pp. 334, 340).

**Propositions 7.4.16 and 7.4.17** (V7.103) ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EP.proposition_7_4_16_all⟧. *If $X$ has (VSLUC), so does every $X^i$, and in particular every $X^i$ has LUC; so (VSLUC) implies (SLUC).* For $x \in X_1$ smooth, the text's $V(x)$ is taken inside a natural representation $U'(x)$ of $X^1$ at $x$, with $U'(x) \subseteq U(x)$: $V'(x) = V(x) \cap U'(x)$, an open invariant subset of $(X^1)_\infty = X_\infty$, and $\hat g$ is the same map on it ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.isVSLUC_liftOne⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EP.isVSLUC_lift⟧. The density of $X_\infty$ in every level passes to $X^1$ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · MPolyfold.DenseSmooth.shift⟧ and so to every $X^i$ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EP.denseSmooth_lift⟧. Lemma 7.4.15 on every $X^i$ (§VII.38), with `SmoothConnected` on every $X^i$, gives LUC; and (SLUC) follows ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EP.proposition_7_4_17_all⟧. Witnesses ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.Examples.isVSLUC_pointEP⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.Examples.proposition_7_4_17_all_pointEP⟧ (Findings, Chapter 7, item 149) (p. 336).

**Proposition 7.4.18** (V7.104) ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EP.proposition_7_4_18⟧. *(VSLUC) and (SLUC) are equivalent.* One direction is Proposition 7.4.17. *(SLUC) ⇒ (VSLUC)*, the text's proof: take $V(x) = U(x) \cap X_\infty$; an open subset of it on which $\hat g = \mathrm{id}$ contains $W' \cap X_\infty$ for a nonempty open $W'$ of some $X_N$; by density and continuity $\hat g = \mathrm{id}$ on $W'$, and LUC for $X^N$ gives $\hat g = \mathrm{id}$ on $U(x)$, $U(x) \cap X_N$ being connected "by construction". *The neighbourhood basis.* The inclusion $X_N \to X_0$ through the levels ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · MPolyfold.levelDownTo⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · MPolyfold.continuous_levelDownTo⟧ is continuous, and the sets $O \cap X_\infty$, $O$ open in some $X_{N+1}$, form a neighbourhood basis of every smooth point ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · MPolyfold.exists_level_nhds_smooth⟧. *Natural representations one level up.* An isotropy element of $x \in X_1$ in $X$ is one in $X^1$ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.isotropyLevelMk⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.isotropyLevelMk_levelVal⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.isotropyLevelVal_mul⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.isotropyLevelVal_inv⟧. If $U(x) \cap X_1$ is connected in $X^1$, the natural action of $X$ restricts to $U(x) \cap X_1$ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.liftOneΦ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.levelVal_liftOneΦ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mapsTo_liftOneΦ⟧ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isScDiffeoOn_liftOneΦ⟧ and is a natural representation of $X^1$ at $x$ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.liftOneRep⟧, with the same $\hat g$ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouLevels · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.eqOn_of_liftOneRep⟧. ### VII.44 Definition 7.1.4 (2017: 7.4): $T\varphi$ as an sc-isomorphism; the facts (3), (4); $|X_\infty|$ and the density of $X_\infty$

The first reading left these statements of §7.1 as definitions, for want of the linear structure of $T_xX$ and of the density of smooth points in an M-polyfold. Part I now gives $T_xX$ the linear structure of Definition 2.3.14, transported from the tangent space $T_oO = Dr(o)E$ of a retract through any chart (gap G.7, closed), and the remaining steps are the chain rule and a density argument.

**$T\varphi$ as a map** (V7.5) ⟦Chapter7/TangentMorphism · EpGroupoid.definition_7_1_4⟧. *For $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$: $\hat\varphi(s(\varphi)) = t(\varphi)$; $T\varphi = T\hat\varphi(s(\varphi))$ on $T_{s(\varphi)}X$; $T\varphi$ is a bijection $T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}X$ with inverse $T(\varphi^{-1})$; $T(\psi \circ \varphi) = T\psi \circ T\varphi$; and in charts it is a bounded linear isomorphism.* *Step 1, $T\varphi = T\hat\varphi$.* On the sheet of Definition 7.1.4, $t = \hat\varphi \circ s$, and the chain rule for Part I's tangent maps gives $Tt = T\hat\varphi \circ Ts$ on $T_\varphi\mathbf X$; so $Tt \circ (Ts|_{T_\varphi\mathbf X})^{-1}$, the definition of §VII.3, is $T\hat\varphi$ at $s(\varphi)$ ⟦Chapter9/Tangent · EpGroupoid.tangentMor_eq_tangentMapOn_hat⟧. *Step 2, the inverse.* The inverse map $\iota$ exchanges $s$ and $t$, so $T(\varphi^{-1})$ inverts $T\varphi$ on the fibres, and $T\varphi$ is a bijection between them ⟦Chapter7/TangentMorphism · EpGroupoid.bijOn_tangentMor⟧ ⟦Chapter7/TangentMorphism · EpGroupoid.invOn_tangentMor⟧. *Step 3, in charts.* For charts $\chi$ around $s(\varphi)$ and $\psi$ around $t(\varphi)$, $T\varphi$ is represented on the fibres by $L = D(\psi \circ \hat\varphi \circ \chi^{-1} \circ r)(\chi(s\varphi))$, a bounded operator ⟦Chapter7/TangentMorphism · EpGroupoid.tangentMor_chart⟧, and $L$ and the operator $L'$ of $\varphi^{-1}$ restrict to mutually inverse maps $T_{\chi(s\varphi)}O \rightleftarrows T_{\psi(t\varphi)}O'$, by Step 2 ⟦Chapter7/TangentMorphism · EpGroupoid.tangentMor_chart_iso⟧.

**Linearity** (V7.5) ⟦Chapter7/TangentMorphismLinear · EpGroupoid.definition_7_1_4_linear⟧. *For $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$, $T\varphi : T_{s(\varphi)}X \to T_{t(\varphi)}X$ is additive, homogeneous, continuous and bijective, with inverse $T(\varphi^{-1})$.* The linear structure of $T_xX$ is the one transported by a chart, so in the charts of Step 3 the fibre map $T\varphi$ is the restriction of the bounded linear $L$ to $T_{\chi(s\varphi)}O$; additivity, homogeneity and continuity are those of $L$, and bijectivity is Step 2. So $T\varphi$ is a continuous linear equivalence of the fibres ⟦Chapter7/TangentMorphismLinear · EpGroupoid.tangentMorCLE⟧.

**An sc-isomorphism for smooth $\varphi$** (V7.5) ⟦Chapter7/TangentMorphismLinear · EpGroupoid.definition_7_1_4_sc⟧. *If $\varphi$ is smooth, $T\varphi$ is an sc-isomorphism.* For smooth $\varphi$ the point $\chi(s\varphi)$ is smooth, and the derivative at a smooth point of an sc-smooth map is an sc-operator (Part I), so $L$ and $L'$ are sc-operators ⟦Chapter7/TangentMorphismLinear · EpGroupoid.tangentMor_chart_sc⟧; they restrict to mutually inverse maps of the sc-subspaces $T_{\chi(s\varphi)}O$ and $T_{\psi(t\varphi)}O'$, which are $T_{s(\varphi)}X$ and $T_{t(\varphi)}X$ as sc-Banach spaces. This closes gap G.70; the paragraph's "bounded linear isomorphism" on level $0$ for $\varphi \in \mathbf X_1$ and "sc-isomorphism" for smooth $\varphi$ hold as we read them (Findings, Chapter 7, items 5, 110, 154) (p. 289 (2017 p. 227)).

**The facts (3), (4) on $A$** (V7.30). For a saturated sub-M-polyfold $A$ of the object M-polyfold, $a \in A_1 \cap V$ and an sc-smooth retraction $r$ of $V$ onto $A \cap V$, the tangent of the inclusion $Ti : T_aA \to T_aX$ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoidTangent · EpGroupoid.subObjInclusionCLM⟧ and that of $i^{-1} \circ r$, $T_aX \to T_aA$ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoidTangent · EpGroupoid.subObjRetractionCLM⟧, are bounded linear. *(3)* $Ti(T_aA)$ is a closed subspace of $T_aX$ with the closed complement $\ker T(i^{-1} \circ r)$ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoidTangent · EpGroupoid.fact_3_subObj⟧, and at a smooth $a$ the complement is an sc-complement, read in a chart around $a$ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoidTangentSc · EpGroupoid.fact_3_subObj_sc⟧. *(4)* $T(i^{-1} \circ r)$ is onto, $Ti \circ T(i^{-1} \circ r) = Tr(a)$, and $Tr(a)T_aX = Ti(T_aA)$, i.e. $T_aA = Tr(a)T_aX$ ⟦Chapter7/SubGroupoidTangent · EpGroupoid.fact_4_subObj⟧. *Proof.* Both are Part I's Proposition 2.3.19 (3) in its linear form, applied to the object M-polyfold ⟦Chapter2/SubMPolyfoldTangent · MPolyfold.proposition_2_3_19_3_linear⟧: since $r \circ r = r$ near $a$, $Tr(a)$ is a bounded projection of $T_aX$ with range $Ti(T_aA)$, and $i^{-1} \circ r \circ i = \mathrm{id}$ gives the surjectivity (Findings, Chapter 7, items 40, 154) (pp. 305–307 (2017 pp. 237–238)).

**The density of $X_\infty$** (V7.6) ⟦Chapter7/SmoothPointsDense · MPolyfold.denseSmooth⟧. *For every M-polyfold and every $m$, $X_\infty$ is dense in $X_m$, with the topology of $X_m$.* The text states this on p. 289 without proof; Part I had it for sc-Banach spaces only. *Step 1, a retract.* For an sc-smooth retraction $r$ of an open subset $U$ of a partial quadrant $C$ with retract $O$, the points of $O_\infty$ are dense in $O_m$ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothPointsDense · IsScRetract.lvlSet_subset_closure_smooth⟧: for a partial quadrant $C$, $C_m \cap E_\infty$ is dense in $C_m$, since the smooth points of $E$ are dense in $E_m$ and $C$ is defined by finitely many continuous linear inequalities; the same holds for $U$ relatively open in $C$, the fact Part I uses in the proof of Lemma 2.2.1; and a point $o \in O_m$ is the limit in $E_m$ of smooth points $e_n$ of $U$, $r$ maps smooth points to smooth points and is continuous on level $m$, so $r(e_n) \to r(o) = o$ in $O_m$. *Step 2, the M-polyfold.* The level lift of a chart is an embedding of the chart domain in $X_m$ onto the level $m$ of its retract, so density passes to $X_m$. For an ep-groupoid, $X_\infty$ is dense in every $X_k$ and $\mathbf X_\infty$ in every $\mathbf X_k$ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothPointsDense · EpGroupoid.p289_dense⟧; with the density of $X_\infty$ in $X$, Chapter 7's hypothesis of the first reading becomes a theorem (gap G.73, closed; Findings, Chapter 7, items 116, 153).

**The filtration of $|X|$** (V7.6) ⟦Chapter7/SmoothPointsDense · EpGroupoid.p290_orbit_filtration⟧. *$|X| = |X_0| \supset |X_1| \supset \cdots \supset |X_\infty| = \bigcap_k|X_k|$.* $|X_\infty| = \pi(X_\infty)$ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothPointsDense · EpGroupoid.orbitSmooth⟧. Since morphisms preserve the levels (§VII.3), $X_k$ is saturated and $\pi^{-1}(|X_k|) = X_k$ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothPointsDense · EpGroupoid.preimage_orbitLevel⟧; so the $|X_k|$ decrease ⟦Chapter7/SmoothPointsDense · EpGroupoid.orbitLevel_antitone⟧ and their intersection is $\pi$ of $\bigcap_k X_k = X_\infty$ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothPointsDense · EpGroupoid.orbitSmooth_eq_iInter⟧. The text does not state that $|X_\infty|$ is dense in $|X|$; it follows from the density of $X_\infty$, $\pi$ being continuous and onto ⟦Chapter7/SmoothPointsDense · EpGroupoid.dense_orbitSmooth⟧. For M-polyfolds the density is also recorded in the form Chapter 9 uses ⟦Chapter7/SmoothPointsDense · MPolyfold.denseSmooth⟧ (gap G.72, closed; Findings, Chapter 7, items 6, 112) (pp. 289–290 (2017 pp. 227–228)).

### VII.45 §7.4: the Part I facts as theorems, and §7.4 without them

§VII.37 listed the facts about M-polyfolds that the proofs of §7.4 use without statement; the first reading took them as one hypothesis, satisfiable on a point. They hold for every M-polyfold ⟦Chapter7/SmoothRegularAssembly · MPolyfold.smoothRegular⟧, and every result of §7.4, Appendix 7.6.4 and Proposition 8.1.17 is restated without them (gap G.85, closed; Findings, Chapter 7, item 153).

**The four facts** (V7.86). *(a) Density.* $X_\infty$ is dense in every $X_m$ (§VII.44). *(b) Connectedness.* For a connected open $U$, $U \cap X_\infty$ is connected in $X_\infty$ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · MPolyfold.smoothConnected⟧. The local step: every point $u$ of an open $U$ has a neighbourhood $N \subseteq U$ in which any two smooth points are joined inside $U \cap X_\infty$, for the topology of $X_\infty$, by the retracted segment between their images in a chart, Lemma 2.2.1 for one convex piece followed by the retraction. The global step: for a fixed smooth point $x_0$, the points of $U$ having a neighbourhood whose smooth points are joined to $x_0$ form an open set, and by the local step so does its complement in $U$; by density it is nonempty, so it is all of the connected $U$, and $U \cap X_\infty$ is path connected ⟦Chapter2/SmoothPaths · MPolyfold.isPathConnected_smoothVal_preimage⟧. *(c) Openness of $p : TX \to X^1$* ⟦Chapter2/TangentProjOpen · MPolyfold.isOpenMap_tangentProj⟧, Part I's gap G.8, closed. *(d) Locality of tangents.* Two maps sc-smooth on open sets that agree near a smooth point $y$ in $X_\infty$ have the same tangent on $T_yX$ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouFacts · MPolyfold.tangentDeterminedSmooth⟧: the sets $O \cap X_\infty$, $O$ open in some $X_{N+1}$, form a neighbourhood basis of $y$ in $X_\infty$ (§VII.43), so the maps agree on $O \cap X_\infty$, by density and continuity on the open set $O$ of $X_{N+1}$, and in a chart the derivative at $y$ of an $\mathrm{sc}^1$ map is determined by its values on a level-$1$ neighbourhood ⟦Chapter7/ZhouFacts · IsSc1.scDeriv_eq_of_eqOn_level⟧. The fifth fact, kept apart in §VII.37: *(e)* $(T_xX)_\infty$, read as $T_xX \cap (TX)_\infty$, is dense in $T_xX$ for smooth $x$ ⟦Chapter7/ZhouFacts · MPolyfold.denseSmoothTangent⟧: in a chart the tangent vectors at $o$ are $(o, Dr(o)k)$, $Dr(o)$ is an sc-operator at the smooth point $o$, so $k \in E_\infty$ gives smooth tangent vectors, and they are dense since $E_\infty$ is dense in $E$ and $Dr(o)$ maps $E$ continuously onto $T_oO$.

**Natural representations** (V7.83, V7.85, V7.104). *Every natural representation $U(x)$ has $U(x) \cap X_m$ connected in $X_m$ for every $m$, and $U(x) \cap X_1$ dense in $U(x)$.* The paths of (b) lie in $X_\infty$ with its topology, finer than that of every $X_m$, so $U(x) \cap X_\infty$ is connected in $X_m$; it is dense in $U(x) \cap X_m$ by (a), and the closure of a connected set is connected ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.levelConnected⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.isPreconnected_liftU⟧; the density is that of $X_\infty \subseteq X_1$ in $X$ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.subset_closure_inter_levelSet⟧. So the hypotheses of Appendix 7.6.4 and of Proposition 7.4.18 hold for every ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EpGroupoid.hasConnectedDenseLevelOneReps⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRep_levelConnected⟧; the text's choice of $U(x)$ "by construction" is automatic.

**The restatements.** With (a)–(e) and the natural representations, the results of §§VII.36–VII.39 and VII.43 hold with only the hypotheses the text states. *(ZHOU).* Lemma 7.4.6 ⟦Chapter7/ZhouFacts · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_4_6_of_isZhou⟧ and Proposition 7.4.8 ⟦Chapter7/SmoothRegularAssembly · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_4_8_unconditional⟧; Proposition 7.4.10 and the unique continuation through $X_\infty$ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothRegularAssembly · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_4_10_of_isZhou⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothRegularAssembly · EpGroupoid.isSmoothUC_of_isZhou'⟧; Corollary 7.4.11 for $X^1$ and for every $X^i$ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothRegularAssembly · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_4_11_of_isZhou⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothRegularAssembly · EP.corollary_7_4_11_all_of_isZhou⟧; Proposition 7.4.9 ⟦Chapter7/SmoothRegularAssembly · EP.proposition_7_4_9_of_isZhou⟧; Theorem 7.4.13 ⟦Chapter7/SmoothRegularAssembly · EP.theorem_7_4_13_all_of_isZhou⟧; Proposition 7.4.22 and Theorem 7.4.24 ⟦Chapter7/SmoothRegularAssembly · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_4_22_of_isZhou⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothRegularAssembly · EP.theorem_7_4_24_all_of_isZhou⟧, all under (ZHOU) for $X$ alone. *(VSLUC).* Lemma 7.4.15 and its unique continuation ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EpGroupoid.isSmoothUC_of_isVSLUC'⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EpGroupoid.lemma_7_4_15_of_isVSLUC⟧; Propositions 7.4.16 and 7.4.17, for $X^1$ and for every $X^i$ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_4_16_of_isVSLUC⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EP.proposition_7_4_16_all_of_isVSLUC⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EP.proposition_7_4_17_of_isVSLUC⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EP.proposition_7_4_17_all_of_isVSLUC⟧, under (VSLUC) for $X$ alone; and Proposition 7.4.18, (VSLUC) $\Leftrightarrow$ (SLUC), with no hypothesis at all ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EP.isVSLUC_of_isSLUC'⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EP.proposition_7_4_18_unconditional⟧. *Appendix 7.6.4.* Theorem 7.6.7 for $i = 1$ as sets under LUC for $X^1$, and Corollary 7.6.8 under (ZHOU) ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_6_7_of_isLUC⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothConnectedReps · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_6_8_of_imp⟧ ⟦Chapter7/SmoothRegularAssembly · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_6_8_of_isZhou'⟧; the full theorem is §VII.46. *The example.* The analogue of Zhou's example fails (ZHOU) with no hypothesis (§VII.39). Lemma 7.4.4 is not restated; its hypothesis now holds (§VII.37). The forms with the hypotheses are kept, since the hypotheses are defined in files the new proofs import (Findings, Chapter 7, items 133, 134, 136–139, 148–150, 153) (pp. 329–340, 349).

### VII.46 Appendix 7.6.4: Theorem 7.6.7 and Corollary 7.6.8 for every $i$

**Theorem 7.6.7 for $i = 1$** (V7.83) ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_6_7_one⟧. *If $T_R$ is Hausdorff for $X$ and for $X^1$ (equivalently, by Theorem 7.2.22, $X$ and $X^1$ have LUC), the natural identification of $(X^1)_R$ with $(X_R)^1$ — the identity on the common object M-polyfold $X^1$ and $[\varphi]_1 \mapsto [\varphi]$ on morphisms — is an sc-diffeomorphism on objects and on morphisms, and the two functors are inverse isomorphisms of ep-groupoids.* §VII.36 had the identification as a continuous injection of sets. *Step 1, the objects.* $(X^1)_R$ and $(X_R)^1$ both have the object M-polyfold $X^1$, by definition. *Step 2, the projection on level $1$.* The projection $\pi^R : \mathbf X \to \mathbf X^R$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism (§VII.16), so its lift $\pi^{R,1} : \mathbf X^1 \to (\mathbf X^R)^1$ is one ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EpGroupoid.reducedπOne⟧ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EpGroupoid.isLocalScDiffeo_reducedπOne⟧. *Step 3, the map.* $[\varphi]_1 \mapsto [\varphi]$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EpGroupoid.reducedRaise⟧ is well defined and injective because the two relations agree on level $1$: $(\mathbf X^1)^T = (\mathbf X^T)^1$ under the Hausdorff hypothesis on $X^1$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EpGroupoid.nonEffectivePart_liftOne_eq_of_t2⟧ (§VII.36, (7.24) and its converse); it is onto, since the class of a level-$1$ point of $\mathbf X^R$ consists of level-$1$ morphisms (levels are preserved, §VII.3) ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EpGroupoid.bijective_reducedRaise⟧. *Step 4, sc-smoothness.* Near $[\varphi]_1$ the map is $\pi^{R,1} \circ (\pi^R_1|U)^{-1}$, with $\pi^R_1 : \mathbf X^1 \to (\mathbf X^1)^R$ the projection of $X^1$, a local sc-diffeomorphism by §VII.16 for $X^1$, and $U$ a sheet; its inverse is locally $\pi^R_1 \circ (\pi^{R,1}|U)^{-1}$. Both are sc-smooth ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_reducedRaise⟧ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothMap_reducedRaiseInv⟧, so the map is an sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EpGroupoid.isScDiffeoOn_reducedRaise⟧. *Step 5, the functors.* The map commutes with sources and composition ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EpGroupoid.src_reducedRaise⟧ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EpGroupoid.reducedRaise_comp⟧, so with the identity on objects it is an ep-functor $(X^1)_R \to (X_R)^1$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EpGroupoid.raiseReducedFunctor⟧, and its inverse another ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EpGroupoid.raiseReducedFunctorInv⟧, the two composites being identities. The hypotheses hold on the point ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EpGroupoid.Examples.theorem_7_6_7_pointEP⟧.

**Theorem 7.6.7 for every $i$, and Corollary 7.6.8** (V7.83) ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EP.theorem_7_6_7⟧. *Under (SLUC), $(X^i)_R \cong (X_R)^i$ in $\mathcal{EP}$ for every $i$; under (ZHOU), the same.* Under LUC, $T_R$ is Hausdorff (Theorem 7.2.22), so $X_R$ is an object of $\mathcal{EP}$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EP.reducedOfLUC⟧, and the case $i = 1$ is an isomorphism $(X^1)_R \cong (X_R)^1$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EP.raiseReducedIso⟧. Lifting to level one carries isomorphisms of $\mathcal{EP}$ to isomorphisms ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EP.liftOneIso⟧. The isomorphism for $i$ is built by recursion ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EP.raiseReducedIsoLift⟧: the identity for $i = 0$, and for $i + 1$ the composite $(X^{i+1})_R = ((X^i)^1)_R \cong ((X^i)_R)^1 \cong ((X_R)^i)^1 = (X_R)^{i+1}$ of the case $i = 1$ for $X^i$, which uses LUC for $X^i$ and $X^{i+1}$, and the lift of the isomorphism for $i$. This is the composite of identifications of the text's proof. Corollary 7.6.8 follows, since (ZHOU) implies (SLUC) (Theorem 7.4.13, §VII.45) ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ARaise · EP.corollary_7_6_8⟧. *Reading.* "The identity on objects" is stated for $i = 1$ only: for variable $i$ the object types of $(X^i)_R$ and $(X_R)^i$ are equal but not by definition, and the statement is an isomorphism in $\mathcal{EP}$ (gap G.82, closed; Findings, Chapter 7, item 131) (pp. 349–351).

### VII.47 Appendix 7.6.3: Zhou's retract

*Appendix 7.6.3 (p. 348), paraphrased.* On $E = L^2(\mathbb R)$ with the levels $E_m = H^{m,\delta_m}(\mathbb R)$, $0 = \delta_0 < \delta_1 < \cdots$, and a smooth compactly supported $\beta \ge 0$ with $\int\beta^2 = 1$, the map $r(t, f) = (t, \pi_t f)$ on $\mathbb R \oplus E$, with $\pi_t = 0$ for $t \le 0$ and $\pi_t f = \langle f, \beta_c\rangle\beta_c$, $\beta_c = \beta(\cdot + c)$, $c = e^{1/t}$, for $t > 0$, is an sc-smooth retraction (the text cites [60] and Part I's Subsection 1.4.4). Its retract $Y$ is a point over each $t \le 0$ and a line over each $t > 0$. $\mathbb Z/2$ acts on $Y$ by $(t, f) \mapsto (t, -f)$; the text computes the non-effective part on $\Sigma \cong Y$ and finds one point in $\mathrm{cl}(\mathbf X^T) \setminus \mathbf X^T$. The first reading used an analogue (§VII.36); the example itself is formalized as follows.

**The sc-Hilbert space** (V7.82) ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Line · ZhouLine.lineSc⟧. *For $0 = \delta_0 < \delta_1 < \cdots$, $E_m = H^{m,\delta_m}(\mathbb R)$ is an sc-structure on $L^2(\mathbb R)$, with level $0$ equal to $L^2(\mathbb R)$* ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Line · ZhouLine.level0_line⟧. *Step 1, the levels.* $H^{m,\delta}(\mathbb R)$ is taken inside $L^2(\mathbb R)$ as the $f$ whose lift $f \circ \mathrm{pr}_1$ to the cylinder $\mathbb R \times S^1$ lies in Part I's weighted Sobolev space $H^{m,\delta}(\mathbb R \times S^1)$, normed by the lift ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Line · ZhouLine.H1⟧ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Line · ZhouLine.liftH⟧; a function of $s$ alone has no $t$-derivatives, so the norm is $\sum_{a \le m}\|e^{\delta|s|}\partial_s^af\|^2_{L^2}$. Completeness holds because the range of the lift is closed. *Step 2, compactness.* The inclusions $E_{m+1} \to E_m$ are restrictions of Part I's compact inclusions on the cylinder ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Line · ZhouLine.isCompactOperator_incl1⟧. *Step 3, density.* Averaging over $S^1$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Line · ZhouLine.avgH⟧, of norm at most $1$ on every level and the adjoint of the lift, maps the dense test functions of the cylinder to test functions of $\mathbb R$, which are therefore dense in every level ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Line · ZhouLine.dense_ofTest1⟧. *Reading.* The level is defined through the lift; the equivalence with the one-dimensional definition by weak derivatives is not formalized, and the norms are the same.

**Translates** (V7.82). The translate $\tau_c\chi = \chi(\cdot + c)$ of a test function lies in every level ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Shift · ZhouLine.trH⟧, with $\|\tau_c\chi\|_{H^{m,\delta}} \le C e^{\delta(|c| + R)}$ for $\chi$ supported in $[-R, R]$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Shift · ZhouLine.norm_trH_le⟧, while the pairing with a far translate is small, $\|\langle\tau_c\chi, \cdot\rangle\|_{(H^{m,\delta})'} \le C e^{-\delta(c - R)}$, since $e^{-\delta|s|} \le e^{-\delta(c - R)}$ on the support of $\tau_c\chi$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Shift · ZhouLine.norm_ellL_tr0_le⟧. Both depend smoothly on $c$, with derivative given by $\chi'$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Shift · ZhouLine.hasDerivAt_trH⟧ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Shift · ZhouLine.hasDerivAt_ellT⟧.

**Flatness at $t = 0$** (V7.82). *If $g = 0$ for $t \le 0$, $g$ is $C^\infty$ on $t > 0$ and every derivative tends to $0$ at $0^+$, then $g$ is $C^\infty$* ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Flat · ZhouFlat.contDiff_of_flat⟧. *If $Q$ is $C^\infty$ with every derivative bounded by $Ke^{-\varepsilon c}$, $\varepsilon > 0$, then $t \mapsto Q(e^{1/t})$ for $t > 0$, $0$ for $t \le 0$, is $C^\infty$* ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Flat · ZhouFlat.contDiff_flat_comp⟧: by Faà di Bruno's formula the derivatives of $Q(e^{1/t})$ are sums of derivatives of $Q$ at $e^{1/t}$ times polynomials in $1/t$ and $e^{1/t}$, and the decay $e^{-\varepsilon e^{1/t}}$ beats them as $t \to 0^+$.

**The retraction** (V7.82) ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Family · ZhouLine.zhouRetraction⟧. *$r(t, f) = (t, \pi_t f)$ is an sc-smooth retraction of $\mathbb R \oplus E$.* The operators $\pi_t$ on each level ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Family · ZhouLine.zhouFam⟧ form a loss family in the sense of Part I's criterion of Remark 4.1.3 ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Family · ZhouLine.isLossFamily_zhouFam⟧, which gives the sc-smoothness of $r$: *compatibility*, $\pi_t$ commutes with the inclusions of the levels; *continuity*, $(t, f) \mapsto \pi_t f$ is continuous on every level, from a bound on $\|\pi_t\|$ uniform in $t$ and the continuity on the dense test functions; *loss of one level*, $t \mapsto \pi_t \circ \iota$, $\iota : E_{m+1} \to E_m$, is $C^\infty$ into the bounded operators: for $t > 0$ it is $Q(e^{1/t})$ with $Q(c) = \langle\cdot, \beta_c\rangle\beta_c$ as an operator $E_{m+1} \to E_m$, whose derivatives satisfy $\|D^nQ(c)\| \le Ke^{-(\delta_{m+1} - \delta_m)c}$ by the two bounds on translates ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Family · ZhouLine.norm_iteratedFDeriv_zhouQ_le⟧, and flatness applies with $\varepsilon = \delta_{m+1} - \delta_m > 0$; *idempotence*, $\pi_t\pi_t = \pi_t$ since $\langle\beta_c, \beta_c\rangle = \int\beta^2 = 1$. So the sc-smoothness the text cites from [60] is proved, and only one level of loss is used. *The data* ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.Data⟧ are the weights and a test function $\beta$ with $\int\beta^2 = 1$; the text's $\beta \ge 0$ is not needed. A $\beta$ as the book requires exists ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Family · ZhouLine.exists_beta⟧, and $\delta_m = m$ with a normalized bump is a witness of the data ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.Data.std⟧.

**The ep-groupoid and its non-effective part** (V7.82) ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.appendix_7_6_3⟧. *For $\mathbb Z/2$ acting on $Y$ by $(t, f) \mapsto (t, -f)$: $\mathbf X^T = (\{1\} \times Y) \cup (\{-1\} \times \{t < 0\})$, $\mathrm{cl}(\mathbf X^T) \setminus \mathbf X^T = \{(-1, (0, 0))\}$, $T_R$ is not Hausdorff, and LUC and (ZHOU) fail.* The action is the restriction of the sc-operator $(t, f) \mapsto (t, \pm f)$, which commutes with $r$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.isScSmoothMap_smul⟧, and the translation groupoid of §VII.30 is an ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.X⟧. *Step 1, the retract as printed.* $Y$ is $\{(t, 0)\}$ over $t \le 0$ and the line $\mathbb R\beta_{e^{1/t}}$ over each $t > 0$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.mem_O_iff'⟧. *Step 2, $\mathbf X^T$.* $1$ acts trivially; $-1$ acts trivially near a point over $t < 0$, where $Y$ is the half-line of points $(t, 0)$, and near no point over $t \ge 0$, where points with $f \ne 0$ accumulate ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.nonEffectivePart_eq⟧. *Step 3, the closure.* $(-1, (0, 0))$ is the limit of $(-1, (t, 0))$, $t \to 0^-$, and the only point of the closure not in $\mathbf X^T$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.closure_nonEffectivePart_diff⟧. *Step 4, the consequences.* $\mathbf X^T$ is not closed, so $T_R$ is not Hausdorff ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.not_t2Space_reducedMor⟧ and LUC fails ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.not_isLUC⟧ (Theorem 7.2.22); (ZHOU) implies LUC (Proposition 7.4.10, whose Part I facts hold, §VII.45), so (ZHOU) fails ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2ZhouGroupoid · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.not_isZhou⟧.

**$\Sigma$ as printed** (V7.82) ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Sigma · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.appendix_7_6_3_sigma⟧. The text works on $\Sigma = \{(s, t) \in \mathbb R^2 \mid t = 0 \text{ if } s \le 0\}$, with $\mathbb Z/2$ written $\{0, 1\}$. $(s, t) \mapsto (s, t\beta(\cdot + e^{1/s}))$ (and $(s, 0)$ for $s \le 0$) is a homeomorphism $\Sigma \cong Y$, with inverse $(s, f) \mapsto (s, \langle f, \beta_{e^{1/s}}\rangle)$, using $\|\beta_c\| = 1$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Sigma · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.sigmaHomeo⟧; pulled back to $\{0, 1\} \times \Sigma$ (with $0 \mapsto 1$, $1 \mapsto -1$), the non-effective part and $\mathrm{cl}(\mathbf X^T) \setminus \mathbf X^T$, the single point $(1, (0, 0))$ in the text's notation, are the printed sets ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Sigma · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.nonEffectivePart_sigma⟧ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_A2Sigma · EpGroupoid.Examples.ZhouRetract.closure_nonEffectivePart_sigma⟧. Every claim of the appendix holds as we read it (gap G.83, closed; rows V7.82, V7.95; Findings, Chapter 7, items 130, 139, 156) (pp. 331, 348).

### VII.48 Propositions 7.2.10, 7.2.16 and Theorem 7.2.14 in the 2021 form; Corollary 7.6.6 as printed

**Proposition 7.2.10, 2021 form** (V7.39) ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_AReduced · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_10_natural_charts⟧. *$\mathbf X^R$ with the quotient topology $T_R$ has the natural charts $\Psi_\varphi = \psi \circ \sigma \circ s$; their domains cover $\mathbf X^R$ and any two are sc-smoothly compatible.* This is Steps 1–5 of §VII.16, which need no hypothesis; the 2021 text states the proposition as the charts, and leaves Hausdorffness to Theorem 7.2.14, as the formalization had. The charts form the atlas of §VII.16 ⟦Chapter7/Reduced · EpGroupoid.reducedAtlas⟧ (p. 313).

**Theorem 7.2.14 and Proposition 7.2.16** (V7.40) ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_AReduced · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_2_14_reduced⟧ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_AReduced · EpGroupoid.proposition_7_2_16⟧. *If $T_R$ is Hausdorff, $X_R = (X, \mathbf X^R)$ is an ep-groupoid with the structure maps of $X$ descended to $\mathbf X^R$, the object M-polyfold of $X$ and the natural M-polyfold structure on $\mathbf X^R$; it is effective; its isotropy group at $x$ is $G_x/T_x$; and $\pi$ is an ep-functor $X \to X_R$.* The proof is §VII.17 — Proposition 7.10 (2017) — with the Hausdorff hypothesis only: paracompactness is Proposition 7.2.12 (§VII.34), an instance, so the M-polyfold $\mathbf X^R$ of §VII.16 is built from Hausdorffness alone. Each clause is a component already proved: the groupoid and the structures are those of §§VII.16–VII.17 by definition, effectiveness is §VII.17, the isotropy is §VII.17's $G_x/T_x$, and the functor is the reduction functor. The hypothesis is the text's own, satisfied by every effective ep-groupoid and by every ep-groupoid with LUC (§VII.35) (rows V7.39, V7.40, now same; Findings, Chapter 7, items 56, 60, 107, 111, 125, 126) (pp. 318–319).

**Corollary 7.6.6 as printed** (V7.68) ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ACor766 · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_6_6_unconditional⟧. *If $|X|$ is paracompact and the object M-polyfold has an atlas whose local models have Hilbert spaces $E_0$, $X$ has sc-smooth partitions of unity.* The text's proof: Part I's Corollary 5.5.17 and Theorem 5.5.10 give sc-smooth partitions of unity on the object M-polyfold, and Theorem 7.5.7 applies. With Part I's Theorem 5.5.16 now a theorem (§VII.29), the first step needs no hypothesis ⟦Chapter5/GapP1_SeparablePOU · MPolyfold.admitsScPartitionsOfUnity_of_hilbert_unconditional⟧ and the corollary is the text's two lines. The hypotheses are satisfiable on $\mathbb R^1$ ⟦Chapter7/GapP2_ACor766 · EpGroupoid.corollary_7_6_6_hypotheses_rn_unconditional⟧ (row V7.68, now same; Findings, Chapter 7, item 95) (p. 347). Remark 7.5.6, which points to this case, is an assessment with nothing to formalize (row V7.57; §VII.24).

### VII.49 Property (5) does not follow from (1)–(4): an ep-groupoid with a non-paracompact orbit space

*The text (p. 340 (2017 p. 249)).* After Definition 7.5.1 the text recalls that $|X|$ is always Hausdorff (Lemma 7.3.4), says that it is presently not known whether (5) is a consequence of (1)–(4), and that it is when $X$ is second countable. **The answer is no** ⟦Chapter7/PropertyFiveResearch · EpGroupoid.Examples.Pruefer.exists_epGroupoid_not_hasParacompactOrbitSpace⟧. The orbit space of an ep-groupoid is Hausdorff and locally the quotient of an M-polyfold by a finite group; a non-metrizable surface is such a space, as the orbit space of the Čech groupoid of an atlas. The example is the Čech groupoid of the atlas of a Prüfer-type surface (after Prüfer; Calabi–Rosenlicht 1953).

**The surface.** One chart $\mathbb R^2$ for each $a$ in an uncountable discrete index set $\iota$, injected into $\mathbb R$ by $c$; the chart $a$ is glued to the chart $b$ along the open upper half-planes by $(u, y) \mapsto (u + (a - b)/y, y)$. In the canonical coordinates $(X, l)$, $y = e^l$, $X = u + ae^{-l}$, the gluing is the identity; the coordinate change $\mathrm{chartPt}_a(X, l) = (X - ae^{-l}, e^l)$ ⟦Chapter7/PropertyFiveResearch · EpGroupoid.Examples.Pruefer.chartPt⟧ is a diffeomorphism of $\mathbb R^2$ onto the open upper half-plane, with inverse $\mathrm{canon}_a$ ⟦Chapter7/PropertyFiveResearch · EpGroupoid.Examples.Pruefer.canon⟧. So the surface is the open upper half-plane with one closed lower half-plane attached along its own copy of the real axis for each $a$.

**The ep-groupoid** ⟦Chapter7/PropertyFiveResearch · EpGroupoid.Examples.Pruefer.epGroupoid⟧. Objects $\iota \times \mathbb R^2$ and morphisms $(\iota \sqcup \{(a, b) \mid a \ne b\}) \times \mathbb R^2$, disjoint unions of copies of $\mathbb R^2$ over discrete sets, hence M-polyfolds, metrizable and paracompact. The sheet of $a$ carries the units of the chart $a$, and the sheet of $(a, b)$ the morphisms from $(a, \mathrm{chartPt}_{c(a)}(p))$ to $(b, \mathrm{chartPt}_{c(b)}(p))$, $p$ the canonical coordinates. There is at most one morphism between two objects, so composition, units and inverses are determined by sources and targets, and the groupoid laws reduce to that uniqueness. *(1)* On each sheet, $s$ and $t$ are the identity or $\mathrm{chartPt}$, diffeomorphisms onto open sets; a $C^\infty$ map on an open subset of $\mathbb R^m$ is sc-smooth there ⟦Chapter7/PropertyFiveResearch · isScSmoothOn_rn_rn_of_contDiffOn⟧. *(2), (4)* are checked sheet by sheet, (4) in the sheet form ⟦Chapter7/PropertyFiveResearch · EpGroupoid.Examples.Pruefer.isScSmoothCompSheet⟧. *(3)* With $V(x)$ a unit ball in one chart: a morphism with source over $\mathrm{cl}\,V(x)$ and target in a compact $K$ lies in one of finitely many sheets, and on the sheet $(a, b)$, $a \ne b$, both $e^l$ and $(a - b)e^{-l}$ are bounded, so the canonical coordinates are bounded ⟦Chapter7/PropertyFiveResearch · EpGroupoid.Examples.Pruefer.exists_isProperMap⟧.

**Not (5)** ⟦Chapter7/PropertyFiveResearch · EpGroupoid.Examples.Pruefer.not_paracompactSpace_orbitSpace⟧. *Step 1.* The point $d_a = |(a, 0)|$ is the only point of its orbit in the charts, since the axis $y = 0$ is not glued. The open sets $W_a = |X| \setminus \{d_b \mid b \ne a\}$ cover $|X|$, and $d_a \in W_b$ only for $b = a$; so a locally finite open refinement has, for every $a$, a member containing $d_a$, and these members are distinct for distinct $a$. *Step 2, the density step.* Every open set containing $d_a$ contains $|(a, (0, y))|$ for small $y > 0$, which is a point $|(a_0, q)|$ of a fixed chart $a_0$, and so a point $|(a_0, r)|$ with $r \in \mathbb Q^2$ ⟦Chapter7/PropertyFiveResearch · EpGroupoid.Examples.Pruefer.exists_rat_mem_of_mem⟧. *Step 3.* Each of the countably many points $|(a_0, r)|$ lies in finitely many members of the refinement, so only countably many members contain some $d_a$, and $\iota$ would be countable. For $\iota = \mathbb R$ with the discrete topology ⟦Chapter7/PropertyFiveResearch · EpGroupoid.Examples.Pruefer.pruefer⟧ this is absurd: the orbit space is not paracompact ⟦Chapter7/PropertyFiveResearch · EpGroupoid.Examples.Pruefer.pruefer_not_hasParacompactOrbitSpace⟧, though Hausdorff, as Lemma 7.3.4 says ⟦Chapter7/PropertyFiveResearch · EpGroupoid.Examples.Pruefer.t2Space_orbitSpace_pruefer⟧. *Reading.* "(1)–(4)" are the four conditions of Definition 7.1.3 as formalized, including the existential reading of (3) and the sheet form of (4); no second countability is assumed. The object space has uncountably many components and is not second countable, in line with the text's remark that second countability gives (5) (§VII.23) (Findings, Chapter 7, items 82, 113, 152) (p. 340 (2017 p. 249)).

### VII.50 Appendix 7.6.5: Theorem 7.6.9 for every representative, and in the book's form

**Theorem 7.6.9 for every representative** (V7.101) ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryFull · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_6_9_allReps⟧. *For a tame ep-groupoid: (1)–(5) and "$B$ is an ep-functor" as in §VII.42, and, for every representative $(x, V, \theta)$ of $bX$ and of $b\mathbf X$, centred or not: $U(x, V, \theta)$ and $\theta \cap V^x$ are open, $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is an sc-diffeomorphism of $U(x, V, \theta)$ onto $\theta \cap V^x$, which is all of $\theta$ for $V$ centred at $x$; and every M-polyfold structure with this property for every representative is equivalent to the one of (2).* §VII.42 characterized the structure through centred representatives. The proof applies Part I's Theorem 2.7.13 for every representative — the chart $\Phi$ of a non-centred triple is an sc-diffeomorphism onto $\theta \cap V^x$, and the uniqueness holds for that family — to the object and to the morphism M-polyfold (§II.37; gap G.78, closed). No hypothesis is added; tameness is met by the trivial ep-groupoid of a quadrant (§VII.42) (Findings, Chapter 7, item 151).

**Theorem 7.6.9 in the book's form** (V7.98) ⟦Chapter7/BookFormTameBoundaryEp2021 · EpGroupoid.theorem_7_6_9_book⟧. *For a tame ep-groupoid: (1) $bX$, $b\mathbf X$ are metrizable, with the only topologies for which every $U(x, V, \theta)$ is open and every $\Phi_{(x, V, \theta)}$ is open into $\theta$; (2) the structures are tame, every $\Phi$ is an open embedding and an sc-diffeomorphism onto the open set $\theta \cap V^x$, onto $\theta$ for centred $V$, and the structures are unique up to equivalence; (3) both maps $B$ are sc-smooth; (4) the index formulas hold; (5) the boundary ep-groupoid is tame with the structure maps (7.25)–(7.29); and $B$ is an ep-functor.* The statement assembles the topological half of §VII.40 and the previous paragraph into the order of the text. *Reading.* After the theorem the text says that $\Phi$ is a homeomorphism onto $\theta$. That holds as we read it for $V$ centred at $x$ only; for other representatives the image is $\theta \cap V^x$, a proper subset in general, as in Chapter 2's (2.44); the counterexample is a non-centred triple of the quadrant $[0, \infty)^3 \oplus W$, whose $\Phi$ is not onto $\theta$ ⟦Chapter2/TameBoundaryNonCentred · MPolyfold.not_surjOn_phiTot⟧, and every class has a centred representative ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEp · TameBoundary.exists_rep_centered⟧. This is the one row of the chapter formalized in a narrower form (row V7.98; Findings, Chapter 7, items 141, 155) (p. 355).

## Part VIII. Bundles and covering functors (HWZ Chapter 8, §§8.1–8.3, 8.5, 8.6 (2017 §§8.1–8.5))

Chapter 8 continues Part II; as for Chapter 7, its numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021, pp. 357–400), with the 2017 text's in parentheses (2017 pp. 257–289). It treats bundles over ep-groupoids and covering functors. §8.1 equips the tangent $T(X, \mathbf X) = (TX, T\mathbf X)$ of an ep-groupoid with the structure maps (8.1)–(8.9) and proves that it is an ep-groupoid, tame if $X$ is, with an sc-smooth projection functor to $X^1$ (Theorem 8.1.1 (2017: 8.1), Lemmas 8.1.2–8.1.9 (2017: 8.1–8.8)); it describes the morphisms of $T\mathbf X$ by pairs $(T\varphi, a)$ (Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1)), proves that the tangent of an sc-smooth functor is an sc-smooth functor and that $T : \mathcal{EP} \to \mathcal{EP}$ is a functor (Theorems 8.1.11, 8.1.12 (2017: 8.2, 8.3)), defines natural transformations and natural equivalence (Definition 8.1.13 (2017: 8.1)), proves that the tangent of a natural transformation is one (Proposition 8.1.14 (2017: 8.1)), and that the paracompactness of $|X|$ passes to $|TX|$ (Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4)). §8.2 defines sc-differential forms on ep-groupoids and the sc-de Rham complex (Definitions 8.2.1, 8.2.2 (2017: 8.2, 8.3)). §8.3 defines strong bundles over ep-groupoids (Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4)) with their functorial picture (pp. 375–377 (2017 pp. 271–272)), strong bundle maps and strong bundle functors (Definitions 8.3.2, 8.3.3 (2017: 8.5, 8.6)) and section functors (Definition 8.3.4 (2017: 8.7)). §8.5 (2017 §8.4) defines proper covering functors (Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8)), proves that they compose (Proposition 8.5.2 (2017: 8.2)), describes them near a fibre (Theorem 8.5.3 (2017: 8.5), Remark 8.5.4 (2017: 8.2)), defines covering functors of finite groupoids and geometric lifts (Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9)), constructs the proper covering functor of a geometric lift (Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3)), shows that every proper covering functor is locally of this form (Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6)), and defines proper strong bundle covering functors (Definition 8.5.9 (2017: 8.10)). The appendix counts the fibres of a proper covering functor (§8.6.1 (2017 §8.5.1): Lemmas 8.6.1–8.6.3 (2017: 8.9–8.11), Proposition 8.6.4 (2017: 8.4)) and describes strong bundle coverings fibrewise (§8.6.2 (2017 §8.5.2)). This Part retells §8.1 in §§VIII.1–VIII.9 — the tangent data (8.1)–(8.9) and the tangents of maps defined on open sets (§VIII.1), Theorem 8.1.1 (2017: 8.1) and Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1) (§VIII.2), Lemmas 8.1.3–8.1.6 (2017: 8.2–8.5) (§VIII.3), Lemmas 8.1.7 and 8.1.8 (2017: 8.6 and 8.7) (§VIII.4), Lemma 8.1.9 (2017: 8.8) (§VIII.5), Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1) (§VIII.6), Theorems 8.1.11 and 8.1.12 (2017: 8.2 and 8.3) (§VIII.7), Definition 8.1.13 (2017: 8.1), the equivalence relation $\simeq$ and Proposition 8.1.14 (2017: 8.1) (§VIII.8), Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4) (§VIII.9); §8.3 in §§VIII.10–VIII.14 — strong bundle maps and the pull-back along $s$ (§VIII.10), Definition 8.3.1 (2017: 8.4) and the fibre maps (§VIII.11), the functorial picture (§VIII.12), Definitions 8.3.2, 8.3.3 (2017: 8.5, 8.6) and their equivalence (§VIII.13), Definition 8.3.4 (2017: 8.7) (§VIII.14); §8.5 (2017 §8.4) in §§VIII.15–VIII.22 — Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8) and the degeneracy remark (§VIII.15), Proposition 8.5.2 (2017: 8.2) (§VIII.16), Theorem 8.5.3 (2017: 8.5) and Remark 8.5.4 (2017: 8.2) (§VIII.17), $\mathrm{Diff}_{sc}$, Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9) and the discussion after it (§VIII.18), disjoint unions of M-polyfolds (§VIII.19), Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) (§VIII.20), Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6) (§VIII.21), Definition 8.5.9 (2017: 8.10) (§VIII.22); the appendix in §§VIII.23–VIII.25 — §8.6.1 (2017 §8.5.1) and Lemmas 8.6.1–8.6.3 (2017: 8.9–8.11) (§VIII.23), Proposition 8.6.4 (2017: 8.4) (§VIII.24), §8.6.2 (2017 §8.5.2) (§VIII.25); the witnesses and the counterexample (§VIII.26); what is not formalized, among it §8.2 (§VIII.27); and what the formalization taught us (§VIII.28). Each item carries the number of its comparison item (V8.1–V8.43) in `Exposition/verification/ch08.md`. The additions of the 2021 edition (V8.44–V8.52) are retold in §§VIII.29–VIII.33: §8.1 (§VIII.29), §§8.3–8.4 (§VIII.30), §8.5 (§VIII.31), what is not formalized and what they taught us (§VIII.32), and Proposition 8.1.17 (2) for every $(TX)^i$ (§VIII.33). The work that closed the remaining gaps is retold in §§VIII.34–VIII.40: Lemma 8.1.2 as printed and the M-polyfold of pairs of Remark 8.1.10 (§VIII.34), Definition 8.2.1 (§VIII.35), Definition 8.2.2 and the pull-back of forms (§VIII.36), the Poincaré lemma, Proposition 8.2.3 (§VIII.37), Proposition 8.1.16 without added hypothesis (§VIII.38), Propositions 8.4.1 and 8.4.3 (§VIII.39), and Lemma 8.5.10, Proposition 8.5.7 for $D = \emptyset$, Theorem 8.5.8 in every universe and Proposition 8.1.17 without added hypotheses (§VIII.40).

**What is proved, and what is not.** Every statement and every definition of the chapter is formalized, and every gap of the chapter is closed: G.74 (Definitions 8.2.1, 8.2.2, §§VIII.35–VIII.36), G.75 (Lemma 8.1.2 as printed, §VIII.34), G.86 (Proposition 8.4.1 (3), §VIII.39), G.87 (the Poincaré lemma, Proposition 8.2.3, §VIII.37), G.88 (Proposition 8.1.16 without added hypothesis, §VIII.38) and G.89 (Lemma 8.5.10, §VIII.40). Theorems 8.1.1–8.5.8 (2017: 8.1–8.6) are proved, Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6) for ep-groupoids in any one universe, and Theorem 8.5.3 (2017: 8.5) with (5) read with $s$ on both vertical arrows; so are Propositions 8.1.14, 8.5.2 and 8.6.4 (2017: 8.1, 8.2 and 8.4), the 2021 Propositions 8.1.16, 8.1.17, 8.2.3, 8.4.1 and 8.4.3, Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) for nonempty $D$, Lemmas 8.1.2–8.6.3 (2017: 8.1–8.11), Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1) also as printed, Lemma 8.5.10, Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1) with its M-polyfold of pairs and its triples, and Remark 8.5.4 (2017: 8.2). Three rows are formalized in a narrower form. In Remark 8.1.10 (2017: 8.1) (row V8.12) the map $G(\varphi, h) = (T\varphi, Ts(h))$ is a bijection with $T\varphi$ labelled by $\varphi$; read with the bare linear map $T\varphi$, it does not hold as we read it, and the trivial $\mathbb Z/3$-action is the counterexample ⟦Chapter8/TangentEpNotInjective · EpGroupoid.Examples.remark_8_1_10_not_injective⟧ (§VIII.6). The degeneracy remark after Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8) (row V8.28) is proved for tame $X$, $Y$, a hypothesis the text does not state, and as an inequality in general; equality without tameness is open in the project (§VIII.15). Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) (row V8.35) is proved for nonempty $D$; for $D = \emptyset$ it does not hold as we read it, and a covering functor of the empty groupoid with a geometric lift on $\mathbb R$ is the counterexample ⟦Chapter8/GeometricLiftEmpty2021 · CoveringExamples.not_proposition_8_5_7_empty⟧ (§§VIII.20, VIII.40). Three places of the 2017 text needed more than a reading. Theorem 8.5.3 (5) (2017: 8.5), as printed with $t$ on the right vertical arrow, does not hold as we read it: the identity functor of $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ violates it in every chart at $0$, and the square holds with $s$ (§VIII.17). Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9) allows $D = \emptyset$, and then the functor of Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) is surjective on objects only if $U(x) = \emptyset$; Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) is proved for nonempty $D$, which holds where Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6) uses it (§VIII.20). The degeneracy remark after Definition 8.5.1 (2017: 8.8) uses the product formula $d_{\mathbf X \times Y} = d_{\mathbf X} + d_Y$, which Part I has for tame M-polyfolds; it is proved for tame $X$, $Y$, and as an inequality in general (§VIII.15). Several omitted steps are supplied: the tangents of maps defined on open sets, which the proofs of §8.1 differentiate without a definition (§VIII.1); the tameness of $Tr$ in Lemma 8.1.9 (2017: 8.8), asserted without argument (§VIII.5); that $\simeq$ is an equivalence relation (§VIII.8); the open embedding $G_x\backslash TU(x) \to |TX|$ in the proof of Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4) (§VIII.9); the ep-groupoid of the functorial picture (§VIII.12); the equivalence of Definitions 8.3.2 and 8.3.3 (2017: 8.5 and 8.6) (§VIII.13); and the "one verifies" of Proposition 8.5.7 (2017: 8.3) and of Theorem 8.5.8 (2017: 8.6) (§§VIII.20, VIII.21). Several proofs take another route: Lemmas 8.1.4–8.1.6 (2017: 8.3–8.5), Theorem 8.1.11 (2017: 8.2) and Proposition 8.1.14 (2017: 8.1) by fibre injectivity instead of differentiating identities (§§VIII.3, VIII.7, VIII.8); condition (4) of Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3) for $T\mathbf X$ in Chapter 7's sheet form (§VIII.4); Theorem 8.1.15 (2017: 8.4) by metrizability instead of a closed paracompact cover (§VIII.9); Theorem 8.5.3 (2017: 8.5) through Definition 8.5.1 (3) (2017: 8.8) instead of sheets and natural representations in $Y$ (§VIII.17). Not formalized: a few remarks that nothing uses, and equality in the degeneracy remark without tameness (§VIII.27).

**Seven structural choices.** (1) *The tangent is Part I's.* $TX$ and $T\mathbf X$ are Part I's tangent M-polyfolds and $Ts$, $Tt$, $Tu$, $T\iota$ Part I's tangent maps (§§II.8, II.9); for $X$ in `Type u` they live in `Type (max u 1)`, and so does the tangent functor of Theorem 8.1.12 (2017: 8.3). The fibres $T_xX$ carry Part I's linear structure, transported through charts (Definition 2.3.14; gap G.7, closed since the first reading), which gives $T\varphi$ as a linear isomorphism (§VII.44) and the forms of §8.2 (§VIII.35); the proofs of §8.1 do not use it. (2) *The composition of $T\mathbf X$ is defined by choice*: total, with a junk value off composable pairs, as Chapter 7's composition, and unique on composable pairs. (3) *Fibre injectivity.* $s$ being a local sc-diffeomorphism, two vectors of $T\mathbf X$ with the same base point and the same image under $Ts$ are equal; most identities of §8.1 are proved this way instead of by differentiating identities. (4) *Tangents of maps defined on open sets* are built from the charts, as Part I builds $Tf$, with a junk value off $p^{-1}(U)$. (5) *Condition (4) in sheet form*, as in Chapter 7 (§VII.2): for $T\mathbf X$, for the functorial picture of a strong bundle and for the ep-groupoid of a geometric lift; Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1) is stated in this form. (6) *Strong bundle maps between strong bundles over M-polyfolds are a reading*: Part I defines strong bundle maps only between local models, and the global notion is a map covering a map of the bases, linear on the fibres, sc-smooth on $[0]$ and on $[1]$ (§VIII.10). (7) *Data, not hypotheses.* "A connected and sufficiently small $U(x)$ admitting the natural $G_x$-action" in Theorems 8.5.3 and 8.5.8 (2017: 8.5 and 8.6) is a datum, a chart of Theorem 8.5.3 (2017: 8.5), as natural representations are in Chapter 7; Definition 8.5.5 (2017: 8.9) is stated with Mathlib's groupoids, $C$ being `SingleObj G`, and its finiteness enters as instance arguments of the results that use it.

Throughout, $X = (X, \mathbf X)$ is an ep-groupoid as in Part VII, with source and target $s, t$, composition $m(\psi, \varphi) = \psi \circ \varphi$, unit $u(x) = 1_x$ and inverse $\iota(\varphi) = \varphi^{-1}$. $TX$ and $T\mathbf X$ are Part I's tangent M-polyfolds (§II.8), $p$ the projection of a tangent vector to its base point on level $1$, and $Tf$ Part I's tangent map of an sc-smooth $f$ (§II.9). For a vector $v \in T\mathbf X$ we write $p(v) \in \mathbf X_1$ for its base point, so $p(Ts(v)) = s(p(v))$. A *sheet* of $s$ is an open set $\mathbf W \subseteq \mathbf X$ on which $s$ is an sc-diffeomorphism onto an open $V$, its inverse $\sigma$ a *local inverse* of $s$; for open $U \subseteq X$, $TU = p^{-1}(U)$. $G_x$ is the isotropy group of $x$, and a natural representation $(U(x), \Phi, \Gamma)$ is Chapter 7's (§VII.7), with $U(x)$ open and connected. Part I results are cited in the same way, by their 2021 numbers with the 2017 numbers in parentheses (Definition 2.5.2, tame retractions, is 2017 Definition 2.17, §II.14; Proposition 2.5.20, fibred products, is 2017 Proposition 2.15, §II.17; Proposition 2.6.8, the pull-back strong bundle, is 2017 Proposition 2.16, §II.20; Proposition 2.4.4, 2017 Proposition 2.7, is `proposition_2_4_4`, §II.11; Lemma 1.3.4 is 2017 Lemma 1.1, §I.18); the Lean names of Parts I and II carry the 2021 numbers. Findings are those of `Exposition/Findings.md`, "Chapter 8".

### VIII.1 The tangent data (8.1)–(8.9), and tangents of maps on open sets

**The tangent data** (V8.1). The objects of $T(X, \mathbf X)$ are the points of $TX$ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.TangentSpace⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentPolyfold⟧, the morphisms those of $T\mathbf X$; a vector $(\varphi, h) \in T_\varphi\mathbf X$ is viewed as a morphism $Ts(\varphi)(h) \to Tt(\varphi)(h)$ (8.2), so that $s_T = Ts$ and $t_T = Tt$ (8.3) ⟦Chapter8/Basic · EpGroupoid.tSrc⟧ ⟦Chapter8/Basic · EpGroupoid.tTgt⟧, Part I's tangent maps ⟦Chapter2/TangentMap · MPolyfold.tangentMap⟧. The unit is $u_T = Tu$ and the inverse $\iota_T = T\iota$ (8.9) ⟦Chapter8/Basic · EpGroupoid.tUnit⟧ ⟦Chapter8/Basic · EpGroupoid.tInv⟧, and the base point $p : T\mathbf X \to \mathbf X^1$ is Part I's projection ⟦Chapter8/Basic · EpGroupoid.tBase⟧ ⟦Chapter2/TangentBundle · MPolyfold.tangentProj⟧. *The composition* (8.5), $(\psi, k) \circ (\varphi, h) = (\psi \circ \varphi, Ts(\psi \circ \varphi)^{-1}(Ts(\varphi)(h)))$ for $Ts(\psi)(k) = Tt(\varphi)(h)$ (8.4), needs the inverse of $Ts$ on one fibre. *Step 1, fibre bijectivity.* Since $s$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, $Ts$ maps every fibre $T_\varphi\mathbf X$ bijectively onto $T_{s(\varphi)}X$ (Step 4 of the next paragraph). So two vectors of $T\mathbf X$ with the same base point and the same image under $Ts$ are equal ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.tangent_ext⟧, and every vector over $s(\varphi)$ is $Ts(v)$ for a $v$ over $\varphi$ ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.exists_tSrc_eq⟧. *Step 2, the choice.* For a composable pair, $s(p\,k) = t(p\,h)$ ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.src_tBase_eq⟧, and $k \circ h$ is chosen as a vector over $p(k) \circ p(h)$ with $Ts(k \circ h) = Ts(h)$ ⟦Chapter8/Basic · EpGroupoid.tComp⟧ ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.tComp_spec⟧ ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.tBase_tComp⟧ ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.tSrc_tComp⟧; off composable pairs it is the junk value $h$, which no statement uses. By Step 1 the choice is the only possible one, which is (8.5) in this form ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.tComp_eq⟧. *Step 3, the units.* $u_T = Tu$ is (8.8), $1_a = (1_x, Ts(1_x)^{-1}a)$: $Tu(a)$ lies over $1_x$, and $Ts(Tu(a)) = a$ by the chain rule for $s \circ u = \mathrm{id}$, so Step 1 identifies the two ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.tUnit_eq⟧. (8.5) writes $T_{\varphi \circ \psi}\mathbf X$ for $T_{\psi \circ \varphi}\mathbf X$ (possible misprint) (Findings, Chapter 8, items 1, 2) (pp. 357–359 (2017 pp. 257–258)).

**Tangents of maps on open sets** (V8.2). The proofs of §8.1 differentiate maps that are defined only on open sets, such as a local inverse $(s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}$ and the map $\alpha$ of Lemma 8.1.3 (2017: 8.2), and write $TU$ for the part of $TX$ over an open $U$; Part I defines $Tf$ only for maps sc-smooth on the whole M-polyfold. Here $TU$ is the open set $p^{-1}(U)$ ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.tangentPreimage⟧ ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.isOpen_tangentPreimage⟧, and it is the tangent of the open sub-M-polyfold $U$ when $U \ne \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.isScDiffeoOn_tangentMap_subtypeVal⟧ ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.isOpenEmbedding_tangentMap_subtypeVal⟧. *Step 1, the construction.* For $f$ sc-smooth on $U$, $Tf$ on $p^{-1}(U)$ is built from the charts as Part I builds $Tf$ (§II.9), with $U \cap V \cap f^{-1}(V')$ in place of $V \cap f^{-1}(V')$ ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.TangentPre.fimageOn⟧ ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.tangentMapOn⟧; off $p^{-1}(U)$ it takes a junk value, which exists because a nonempty M-polyfold has points on level $1$ ($E_1$ is dense in $E_0$ and a nonempty retract meets it) ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.exists_mem_levelSet_one⟧ ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.nonempty_tangentSpace⟧. *Step 2, the calculus.* $Tf$ lies over $f$ ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.levelVal_tangentProj_tangentMapOn⟧, agrees with Part I's tangent when $f$ is sc-smooth everywhere ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.tangentMapOn_eq_tangentMap⟧, satisfies the chain rule ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.tangentMapOn_comp⟧ and is sc-smooth on $p^{-1}(U)$ ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.tangentMapOn_isScSmoothOn⟧. *Step 3, sc-diffeomorphisms between open sets.* The tangent of an sc-diffeomorphism $U \to V$ is an sc-diffeomorphism $p^{-1}(U) \to p^{-1}(V)$ with the tangent of the inverse as its inverse, by the chain rule ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.tangent⟧ ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.tangentMap⟧, and it is bijective on every fibre ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.bijOn_tangentFiber⟧; this is the step "$Ts : T\mathbf U(\varphi) \to TU(x)$ is an sc-diffeomorphism" of Lemma 8.1.8 (2017: 8.7). *Step 4, local sc-diffeomorphisms.* A sheet of $Tf$ around $v$ is $p^{-1}(U)$ for a sheet $U$ of $f$ around $p(v)$, so $Tf$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.tangentMap⟧, bijective on the fibres ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.bijOn_tangentFiber⟧ and surjective when $f$ is ⟦Chapter8/TangentLocal · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.surjective_tangentMap⟧. Step 4 is Lemma 8.1.7's (2017: 8.6) "by construction". The chain rule with a globally sc-smooth outer map, $TF \circ Tf = T(F \circ f)$ on $p^{-1}(U)$, is used throughout ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · MPolyfold.tangentMap_tangentMapOn⟧ (Findings, Chapter 8, item 3) (used on pp. 358–364 (2017 pp. 258–263)).

### VIII.2 Theorem 8.1.1 (2017: 8.1), and Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1)

**Theorem 8.1.1 (2017: 8.1)** (V8.3) ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.theorem_8_1_1⟧. *$T(X, \mathbf X) = (TX, T\mathbf X)$ with the structure maps (8.3)–(8.9) is an ep-groupoid; it is tame if $X$ is; and the projections form an sc-smooth functor $(p, \mathbf p) : T(X, \mathbf X) \to (X, \mathbf X)^1$.* The text proves it on pp. 363–365 (2017 pp. 263–264) by collecting Lemmas 8.1.2–8.1.9 (2017: 8.1–8.8), and the formalization does the same. The groupoid laws are Lemmas 8.1.3–8.1.6 (2017: 8.2–8.5) (§VIII.3) ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.tangentGroupoidStr⟧; conditions (1), (2) and (4) of Definition 7.1.3 (2017: 7.3) are Lemma 8.1.7 (2017: 8.6) and condition (3) is Lemma 8.1.8 (2017: 8.7) (§VIII.4); together they make the ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.tangentEpGroupoid⟧, and `theorem_8_1_1` records that it has the M-polyfolds $TX$, $T\mathbf X$, the structure maps of the text, and the base point and source of a composite. The tameness sentence is Lemma 8.1.9 (2017: 8.8) (§VIII.5) ⟦Chapter8/TangentTame · EpGroupoid.theorem_8_1_1_tame⟧. *The projection functor.* $(X, \mathbf X)^1$ is Chapter 7's lift to level $1$ (§VII.22) ⟦Chapter7/Lift · EpGroupoid.liftOne⟧, and $(p, \mathbf p)$ is a functor into it ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.tangentProjFunctor⟧: it commutes with sources and targets because $p \circ Ts = s \circ p$ and $p \circ Tt = t \circ p$, with the composition because $p(k \circ h) = p(k) \circ p(h)$ (Step 2 of §VIII.1, the text's "This is obvious"), and with the units because $Tu(a)$ lies over $1_x$; the two projections are sc-smooth by Part I (Findings, Chapter 8, items 2, 9) (2017 pp. 258, 263–264).

**Lemma 8.1.2 (2017: 8.1)** (V8.4) ⟦Chapter8/TangentEp · EpGroupoid.lemma_8_1_2⟧. *As printed*: with $T(\mathbf X\,{}_s{\times}_t\,\mathbf X)$ identified with $T\mathbf X\,{}_{Ts}{\times}_{Tt}\,T\mathbf X$, the composition (8.5) is $(\psi, k) \circ (\varphi, h) = Tm(\psi, \varphi)(k, h)$. **The text's proof** varies $\varphi'$ near $\varphi$, writes the partner as $\psi' = F(\varphi') = (s|\mathbf U(\psi))^{-1}(t(\varphi'))$, applies $s$ to $m(F(\varphi'), \varphi')$, which gives $s(\varphi')$, and differentiates this identity at $\varphi$; since $s$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism, $Tm(k, h) = Ts(\psi \circ \varphi)^{-1}Ts(\varphi)(h)$. **The formalized statement** is the form the proof uses; the identification of the tangent of the fibred product with the fibred product of the tangents, and $Tm$ on it, the lemma as printed, are §VIII.34 (gap G.75, closed).
