**Definition 9.5.14 (2017: 9.17) and the paragraph before it** (V9.52). $\partial S = |\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)| \subseteq S$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.orbitSupp_boundaryTheta_subset⟧. $(n-1)$-dimensional measure zero in the boundaries $\partial M_i$ ⟦Chapter9/Boundary · MPolyfold.submanifoldBoundary⟧ is a second system on a class of boundaries, and $K$ has measure zero in $\partial S$ if at every point of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$ a tame structure has boundary preimages null in the $\partial M_i$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroBoundary⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.IsMeasureZeroBoundaryAll⟧. *"A well-defined notion"* ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.isMeasureZeroBoundaryAll_of⟧: the proof of Lemma 9.5.2 applies to the boundaries. By the local formula for $\partial\Theta$ (Proposition 9.2.15), which holds for every structure given the independence of Theorem 9.2.1, a point of $\partial M'_j$ lies in $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$, and a point of $\mathrm{supp}(\partial\Theta)$ lies in some $\partial M_i$ of any structure at it, a positive sum having a nonzero term ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.exists_mem_of_sum_pos⟧; so the boundary preimage in $\partial M'_j$ is covered near each point by the $\partial M_i$ of a structure with null boundary preimages. $L(\partial S)$ is the σ-algebra generated by the Borel sets of $\partial S$ and these sets ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.boundaryMeasureZeroSets⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · EpGroupoid.lebesgueSigmaBoundary⟧. The $(n-1)$-dimensional null sets themselves, a witness with $\partial S \ne \emptyset$ and the σ-algebra $L(\partial S)$ built with them are §IX.34 (gap G.108, closed).

**Witnesses** (V9.53). *Tools.* Measure zero of Definition 9.4.5 is local ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isMeasureZero_image_of_local⟧, holds for subsingletons ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isMeasureZero_of_subsingleton⟧, and on $\mathbb R^2$ is Lebesgue measure zero ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isMeasureZero_rn2_iff⟧. On the trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^n$ every local branching structure restricts to a tame one, on the domain of a natural representation ⟦Chapter9/Measure · exists_tameBranchingStructure_trivial_rn⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · hasTameSheetsIn_trivial_rn⟧, and $\pi$ is injective ⟦Chapter9/Measure · injective_π_trivial_rn⟧. *Example 9.3.5.* The graph sheets of §9.4 carry a `SheetMeasureGeometry` ⟦Chapter9/Measure · graphSheetMeasureGeometry⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · graphNull⟧; for the $\Theta$ of the two graphs $G^{++}$, $G^{--}$, which touch at $0$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · theta935⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_theta935⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · hasTameSheetsIn_theta935⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · zero_mem_supp_theta935⟧, the point $|0|$ has measure zero ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isMeasureZeroSupp_theta935_zero⟧, $S$ does not ⟦Chapter9/Measure · not_isMeasureZeroSupp_theta935⟧, and both are in $L(S)$ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · lebesgueSigma_theta935⟧. *The plane.* For $\Theta = 1$ on $\mathbb R^2$, with the open subsets of $\mathbb R^2$ as sheets and Lebesgue null sets ⟦Chapter9/Measure · planeSheets⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · planeNull⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · planeSheet⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isSmoothSubmanifold_univ_rn2⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · thetaPlane⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_thetaPlane⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · mem_supp_thetaPlane⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Measure · hasTameSheetsIn_thetaPlane⟧, some member of $L(S)$ is not Borel ⟦Chapter9/Measure · exists_mem_lebesgueSigma_not_borel_thetaPlane⟧: every subset of the null axis is in $L(S)$, there are $2^{\mathfrak c}$ of them, and only $\mathfrak c$ Borel sets.

### IX.20 §9.5: the isotropy factors (Lemmas 9.5.9–9.5.11 and Proposition 9.5.13 (2017: Lemmas 9.18, 9.19))

The measures $\mu_\omega$ of Theorems 9.5.4 and 9.5.5 are local weighted integrals of a form over the sheets, divided by $\#G_x$ or $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$. This subsection gives what the proofs of Lemmas 9.5.9–9.5.11 and Proposition 9.5.13 rest on, the orders of the isotropy groups and the decompositions of the preimages; the measure identities themselves are stated and proved in §IX.31 (Lemmas 9.5.7, 9.5.9–9.5.11, Proposition 9.5.13 (1)) and §IX.33 (Proposition 9.5.13 (2)), and rows V9.54–V9.56 are explicit.

**Lemma 9.5.9 (2017: 9.18)** (V9.54). **The text's proof** identifies $H = \{g \mid g * y = y\}$ with $G_y$, writes $G = \bigcup_{r \in R} rH$, chooses $V(y)$ invariant under $H$ and disjoint from its other translates, notes that $\tilde M_j = V \cap M_j$ is a branching structure on $V$, decomposes the preimage of $K$ as $\bigcup_r \varphi_r(\tilde K)$, and uses $\#R = \#G/\#H$. **The formalized part.** *Step 1, $\#R \cdot \#G_y = \#G_x$* ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.card_quotient_stabilizer_mul_card_isotropy⟧: the stabilizer $H$ of $y$ for the action of $G_x$ on $U(x)$ is isomorphic to $G_y$ by the natural representation (Chapter 7) ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mem_stabilizer_iff_Φ⟧, and $R$ is `Quotient.out` on $G_x/H$. *Step 2, the slice* ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.exists_slice⟧: inside any neighbourhood of $y$ there is an open $V$ with $\varphi_g(V) = V$ for $g \in H$ and $\varphi_g(V) \cap V = \emptyset$ for $g \notin H$: separate $y$ from $\varphi_g(y) \ne y$ for the finitely many $g \notin H$, and make the neighbourhood $H$-invariant. *Step 3, the preimage.* $|\varphi_g(z)| = |z|$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.π_Φ⟧, so $\varphi_g$ maps $M_U = \mathrm{supp}(\Theta) \cap U$ to itself, $\Theta$ being a functor ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.mapsTo_Φ_MU⟧; for $K \subseteq |M_U \cap V|$, $M_U \cap \pi^{-1}(K) = \bigcup_{g} \varphi_g(M_U \cap V \cap \pi^{-1}(K))$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.MU_inter_preimage_eq_iUnion⟧, the same with $g$ running over the representatives $r$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.MU_inter_preimage_eq_iUnion_quotient⟧, and the union over $R$ is disjoint ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.pairwise_disjoint_image_Φ_out⟧. The restriction $\tilde M_j$ is §IX.3's `restrictAt`: the project's structures pass through their base point, so at $y$ the sheets through $y$ are kept.

**Lemma 9.5.10** (V9.55), new in the 2021 edition. *Step 1.* $\#T_x \cdot \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x = \#G_x$ for the subgroup $T_x$ acting trivially near $x$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.card_effIsotropy_mul_card_trivialSubgroup⟧. *Step 2.* Under LUC for the given $U(x)$ (Definition 7.2.18, `NaturalRep.HasLUC`), $T_x$ is the kernel of the representation ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerΦ_eq_trivialSubgroup⟧, hence lies in every stabilizer ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.kerΦ_le_stabilizer⟧, and corresponds to $T_y$ under $H \cong G_y$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.stabilizerEquivIsotropy_mem_trivialSubgroup_iff⟧, so $\#T_y = \#T_x$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.card_trivialSubgroup_eq⟧. *Step 3, (9.23).* Dividing Step 1 of Lemma 9.5.9 by $\#T_x = \#T_y$ gives $\#R \cdot \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_y = \#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.card_quotient_stabilizer_mul_card_effIsotropy⟧.

**Lemma 9.5.11 (2017: 9.19)** (V9.56). The orders $\#G_x$ and $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x$ are invariant along morphisms, by conjugation with $\varphi$ (Lemma 7.2.6) ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.card_isotropy_eq_of_mor⟧ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.card_effIsotropy_eq_of_mor⟧. A functor is constant on orbits ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.IsFunctorial.eq_of_π_eq⟧, so for structures on $U$, $U'$ and any map $\hat\varphi$ of $U$ onto $U'$ with $|\hat\varphi(z)| = |z|$, $|M_U| = |M_{U'}|$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.image_π_MU_eq⟧; the maps $\varphi_g$ of a natural representation are such maps ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.Φ_hyps⟧. The "change of variables" in the integrals is the invariance of the sheet integration under the local sc-diffeomorphism $\hat\varphi$, and gives Lemma 9.5.11 as a measure identity in §IX.31.

**Proposition 9.5.13** (V9.57), new in the 2021 edition. *(1)* For effective $X$, $T_x = \{1\}$, so $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x = \#G_x$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.card_effIsotropy_eq_of_isEffective⟧ and the normalizing factors of the two integrals agree. *(2)* The reduced ep-groupoid $X_R$ (Chapter 7) has the object M-polyfold of $X$, with Hausdorff and paracompact morphism space as instances (Hausdorff under LUC); functors ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.isFunctorial_reduced_iff⟧ and local branching structures ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.toReduced⟧ of $X$ and $X_R$ coincide, and $\#G^{\mathrm{eff}}_x = \#G^R_x = \#(G^R_x)^{\mathrm{eff}}$ ⟦Chapter9/MeasureEffective · EpGroupoid.card_effIsotropy_eq_reduced⟧. The identity of the integrals, $\oint_{\hat\Theta}\omega = \int_{\hat\Theta_R}\omega$, is §IX.33 (row V9.57 restated).

### IX.21 Appendix §9.6.1: Lemmas 9.6.1 and 9.6.2, Definition 9.6.3 and Lemma 9.6.4

**In place of "measure zero."** The text's proofs of Lemmas 9.6.1, 9.6.2 and 9.6.4 remove sets of smaller dimension or not containing a sheet near the point, "of measure zero", and move a point slightly. The formalization uses a topological covering lemma instead, with no Lebesgue measure and no Baire category. *Step 1.* If $A \cap W \subseteq N$ for an open $W \ni a$, then $\dim_aA \le \dim_aN$, by the inclusion of the chart tangent spaces ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · MPolyfold.HasDimAt.le_of_inter_subset⟧. *Step 2,* the covering lemma ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · MPolyfold.exists_mem_forall_notMem⟧: a nonempty open piece of a $k$-dimensional submanifold is not covered by finitely many submanifolds of smaller dimension closed in an open set, by induction on the family: removing one closed set of smaller dimension leaves a nonempty open piece, by Step 1. *Step 3,* "moving $z$ slightly": a point of the piece off all the given sets ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.IsGeneric⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.exists_isGeneric⟧.

**Lemma 9.6.1** (V9.58) ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_6_1⟧. *Two structures at $x$ have the same top dimension* ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.topDim⟧. If the first has top dimension $k$ and the second $\ell < k$, a generic point of a $k$-dimensional sheet of the first has $\Theta > 0$ by the first structure and $\Theta = 0$ by the second. So $\dim_\Theta(x)$ is well defined ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.localTopDim⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.localTopDim_eq⟧, $-\infty$ off the support ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.localTopDim_eq_bot⟧.

**Lemma 9.6.2** (V9.59) ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_6_2⟧. *The unions $M^k_U$ of the top-dimensional sheets agree on $U \cap U'$* ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.topUnion⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.mem_topUnion_iff_of_mem⟧: a generic point of $M^k_U \setminus M'^k_{U'}$ would have $\Theta > 0$ by the first structure and, off the lower-dimensional sheets of the second, $\Theta = 0$.

**Definition 9.6.3** (V9.60) ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.IsTopGoodPoint⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.IsTopBadPoint⟧, as in the text. At points top-good for both structures the top parts agree, with no hypothesis ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_topDim_eq_of_isTopGoodPoint⟧: near such a point the top part is $\sigma \cdot 1_M$ for both, and $\sigma$ is read off $\Theta$ at a generic point of $M$.

**Lemma 9.6.4** (V9.61). *Top-goodness does not depend on the structure.* **The text's proof**: near a top-good $z$, $\Theta = \sigma \cdot \delta_M + \Theta_0 + \cdots + \Theta_{k-1}$; a point of $M$ near $z$ off the lower-dimensional sets has $\Theta = \sigma$, and "similarly as good points", $z$ is top-good for the second structure. **As we read it, this needs that the top weight of the second structure at $y$ is $\sigma$**, an argument the text does not give: the second structure could a priori have, through $y$, several top-dimensional sheets with tangent spaces that differ. **The formalized proof** makes this step the hypothesis `TopMultiplicity` ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · MPolyfold.TopMultiplicity⟧: at a point where $\Theta$ equals $\sigma$ on generic points of a $k$-dimensional sheet, the top weight of any structure is $\sigma$. Under it the lemma holds ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_6_4⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.isTopBadPoint_iff⟧, the top parts agree on $U \cap U'$ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_topDim_eq_of_topMultiplicity⟧, and Proposition 9.1.12 follows by the descending induction of p. 454: subtract the top parts ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.subOn⟧ and repeat ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartsAgreeNear_of_topMultiplicity⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_of_topMultiplicity⟧. Witnesses: $k = 0$ on every M-polyfold ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · MPolyfold.topMultiplicity_zero⟧, and $k \ge n$ on $\mathbb R^n$, where an $n$-dimensional submanifold is a neighbourhood of each of its points ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · rnPolyfold_mem_nhds_of_hasDimAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · topMultiplicity_rn_of_le⟧; so Proposition 9.1.12 holds on $\mathbb R^0$ and $\mathbb R^1$ unconditionally ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · proposition_9_1_12_rn_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter9/Appendix · proposition_9_1_12_rn_one⟧. The step itself is proved from the graph representation in §IX.22 ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · MPolyfold.topMultiplicityAt_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.lemma_9_6_4_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧, and now on every M-polyfold ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · topMultiplicityAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · topMultiplicity⟧, so Lemma 9.6.4 holds for every ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · lemma_9_6_4_general⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · isTopBadPoint_iff_general⟧. In the proof the top-good point is called $z$ and then $y$.

### IX.22 Proposition 9.6.5, the formula on p. 457, and the proof of Proposition 9.1.12

**Proposition 9.6.5** (V9.62) ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.proposition_9_6_5⟧. *At a top-bad $x$, a class $\Xi$ of top-dimensional indices with one tangent space splits as $I^1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I^p$ with sequences of top-good points $x^e_j \to x$ lying on $M_i$ exactly for $i \in I^e$.* In (1) the text writes "$I_k = I^1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I^p$"; the $I^e$ being subsets of $\Xi$, it reads as $\Xi = I^1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup I^p$. **The slice form.** Under `HasGraphChartAt` at $x$, for every class and every neighbourhood $W$ of $x$ there is a finite top slice in $W$ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.IsTopSlice⟧: it meets each sheet of the class once, misses the other top-dimensional sheets and all lower-dimensional ones, using a generic slice (§IX.9). Top slices in every $W$ replace the top-good sequences.

**The formula on p. 457** ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_topDim_eq_sum_slices⟧. $\Theta_k(x) = \sum_\Xi \sum_{y \in \text{slice}} \Theta(y)$; for one class the slice gives $\sum_{i \in \Xi} \sigma_i$ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.sum_class_eq_sum_of_isTopSlice⟧. The text's $\Theta_k(x^k_e)$ uses points $x^k_e$ not introduced, presumably points $x^e_j$ of the sequences. **The independence of the right-hand side**, which the text asserts while $\Xi$, $I^e$ and $x^e$ come from the first structure, is an argument the text does not give. It is proved by choosing one slice for the sheets of both structures, off all lower-dimensional sets of both, so that both class weights are the same sum of values of $\Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.sum_class_eq_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPart_topDim_eq_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧. The same grouping proves `TopMultiplicityAt` ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · MPolyfold.TopMultiplicityAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · MPolyfold.topMultiplicity_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧, on $\mathbb R^m$ in all dimensions ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · MPolyfold.topMultiplicity_rn⟧. A per-dimension graph representation is not enough here: the lower-dimensional sheets through $y$ must be avoided in the chart in which the top sheets are graphs, which is why one chart for all dimensions was asked. One cone per tangent space in that chart suffices, since the slice for a class only uses the cone of that class; with this change the slices exist at every point of every M-polyfold ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · exists_slice_of_classGraphChart⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · exists_generic_slice_general⟧, and Proposition 9.6.5 and the formula on p. 457 hold for every ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · proposition_9_6_5_general⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · sum_class_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · dimPart_topDim_eq⟧.

**The proof of Proposition 9.1.12.** With the top parts agreeing near $x$, subtract them from both structures and repeat in lower dimensions ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartsAgreeNear_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_of_hasGraphChartAt⟧; on $\mathbb R^m$ without hypothesis ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.proposition_9_1_12_rn⟧, and on every ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · LocalBranchingStructure.dimPartsAgreeNear⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · proposition_9_1_12⟧. "This completes the proof of Proposition 9.6.5" (p. 457) refers to Proposition 9.1.12, Proposition 9.6.5 being stated without proof.
