### X.34 Theorem 10.3.10 (2017: 10.4) for strong bundles: the converse

**Isomorphisms of $\mathcal{SEP}(F^{-1})$ are generalized strong bundle isomorphisms** (V10.71) ⟦Chapter10/GapP2_F2_SBConverse · SBLocalization.SEPLoc.equivalences_Ψ_of_isIso⟧ ⟦Chapter10/GapP2_F2_SBConverse · SBLocalization.SEPLoc.isIso_homMk_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter10/GapP2_F2_SBConverse · SBLocalization.SEPLoc.isIso_iff_isGeneralizedIso⟧. Remark 10.5.3 says "a similar result can be proved" and builds it into Definition 10.5.2. Let $[E] = [W' \xleftarrow{\Phi'} V'' \xrightarrow{\Psi'} W]$ be the inverse of $[D]$. *Step 1, the base.* $\psi$ is an equivalence (§X.22). *Step 2, fibrewise injectivity from $[D] \circ [E] = 1$.* A strong bundle equivalence $H$ into the middle $W'' \times_{W'} V''$ makes $\Psi' \circ \Pi_{V''} \circ H$ naturally equivalent to a strong bundle equivalence ⟦Chapter10/GapP2_F2_SBConverse · SBLocalization.SDiagram.exists_natEquiv_of_equiv⟧. Since $\Pi_{V''}(m)$ is determined by $\Psi(\Pi_{W''}(m))$, $\Psi$ is injective on the fibres over the points $\Pi_{W''}(H(c))$, and on all fibres by transport along morphisms ⟦Chapter10/GapP2_F2_SBConverse · SEP.FibInj⟧ ⟦Chapter10/GapP2_F2_SBConverse · SBLocalization.SDiagram.fibInj_Ψ_of_equiv⟧. *Step 3, a natural equivalence from $[E] \circ [D] = 1$.* Likewise $\Psi \circ G$ is naturally equivalent to a strong bundle equivalence $K$ for $G = \Pi_{W''} \circ H$. *Step 4, local inverses.* For $x$ choose $\gamma : g(c) \to x$. The transport along $\gamma$ gives $G' = H_{\hat\gamma} \circ G$ (§X.32), and $\Psi \circ G'$ is the transport of $K$, a local strong bundle isomorphism near $c$. So $G' \circ (\Psi \circ G')^{-1}$ is a local right inverse of $\Psi$ near $\psi(x)$, at levels $[0]$ and $[1]$. With the fibrewise injectivity and the local injectivity of $\psi$, $\Psi$ is a strong bundle isomorphism near $x$ ⟦Chapter10/GapP2_F2_SBConverse · SEP.isStrongBundleIsoOn_of_rightInv⟧ ⟦Chapter10/GapP2_F2_SBConverse · SEP.exists_isStrongBundleIsoOn⟧, and on morphisms through the pull-back projections ⟦Chapter10/GapP2_F2_SBConverse · SEP.isLocalStrongBundleIso_mor_of_obj⟧. *Step 5, the total space and $|W[1]|$.* The total functor is full ⟦Chapter10/GapP2_F2_SBConverse · SEP.full_total⟧ and an equivalence by Lemma 10.1.2 ⟦Chapter10/GapP2_F2_SBConverse · SEP.isEquivalence_total⟧. $|\Psi|$ on $|W''[1]|$ is a continuous bijection with the continuous inverse $|G| \circ |K|^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter10/GapP2_F2_SBConverse · SEP.NatEquiv.oneOrbitMap_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter10/GapP2_F2_SBConverse · SEP.isHomeomorph_oneOrbitMap_of⟧. Together, the saturation step ⟦Chapter10/GapP2_F2_SBConverse · SEP.equivalences_of_natEquiv_comp⟧: a strong bundle functor covering an equivalence, injective on fibres, with $\Psi \circ G \simeq K$ for a strong bundle equivalence $K$, is a strong bundle equivalence. This replaces the claims (C1), (C2) of Appendix §10.6.2, which the text does not restate for strong bundles (G.123).

## Part XI. Geometry up to equivalences (HWZ Chapter 11, §§11.1–11.6 (2017 §§11.1–11.6))

Chapter 11 closes the ep-groupoid half of Part II; its numbers and pages are those of the book (Springer 2021, pp. 521–566), with the 2017 text's in parentheses (2017 pp. 375–416). It asks which of the notions built on ep-groupoids in Chapters 8 and 9 survive the passage to $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ of Chapter 10, where generalized isomorphisms are the isomorphisms. §11.1 extends the tangent functor (Theorem 11.1.1 (2017: 11.1)), shows that the degeneracy index is invariant (Proposition 11.1.2 (2017: 11.1)) and treats faces (Definition 11.1.3, Example 11.1.4, Remark 11.1.5, Proposition 11.1.6, Remark 11.1.7, Proposition 11.1.8 (2017: Definition 11.1, Example 11.1, Remark 11.1, Proposition 11.2, Remark 11.2, Proposition 11.3)). §11.2 does the same for sc-differential forms (Theorem 11.2.1 to Proposition 11.2.9 (2017: Theorem 11.2 to Proposition 11.5)). §11.3 pushes forward and pulls back functors $\Theta : X \to \mathbb Q^+$ (Definition 11.3.1, Lemma 11.3.2, Theorem 11.3.3 (2017: Definition 11.4, Lemma 11.5, Theorem 11.3)) and continues with the bundles of tangent sets and orientations (Lemma 11.3.4 to Theorem 11.3.9 (2017: Lemma 11.6 to Theorem 11.7)). §11.4 transforms the canonical measures (Theorems 11.4.1, 11.4.2, 11.4.4, 11.4.5, Remark 11.4.3 (2017: Theorems 11.8, 11.9, Remark 11.3)). §11.5 carries auxiliary norms and sc⁺-multisections along generalized strong bundle isomorphisms (Proposition 11.5.1, Lemma 11.5.2, Proposition 11.5.3 (2017: Proposition 11.6, Lemma 11.7, Proposition 11.7)). §11.6 studies proper covering functors up to equivalence (Lemmas 11.6.1–11.6.3, Definitions 11.6.4, 11.6.5, 11.6.7, Theorem 11.6.6, Proposition 11.6.8, Remark 11.6.9 (2017: Lemmas 11.8, 11.9, Definitions 11.6–11.8, Theorem 11.10, Proposition 11.8, Remark 11.4); Lemma 11.6.1 is new in the 2021 edition).

**What is proved, and what is not.** Since 2026-11-13 all eight gaps of Chapter 11 are closed (G.128–G.135). None is set aside as having nothing to formalize. *§11.1.* Theorem 11.1.1, Proposition 11.1.2, Definition 11.1.3, Example 11.1.4 (for $[0, \infty)^2 \oplus W$ with any $W$), Remark 11.1.5 (with the result it quotes), Remark 11.1.7 and Proposition 11.1.8 are proved (§§XI.1–XI.3). Proposition 11.1.6 is proved except for its intersection clause, which does not hold as we read it and holds in a union form (§§XI.3, XI.19, XI.20; G.128): the faces of a face structured tame ep-groupoid are tame ep-groupoids, and a generalized isomorphism induces generalized isomorphisms $[d]_F$ of faces. *§11.2.* All of it is proved: Theorem 11.2.1, Lemmas 11.2.2, 11.2.4–11.2.6, Definitions 11.2.3, 11.2.7, (11.5) and Propositions 11.2.8, 11.2.9 (§XI.4; G.129). *§11.3.* Proved: Definition 11.3.1, Lemma 11.3.2 in a stronger form, the push-forward and pull-back along generalized maps, and all six parts of Theorem 11.3.3, (6) for every dimensional decomposition (§§XI.5–XI.7). Also proved: Lemma 11.3.4 with (11.8) and (11.9), Theorem 11.3.5, Definition 11.3.6 with (11.10), and Theorems 11.3.7 and 11.3.8, whose proofs the text leaves to the reader (§XI.8). They were first proved under Chapter 9's hypothesis that the tangent sums of Theorem 9.2.1 are independent, which Chapter 9 now proves for every $\Theta$. Theorem 11.3.9 is proved for the intrinsic boundary orientation of Definition 9.3.10, independently of the representative and with no hypothesis (§XI.8; G.130). *§11.4.* Formalized (§XI.9; G.131). Theorems 11.4.1 and 11.4.2 and Remark 11.4.3 are proved, with no added hypothesis, for the canonical measures of Chapter 9 built from its concrete sheet integrals. Theorems 11.4.4 and 11.4.5 are proved with the text's hypotheses, for every $n \ge 1$, for the boundary measures of Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16. *§11.5.* Proposition 11.5.1 is proved with conditions (1) and (2) of Definition 8.3.5 (§XI.10; G.132), and Lemma 11.5.2 and Proposition 11.5.3 for sc⁺-multisections with their local section structures (§XI.11; G.133). *§11.6.* Proved: Lemmas 11.6.1–11.6.3, Definitions 11.6.4, 11.6.5, 11.6.7, all claims of Theorem 11.6.6 and Proposition 11.6.8 (§§XI.12–XI.15). Also proved: the localization $\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$ with $I$ (§XI.21; G.134), and the category of proper strong bundle coverings of Remark 11.6.9 with its localization (§XI.22; G.135), both sketched in the text with the details left to the reader. *The narrower row.* V11.6, Proposition 11.1.6: the clause that two faces meet in a face of each does not hold as we read it. The Lean counterexample is `FaceMeetExample.not_facesMeetInFaces`, two faces of $([0, \infty)^3 \oplus W) \setminus K$ meeting in two pieces of an edge. What is proved is that they meet in a union of faces of each (§XI.20). V11.29, Theorems 11.4.4 and 11.4.5, is restated since 2026-11-13: the class hypothesis `hcov` is derived in Chapter 9 and $n = 1$ is covered (§XI.9).

**Six structural choices.** (1) *Faces by their object sets.* A face $X_\theta$ of $X$ is the saturated set $\pi^{-1}(\theta)$ with the morphisms whose source lies in it; the faces of $|X|$ are Chapter 2's faces for the index $d_{|X|}$ on the open set $|X|$, so Chapter 2's lemmas on faces apply to them (§XI.2). (2) *Total push-forwards.* $F_*\Theta$ is defined for every sc-smooth functor and every map on objects, with one choice of $x$ and of a morphism $F(x) \to y$, and $0$ where there is none; the statements say when the choice does not matter (§XI.5). (3) *Classes through representatives.* $f_*$ and $f^*$ on $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ are computed on a chosen representative with an equivalence as left leg (`rep`), and shown independent of it (§XI.6). (4) *Multisections as functors.* A multisection functor on a strong bundle is a map on the total object space constant along the morphisms of the total ep-groupoid; the local section structures of Definition 13.2.1 are a predicate on top of it (§XI.11). (5) *Functors of proper coverings as pairs.* A functor $F \to F'$ is a structure with the two functors and the two commutation equations, on objects and on morphisms, and $\mathcal{PC}$ is a category with composition associative on the nose (§§XI.13, XI.15). (6) *Sections and boundary operations.* Section functors of $\widehat{Gr}$ are functions on all objects, $0$ off $X_\infty$; Chapter 9's boundary lift depends on a boundary operation given as data, so Theorem 11.3.9 is first proved for a representative under a hypothesis relating the boundary operations on the two sides, and then, for the intrinsic boundary orientation of Definition 9.3.10, with no hypothesis (§XI.8).

### XI.1 Theorem 11.1.1 (2017: 11.1): the tangent functor on $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$

**The tangent of a diagram** (V11.1) ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.Diagram.tangent⟧. For $d = [X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} Y]$ the diagram $Td = [TX \xleftarrow{TF} TA \xrightarrow{T\Phi} TY]$; $TF$ is an equivalence by Theorem 10.1.7. Chapter 8's functoriality of $T$ is used in the form $T(G \circ F) = TG \circ TF$ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EpFunctor.tangent_comp⟧ and $T1 = 1$ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EpFunctor.tangent_id⟧. *Step 1, refinements.* A refinement $H : d' \to d$ with natural transformations $\sigma : F' \to F \circ H$, $\tau : \Phi' \to \Phi \circ H$ gives $TH$ with $T\sigma$, $T\tau$ (Proposition 8.1.14), so $TH : Td' \to Td$ is a refinement ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.tangent⟧, and equivalent diagrams have equivalent tangents ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.tangent⟧; this is the argument of the text. *Step 2, identities.* $T$ of the identity diagram refines the identity diagram of $TX$ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_tangent_id⟧. *Step 3, composition, left to the reader.* For functors $P : C \to X$, $Q : C \to Z$ and a natural transformation $\Phi \circ P \to G \circ Q$, $c \mapsto (P(c), \tau(c), Q(c))$ is a functor into the weak fibred product ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.wfpLift⟧ with the right projections ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.projLeft_comp_wfpLift⟧ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.projRight_comp_wfpLift⟧. Applied to $T\pi_A$, $T\pi_B$ and $T$ of the transformation of $A \times_Y B$, it gives $T(A \times_Y B) \to TA \times_{TY} TB$; its composite with the projection to $TA$ is the equivalence $T\pi_A$, so it is an equivalence by two out of three, and it refines $Td \circ Te$ by $T(d \circ e)$ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.Diagram.isRefinement_tangent_comp⟧. *Step 4, the functor.* `tangentFunctor` on classes ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.EPLoc.tangentFunctor⟧ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.EPLoc.tangentFunctor_obj⟧ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.EPLoc.tangentFunctor_map_homMk⟧, compatible with the localization functor ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.EPLoc.tangentFunctor_map_localizationFunctor⟧; it maps generalized isomorphisms to generalized isomorphisms ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.EPLoc.isGeneralizedIso_tangent⟧. **Theorem 11.1.1** ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_11_1_1⟧ collects these.

### XI.2 Proposition 11.1.2 (2017: 11.1), Definition 11.1.3 (2017: 11.1) and Example 11.1.4 (2017: 11.1)

**Proposition 11.1.2 (2017: 11.1)** (V11.2) ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.EPLoc.proposition_11_1_2⟧. *Step 1, equivalences.* An equivalence is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, and a local sc-diffeomorphism preserves the degeneracy index, so $d_Y(F(x)) = d_X(x)$, and $d$ is constant on orbits ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.degIndexOrbit_orbitMap⟧ ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.degIndexOrbit⟧. *Step 2, diagrams.* For a diagram with both legs equivalences, $|d| = |\Phi| \circ |F|^{-1}$ preserves $d_{|\cdot|}$ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.Diagram.degIndexOrbit_orbitMap⟧. *Step 3, classes.* A generalized isomorphism has such a representative (Theorem 10.3.10; the proof says "Proposition 10.3.10", a possible misprint) ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometry · EPLocalization.EPLoc.degIndexOrbit_orbitMap⟧.

**Definition 11.1.3 (2017: 11.1)** (V11.3) ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.IsOrbitFace⟧ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.faceObj⟧ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.faceMor⟧ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.IsEpFace⟧ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.IsEpFaceStructured⟧ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.IsWeaklyFaceStructured⟧. The object set of $X_\theta$ is saturated ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.isSaturated_faceObj⟧ and its morphisms are those between its objects ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.faceMor_eq⟧. A face of $|X|$ is exactly a face, in Chapter 2's sense, of the open set $|X|$ for the index $d_{|X|}$ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.isOrbitFace_iff_isFaceIn⟧, so the faces through $z$ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.orbitFacesThrough⟧ are Chapter 2's ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.orbitFacesThrough_eq⟧ and face-structuredness is Chapter 2's condition for $|X|$ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.isEpFaceStructured_iff⟧. The number of faces through $z$ is counted in $\mathbb N \cup \{\infty\}$, so that infinitely many faces do not count as $0$.

**Example 11.1.4 (2017: 11.1)** (V11.4) ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.Examples.example_11_1_4⟧. *The trivial groupoid.* With only identities, $\pi$ is a homeomorphism ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.Examples.isHomeomorph_π_trivial⟧ and the face structure of $C = [0, \infty)^2 \oplus W$ is that of the quadrant ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.Examples.isFaceStructured_quadrant⟧. *The swap.* $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes C$ with $-1$ exchanging the two coordinates ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.Examples.swapEpGroupoid⟧; its object M-polyfold is $C$, face structured. In $|X|$ the set $\{d_{|X|} = 1\}$ is the image of one connected stratum, since the swap identifies the two open half-axes ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.Examples.setOf_degIndexOrbit_eq_one_swap⟧; $|X|$ has exactly one face ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.Examples.isOrbitFace_swap_iff⟧, and $|0|$, of index $2$, lies in one face only ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpGroupoid.Examples.not_isEpFaceStructured_swap⟧. The text gives no reason; this is it.

For the faces of Chapter 2 on open sets: such a homeomorphism maps faces to faces ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · TameBoundary.isFaceIn_univ_image⟧, every face is the image of one ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · TameBoundary.exists_isFaceIn_univ_preimage⟧, the orbit map of an equivalence is such a homeomorphism ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · TameBoundary.isDHomeoOn_univ⟧, and face-structuredness transfers ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · TameBoundary.isFaceStructuredOpen_univ_iff⟧. *Equivalences.* $|\Phi|$ induces the bijection of faces ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.bijOn_faces⟧, with $\Phi_*(X_\theta) = \mathrm{saturation}(\Phi(X_\theta)) = Y_{|\Phi|(\theta)}$ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpFunctor.saturation_image_faceObj⟧ and $\Phi^{-1}(Y_{\theta'}) = X_{|\Phi|^{-1}(\theta')}$ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EpFunctor.preimage_faceObj⟧. *Generalized isomorphisms.* $|[d]|$ is a homeomorphism ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EPLocalization.EPLoc.isHomeomorph_orbitMap⟧; `faceMap` and `faceComap` are the image and preimage of faces ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EPLocalization.EPLoc.faceMap⟧ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EPLocalization.EPLoc.faceComap⟧, computed on a representative as $\Psi_* \circ \Phi^*$ and $\Phi_* \circ \Psi^*$ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EPLocalization.EPLoc.faceMap_homMk⟧ ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EPLocalization.EPLoc.faceComap_homMk⟧, and mutually inverse bijections ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EPLocalization.EPLoc.bijOn_faceMap⟧. **Remark 11.1.5** ⟦Chapter11/EpEquivalenceGeometryFaces · EPLocalization.EPLoc.remark_11_1_5⟧.

### XI.4 §11.2: sc-differential forms (Theorem 11.2.1 to Proposition 11.2.9 (2017: Theorem 11.2 to Proposition 11.5))

Since 2026-11-12 §11.2 is formalized (G.129), for Chapter 8's forms $\Omega^k_{ep}$ of an ep-groupoid and their direct limit $\Omega^*_{ep,\infty}$ over the index lifts $X^i$. The pattern is that of §11.3: a push-forward along equivalences by a choice of $x$ and $\psi : F(x) \to y$ that does not matter, composition rules, invariance under refinements, and generalized maps through $F_* \circ G^*$. The formal route differs in one point: $F_*$ is defined as the inverse of $F^*$, and the text's defining formula becomes a theorem.

**Descent along a surjective local sc-diffeomorphism.** For M-polyfolds and a surjective local sc-diffeomorphism $q : X \to Y$, the tangent spaces of $Y$ are images ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_B2_FormDescent · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.exists_tangentFiber_lift⟧, so $q^*$ is injective on families of alternating forms ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_B2_FormDescent · MPolyfold.formPullback_injective_of_isLocalScDiffeo⟧. A family $\tau$ on $Y$ with $q^*\tau$ an sc-form is an sc-form: on the image $V$ of a sheet of $q$, with inverse $g$, $\tau|V = g^*(q^*\tau)$, the text's (11.4), and sc-smoothness of a form is local ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_B2_FormDescent · MPolyfold.isScForm_of_formPullback⟧. A family $\eta$ on $X$ taking the same values on vectors with the same image under $Tq$ descends, $\tau_y = \eta_x \circ (Tq(x))^{-1}$, with $q^*\tau = \eta$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_B2_FormDescent · MPolyfold.formDescend⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_B2_FormDescent · MPolyfold.formPullback_formDescend⟧.

**Lemma 11.2.2 and Definition 11.2.3 (2017: Lemma 11.1, Definition 11.2)** (V11.10). *Step 1, the full case.* For $F$ full and a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, a form of the ep-groupoid $X$ takes the same values on vectors over $x$, $x'$ with $F(x) = F(x')$ and the same images under $TF$, since a morphism $x \to x'$ exists and forms of ep-groupoids are invariant under morphisms; if $F$ is also surjective on objects, every form on $X$ descends to a form $\tau$ on $Y$ with $F^*\tau$ the given one ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_B2_EquivForms · EpFunctor.exists_epForms_formPullback_eq_of_surjective⟧. *Step 2, equivalences, through the weak fibred product.* For an equivalence $F$, $A = X \times_Y Y$ of $F$ and $1_Y$ has the objects $(x, \psi, y)$, $\psi : F(x) \to y$, of the text's definition; $\pi_Y : A \to Y$ is an equivalence surjective on objects and $F \circ \pi_X \simeq \pi_Y$. Pull-backs compose ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_B2_EquivForms · EpFunctor.formPullback_comp_functor⟧, and $F^*$ is injective ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_B2_EquivForms · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.injOn_formPullback⟧ and onto, $F_*\omega$ being the descent of $\pi_X^*\omega$ along $\pi_Y$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_B2_EquivForms · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.exists_formPullback_eq⟧. So $F^* : \Omega^k_{ep}(Y) \to \Omega^k_{ep}(X)$ is bijective ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_B2_EquivForms · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.bijective_formPullback⟧, and $F_*$ is its inverse ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_B2_EquivForms · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.formPush⟧. *Step 3, the text's formula.* $(F_*\omega)_y(T\psi(TF(x)l_1), \ldots, T\psi(TF(x)l_k)) = \omega_x(l_1, \ldots, l_k)$ for every $x$, $\psi : F(x) \to y$ and $l_j \in T_xX$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_B2_EquivForms · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.definition_11_2_3⟧, and every $h_1, \ldots, h_k \in T_yY$ is of this form ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_B2_EquivForms · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.exists_lift_tangent⟧, so the formula determines $F_*\omega$. *Step 4, Lemma 11.2.2* ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_B2_EquivForms · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.lemma_11_2_2⟧: both sides equal $(F_*\omega)_y(h_1, \ldots, h_k)$. Before Definition 11.2.3 the text's $\Omega(X)$ for the target is read $\Omega(Y)$.

### XI.9 §11.4: integration (Theorems 11.4.1, 11.4.2, 11.4.4, 11.4.5, Remark 11.4.3 (2017: Theorems 11.8, 11.9, Remark 11.3))

Since 2026-11-13 §11.4 is formalized (G.131). Theorems 11.4.1, 11.4.2 and Remark 11.4.3 hold with no added hypothesis. Theorems 11.4.4 and 11.4.5 were first proved under the class hypothesis of Chapter 9's boundary measures and for $n \ge 2$; they now hold with the text's hypotheses for every $n \ge 1$. The measures are Chapter 9's: the canonical measures of Theorems 9.5.4 and 9.5.5 built from the concrete sheet integrals ⟦Chapter9/GapP2_E1_BranchedIntegral · EpGroupoid.theorem_9_5_4⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GapP2_E1_BranchedIntegral · EpGroupoid.theorem_9_5_5⟧, and the boundary measures of Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16 on sheets covered by countably many graph charts ⟦Chapter9/GapP2_E7_BoundaryMeasure · EpGroupoid.theorem_9_5_15_msheets⟧ ⟦Chapter9/GapP2_E7_BoundaryMeasure · EpGroupoid.theorem_9_5_16_msheets⟧. "Oriented, tame" is read as in §XI.8, and the independence of the tangent sums holds for every $\Theta$.

**What the proof uses of the forms.** For an equivalence $\Phi$ the identity $\mu^{\Phi^*\hat\Theta'}_{\Phi^*\omega'} = |\Phi|^*\mu^{\hat\Theta'}_{\omega'}$ uses two facts about the pull-back of forms, recorded as a structure ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Compat · EpGroupoid.FormEval.IsPullback⟧: $(\Phi^*\omega')(\alpha_1, \ldots, \alpha_n) = \omega'(T\Phi\,\alpha_1, \ldots, T\Phi\,\alpha_n)$ on the tangent spaces of finite-dimensional submanifolds, and every form on $X$ is a pull-back (§XI.4). Both hold for $\Omega^n_{ep}$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4CompatInst · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.epFormEval_isPullback⟧ and for the direct limit $\Omega^n_{ep,\infty}$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4CompatInst · EP.epFormsInftyEval_isPullback⟧.

**Theorem 11.4.1 for an equivalence** (V11.27) ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Measure · EpFunctor.theorem_11_4_1_pull_equiv⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Measure · EpFunctor.theorem_11_4_1_push_equiv⟧. The text takes $U(x)$, $U(F(x))$ on which $F$ is an sc-diffeomorphism, both with the properness property and the natural actions, and moves the local branching structure by $F$. *Step 1, between two M-polyfolds.* An sc-diffeomorphism $f : U \to U'$ between open subsets of two M-polyfolds carries graph charts to graph charts in the transported chart ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4CrossChart · MPolyfold.GraphChart.mapDiffeoCross⟧, null sets to null sets ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4CrossChart · MPolyfold.IsHNull.image_of_isScDiffeoOn_cross⟧, and tame induced structures to tame induced structures ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4CrossChart · MPolyfold.HasTameInducedStructure.image_of_isScDiffeoOn⟧. *Step 2, moving structures.* An oriented tame structure is restricted to a smaller natural representation ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Move · EpGroupoid.OrientedTameStructure.restrictRep⟧ and moved, $(f(M_i \cap W), f_*o_i)$, $(\sigma_i)$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Move · EpGroupoid.OrientedTameStructure.move⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Move · EpGroupoid.OrientedTameStructure.represents_move⟧. *Step 3, (11.12) = (11.13).* When $\omega_T(Tf \circ \beta) = \omega_S(\beta)$ on the frames of a sheet ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Move · EpGroupoid.FormEval.EvCompatOn⟧, $\int_{f(A)} \omega_T|(f(N), f_*o) = \int_A \omega_S|(N, o)$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Move · EpGroupoid.FormEval.integ_image_cross⟧, and so the weighted sums of a structure and of its moved structure agree ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Move · EpGroupoid.OrientedTameStructure.sheetSum_move⟧; the same holds for sheets covered by several graph charts ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4MSheets · EpGroupoid.FormEval.image_mem_msheets_cross⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4MSheets · EpGroupoid.FormEval.msInteg_image_cross⟧. *Step 4, the transport chart.* For $Q = \hat\psi \circ \Phi$ (Chapter 10), $Q$ preserves $X_\infty$ and $\Phi^*\Theta'$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Pairs · EpFunctor.TransportChart.pullbackTheta_Q⟧, moves the orientations ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Pairs · EpFunctor.TransportChart.pullSection_Q⟧ and moves $\omega'$ to $\Phi^*\omega'$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Pairs · EpFunctor.TransportChart.evCompatOn_Q⟧. For small $U(x)$ there are natural representations on $U(x)$ and on $Q(U(x))$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Pairs · EpFunctor.TransportChart.exists_rep_push⟧. A structure at $y$ is restricted to $Q(U(x))$ and moved to $x$ by $Q^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Pairs · EpGroupoid.OrientedTameStructure.pullStructure⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Pairs · EpGroupoid.OrientedTameStructure.represents_pullStructure⟧, and one at $x$ is moved to $y$ by $Q$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Pairs · EpGroupoid.OrientedTameStructure.exists_push_structure⟧; this is the text's "$F^*\hat\Theta'$, $F_*\hat\Theta$ are oriented and tame" ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Measure · EpFunctor.hcov_pull⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Measure · EpFunctor.hcov_push⟧. *Step 5, the isotropy factor.* $\sharp G_x = \sharp G_y$ by the isomorphism $g \mapsto \psi \circ \Phi(g) \circ \psi^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter10/EquivalenceLR · EpFunctor.TransportChart.bijective_conj⟧. *Step 6, $\mathcal L$.* $|\Phi|$ and its inverse map sets of measure zero (Definition 9.5.1) to sets of measure zero ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Measure · EpFunctor.isMeasureZeroSupp_image⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Measure · EpFunctor.isMeasureZeroSupp_preimage⟧, so $|\Phi| : |\mathrm{supp}\,\Phi^*\Theta'| \to |\mathrm{supp}\,\Theta'|$ is an isomorphism of the $\sigma$-algebras $\mathcal L$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Measure · EpFunctor.measurable_suppMap⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Measure · EpFunctor.measurable_suppInv⟧. The text uses this without comment. *Step 7, gluing.* By Steps 3–5 the local formulas of Theorem 9.5.4 for $\mu^{\Phi^*\hat\Theta'}_{\Phi^*\omega'}$ and for $\mu^{\hat\Theta'}_{\omega'} \circ |\Phi|$ agree on the sets $|U(x)|$, and the measure with these local formulas is unique ⟦Chapter9/GapP2_E2MeasureGlue · existsUnique_linearMap_signedMeasure_of_openCover⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Measure · EpFunctor.measure_pull_core⟧. The push-forward identity is the same with $\Phi_*\omega$ any $\omega'$ with $\Phi^*\omega' = \omega$. The integrals follow with $K = |\mathrm{supp}|$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Measure · EpFunctor.integral_pull_equiv⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Measure · EpFunctor.integral_push_equiv⟧.

**Theorem 11.4.1 (2017: 11.8) and Remark 11.4.3 (2017: 11.3)** (V11.27, V11.28) ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Diagram · EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_11_4_1_pull⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Diagram · EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_11_4_1_push⟧. As in the text: for equivalences $F : A \to X$, $G : A \to Y$ and $\Theta_A = F^*\Theta_X = G^*\Theta_Y$, the equivalence case along $F$ and along $G$ gives $\mu^{\hat\Theta_X}_{\omega_X}(K) = \mu^{\hat\Theta_Y}_{\omega_Y}(|G|(|F|^{-1}(K)))$ when $F^*\omega_X = G^*\omega_Y$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Diagram · EpFunctor.measure_span_core⟧. With the forms of Definition 11.2.7 on the chosen representative this is the theorem for diagrams ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Diagram · EPLocalization.Diagram.theorem_11_4_1_pull⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4Diagram · EPLocalization.Diagram.theorem_11_4_1_push⟧ and for generalized isomorphisms. **Theorem 11.4.2 (new in 2021)** (V11.27) ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4EffDiagram · EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_11_4_2_pull⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H4EffDiagram · EPLocalization.EPLoc.theorem_11_4_2_push⟧. (2): the fibre condition ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalence · ProperCoveringHom.IsFiberBijective⟧ and equivalences ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalence · ProperCoveringHom.IsEquivalence⟧ ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalence · ProperCoveringHom.IsEquivalence.id⟧ ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalence · ProperCoveringHom.IsEquivalence.comp⟧. *The fibre condition is redundant* ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalence · ProperCoveringHom.isFiberBijective_of_isEquivalence⟧ ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalence · ProperCoveringHom.isEquivalence_iff⟧. *Injectivity.* If $\Psi(y_1) = \Psi(y_2)$ with $F(y_1) = F(y_2) = x$, fullness of $\Psi$ gives $\eta : y_1 \to y_2$ with $\Psi(\eta) = 1$; then $\Phi(F(\eta)) = F'(\Psi(\eta)) = 1 = \Phi(1_x)$ and faithfulness of $\Phi$ give $F(\eta) = 1_x$, so $\eta$ and $1_{y_1}$ lift the same $(1_x, y_1)$ and $y_2 = y_1$. *Surjectivity.* For $y' \in Y'_{\Phi(x)}$, essential surjectivity gives $y$ and $\eta' : \Psi(y) \to y'$; $F'(\eta') : \Phi(F(y)) \to \Phi(x)$ is $\Phi(\varphi)$ for some $\varphi : F(y) \to x$ by fullness; then $\Psi(\mathrm{lift}(\varphi, y))$ and $\eta'$ lift the same morphism with the same source, so $\Psi(B_\varphi(y)) = y'$. *Witness.* The functor from the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ to the point, between the identity coverings ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalence · CoveringEquivalence.Examples.pairToPointCovering⟧, is an equivalence ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalence · CoveringEquivalence.Examples.isEquivalence_pairToPointCovering⟧.

**The functor $H$** (V11.38) ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · ProperCoveringHom.hObj⟧ ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · ProperCoveringHom.hMor⟧ ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · ProperCoveringHom.hFunctor⟧. On morphisms (11.19), with sources and targets checked through the commutation equations ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · ProperCoveringHom.mor_conj⟧ ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · ProperCoveringHom.hMor_src⟧ ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · ProperCoveringHom.hMor_tgt⟧. Assume $\Psi$ and $\Phi$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms on objects and $\Psi$ maps each $Y_x$ onto $Y'_{\Phi(x)}$. *Step (A), objects.* Surjectivity: for $(x, \varphi', x'')$ lift $x''$ to $y''$, then $\varphi' : \Phi(x) \to \xi(x'')$ along $F'$ to $\psi'$ with target $\zeta(y'')$; the source of $\psi'$ lies over $\Phi(x)$, so it is $\Psi(y)$ for some $y \in Y_x$ by the hypothesis on fibres ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · ProperCoveringHom.surjective_hObj⟧. The local sc-diffeomorphism property: the projections $P \to Y''$ and $Q \to X''$ are local sc-diffeomorphisms on objects because $\Psi$ and $\Phi$ are, $F''$ is one, and $\pi_{X''} \circ H = F'' \circ \pi_{Y''}$, so $H$ is one by two out of three ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · ProperCoveringHom.isLocalScDiffeo_hObj⟧. The text's heading of (A) has $P$ and $Q$ in the reverse order (possible misprint). *Step (B), $\alpha$.* The map $\psi \mapsto (H(\psi), s(\psi))$ for $H$ is an sc-diffeomorphism onto the fibred product, its inverse built from those of $F$ and $F''$ ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · ProperCoveringHom.isScDiffeo_fibredMap_hFunctor⟧. *Step (C), finite fibres and properness.* A fibre of $H$ sits in the product of fibres of $F$ and $F''$ ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · ProperCoveringHom.finite_fiber_hObj⟧; a proper covering is proper on objects ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · EpFunctor.IsProperCovering.isProperMap⟧, and so is $H$ ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · ProperCoveringHom.isProperMap_hObj⟧; a proper local sc-diffeomorphism is evenly covered near a point with finite fibre, by disjoint sheets around the points of the fibre and the closedness of proper maps ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.evenlyCovered_of_isProperMap⟧, the sheets cut down to the neighbourhood found ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · MPolyfold.IsScDiffeoOn.restrictTarget⟧. The properness of $H$ is an ultrafilter argument from the properness of $F$ and $F''$ on objects and the continuity of the inverse of the map $\alpha$ of $F'$; it replaces the text's argument with sequences. **(1)** ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · ProperCoveringHom.isProperCovering_hFunctor_of⟧.

**Theorem 11.6.6** (V11.39) ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · ProperCoveringHom.theorem_11_6_6⟧. If $(\zeta, \xi)$ is an equivalence, the other projection ⟦Chapter11/CoveringEquivalenceTheorem · ProperCoveringHom.projLeftHom⟧ is one by symmetry. ### XI.16 Witnesses and the hypotheses

**Hypotheses taken.** *§XI.8.* Chapter 9's independence of the tangent sums of Theorem 9.2.1 was assumed for the branched ep⁺-subgroupoid being moved and proved for its images. Chapter 9 now proves it for every $\Theta$ ⟦Chapter9/GeneralCorollaries · EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums⟧, so it is no longer a restriction; it holds on $\mathbb R^n$ ⟦Chapter9/AppendixSlices · EpGroupoid.hasIndependentTangentSums_rn⟧. The boundary-transfer hypothesis of Theorem 11.3.9 for a representative holds along the identity, on every M-polyfold and on $\mathbb R^2$. Theorem 11.3.9 for the intrinsic boundary orientation needs no hypothesis. The boundary-lift form of Theorem 11.3.9 asks that $f$ carry tame tangent sets and that $f_*\hat\Theta$ be tame; both hold along the identity and for Example 9.3.5. *§XI.9.* The first forms of Theorems 11.4.4 and 11.4.5 carry the class hypothesis `hcov` of Chapter 9; it is derived from the text's hypotheses (§IX.36), and the forms with `hloc` take none beyond the text's. The local regularity property in Propositions 11.2.8, 11.2.9 and the local unique continuation property in Theorems 11.4.2, 11.4.5 are the text's. *Elsewhere.* The branched statements of §11.3 and the category $\mathcal{PC}$ take their ep-groupoids in one universe; the tangent functor on $\mathcal{EP}(E^{-1})$ lives where Chapter 8's $T$ does. In Remark 11.6.9 the class $E_{SBPC}$, which the text does not define, is read as "both components strong bundle equivalences" (§XI.22). Several statements need less than the text assumes: Lemma 11.3.2 (§XI.5), Proposition 11.1.6 (§XI.3), Theorem 11.6.6 (1) (§XI.14), and Proposition 11.2.8 with the property on one side (§XI.4).

**Every definition has a witness.** Faces and (weak) face structure: the quadrant with and without the swap (§XI.2). Push-forwards, pull-backs, branched ep⁺-subgroupoids along an equivalence that is not injective on objects and along a generalized isomorphism: $1_{\{0\}}$ on $\mathbb Z/2 \ltimes \mathbb R$ (§XI.7). Section functors and oriented branched ep⁺-subgroupoids: Example 9.3.5 on $\mathbb R^2$ (§XI.8). Auxiliary norms and multisection functors: the constant functions (§§XI.10, XI.11). Functors, equivalences and natural transformations of proper coverings, Theorem 11.6.6, diagrams and common refinements: the pair groupoid of $\mathbb Z$ over the point (§§XI.13–XI.15). Two faces meeting in more than one face: $([0, \infty)^3 \oplus W) \setminus K$ (§XI.20). The local regularity property in Propositions 11.2.8 and 11.2.9: the point and $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ (§XI.4). The class hypothesis of Theorems 11.4.4 and 11.4.5: compact boundary sheets and the closed upper hemisphere (§XI.9). sc⁺-multisections: the zero section (§XI.11). $\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$: $\mathrm{pair} \to \mathrm{point}$ (§XI.21). Proper strong bundle coverings and their weak fibred products: $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n$ (§XI.22).

### XI.17 What is not formalized

Since 2026-11-13 all eight gaps of Chapter 11 are closed.

- Closed in wave K: §11.4 (G.131, §XI.9). Theorems 11.4.1, 11.4.2 and Remark 11.4.3 are proved with no added hypothesis, and Theorems 11.4.4 and 11.4.5 with the text's hypotheses for every $n \ge 1$.
- Closed: §11.1, Proposition 11.1.6 with the second claim of Proposition 11.1.8 (G.128, §§XI.3, XI.19, XI.20; the intersection clause does not hold as we read it, and holds in a union form); §11.2 (G.129, §XI.4); §11.3, Theorem 11.3.9 for the intrinsic boundary orientation (G.130, §XI.8); §11.5, conditions (1) and (2) in Proposition 11.5.1 (G.132, §XI.10) and the local section structures of sc⁺-multisections (G.133, §XI.11); §11.6, $\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$ and $I$ (G.134, §XI.21) and the category of Remark 11.6.9 with its localization (G.135, §XI.22).
- Within closed items, the boundary-lift form of Theorem 11.3.9 keeps two hypotheses that the intrinsic form does not need: that sc-diffeomorphisms carry tame induced structures on submanifolds to tame induced structures, and that $f_*\hat\Theta$ is tame. The ordered face structures of Remark 11.1.5 have no formal content.

### XI.18 What the formalization taught us

Most of Chapter 11 is Chapter 10's machinery applied to one more kind of object, and the formal work went into the two places where an object is carried along an equivalence by a choice. For functors $\Theta$ the choice of $x$ and $F(x) \to y$ does not matter as soon as $F$ is full, which is all that the well-definedness in Lemma 11.3.2 uses; the statements for generalized maps then reduce, through one base change formula in the weak fibred product, to statements for equivalences, and the pull-back is defined for every generalized map. For branched ep⁺-subgroupoids the text's proof moves a local branching structure by $\hat\psi \circ F$; written out, the sheets must first be cut down to the domain of that local sc-diffeomorphism, and the paracompactness of the support, part of 2021 Definition 9.1.2, must be carried along too. Theorem 11.3.3 (6) refers to the uniqueness of dimensional decompositions, which does not hold as we read it (Chapter 9); the statement for every decomposition is what the proof gives. The rest of §11.3, whose proofs the text leaves to the reader, needed Chapter 9's notions between two M-polyfolds rather than on one, Chapter 9's independence hypothesis carried along, and, for Theorem 11.3.9, a condition on the boundary operations that Chapter 9 takes as data. Faces are a question about $|X|$ alone: once the faces of $|X|$ are Chapter 2's faces for $d_{|X|}$, Remark 11.1.5 and the bijections of Proposition 11.1.6 are statements about homeomorphisms preserving an index, and hold for every generalized isomorphism; only the ep-groupoid structure of a face needs more. In §11.6 the fibre condition of Definition 11.6.4 (2) comes for free for proper coverings, by unique lifting; and the chain of natural equivalences in Proposition 11.6.8 needs one more step than it displays.

The work of 2026-11-12 and 11-13 adds the following. Proposition 11.1.6 splits: its first and last claims hold, the faces being tame ep-groupoids because near each of its points $X_\theta$ is one face of the object M-polyfold, and the faces of a generalized isomorphism being related by the restricted diagram (11.1); but two faces can meet in several components, so the intersection is a union of faces of each, not one face. In §11.2 the forms behave best when $F_*$ is defined as the inverse of $F^*$: the bijectivity of $F^*$ is a descent along the projection $X \times_Y Y \to Y$, which is a surjective local sc-diffeomorphism, and the text's formula, composition rules, naturality and independence of the representative all follow by inverting statements about pull-backs. Theorem 11.3.9 needed no condition once the boundary orientation is taken intrinsically: Definition 9.3.8's operation is built from presented charts, which sc-diffeomorphisms transport, and "$d_M(x)$ is preserved" is read for the reduced codimension, which needs no tameness. §11.4 follows the text's proof, structures moved along transport charts and the sums (11.12), (11.13) compared, with two additions: $|f|$ preserves the $\sigma$-algebra $\mathcal L$, which the text uses silently, and in the effective case $\sharp G^{eff}$ is preserved because the transport isomorphism carries $T_x$ onto $T_y$. The boundary versions first inherited Chapter 9's class condition near corners; once Chapter 9 derived it, and covered $n = 1$, they hold with the text's hypotheses. In §11.5 conditions (1) and (2) need a local lift of a sequence through local inverses of $t$ and $\phi$, and the push-forward of local section structures needs the explicit domain on which the text's sections $s'_i$ are defined. In §11.6 the localizations of $\mathcal{PC}$ and of proper strong bundle coverings follow §10.3 once Theorem 11.6.6 is stated with the equivalence on the left; for strong bundles the weak fibred product is a pull-back, and conditions (2) and (3) of Definition 8.5.9 come for free over a proper covering.

### XI.19 Proposition 11.1.6 (2017: 11.2): faces as ep-groupoids, and Proposition 11.1.8 (2017: 11.3) for $[d]_F$

**Faces are tame ep-groupoids** (V11.6) ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · EpGroupoid.proposition_11_1_6_faces⟧. The text: for a face structured tame $X$, the object and morphism sets of a face $X_\theta$ are sub-M-polyfolds with tame induced structures, and $X_\theta$ is an ep-groupoid. The proof (pp. 524–525) passes through the faces of the object M-polyfold, and so does the formal one. *Step 1, local pieces.* $\pi$ maps the face of the object M-polyfold through $p$ into the face of $|X|$ through $|p|$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · EpGroupoid.image_faceAt_subset⟧. For the local pieces of $\{d_X = 1\}$ at $x$, the faces of $|X|$ through $|x|$ are those through the images of the pieces ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · EpGroupoid.orbitFacesThrough_eq_range⟧, and for face structured $X$ the map is injective ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · EpGroupoid.injective_orbitFaceAt_pt⟧. This is the text's count: if $x$ lay in fewer global faces of the object M-polyfold, fewer faces of $|X|$ would pass through $|x|$. So the object M-polyfold is weakly face structured ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · EpGroupoid.IsEpFaceStructured.isWeaklyFaceStructured⟧. *Step 2, one face near each point.* Every $x \in X_\theta$ lies in exactly one face of the object M-polyfold contained in $X_\theta$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · EpGroupoid.IsEpFaceStructured.existsUnique_face_subset⟧, and near $x$, $X_\theta$ is that face ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · EpGroupoid.IsEpFaceStructured.exists_nhds_eq_face⟧. The text's "disjoint union" is read in this local form, which is what is used. *Step 3, sub-M-polyfold.* A set that near each of its points agrees with a sub-M-polyfold is one ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · MPolyfold.isSubMPolyfold_of_forall_nhds⟧, and faces are sub-M-polyfolds with tame induced structure (Theorem 2.5.17); so $X_\theta$ is a closed ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · EpGroupoid.isClosed_faceObj⟧ saturated sub-M-polyfold ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · EpGroupoid.isSubMPolyfold_faceObj⟧. *Step 4, the ep-groupoid.* With the morphisms between its points it is an ep-subgroupoid ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · EpGroupoid.isEpSubgroupoid_faceObj⟧ (Proposition 7.1.22) ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · EpGroupoid.faceEpGroupoid⟧, tame on objects and on morphisms ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · EpGroupoid.isTame_faceEpGroupoid⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · EpGroupoid.isTame_faceEpGroupoid_mor⟧, with $d_X(x) = d_{X_\theta}(x) + 1$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaces · EpGroupoid.degIndex_faceEpGroupoid⟧.

**The generalized isomorphisms $[d]_F$ of (11.1)** ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EPLocalization.EPLoc.proposition_11_1_6_faceIso⟧. The text: for $X \xleftarrow{\Phi} A \xrightarrow{\Psi} Y$ and a face $F$ of $X$, $B = \Phi^{-1}(F)$ is a face of $A$, the saturation $C$ of $\Psi(B)$ is a face of $Y$, and $F \leftarrow B \to C$ is a generalized isomorphism by Theorem 10.3.10. *Step 1, restriction.* An sc-smooth functor restricts to ep-subgroupoids $A = G^{-1}(B)$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EpFunctor.restrictSub⟧, and so do natural transformations ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EpNatTrans.restrictSub⟧. For an equivalence and saturated $B$ the restriction is full, faithful, essentially surjective and a local sc-diffeomorphism, hence an equivalence by Lemma 10.1.2 ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.restrictSub⟧; this is the text's argument. Face structure passes both ways along equivalences ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isEpFaceStructured_iff⟧. *Step 2, the diagram (11.1).* The face as an object of $\mathcal{EP}$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EPLocalization.faceEP⟧ and the restricted diagram ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EPLocalization.Diagram.restrictFace⟧, with $C = Y_{|\Psi|(\theta_A)}$ (Remark 11.1.5). Refinements and equivalent diagrams restrict to refinements and equivalent diagrams ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EPLocalization.Diagram.IsRefinement.restrictFace⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.restrictFace⟧, and $|d_F|$ is the restriction of $|d|$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EPLocalization.Diagram.orbitMap_restrictFace⟧. *Step 3, the class.* $[d]_F$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EPLocalization.EPLoc.faceIso⟧ is the class of the restriction of every representative ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EPLocalization.EPLoc.homMk_restrictFace_eq_faceIso⟧. It is a generalized isomorphism ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EPLocalization.EPLoc.isGeneralizedIso_faceIso⟧ whose orbit map is the restriction of $|[d]|$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitMap_faceIso⟧. The target face is passed as a set with a proof that it is $f_*\theta$, so that $[f]_F$ and $[g]_F$ have the same type when $f_* = g_*$.

**Proposition 11.1.8, the second claim** (V11.8) ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HFaceIso · EPLocalization.EPLoc.proposition_11_1_8_faceIso⟧. If $|f| = |g|$, then $f_* = g_*$ (§XI.3), and the generalized isomorphisms $F \to f_*F$ and $F \to g_*F$ induce the same map $|F| \to |f_*F|$, both being restrictions of $|f| = |g|$.

### XI.20 Proposition 11.1.6 (2017: 11.2): the intersection clause

**The clause as printed does not hold as we read it** (V11.6) ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeet · EpGroupoid.FacesMeetInFaces⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeet · FaceMeetExample.not_facesMeetInFaces⟧. The text: if two faces $F$, $G$ meet, $F \cap G$ is a face in $F$ as well as in $G$. We read "face in $F$" in the ep-groupoid $X_\theta$ of §XI.19. *The example.* An open subset of a tame M-polyfold, with Part I's open-subset structure, has the same degeneracy index, is tame, and is face structured when the open set is ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeet · MPolyfold.isTame_restrictOpen⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeet · MPolyfold.isFaceStructuredOpen_restrictOpen⟧; its trivial ep-groupoid is then face structured ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeet · EpGroupoid.isEpFaceStructured_trivial_restrictOpen⟧. Take $V = ([0, \infty)^3 \oplus W) \setminus K$ with $K = \{p_0 + p_1 \le 1/4,\ 1 \le p_2 \le 2\}$, a closed block cutting the edge $p_0 = p_1 = 0$ at heights $[1, 2]$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeet · FaceMeetExample.V⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeet · FaceMeetExample.isEpFaceStructured_XV⟧. *Step 1.* $\theta_0 = \{p_0 = 0\}$ and $\theta_1 = \{p_1 = 0\}$ are distinct faces ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeet · FaceMeetExample.isOrbitFace_θ₀⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeet · FaceMeetExample.θ₀_ne_θ₁⟧, connected by paths in them ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeet · FaceMeetExample.mem_face_of_path⟧. *Step 2.* They meet in the two pieces $p_2 \in [0, 1)$ and $p_2 \in (2, \infty)$ of the edge. A face of $X_{\theta_0}$ is the closure of one connected component of its index-one set, and the continuous function $p_2$ takes values below $1$ or above $2$ on the edge ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeet · FaceMeetExample.cF_lt_or_gt⟧, so the intersection is not one face ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeet · FaceMeetExample.not_isEpFace_inter⟧. With $W = 0$ this is a 3-manifold with boundary and corners.

**The union form** ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeetUnion · EpGroupoid.IsEpFaceStructured.faceObj_inter_eq_sUnion⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeetUnion · EpGroupoid.IsEpFaceStructured.facesMeetInUnions⟧. For distinct faces $\theta \ne \theta'$ of $|X|$, $X_\theta \cap X_{\theta'}$ is the union of the faces of $X_\theta$ it contains, and likewise for $X_{\theta'}$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeetUnion · EpGroupoid.FacesMeetInUnionsOfFaces⟧. *Step 1, a ray in a tame chart.* A point $x$ of two distinct faces is a limit of points of $F_1 \cap F_2$ with $d_X = 2$: in a tame chart the faces are those of two distinct indices $i \ne j$ of Lemma 4.C, and the points $r(o + ty)$ with $\lambda_i(y) = \lambda_j(y) = 0$ and $\lambda_l(y) = 1$ otherwise have index $2$ and lie in both closures ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeetUnion · MPolyfold.mem_closure_inter_faces⟧. *Step 2.* Near a point $y \in X_{\theta'}$ with $d_X(y) = 2$, every point with $d_X = 2$ lies in $X_{\theta'}$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_H2FaceMeetUnion · EpGroupoid.IsEpFaceStructured.exists_nhds_degIndex_two⟧. *Step 3.* Those points lie in a local piece of $\{d_{X_\theta} = 1\}$ at $x$. The face of $X_\theta$ through that piece contains $x$, and it lies in $X_{\theta'}$ because $X_{\theta'} \cap \{d_{X_\theta} = 1\}$ is open and closed in $\{d_{X_\theta} = 1\}$.

### XI.21 The localization $\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$ and $I$ (2021 pp. 561–563)

**$\mathcal{PC}(E^{-1})$** (V11.43) ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PCLoc⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PCLoc.I⟧. The text sketches the localization of $\mathcal{PC}$ at $E_{PC}$ "as in the ep-groupoid case" and leaves the details to the reader. *Step 1, maps into weak fibred products.* For functors $L : P \to X$, $R : P \to Z$ and $\alpha : F \circ L \to G \circ R$, $p \mapsto (L(p), \alpha(p), R(p))$ is a functor into $X \times_Y Z$ with $\pi_X \circ \langle L, R \rangle = L$ and $\pi_Z \circ \langle L, R \rangle = R$ on the nose ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · WeakFibredProduct.pairFunctor⟧. Its version for proper coverings, with the square (11.20) for $\alpha$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PC.fibredLift⟧, is an equivalence by two out of three ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PC.IsEquivalence.of_comp_left⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PC.isEquivalence_fibredLift⟧, the projection to the side of the equivalence being one (Theorem 11.6.6 (2)). *Step 2, composition.* The composite of $d : F \leftarrow A \to F'$ and $d' : F' \leftarrow A' \to F''$ is taken through the weak fibred product $A' \times_{F'} A$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PC.Diagram.comp⟧. The text takes $A \times_{F'} A'$; Theorem 11.6.6 is stated here with the equivalence on the left, and the two products are isomorphic. Its class does not depend on the representatives ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PC.Diagram.hasCommonRefinement_comp⟧: a single equivalence $M$ with $\Gamma' \circ M \simeq \Gamma$ and $\varepsilon' \circ M \simeq \varepsilon$ gives a common refinement ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PC.Diagram.hasCommonRefinement_of_map⟧, and Step 1 gives such maps. Associativity and the units hold up to common refinement ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PC.Diagram.hasCommonRefinement_assoc⟧. *Step 3, $I$.* $I$ is the identity on objects with $I(\varepsilon) = [F \xleftarrow{1} F \xrightarrow{\varepsilon} F']$. Equivalences go to isomorphisms with inverse $[F' \xleftarrow{\Gamma} F \xrightarrow{1} F]$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PCLoc.isIso_I_map⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PCLoc.inv_I_map⟧, $[d] = I(\Gamma)^{-1} \circ I(\varepsilon)$ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PCLoc.homMk_eq⟧, and the inverse of $[F \xleftarrow{\Gamma} A \xrightarrow{\Gamma'} F']$ for an equivalence $\Gamma'$ is the reversed class ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PCLoc.isIso_homMk⟧ ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PCLoc.inv_homMk⟧ (G.134). *Witness.* $\mathrm{pair} \to \mathrm{point}$ is not an isomorphism of $\mathcal{PC}$, and its image under $I$ is one ⟦Chapter11/GapP2_HPCLocalization · PCLoc.Examples.not_isIso_pairToPoint_isIso_I_map⟧.

## Part XII. Sc-Fredholm sections on ep-groupoids (HWZ Chapter 12, §§12.1–12.5)

Chapter 12 opens Part III of the book (Springer 2021, pp. 569–597); its numbers are the 2021 ones, with the 2017 text's in parentheses. It carries the Fredholm package of Part I (Chapters 5 and 6) from strong bundles over M-polyfolds to strong bundles $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ over ep-groupoids. §12.1 defines sc-Fredholm section functors (Definition 12.1.1 (2017: 12.1)). §12.2 builds auxiliary norms (Definition 12.2.1, Theorem 12.2.2, Definitions 12.2.3, 12.2.4, Proposition 12.2.5, Theorems 12.2.6, 12.2.7 (2017: Definition 12.2, Theorem 12.1, Definitions 12.3, 12.4, Proposition 12.1, Theorems 12.2, 12.3)) and their reflexive variant (Definitions 12.2.8, 12.2.10, Remarks 12.2.9, 12.2.12, Theorems 12.2.11, 12.2.13 (2017: Definitions 12.5, 12.6, Remarks 12.1, 12.2, Theorems 12.4, 12.5)). §12.3 supplies sc⁺-section functors (Definition 12.3.1, Theorems 12.3.2, 12.3.3, Remarks 12.3.4, 12.3.5, Definition 12.3.6, Proposition 12.3.7, Corollary 12.3.8, Theorem 12.3.9 (2017: Definition 12.7, Theorems 12.6, 12.7, Remarks 12.3, 12.4, Definition 12.8, Proposition 12.2, Corollary 12.1, Theorem 12.8)). §12.4 treats compactness (Definition 12.4.1, Theorem 12.4.2, Definition 12.4.3, Lemma 12.4.4, Proposition 12.4.5, Theorem 12.4.6 (2017: Definition 12.9, Theorem 12.9, Definition 12.10, Lemma 12.1, Proposition 12.3, Theorem 12.10)), and §12.5 the orientation bundle $O_f$ (Lemma 12.5.1, Definition 12.5.2, Theorem 12.5.3, Definition 12.5.4, Remark 12.5.5, Proposition 12.5.6, Theorem 12.5.7 (2017: Lemma 12.2, Definition 12.11, Theorem 12.11, Definition 12.12, Remark 12.5, Proposition 12.4, Theorem 12.12)). This Part retells §12.1 (§XII.1), the auxiliary norms of §12.2 (§§XII.2–XII.5), §12.3 up to Corollary 12.3.8 (§§XII.6–XII.8), the first half of §12.4 (§XII.9) and §12.5 up to Proposition 12.5.6 (§§XII.10–XII.11); then the witnesses (§XII.12), what is not formalized (§XII.13) and what the formalization taught us (§XII.14), then, in waves 2–4, Theorem 12.2.7 as printed (§XII.15), the reflexive auxiliary norms (§§XII.16–XII.17), Theorem 12.3.9 (§XII.18), the rest of §12.4 (§XII.19), Theorem 12.5.7 without topology (§XII.20), the wave-2 witnesses (§XII.21), Theorem 12.2.13 as printed (§XII.22), the chart-level half of the last sentence of Theorem 12.5.3 (§XII.23) and the witnesses of waves 3 and 4 (§XII.24), then, in wave 5, the last sentence of Theorem 12.5.3 (§XII.25), Proposition 12.5.6 with continuity (§XII.26), the continuity in Theorem 12.5.7 (2) (§XII.27) and the witnesses of wave 5 (§XII.28).

**What is proved, and what is not.** Waves 1–5 of Part III (2026-11-13) formalize Chapter 12; what remains open is that the orbit map of orientations in Theorem 12.5.7 is a homeomorphism and independent of the representative, and §12.5's inheritance of Part I's hypotheses. *§12.1.* Definition 12.1.1 and the remark after it (regularizing on objects and on morphisms, sc-Fredholm germs) are formalized (§XII.1). *§12.2.* Definition 12.2.1, Theorem 12.2.2, Definitions 12.2.3, 12.2.4 with the remark between them, Proposition 12.2.5 and the good neighbourhood Theorem 12.2.6 are proved as printed (§§XII.2–XII.4). Theorem 12.2.7 is proved as printed: wave 1 proved its global part with the local step as a hypothesis (§XII.5), and wave 2 proves the local step, the extension of the norm near a boundary point by $N(rq(u), A(rq(u))w) + \|w - A(rq(u))w\|_{F_1}$, for every tame $X$ (§XII.15); gap G.136 is closed. The reflexive auxiliary norms: Definitions 12.2.8 and 12.2.10 are formalized, Remark 12.2.9 is proved in a stronger form (morphisms preserve mixed convergence), Theorem 12.2.11 is proved as printed with its three clauses, and Remark 12.2.12 as printed, its clause (3) in a stronger form (§XII.16). Theorem 12.2.13 is proved with the text's hypotheses and the paracompactness of $|X|$ that its proof takes from Theorem 12.2.11 made explicit: wave 2 proved its global part (§XII.17), and wave 3 proves the local step the text settles "by inspection", the lower semicontinuity of the local extension of §XII.15 under mixed convergence (§XII.22); gap G.147 is closed. *§12.3.* Definition 12.3.1 is formalized as printed and in a pointwise reading. Theorem 12.3.2 (1) is proved in each of the two consistent readings, and Theorem 12.3.2 (2) and Theorem 12.3.3 in the pointwise reading (§§XII.6–XII.7); the printed pairing of Definition 12.3.1 with Part I's pointwise bump functions would need Part I's open weak-to-pointwise question, which is recorded as a reading, not as formalization work. Remarks 12.3.4 and 12.3.5 are proved in explicit forms (§XII.7). Definition 12.3.6 is formalized in its local form, Proposition 12.3.7 in a stronger form and Corollary 12.3.8 explicitly (§XII.8); the ep-groupoid form of Definition 12.3.6 is formalized, and Theorem 12.3.9, the extension of sc⁺-section functors from $\partial X$ with the bound $N(\tilde s) \le \delta$, is proved as printed (§XII.18); gap G.137 is closed. *§12.4.* Definition 12.4.1, Theorem 12.4.2 and Lemma 12.4.4 are proved (§XII.9); Definition 12.4.3 is formalized, and Proposition 12.4.5 and Theorem 12.4.6 are proved in stronger forms, several of the text's hypotheses being unused (§XII.19). *§12.5.* Lemma 12.5.1 and the orientation action $\varphi_*$ are proved with Part I's standing hypothesis that sc⁺-sections pass through smooth fibre points (§XII.10). Definition 12.5.2 is $O_f$ of Part I, Definition 12.5.4 is formalized, and Theorem 12.5.3 is proved under Part I's hypotheses (§XII.11), its last sentence in wave 5: the local isomorphism of a morphism carries a continuous local orientation section near $x$ to one near $x'$, with value $\sigma_*o_x$ at $x'$ (§XII.25, with the chart-level half of wave 3 in §XII.23); gap G.138 is closed. Proposition 12.5.6 is proved in both directions, the direction (⇐) with the continuity of the orientation for Part I's topology in wave 5 (§§XII.11, XII.26); gap G.139 is closed. Remark 12.5.5 is prose. Theorem 12.5.7 is proved for one representative of the generalized strong bundle isomorphism: a bijection $|O_f| \to |O_{f'}|$ over the bijection $|X_\infty| \to |X'_\infty|$, compatible with the diagram, and a unique invariant push-forward of an invariant orientation (§XII.20), which in wave 5 is continuous when the given orientation is, continuity read as Part I's continuity of orientations over all of $X$ (§XII.27). That the bijection is a homeomorphism, that the two readings of continuity agree, and that the maps are independent of the representative and functorial, is gap G.158, formalized in part. *Open:* G.140 (Part I's hypotheses carried by §12.5) and G.158 (in part). No statement of Chapter 12 was found not to hold as we read it.

**Four structural choices.** (1) *Part I on the object M-polyfold.* An sc-Fredholm section functor is an sc-smooth section functor that is a Part I sc-Fredholm section of $W \to X$; an auxiliary norm is a Part I auxiliary norm invariant under $\mu$ (Definition 8.3.5). So every Part I theorem applies to the objects, and Chapter 12's work is the passage through the morphisms. (2) *Norms are built from Part I norms.* The local norms that the text takes from a chart are Part I auxiliary norms (Proposition 5.1.3), and completeness of a glued fibre norm is not checked by hand: a new Part I lemma shows that a continuous fibrewise seminorm with condition (2) is an auxiliary norm (§XII.2). (3) *Bump functions in two readings.* Definition 12.3.1 asks for "not identically $0$"; Part I's Definition 5.3.1 is read pointwise in this project (Part V). Both readings are kept for ep-groupoids (§XII.6). (4) *Orientations in chart points.* $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ and $\mathrm{Or}^f_x$ are Part I's, read in a chosen chart point; a morphism $\varphi$ acts through a local strong bundle isomorphism built from the sheet of $\varphi$ (§XII.10).
