### XII.1 Definition 12.1.1 (2017: 12.1) and the remark after it

**Definition 12.1.1** ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.definition_12_1_1⟧ is the project's definition unfolded: an sc-smooth section functor is sc-Fredholm when it is an sc-Fredholm section of the object bundle. **The remark after it, p. 569.** *On objects:* $x \in X_m$ and $f(x) \in W_{m,m+1}$ give $x \in X_{m+1}$, which is Part I's regularizing property ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_1_1_regularizing_obj⟧. *On morphisms:* the text writes $f(\varphi)$ for a morphism; this is read as the section $\varphi \mapsto (\varphi, f(s(\varphi)))$ of the pull-back bundle $\mathbf X\,{}_s\!\times_P W \to \mathbf X$. If $\varphi \in \mathbf X_m$ and $f(\varphi)$ lies on level $(m, m+1)$, the projection to $W$, a strong bundle map, puts $f(s(\varphi))$ on level $(m, m+1)$, so $s(\varphi) \in X_{m+1}$, and $\varphi \in \mathbf X_{m+1}$ because levels of morphisms are those of their sources ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_1_1_regularizing_mor⟧. *Germs:* at a smooth $x$ the germ of $f$ is an sc-Fredholm germ ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_1_1_germ⟧.

### XII.2 Definition 12.2.1 (2017: 12.2) and Theorem 12.2.2 (2017: 12.1): auxiliary norms exist

**Definition 12.2.1** recalls Definition 8.3.5 and is not restated: an auxiliary norm is a Part I auxiliary norm $N : W_{0,1} \to [0, \infty)$ (continuous, a complete norm on each fibre, and $P(h_k) \to x$, $N(h_k) \to 0$ imply $h_k \to 0_x$) with $N(\mu(\varphi, k)) = N(k)$ ⟦Chapter8/Book2021 · EpStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm⟧.

**Completeness is automatic** (extra, Part I) ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · StrongBundle.isAuxNorm_of_tendsto⟧. The text says that the glued norms are complete on the fibres; the formal proof replaces this by a lemma about Part I's Definition 5.1.1. Let $N$ be continuous, a seminorm on each fibre ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · StrongBundle.IsFiberSeminorm⟧, with condition (2) ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · StrongBundle.TendstoZeroOne⟧. *Step 1, upper bound.* Near a point, in a strong bundle chart, continuity gives $N(w) \le c\,|w|_1$, where $|\cdot|_1$ is the chart norm of $\Phi[1]$. *Step 2, lower bound.* If no $c > 0$ had $|w|_1 \le c\,N(w)$ nearby, there would be $w_k$ over points converging to $x$ with $|w_k|_1 = 1$ and $N(w_k) \to 0$; condition (2) then gives $w_k \to 0_x$, against $|w_k|_1 = 1$ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · StrongBundle.exists_norm_liftOne_le_of_tendsto⟧. *Step 3.* A seminorm squeezed between two multiples of a complete norm is a complete norm. A *local auxiliary norm* on $U$ asks for continuity, the seminorm property and condition (2) over $U$ only ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · StrongBundle.IsLocalAuxNorm⟧.

**Theorem 12.2.2** ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_2⟧: every strong bundle over an ep-groupoid with paracompact orbit space admits an auxiliary norm; also for a bundled object of $\mathcal{SEP}$ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · SEP.theorem_12_2_2⟧. The proof follows the text's three steps. *Step 0, the lifted action.* For a choice $\alpha$ of morphisms with $s(\alpha(y)) = y$, $w \mapsto \mu(\alpha(P(w)), w)$ is a map of $W_{0,1}$ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.actOne⟧, and along a natural representation it is a group action of $G_x$ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.actOne_Γ_mul⟧. *Step 1, average.* For a local norm $M$ on $U(x)$, $\bar M(w) = |G_x|^{-1}\sum_{g \in G_x}M(g * w)$ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.avgNorm⟧ is $G_x$-invariant ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.avgNorm_actOne⟧ and again a local norm ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.isLocalAuxNorm_avgNorm⟧. *Step 2, transport.* The saturation of $U(x)$ is the set of $y$ with a morphism into $U(x)$ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.satSet⟧; choose one, $\varphi_y$ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.selMor⟧, and put $T(w) = \bar M(\mu(\varphi_{P(w)}, w))$, and $0$ off the saturation ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.transNorm⟧. Two choices differ by an element of $G_x$ acting through the natural representation, because a morphism between points of $U(x)$ is $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$ for a unique $g$; so $T$ does not depend on the choice, by the invariance of $\bar M$ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.transNorm_eq_of⟧. The text uses Theorem 12.2.6 (5) at this point; the invariance makes it unnecessary. $T$ is a local norm on the saturation ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.isLocalAuxNorm_transNorm⟧ and invariant under every morphism ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.transNorm_μ⟧. *Step 3, glue.* For a partition of unity $(\beta_i)$ of $|X|$ subordinate to the images $\pi(\text{saturation of } U(x_i))$, $N(w) = \sum_i\beta_i(\pi(P(w)))\,T_i(w)$ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.glueNorm⟧ is continuous, a fibrewise seminorm, satisfies (2), and is invariant; so it is an auxiliary norm by the lemma above ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.isAuxNorm_glueNorm⟧. The local norms are the restrictions of one Part I norm ⟦Chapter5/AuxNorm · proposition_5_1_3_exists⟧, the natural representations come from Theorem 7.1.13 on all of $X$, and $|X|$ is metrizable, hence admits the partition of unity, by Theorem 7.3.1 ⟦Chapter7/OrbitTopology · theorem_7_3_1_metrizable⟧.

### XII.3 Definitions 12.2.3, 12.2.4 (2017: 12.3, 12.4) and Proposition 12.2.5 (2017: 12.1)

**Definition 12.2.3** ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.IsContPartitionOfUnity⟧: continuous $\beta_\lambda : X \to [0, 1]$, constant along morphisms, locally finite through saturated open neighbourhoods, with $\sum_\lambda\beta_\lambda = 1$. Supports are closures in $X$. The paracompactness of $|X|$ in the text's preamble is not a field, since the definition does not use it. **The remark after it.** A partition of unity of $|X|$ composed with $\pi$ is one of $X$ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.isContPartitionOfUnity_comp_π⟧; conversely one of $X$ descends to $|X|$ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.IsContPartitionOfUnity.descend⟧. In the second direction the functions descend by (1), and local finiteness on $|X|$ uses that $\pi$ is open (Proposition 7.1.8). **Definition 12.2.4** ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.IsContPartitionOfUnity.IsSubordinate⟧: $\operatorname{supp}\beta_\lambda \subset U_\lambda$. **Proposition 12.2.5** ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.proposition_12_2_5⟧: for paracompact $|X|$, every cover of $X$ by saturated open sets has a subordinate continuous partition of unity. The proof is the text's: the sets $\pi(U_\lambda)$ are open and cover $|X|$, which is normal by Theorem 7.3.1; a partition of unity of $|X|$ subordinate to them, composed with $\pi$, is subordinate to $(U_\lambda)$ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormEp · EpGroupoid.isSubordinate_comp_π⟧.

### XII.4 Theorem 12.2.6 (2017: 12.2): good neighbourhoods

**Theorem 12.2.6** ⟦Chapter12/P3N_GoodNeighborhood · EpGroupoid.theorem_12_2_6⟧. Every object $x$ has open neighbourhoods $U'(x) \subset U''(x)$ with (1) $\overline{U'} \subset U''$; (2) $U''$ is the domain of a natural representation of $G_x$, which leaves $U'$ invariant; (3) $U''$ lies in the base of one strong bundle chart, which restricted to $P^{-1}(U'')$ is the isomorphism with a local model; (4) a sequence of morphisms with sources in $\overline{U''}$ and convergent targets $t(\varphi_k) \to z$ has a subsequence converging to a $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) \in \overline{U''}$, $t(\varphi) = z$; (5) $(\pi^{-1}(\pi(U')) \setminus U') \cap \overline{U''} = \emptyset$. *Step 1.* A neighbourhood $V_0$ of $x$ on which $t$ is proper on $s^{-1}(\overline{V_0})$, inside a chart domain. *Step 2.* A natural representation in $V_0$ (Theorem 7.1.13), shrunk twice ⟦Chapter7/NaturalRep · exists_naturalRep_shrink⟧, to $U''$ and to $U'$ with $\overline{U'} \subset U''$; the image of an invariant set under the representation is computed once ⟦Chapter12/P3N_GoodNeighborhood · EpGroupoid.NaturalRep.image_Φ_eq⟧. *Step 3, (4).* Properness of $t$ gives the subsequence ⟦Chapter12/P3N_GoodNeighborhood · EpGroupoid.exists_subseq_of_isProperMap⟧. *Step 4, (5).* A point $y \in \overline{U''}$ with a morphism to a point of $U'$ is moved into $U'$ by a unique group element, by the uniqueness clause of Theorem 7.1.13, so $y \in U'$. No hypothesis is added.

### XII.5 Theorem 12.2.7 (2017: 12.3): extension of auxiliary norms from the boundary

**Auxiliary norms over a subset.** For $A \subset X$, Definition 12.2.1 over $A$ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.IsAuxNormOn⟧: continuity on $W_{0,1}|A$, a complete norm on the fibres over $A$, condition (2) for sequences converging to points of $A$, and invariance where $P(k) \in A$. The text's $N$ is defined on $W_{0,1}|\partial X$; here it is a function on $W_{0,1}$ with conditions over $\partial X$ only, which is the same thing. A global norm restricts ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.isAuxNormOn⟧.

**The added hypothesis** ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.HasLocalExtensions⟧: every $x \in \partial X$ has an open $V \ni x$ and a local auxiliary norm $M$ on $V$ equal to $N$ on $W_{0,1}|(V \cap \partial X)$. It is not derived from the text; it is the text's local step, the norm $N(rq(u), A(rq(u))w) + \|w - A(rq(u))w\|_{F_1}$ in a tame local model. Its satisfiability witness is `theorem_12_2_7_hyp_witness`: over every ep-groupoid with paracompact $|X|$ there is an $N$ with both properties, the restriction of a norm of Theorem 12.2.2 ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_7_hyp_witness⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.hasLocalExtensions_of_isAuxNorm⟧.

**Theorem 12.2.7** (narrower) ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_7_hyp⟧: for paracompact $|X|$, an auxiliary norm $N$ over $\partial X$ with local extensions extends to an auxiliary norm $\tilde N$ of $W$ with $\tilde N = N$ over $\partial X$. *Step 1, data at each point.* At $x \in \partial X$: the local extension $M$, and a natural representation inside its $V$. At $x \notin \partial X$: a natural representation inside the open set $X \setminus \partial X$ ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormExtension · EpGroupoid.isOpen_compl_boundary⟧ carrying a Part I norm, restricted ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormExtension · StrongBundle.IsLocalAuxNorm.mono⟧. *Step 2, average and transport,* as in §XII.2. Over $\partial X$ the average of $M$ is still $N$, because $N$ is invariant and $\partial X$ is preserved by the morphisms ⟦Chapter12/P3N_AuxNormExtension · EpGroupoid.tgt_mem_boundary_iff⟧. *Step 3, glue.* Over a boundary point every nonzero term of $\sum_i\beta_iT_i$ is $\beta_i N$: the saturation of an interior neighbourhood misses $\partial X$, and the terms from boundary points are $N$ there. So the sum is $N$ over $\partial X$. Tameness of $X$, which the text assumes, is not used in the global part; it would serve only to discharge the hypothesis.

### XII.6 Definition 12.3.1 (2017: 12.7) and Theorem 12.3.2 (2017: 12.6): bump functions

**Definition 12.3.1, as printed** ⟦Chapter12/P3S_BumpEp · EpGroupoid.AdmitsBumpFunctions⟧: for every $x$ and saturated open $U \ni x$, an sc-smooth $f : X \to \mathbb R$, not identically $0$, with $\operatorname{supp}f \subset U$ and $f(s(\varphi)) = f(t(\varphi))$. **The pointwise reading** ⟦Chapter12/P3S_BumpEp · EpGroupoid.AdmitsBumpFunctionsPointwise⟧ asks $f(x) \ne 0$, as the project reads Part I's Definition 5.3.1; it implies the printed form ⟦Chapter12/P3S_BumpEp · EpGroupoid.AdmitsBumpFunctionsPointwise.weak⟧.

**Theorem 12.3.2 (1)**, $X$ admits sc-smooth bump functions iff the object M-polyfold does, is proved in each consistent reading: pointwise on both sides ⟦Chapter12/P3S_BumpEp · EpGroupoid.theorem_12_3_2_1⟧ and "not identically $0$" on both sides ⟦Chapter12/P3S_BumpEp · EpGroupoid.theorem_12_3_2_1_weak⟧. The printed form pairs Definition 12.3.1 with Part I's pointwise bump functions; its direction (⇒) would then be Part I's weak-to-pointwise question (Part V, §V.31), which is open. *(⇒).* Given an ep bump function $f$ near $x$, take an invariant $V(x)$ with the natural action inside $U$ and cut off: $\mathbf 1_V f$ is sc-smooth on the objects ⟦Chapter12/P3S_BumpEp · EpGroupoid.exists_objBump_of_epBump⟧. *(⇐).* Given a bump function $g$ of the object M-polyfold supported in an invariant $V$ with $\overline V$ in the domain of a natural representation, average over $G_x$ ⟦Chapter12/P3S_BumpEp · EpGroupoid.exists_natAverage⟧ and extend to the saturation by the morphisms ⟦Chapter12/P3S_BumpEp · EpGroupoid.exists_invariant_extension⟧; the extension is sc-smooth because the saturation of the proper closed set $\overline V$ is closed ⟦Chapter7/ProperSubsets · isClosed_saturation_of_isProperSubset⟧. The text averages $f$ itself, and that average can cancel to $0$; the formal proof averages $g^2$, presumably what is intended, since the bump functions of Proposition 5.5.3 are nonnegative ⟦Chapter12/P3S_BumpEp · EpGroupoid.exists_epBump_of_objBump⟧.

**Theorem 12.3.2 (2)** (narrower) ⟦Chapter12/P3S_BumpEp · EpGroupoid.theorem_12_3_2_2⟧: from pointwise ep bump functions, for every $x$ and saturated open $U \ni x$ an invariant sc-smooth $f : X \to [0, 1]$ with $f(x) = 1$ and $\operatorname{supp}f \subset U$. The proof is the text's: a function $\equiv 1$ near $x$ from Proposition 5.5.3 ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · proposition_5_5_3⟧, averaged and extended; $f(x) = 1$ because every $\Phi(g)$ fixes $x$. The hypothesis is the pointwise reading of Definition 12.3.1. Witness: the trivial ep-groupoid on $\mathbb R^n$ ⟦Chapter12/P3S_BumpEp · EpGroupoid.admitsBumpFunctionsPointwise_trivial_rn⟧, and every ep-groupoid whose object M-polyfold admits bump functions ⟦Chapter12/P3S_BumpEp · EpGroupoid.admitsBumpFunctionsPointwise_of_objects⟧.

### XII.7 Theorem 12.3.3 (2017: 12.7), Remarks 12.3.4 and 12.3.5 (2017: 12.3, 12.4)

**Morphisms acting on sections.** For a section $\sigma$ and a morphism $\varphi$, $\mu(\varphi, \sigma(s(\varphi)))$ ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · EpStrongBundle.secAct⟧, compatible with composition ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · EpStrongBundle.secAct_comp⟧. If $\tau$ is a local sc-smooth choice of morphisms, $y \mapsto \mu(\tau(y), \sigma(s(\tau(y))))$ is sc-smooth into $W[1]$ where $\tau$ is ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · EpStrongBundle.exists_isScSmoothOn_one_secAct⟧, and sc⁺ is a local property ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · StrongBundle.isScPlusSection_of_locally⟧.

**Remark 12.3.5** (explicit) ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_3_5⟧. Let $U(x)$ carry a natural representation, $\overline V \subset U(x)$ with $\overline V$ proper, and $\sigma$ an sc⁺-section supported in $\overline V$ and equivariant under the morphisms of $U(x)$. Then the natural extension ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · EpStrongBundle.natExtension⟧ is an sc⁺-section functor ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · EpStrongBundle.natExtension_isFunctorial⟧, equal to $\sigma$ on $U(x)$, supported in the saturation of $\operatorname{supp}\sigma$, and every bound $N(\sigma) \le b$ for an auxiliary norm carries over ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · EpStrongBundle.NormBound⟧. *Proof.* At a point of the saturation, take a sheet $\tau$ of $t$ through a morphism into $U(x)$ and put $\mu(\tau(y), \sigma(s(\tau(y))))$; equivariance makes this independent of the sheet, and it is sc⁺ there. Off the saturation of $\operatorname{supp}\sigma$ it is $0$ ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · EpStrongBundle.natExtension_eq_zero⟧. The bound holds because $N$ is $\mu$-invariant ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · EpStrongBundle.IsAuxNorm.secAct_eq⟧. The text's $f \cdot s$ is $\sigma$, already cut off, and "controlled" is the bound $b$.

**Theorem 12.3.3** (narrower) ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_3_3⟧. Hypotheses: pointwise ep bump functions; paracompact $|X|$; an auxiliary norm $N$; a smooth $x$; a smooth $e \in W_x$ with $\mu(g, e) = e$ for $g \in G_x$; an open $\hat O \ni |x|$; $\varepsilon > 0$. Conclusion: an sc⁺-section functor $\sigma$ with $\operatorname{supp}\sigma \subset \pi^{-1}(\hat O)$, $\sigma(x) = e$ and $N(\sigma(y)) \le N(e) + \varepsilon$. *Step 1.* An invariant neighbourhood with the natural action, inside $\pi^{-1}(\hat O)$ and with proper closure. *Step 2, a local section through $e$.* Part I's Lemma 5.3.3 ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · lemma_5_3_3⟧ gives an sc⁺-section through $e$, supported in that neighbourhood, with $N \le N(e) + \varepsilon$; it replaces the text's constant section in a chart times a cut-off $\beta$, so no separate cut-off is needed. *Step 3, average.* $\sigma'' = |G_x|^{-1}\sum_kh_k$ with $h_k(y) = \mu(\Gamma(k, \Phi(k^{-1})y), s(\Phi(k^{-1})y))$ ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · EpStrongBundle.natTerm⟧ is equivariant, keeps the value $e$ at $x$ because $e$ is $G_x$-fixed, and keeps the bound ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · EpStrongBundle.exists_equivariant_average⟧. *Step 4.* Remark 12.3.5 extends it. Paracompactness is kept from the text and not used: the text needs it only for the existence of $N$, which is here a hypothesis.

**Remark 12.3.4** (explicit) ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_3_4⟧: for a functorial section $\sigma$ and $g \in G_x$, $\mu(g, \sigma(x)) = \sigma(x)$; so the invariance of $e$ in Theorem 12.3.3 cannot be dropped. The rest of the remark is commentary.

### XII.8 Definition 12.3.6 (2017: 12.8), Proposition 12.3.7 (2017: 12.2), Corollary 12.3.8 (2017: 12.1)

**Definition 12.3.6, local form.** In a tame local strong bundle model $K = R(U \triangleleft F) \to O$ with a tame presentation $T$, $\partial O$ is the set of $z \in O$ with $d_C(z) \ne 0$ ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · retractBoundary⟧, equivalently with nonempty index set $I(z)$ ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · mem_retractBoundary_iff⟧. A section over $D \subset \partial O$ is an sc⁺-section over the boundary when, for $x \in D$ and $i \in I(x)$, its restriction to the face germ $O \cap V \cap \{t_i = 0\}$ is sc⁺ for some open $V \ni x$ ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · IsScPlusOnFaceNear⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · IsBoundaryScPlusSectionOn⟧. Witness of the quantifier over charts and presentations: the zero section ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · isBoundaryScPlusSectionOn_zero⟧. The M-polyfold form is Definition 5.4.1 (Part V, §V.54); the ep-groupoid wrapper is not stated.

**The extension by inclusion–exclusion.** For $z$ near $x_0$ and $\emptyset \ne I \subseteq \sigma = I(x_0)$, $z_I$ is $z$ with the coordinates $t_i$, $i \in I$, set to $0$ and retracted; then $\tilde s(z) = R(z, \sum_{\emptyset \ne I \subseteq \sigma}(-1)^{|I|+1}s(z_I))$ ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · boundaryExtension⟧, which is the text's sum ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · boundaryExtension_toBase_snd⟧ and lies in $K[1]$ ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · boundaryExtension_mem⟧. Each term is sc-smooth through the corner retraction of the face ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · exists_isScSmooth_faceTerm⟧ ⟦Chapter2/CornerGerms · corner_retraction⟧. *The cancellation.* If $v(I \cup \{i_0\}) = v(I)$ for all $I$, then $\sum_{\emptyset \ne I \subseteq \sigma}(-1)^{|I|+1}v(I) = v(\emptyset)$, because $\sum_{I \subseteq \sigma}(-1)^{|I|}v(I) = 0$ by pairing $I$ with $I \cup \{i_0\}$ ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · sum_powerset_erase_empty_alternating⟧. On the face $t_{i_0} = 0$, killing $i_0$ changes nothing ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · cornerKill_insert_of_coord_eq_zero⟧, so $\tilde s = s$ there.

**Proposition 12.3.7** (stronger) ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · proposition_12_3_7_of_faces_at⟧: only the face germs at $x_0$ itself are needed. $V$ is the intersection of a neighbourhood where $I(z) \subseteq \sigma$, of the neighbourhoods where the $z_I$ stay in the domains, and of the face germs' domains. Sc-smoothness on $O \cap V$ goes through the restricted retraction; equality on $\partial O \cap V$ holds because at $z \in \partial O \cap V$ some $i_0 \in I(z) \subseteq \sigma$, and the cancellation applies. The text's form follows ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · proposition_12_3_7⟧, with an arbitrary tame presentation in place of $\mathbb R^n \oplus H$. Witness with $\partial O \ne \emptyset$: $C = [0, \infty) \oplus W$, $R = \mathrm{id}$, $x_0 = 0$ and the zero section ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · proposition_12_3_7_nonvacuous⟧.

**Corollary 12.3.8** (explicit) ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · corollary_12_3_8⟧. "$G_{x_0}$ acts on $O$ with a lift to $K$" is a structure: a finite group acting by sc-smooth maps of $O$, with an sc-smooth, fibre-linear lift to $K[1]$ covering the action, with unit and composition laws ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · LocalBundleAction⟧; witness, the trivial action ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · LocalBundleAction.trivial⟧. That the group fixes $x_0$, true of an isotropy group, is an explicit hypothesis; $\partial O \cap V_0$ is invariant and $s$ equivariant there. Then $\hat s(x) = |G|^{-1}\sum_gg^{-1} * \tilde s(g * x)$ ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · LocalBundleAction.average⟧, for the extension $\tilde s$ of Proposition 12.3.7 on an invariant neighbourhood, is sc⁺ (sums of sc⁺ terms stay in $K[1]$ ⟦Chapter12/P3B_LocalBoundaryExtension · mem_strongShiftOne_sum_smul⟧), equivariant, and equal to $s$ on $\partial O \cap V$, where each term is $g^{-1} * s(g * x) = s(x)$. "Invariant" is read as equivariant.

### XII.9 Definition 12.4.1 (2017: 12.9), Theorem 12.4.2 (2017: 12.9), Lemma 12.4.4 (2017: 12.1)

**Lemma 12.4.4** ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpGroupoid.lemma_12_4_4_1⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpGroupoid.lemma_12_4_4_2⟧: $\operatorname{cl}_{|X|}\pi(\Sigma) = \pi(\operatorname{cl}_X\Sigma)$ for saturated $\Sigma$, and for $\Sigma$ with compact closure. For saturated $\Sigma$, $\pi$ open gives $\pi^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}\pi(\Sigma)) = \operatorname{cl}\pi^{-1}(\pi(\Sigma)) = \operatorname{cl}\Sigma$; for compact closure, $\pi(\operatorname{cl}\Sigma)$ is compact, hence closed. The image of a closed saturated set is closed ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpGroupoid.isClosed_image_π_of_isSaturated⟧.

**Definition 12.4.1** ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.HasCompactSolutionSetEp⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.IsProperFunctor⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.IsProperLtInftyFunctor⟧: (1) $|S_f|$ compact; (2) proper: $|S_f|$ compact, and for every auxiliary norm $N$ a saturated open $U \supset S_f$ with $\operatorname{cl}_{|X|}|\{x \in U : N(f(x)) \le 1\}|$ compact; (3) proper$_{<\infty}$: the same for every $0 < C < \infty$ with one $U$. $N(f(x)) \le C$ is Part I's relation, and it passes along morphisms ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.auxLe_tgt_of_auxLe_src⟧.

**Theorem 12.4.2** ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_4_2⟧: for an sc-Fredholm section functor, (1), (2), (3) are equivalent. The text's proof labels its steps (3)⇒(2), (2)⇒(1), (1)⇒(3); their arguments are presumably those of (3)⇒(1), (1)⇒(2), (2)⇒(3), and the formal proof follows the arguments. *(3)⇒(1)* is $C = 1$ ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.IsProperLtInftyFunctor.isProperFunctor⟧, and *(1)⇒(2)* is the first clause ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.IsProperFunctor.hasCompactSolutionSetEp⟧. *(2)⇒(3)* ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.isProperLtInftyFunctor_of_hasCompactSolutionSetEp⟧. *Step 1, local.* At each zero $x$, Part I's Theorem 5.2.2 ⟦Chapter5/Book2021 · theorem_5_2_2⟧ gives a neighbourhood $V(x)$ on which $\{N(f) \le C\}$ has compact closure, for each $C$ ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · exists_nhds_isCompact_closure_auxLe⟧. *Step 2.* The open sets $\pi(V(x))$ cover the compact $|S_f|$; take finitely many and $U = \pi^{-1}$ of their union. *Step 3.* $|\{x \in U : N(f(x)) \le C\}|$ lies in the finite union of the compact sets $\pi(\operatorname{cl}\{y \in V(x_i) : N(f(y)) \le C\})$, so its closure is compact. The text's shrinking to neighbourhoods with the natural action is not needed. Paracompactness of $|X|$ is kept from the text and not used, since (1)–(3) quantify over all auxiliary norms.

### XII.10 Lemma 12.5.1 (2017: 12.2): morphisms act on linearizations

**The isomorphism of a morphism.** For a morphism $\varphi$, let $\tau$ be the local inverse of $t$ on the sheet of $\varphi$. Then $y \mapsto s(\tau(y))$ on the base and $w \mapsto \mu(\tau(P(w))^{-1}, w)$ on the bundle form a local strong bundle isomorphism from a neighbourhood of $t(\varphi)$ to one of $s(\varphi)$ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_MorphismIso · EpStrongBundle.morIso⟧, the inverse of the text's $\hat\Phi$; on the fibre over $t(\varphi)$ it is $\mu(\varphi^{-1}, \cdot)$ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_MorphismIso · EpStrongBundle.morIso_Φ_eq⟧. A section functor is unchanged by it ⟦Chapter12/P3O_MorphismIso · EpStrongBundle.eqOn_morIso⟧, and for composable morphisms the isomorphisms compose as germs ⟦Chapter12/P3O_MorphismIso · EpStrongBundle.germAgree_morIso_comp⟧.

**Chart points pulled back.** Part I reads $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ in a chart point. A local isomorphism pulls a chart point at $x$ back to one at $x'$ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_PullChart · StrongBundle.LocalIso.pullPt⟧; if $f$ is unchanged by the isomorphism, the principal parts agree and so do the sets $\mathrm{Lin}$ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_PullChart · StrongBundle.LocalIso.linSet_pullPt⟧. Pulling back commutes with Part I's identifications between chart points ⟦Chapter12/P3O_PullChart · StrongBundle.LocalIso.transferT_pullPt⟧, also twice, for germs that agree ⟦Chapter12/P3O_PullChart · StrongBundle.LocalIso.transferT_pullPt_pullPt⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_PullChart · StrongBundle.LocalIso.GermAgree⟧.

**$T\varphi$ and $\mu(\varphi, \cdot)$** ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.morTx⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.morKx⟧ are Part I's identifications from the chosen chart point at $x$ to a chart at $x$ inside the sheet, the identity to its pulled chart at $x'$, and from there to the chosen chart point at $x'$. They respect composition, units and inverses ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.morTx_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.morTx_unit⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.morTx_inv⟧. Then $\varphi_*S = \mu(\varphi, \cdot) \circ S \circ (T\varphi)^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.linMor⟧.

**Lemma 12.5.1** (explicit). The added hypothesis `hsec`, sc⁺-sections through every smooth fibre point, is not derived from the text; it is Part I's standing hypothesis for $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x) \ne \emptyset$, which §12.5 uses through Part I's $\mathrm{Lin}$. Its witness: bump functions on the objects give it ⟦Chapter3/IndexLocallyConstantLocal · MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctions.hasScPlusSectionsThrough⟧. (1) $\varphi_*S \in \mathrm{Lin}(f, x')$ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.lemma_12_5_1_one⟧: $S = (f - s_0)'(x)$ for an sc⁺-section $s_0$, and pushed by the isomorphism of $\varphi$ it is $(f - \hat\Phi_*s_0)'(x')$, by the agreement of $\mathrm{Lin}$ in a chart and its pulled chart. (2) $\varphi_*$ is a bijection $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x) \to \mathrm{Lin}(f, x')$ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.lemma_12_5_1_two⟧, directly, as conjugation by isomorphisms; the text derives (2) from (1) and (3). (3) $(1_x)_* = \mathrm{Id}$ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.lemma_12_5_1_three_unit⟧ and $(\psi\varphi)_* = \psi_*\varphi_*$ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.lemma_12_5_1_three_comp⟧, from the germ identity of the composed isomorphisms. The text calls the lemma obvious. **On orientations** (p. 593) $\varphi_*o$ is conjugation of a line orientation by $T\varphi$ and $\mu(\varphi, \cdot)$ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.orMor⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.orMor_apply⟧, functorial ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.orMor_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.orMor_unit⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationBundleEp · EpStrongBundle.orMor_inv⟧.

### XII.11 Definition 12.5.2 to Proposition 12.5.6 (2017: Definition 12.11 to Proposition 12.4): the orientation bundle

**Definition 12.5.2** (restated) ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationOrbit · EpStrongBundle.definition_12_5_2⟧: $O_f$ is Part I's orientation space of $f$ as a section of the object bundle, with projection $\sigma : O_f \to X_\infty$, surjective with exactly two points over each $x$ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationOrbit · orProj_two⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationOrbit · exists_other_or⟧ (with `hsec`), and with Part I's topology. The morphisms act as a relation, an equivalence ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationOrbit · EpStrongBundle.OrRel⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationOrbit · EpStrongBundle.orRel_equivalence⟧, with the projection $|\sigma| : |O_f| \to |X_\infty|$ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationOrbit · EpStrongBundle.orbitProj⟧; $|X_\infty|$ is the quotient by the morphisms between smooth points ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationOrbit · EpGroupoid.SmoothRel⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationOrbit · EpGroupoid.smoothRel_equivalence⟧. The text uses these orbit spaces in Proposition 12.5.6 without defining them; they carry the quotient topologies.

**Theorem 12.5.3** (narrower) ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationOrbit · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_5_3_hyp⟧: there is exactly one topology on $O_f$ for which it is Hausdorff, $\sigma$ is a local homeomorphism, there are exactly two continuous sections near each point and they propagate; every fibre has two points. The proof is Part I's Theorem 6.6.17 ⟦Chapter6/OrientationMainClean · theorem_6_6_17⟧ applied to the object bundle, with the two-point fibres. Its hypotheses are Part I's: $X$ tame, bump functions on the objects, and tame germ data for $f$. They are inherited from Theorem 6.6.17, not new, and the text assumes only a tame $X$. The last sentence, that the isomorphism of a morphism pushes continuous local sections of $\sigma$ to continuous local sections, is proved in wave 5 under the same hypotheses (§XII.25); the fibre bijections and their functoriality are §XII.10.

**Definition 12.5.4** ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationOrbit · EpStrongBundle.definition_12_5_4⟧: an orientation is a section $x \mapsto o_x$ of $\sigma$, continuous for a given topology on $O_f$ (Part I's, by Theorem 12.5.3), with $\varphi_*o_{s(\varphi)} = o_{t(\varphi)}$ for every morphism between smooth points. **Remark 12.5.5** is prose pointing to Chapter 15, and is not formalized.

**Proposition 12.5.6.** *(⇒)* ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationOrbit · EpStrongBundle.proposition_12_5_6_mp⟧: an orientation makes $|\sigma|$ two-to-one ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationOrbit · EpStrongBundle.IsTwoToOne⟧ and gives the continuous section $|x| \mapsto |(x, o_x)|$ of $|\sigma|$, well defined by functoriality and continuous through the quotient. *(⇐), without continuity* (narrower) ⟦Chapter12/P3O_OrientationOrbit · EpStrongBundle.proposition_12_5_6_mpr_invariant⟧: if $|\sigma|$ is two-to-one, every section of it lifts to a section $o$ of $\sigma$ with $\varphi_*o_x = o_{x'}$ for all morphisms and $|(x, o_x)| = s(|x|)$. Since $|\sigma|$ is two-to-one, exactly one of the two orientations over $x$ lies in the class $s(|x|)$; it is $o_x$, and $\varphi_*o_x$ lies in the same class, so it is $o_{x'}$. That $o$ is continuous when the section of $|\sigma|$ is continuous is proved in wave 5 from the last sentence of Theorem 12.5.3 (§XII.26).

### XII.12 Witnesses and the hypotheses

**Hypotheses taken.** *§XII.5.* `HasLocalExtensions`, the local step of Theorem 12.2.7, not derived from the text; witness `theorem_12_2_7_hyp_witness`. Tameness of $X$ is dropped there. *§§XII.6–XII.7.* Theorem 12.3.2 (2) and Theorem 12.3.3 take pointwise ep bump functions, the project's reading of Part I's Definition 5.3.1; witness `admitsBumpFunctionsPointwise_trivial_rn`. *§§XII.10–XII.11.* `hsec`, sc⁺-sections through smooth fibre points, not derived from the text, Part I's standing hypothesis for $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x) \ne \emptyset$; witness `MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctions.hasScPlusSectionsThrough`. Theorem 12.5.3 takes Part I's hypotheses of Theorem 6.6.17 (bump functions on the objects, tame germ data), inherited. *§XII.8.* Corollary 12.3.8 makes explicit that the group fixes $x_0$ and models "acts with a lift" as a structure. *Kept and unused.* Paracompactness of $|X|$ in Theorems 12.3.3 and 12.4.2. Several statements need less than the text assumes: Theorem 12.2.2 does not use Theorem 12.2.6 (5) (§XII.2), Proposition 12.3.7 uses the face germs at $x_0$ only (§XII.8).

**Every definition has a witness.** Auxiliary norms: Theorem 12.2.2 itself. Auxiliary norms over $\partial X$ with local extensions: restrictions of global ones (§XII.5). Ep bump functions, pointwise: the trivial ep-groupoid on $\mathbb R^n$ (§XII.6). sc⁺-sections over the boundary, in every tame chart and presentation: the zero section, and with nonempty boundary $[0, \infty) \oplus W$ (§XII.8). Local bundle actions: the trivial action (§XII.8). `hsec`: bump functions on the objects (§XII.10).

### XII.13 What is not formalized

- *Closed in wave 2.* G.136, the local step of Theorem 12.2.7 (§XII.15); G.137, the ep-groupoid form of Definition 12.3.6 (§XII.18).
- *Closed in wave 3.* G.147, the local step of Theorem 12.2.13, the lower semicontinuity under mixed convergence of the local extension of §XII.15 (§XII.22).
- *Closed in wave 5.* G.138, the last sentence of Theorem 12.5.3, that the isomorphism of a morphism keeps local orientation sections continuous (§§XII.23, XII.25); G.139, the continuity in Proposition 12.5.6 (⇐) (§XII.26).
- Gap G.140: §12.5 with a tame $X$ only. Theorem 12.5.3, with its last sentence, Proposition 12.5.6 (⇐) and the continuity in Theorem 12.5.7 carry the hypotheses of Part I's Theorem 6.6.17 (bump functions on the objects, tame germ data), and Lemma 12.5.1, Proposition 12.5.6 and Theorem 12.5.7 the hypothesis that sc⁺-sections pass through smooth fibre points. These are inherited from Part I; removing them needs Part I's orientation transport without bump functions and for untamed germ data. In the tame case, sc⁺-sections through points would follow from Theorem 12.3.9, but only under the hypothesis that partitions of unity exist, which is no improvement.
- Gap G.158, formalized in part: Theorem 12.5.7 (§§XII.20, XII.27). Present: the bijection over the bijection of orbit spaces, the unique invariant push-forward, and its continuity, read as Part I's continuity of orientations over all of $X$, with the local tools in both directions (§XII.27). Missing: (a) that the orbit map $|O_f| \to |O_{f'}|$ is a homeomorphism, by carrying the basic open sets of Part I's topology near $a$ to those of the carried section near $\phi(a)$ and passing to the quotients, about 250–350 lines; (b) that continuity of the section $x \mapsto (x, o_x)$ for Part I's topology, the form of Definition 12.5.4, implies Part I's continuity of orientations, which gives (2) exactly in the book's form, by Part I's propagation along sc-smooth paths and the connectedness of $[0, 1]$, about 100–200 lines; (c) the independence of the representative and functoriality, which need a notion of equivalent representatives (a common refinement with natural transformations) not yet in the project, about 300–500 lines; about 650–1,050 lines in all.
- A reading, not formalization work: Theorem 12.3.2 (1) with Definition 12.3.1 as printed on one side and Part I's pointwise bump functions on the other; its (⇒) is Part I's open weak-to-pointwise question (§XII.6).
- Remark 12.5.5 is prose.

### XII.14 What the formalization taught us

Chapter 12 is Part I seen through the morphisms, and most of its formal content is one pattern used again and again: build an object on a neighbourhood with the natural action of $G_x$, average it over $G_x$, transport it to the saturation by a choice of morphisms, and glue with a partition of unity of $|X|$. Norms (Theorems 12.2.2, 12.2.7), reflexive norms (Theorems 12.2.11, 12.2.13), bump functions (Theorem 12.3.2) and sc⁺-sections (Theorems 12.3.3, 12.3.9, Remark 12.3.5) all follow it. What makes the transport well defined is invariance under $G_x$, not the good neighbourhood property (5) of Theorem 12.2.6 that the text invokes: two morphisms from $y$ into $U(x)$ differ by a unique element of $G_x$. Averaging has one trap. The average of a bump function over a finite group can vanish identically; the average of its square cannot, and the text's functions are nonnegative anyway. Completeness of glued fibre norms is not a separate check: a continuous fibrewise seminorm satisfying condition (2) of an auxiliary norm is squeezed, near every point, between two multiples of the chart norm, so completeness comes for free in Part I as well. For the reflexive variant one more fact carries the pattern: morphisms preserve mixed convergence, because they act boundedly on the fibres and continuously on level $0$, and a bounded, level-$0$ convergent sequence in a reflexive fibre is mixed convergent. With it, averaging, transport and gluing all keep lower semicontinuity, and the question whether lower semicontinuity survives the gluing (it does: near a point only finitely many terms matter, and the others are nonnegative) is settled. The local step that the text calls an inspection rests on the same fact used once more, inside one chart: the fibre maps $A(u)$ of the retraction are uniformly bounded near a point and continuous on level $0$, so $A(u_k)h_k$ is bounded and convergent in $F_0$, hence weakly convergent in the reflexive $F_1$ (§XII.22).

Several places carried more, or less, than the text shows. The inclusion–exclusion formula of Proposition 12.3.7 restricts to $s$ on the boundary because an alternating sum over subsets collapses when one index is already on its face; written out, the face germs at $x_0$ are all that is used, so the proposition holds in a stronger form, and Part I's ∂-extension theorem is assembled from it (Part V, §V.55). The local step of Theorem 12.2.7 needs less than the text's tame local model: the retraction onto the boundary is built in a tame chart of the base, and the fibre formula can be evaluated in any strong bundle chart of the atlas, since only the continuity of the retraction and its two properties (values in $\partial X$, identity on $\partial X$) enter. Theorem 12.3.9 uses bump functions on the objects, which the text takes from Theorem 12.3.2 (2); they come from the assumed partitions of unity, so no hypothesis is added, and the second neighbourhood $V'$ of the text's bound is not needed. In §12.5 the text's "obvious" Lemma 12.5.1 took about 1.1k lines: a morphism acts on $\mathrm{Lin}(f, x)$ through a local strong bundle isomorphism built from its sheet, and Part I's linearizations, which live in chart points, have to be pulled back along it and compared; Theorem 12.5.7 repeats this between two different bundles. Hypotheses of the text that turned out not to be used: paracompactness of $|X|$ in Theorems 12.3.3, 12.3.9 (where partitions of unity are assumed), 12.4.2 and 12.4.6; tameness in the global part of Theorem 12.2.7 and in Theorem 12.4.6; reflexivity, sc-smoothness and the regularizing property in Proposition 12.4.5. One hypothesis is used but not printed: Theorem 12.2.13 needs paracompactness of $|X|$, which its proof takes from Theorem 12.2.11 and which Theorem 12.2.7 states. The step (3)⇒(1) of Proposition 12.4.5, "easily obtained" in the text, needs a lifting argument through the properness of $t$. The proof of Theorem 12.4.2 labels its three implications in an order that its arguments presumably permute.

The orientation bundle is Part I's, and Part I's Theorem 6.6.17 supplies its topology; what §12.5 adds is one statement, used three times (Theorem 12.5.3's last sentence, Proposition 12.5.6 (⇐), Theorem 12.5.7 (2)), that compares Part I's propagation of orientations along paths with local strong bundle isomorphisms. It took about 2,100 lines over waves 3 and 5, and three ingredients the text does not mention. First, the stabilizing sc⁺-section of Part I's push-forward must itself be carried along the isomorphism, which needs a cut-off, and then stabilized kernels, orientation rays and push-forwards correspond term by term (§XII.23). Second, Part I never states that continuity of an orientation is a local property; it is, by a dyadic induction on sc-smooth paths with a Lebesgue number of the cover by chart domains, and this locality lemma is what turns the chart-level comparison into continuity (§XII.25). Third, the orientation map of a local isomorphism depends only on its germ, so the isomorphisms of two sheets through one morphism, or of an equivalence at two nearby objects, act alike; the text uses this silently in passing from one sheet to another. With these, Proposition 12.5.6 (⇐) is short: over a two-to-one $|\sigma|$ the isotropy fixes the orientations, so near a point every morphism maps a continuous local orientation to itself, and the lifted section is that orientation there. What is still missing in Theorem 12.5.7 is topology of quotients and the comparison of representatives, not orientation theory.

### XII.15 Theorem 12.2.7 (2017: 12.3) as printed: the local step near the boundary

Wave 1 proved Theorem 12.2.7 with its local step as the hypothesis `HasLocalExtensions` (§XII.5). That hypothesis is now proved for every tame $X$, so the theorem holds as printed. The local step is a Part I statement about one strong bundle over a tame M-polyfold, the object bundle.

**The retraction onto the boundary** (extra, Part I) ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · MPolyfold.exists_retraction_boundary⟧. In a tame M-polyfold every boundary point $x_0$ has an open $V \ni x_0$ and a map $\rho$, continuous on $V$, with values in $\partial X$ and $\rho(y) = y$ for $y \in V \cap \partial X$. *The coordinates.* Let $C = [0, \infty)^n \oplus H$ be the partial quadrant of a tame chart $\psi$ at $x_0$, read through a presentation $T$. Put $\tau(t, h) = \min(t_1, \dots, t_n)$ ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · minCoord⟧ and $q(t, h) = (t, h) - \tau(t, h)(1, \dots, 1, 0)$ ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · boundaryShift⟧. Then $q$ is continuous ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · continuous_boundaryShift⟧ and takes values in $C$ ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · mem_quadrant_boundaryShift⟧, the coordinate where the minimum is attained becomes $0$, so the values lie in $\partial C$ ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · exists_coord_boundaryShift_eq_zero⟧, and on $\partial C$ the minimum is $0$, so $q$ is the identity there ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · boundaryShift_eq_self⟧. A point is on $\partial C$ iff some half-line coordinate vanishes ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · one_le_degIndexWith_iff⟧. *The retraction.* With $r$ the tame retraction of the chart, $\rho = \psi^{-1} \circ r \circ q \circ \psi$ on the open set where this is defined. Tameness of the chart gives $d_X = d_C$ on its domain, so $r$ maps $\partial C$ to boundary points and $\rho$ has values in $\partial X$; and $r$ fixes $O = r(U)$, so $\rho$ fixes $V \cap \partial X$. The text takes $x_0 = (0, h_0)$; this is not needed, since $q$ maps into $\partial C$ and fixes $\partial C$ whatever the coordinates of $x_0$.

**The norm $N'$** (extra, Part I) ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.retractNorm⟧. In a strong bundle chart $c$ of the atlas around $x_0$, $A(u)h$ is the fibre part of the retraction $R[1]$ ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.chartFibMap⟧, linear in $h$ ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.isLinearMap_chartFibMap⟧ and the identity on the image $K[1]$ ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.chartFibMap_of_mem⟧. A vector $w$ over $y$ with chart coordinates $(u, h)$ is moved to the fibre over $\rho(y)$ by $h \mapsto A(\varphi(\rho(y)))h$, read back through $\Phi[1]^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.retractTransport⟧, a linear fibre map. Then $N'(w) = N(\text{transported } w) + \|h - A(\varphi(\rho(y)))h\|_{F_1}$, the text's formula read in $\Phi[1]$ ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.retractNorm_toOne⟧.

**$N'$ is a local auxiliary norm** ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.isLocalAuxNorm_retractNorm⟧. The lemma is stated for any set $A$ of base points and any $N$ that is continuous on $W_{0,1}|A$, a seminorm on the fibres over $A$, and satisfies condition (2) for sequences in $A$, and any $\rho$ continuous on an open $V$ inside the chart domain with values in $A$. By the Part I lemma of §XII.2, a local auxiliary norm needs only three checks. *Continuity.* $(u, h) \mapsto A(u)h$ is continuous on $U \oplus F_1$, because it is level $0$ of the sc-smooth retraction $R : (U \triangleleft F)[1] \to (U \triangleleft F)[1]$ ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.continuousOn_shiftFiber_R⟧; so both terms are continuous on $W_{0,1}|V$. *Seminorm.* The transport is linear on each fibre, and the second term is a norm of a linear expression ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.isFiberSeminorm_retractNorm⟧. *Condition (2).* Let $P(w_k) \to y$ in $V$ and $N'(w_k) \to 0$. Both terms tend to $0$. The transported vectors lie over $\rho(P(w_k)) \to \rho(y) \in A$, so condition (2) for $N$, applied to a tail of the sequence, makes them converge to $0_{\rho(y)}$; hence $A(u_k)h_k \to 0$ in $F_1$, and with $\|h_k - A(u_k)h_k\| \to 0$ also $h_k \to 0$. Convergence in the chart gives $w_k \to 0_y$ ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · MChart.tendsto_of_tendsto_apply⟧. **$N' = N$ where $\rho$ is the identity** ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.retractNorm_eq⟧: over $y \in V \cap A$ with $\rho(y) = y$, a vector of the fibre has $h \in K[1]$, so $A h = h$, the transport is the identity and the second term vanishes.

**The local step** ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · StrongBundle.exists_localExtension_of_isTame⟧: for a tame M-polyfold and $N$ as above over $\partial X$, every $x_0 \in \partial X$ has an open $V \ni x_0$ and a local auxiliary norm $M$ on $V$ with $M = N$ over $V \cap \partial X$. Take $\rho$ from the retraction lemma on $V_1$, a chart $c$ at $x_0$, and $V = V_1 \cap \operatorname{dom}c \cap \rho^{-1}(\operatorname{dom}c)$, open by the continuity of $\rho$ and containing $x_0$ because $\rho(x_0) = x_0$; then $M = N'$. For an ep-groupoid this discharges the hypothesis of wave 1 ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · EpStrongBundle.hasLocalExtensions_of_isTame⟧.

**Theorem 12.2.7** ⟦Chapter12/P3E_AuxNormLocalExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_7⟧: for a strong bundle over a tame ep-groupoid with paracompact $|X|$, every auxiliary norm $N$ over $\partial X$ extends to an auxiliary norm $\tilde N$ of $W$ with $\tilde N = N$ over $\partial X$. It is the theorem of §XII.5 with its hypothesis discharged; the hypotheses are the text's. Two readings. The text works in one local strong bundle model whose base retraction is tame; here the retraction onto the boundary lives in a tame chart of $X$ and the fibre formula in an arbitrary strong bundle chart, so no tame strong bundle chart is needed. The invariance of $N$ under morphisms is not used in the local step; it enters through the average over $G_{x_0}$ (§XII.5).

### XII.16 Definitions 12.2.8, 12.2.10, Remarks 12.2.9, 12.2.12 and Theorem 12.2.11 (2017: Definitions 12.5, 12.6, Remarks 12.1, 12.2, Theorem 12.4): reflexive auxiliary norms

**Reflexive $1$-fibres and mixed convergence.** A strong bundle over an ep-groupoid has reflexive $1$-fibres when the object bundle has them in the sense of Part I's Definition 5.1.4 (Part V, §V.49) ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.HasReflexiveFibers⟧: the compatible charts whose $F_1$ is reflexive cover $X$. **Definition 12.2.8** ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.MixedTendsto⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.definition_12_2_8⟧ is Part I's mixed convergence on the object bundle (§V.50): $P(w_k) \to P(w)$ in $X_0$ and, in a chart with reflexive $F_1$, the fibre parts converge weakly in $F_1$.

**Remark 12.2.9** (stronger) ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_2_9⟧. For $w_k \to w$ mixed: (i) the fibre parts converge weakly in every compatible chart around $P(w)$ with reflexive $F_1$, which is the remark, from Part I's Lemma 5.1.5; (ii) $w_k \to w$ in $W$; (iii) for every sc-smooth local section $\alpha$ of the source map $s$ on an open $S \ni P(w)$, $\mu(\alpha(P(w_k)), w_k) \to \mu(\alpha(P(w)), w)$ mixed ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.mixedTendsto_actOne⟧. So morphisms preserve mixed convergence; through a given morphism $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) = P(w)$ such an $\alpha$ is the local inverse of $s$ on the sheet of $\varphi$, and then $\mu(\alpha(P(w_k)), w_k) \to \mu(\varphi, w)$ mixed ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.exists_mixedTendsto_μ⟧. *Proof of (iii)*, the remark's argument with the fibre maps of $\mu$ in place of a transition map. *Step 1, level $0$.* $\mu$ is continuous, so the images converge on level $0$. *Step 2, a bound.* For a Part I auxiliary norm $N_0$, near $P(w)$ one has $N_0(\mu(\alpha(\cdot), v)) \le C\,N_0(v)$ ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.exists_le_mul_auxNorm⟧, and a mixed convergent sequence is eventually bounded in $N_0$ ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.MixedTendsto.exists_eventually_le⟧; so the images are eventually bounded. *Step 3.* A bounded sequence that converges on level $0$ is mixed convergent ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.mixedTendsto_of_bounded⟧: by reflexivity every subsequence has a weakly convergent subsequence (Part V, §V.48), and its weak limit is identified by the level-$0$ limit, so the whole sequence converges weakly.

**Lower semicontinuity along mixed convergence** (extra) ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.MixedLscAt⟧: $M$ is mixed lower semicontinuous at $y$ if for every $w_k \to y$ mixed and $\varepsilon > 0$, eventually $M(y) - \varepsilon < M(w_k)$; this gives $M(y) \le \liminf M(w_k)$ ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.MixedLscAt.le_liminf⟧. It is stable under sums ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.MixedLscAt.add⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.mixedLscAt_finset_sum⟧, nonnegative constant multiples ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.MixedLscAt.const_mul⟧ and products with continuous positive functions of the base point ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · StrongBundle.MixedLscAt.mul_comp⟧, and through morphisms ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.mixedLscAt_comp_actOne⟧.

**Definition 12.2.10** ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.IsReflexiveAuxNorm⟧: an auxiliary norm (Definition 12.2.1, with continuity, the functor property, complete fibre norms and condition (2)) with (3), $N(w) \le \liminf_k N(w_k)$ for $w_k \to w$ mixed, the liminf taken in the extended reals. The printed $\liminf_{k \to 0}$ is presumably $k \to \infty$, as in Part I (§V.50). A reflexive auxiliary norm is one of Part I's Definition 5.1.7 on the objects ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.IsReflexiveAuxNorm.toStrong⟧, and (3) follows from mixed lower semicontinuity at every point ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.isReflexiveAuxNorm_of_mixedLscAt⟧.

**Theorem 12.2.11** ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_11⟧, with exactly the text's hypotheses, paracompact $|X|$ and reflexive $1$-fibres. *(1) Existence* ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_11_exists⟧. The proof is the construction of Theorem 12.2.2 (§XII.2), with lower semicontinuity carried through each step. The local norm on a neighbourhood with the natural action is a reflexive auxiliary norm of Part I's Proposition 5.1.8 (§V.51), where the text writes $\|\mathrm{pr}_2 \circ \Psi(g * h)\|_{F_1}$. *Average.* Each term $M(g * w)$ is mixed lower semicontinuous because $g *$ acts through morphisms, which preserve mixed convergence; so is the finite sum ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.mixedLscAt_avgNorm⟧. *Transport.* Near a point of the saturation the chosen morphisms into $U(x)$ can be taken from a local sc-smooth section of $s$, and (iii) of Remark 12.2.9 applies ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.mixedLscAt_transNorm⟧. *Glue.* Near $|P(w)|$ only finitely many $\beta_\lambda$ are nonzero; a term with $\beta_\lambda(|P(w)|) > 0$ is a continuous positive function times a lower semicontinuous one, and a term with $\beta_\lambda(|P(w)|) = 0$ contributes $0$ at the limit and $\ge 0$ along the sequence ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.mixedLscAt_glueNorm⟧. So the glued norm of §XII.2 is a reflexive auxiliary norm ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.isReflexiveAuxNorm_glueNorm⟧. *(2)* $h \mapsto f(P(h))N(h)$ is reflexive for a continuous functorial $f > 0$ ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_11_mul⟧, which is Remark 12.2.12 (1). *(3) The sandwich* ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_11_sandwich⟧: for an auxiliary norm $N'$ and a reflexive $N$, Remark 12.2.12 (2) gives functorial $f, g > 0$ with $N \le (f \circ P)N'$ and $N' \le (g \circ P)N$; then $N_1 = (f \circ P)^{-1}N \le N' \le (g \circ P)N = N_2$, both reflexive by (2).

**Remark 12.2.12.** *(1)* ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_2_12_1⟧ as printed: continuity, functor property and condition (2) pass to $(f \circ P)N$, and lower semicontinuity by the product rule above. *(2)* ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_2_12_2⟧: for auxiliary norms $N_1, N_2$ and paracompact $|X|$, which the remark's context has, there is a continuous $f > 0$ constant along morphisms with $N_1 \le (f \circ P)N_2$. Near each point Part I's comparison of auxiliary norms (Lemma 5.1.2) gives a constant; invariance of both norms makes the bound hold on the saturation; a partition of unity of $|X|$ glues the constants into $f$. *(3)* (stronger) ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormEp · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_2_12_3⟧: for $U$ open, $N \ge 0$ mixed lower semicontinuous over $U$ and $f \ge 0$ continuous, $\tilde N = f \cdot N$ on $U$ and $0$ off $U$ satisfies $\tilde N(w) \le \liminf\tilde N(w_k)$ for $w_k \to w$ mixed. Off $U$, $\tilde N(w) = 0 \le \tilde N(w_k)$; on $U$ the sequence eventually lies over $U$. The saturation of $U$, the functoriality of $f$ and $\operatorname{supp}f \subset U$ serve the continuity and the functor property of $\tilde N$, not the estimate, and are not needed for it.

### XII.17 Theorem 12.2.13 (2017: 12.5): extension of reflexive auxiliary norms, with the local step as a hypothesis

**Over the boundary** ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.IsReflexiveAuxNormOn⟧: an auxiliary norm over $A$ in the sense of §XII.5, with the liminf inequality for mixed convergent sequences over $A$; a global reflexive norm restricts ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.IsReflexiveAuxNorm.isReflexiveAuxNormOn⟧.

**The added hypothesis** ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.HasReflexiveLocalExtensions⟧: every $x \in \partial X$ has an open $V \ni x$ and a local auxiliary norm $M$ on $V$, mixed lower semicontinuous at every vector over $V$, with $M = N$ over $V \cap \partial X$. It is not derived from the text; it is the text's local step, the norm $N'$ of §XII.15, which the text calls well behaved under mixed limits "by inspection". It implies the hypothesis of Theorem 12.2.7 ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.HasReflexiveLocalExtensions.hasLocalExtensions⟧. Its witnesses: the restriction of a global reflexive norm has reflexive local extensions ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.hasReflexiveLocalExtensions_of_isReflexiveAuxNorm⟧, so every bundle with reflexive fibres and paracompact $|X|$ satisfies all hypotheses ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_13_hyp_witness⟧; concretely the trivial bundle $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n$ over the trivial ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · TrivialBundle.epBundle_reflexive_witness⟧.

**Theorem 12.2.13** (narrower) ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveAuxNormExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_13_hyp⟧: for paracompact $|X|$, reflexive $1$-fibres, and a reflexive auxiliary norm $N$ over $\partial X$ with reflexive local extensions, there is a reflexive auxiliary norm $\tilde N$ with $\tilde N = N$ over $\partial X$. The proof is that of Theorem 12.2.7 (§XII.5) with the lower semicontinuity of §XII.16 carried along: at boundary points the local extensions of the hypothesis, at interior points the average of a reflexive norm of Part I's Proposition 5.1.8; average, transport and gluing keep mixed lower semicontinuity. Paracompactness of $|X|$, which the text uses through the partition of unity of Theorem 12.2.7, is a hypothesis; tameness enters only the local step and is dropped. **What is missing** (a new gap, §XII.13): that $N'$ of §XII.15 is mixed lower semicontinuous when $N$ is. For $w_k \to w$ mixed near $\partial X$, the transported vectors converge on level $0$ and are bounded, hence are mixed convergent in $W|\partial X$ by the argument of Remark 12.2.9, so the first term is lower semicontinuous; the second term is weakly lower semicontinuous once $h_k - A(u_k)h_k$ converges weakly in $F_1$.

### XII.18 Definition 12.3.6 (2017: 12.8) on ep-groupoids, and Theorem 12.3.9 (2017: 12.8): extension of sc⁺-section functors

**Definition 12.3.6, ep-groupoid form** ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpStrongBundle.IsBoundaryScPlusSection⟧: a section $s$ over $\partial X$ is an sc⁺-section over the boundary when it is one for the object bundle in the sense of Part I's Definition 5.4.1 (Part V, §V.54): $P(s(x)) = x$, $s(x) \in W_{0,1}$, and in every tame strong bundle chart and tame presentation the local representative is sc⁺ on each face germ at the point. The local faces are read chart-wise, as in Definition 5.4.1, and the definition does not involve $\mu$. **An sc⁺-section functor of $W|\partial X$**, as Theorem 12.3.9 uses it ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpStrongBundle.IsBoundaryScPlusSectionFunctor⟧, adds $s(t(\varphi)) = \mu(\varphi, s(s(\varphi)))$ for every morphism $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) \in \partial X$; then $t(\varphi) \in \partial X$ as well, because morphisms preserve the degeneracy index ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpGroupoid.tgt_mem_boundary_iff_p3x⟧. Witness: the zero section ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpStrongBundle.isBoundaryScPlusSectionFunctor_fiberZero⟧.

**Bump functions from partitions of unity** (extra) ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpGroupoid.admitsBumpFunctionsPointwise_of_hasScPartitionsOfUnity⟧: an ep-groupoid with sc-smooth partitions of unity (Definition 7.5.5) admits sc-smooth bump functions in the pointwise reading. For $x$ in a saturated open $U$, take an invariant $V \ni x$ with the natural action and proper closure inside $U$; the saturation $K$ of $\overline V$ is closed; the function attached to $U$ of a partition of unity for the cover $\{U, X \setminus K\}$ is $1$ at $x$ and supported in $U$. The text uses this tacitly ("Using Theorem 12.3.2 (2)"); by Theorem 12.3.2 (1) the object M-polyfold then admits bump functions.

**Gluing sc⁺-sections** (extra). For a partition of unity $(\rho_i)$ and sections $\sigma_i$, $\sum_i\rho_i\sigma_i$ ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · glueSection⟧ is supported in $\bigcup_i\operatorname{supp}\rho_i \cap \operatorname{supp}\sigma_i$ ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · sectionSupport_glueSection_subset⟧, is sc⁺ when the $\sigma_i$ are ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · isScPlusSection_glueSection⟧ (locally a finite sum), takes the value $v$ where every $\sigma_i$ with $\rho_i \ne 0$ does ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · glueSection_eq_of⟧, and is an sc⁺-section functor when the $\sigma_i$ are and the $\rho_i$ are constant along morphisms ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpStrongBundle.isScPlusSectionFunctor_glueSection⟧. An invariant function times a functorial section is functorial ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpStrongBundle.isFunctorialSection_sectionSmul_p3x⟧.

**The local step** ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpStrongBundle.exists_local_functor_extension⟧. For $x \in \partial X$ in a saturated open $U$ there are a saturated open $U' \ni x$ and an sc⁺-section functor $\sigma$ supported in $U$ with $\sigma = s$ on $U' \cap \partial X$. *Step 1.* An invariant $V \ni x$ with the natural action and proper closure inside $U$. *Step 2, Part I's local extension.* In a tame strong bundle chart at $x$, the local extension of Theorem 5.4.2 (Proposition 12.3.7 in the chart; §V.55) gives an sc⁺-section near $x$ equal to $s$ on the boundary ⟦Chapter5/P3B_BoundaryExtension2021 · StrongBundle.exists_local_extension⟧; a bump function $\beta$, $\equiv 1$ near $x$ and supported in $V$ ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · proposition_5_5_3⟧, cuts it off. *Step 3, average.* The equivariant average over $G_x$ in the natural representation (§XII.7) ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpStrongBundle.exists_equivariant_average_p3x⟧ keeps the value $w$ at every point where all translates take the value $w$. At a boundary point $y$ near $x$ each translate is $\mu(\Gamma(k, \cdot), s(\cdot))$ applied at $\Phi(k^{-1})y$, which is $s(y)$ because $s$ is functorial on $\partial X$ and the morphisms preserve $\partial X$; so the average still extends $s$. This is Corollary 12.3.8 in its natural-representation form. *Step 4.* Remark 12.3.5 extends the average to the saturation ⟦Chapter12/P3S_ScPlusSectionFunctor · EpStrongBundle.remark_12_3_5⟧.

**The extension** ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpStrongBundle.exists_extension_of_tameCharts⟧. The sets $U'_x$ ($x \in \partial X$) and $X \setminus \partial X$, saturated and open ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpGroupoid.isSaturated_compl_boundary_p3x⟧, cover $X$. Take an sc-smooth partition of unity $(\rho_i)$ subordinate to it, constant along morphisms (Definition 7.5.5), the local extensions $\sigma_x$ on the pieces $U'_x$, and $0$ on the interior piece, and glue. On $\partial X$ the interior piece has $\rho = 0$ and every other $\sigma_x$ with $\rho \ne 0$ equals $s$, so $\tilde s = s$ there; the support lies in $U$; and $\tilde s$ is an sc⁺-section functor. **The bound** ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpStrongBundle.exists_extension_bounded_of_tameCharts⟧. Given an auxiliary norm $N$ and $N(s(x)) < \delta$ on $\partial X$, $V = \{N(\tilde s) < \delta\}$ is open, saturated by the invariance of $N$, and contains $\partial X$. A partition of unity for the two-set cover $\{V, X \setminus \partial X\}$ gives $\beta$ with $\operatorname{supp}\beta \subset V$ and $\beta = 1$ on $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpGroupoid.partitionOfUnity_true_eq_one_p3x⟧, and $\beta\tilde s$ has $N \le \delta$ everywhere. The text's second neighbourhood $V'$ is not needed.

**Theorem 12.3.9** ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_3_9⟧: for a strong bundle over a tame ep-groupoid (the object bundle tame, as in Theorem 5.4.2), $|X|$ paracompact, admitting sc-smooth partitions of unity, an sc⁺-section functor $s$ of $W|\partial X$ and a saturated open $U \supset \partial X$, there is an sc⁺-section functor $\tilde s$ with $\operatorname{supp}\tilde s \subset U$ and $\tilde s = s$ on $\partial X$; and given an auxiliary norm $N$ with $N(s(x)) < \delta$ on $\partial X$, also $N(\tilde s(x)) \le \delta$ for all $x$. Bump functions on the objects come from the partitions of unity, as above, with Theorem 12.3.2 (1) ⟦Chapter12/P3S_BumpEp · EpGroupoid.theorem_12_3_2_1⟧; paracompactness is the text's hypothesis, kept and unused. No hypothesis is added. Witness for all hypotheses together ⟦Chapter12/P3X_ScPlusExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_3_9_hypotheses_rn⟧: the trivial bundle $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n$ over the trivial ep-groupoid, the zero section, and $U = X$.

### XII.19 Definition 12.4.3, Proposition 12.4.5 and Theorem 12.4.6 (2017: Definition 12.10, Proposition 12.3, Theorem 12.10)

**Definition 12.4.3** ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveCompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.HasReflexiveLocalCompactnessEp⟧: a section functor $f$ has the ep-groupoid reflexive local compactness property if for every reflexive auxiliary norm $N$ and every object $x$ there is an open $U(x) \ni x$ with $\operatorname{cl}_X\{y \in U(x) : N(f(y)) \le 1\}$ compact. The text's standing assumptions (reflexive $(0, 1)$-fibres, $f$ sc-smooth and regularizing) are hypotheses of the statements that use it, and $N(f(y)) \le 1$ is Part I's relation ($N = \infty$ off $W_{0,1}$). Part I's Definition 5.2.6 on the object bundle implies it ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveCompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.hasReflexiveLocalCompactnessEp_of_strong⟧.

**Two tools.** The set $\{y \in \tilde U : N(f(y)) \le 1\}$ is saturated when $\tilde U$ is, because $N$ is invariant and $f$ a functor ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveCompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.isSaturated_setOf_auxLe⟧. *Compact closures from orbit sets* ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveCompactnessEp · EpGroupoid.isCompact_closure_of_isProperMap⟧: if $t : s^{-1}(\overline{V_0}) \to X$ is proper and $A \subset V_0$ has $\operatorname{cl}_{|X|}|A|$ compact, then $\operatorname{cl}_XA$ is compact. Given a sequence in $\operatorname{cl}A$, its orbits have a convergent subsequence in $|X|$; a convergent sequence of $|X|$ lifts to a convergent sequence of objects ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveCompactnessEp · EpGroupoid.exists_lift_tendsto⟧; morphisms connect the given points to the lifts, with sources in $\overline{V_0}$ and convergent targets, and properness gives a convergent subsequence of these morphisms, whose sources converge.

**Proposition 12.4.5** (stronger) ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveCompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.proposition_12_4_5⟧: for an sc-smooth section functor the three conditions are equivalent: (1) Definition 12.4.3; (2) for every reflexive $N$ and $z \in |X|$ a saturated open $\tilde U$ with $z \in |\tilde U|$ and $|\operatorname{cl}_X\{y \in \tilde U : N(f(y)) \le 1\}|$ compact; (3) the same with $\operatorname{cl}_{|X|}|\{y \in \tilde U : N(f(y)) \le 1\}|$ compact. It holds for every section functor ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveCompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.proposition_12_4_5_of_functorial⟧; reflexive fibres, sc-smoothness and the regularizing property are not used. *(2)⇔(3)* by Lemma 12.4.4 (1), the set being saturated (§XII.9). *(1)⇒(3).* $\tilde U$ is the saturation of $U(x)$, which has the same orbit set, and Lemma 12.4.4 (2) applies to the compact closure. *(3)⇒(1)*, "easily obtained" in the text, uses the tool above: with $V_0 \ni x$ on which $t$ is proper over $s^{-1}(\overline{V_0})$, put $U = \tilde U \cap V_0$, open ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveCompactnessEp · EpGroupoid.isSaturated_inter⟧; its sublevel set lies in $V_0$ and has an orbit set with compact closure, so its closure in $X$ is compact.

**Theorem 12.4.6** (stronger) ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveCompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_4_6⟧. Hypotheses, as printed: $X$ tame, $|X|$ paracompact, reflexive $(0, 1)$-fibres, $N$ reflexive, $f$ an sc-Fredholm section functor with compact $|S_f|$ and the reflexive local compactness property, and $U_\partial = W' \cap \partial X$ ($W'$ open, so $U_\partial$ is open in $\partial X$), saturated, containing $S_f \cap \partial X$, with $\operatorname{cl}_{|X|}|\{y \in U_\partial : N(f(y)) \le 1\}|$ compact. Conclusion: a saturated open $U \supset S_f$ with $U \cap \partial X = U_\partial$ and $\operatorname{cl}_{|X|}|\{x \in U : N(f(x)) \le 1\}|$ compact. It holds for every continuous section functor with local compactness at the given $N$ ⟦Chapter12/P3R2_ReflexiveCompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_4_6_of_continuous⟧; tameness, paracompactness and the Fredholm property beyond continuity are unused. *Proof*, the text's, in $|X|$. *Step 1.* Finitely many $|U(\bar x_i)|$, from local compactness at boundary points, cover the compact $\operatorname{cl}|U_\partial \cap \{N \circ f \le 1\}|$. *Step 2.* $\{N \circ f > 1\}$ is open (Part I's Proposition 5.2.7 (2)) and saturated. *Step 3.* Finitely many interior sets $|U(x_i) \setminus \partial X|$ cover the rest of the compact $|S_f|$. *Step 4.* $U$ is the preimage of the union of these orbit sets, cut by $|W'| \cup |X \setminus \partial X|$; since $\partial X$ and $U_\partial$ are saturated, $U \cap \partial X = U_\partial$, and the sublevel set of $U$ lies in finitely many sets with compact closure.

### XII.20 Theorem 12.5.7 (2017: 12.12): naturality of the orientation bundle, without topology

**The setting.** A generalized strong bundle isomorphism is represented by a diagram $W \xleftarrow{h_1} V \xrightarrow{h_2} W'$ of strong bundle equivalences over $\phi_1$, $\phi_2$, with sc-Fredholm section functors $f$, $f'$, $f''$ such that $f'' = h_1^*f = h_2^*f'$. The text's $f'$ is the push-forward of $f$; any section with the same pull-back serves, and the push-forward is one ⟦Chapter12/P3F_Naturality · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pullback_pushforward_witness⟧. Orientations are those of §XII.11; an orientation section is invariant if $\varphi_*o_{s(\varphi)} = o_{t(\varphi)}$ ⟦Chapter12/P3F_Naturality · EpStrongBundle.IsOrInvariant⟧, the second clause of Definition 12.5.4 ⟦Chapter12/P3F_Naturality · EpStrongBundle.definition_12_5_4_iff⟧.

**Linearizations between different bundles** (extra) ⟦Chapter12/P3F_MixedPull · StrongBundle.LocalIso.mpullPt⟧. Wave 1 pulled chart points back along a local strong bundle isomorphism of a bundle to itself (§XII.10); the same construction works between two bundles over different bases. If $f = \Psi \circ f' \circ \phi$ near the point, the pulled chart point has the same set $\mathrm{Lin}$ ⟦Chapter12/P3F_MixedPull · StrongBundle.LocalIso.linSet_mpullPt⟧, pulling back commutes with Part I's identifications between chart points, also for two composites with the same germ ⟦Chapter12/P3F_MixedPull · StrongBundle.LocalIso.GermAgree₄⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3F_MixedPull · StrongBundle.LocalIso.transferT_mpullPt₄⟧, and the resulting map of orientations ⟦Chapter12/P3F_MixedPull · StrongBundle.LocalIso.morVia⟧ does not depend on the auxiliary chart point ⟦Chapter12/P3F_MixedPull · StrongBundle.LocalIso.morVia_eq⟧. For a bundle to itself it is wave 1's construction ⟦Chapter12/P3F_MixedPull · StrongBundle.LocalIso.mpullPt_eq_pullPt⟧.

**One equivalence.** Let $h : V \to W$ be a strong bundle equivalence over $\phi$ with $f'' = h^*f$. At each object $a$, $h$ is a local strong bundle isomorphism near $a$ ⟦Chapter12/P3F_EquivalenceOr · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.locIso⟧, and conjugation by its linearizations is a bijection of orientation sets $\mathrm{orEqv}_a : \mathrm{Or}^f_{\phi(a)} \to \mathrm{Or}^{f''}_a$ ⟦Chapter12/P3F_EquivalenceOr · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.orEqv⟧. *Naturality* ⟦Chapter12/P3F_EquivalenceOr · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.orMor_orEqv⟧: for a morphism $\alpha : a \to b$, $\alpha_* \circ \mathrm{orEqv}_a = \mathrm{orEqv}_b \circ (\phi\alpha)_*$. The local isomorphism of $\alpha$ followed by that of $h$ at $b$ and the local isomorphism of $h$ at $a$ followed by that of $\phi(\alpha)$ have the same germ, because $h$ is a functor; so the two composite transfers agree, and so do the conjugations. The orbit maps: $\phi$ induces a bijection of the smooth orbit spaces $|V_\infty| \to |X_\infty|$ ⟦Chapter12/P3F_Naturality · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.smoothOrbitMap_bijective⟧ (an equivalence is essentially surjective and fully faithful, and preserves smoothness), and $\mathrm{orEqv}^{-1}$ induces a bijection $|O_{f''}| \to |O_f|$ ⟦Chapter12/P3F_Naturality · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.orbitOrMap_bijective⟧ over it ⟦Chapter12/P3F_Naturality · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.orbitProj_orbitOrMap⟧, well defined by naturality. *Orientations.* An invariant orientation of $f$ pulls back to an invariant one of $f''$ ⟦Chapter12/P3F_Naturality · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isOrInvariant_pullOr⟧, and an invariant orientation of $f''$ pushes forward ⟦Chapter12/P3F_Naturality · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pushOr⟧: at $x$ choose $a$ with an isomorphism $\phi(a) \cong x$ and transport by it; invariance makes this independent of the choice, the result is invariant ⟦Chapter12/P3F_Naturality · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isOrInvariant_pushOr⟧ and it is the only invariant orientation that corresponds to the given one at the points $\phi(a)$ ⟦Chapter12/P3F_Naturality · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pushOr_unique⟧.

**Theorem 12.5.7** (narrower). *(1)* ⟦Chapter12/P3F_Naturality · theorem_12_5_7_one_hyp⟧: for the diagram above, there are bijections $F : |O_f| \to |O_{f'}|$ and $G : |X_\infty| \to |X'_\infty|$ with $|\sigma'| \circ F = G \circ |\sigma|$, and $F$, $G$ are the maps of the diagram, composed from the bijections of $h_1$ and $h_2$. *(2)* ⟦Chapter12/P3F_Naturality · theorem_12_5_7_two_invariant⟧: for an invariant orientation $o$ of $f$ there is exactly one invariant orientation $o'$ of $f'$ that corresponds to $o$ through the two equivalences at every smooth object of $V$: pull back along $h_1$, push forward along $h_2$. The added hypotheses are §12.5's standing hypothesis that sc⁺-sections pass through smooth fibre points, for $W$, $W'$ and $V$, not derived from the text, with witness that bump functions give it (§XII.10); and that $f''$ is an sc-Fredholm section functor, which holds for the pull-back of one (Theorem 10.4.5) ⟦Chapter10/FredholmEquivalence · theorem_10_4_5_fred⟧. The identity diagram is a witness of the representative data. The continuity of $o'$ is proved in wave 5 (§XII.27). *Not proved* (gap G.158, §XII.13): that $F$ is a homeomorphism, and the independence of the representative and functoriality, which the text leaves to the reader.
