### XII.22 Theorem 12.2.13 (2017: 12.5) as printed: the local step under mixed convergence

**The local extension** is that of §XII.15: near $x_0 \in \partial X$, in a tame chart of the base with retraction $\rho$ onto $\partial X$ and a strong bundle chart $\Phi$ with fibre $F$ in which $F_1$ is reflexive, write $u = \varphi(\rho(P(\cdot)))$ and $A(u)$ for the fibre map of the retraction of the chart; then $N'(w) = N(\Phi[1]^{-1}(u, A(u)h)) + \|h - A(u)h\|_{F_1}$, where $h$ is the fibre coordinate of $w$. A chart with reflexive $F_1$ around every point is what reflexive $1$-fibres provide.

**Two facts about the fibre maps.** *A uniform bound* ⟦Chapter12/P3W3K_ReflexiveLocalExtension · StrongBundle.exists_norm_chartFibMap_le⟧: near a point $u$ of the chart domain, the operators $A(u')$ on $F_1$ are bounded uniformly in $u'$; this is the joint continuity of the retraction on level $1$. *Weak convergence* ⟦Chapter12/P3W3K_ReflexiveLocalExtension · StrongBundle.weakTendsto_chartFibMap⟧: if $u_k \to u$ and $h_k \rightharpoonup h$ in the reflexive $F_1$, then $A(u_k)h_k \rightharpoonup A(u)h$. The sequence $A(u_k)h_k$ is bounded by the uniform bound; it converges to $A(u)h$ in $F_0$, by the level-$0$ continuity of the retraction and the compactness of $F_1 \to F_0$, which turns the weak convergence of $h_k$ into strong convergence on level $0$; a bounded sequence in a reflexive space whose every weakly convergent subsequence has the same limit converges weakly. The fibre map lies over the base point ⟦Chapter12/P3W3K_ReflexiveLocalExtension · StrongBundle.toBase_chartFibMap⟧, and differences of weakly convergent sequences converge weakly ⟦Chapter12/P3W3K_ReflexiveLocalExtension · WeakTendsto.sub⟧.

**The inspection** ⟦Chapter12/P3W3K_ReflexiveLocalExtension · StrongBundle.mixedLscAt_retractNorm⟧: $N'$ is lower semicontinuous along mixed convergent sequences $w_k \to w$ with $P(w)$ in the chart, provided $N$ is lower semicontinuous along mixed convergent sequences over a set $A$ containing the image of $\rho$. *Second term.* The fibre coordinates satisfy $h_k \rightharpoonup h$ in $F_1$, so $h_k - A(u_k)h_k \rightharpoonup h - A(u)h$ by the two facts, and the norm of a reflexive space is weakly lower semicontinuous. *First term.* The vectors $\Phi[1]^{-1}(u_k, A(u_k)h_k)$ lie over $\rho(P(w_k)) \in \partial X$, converge on level $0$ and are bounded on level $1$ in one chart, so they are mixed convergent; the lower semicontinuity of $N$ over $\partial X$ applies. The liminf of a sum is at least the sum of the liminfs. The set $A$ is a parameter, so the lemma serves any ∂-extension step, not only $A = \partial X$.

**The local step** ⟦Chapter12/P3W3K_ReflexiveLocalExtension · StrongBundle.exists_reflexiveLocalExtension_of_isTame⟧: on a tame M-polyfold with a strong bundle with reflexive $1$-fibres, a norm $N$ over $\partial X$ that is continuous, a fibre seminorm, satisfies condition (2) for sequences in $\partial X$ and is lower semicontinuous under mixed convergence inside $\partial X$ has, at every $x_0 \in \partial X$, a local auxiliary norm $M$ on an open $V \ni x_0$, mixed lower semicontinuous at every vector over $V$, with $M = N$ over $V \cap \partial X$. $M$ is the norm $N'$ of §XII.15 in a chart with reflexive $F_1$; that it is a local auxiliary norm agreeing with $N$ on the boundary is §XII.15, and its lower semicontinuity is the inspection. Tameness enters only through the retraction onto the boundary of §XII.15. On the ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter12/P3W3K_ReflexiveLocalExtension · EpStrongBundle.hasReflexiveLocalExtensions_of_isTame⟧, this is the hypothesis of §XII.17 for every tame $X$, applied in the object M-polyfold.

**Theorem 12.2.13** (explicit) ⟦Chapter12/P3W3K_ReflexiveLocalExtension · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_2_13⟧: for a tame ep-groupoid $X$ with paracompact $|X|$, a strong bundle with reflexive $1$-fibres, and a reflexive auxiliary norm $N$ over $\partial X$, there is a reflexive auxiliary norm $\tilde N$ with $\tilde N = N$ over $\partial X$. The proof is one line: the global part of §XII.17 with its local hypothesis discharged by the local step. *Explicit:* paracompactness of $|X|$ is not printed in the statement; the proof's "partitions of unity, as in Theorem 12.2.11" takes it from Theorem 12.2.11, and Theorem 12.2.7, whose construction is reused, states it. *A reading*, as in wave 2: "reflexive auxiliary norm for $W_{0,1}|\partial X$" asks lower semicontinuity only for mixed convergent sequences inside $\partial X$; the proof needs no more, since the first term of $N'$ is evaluated over $\rho(\cdot) \in \partial X$. The hypotheses together are satisfiable ⟦Chapter12/P3W3K_ReflexiveLocalExtension · TrivialBundle.theorem_12_2_13_witness⟧: the trivial bundle $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k$ over the tame trivial ep-groupoid of $\mathbb R^n$, with a reflexive auxiliary norm over its boundary.

### XII.23 The last sentence of Theorem 12.5.3 (2017: 12.11), the chart-level half: push-forwards carried along a local strong bundle isomorphism

**What is carried.** Let $L$ be a local strong bundle isomorphism from a bundle $Y \to U$ to a bundle $Y' \to U'$ over an sc-diffeomorphism $\phi$, with $f = \Psi \circ f' \circ \phi$ on $U$, the text's "$\hat\Phi$ maps $f$ to $f'$". Part I's push-forward of an orientation along a path $\gamma$ (§6.6, Part VI) is defined in one chart: it stabilizes the linearizations along the path by an sc⁺-section $S$ of the pull-back bundle over $[0, 1] \times$ (the path's parameter space), takes the stabilized kernels, and transports the orientation of their determinant line. Each ingredient is carried from the chart $c$ of $Y'$ along $\phi \circ \gamma$ to the transported chart $c_T$ of $Y$ along $\gamma$.

**The stabilizing section** ⟦Chapter12/P3W3O_SectionPull · StrongBundle.LocalIso.exists_pullSection⟧: an sc⁺-section $S'$ of the pull-back of $Y'$ gives an sc⁺-section $S$ of the pull-back of $Y$ whose principal part in $c_T$ is $\beta \cdot S'$ read in $c$, for a cut-off $\beta$ with support in the domain of $c_T$. The cut-off is needed because $S'$ composed with $L$ is defined only over the image of the chart, and an sc⁺-section must be global. On the set where $\beta = 1$, principal parts and linearizations in $c_T$ are those in $c$, also for $f + S$ ⟦Chapter12/P3W3O_StabTransfer · StrongBundle.LocalIso.principal_transportChart_eq⟧.

**The kernels and the push-forward.** *Stabilized kernels* ⟦Chapter12/P3W3O_StabTransfer · StrongBundle.LocalIso.isStabKernels_mpull⟧: if $(f', S', s')$ stabilizes along $\phi \circ \gamma$ in $c$, the carried data stabilize along $\gamma$ in $c_T$. The pulled-back chart points of §XII.20 act on orientations by conjugation ⟦Chapter12/P3W3O_StabTransfer · StrongBundle.LocalIso.morPull_apply⟧, compatibly with the orientation rays of the stabilized kernels ⟦Chapter12/P3W3O_StabTransfer · StrongBundle.LocalIso.orRay_mpull⟧ and with the push-forward of Part I ⟦Chapter12/P3W3O_StabTransfer · StrongBundle.LocalIso.push_mpull⟧: pushing forward and then pulling back is pulling back and then pushing forward. Conjugation by identity maps leaves line orientations unchanged ⟦Chapter12/P3W3O_StabTransfer · LineOrientation.conj_refl_apply⟧. Zeros of $f' + S'$ at $\phi(x)$ are zeros of $f + S$ at $x$ ⟦Chapter12/P3W3O_PushPull · StrongBundle.LocalIso.isZeroAt_of_transportChart⟧.

**The chart-level statement** ⟦Chapter12/P3W3O_PushPull · StrongBundle.LocalIso.isPush_mpull⟧: if $e'$ is a push-forward of $f'$ along $\phi \circ \gamma$ in a chart $c_0$ of $Y'$ restricted to an open $W$, then the conjugate of $e'$ by the pulled-back chart points at the two ends is a push-forward of $f$ along $\gamma$ in the transported chart. The proof assembles the four steps above: the carried section stabilizes, the carried kernels are the stabilized kernels, and the orientation transport commutes with the conjugation. The hypotheses are those of §§XII.10–XII.20 (sc⁺-sections through smooth fibre points for both bundles, $f = \Psi \circ f' \circ \phi$, Part I's paracompactness instances for its push-forwards), and proof data: the chart $c_0$, the open $W$ and a cut-off equal to $1$ on the transported $c_0|W$. **The rest** of G.138 is proved in wave 5 (§XII.25): the comparison with Part I's local transports on short paths, for any charts, and a dyadic subdivision of the path, which gives the continuity of carried orientation sections.

Paracompactness of $|X|$ in Theorem 12.2.13 is made explicit, not added: the proof takes it from Theorem 12.2.11; witness `TrivialBundle.theorem_12_2_13_witness`. The hypothesis `HasReflexiveLocalExtensions` of §XII.17 is now discharged for every tame $X$, so the wave-2 form remains only as the global part. *§XII.23.* Hypotheses of step lemmas, not of book statements: sc⁺-sections through smooth fibre points for both bundles (§XII.10's standing hypothesis; witness from bump functions); $f = \Psi \circ f' \circ \phi$ on $U$, the text's "$\hat\Phi$ maps $f$ to $f'$" (witness: $f$ defined by this formula, as in §XII.20); the chart, the open set and the cut-off, which are proof data that the missing step (a) constructs; Part I's paracompactness instances on $\mathbb R^n \times X$, which hold for metrizable $X$.

### XII.25 The last sentence of Theorem 12.5.3 (2017: 12.11): morphisms keep orientation sections continuous

**Continuity of orientations is local** (extra), a Part I fact the text uses without comment ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_PathInduction · isContOrOn_of_local_or⟧: for any of Part I's local transports $L$ and an open $U$, if every smooth point of $U$ has an open neighbourhood $V$ over which the orientation section $o$ is continuous for $L$, then $o$ is continuous over $U$. Part I's continuity over $U$ asks that $o$ propagate along every sc-smooth path in $U$, and a path in $U$ need not lie in any one $V$. *Dyadic induction* ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_PathInduction · scPath_induction_or⟧: a property of sc-smooth paths that holds for all paths whose image lies in one set of an open cover, and passes from the two halves of a path to the whole path, holds for every path; the image of a path is compact, so the cover has a Lebesgue number, and after finitely many halvings every piece is small. The halves are reparametrized to sc-smooth paths by the smooth transition function, so that the reparametrized path is constant near its ends ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_PathInduction · smoothTransPath_or⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_PathInduction · isScSmoothMap_smoothTransPath_or⟧, and propagation along a path is propagation along its halves, by Part I's transport cocycle. Continuity passes to open subsets and to sections with the same values ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_PathInduction · IsContOrOn.mono_or⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_PathInduction · IsContOrOn.congr_or⟧.

**The orientation map of a local isomorphism.** Let $L$ be a local strong bundle isomorphism from $Y \to U$ to $Y' \to U'$ over $\phi$, with $f = \Psi \circ f' \circ \phi$ on $U$. Conjugation by the pulled-back chart points of §XII.20 gives, at each $a \in U$, a bijection $\mathrm{Or}^{f'}_{\phi(a)} \to \mathrm{Or}^f_a$ ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_LocalComm · StrongBundle.LocalIso.orxVia⟧, and an orientation section $o'$ of $f'$ is pulled back to $a \mapsto \mathrm{orxVia}_a(o'_{\phi(a)})$ ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_LocalComm · StrongBundle.LocalIso.pullOrx⟧. *It commutes with transport* ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_LocalComm · StrongBundle.LocalIso.orxVia_comm⟧: for every sc-smooth path $\gamma$ in $U$ between smooth points, Part I's transport along $\phi \circ \gamma$ followed by $\mathrm{orxVia}$ at the end equals $\mathrm{orxVia}$ at the start followed by the transport along $\gamma$. On short paths ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_LocalComm · StrongBundle.LocalIso.orxVia_comm_local⟧, Part I's transport is a push-forward in one chart (property (∗) of Part I's local transport), and wave 3's chart-level statement (§XII.23) carries it along $L$; the cut-off it needs is built here from the bump functions, equal to $1$ near the compact image of the path, and the change between the chart of the transport and the transported chart is Part I's transfer cocycle. For arbitrary paths in $U$ the dyadic induction joins the short pieces. *Continuity* ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_LocalComm · StrongBundle.LocalIso.isContOrOn_pullOrx⟧: if $o'$ is continuous over an open $V'$, then the pulled-back section is continuous over $U \cap \phi^{-1}(V')$; propagation along a path $\gamma$ there is propagation of $o'$ along $\phi \circ \gamma$, conjugated, by the commutation, and locality reduces to paths inside $U$. The converse holds as well ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_EquivCont · StrongBundle.LocalIso.isContOrOn_of_pullOrx⟧: if the pulled-back section is continuous over $U \cap \phi^{-1}(V')$, then $o'$ is continuous over $U' \cap V'$, since $\phi$ is an sc-diffeomorphism and paths in $U'$ come from paths in $U$. *Germs* ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Germ · StrongBundle.LocalIso.GermEq⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Germ · StrongBundle.LocalIso.morVia_germ⟧: two local isomorphisms whose base and bundle maps agree near $a$ have the same orientation map at $a$, because the pulled-back chart points, the transfers and the linearizations depend only on germs ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Germ · StrongBundle.LocalIso.mmorT_germ⟧ ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Germ · StrongBundle.LocalIso.mmorK_germ⟧. Two sheets through one morphism have the same local inverse of $t$ near its target ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Germ · EpGroupoid.Sheet.tgtInv_eq_near_or⟧.

**Theorem 12.5.3, last sentence** (narrower, by Part I's hypotheses only) ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Theorem1253 · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_5_3_push⟧: let $X$ be tame with bump functions on the objects, $f$ an sc-Fredholm section functor with tame germ data, $\sigma : x \to x'$ a morphism between smooth points, and $o$ an orientation section continuous over an open $V \ni x$. Then there is an open $V' \ni x'$ over which the section carried by the local isomorphism of $\sigma$ is continuous, and its value at $x'$ is $\sigma_*o_x$. The text's $\hat\Phi$ is read as the local strong bundle isomorphism of the sheet of $\sigma$ (§XII.10), from the target side to the source side; it maps $f$ to $f$ because $f$ is a functor ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Theorem1253 · EpStrongBundle.eqOn_morIso_of_functor⟧. *Proof.* The carried section is the pull-back of $o$ along that isomorphism, so continuity over $t(\text{sheet}) \cap \phi^{-1}(V)$ is the continuity statement above ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Theorem1253 · EpStrongBundle.theorem_12_5_3_push_hyp⟧, the form with Part I's paracompactness instances, which are discharged for metrizable spaces. At every point $y'$ of the target of the sheet, the carried value is $\sigma'_*o_{s(\sigma')}$ for the morphism $\sigma'$ of the sheet over $y'$ ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Germ · EpStrongBundle.pullOrx_morIso_eq_orMor⟧: the isomorphism of the sheet and that of $\sigma'$ have the same germ at $y'$ ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Germ · EpStrongBundle.germEq_morIso_sheet⟧; at $x'$ this is $\sigma_*o_x$ ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Theorem1253 · EpStrongBundle.pullOrx_morIso_tgt⟧. "Continuous local section" is read as Part I's continuity of orientations over an open set, whose section $y \mapsto (y, o_y)$ is continuous for Part I's topology. The hypotheses are those of the topological part of the theorem (§XII.11): bump functions and tame germ data, inherited from Part I's Theorem 6.6.17 (G.140), and sc⁺-sections through smooth fibre points, which bump functions give.

### XII.26 Proposition 12.5.6 (2017: 12.4) (⇐) with continuity

**Two facts about a two-to-one $|\sigma|$.** If $|\sigma| : |O_f| \to |X_\infty|$ is two-to-one, two orientations at $x$ with the same class in $|O_f|$ are equal ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Orientable · EpStrongBundle.eq_of_quot_eq_of_isTwoToOne⟧: the fibre of $\sigma$ over $x$ has two points, and if they had the same class the fibre of $|\sigma|$ over $|x|$ would have one. Hence the isotropy group fixes the orientations at $x$ ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Orientable · EpStrongBundle.orMor_isotropy_of_isTwoToOne⟧: $g_*\mathfrak o$ and $\mathfrak o$ have the same class.

**Morphisms near a point fix a continuous orientation** ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Orientable · EpStrongBundle.exists_nhds_orMor_eq_hyp⟧: if $|\sigma|$ is two-to-one and $\hat o$ is continuous near $x_0$, there is an open $V \ni x_0$ such that every morphism $\varphi : z \to y$ between smooth points of $V$ maps $\hat o_z$ to $\hat o_y$. *Proof.* Take a natural representation of $G_{x_0}$ on $U(x_0)$ inside the domain of $\hat o$ (Theorem 7.1.13); every morphism between points of $U(x_0)$ is $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$ for a unique $g \in G_{x_0}$. For each of the finitely many $g$, §XII.25 carries $\hat o$ along the sheet of $g$ to a section continuous near $x_0$ whose value at $x_0$ is $g_*\hat o_{x_0} = \hat o_{x_0}$, by the fixed-point fact. Near $x_0$ every smooth point is joined to $x_0$ by an sc-smooth path inside the domains of both sections, and both propagate along it from the same value, so they agree there. Let $V$ be $U(x_0)$ intersected, over $g$, with these neighbourhoods and with the points whose $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$ lies in the sheet of $g$. For $\varphi : z \to y$ in $V$, $\varphi = \Gamma(g, z)$ lies in the sheet of $g$, and the carried value at $y$ is $\varphi_*\hat o_z$ (§XII.25), which equals $\hat o_y$. *Openness* ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Orientable · EpStrongBundle.isOpen_orSat_hyp⟧: for $\hat o$ continuous over $V$, the preimage in $O_f$ of the set of classes $|(z, \hat o_z)|$, $z \in V$, is open for Part I's topology: near a point $(y, \varphi_*\hat o_z)$ of it, the section carried along the sheet of $\varphi$ is continuous by §XII.25, its basic open set is open, and its points are again of the form $(y', \varphi'_*\hat o_{z'})$.

**Proposition 12.5.6, (⇐)** (narrower, by Part I's hypotheses only) ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Orientable · EpStrongBundle.proposition_12_5_6_mpr_hyp⟧: under the hypotheses of Theorem 12.5.3, if $|\sigma|$ is two-to-one and has a continuous section $s$, for the quotient topologies on $|O_f|$ and $|X_\infty|$ and Part I's topology on $O_f$, then there is an orientation $o$ in the sense of Definition 12.5.4, continuous and invariant, with $|(x, o_x)| = s(|x|)$. *Proof.* Wave 1's invariant lift $o$ (§XII.11) is the candidate; it remains to show that $x \mapsto (x, o_x)$ is continuous at every smooth $x_0$. Part I gives a continuous orientation $\hat o$ near $x_0$ with $\hat o_{x_0} = o_{x_0}$, and the lemma gives $V$. The set $A$ of classes $|(z, \hat o_z)|$, $z \in V$, is open in $|O_f|$ by the openness just proved, and contains $s(|x_0|)$; by continuity of $s$, every smooth $y \in V$ near $x_0$ has $s(|y|) \in A$, so $s(|y|) = |(w, \hat o_w)|$ for some $w \in V$. Since $s(|y|) = |(y, o_y)|$, a morphism $\varphi : w \to y$ maps $\hat o_w$ to $o_y$; by the lemma it maps $\hat o_w$ to $\hat o_y$. So $o = \hat o$ near $x_0$, and the section of $\hat o$ is continuous for Part I's topology. The form with Part I's instance arguments ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Orientable · EpStrongBundle.proposition_12_5_6_mpr_hyp'⟧. *Narrower* only by Part I's hypotheses (G.140); the topology of $O_f$ is Part I's, which Theorem 12.5.3 shows is the only one with its properties.

### XII.27 Theorem 12.5.7 (2017: 12.12) (2): the push-forward is continuous

**One equivalence, both directions.** Let $h : V \to W$ be a strong bundle equivalence over $\phi$ with $f'' = h^*f$ (§XII.20). Its orientation bijection at $b$ is the orientation map of the local isomorphism of $h$ at any $a$ near which $b$ lies ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Germ · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.orEqv_eq_orxVia⟧, by the germ lemma, since the local isomorphisms at $a$ and at $b$ have the same germ at $b$ ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_Germ · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.germEq_locIso⟧. So the pull-back of orientations along $h$ is, near $a$, the pull-back of §XII.25 ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_EquivCont · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.pullOr_eq_pullOrx⟧. *Pull-back* ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_EquivCont · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isContOrOn_pullOr_hyp⟧: an orientation of $f$ continuous over $V'$ pulls back to one of $f''$ continuous over $\phi^{-1}(V')$, by §XII.25 and locality. *Push-forward* ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_EquivCont · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.isContOrOn_pushOr_hyp⟧: the push-forward of an invariant orientation of $f''$ that is continuous on all of $V$ is continuous on all of $X$. Near a point $\phi(a)$, it is the converse of §XII.25 applied to the local isomorphism at $a$; near an arbitrary $x$, choose a morphism $\phi(a) \to x$ (essential surjectivity) and apply the last sentence of Theorem 12.5.3 (§XII.25), the push-forward being invariant; locality joins the neighbourhoods.

**Theorem 12.5.7 (2)** (narrower) ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_EquivCont · theorem_12_5_7_two_hyp⟧: for a representative $W \xleftarrow{h_1} V \xrightarrow{h_2} W'$ with Part I's hypotheses on $X$, $X'$ and the base of $V$, an invariant orientation $o$ of $f$ that is continuous over all of $X$ has exactly one invariant $o'$ corresponding to it (§XII.20), and $o'$ is continuous over all of $X'$: pull back along $h_1$, push forward along $h_2$. The form without instance arguments ⟦Chapter12/P3W5OR_EquivCont · theorem_12_5_7_two_cont⟧. *Narrower*: "continuous" is read, for input and output, as Part I's continuity of orientations over all of $X$, from which the continuity of $x \mapsto (x, o_x)$ in Definition 12.5.4 follows; the converse implication, the homeomorphism of (1), and the independence of the representative and functoriality are gap G.158 (§XII.13). The hypotheses are Part I's, as in §XII.25, for the three bases.

### XII.28 Witnesses and the hypotheses of wave 5

**Hypotheses taken.** *§§XII.25–XII.27.* No hypothesis outside Part I's standing ones is added to a book statement: $X$ tame, bump functions on the objects and tame germ data, the hypotheses of Part I's Theorem 6.6.17 inherited exactly as in the topological part of Theorem 12.5.3 (G.140), for $X$, $X'$ and $V$ in Theorem 12.5.7; sc⁺-sections through smooth fibre points, §12.5's standing hypothesis, which bump functions give (`MPolyfold.AdmitsBumpFunctions.hasScPlusSectionsThrough`); Part I's paracompactness instances for its transports, which hold for metrizable spaces and are discharged inside `theorem_12_5_3_push`, `proposition_12_5_6_mpr_hyp` and `theorem_12_5_7_two_cont`. Step lemmas take $f = \Psi \circ f' \circ \phi$ on $U$, the text's "$\hat\Phi$ maps $f$ to $f'$", discharged for morphisms by functoriality (`eqOn_morIso_of_functor`) and for equivalences by the pull-back; in general it holds for $f$ defined by the formula. Continuity hypotheses on orientations are satisfiable by Part I's existence of continuous local orientations. No hypothesis quantifies over all charts.

**Every definition has a witness.** Germ equality of local isomorphisms: reflexivity. Pulled-back orientation sections: those of any continuous orientation, for instance from Part I's Theorem 6.6.17 near a point.

## Part XIII. Sc⁺-multisections (HWZ Chapter 13, §§13.1–13.5)

Chapter 13 (Springer 2021, pp. 599–635; 2017 numbers in parentheses) builds the perturbations of the Fredholm theory on ep-groupoids. §13.1 constructs good systems of neighbourhoods, in which every neighbourhood carries the natural action of its isotropy group and the morphisms between two neighbourhoods fall into components on which source and target are sc-diffeomorphisms (Lemma 13.1.1, Definition 13.1.2, Proposition 13.1.3, Definitions 13.1.4, 13.1.5, Lemma 13.1.6, Theorems 13.1.7, 13.1.8, Proposition 13.1.9 (2017: Lemma 13.1, Definition 13.1, Proposition 13.1, Definitions 13.2, 13.3, Lemma 13.2, Theorems 13.1, 13.2, Proposition 13.2)). §13.2 defines sc⁺-multisections, their supports, symmetric section structures and their algebra (Definitions 13.2.1–13.2.5, Lemma 13.2.6, Definitions 13.2.7–13.2.10, Lemma 13.2.11, Definition 13.2.12, Lemma 13.2.13 (2017: Definitions 13.4–13.8, Lemma 13.3, Definitions 13.9–13.12, Lemma 13.4, Definition 13.13, Lemma 13.5)). §13.3 structures them (structurable sc⁺-multisections), §13.4 relates them along equivalences and coverings, and §13.5 constructs them. This Part retells §13.1 (§§XIII.1–XIII.5) and the functor-level part of §13.2 (§§XIII.6–XIII.9); then the witnesses (§XIII.10), what is not formalized (§XIII.11) and what the formalization taught us (§XIII.12), then, in wave 2, Theorem 13.1.7 as printed (§XIII.13), decorated sc⁺-multisections and their algebra (§§XIII.14–XIII.15), §13.3 (§§XIII.16–XIII.18) and atomic sc⁺-multisections (§§XIII.19–XIII.20), and, in waves 3 and 4, Proposition 13.3.19 (§XIII.21), Theorem 13.5.3 (§XIII.22), the pull-backs and push-forwards of §13.4 (§§XIII.23–XIII.24), commensurable sums (§XIII.25), Theorem 13.5.7 (§XIII.26) and the witnesses of waves 3 and 4 (§XIII.27), then, in wave 5, Proposition 13.4.2 (§XIII.28) and the witnesses of wave 5 (§XIII.29).

**What is proved, and what is not.** Waves 1–5 of Part III (2026-11-13) formalize Chapter 13. *§13.1.* Everything is proved. Lemma 13.1.1 is proved in a stronger form, without the invariance of $V$ (§XIII.1). Definition 13.1.2 is formalized with "carries the natural $G_x$-action" read as an invariant open subset of the domain of a natural representation (§XIII.1). Proposition 13.1.3 holds as printed in that reading, and Definition 13.1.4 is formalized (§XIII.2). Definition 13.1.5, the natural bi-action, is formalized with its laws and its sc-smoothness, and Lemma 13.1.6 is proved in a stronger form (§XIII.3). Theorem 13.1.7 is proved as printed, with properness read in the full subcategory on the open set $Q$ (§XIII.13; gap G.141 is closed), and in a stronger form that reads properness in $X$ and needs neither $Q$ open nor $\operatorname{cl}_XU(q) \subset Q$ (§XIII.4). Theorem 13.1.8 is proved as printed (§XIII.4), and Proposition 13.1.9 in a stronger form, uniqueness holding among all maps (§XIII.5). *§13.2.* Definition 13.2.1 is Chapter 11's (Part XI, §XI.11). Definitions 13.2.2–13.2.4 and the claims after them are proved (§XIII.6). Definition 13.2.5 is formalized and Lemma 13.2.6 proved (§XIII.7). Definitions 13.2.9 and 13.2.10 and Lemmas 13.2.11 and 13.2.13 are proved at the level of functors with local section structures (§§XIII.8–XIII.9) and, in wave 2, at the level of decorated sc⁺-multisections: Definitions 13.2.7 and 13.2.8 are formalized, and the sum, the scalar multiples, the products with functions and the locally finite sums are decorated and compatible with the equivalence (§§XIII.14–XIII.15); gap G.142 is closed. The remark that there are in general no inverses is proved by an example (§XIII.15); gap G.143 is closed. In Definition 13.2.9 and Lemma 13.2.13 the intersection $U'(x) \cap U''(x)$ is read as a neighbourhood inside it carrying one natural action for both structures. *§13.3.* Definitions 13.3.1, 13.3.2, Example 13.3.3, Definition 13.3.4 and Remark 13.3.5 (correspondences) are formalized and proved, Definition 13.3.2 with its action laws (§XIII.16). Definitions 13.3.6, 13.3.8, 13.3.10, 13.3.11 and Remark 13.3.7 are formalized, Proposition 13.3.12 is proved, Lemma 13.3.14 as printed, and Remark 13.3.13 in its positive half (§XIII.17). The construction before Proposition 13.3.15 is proved with the compatibility the text does not check, Proposition 13.3.15 with bijections in place of equalities of index sets, Definition 13.3.17 and Corollary 13.3.18 as printed (§XIII.18). Proposition 13.3.19, locally finite sums of structurable sc⁺-multisections, is proved as printed for a nonempty family, with the product of correspondences the text leaves to the reader written out; the empty family needs a good system, which paracompactness of $|X|$ supplies (§XIII.21); gap G.148 is closed. Remarks 13.3.9 and 13.3.16 are prose. *§13.4.* Theorem 13.4.1 is proved in a stronger form: the canonical structure on $\Phi^*\Lambda'$ is a map of structured classes, independent of the representative and of the adapted good system (§XIII.23). Theorem 13.4.4 is proved as printed by the same construction, with the same canonicity (§XIII.23). Theorem 13.4.3 is proved as printed, directly, without Proposition 13.4.2; push-forwards and pull-backs along generalized strong bundle isomorphisms preserve structurability (§XIII.24). Proposition 13.4.2 is proved in wave 5, restated: the project has no strong bundle over an open sub-ep-groupoid, so "$\Lambda$ structured on $W|V$" is read as structured data relative to $V$, and "canonical" as uniqueness among the functors on $W$ that extend $\Lambda$; both clauses hold with no added hypothesis (§XIII.28); gap G.163 is closed. Definition 13.4.5 is formalized, its sum and its locally finite sum as printed, with the "evident" well-definedness proved (§XIII.25). *§13.5.* Definition 13.5.1 is formalized, and read also on neighbourhoods with the natural action (§§XIII.19, XIII.26); Theorems 13.5.4 and 13.5.6 are proved, narrower only through the pointwise reading of bump functions and otherwise stronger; Theorem 13.5.5 is proved as printed for existence and uniqueness (with $I \ne \emptyset$, which the text presupposes) (§XIII.19). Theorem 13.5.3 and the last clause of Theorem 13.5.5, that atomic sc⁺-multisections are structurable, are proved with the added hypothesis that a good system exists, which is necessary, since a structurable multisection carries one, and which holds for paracompact $|X|$ (§XIII.22); gap G.149 is closed. Theorem 13.5.7 is proved in a stronger form: for every structured lift, without the paracompactness of $|X|$ (§XIII.26). Remark 13.5.2 is prose. *Open:* no gap of Chapter 13. No statement of Chapter 13 was found not to hold as we read it.

**Three structural choices.** (1) *Neighbourhoods with the natural action.* The project's natural representation of $G_x$ (Theorem 7.1.13) has a connected domain; the invariant subsets of §13.1 need not be connected. A neighbourhood with the natural action is therefore a natural representation together with an open $U \ni x$ inside its domain, invariant under every $\Phi(g)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.NatNbhd⟧. In this reading every claim of §13.1 that an invariant open subset carries the natural action holds as printed. (2) *Components named by a point.* A component of $\mathcal U(x, x')$ is the connected component in $\mathcal U(x, x')$ of one of its morphisms, and empty if the morphism is not in $\mathcal U(x, x')$; so no statement needs a separate index set of components. (3) *Multisections as functors.* §13.2 is formalized for functors $\Lambda : W \to \mathbb Q^+$ satisfying Chapter 11's predicate of sc⁺-multisection, with local section structures on open sets ⟦Chapter11/MultisectionLocalStructure2021 · SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisection⟧ ⟦Chapter11/MultisectionLocalStructure2021 · SBLocalization.IsLocalRepOn⟧; the decorations $[\Lambda, \mathcal U, \mathcal S]$ wait for wave 2. The local section structures of a sum, a multiple and a locally finite sum are proved, which is the content of the decorations.

**Map.**

Throughout, $X$ is an ep-groupoid with source and target maps $s$, $t$, $\pi : X \to |X|$ the orbit map, and $\mathcal U(x, x') = \{\varphi : s(\varphi) \in U(x),\ t(\varphi) \in U(x')\}$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.morBetween⟧. In §§XIII.6–XIII.9, $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ is a strong bundle and $\Lambda : W \to \mathbb Q^+$.

### XIII.1 Lemma 13.1.1 (2017: 13.1) and Definition 13.1.2 (2017: 13.1)

**Lemma 13.1.1** (stronger) ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.lemma_13_1_1⟧. Let $U(x)$ carry the natural action, with $t : s^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}U(x)) \to X$ proper, and $V \subset U(x)$. Then $\operatorname{cl}_XV \subset U(x)$ iff $\operatorname{cl}_{|X|}|V| \subset |U(x)|$. The text assumes $V$ invariant; that form follows ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.lemma_13_1_1_book⟧. *(⇒)* uses only properness: $\pi(\operatorname{cl}V) = \operatorname{cl}\pi(V)$ for a set with proper closure (Proposition 7.1.10). *(⇐)* uses only the natural action. A point $y \in \operatorname{cl}V$ has $|y| \in |U(x)|$, so there is a morphism between $y$ and a point of $U(x)$; along it, the points of $V$ near $y$ are carried by morphisms between points of $U(x)$, each of the form $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$, and by pigeonhole over the finite $G_x$ one $g$ occurs along a sequence converging to $y$, which places $y$ in $U(x)$. Inside every open $W \ni x$ there is a neighbourhood with the natural action and proper closure ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.exists_natNbhd_isProperSubset⟧.

**Definition 13.1.2** (restated) ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem⟧: a family of neighbourhoods $U(x)$ with the natural action (2), with $t : s^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}U(x)) \to X$ proper (1), and such that (3) for every component $\Sigma$ of $\mathcal U(x, x')$, $s|_\Sigma$ and $t|_\Sigma$ are sc-diffeomorphisms onto their images ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.IsDiffeoComponent⟧. The images are open automatically. For an open component, (3) is the injectivity of $s$ and of $t$ on it, since both are local sc-diffeomorphisms ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.isDiffeoComponent_iff_injOn⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.isScDiffeoOn_invFunOn⟧. The inverses $(s|_\Sigma)^{-1}$ are functions on the objects ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.srcInv⟧.

### XIII.2 Proposition 13.1.3 (2017: 13.1) and Definition 13.1.4 (2017: 13.2)

**Proposition 13.1.3** ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.proposition_13_1_3⟧: if $(U(x))$ is a good system and $\tilde U(x) \subset U(x)$ are invariant open neighbourhoods, then $(\tilde U(x))$ is a good system, with the same natural representations ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.restrict⟧. (2) holds in the reading of structural choice (1); under the reading "natural action on a connected domain" $\tilde U(x)$ could fail to be such a domain. (1) passes to the smaller set because a closed subset of a set with proper closure has proper closure. (3) passes because a component of $\mathcal U$ for smaller sets lies in a component for the larger ones, on which $s$ and $t$ are injective ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.isDiffeoComponent_of_subset⟧. *The step after the proposition.* Inside $U(x) \cap V(x)$ there is an invariant open neighbourhood, the largest invariant open subset ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.NatNbhd.invariantCore⟧, so every good system has a refinement inside any family of open neighbourhoods ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.exists_refinement_subset⟧.

**Definition 13.1.4** ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.IsRefinement⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.IsSubordinate⟧: $\mathcal W$ refines $\mathcal U$ if $W(x) \subset U(x)$ for all $x$; $\mathcal U$ is subordinate to an open cover if each $U(x)$ lies in a member. Restrictions are refinements ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.isRefinement_restrict⟧.

### XIII.3 Definition 13.1.5 (2017: 13.3) and Lemma 13.1.6 (2017: 13.2)

**Definition 13.1.5** (restated) ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.biact⟧. The text names the map $G_{x'} \times \mathcal U(x, x') \times G_x \to \mathcal U(x, x')$; the formalization writes the formula that its proofs use: $g' * \varphi * g = \Gamma'(g', t(\varphi)) \circ \varphi \circ \Gamma(g, \Phi(g^{-1})(s(\varphi)))$, with source $\Phi(g^{-1})(s(\varphi))$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.src_biact⟧ and target $\Phi'(g')(t(\varphi))$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.tgt_biact⟧, again in $\mathcal U(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.biact_mem⟧. It is an action, $g' * (h' * \varphi * h) * g = (g'h') * \varphi * (hg)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.biact_biact⟧, of $G_{x'} \times G_x^{\mathrm{op}}$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.biactMulAction⟧, and each $\varphi \mapsto g' * \varphi * g$ is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.isScSmoothOn_biact⟧. On a good system ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.biact⟧ it maps components onto components ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.image_biact_comp⟧, as the text says before Lemma 13.1.6; inversion maps components of $\mathcal U(x, x')$ onto components of $\mathcal U(x', x)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.image_inv_comp⟧, and the components partition $\mathcal U(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.components⟧.

**Two tools.** Two morphisms of $\mathcal U(x, x')$ with the same source differ by a left factor $g'$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.exists_biact_left_of_src⟧, because their composite $\psi \circ \varphi^{-1}$ is a morphism between points of $U(x')$, hence $\Gamma'(g', \cdot)$; similarly with the same target and a right factor ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.exists_biact_right_of_tgt⟧.

**Lemma 13.1.6** (stronger). (1) If $\psi \in \Sigma$ and $g' * \psi \in \Sigma$ then $g' = 1$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.eq_one_of_biact_left_mem⟧: both have the same source, and $s$ is injective on $\Sigma$, so $g' * \psi = \psi$, and $g' = 1$ by left cancellation. The text's (1), $g' * \Sigma = \Sigma \Rightarrow g' = 1$, follows ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.lemma_13_1_6_one⟧. (2) is the same on the right ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.eq_one_of_biact_right_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.lemma_13_1_6_two⟧. (3) For two components, $s(\Sigma_1)$ and $s(\Sigma_2)$ are equal or disjoint ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.lemma_13_1_6_three_src⟧, and so are $t(\Sigma_1)$, $t(\Sigma_2)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.lemma_13_1_6_three_tgt⟧. If $s(\varphi_1) = s(\varphi_2)$ with $\varphi_i \in \Sigma_i$, then $\varphi_2 = g' * \varphi_1$, so $\Sigma_2 = g' * \Sigma_1$ and $s(\Sigma_2) = s(\Sigma_1)$. No membership hypotheses are needed, since the component of a morphism outside $\mathcal U(x, x')$ is empty.

### XIII.4 Theorems 13.1.7 and 13.1.8 (2017: 13.1 and 13.2): good systems exist

**Good on a set** ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.IsGoodOn⟧. A family of neighbourhoods with the natural action is good on $Q$ if for $q, q' \in Q$: $U(q) \subseteq Q$, $t : s^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}_XU(q)) \to X$ is proper, and (3) holds for $\mathcal U(q, q')$. The text asks for a good system of the full sub-ep-groupoid on the open set $Q$, whose properness is read in $Q$; here it is read in $X$. The natural actions and the sets $\mathcal U(q, q')$ are the same in $Q$ and in $X$, because $Q$ is open and the subcategory full.

**Transports** ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystemExistence · EpGroupoid.IsTransport⟧: a continuous injective choice $\sigma$ of morphisms on $U(y)$ with $t(\sigma(z)) = z$ and $s(\sigma(z)) \in U(q)$. Along transports $\sigma$, $\sigma'$ the map $\varphi \mapsto \sigma'(t\varphi)^{-1} \circ \varphi \circ \sigma(s\varphi)$ carries $\mathcal U(y, y')$ into $\mathcal U(q, q')$, so injectivity of $s$ and $t$ on components passes back ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystemExistence · EpGroupoid.injOn_comp_of_transport⟧.

**Theorem 13.1.7** (narrower) ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystemExistence · EpGroupoid.theorem_13_1_7⟧. Let $|Q| = |X|$, let the family $(U(q))_{q \in Q}$ be good on $Q$, and let $W(y) \ni y$ be open for $y \notin Q$. Then there is a good system of $X$ that keeps $U(q)$ for $q \in Q$ and has $U(y) \subset W(y)$ for $y \notin Q$. *Step 1, a transport at each $y \notin Q$* ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystemExistence · EpGroupoid.exists_transport_of_isGoodOn⟧. Choose a morphism $\psi$ from some $q_y \in Q$ to $y$, and an open $O \ni \psi$ on which $s$ and $t$ are injective ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystemExistence · EpGroupoid.exists_isOpen_injOn_src_tgt⟧ and $s(O) \subset U(q_y)$. Then $(t|_O)^{-1}$ is a transport on any neighbourhood $U(y)$ with the natural action and proper closure inside $W(y) \cap t(O)$ (§XIII.1). *Step 2.* The family is good on all of $X$ by the transports, and a family good on $X$ is a good system. The text's further smallness condition on the closures of $U(y)$ is not used, and neither is the openness of $Q$. That $Q$-properness implies $X$-properness when $|Q| = |X|$ is presumably true and is the gap of this Part (§XIII.11).

**Theorem 13.1.8** ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystemExistence · EpGroupoid.theorem_13_1_8⟧: if $|X|$ is paracompact, for every family of open $W(x) \ni x$ there is a good system with $U(x) \subset W(x)$. The text's "for all $\in X$" is read as "for all $x \in X$", presumably a dropped symbol. *Step 1.* Neighbourhoods $W'(x) \subset W(x)$ with the natural action and proper closure. *Step 2.* A locally finite open refinement $(\tilde V_a)$ of $(|W'(a)|)$, shrunk so that the closures are in it and still locally finite. *Step 3.* $V_a = \pi^{-1}(\tilde V_a) \cap W'(a)$ and $V = \bigcup_aV_a$, with $|V| = |X|$; by Lemma 13.1.1, $\operatorname{cl}V_a \subset W'(a)$, and the closures are locally finite. *Step 4, good on $V$.* Near each $x$ only finitely many $\operatorname{cl}V_a$ matter, and near a point there are finitely many morphisms out of a finite union of sets with proper closure ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystemExistence · EpGroupoid.exists_nhds_injOn_of_isProperSubset⟧; a small neighbourhood $U(x)$, $x \in V$, makes $s$ and $t$ injective on the components. *Step 5.* Theorem 13.1.7 extends the system from $V$ to $X$. Metrizability of $|X|$ is not used.

### XIII.5 Proposition 13.1.9 (2017: 13.2)

**Stabilizers and $D_\Sigma$.** For a component $\Sigma$ with $O = s(\Sigma)$, $G_{x,\Sigma} = \{g : g * O = O\}$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.stabSrc⟧ and $G_{x',\Sigma}$ with $t(\Sigma)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.stabTgt⟧. $D_\Sigma = t \circ (s|_\Sigma)^{-1} : s(\Sigma) \to t(\Sigma)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.D⟧ is an sc-diffeomorphism with inverse $s \circ (t|_\Sigma)^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.isScDiffeoOn_D⟧.

**Proposition 13.1.9** (stronger) ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.proposition_13_1_9⟧: there is a group isomorphism $g \mapsto g'(g)$, $G_{x,\Sigma} \to G_{x',\Sigma}$, with $(s|_\Sigma)^{-1}(g * z) = g'(g) * (s|_\Sigma)^{-1}(z) * g^{-1}$ for $z \in s(\Sigma)$, and every map with this property equals it. *Step 1, the partner.* For $g \in G_{x,\Sigma}$ and $\varphi \in \Sigma$, $\varphi * g^{-1}$ has source $g * s(\varphi) \in O$, so there is $\psi \in \Sigma$ with the same source, and $\psi = g' * \varphi * g^{-1}$ for some $g'$; by Lemma 13.1.6 (1) $g'$ is unique ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.partner⟧. *Step 2.* It does not depend on $\varphi$: the bi-action maps the component of $\varphi * g^{-1}$, which is $\Sigma * g^{-1}$, onto $\Sigma$, so the same $g'$ works for all of $\Sigma$. *Step 3.* $g \mapsto g'(g)$ is a homomorphism by the action law ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.partnerHom⟧, with inverse given by the same construction on $\Sigma^{-1}$; uniqueness holds among all maps by Lemma 13.1.6 (1). The text proves the identity through the smoothness of a map $\Theta_g$; the formal proof needs only Lemma 13.1.6 and the action laws. *Equivariance of $D_\Sigma$*: $\Phi'(g'(g)) \circ D_\Sigma = D_\Sigma \circ \Phi(g)$ on $s(\Sigma)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_BiAction · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.proposition_13_1_9_D⟧.

### XIII.6 Definitions 13.2.2–13.2.4 (2017: 13.5–13.7): supports, norms, triviality

$\Lambda : W \to \mathbb Q^+$ is an sc⁺-multisection in Chapter 11's sense: a functor with local section structures, finitely many local sc⁺-sections $s_i$ with weights $\sigma_i$ and $\Lambda(w) = \sum_{i : s_i(P(w)) = w}\sigma_i$ near each point (Definition 13.2.1, Part XI, §XI.11).

**Definition 13.2.2** ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.domSupp⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.supp⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.suppAt⟧: $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda) = \operatorname{cl}\{x : \exists w \in W_x,\ w \ne 0_x,\ \Lambda(w) > 0\}$, and $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda) = \{w : \Lambda(w) > 0\}$ with fibres $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda)(x)$. The claims after it are proved: $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda)(x)$ is $\{s_1(x), \dots, s_k(x)\}$ on the domain of a local structure ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.IsLocalRepOn.suppAt_eq⟧, hence finite ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisection.finite_suppAt⟧ and nonempty ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisection.suppAt_nonempty⟧, with weights summing to $1$ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisection.sum_suppAt⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisection.finsum_suppAt⟧; and $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda) = \operatorname{cl}P(\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda) \setminus 0_W)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.domSupp_eq_closure_image⟧.

**Definition 13.2.3** (restated) ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm⟧: $N(\Lambda)(x) = \max\{N(w) : w \in \operatorname{supp}(\Lambda)(x)\}$, written as a supremum ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.normW⟧ and shown to be attained ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisection.isGreatest_pointwiseNorm⟧. The values of sc⁺-sections lie in $W_{0,1}$, where $N$ is defined ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisection.suppAt_subset_oneSet⟧. For an auxiliary norm, $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda) = \operatorname{cl}\{N(\Lambda) > 0\}$ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisection.domSupp_eq_closure_pointwiseNorm⟧.

**Definition 13.2.4** ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.IsTrivialOn⟧: $\Lambda$ is trivial on $V$ if $\Lambda(0_x) = 1$ for $x \in V$; "and hence" $\Lambda(w) = 0$ for $w \ne 0_x$, because the weights over $x$ sum to $1$ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisection.apply_fiberZero_eq_one_iff⟧. $\operatorname{dom-supp}(\Lambda)$ is the smallest closed set off which $\Lambda$ is trivial ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisection.isLeast_domSupp⟧. The zero multisection is trivial everywhere ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSupport · SBLocalization.isTrivialOn_zeroMultisection⟧.

### XIII.7 Definition 13.2.5 (2017: 13.8) and Lemma 13.2.6 (2017: 13.3): symmetric structures

**Definition 13.2.5** (restated) ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSymmetric · SBLocalization.SymmetricStructure⟧: at $x$, the domain $U(x)$ of a natural representation of $G_x$ with the properness property; a finite index set $I_x$ with an action of $G_x$; sc⁺-sections $s_i$ on $U(x)$ with (1) $s_{g(i)}(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g, y), s_i(y))$ and (2) $\Lambda(w) = |I_x|^{-1}\#\{i : s_i(P(w)) = w\}$ over $U(x)$. "$G_x$-invariant with the natural action" is read here as the domain of a natural representation, the reading of Chapter 11; the index set lives in the universe of the isotropy groups.

**Lemma 13.2.6** ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSymmetric · SBLocalization.lemma_13_2_6⟧: every sc⁺-multisection admits a symmetric structure at every point. The proof is the text's, before Definition 13.2.5. *Step 1.* A local structure $(s_i, \sigma_i)$ near $x$, on the domain of a natural representation with the properness property (Theorem 7.1.13). *Step 2, equal weights.* Rational weights $\sigma_i = n_i/d_i$ are made equal by repeating $s_i$ $n_i\prod_{j \ne i}d_j$ times, with common weight $1/\prod_jd_j$ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSymmetric · SBLocalization.IsLocalRepOn.exists_equal_weights⟧; this is the text's $k_jq$. *Step 3, symmetrize.* $\hat I = I \times G_x$ with $s_{(i,g)}(z) = \mu(\Gamma(g, g^{-1} * z), s_i(g^{-1} * z))$ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSymmetric · SBLocalization.transportSection⟧ and $h \cdot (i, g) = (i, hg)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSymmetric · SBLocalization.prodIsotropyAction⟧. The transported sections are sc⁺ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionSymmetric · SBLocalization.isScPlusSectionOn_transportSection⟧, (1) is the action law of $\Gamma$, and (2) holds because $\Lambda$ is a functor, so each $g$ contributes the same count. Before transport the local sections are extended by $0$ off $U(x)$, so that they are functions on all objects ⟦Chapter13/P3M_ScPlusSectionOn · SBLocalization.extendZero⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_ScPlusSectionOn · SBLocalization.IsLocalRepOn.extendZero⟧.

### XIII.8 Definitions 13.2.9, 13.2.10 (2017: 13.11, 13.12) and Lemma 13.2.11 (2017: 13.4): the algebra, at functor level

**Convolution.** For finitely many $\Lambda_i$, $(\ast_i\Lambda_i)(w) = \sum_{(w_i) : \sum_iw_i = w}\prod_i\Lambda_i(w_i)$, the sum over tuples in the fibre of $w$ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionConvolution · SBLocalization.convAt⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionConvolution · SBLocalization.conv⟧; it is a functor ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionConvolution · SBLocalization.isWFunctor_conv⟧. If each $\Lambda_i$ has a local structure $(s^i_j, \sigma^i_j)$ on $O$, the convolution is given there by the sections $\sum_is^i_{j_i}$ with weights $\prod_i\sigma^i_{j_i}$ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionConvolution · SBLocalization.conv_eq_sum_of_isLocalRepOn⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionConvolution · SBLocalization.isLocalRepOn_conv⟧, which are sc⁺ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_ScPlusSectionOn · SBLocalization.IsScPlusSectionOn.sectionAdd⟧; so it is an sc⁺-multisection ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionConvolution · SBLocalization.isScPlusMultisection_conv⟧.

**Definition 13.2.9** (narrower: no decoration). (1) is $\Lambda' \oplus \Lambda''(w) = \sum_{w' + w'' = w}\Lambda'(w')\Lambda''(w'')$ verbatim ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionAlgebra · SBLocalization.multisectionAdd⟧, the convolution of two ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionAlgebra · SBLocalization.multisectionAdd_eq_conv⟧. It is an sc⁺-multisection ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionAlgebra · SBLocalization.definition_13_2_9⟧, and (2)–(3) hold for local structures: sections $s'_i + s''_j$ with weights $\sigma'_i\sigma''_j$ on a common domain ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionAlgebra · SBLocalization.multisectionAdd_eq_sum_of_isLocalRepOn⟧. $\oplus$ is commutative for all functions ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionAlgebra · SBLocalization.multisectionAdd_comm⟧ and associative on sc⁺-multisections ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionAlgebra · SBLocalization.multisectionAdd_assoc⟧, where the fibres are finitely supported.

**Definition 13.2.10** (narrower: no decoration) ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionAlgebra · SBLocalization.multisectionSmul⟧: $(0\Lambda)(0_x) = 1$, $(0\Lambda)(w) = 0$ for $w \ne 0$, so $0\Lambda$ is the zero multisection ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionAlgebra · SBLocalization.multisectionSmul_zero⟧; $(a\Lambda)(w) = \Lambda(w/a)$ for $a \ne 0$. It is an sc⁺-multisection ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionAlgebra · SBLocalization.definition_13_2_10⟧, locally given by the sections $as_i$ with the same weights ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionAlgebra · SBLocalization.multisectionSmul_eq_sum_of_isLocalRepOn⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_ScPlusSectionOn · SBLocalization.IsScPlusSectionOn.sectionSmul⟧.

**Lemma 13.2.11** ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionAlgebra · SBLocalization.lemma_13_2_11⟧: for an sc-smooth functor $\beta : X \to \mathbb R$ (sc-smooth on the objects and constant along morphisms, the text's hypotheses), $(\beta\Lambda)(w) = (\beta(P(w))\Lambda)(w)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionAlgebra · SBLocalization.multisectionSmulFun⟧ is an sc⁺-multisection, given near a point by the sections $\beta s_i$ with the weights $\sigma_i$: where $\beta \ne 0$ this is Definition 13.2.10 pointwise, and where $\beta = 0$ all $\beta s_i$ are $0$, with total weight $1$.

### XIII.9 Definition 13.2.12 (2017: 13.13) and Lemma 13.2.13 (2017: 13.5): locally finite sums

**Definition 13.2.12** ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionLocallyFinite · SBLocalization.IsLocallyFiniteFamily⟧: every $x$ has an open saturated $O(x)$ for which only finitely many $j$ have a $w \ne 0$ over $O(x)$ with $\Lambda_j(w) > 0$ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionLocallyFinite · SBLocalization.nontrivIdx⟧. The remark after it, that $O(x)$ can be chosen so that the index set does not change on smaller saturated neighbourhoods, is proved for open saturated $O' \ni x$, by taking an $O(x)$ whose index set has the fewest elements ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionLocallyFinite · SBLocalization.IsLocallyFiniteFamily.exists_stable⟧.

**Lemma 13.2.13** ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionLocallyFinite · SBLocalization.lemma_13_2_13⟧: the sum of a locally finite family of sc⁺-multisections is an sc⁺-multisection. The text does not write out $\bigoplus_j\Lambda_j$ for infinitely many $j$; it is read as the sum over finitely supported families $(w_j)$ in the fibre with $\sum_jw_j = w$ of $\prod_j\Lambda_j(w_j)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionLocallyFinite · SBLocalization.lfSum⟧, which for finite index sets is the convolution ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionLocallyFinite · SBLocalization.lfSum_eq_conv⟧. *Proof.* Over $O(x)$ an index outside the finite set $J_x$ contributes only $0$ with weight $\Lambda_j(0) = 1$, so there the sum equals the finite convolution over $J_x$ ⟦Chapter13/P3M_MultisectionLocallyFinite · SBLocalization.lfSum_eq_conv_of_mem⟧, which has a local structure by §XIII.8.

### XIII.10 Witnesses and the hypotheses

**Hypotheses taken.** None is added to a statement of the text. Lemma 13.1.1 drops the invariance of $V$; the form with it is kept. Theorem 13.1.7 reads the properness of the partial system in $X$ (§XIII.4). Lemma 13.2.11 assumes $\beta$ sc-smooth and constant along morphisms, the text's "sc-smooth functor"; the identity for $\operatorname{dom-supp}$ in Definition 13.2.3 assumes $N$ an auxiliary norm, as the text does.

**Every definition has a witness.** Good systems: every M-polyfold seen as a trivial ep-groupoid has one ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystemExistence · EpGroupoid.nonempty_goodSystem_trivial⟧ (through Theorem 13.1.8). Neighbourhoods with the natural action and proper closure: inside every open set (§XIII.1). Families good on a set: every good system is good on $X$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystem · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.isGoodOn⟧. Symmetric structures: Lemma 13.2.6. Triviality: the zero multisection (§XIII.6).

### XIII.11 What is not formalized

- *Closed in wave 2.* G.141, Theorem 13.1.7 with properness in the full subcategory on $Q$ (§XIII.13); G.142, decorated sc⁺-multisections and their algebra (§§XIII.14–XIII.15); G.143, no inverses (§XIII.15).
- *Closed in waves 3 and 4.* G.148, Proposition 13.3.19, with "locally finite domain supports" in the topological sense (§XIII.21); G.149, Theorem 13.5.3 and the last clause of Theorem 13.5.5 (§XIII.22).
- *Closed in wave 5.* G.163, Proposition 13.4.2, in the reading of structured data relative to the open $V$ (§XIII.28).
- Remark 13.3.13, the negative half: that the structured sums $\Lambda_1 \oplus \Lambda_2$ and $\Lambda_2 \oplus \Lambda_1$ differ, because $I^1_x \times I^2_x$ and $I^2_x \times I^1_x$ differ, is a statement about inequality of types and has no formal counterpart.
- Remarks 13.3.9, 13.3.16 and 13.5.2 are prose.

### XIII.12 What the formalization taught us

§13.1 is a study of the bi-action, and once it is written as a formula almost everything follows from two facts: morphisms between points of a neighbourhood with the natural action are $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$ for a unique $g$, and $s$, $t$ are injective on each component. Lemma 13.1.6 (1) then needs one morphism with $g' * \psi \in \Sigma$, not $g' * \Sigma = \Sigma$, and Proposition 13.1.9 follows from Lemma 13.1.6 with the action laws, without the smoothness argument of the text, and with uniqueness among all maps. The phrase "carries the natural $G_x$-action" needed a decision. Proposition 13.1.3 shrinks to invariant subsets that need not be connected, so a neighbourhood with the natural action cannot be the connected domain of a natural representation; it is an invariant open subset of one. With that reading the section holds as printed. In Lemma 13.1.1 the two directions use different halves of the hypotheses (properness one way, the natural action the other), and the invariance of $V$ is used by neither. Theorem 13.1.7 holds in two forms. With properness read in $X$ it needs neither the openness of $Q$ nor the smallness of the closures of $U(y)$. As printed, with properness read in the full subcategory on the open $Q$, the hypothesis turns out to be equivalent to properness in $X$ together with $\operatorname{cl}_XU(q) \subset Q$: a limit of points of $U(q)$ outside $Q$ is moved into $Q$ by a local section of $s$, and properness in $Q$ then places it in $Q$. No sub-ep-groupoid structure is needed; the full subcategory is its set of morphisms with the restricted source and target.

In §13.2 the multisection algebra is convolution: $\oplus$, scalar multiples and locally finite sums are all sums over decompositions of a vector in a fibre, and their local structures are sums of sections with products of weights. A locally finite sum over infinitely many indices, which the text does not write out, is a sum over finitely supported families, and over $O(x)$ it is a finite convolution. The decorations add one subtlety: the intersection $U'(x) \cap U''(x)$ of two neighbourhoods with natural actions need not carry one natural action for which both structures are symmetric, so the sum is decorated on a smaller neighbourhood inside it on which the two actions agree, which Definition 13.2.8 allows. The absence of inverses is a one-line computation once a neutral element is fixed: a two-valued multisection convolved with anything gives weight at most $\tfrac12$ to the zero vector. §13.3 is mostly combinatorics of finite index sets, and two points needed care. The text writes equalities of index sets ($I'_x = \{*\}$, $I'_x = I_x$) where a formalization has bijections, and the correspondences are compared after transport along them. And the tight version of Proposition 13.3.15 needs a compatibility the text does not check; it holds because every section of a structure vanishes where $\Lambda$ is trivial. Definition 13.3.8 as printed puts no condition on the sections; presumably they are meant to agree as in Definition 13.2.8, and nothing proved depends on it. In §13.5 the atomic multisection is determined by its data, the count in Definition 13.5.1 (3) does not depend on the morphism used, and its local structure near any point is the given sections transported by a local inverse of $t$; what the text does not say is that the index set must be nonempty, since the weights of a multisection sum to $1$.

The structurability proofs of waves 3 and 4 turned on three points. First, products of infinitely many correspondences are well defined only because, near any two points, all but finitely many factors are the unit diagram $[\{*\} \leftarrow \{*\} \to \{*\}]$; the text's "left to the reader" in Proposition 13.3.19 is this bookkeeping, about 500 lines with the tight versions over a common good system. Second, in Theorem 13.5.3 the action of $G_y$ on the index set comes from a single function $H$ that assigns to a morphism the element of $G_{x_0}$ it becomes after both ends are transported into $U(x_0)$; $H$ is functorial, and locally constant because $G_{x_0}$ is finite and $X$ Hausdorff, and every compatibility follows from these two properties. Using the index set $I_{x_0}$ everywhere, with zero sections where $\Lambda$ is trivial and the full correspondence across the frontier of the saturation, avoids the case distinction of the text's $\{*\}$. The theorem needs a good system and nothing else: structurability is equivalent to the existence of one. Third, §13.4 is simpler than printed. The pull-back needs only $F$ injective on $U(x)$ with $F(U(x)) \subset U'(F(x))$, not the equality the text arranges, and the canonicity it asserts is a short argument once the pull-back is written as a map of structured classes. The push-forward does not need Proposition 13.4.2: every point of $X'$, in $F(X)$ or not, gets a chart along a morphism $F(x_y) \to y$, which merges the text's two steps; the lifted morphisms are continuous because $F$ is faithful and a local sc-diffeomorphism. Theorem 13.5.7 needs regularity of $|X|$ for its shrinking, which every ep-groupoid has, and partitions of unity, not paracompactness; the atomic pieces are atomic on neighbourhoods with the natural action, since the sets of a good system need not be connected domains of natural representations.

### XIII.13 Theorem 13.1.7 (2017: 13.1) as printed: properness in the full subcategory on $Q$

**The full subcategory on $Q$.** For $Q \subset X$ the morphisms between points of $Q$, with source and target ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.subSrc⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.subTgt⟧. A subset $A \subset Q$ is proper in $Q$ if $t : s^{-1}(A) \to Q$ is proper in the subcategory ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.IsProperSubsetIn⟧. A family $(U(q))_{q \in Q}$ is a good system for $Q$ ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.IsGoodIn⟧ if $U(q) \subset Q$, $\operatorname{cl}_QU(q)$ is proper in $Q$ (Definition 13.1.2 (1) read in $Q$), and (3) holds for $q, q' \in Q$; conditions (2) and (3) are the same in $Q$ and in $X$, since a natural representation of the ep-groupoid $Q$ is one of $X$. Every good system of $X$ is one for $Q = X$ ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.isGoodIn_univ⟧, which with §XIII.10 is the witness.

**Properness by ultrafilters** (extra). A map defined on a subspace is proper iff every ultrafilter on the ambient space that lives on the subspace and whose image converges has a limit in the subspace mapping to the image limit ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.isProperMap_iff_ultrafilter_of_isInducing⟧; so properness of $\operatorname{cl}U$ in $X$ ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.isProperSubset_iff_ultrafilter⟧ and in $Q$ ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.isProperSubsetIn_iff_ultrafilter⟧ become statements about ultrafilters of morphisms. Two tools: for $|Q| = |X|$ every object has a morphism to a point of $Q$ ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.exists_mor_tgt_mem⟧; and through a morphism $\chi$ with target in an open $O$ there is a local section $\sigma$ of $s$ with $\sigma(s(\chi)) = \chi$ and targets in $O$ ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.exists_localSection⟧, the local inverse of the étale map $s$ cut down by the continuity of $t$.

**Step 1: the closure stays in $Q$** ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.closure_subset_of_isProperSubsetIn⟧. Let $Q$ be open with $|Q| = |X|$, $U \subset Q$, and $\operatorname{cl}_QU$ proper in $Q$; then $\operatorname{cl}_XU \subset Q$. A point $z \in \operatorname{cl}_XU$ has a morphism $\chi : z \to q''$ with $q'' \in Q$; take $\sigma$ through $\chi$ with targets in $Q$. For $y'$ in $U$ near $z$, $\sigma(y')$ is a morphism of the subcategory with source in $U$ and target near $q''$; its targets converge in $Q$, so properness in $Q$ gives a limit of the morphisms $\sigma(y')$ in the subcategory, which is $\chi$; its source $z$ is then in $Q$.

**Step 2: properness in $X$** ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.isProperSubset_of_isProperSubsetIn⟧. Let an ultrafilter of morphisms $\varphi$ with sources in $\operatorname{cl}_XU = \operatorname{cl}_QU$ have targets converging to some $y \in X$. Choose $\chi : y \to q''$ into $Q$ and $\rho$ a local section of $s$ through $\chi$ with targets in $Q$; then $\rho(t(\varphi)) \circ \varphi$ is a morphism of the subcategory whose targets converge to $q''$. Properness in $Q$ gives a limit $\psi$; then $\chi^{-1} \circ \psi$ is the limit of the $\varphi$, with target $y$. The converse, that properness in $X$ with $\operatorname{cl}_XU \subset Q$ gives properness in $Q$, holds as well ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.isProperSubsetIn_of_isProperSubset⟧, so ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.isGoodIn_iff⟧: for open $Q$ with $|Q| = |X|$, a family is a good system for $Q$ iff it is good on $Q$ in the sense of §XIII.4 and $\operatorname{cl}_XU(q) \subset Q$ for all $q$.

**Theorem 13.1.7, as printed** ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.theorem_13_1_7_book⟧: let $Q$ be open with $|Q| = |X|$ and $(U(q))_{q \in Q}$ a good system for the ep-groupoid $Q$. Given open $W(y) \ni y$ for $y \notin Q$, there is a good system of $X$ which keeps $U(q)$ for $q \in Q$ and has $U(y) \subset W(y)$ for $y \notin Q$. *Proof.* A good system for $Q$ is good on $Q$ in the sense of §XIII.4 ⟦Chapter13/P3E_GoodSystemRelative · EpGroupoid.IsGoodIn.isGoodOn⟧, and the stronger Theorem 13.1.7 of §XIII.4 applies ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystemExistence · EpGroupoid.theorem_13_1_7⟧. No hypothesis is added; $|Q| = |X|$ is the text's $|Q| = |Y|$.

### XIII.14 Definitions 13.2.7 and 13.2.8 (2017: 13.9 and 13.10): decorated sc⁺-multisections

**Symmetric structures on a neighbourhood** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn · SBLocalization.SymmetricStructureOn⟧. Definition 13.2.5 on a neighbourhood $N$ of $x$ with the natural action of §XIII.1: a finite index set $I$ with an action of $G_x$, sc⁺-sections $s_i$ on $N$ with $s_{g(i)}(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g, y), s_i(y))$, and $\Lambda(w) = |I|^{-1}\#\{i : s_i(P(w)) = w\}$ over $N$. The structures of §XIII.7 restrict to such ⟦Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn · SBLocalization.SymmetricStructure.toOn⟧, so they exist at every point ⟦Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn · SBLocalization.exists_symmetricStructureOn⟧ (Lemma 13.2.6), and $I \neq \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn · SBLocalization.SymmetricStructureOn.card_pos⟧. Where $\Lambda(0_y) = 1$ all sections vanish ⟦Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn · SBLocalization.SymmetricStructureOn.s_eq_fiberZero⟧. A structure restricts to a smaller neighbourhood with the same action ⟦Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn · SBLocalization.SymmetricStructureOn.restrict⟧; "the same action" is a relation between neighbourhoods ⟦Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn · EpGroupoid.NatNbhd.Le⟧, and inside finitely many neighbourhoods of $x$ with natural actions there is one whose action agrees with all of them ⟦Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn · EpGroupoid.NatNbhd.exists_le_of_finite⟧, because two natural representations at $x$ agree on the connected component of $x$ in the intersection of their domains (the uniqueness of natural representations, Part VII, §VII.9), and an invariant neighbourhood can be taken inside it.

**Definition 13.2.7** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.DecoratedTuple⟧: an sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda$ with a good system $\mathcal U$ and, for every $x$, a symmetric structure on $U(x)$. The good system carries a natural action at each point (§XIII.1), and the properness clause of Definition 13.2.5 is Definition 13.1.2 (1). Every sc⁺-multisection over an ep-groupoid with paracompact orbit space has a decoration ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.exists_decoration⟧: a good system from Theorem 13.1.8, a symmetric structure at each point from Lemma 13.2.6, a good system inside their domains from Theorem 13.1.8, shrunk at each point to a neighbourhood where the action of the good system agrees with that of the structure ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.ofSubset⟧, and the structures restricted to it. The paracompactness is the text's, through Theorem 13.1.8.

**Definition 13.2.8** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.Rel⟧: $(\Lambda, \mathcal U, S) \sim (\Lambda', \mathcal U', S')$ if $\Lambda = \Lambda'$ and there are a good system $\mathcal U''$ with $U''(x) \subset U(x) \cap U'(x)$ and $G_x$-equivariant bijections $b_x : I_x \to I'_x$ with $s'_{b_x(i)} = s_i$ on $U''(x)$. Reflexivity and symmetry are direct ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.Rel.refl⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.Rel.symm⟧; transitivity composes the bijections on a common refinement of the two intermediate good systems ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.Rel.trans⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.exists_subset_inter⟧, which exists by the refinement step after Proposition 13.1.3. The classes are the decorated sc⁺-multisections ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.DecoratedTuple.equivalence⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.DecoratedMultisection⟧, with the map to the underlying functor ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.DecoratedMultisection.forget⟧.

### XIII.15 Definitions 13.2.9, 13.2.10, Lemmas 13.2.11, 13.2.13 (2017: 13.11, 13.12, 13.4, 13.5) decorated, and the remark that there are no inverses

**Moving sections by morphisms.** $\mu(\psi, v)$ for $v$ over $s(\psi)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn · SBLocalization.fibAct⟧ is additive and homogeneous in the section ⟦Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn · SBLocalization.fibAct_sectionAdd⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn · SBLocalization.fibAct_sectionSmul⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn · SBLocalization.fibAct_sectionSum⟧, since $\mu(\psi, \cdot)$ is linear on fibres. This is what makes the new families equivariant.

**Definition 13.2.9, decorated** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.definition_13_2_9_decorated⟧. Given decorations of $\Lambda'$ and $\Lambda''$, the decoration of $\Lambda' \oplus \Lambda''$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.add⟧ has index sets $I'_x \times I''_x$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.add_I⟧ with the diagonal action, sections $s_{(i,i')} = s'_i + s''_{i'}$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.add_s_apply⟧, and neighbourhoods inside $U'(x) \cap U''(x)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.add_U_subset⟧. *Reading.* The text takes $U(x) = U'(x) \cap U''(x)$. The two natural actions on it need not agree, and a symmetric structure needs one action for which both families are equivariant; so $U(x)$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$ inside the intersection on which the two actions agree (§XIII.14), and the class does not depend on this choice, since Definition 13.2.8 allows shrinking. The symmetric structure of the sum ⟦Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn · SBLocalization.SymmetricStructureOn.add⟧: equivariance of $s'_i + s''_{i'}$ is that of the summands with the additivity of $\mu(\psi, \cdot)$, and the count is the convolution formula of §XIII.8. *Well defined on classes* ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.add_rel⟧: equivalent summands give equivalent sums, with the product bijections $b'_x \times b''_x$. So $\oplus$ is defined on decorated sc⁺-multisections ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.DecoratedMultisection.add⟧, compatibly with forgetting ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.DecoratedMultisection.forget_add⟧, and commutative ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.DecoratedMultisection.add_comm⟧ and associative ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.DecoratedMultisection.add_assoc⟧ there, through the swap and reassociation bijections of index sets ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.add_comm_rel⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.add_assoc_rel⟧.

**Definition 13.2.10 and Lemma 13.2.11, decorated.** $a\Lambda$ is decorated by the sections $as_i$ on the same good system and index sets ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.smul⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.definition_13_2_10_decorated⟧; for $a = 0$ the sections are $0$ and the count gives the zero multisection. For an sc-smooth functor $\beta : X \to \mathbb R$, $\beta\Lambda$ is decorated by $\beta s_i$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.smulFun⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.lemma_13_2_11_decorated⟧; equivariance uses $\beta(t(\psi)) = \beta(s(\psi))$. Both are compatible with Definition 13.2.8 ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.smulFun_rel⟧ and hence defined on classes ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.DecoratedMultisection.smul⟧.

**Lemma 13.2.13, decorated** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.lemma_13_2_13_decorated⟧. For a locally finite family $(\Lambda_j)$ with decorations, the decoration of $\oplus_j\Lambda_j$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.Decoration.lfSum⟧ has, at $x$, a neighbourhood inside $O(x) \cap \bigcap_{j \in J_x}U_j(x)$ on which the natural actions agree, index set $\prod_{j \in J_x}I^j_x$ and sections $\sum_{j \in J_x}s^{j,x}_{i_j}$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Decorated · SBLocalization.lfSumStructure⟧, the symmetric structure of a finite product ⟦Chapter13/P3D_SymmetricOn · SBLocalization.SymmetricStructureOn.pi⟧. Over $O(x)$ the indices outside $J_x$ contribute only the zero vector (§XIII.9). The intersection is read as for Definition 13.2.9. When $J_x = \emptyset$ the text leaves the natural action on $O(x)$ open; it is taken from a given good system $\mathcal U_0$, an argument of the construction (any $\mathcal U_j$, or Theorem 13.1.8).

**The remark after Definition 13.2.9: no inverses.** The zero multisection is neutral ⟦Chapter13/P3D_NoInverse · SBLocalization.multisectionAdd_zeroMultisection⟧. On the trivial bundle $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n$ over the trivial ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter13/P3D_NoInverse · SBLocalization.NoInverse.A⟧, for $c \ne 0$ let $\Lambda_c$ give weight $\tfrac12$ to the zero section and $\tfrac12$ to the constant section $c$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_NoInverse · SBLocalization.NoInverse.twoValued⟧, an sc⁺-multisection ⟦Chapter13/P3D_NoInverse · SBLocalization.NoInverse.isScPlusMultisection_twoValued⟧. **Then $\Lambda_c \oplus \Lambda' \ne \Lambda_0$ for every sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda'$** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_NoInverse · SBLocalization.NoInverse.remark_13_2_9_no_inverse⟧. Over $x = 0$, $(\Lambda_c \oplus \Lambda')(0_x) = \tfrac12\Lambda'(0) + \tfrac12\Lambda'(-c)$, and since $0 \ne -c$ and the weights of $\Lambda'$ over $x$ sum to $1$, this is at most $\tfrac12$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_NoInverse · SBLocalization.NoInverse.add_le_one_of_ne⟧, while $\Lambda_0(0_x) = 1$. Such a $\Lambda_c$ exists when $k \ge 1$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_NoInverse · SBLocalization.NoInverse.exists_no_inverse⟧. "Inverse" is read with respect to the neutral element $\Lambda_0$.

### XIII.16 Definitions 13.3.1, 13.3.2, Example 13.3.3, Definition 13.3.4, Remark 13.3.5 (2017: Definitions 13.14, 13.15, Example 13.1, Definition 13.16, Remark 13.1): correspondences

**Definition 13.3.1** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexDiagram⟧: a diagram $I_x \xleftarrow{a} I \xrightarrow{b} I_{x'}$ of finite sets, $a$ and $b$ surjective, all fibres of $a$ of one size and all fibres of $b$ of one size. Two diagrams are equivalent if a bijection $c : I \to I'$ makes both triangles commute ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexDiagram.Equiv⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexDiagram.equivalence⟧; $J(x, x')$ is the set of classes, the correspondences ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr⟧. A bijection $e : I_x \to I_x$ gives the class $[\mathrm{id}, e]$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.ofPerm⟧, and relabelling the two index sets by bijections acts on classes ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.map⟧.

**Definition 13.3.2** (stronger) ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.swap⟧: the pseudo-inverse $\sharp$ reverses the diagram; it is an involution ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.swap_swap⟧ and so a bijection $J(x, x') \to J(x', x)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.swapEquiv⟧. The bi-action $g' * [a, b] * g = [g^{-1} \circ a, g' \circ b]$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.biact⟧ is well defined, and the text's maps satisfy the action laws, which it does not state: $1 * \tau * 1 = \tau$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.biact_one_one⟧ and $g' * (h' * \tau * h) * g = (g'h') * \tau * (hg)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.biact_biact⟧, an action of $G_{x'} \times G_x^{\mathrm{op}}$.

**Example 13.3.3** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.example_13_3_3⟧: if $I_x = \{*\}$, then $g' * \tau * g = \tau$ for all $g, g'$. A bijection $c : I \to I$ with $b \circ c = g' \circ b$ is built fibre by fibre from the equal sizes of the fibres of $b$; and $a$ is constant.

**Definition 13.3.4** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.Decoration.IsCorrespondence⟧: for a decoration and points $x, x'$, a map $\tau$ from the morphisms to $J(x, x')$ is a correspondence if on $\mathcal U(x, x')$ it is (1) locally constant with finitely many values, (2) equivariant, $\tau(g' * \varphi * g) = g' * \tau(\varphi) * g$ with the bi-action of the good system (§XIII.3), and (3) compatible: for every representative $I_x \xleftarrow{a} I \xrightarrow{b} I_{x'}$ of $\tau(\varphi)$, $s^{x'}_{b(k)}(t(\psi)) = \mu(\psi, s^x_{a(k)}(s(\psi)))$ for all $k$ and all $\psi$ in the component of $\varphi$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.Decoration.Compat⟧. The action of $G_x$ on $I_x$ is the one of the symmetric structure. **Remark 13.3.5** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.sat_iff⟧: for any relation $R$ on $I_x \times I_{x'}$, "$R(a(k), b(k))$ for all $k$" is invariant under equivalence of diagrams ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexDiagram.sat_iff_of_equiv⟧ (the bijection $c$ only renames $k$), so it is a property of the class ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.Sat⟧, held by $\tau$ iff by every representative; condition (3) is of this form.

### XIII.17 Definitions 13.3.6–13.3.11, Proposition 13.3.12, Remark 13.3.13, Lemma 13.3.14 (2017: Definitions 13.17–13.20, Remarks 13.2–13.4, Proposition 13.3, Lemma 13.6): structurable sc⁺-multisections

**Definition 13.3.6** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.Decoration.Tau⟧: a structure on a decoration is a family of correspondences $\tau_{x,x'}$ for all $x, x'$ with (1) $\tau_{x,x}(\Gamma(g, y)) = [\mathrm{id}, g]$ and (2) $\tau_{x',x}(\varphi) = \tau_{x,x'}(\varphi^{-1})^\sharp$ for $\varphi \in \mathcal U(x', x)$. A decorated sc⁺-multisection is structurable if a representative carries one ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.DecoratedMultisection.IsStructurable⟧, and a functor is structurable if it is an sc⁺-multisection with a decoration carrying one ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.IsStructurable⟧, equivalently if it underlies a structurable decorated class ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.isStructurable_iff⟧. $\tau_{x,x'}$ is a function on all morphisms; only its values on $\mathcal U(x, x')$ enter. Witness: the zero multisection, with all index sets $\{*\}$ and all $\tau$ the unit diagram, over a paracompact orbit space ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.isStructurable_zeroMultisection⟧.

**Remark 13.3.7, Definitions 13.3.8, 13.3.10, 13.3.11.** The tuples $(\Lambda, \mathcal U, S, \tau)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.StructuredTuple⟧ are equivalent ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.StructuredTuple.Equiv⟧ if $\Lambda = \Lambda'$, a good system $\mathcal U''$ lies in $U(x) \cap U'(x)$, $I_x = I'_x$, and $\tau = \tau'$ on $\mathcal U''(x, x')$. The equality of index sets is an equality of types, and $\tau'$ is compared with $\tau$ after transport along it; this is an equivalence relation ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.StructuredTuple.equivalence⟧. As printed, the definition puts no condition on the sections; presumably they are meant to agree on $U''(x)$ as in Definition 13.2.8. It is formalized as printed, and nothing below uses the sections of an equivalent tuple. The classes are the structured sc⁺-multisections ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.StructuredMultisection⟧.
