Definition 13.3.11: $\Gamma^+_m(P)$, $\Gamma^+_s(P)$, $\Gamma^+_{st}(P)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.Γm⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.Γs⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.Γst⟧, with $\Gamma^+_s \subset \Gamma^+_m$ and forget mapping $\Gamma^+_{st}$ onto $\Gamma^+_s$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.StructuredMultisection.range_forget⟧, which is the text's statement that every structurable $\Lambda$ lifts.

**Proposition 13.3.12** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.proposition_13_3_12⟧: the sum of two structurable sc⁺-multisections is structurable. *The product of correspondences* ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.prod⟧: $[a_1, b_1] \times [a_2, b_2] = [a_1 \times a_2, b_1 \times b_2]$; the fibres of a product map are products of fibres ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexDiagram.card_fiber_prodMap⟧, so they have equal sizes; the product commutes with $\sharp$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.prod_swap⟧, with the bi-action ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.prod_biact⟧ and with $[\mathrm{id}, g]$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Correspondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.prod_ofPerm⟧. *"We may assume $\mathcal U_1 = \mathcal U_2$."* Both structures are restricted to the neighbourhoods of the decorated sum (§XIII.15), with the same actions ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.Decoration.Tau.restrict⟧; the bi-action does not change on a smaller neighbourhood with the same action ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · EpGroupoid.GoodSystem.biact_congr_of_le⟧. *The structure of the sum* ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.Decoration.Tau.prod⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.Decoration.Tau.add⟧ is $\tau = \tau^1 \times \tau^2$, with index sets $I^1_x \times I^2_x$ and sections $s^1_i + s^2_j$. Local constancy, finiteness, equivariance and (1)–(2) hold factorwise; compatibility (3) is the text's computation, $\mu(\psi, s^1_{a_1(k)} + s^2_{a_2(l)}) = s^1_{b_1(k)} + s^2_{b_2(l)}$ by the additivity of $\mu(\psi, \cdot)$ (§XIII.15). For structured tuples the sum is again structured ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.StructuredTuple.add⟧, over $\Lambda_1 \oplus \Lambda_2$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.StructuredTuple.add_Λ⟧.

**Remark 13.3.13** (narrower): the structured sums $\Lambda_1 \oplus \Lambda_2$ and $\Lambda_2 \oplus \Lambda_1$ have the same underlying functor (`StructuredTuple.add_Λ` with the commutativity of §XIII.8); that they differ as structured classes, the index sets being $I^1_x \times I^2_x$ and $I^2_x \times I^1_x$, is a statement that two types are unequal, which has no formal statement.

**Lemma 13.3.14** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.lemma_13_3_14⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.lemma_13_3_14_fun⟧: $r\Lambda$, for every $r \in \mathbb R$ including $0$, and $\beta\Lambda$ for an sc-smooth functor $\beta$, are structurable when $\Lambda$ is. The same $\tau$ serves ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.Decoration.Tau.smul⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Structurable · SBLocalization.Decoration.Tau.smulFun⟧: compatibility (3) is homogeneity of $\mu(\psi, \cdot)$, with $\beta(t(\psi)) = \beta(s(\psi))$ for $\beta$.

### XIII.18 The construction before Proposition 13.3.15, Proposition 13.3.15, Definition 13.3.17, Corollary 13.3.18 (2017: Proposition 13.4, Definition 13.21, Corollary 13.1): tight structures

**$T_\Lambda$** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.trivialSet⟧: the set of points near which $\Lambda$ is trivial, $\Lambda(0_y) = 1$; it is open ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.isOpen_trivialSet⟧ and $\Lambda$ is trivial on it ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.isTrivialOn_trivialSet⟧. Triviality at $s(\psi)$ and at $t(\psi)$ are the same, $\Lambda$ being a functor ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.apply_fiberZero_tgt⟧.

**The construction.** For $x \in T_\Lambda$, shrink $U(x)$ to a neighbourhood with the same action inside $U(x) \cap T_\Lambda$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.Decoration.exists_tightNbhd⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.Decoration.tightNbhd⟧, and put the single zero section on $I'_x = \{*\}$; for $x \notin T_\Lambda$ keep $U(x)$, $I_x$ and the sections. The index set is one type, $\{*\}$ when $x \in T_\Lambda$ and $I_x$ otherwise ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.TightIdx⟧, with bijections $\{*\} \simeq I'_x$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.TightIdx.eT⟧ and $I_x \simeq I'_x$ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.TightIdx.eN⟧; the text's equalities $I'_x = \{*\}$, $I'_x = I_x$ are these bijections. The new decoration ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.Decoration.tight⟧ replaces $\tau$ by the unit diagrams when $x$ or $x'$ lies in $T_\Lambda$, and keeps it, relabelled, otherwise ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.Decoration.tightτ⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.Decoration.tightτ_TN⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.Decoration.tightτ_NN⟧. **It is again structured** (stronger) ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.Decoration.Tau.tight⟧. The text does not check condition (3) of Definition 13.3.4 for the new $\tau'$. It holds: at a morphism $\psi$ with $t(\psi)$ or $s(\psi)$ in $T_\Lambda$, both are, since triviality passes along morphisms, and every section of a symmetric structure vanishes where $\Lambda(0_y) = 1$ (§XIII.14), so both sides of (3) are $0$. Constant correspondences are correspondences ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.Decoration.isCorrespondence_const⟧, and the unit diagrams satisfy (1)–(2) of Definition 13.3.6 because relabelling commutes with $\sharp$ and the bi-action ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.swap_map⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.biact_map⟧.

**Proposition 13.3.15** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.proposition_13_3_15⟧: from a structured representative $(\Lambda, \mathcal U, S, \tau)$ one gets a structured $(\Lambda, \mathcal U', S', \tau')$ with (1) for $x \in T_\Lambda$: $I'_x = \{*\}$, the zero section, and $U'(x) \subset T_\Lambda$ with the action of $U(x)$; (2) for $x \notin T_\Lambda$: $U'(x) = U(x)$ and equivariant bijections $e_x : I_x \to I'_x$ with $s'_{e_x(i)} = s_i$; (3) $\tau' = \tau$ relabelled by $e_x$, $e_{x'}$, for $x, x' \notin T_\Lambda$; (4)–(5) the unit diagrams otherwise. It is the construction above ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.Decoration.isTight_tight⟧; (3) holds for all morphisms.

**Definition 13.3.17** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.Decoration.IsTight⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.StructuredMultisection.IsTight⟧: a representative is tight if (1) $I_x = \{*\}$ with the zero section for $x \in T_\Lambda$, (2) $\tau_{x,x'}$ is $[* \leftarrow I_{x'} \xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}} I_{x'}]$, resp. $[I_x \xleftarrow{\mathrm{id}} I_x \to *]$, when exactly one of $x, x'$ lies in $T_\Lambda$, and (3) $[\{*\} \leftarrow \{*\} \to \{*\}]$ when both do. $I_x = \{*\}$ is a bijection $\{*\} \simeq I_x$, and (2)–(3) are stated for every such bijection (all are equal). **Corollary 13.3.18** ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.corollary_13_3_18⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3D_Tight · SBLocalization.corollary_13_3_18_structured⟧: every structurable $\Lambda$ has a tightly structured version, and every element of $\Gamma^+_s$ underlies a tightly structured class.

### XIII.19 Definition 13.5.1, Theorems 13.5.4, 13.5.5 and 13.5.6 (2017: Definition 13.23, Theorems 13.7, 13.8, 13.9): atomic sc⁺-multisections

**Definition 13.5.1** ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.IsAtomic⟧. Atomic data are: a point $x$ and a natural representation of $G_x$ on $U(x)$ with the properness property; an open invariant $V \ni x$ with $\overline V \subset U(x)$; a finite index set $I$ with a $G_x$-action; and sc⁺-sections $s_i$ on $U(x)$, equivariant, $s_{g(i)}(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g, y), s_i(y))$, and vanishing on $U(x) \setminus V$. An sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda$ is related to the data ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.IsRelated⟧ if, for $w$ over a point joined by a morphism $\varphi$ to $U(x)$, $\Lambda(w) = |I|^{-1}\#\{i : s_i(t(\varphi)) = \mu(\varphi, w)\}$ ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.count⟧, and $\Lambda$ is trivial over the other points; it is atomic if it is related to some data. The count is taken at $t(\varphi)$, with $w' = \mu(\varphi, w)$. *The count does not depend on $\varphi$* ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.count_μ_eq⟧: two morphisms into $U(x)$ from the same point differ by some $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$, and equivariance permutes the indices by $g$ ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.count_μ_Γ⟧. So $\Lambda$ is determined by the data ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.IsRelated.eq_mult⟧; the data form a symmetric structure of $\Lambda$ at $x$ in the sense of Definition 13.2.5 ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.IsRelated.symmetricStructure⟧, so (2) holds as printed; and $I \ne \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.IsRelated.nonempty⟧. Witness: the zero multisection is atomic at every point, with one index and the zero section ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.isAtomic_zeroMultisection⟧.

**The multisection of the data** ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.mult⟧ is the formula of (3). It is a functor ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.isWFunctor_mult⟧ and an sc⁺-multisection when $I \ne \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.isScPlusMultisection_mult⟧. *Near a point $y$ joined to $U(x)$* ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.exists_isLocalRepOn_transport⟧: a morphism from a point of $U(x)$ to $y$ has a sheet on which $t$ has an sc-smooth local inverse $\tau$, with $t(\tau(z)) = z$ and $s(\tau(z)) \in U(x)$, and $s'_i(z) = \mu(\tau(z), s_i(s(\tau(z))))$ is a local structure with weights $|I|^{-1}$. *Away from such points:* the saturation of $\overline V$ is closed, by properness ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.isClosed_saturation_closure_V⟧, and off it the multisection is the zero multisection ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.mult_eq_zeroMultisection⟧, because the sections vanish off $V$. So the domain support lies in the saturation of $\overline V$ ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.domSupp_mult_subset⟧, and the multisection of the data is atomic ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.isAtomic_mult⟧.

**Symmetric families** ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.SymmetricFamily⟧: global sc⁺-sections of $W \to X$ supported in $U(x)$, with a $G_x$-action on the index set and equivariance on $U(x)$. *From one seed* ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.SymmetricFamily.ofSeed⟧: for an sc⁺-section $s_0$ supported in an invariant $V$, $I = G_x$ acting by left multiplication and $s_g$ the translate of $s_0$ by $g$ (the terms of the average of §XII.7); $s_1 = s_0$ ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.SymmetricFamily.ofSeed_one⟧, the family vanishes off $V$ ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.SymmetricFamily.ofSeed_vanish⟧, and for an invariant auxiliary norm the translates have the bound of the seed ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.SymmetricFamily.ofSeed_normW_le⟧.

**Theorem 13.5.4 (Construction I).** Setting: $X$ with bump functions (pointwise reading), $x$ smooth, $U(x)$ with the natural action and the properness property, $V$ open invariant with $\overline V \subset U(x)$. *(1)* ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_4_1⟧: for a smooth $w \in W_x$ there is a symmetric family vanishing off $V$ with $s_{i_0}(x) = w$. The seed is an sc⁺-section through $w$ supported in $V$, from Part I's Lemma 5.3.3 with a Part I auxiliary norm ⟦Chapter5/BumpFunctions · lemma_5_3_3⟧. *(2)* ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_4_2⟧: for an sc⁺-section $s$ on an open $O \ni x$ there is such a family with $s_{i_0} = s$ near $x$. The seed is $\beta s$ with $\beta \equiv 1$ near $x$ and supported in $V \cap O$ ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.exists_cutoff⟧, from Proposition 5.5.3; "$s_{i_0} = s$ near $x$" needs $\beta \equiv 1$ near $x$, not only $\beta(x) = 1$. The conclusion is stronger than printed: the sections are global sc⁺-sections vanishing off $V$, not only on $U(x) \setminus V$. The properness property, and in (2) the smoothness of $x$, are kept and unused. Narrower only through the pointwise reading of bump functions, as Theorem 12.3.3 (§XII.7).

**Theorem 13.5.5 (Construction II)** ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_5⟧: a symmetric family on $U(x)$ with nonempty index set determines a unique atomic $\Lambda$ that is trivial off the saturation of $U(x)$ and equals $|I|^{-1}\#\{i : s_i(P(w)) = w\}$ over $U(x)$. *Step 1, $V(x)$* ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.SymmetricFamily.exists_vanishing_nbhd⟧: by normality an open set around $\{x\} \cup \bigcup_i\operatorname{supp}s_i$ with closure in $U(x)$, intersected over the translates by $G_x$, is invariant, and the family vanishes off it. *Step 2.* The data so obtained ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.AtomicData.ofFamily⟧ give the multisection of the data, which is atomic, trivial off the saturation, and has the formula over $U(x)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3A_Atomic · SBLocalization.AtomicData.mult_of_mem⟧. *Uniqueness* is that $\Lambda$ is determined by its data. The added $I \ne \emptyset$ is implicit in the text: with $I = \emptyset$ the printed formula gives $\Lambda = 0$ over $U(x)$, which is not a multisection; for atomic $\Lambda$ it is automatic, and the seed families have $I = G_x$. "Supported in the saturation of $U(x)$" is read as triviality over the points not isomorphic to a point of $U(x)$. Bump functions and the smoothness of $x$ are not used. The last clause of the theorem, that $\Lambda$ is structurable, rests on Theorem 13.5.3 (§XIII.20).

**Theorem 13.5.6.** Setting: $|X|$ paracompact, bump functions (pointwise reading), an auxiliary norm $N$. *Part 1* ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_6_1⟧: for a smooth $w \ne 0$ over $x$ and $U(x)$ with the natural action, an atomic $\Lambda$ with domain support in the saturation of $U(x)$ and $\Lambda(\mu(g, w)) > 0$ for all $g \in G_x$: Construction I (1) through $w$, then Construction II; each $\mu(g, w)$ is the value of the section $s_g$ at $x$. *Part 2* ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_6_2⟧: for an sc⁺-section $s$ on $U(x)$ and $\varepsilon > 0$, an atomic $\Lambda$ supported there with $N(\Lambda)(y) \le N(s(x)) + \varepsilon$ for all $y$, whose local structure near $x$ contains $s$ with positive weight, read as: a local structure on an open $O \ni x$ one of whose sections equals $s$ on $O$ ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.AtomicData.isLocalRepOn_mult⟧. The seed $\beta s$ is chosen with $N(\beta s) \le N(s(x)) + \varepsilon$ near $x$; the translates keep the bound, because $N$ is $\mu$-invariant ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.normW_μ⟧, and the pointwise norm of the multisection is a maximum over the transported sections ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.AtomicData.pointwiseNorm_mult_le⟧. Both parts together ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicConstruction · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_6⟧. Paracompactness is kept and unused: the text uses it for the existence of $N$, which is a hypothesis here. **Remark 13.5.2** is prose; Theorems 13.5.4–13.5.6 use bump functions only, no partitions of unity, as the remark says.

### XIII.20 Theorem 13.5.3 (2017: 13.6): atomic sc⁺-multisections are structurable, with the correspondences as a hypothesis

**The local alternative** ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicData.IsLocallyTransported⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_3_local⟧: for atomic data of $\Lambda$, at every point $y$ either $\Lambda$ is trivial on an open $O \ni y$, or on an open $O \ni y$ there is an sc-smooth choice $\tau$ of morphisms with $t(\tau(z)) = z$ and $s(\tau(z)) \in U(x_0)$ such that $\Lambda$ is represented there by $s'_i(z) = \mu(\tau(z), s_i(s(\tau(z))))$, $i \in I$, with weights $|I|^{-1}$. This is the case distinction of the text's proof, with index set $I$ near points joined to $U(x_0)$ and $\{*\}$ elsewhere; it comes from the local structure of §XIII.19 and from the closedness of the saturation of $\overline V$.

**Theorem 13.5.3** (narrower) ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_3_hyp⟧: for a predicate "structurable" and the hypothesis that every sc⁺-multisection related to atomic data and locally transported at every point is structurable, every atomic $\Lambda$ is structurable. The hypothesis is the remaining step of the text's proof: that the transported structures fit together through correspondences. It was stated before Definition 13.3.6 was available to this block; the predicate of §XIII.17 can be substituted. It is satisfiable ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_3_hyp_witness⟧ (with "structurable" read as "is an sc⁺-multisection"), a witness of consistency only. The last clause of Theorem 13.5.5 follows in the same form ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_5_structurable_hyp⟧. What remains is a new gap (§XIII.11): a good system refining the sets $O$, the $G_y$-actions on $I_y = I$ through the partner homomorphism of Proposition 13.1.9, and the correspondences from the sheet indices in $U(x_0)$.

### XIII.21 Proposition 13.3.19 (2017: 13.5): locally finite sums of structurable sc⁺-multisections

**Products of correspondences** ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_PiCorrespondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.pi⟧. For a family of correspondences $\tau^l = [I^l \leftarrow M^l \to I'^l]$ all but finitely many of which have one-point index sets, the product $[\prod_l I^l \leftarrow \prod_l M^l \to \prod_l I'^l]$ is a correspondence; finiteness of the products is that all but finitely many factors are singletons ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_PiCorrespondence · SBLocalization.finite_pi_of_subsingleton⟧. The product saturates when every factor does ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_PiCorrespondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.sat_pi⟧, commutes with the swap ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_PiCorrespondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.swap_pi⟧ and with the bi-action of the isotropy groups ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_PiCorrespondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.biact_pi⟧, and the product of the diagrams of permutations is the diagram of the product permutation ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_PiCorrespondence · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.pi_ofPerm⟧. Symmetric structures can be reindexed along bijections ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_PiCorrespondence · SBLocalization.SymmetricStructureOn.reindex⟧, and $\mu(\psi, \cdot)$ is additive over finite sums ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_PiCorrespondence · SBLocalization.fibAct_sum⟧.

**Tight versions over a given good system** ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_TightOn · SBLocalization.Decoration.tightOn⟧. Wave 2 built the tight version of Proposition 13.3.15 over the decoration's own good system (§XIII.18); the sum needs them over one common good system that refines all of them. A good system is adapted to a decoration if each $U(x)$ lies in the decoration's $U(x)$ and, where $\Lambda$ is trivial, in its trivial set ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_TightOn · SBLocalization.Decoration.IsAdapted⟧. Over an adapted system the tight structure (index set $\{*\}$ at the points near which $\Lambda$ is trivial) and its correspondences in the four cases trivial/nontrivial are defined ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_TightOn · SBLocalization.Decoration.Tau.tightOn⟧, and the result is tight ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_TightOn · SBLocalization.Decoration.isTight_tightOn⟧.

**The data of the sum** ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_LocallyFiniteStructurable · SBLocalization.LFStructData⟧. Given structures $\tau^l$ of the $\Lambda_l$ and a locally finite family, choose for every $x$ an open saturated $O(x)$ on which only the $\Lambda_l$ with $l$ in a finite set $F(x)$ are nontrivial, and inside it an open $M(x)$ in all the decorations' $U^l(x)$ for $l \in F(x)$. A good system inside the sets $M(x)$ exists by Theorem 13.1.7 (§XIII.4) and is adapted to every decoration ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_LocallyFiniteStructurable · SBLocalization.LFStructData.isAdapted⟧: for $l \notin F(x)$, $U(x)$ lies in the trivial set of $\Lambda_l$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_LocallyFiniteStructurable · SBLocalization.subset_trivialSet_of_not_mem_nontrivIdx⟧. Pass to the tight versions over it. Then the index set $K_x = \prod_l K^l_x$ is finite ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_LocallyFiniteStructurable · SBLocalization.LFStructData.finite_K⟧, because the tight index sets of the trivial members are singletons; the sections $s^x_k = \sum_l s^{l,x}_{k(l)}$, a finite sum on $U(x)$, are the locally finite sum structure of wave 2 relabelled ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_LocallyFiniteStructurable · SBLocalization.LFStructData.Sx⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_LocallyFiniteStructurable · SBLocalization.LFStructData.Dsum⟧; and $\tau_{x,x'} = \prod_l \tau^l_{x,x'}$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_LocallyFiniteStructurable · SBLocalization.LFStructData.τ⟧, which is a correspondence ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_LocallyFiniteStructurable · SBLocalization.LFStructData.isCorrespondence⟧ because near $x$ and $x'$ all factors with $l$ outside $F(x) \cup F(x')$ are the unit. *The step left to the reader* ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_LocallyFiniteStructurable · SBLocalization.LFStructData.tau⟧: Definitions 13.3.4 and 13.3.6 for the product, factor by factor through the product lemmas above; the compatibility of the sections with $\tau$ is that a sum of compatible sections is compatible, since $\mu(\varphi, \cdot)$ is additive.

**Proposition 13.3.19** (as printed) ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_LocallyFiniteStructurable · SBLocalization.proposition_13_3_19⟧: for a nonempty family of structurable sc⁺-multisections, locally finite in the sense of Definition 13.2.12, the sum is structurable ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_LocallyFiniteStructurable · SBLocalization.LFStructData.isStructurable⟧. For any family, including the empty one, given a good system ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_LocallyFiniteStructurable · SBLocalization.proposition_13_3_19_of_goodSystem⟧, and for paracompact $|X|$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_LocallyFiniteStructurable · SBLocalization.proposition_13_3_19_of_paracompact⟧. The sum over the empty family is the trivial multisection, which is structurable when a good system exists, as Definition 13.3.6 requires; for a nonempty family a member provides one.

**Locally finite domain supports** ⟦Chapter13/P3W4SM_LocallyFiniteBridge · SBLocalization.isLocallyFiniteFamily_of_locallyFinite⟧. The text's hypothesis is that the domain supports form a locally finite family of subsets of $X$. It implies Definition 13.2.12's: for $x$ take an open $V \ni x$ meeting finitely many domain supports; $O = \pi^{-1}(\pi(V))$ is open by Proposition 7.1.8 and saturated. If $\Lambda_l(w) > 0$ for a vector $w \ne 0$ over $y \in O$, a morphism $\varphi : y \to v$ with $v \in V$ moves $w$ to $\mu(\varphi, w) \ne 0$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4SM_LocallyFiniteBridge · SBLocalization.μ_ne_fiberZero_lf⟧ with the same weight, so $v$ lies in the domain support of $\Lambda_l$ and in $V$. The saturation of the domain support is not needed. So Proposition 13.3.19 holds with the hypothesis as printed ⟦Chapter13/P3W4SM_LocallyFiniteBridge · SBLocalization.proposition_13_3_19_locallyFinite⟧, and for any family over a paracompact $|X|$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4SM_LocallyFiniteBridge · SBLocalization.proposition_13_3_19_locallyFinite_of_paracompact⟧.

### XIII.22 Theorem 13.5.3 (2017: 13.6) and the last clause of Theorem 13.5.5 (2017: 13.8): atomic sc⁺-multisections are structurable

**The data of the proof** ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData⟧. Let $\Lambda$ be atomic with data at $x_0$: $U(x_0)$, $V(x_0)$ with $\operatorname{cl}V(x_0) \subset U(x_0)$, sections $s_i$, $i \in I$. Let $Z = \pi^{-1}\pi(\operatorname{cl}V(x_0))$, closed and saturated ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData.isClosed_Z⟧ by the properness of $t$ on $s^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}U(x_0))$. For $y \in Z$ there are an open $O(y) \ni y$ and an sc-smooth choice $\tau_y$ of morphisms on it with $t(\tau_y(z)) = z$ and $s(\tau_y(z)) \in U(x_0)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.exists_atomicStructData⟧, from the local transports of §XIII.19.

**The partner homomorphisms.** For points $y, y'$ and a morphism $\psi$ between points near them, the morphism $\tau_{y'}(t\psi)^{-1} \circ \psi \circ \tau_y(s\psi)$ joins two points of $U(x_0)$, so it is $\Gamma(h, \cdot)$ for a unique $h \in G_{x_0}$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData.existsUnique_rel⟧; call it $H(\psi)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData.H⟧ (and $H = 1$ off $Z$). $H$ is functorial: $H(\psi' \circ \psi) = H(\psi')H(\psi)$, $H(1_z) = 1$, $H(\psi^{-1}) = H(\psi)^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData.H_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData.H_unit⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData.H_inv⟧. It is locally constant ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData.H_eventually⟧: the conjugated morphism depends continuously on $\psi$, and a continuous choice among the finitely many sheets $\Gamma(h, \cdot)$, $h \in G_{x_0}$, which are separated since $X$ is Hausdorff, is locally constant ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.eventually_eq_of_existsUnique⟧. At $y \in Z$, $\gamma_y(g) = H(\Gamma(g, y))$ is a homomorphism $G_y \to G_{x_0}$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData.γ⟧, the text's $\gamma_x$.

**The structure.** *Good system* ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData.𝒰⟧: inside the given one, with the same natural actions, small enough that $H(\Gamma(g, z)) = \gamma_y(g)$ for $z \in U(y)$, $y \in Z$, and $U(y) \cap Z = \emptyset$ for $y \notin Z$. *Sections* ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData.sec⟧: index set $I$ at every point; on $U(y)$ for $y \in Z$ the sections $z \mapsto \mu(\tau_y(z)^{-1}, s_i(s\tau_y(z)))$, and zero sections for $y \notin Z$. They are equivariant through $\gamma_y$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData.sec_compat⟧, and they represent $\Lambda$ by the count of Definition 13.5.1 (3). *Correspondences* ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData.corr⟧: for $\varphi$ between $U(y)$ and $U(y')$, the diagram $[I \xleftarrow{\mathrm{id}} I \xrightarrow{H(\varphi)} I]$ when $y, y'$ are both in $Z$ or both outside it, and the full correspondence $[I \leftarrow I \times I \to I]$ otherwise ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.full⟧; in the second case $\Lambda$ is trivial on both sides near the morphisms that occur. Definitions 13.3.4 (1)–(3) and 13.3.6 (1)–(2) follow from the functoriality and local constancy of $H$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData.tau⟧, and $\Lambda$ is structurable ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.AtomicStructData.isStructurable⟧. The text uses the index set $\{*\}$ where $\Lambda$ is trivial; $I$ with zero sections is another structure in the sense of Definition 13.3.6, so this is a different witness, not a different statement.

**Theorem 13.5.3** (narrower) ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_3_of_goodSystem⟧: if $X$ has a good system, every atomic sc⁺-multisection is structurable. *The added hypothesis*, that a good system exists, is not derived from the text, whose statement assumes nothing on $X$; it is necessary, since Definition 13.3.6 includes a good system: for atomic $\Lambda$, structurable is equivalent to the existence of a good system ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_3⟧. Its witness is Theorem 13.1.8 for paracompact $|X|$ ⟦Chapter13/P3G_GoodSystemExistence · EpGroupoid.theorem_13_1_8⟧, which gives the form ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_3_of_paracompact⟧. **The last clause of Theorem 13.5.5** (narrower, same hypothesis) ⟦Chapter13/P3W3C_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_5_structurable⟧: the atomic $\Lambda$ of Construction II is structurable; this is wave 2's hypothesis form ⟦Chapter13/P3A_AtomicStructurable · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_5_structurable_hyp⟧ discharged by Theorem 13.5.3. The local alternatives of §XIII.20 remain as a step of the proof.

### XIII.23 Theorems 13.4.1 and 13.4.4 (2017: 13.3 and 13.5): pull-backs along equivalences and coverings

**The common setting** ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_PullMap · SBLocalization.PullMap⟧. Both theorems pull back along a map of strong bundles $\Phi : W \to W'$ over a functor $F : X \to X'$ that is a local sc-diffeomorphism on objects, a linear homeomorphism on fibres and faithful. Strong bundle equivalences ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_PullMap · SBLocalization.PullMap.ofEquivalence⟧ and proper strong bundle coverings ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_PullMap · SBLocalization.PullMap.ofCovering⟧ are such maps. The pull-back $\Phi^*\Lambda' = \Lambda' \circ \Phi$ is an sc⁺-multisection ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.PullMap.isScPlusMultisection_pull⟧.

**Adapted neighbourhoods** ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.PullMap.IsPullNbhd⟧: for a good system $\mathcal U'$ of $X'$, a neighbourhood $U(x)$ with the natural action of $G_x$ is adapted if $F$ is injective on $U(x)$, $F(U(x)) \subset U'(F(x))$, and $F(\Gamma(g, z)) = \Gamma'(F(g), F(z))$. They exist inside every open set, with the properness property ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.PullMap.exists_isPullNbhd⟧: a small natural representation at $x$ is carried by $F$ into $U'(F(x))$, and faithfulness identifies $G_x$ with a subgroup of $G'_{F(x)}$. A good system of adapted neighbourhoods exists ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.PullMap.exists_pullData⟧; on it, components of morphisms are carried to components ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.PullMap.isDiffeoComponent_of_isPull⟧. The text arranges $F(U(x)) = U'(F(x))$ "without loss of generality"; the inclusion with injectivity is all that is used.

**The structure** ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.PullMap.pullTuple⟧: index sets $I_x = I'_{F(x)}$; sections $\Phi^{-1} \circ s'^{F(x)}_i \circ F$ on $U(x)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_PullMap · SBLocalization.PullMap.pullSec⟧, sc⁺ because $F$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism and $\Phi$ fibrewise a linear homeomorphism ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_PullMap · SBLocalization.PullMap.isScPlusSectionOn_pullSec⟧; actions of $G_x$ through $F$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.PullMap.pullStructure⟧; correspondences $\tau_{x,y}(\varphi) = \tau'_{F(x),F(y)}(F(\varphi))$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.PullMap.pullTau⟧, whose conditions are those of $\tau'$ carried along the homomorphisms $G_x \to G'_{F(x)}$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.PullMap.biact_compHom⟧. So $\Phi^*\Lambda'$ is structurable ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.PullMap.isStructurable_pull⟧. *Canonicity* ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.PullMap.pullTuple_equiv⟧: equivalent structured tuples, pulled back over any two adapted good systems, give equivalent tuples, so the pull-back is a map of structured classes ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.PullMap.pullStructured⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.PullMap.pullStructured_mk⟧ over the pull-back of functors ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.PullMap.forget_pullStructured⟧.

**Theorem 13.4.1** (stronger) ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.theorem_13_4_1⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.theorem_13_4_1_structured⟧: for a strong bundle equivalence over the equivalence $F$, $\Phi^*\Lambda'$ is structurable when $\Lambda'$ is, and there is a map of structured classes over $\Phi^*$, given on every representative and every adapted good system by the structure above. The text's "canonical way" is read as this map; its independence of all choices is asserted in the text and proved here. **Theorem 13.4.4** (as printed) ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.theorem_13_4_4⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pullback · SBLocalization.theorem_13_4_4_structured⟧: the same for a proper strong bundle covering, the 2021 Definition 8.5.9, with the same canonicity. The text's disjoint decomposition $F^{-1}(U(x)) = \bigsqcup V(z)$ is not needed: adapted neighbourhoods suffice. Neither theorem uses paracompactness or an added hypothesis.

### XIII.24 Theorem 13.4.3 (2017: 13.4) without Proposition 13.4.2, and generalized strong bundle isomorphisms

**Charts along a morphism** ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_PushChart · SBLocalization.PushChart⟧. Let $\Phi$ be a strong bundle equivalence over $F : X \to X'$. For every $y \in X'$, essential surjectivity gives $x_y$ and a morphism $\sigma_y : F(x_y) \to y$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_PushChart · SBLocalization.pushChart⟧; Chapter 10's transport chart is $Q = t \circ (s|_{\text{sheet of } \sigma_y})^{-1} \circ F$ near $x_y$, with morphisms $\psi_u : F(u) \to Q(u)$. Conjugation by $\sigma_y$ identifies $G_{x_y}$ with $G'_y$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_PushChart · SBLocalization.conjEquiv⟧. *Push neighbourhoods* ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_PushChart · SBLocalization.IsPushNbhd⟧: $U'(y) \subset Q(U(x_y))$, and the natural action of $G'_y$ is $\Gamma'(\psi F(g) \psi^{-1}, Q(u)) = \psi_{g*u} \circ F(\Gamma(g, u)) \circ \psi_u^{-1}$. They exist, with properness ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_PushChart · SBLocalization.exists_isPushNbhd⟧.

**Sections and lifted morphisms.** The pushed section is $z = Q(u) \mapsto \mu'(\psi_u, \Phi(s(u)))$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_PushChart · SBLocalization.pushSec⟧, sc⁺ on $U'(y)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_PushChart · SBLocalization.IsPushNbhd.isScPlusSectionOn_pushSec⟧, and the sections of a structure at $x_y$ push to one at $y$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_PushChart · SBLocalization.pushStructure⟧. A morphism $\varphi'$ between points of $U'(y)$ and $U'(y')$ lifts to the unique $\varphi$ with $\psi'_{u'} \circ F(\varphi) = \varphi' \circ \psi_u$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.PushChart.liftMor⟧, by full faithfulness ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.PushChart.comp_liftMor⟧. The lift is continuous ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.PushChart.continuousOn_liftMor⟧ because a map into the morphisms of $X$ is continuous when its source, target and $F$-image are, $F$ being faithful and a local sc-diffeomorphism ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.PushChart.continuousAt_of_mor⟧; it is injective, functorial and compatible with $\Gamma$ and the bi-action ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.PushChart.liftMor_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.PushChart.liftMor_Γ⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.PushChart.liftMor_biact⟧, carries components to components ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.PushChart.isDiffeoComponent_push⟧, and the pushed sections are compatible along it ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.PushChart.pushSec_compat⟧.

**The structure** ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.pushTuple⟧: good system of push neighbourhoods ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.pushGood⟧, $I'_y = I_{x_y}$, the pushed sections ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.pushDecoration⟧, and $\tau'_{y,y'}(\varphi') = \tau_{x_y,x_{y'}}(\mathrm{lift}\,\varphi')$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.pushTau⟧; the conditions of $\tau'$ are those of $\tau$ through the lift. **Theorem 13.4.3** (as printed) ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.theorem_13_4_3⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.theorem_13_4_3_structured⟧: $\Phi_*\Lambda$, Chapter 11's push-forward, is structurable when $\Lambda$ is. The text structures $\Phi_*\Lambda$ on $F(X)$ through $F|_{U(x_y)}$ and then extends by Proposition 13.4.2 from $F(X)$, with $|F(X)| = |X'|$; the formal proof gives every $y$, in $F(X)$ or not, a chart along $\sigma_y$, which does both steps at once, and does not use Proposition 13.4.2. No canonicity is claimed, as in the text.

**Generalized strong bundle isomorphisms** (the opening of §16.5 and the interior case of Proposition 14.1.8). Composing the two theorems along a diagram of strong bundle equivalences: push-forwards and pull-backs of structurable sc⁺-multisections along a diagram ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.SDiagram.isStructurable_pushMult⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.SDiagram.isStructurable_pullMult⟧ and along a generalized strong bundle isomorphism ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.isStructurable_pushMult⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.isStructurable_pullMult⟧ are structurable, as the text says "follows immediately". The boundary version, Proposition 14.1.8, is Part XIV's (§XIV.4).

### XIII.25 Definition 13.4.5 (2017: 13.22): commensurable structured sc⁺-multisections and their sums

**The choice $c$** ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.CommData⟧: a good system, nonempty finite index sets $I_x$ with $G_x$-actions, and maps $\tau_{x,x'}$ with the conditions of Definitions 13.3.4 (1)–(2) and 13.3.6 (1)–(2) that do not involve sections. The actions are determined by $\tau$, by Definition 13.3.6 (1) at $x' = x$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.CommData.smul_eq_of_diag⟧, so including them adds nothing to "$\tau_1 = \tau_2$". Sections over $c$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.CommData.Sections⟧ are sc⁺, equivariant and compatible with $\tau$ (Definition 13.3.4 (3)); data over $c$ for $\Lambda$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.CommData.Over⟧ add the counting formula for $\Lambda$ on every $U(x)$, and give a structured tuple and class ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.CommData.Over.toStructured⟧. Every structured tuple is of this form ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.CommData.Over.ofTuple_toTuple⟧. Nonemptiness of $I_x$ holds for the data of every structured multisection and is needed for the empty family below.

**Definition 13.4.5 (1)** (restated) ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.Commensurable⟧: two structured classes are commensurable if they have representatives over one common $c$; it is reflexive and symmetric ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.Commensurable.symm⟧. The paracompactness of $|X|$ in the text's setting is not needed for the definition.

**Definition 13.4.5 (2)** (as printed) ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.CommData.definition_13_4_5⟧: over a common $c$ the sum with sections $s^x_i = s^{1,x}_i + s^{2,x}_i$ and $\Lambda(w) = |I_x|^{-1}\#\{i : s^x_i(P(w)) = w\}$ on $U(x)$ is an sc⁺-multisection with these data. The "well defined" the text calls evident is two facts. *The count does not depend on $x$* ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.CommData.Sections.countAt_eq⟧: along a correspondence the normalized counts $|I_x|^{-1}\#\{i : s_i = v\}$ and $|I_{x'}|^{-1}\#\{j : s'_j = \mu(\varphi, v)\}$ agree ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.count_eq_of_sat⟧, because a saturated diagram with the same number of elements over each index is a uniform cover. *The count of any sections over $c$ is an sc⁺-multisection* ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.CommData.Sections.isScPlusMultisection_sumMult⟧, with local structure the sections themselves. Sums of sections are sections over $c$ because $\mu(\psi, \cdot)$ is additive ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.fibAct_finsum⟧. **The locally finite commensurable sum** (as printed) ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.CommData.definition_13_4_5_lf⟧: for a locally finite family over one $c$, the sections $\sum_j s^{j,x}_i$, finite near each point ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.CommData.sumSec_eq_sectionSum⟧, are sections over $c$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.CommData.lfSections⟧, and their count is the sum. The binary sum is the locally finite sum over a two-element index set ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_Commensurable · SBLocalization.CommData.commSum₂⟧. "Pairwise commensurable" is read as "over one common $c$", which is what the text's $[\Lambda_j, \mathcal U, S_j, \tau]$ writes.

### XIII.26 Theorem 13.5.7 (2017: 13.10): decomposition into commensurable atomic pieces

**Atomic on a neighbourhood with the natural action** (extra) ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_AtomicSum · SBLocalization.AtomicDataOn⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_AtomicSum · SBLocalization.IsAtomicOn⟧. Definition 13.5.1 with "$G_x$-invariant $U(x)$" read as a neighbourhood with the natural action, the reading of §13.1, rather than as the connected domain of a natural representation (§XIII.19); the sets of a good system are of this kind. Atomic in the sense of §XIII.19 implies atomic in this sense ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_AtomicSum · SBLocalization.IsAtomic.isAtomicOn⟧.

**Theorem 13.5.7** (stronger) ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_AtomicSum · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_7⟧: if $X$ has sc-smooth partitions of unity, then for every structured tuple $T$ with multisection $\Lambda$ there are a locally finite family $(\Lambda_j)_{j \in X}$, each atomic on a neighbourhood with the natural action, and data over the choice $c$ of $T$ for each, such that the locally finite commensurable sum is $\Lambda$, its sections are those of $T$ on every $U(x)$, and its structured class is that of $T$. *Proof.* For each $x$ choose an open $O_x \ni |x|$ in $|X|$ with closure in $|U(x)|$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_AtomicSum · SBLocalization.exists_orbit_nbhd⟧, by the regularity of $|X|$ (Lemma 7.3.5). Take an sc-smooth partition of unity $(\beta_x)$ subordinate to $(\pi^{-1}(O_x))$, and $\Lambda_j = \beta_j \odot \Lambda$ with data $\beta_j s^x_i$ over $c$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_AtomicSum · SBLocalization.CommData.smulFunOver⟧, the product with functions of §XIII.15. $\Lambda_j$ is atomic at $x_j = j$, with $V = U(j) \cap \pi^{-1}(O_j)$, whose closure lies in $U(j)$ by Lemma 13.1.1 (§XIII.1), and the sections $\beta_j s^j_i$, which vanish off $V$; off the saturation of $U(j)$, $\Lambda_j$ is trivial ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_AtomicSum · SBLocalization.multisectionSmulFun_of_eq_zero⟧. The family is locally finite because the partition of unity is, and $\sum_j \beta_j = 1$ gives the sum. *Stronger:* for every structured lift, not only one; the class equality is literal; and the paracompactness of $|X|$ is not used. The text's form ⟦Chapter13/P3W3Q_AtomicSum · SBLocalization.theorem_13_5_7_book⟧ keeps it as an unused hypothesis.

### XIII.27 Witnesses and the hypotheses of waves 3 and 4

**Hypotheses taken.** *§XIII.22.* That $X$ has a good system, in Theorem 13.5.3 and the last clause of Theorem 13.5.5; not derived from the text; necessary (structurable is equivalent to it for atomic $\Lambda$); witness Theorem 13.1.8 for paracompact $|X|$, for instance every M-polyfold seen as a trivial ep-groupoid (§XIII.10). *§XIII.21.* For the empty family the same hypothesis, which Definition 13.3.6 requires; a nonempty family needs none. *None added* to Theorems 13.4.1, 13.4.3, 13.4.4, Definition 13.4.5 or Theorem 13.5.7. *Kept and unused.* Paracompactness of $|X|$ in Theorem 13.5.7 and in the setting of Definition 13.4.5.

**Every definition has a witness.** Adapted neighbourhoods and push neighbourhoods: inside every open set (§§XIII.23–XIII.24). Choices $c$ and data over them: those of any structured tuple, for instance the zero multisection's (§XIII.25). Commensurability: reflexivity. Atomic on a neighbourhood with the natural action: every atomic multisection, for instance the zero multisection (§XIII.19).

### XIII.28 Proposition 13.4.2 (2017: 13.6): extension of a structured sc⁺-multisection from an open $V$ with $|V| = |X|$

**Structured data on $V$.** The text takes the strong bundle $W|V$ over the open full sub-ep-groupoid $V$ and a structured sc⁺-multisection on it. The project has no strong bundle over an open sub-ep-groupoid, so the data are read relative to $V$ inside $W$. A functor on $W|V$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.IsWFunctorOn⟧ is a $\Lambda : W \to \mathbb Q^+$ invariant along morphisms with both ends in $V$; an sc⁺-multisection on $W|V$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisectionOn⟧ is such a functor with a local section structure around every $q \in V$ on the domain of a natural representation inside $V$. Structured data on $V$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.StructuredOn⟧ are Definitions 13.3.4 and 13.3.6 with every index in $V$: neighbourhoods $U(q) \subset V$ with the natural action, good in the sense of Theorem 13.1.7 as printed relative to $V$ (§XIII.13), symmetric structures $(I_q, s^q_i)$ representing $\Lambda$ on $U(q)$, and correspondences $\tau_{q,q'}$ on $\mathcal U(q, q')$, locally constant with finitely many values, with the bi-action, the compatibility with the sections, the diagonal and the swap. Every structured tuple on $X$ gives such data with $V = X$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.StructuredTuple.toStructuredOn⟧, for instance the zero multisection's.

**The extension functor** ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.extendMult⟧: $\bar\Lambda(w) = \Lambda(w_0)$ for a $w_0$ over $V$ in the orbit of $w$, which exists because $|V| = |X|$. It is a functor on $W$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.isWFunctor_extendMult⟧, it equals $\Lambda$ over $V$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.extendMult_eq⟧, because two vectors over $V$ in one orbit are joined by a morphism inside $V$ and $\Lambda$ is a functor there, and every functor on $W$ that agrees with $\Lambda$ over $V$ is $\bar\Lambda$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.eq_extendMult⟧, since every orbit meets $V$. This uniqueness is how "canonical" is read.

**Charts.** For every $x$ choose $q_x \in V$ and a morphism $\psi_x : q_x \to x$; the transport chart of the identity equivalence along $\psi_x$ (Part XIII, §XIII.24, with $F = \mathrm{id}$) ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.ExtChart⟧ carries $U(q_x)$ to a push neighbourhood $U(x)$ with the natural action and the properness property, inside $O(x)$ when $x \notin V$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.IsPushNbhd.of_le⟧. At $q \in V$ the *unit chart* is used: $q_x = q$, $\psi_x = 1_q$, $Q = \mathrm{id}$ and $U(q)$ the given one ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.unitChart⟧, which is a push neighbourhood of itself ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.isPushNbhd_unit⟧; on it the pushed sections are the given sections ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.pushSec_unit⟧ and the lifted morphisms the given morphisms ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.liftMor_unit⟧. The identity is an equivalence ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.equivalences_id_sep⟧, and the push-forward of a functor along it is the functor ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_ExtensionData · SBLocalization.pushMult_id⟧.

**Proposition 13.4.2** (restated) ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_Extension · SBLocalization.proposition_13_4_2⟧: let $V$ be open with $|V| = |X|$ and structured data on $V$ for $\Lambda$ be given. (1) $\bar\Lambda$ is an sc⁺-multisection on $W$, equal to $\Lambda$ over $V$ and the only functor on $W$ with this property. (2) For every family of open $O(x) \ni x$ there is a structured tuple for $\bar\Lambda$ whose neighbourhoods at $q \in V$ are the given $U(q)$, with $U(x) \subset O(x)$ for $x \notin V$, and whose index sets with their $G_q$-actions, sections on $U(q)$ and correspondences on $\mathcal U(q, q')$ are the given ones at the points of $V$, through the identifications of the index types. *Proof.* (1): at every $x$ the sections of the structure at $q_x$, pushed along the chart of $x$, are a local section structure for $\bar\Lambda$ on $U(x)$ ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_Extension · SBLocalization.isScPlusMultisection_extendMult⟧, as for Theorem 13.4.3. (2): the structured tuple ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_Extension · SBLocalization.extTuple⟧ has the good system of the chart neighbourhoods, $I_x = I_{q_x}$ with the pushed sections, and $\tau_{x,x'}(\varphi) = \tau_{q_x,q_{x'}}(\mathrm{lift}\,\varphi)$ for the morphism lifted through both charts. The text distinguishes three cases for $\tau$ (both ends in $V$, one end, neither); the lift covers them uniformly, and at points of $V$, where the charts are unit charts, the lift is the morphism itself, so the given data are kept. Uniqueness in (1) comes from the extension functor. *Structurable* ⟦Chapter13/P3W5FM_Extension · SBLocalization.proposition_13_4_2_structurable⟧: $\bar\Lambda$ is structurable. *Restated*: the structured data relative to $V$ replace a structure on the bundle $W|V$, and the good-system condition on $V$ is that of Theorem 13.1.7 as printed for the open $V$; "canonical" is uniqueness among functors. No hypothesis is added. Theorem 13.4.3 does not use the proposition (§XIII.24); the two proofs share the push charts, which here serve the identity equivalence.

### XIII.29 Witnesses and the hypotheses of wave 5

**Hypotheses taken.** *§XIII.28.* None added. The data on $V$ are inhabited by `StructuredTuple.toStructuredOn` ($V = X$, any structured tuple, for instance the zero multisection on a paracompact orbit space).

**Every definition has a witness.** Functors and sc⁺-multisections on $W|V$, structured data on $V$: those of any structured tuple with $V = X$. Charts for the extension: unit charts at the points of $V$.

## Part XIV. Extension of sc⁺-multisections (HWZ Chapter 14, §§14.1–14.6)

Chapter 14 (Springer 2021, pp. 637–682; 2017 numbers in parentheses) proves the ∂-extension theorem: a structurable sc⁺-multisection functor $\Lambda : W|\partial X \to \mathbb Q^+$ over the boundary of a tame ep-groupoid extends to a structurable $\Lambda' : W \to \mathbb Q^+$ with controlled size and support. §14.1 defines good boundary neighbourhoods, sc⁺-multisections and structured ones over $\partial X$, and states the theorem (Proposition 14.1.1, Definitions 14.1.2, 14.1.3, Proposition 14.1.4, Definition 14.1.5, Theorem 14.1.6, Definition 14.1.7, Proposition 14.1.8, Theorem 14.1.9, Remark 14.1.10 (2017: Remark 14.1, Definitions 14.1, 14.2, Remark 14.2, Definition 14.3, Theorem 14.1, Definition 14.4, Proposition 14.1, Theorem 14.2, Remark 14.3)). §14.2 chooses a good structured representative (Lemmas 14.2.1, 14.2.2, Proposition 14.2.3 (2017: the text before Lemma 14.1, Lemma 14.1, Proposition 14.2)). §14.3 extends the correspondences off the boundary and covers $\partial X$ by the sets $\hat V_a$ (Lemma 14.3.1, Definition 14.3.2, Lemma 14.3.3, Proposition 14.3.4, Remark 14.3.5, Lemmas 14.3.6, 14.3.7, Proposition 14.3.8 (2017: Lemma 14.2, the text before Lemma 14.3, Lemma 14.3, Proposition 14.3, Remark 14.4, Lemmas 14.4, 14.5, Proposition 14.4)). §14.4 controls the index sets by z-loops and extends the boundary sections near each $\hat V_a$ (Remark 14.4.1, Definitions 14.4.2–14.4.4, Lemma 14.4.5, Proposition 14.4.6, Lemma 14.4.7, Definition 14.4.8, Lemma 14.4.9, Proposition 14.4.10, Definition 14.4.11, Remark 14.4.12, Lemma 14.4.13, Proposition 14.4.14 (2017: Remark 14.5, Definitions 14.5–14.7, Lemma 14.6, Proposition 14.5, Lemma 14.7, Definition 14.8, Lemma 14.8, Proposition 14.6, Definition 14.9, Remark 14.6, Lemma 14.9, Proposition 14.7)). §14.5 transports the local extensions and assembles them (Lemmas 14.5.1, 14.5.2, Remark 14.5.3, Proposition 14.5.4, Theorem 14.5.5 (2017: Lemmas 14.10, 14.11, Remark 14.7, Proposition 14.8, Theorem 14.3)), and §14.6 builds boundary data face by face (Definitions 14.6.1, 14.6.2, Theorem 14.6.3 (2017: Definitions 14.10, 14.11, Theorem 14.4)). This Part retells §14.1 (§§XIV.1–XIV.5), §14.2 (§XIV.6), §14.3 (§§XIV.7–XIV.8), §14.4 (§§XIV.9–XIV.12) and §14.5 (§XIV.13); then the witnesses (§XIV.14), what is not formalized (§XIV.15) and what the formalization taught us (§XIV.16), then, in wave 5, the faces of a good neighbourhood as tame M-polyfolds (§XIV.17), Proposition 14.1.8 over $\partial X$ (§XIV.18), the setting of §14.4 from the objects of §14.3 (§XIV.19), Proposition 14.4.6 (2) and what follows from it (§XIV.20), the proof of Proposition 14.5.4 (§XIV.21), the sum over $a$ and the assembly of Theorem 14.1.9 (§XIV.22), §14.6 (§XIV.23) and the witnesses of wave 5 (§XIV.24).

**What is proved, and what is not.** Waves 3–5 of Part III (2026-11-13) formalize Chapter 14. Every step of the construction of §§14.3–14.5 is proved, and the ∂-extension theorem is proved from the data of that construction; the instance of the data for a given $\Lambda$ is a hypothesis whose witness covers only $\partial X = \emptyset$. *§14.1.* Proposition 14.1.1 is proved as printed (§XIV.1). Definitions 14.1.2, 14.1.3, 14.1.5 and 14.1.7 are formalized (§§XIV.1–XIV.2, XIV.4), and the remark after Definition 14.1.2, that the faces $\bar\theta_j$ are tame M-polyfolds, is proved (§XIV.17); gap G.165 is closed. Proposition 14.1.4 is proved as printed (§XIV.3). Theorem 14.1.6 is proved with tameness of $X$ and paracompactness of $|X|$ in place of the paracompactness of $|\partial X|$, which is what its proof uses (§XIV.2). Proposition 14.1.8 is proved in its interior case, along generalized strong bundle isomorphisms of the whole bundle (Part XIII, §XIII.24), and over $\partial X$ for a representative with tame middle, with two hypotheses on the transport of face-wise sc⁺ sections, one of them witnessed only for empty boundary (§XIV.18); gap G.164 is formalized in part. Theorem 14.1.9 is stated as printed and proved from the hypothesis that every structurable $\Lambda$ over $\partial X$ has the data of §§14.3–14.5; the size control (§XIV.5) and the assembly (§XIV.22) are proved. Remark 14.1.10 is prose. *§14.2.* Lemmas 14.2.1, 14.2.2 and Proposition 14.2.3 are proved as printed (§XIV.6). *§14.3.* Lemma 14.3.1 is proved in a stronger form, with the extended sets symmetric under inversion; Definition 14.3.2 is formalized, Lemma 14.3.3 and Proposition 14.3.4 are proved as printed, the diagonal property of Proposition 14.3.4 by an argument the text does not give (§XIV.7). Lemma 14.3.6 and Proposition 14.3.8 are proved with the hypotheses their proofs use made explicit, and Lemma 14.3.7 in a stronger form (§XIV.8). Remark 14.3.5 states nothing to prove. *§14.4.* Definitions 14.4.2–14.4.4 and 14.4.8 are formalized, with the equivalence-relation properties the text asserts proved; Lemmas 14.4.5 and 14.4.7 are proved (§§XIV.9–XIV.10). The setting has an instance from the objects of §14.3 (§XIV.19); gap G.169 is closed. Proposition 14.4.6 is proved, (1) as printed and without Lemma 14.4.7 (§XIV.10), (2) as printed and in a stronger form, for $z_k \in \hat V_a$ and every $z_0 \in \operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$ (§XIV.20); gap G.168 is closed. Lemma 14.4.9, Proposition 14.4.10 and the existence in Definition 14.4.11 are proved as printed, (3) of the lemma in a stronger form (§§XIV.10–XIV.11, XIV.20). Lemma 14.4.13 is proved, its (2) for points of $\operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$ (§XIV.11). Proposition 14.4.14 is proved by a construction different from the text's, for the objects of §14.3 under the hypotheses of Proposition 14.1.4 (§§XIV.12, XIV.20). Remarks 14.4.1 and 14.4.12 are prose. *§14.5.* Lemma 14.5.1 is proved in a stronger form, without tameness; Theorem 14.5.5, the structurability criterion, in a stronger form, without the properness and closure conditions (a), (b) (§XIV.13). Proposition 14.5.4 is proved, restated with the property of the cut-offs that Lemma 14.5.1 (1) gives (§XIV.21); gap G.170 is closed. The sum identity of Lemma 14.5.2 is proved for the sections, which is how the proof of Theorem 14.1.9 uses it; the commensurable family over $\partial X$ is not built (§XIV.22). Remark 14.5.3 is prose. *§14.6.* The faces are Part XI's ep-faces; Definitions 14.6.1 and 14.6.2 are formalized, with sc⁺ on a face read through the charts of $X$, and Theorem 14.6.3 is proved for representatives that agree on the overlaps of faces, its extension part from Theorem 14.1.9 (§XIV.23); gap G.173 is formalized in part. *Open:* G.164, G.171 and G.172 in part, G.173 in part, and the new gaps of §XIV.15. No statement of Chapter 14 was found not to hold as we read it.
