Throughout, $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ is a strong bundle over an ep-groupoid $X$ with source and target maps $s$, $t$, orbit map $\pi : X \to |X|$, and $\partial X$ the set of objects of degeneracy index $d_X \ge 1$. A neighbourhood with the natural action of $G_x$ is Part XIII's (§XIII.1); good systems, symmetric structures, correspondences and structurable sc⁺-multisections are those of Part XIII. $\mathcal U(x, x') = \{\varphi : s(\varphi) \in U(x),\ t(\varphi) \in U(x')\}$.

### XIV.1 Proposition 14.1.1 (2017: Remark 14.1) and Definition 14.1.2 (2017: 14.1): good boundary neighbourhoods

**Faces at a point** ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodBoundary · EpGroupoid.HasBoundaryFaces⟧: for $x \in \partial X$ and an open $V \ni x$, sets $\theta_1, \dots, \theta_{d_X(x)}$, components of $\{d_X = 1\} \cap V$, with $x$ in the closure of each in $V$, $d_X(y) = \#\{i : y \in \bar\theta_i\}$ on $V$, and $V \cap \partial X = \bigcup_i \bar\theta_i$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodBoundary · EpGroupoid.HasBoundaryFaces.inter_boundary_eq⟧. Here $\bar\theta_i$ is the closure in $V$.

**Proposition 14.1.1** (as printed) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodBoundary · EpGroupoid.proposition_14_1_1⟧: in a tame ep-groupoid, every $x \in \partial X$ has, inside every open $W \ni x$, an open $V(x)$ with the natural $G_x$-action, $t$ proper on $s^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}_X V(x))$, $V(x)$ and $V(x) \cap \partial X$ connected, and faces as above. "Arbitrarily small" is read as "inside any open $W \ni x$". *Proof.* Take a neighbourhood with the natural action and the properness property inside $W$ (Part XIII, §XIII.1). Part I's abstract face calculus (`Chapter2/TameBoundary`: the faces at a point and centred face-structured sets) supplies the faces: the connected component of $x$ in a small invariant open set is centred at $x$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodBoundary · TameBoundary.isCenteredAt_connectedComponentIn⟧, its faces are preconnected ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodBoundary · TameBoundary.isPreconnected_faceAt⟧, and the degeneracy index on it counts the faces through a point ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodBoundary · TameBoundary.connectedComponentIn_inter_deg_of_mem_cc⟧. Shrinking to the component of $x$ keeps the natural action, since $G_x$ fixes $x$ and permutes components. A relative form keeps a given natural action and shrinks inside it ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodBoundary · EpGroupoid.exists_isGoodBoundaryNbhd_le⟧. The text's argument goes through charts; the face calculus replaces it.

**Definition 14.1.2** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodBoundary · EpGroupoid.IsGoodBoundaryNbhd⟧: a neighbourhood $V(x)$ with the natural action is good if it has the properties of Proposition 14.1.1; $U(x) = V(x) \cap \partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodBoundary · EpGroupoid.NatNbhd.bdry⟧. The remarks after the definition: $U(x) = \bigcup_i \bar\theta_i$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodBoundary · EpGroupoid.IsGoodBoundaryNbhd.bdry_eq⟧, $U(x)$ is invariant under the natural action ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodBoundary · EpGroupoid.NatNbhd.mapsTo_Φ_bdry⟧, which preserves the degeneracy index ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodBoundary · EpGroupoid.NatNbhd.degIndex_Φ⟧, and the faces lie in $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodBoundary · EpGroupoid.IsGoodBoundaryNbhd.mem_boundary⟧. Good neighbourhoods exist at every boundary point of a tame $X$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodBoundary · EpGroupoid.exists_isGoodBoundaryNbhd⟧. The remark that the $\bar\theta_j$ are tame M-polyfolds is proved in wave 5 (§XIV.17).

### XIV.2 Definitions 14.1.3, 14.1.5 (2017: 14.2, 14.3) and Theorem 14.1.6 (2017: 14.1): sc⁺-multisections and good systems over $\partial X$

**Face-wise sc⁺-sections** ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.IsFaceScPlusSectionOn⟧: a section over a set $U \subset \partial X$ is face-wise sc⁺ if, in every tame strong bundle chart and at every point of $U$, it is sc⁺ on every local face germ: Part I's Definition 5.4.1 with $\partial X$ replaced by $U$. This is the reading of "$s|\bar\theta_j$ is sc⁺": in a tame chart, the germs of the $\bar\theta_j$ at a point of $U(x)$ are the local faces there. The restriction of an sc⁺-section is face-wise sc⁺ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.isFaceScPlusSectionOn_of_isBoundaryScPlusSection⟧.

**Definition 14.1.3** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.BoundarySymmetricStructure⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.IsBoundaryScPlusMultisection⟧: a boundary symmetric structure on a good $V(x)$ is a finite index set $I_x$ with a $G_x$-action and face-wise sc⁺ sections $s^x_i$ on $U(x)$, equivariant, $s^x_{g(i)}(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g, y), s^x_i(y))$, and representing $\Lambda$ by $\Lambda(w) = |I_x|^{-1}\#\{i : s^x_i(P(w)) = w\}$ over $U(x)$. $\Lambda$ is an sc⁺-multisection over $\partial X$ if it is a functor on $W|\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.IsBoundaryWFunctor⟧, invariant along morphisms with source in $\partial X$, and has such a structure at every boundary point. Only the values over $\partial X$ enter. Witness: the zero multisection, with one index and the zero section, for tame $X$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.isBoundaryScPlusMultisection_zero⟧. The text's standing paracompactness of $|X|$ is not used.

**Definition 14.1.5** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · EpGroupoid.BoundaryGoodSystem⟧: a good system for $\partial X$ is a choice of good $V(x)$ with its natural action for every $x \in \partial X$ such that $s$ and $t$ map every component of $\mathcal U(x, x')$, with $U(x) = V(x) \cap \partial X$, sc-diffeomorphically onto open sets. The text says "there exist $V(x)$, $V(x')$" for each pair; one $V(x)$ is fixed for each $x$, which is how the proof of Theorem 14.1.6 chooses it. The condition passes to open subsets ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · EpGroupoid.BoundaryGoodSystem.isDiffeoComponent_of_subset⟧, and every good system has refinements inside any open sets, with the same actions ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · EpGroupoid.BoundaryGoodSystem.exists_refinement⟧.

**Theorem 14.1.6** (narrower) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · EpGroupoid.theorem_14_1_6_hyp⟧: for a tame $X$ with $|X|$ paracompact and open sets $O(x) \ni x$, there is a good system for $\partial X$ with $V(x) \subset O(x)$, so $U(x) \subset O(x) \cap \partial X$. *Proof*, the text's: Theorem 13.1.8 on $X$ gives a good system inside the $O(x)$ (Part XIII, §XIII.4), and Proposition 14.1.1 shrinks each of its neighbourhoods at boundary points to a good one with the same action. *The hypotheses* tameness of $X$ and paracompactness of $|X|$ replace the printed paracompactness of $|\partial X|$; they are not derived from the statement, but the text's proof uses both, through Theorem 13.1.8 and Proposition 14.1.1, and both are standing assumptions of the chapter. Witness: the trivial ep-groupoid of a tame quadrant ⟦Chapter7/TameBoundaryEp · EpGroupoid.trivial_quadrant_witness⟧, whose orbit space is paracompact ⟦Chapter7/EpGroupoid · EpGroupoid.hasParacompactOrbitSpace_trivial⟧. Sets open in $\partial X$ are written $O(x) \cap \partial X$ with $O(x)$ open in $X$.

### XIV.3 Proposition 14.1.4 (2017: Remark 14.2): the local extension

**Averaging** ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.avgSection⟧. For sc⁺-sections $s^0_i$ on $V(x)$, set $\bar s_j(y) = |G_x|^{-1}\sum_{g \in G_x}\mu(\Gamma(g^{-1}, g * y), s^0_{g(j)}(g * y))$. Each term is sc⁺ on $V(x)$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.isScPlusSectionOn_avgTerm⟧, so the average is ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.isScPlusSectionOn_avgSection⟧. It is equivariant ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.avgSection_equivariant⟧, by reindexing the sum along $g \mapsto gh$, and it equals $s^0$ wherever $s^0$ is already equivariant ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.avgSection_eq_of_equivariant⟧, in particular on $U(x)$ when $s^0_i = s_i$ there. So any non-equivariant extensions give the equivariant ones ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryMultisection · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_hyp⟧. The text averages over the stabilizer of $i$ and transports along the orbit; the average over all of $G_x$ gives the same symmetry and needs no orbit representatives.

**The non-equivariant extension on an open set** ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_OpenExtension · SBLocalization.exists_scPlusSectionOn_extension_of_face⟧: a face-wise sc⁺ section on $V \cap \partial X$, for any open $V$, extends to an sc⁺-section on $V$ equal to it on $V \cap \partial X$. *Locally*, Part I's ∂-extension step (Part V, §V.55, the inclusion–exclusion formula of Proposition 12.3.7) works with local hypotheses: near each point of $V$ there is a local sc⁺ extension ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_LocalExtension · StrongBundle.exists_local_extension_of_face⟧. *Gluing.* The object space is metrizable; let $G_n = \{\operatorname{dist}(\cdot, X \setminus V) > 1/(n+1)\}$. For each $n$, a partition of unity of $X$ glues the local extensions to a global sc⁺-section equal to the given one on $G_n \cap \partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_LocalExtension · SBLocalization.exists_scPlusSection_extension_of_face⟧. Sc-smooth cut-offs $\chi_n$ equal to $1$ on $\operatorname{cl}G_n$ and supported in $G_{n+1}$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_OpenExtension · SBLocalization.exists_scSmooth_cutoff_p3w4⟧ join these extensions with weights $\chi_n - \chi_{n-1}$, which are locally finite on $V$; being sc⁺ is local ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_OpenExtension · SBLocalization.IsScPlusSectionOn.of_locally_p3w4⟧. A single partition of unity of $X$ cannot do it: it would have to cover the frontier of $V$, where the face data may be unbounded.

**Proposition 14.1.4** (as printed) ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_OpenExtension · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_full⟧: if every object lies in a tame strong bundle chart and the objects admit sc-smooth partitions of unity, every boundary symmetric structure $(s_i)$ on $U(x)$ extends to sc⁺-sections $\bar s_i$ on $V(x)$ with $\bar s_i = s_i$ on $U(x)$ and the symmetry of Definition 13.2.5: the extension above for each $i$, then the average. The two hypotheses are the readings of the text's "strong bundle over a tame ep-groupoid" and "admits sc-smooth partitions of unity" (Definition 5.5.1 on the object M-polyfold), as in Theorem 12.3.9 (Part XII, §XII.18); witness: the trivial bundle $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R^n$ over the trivial ep-groupoid ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_OpenExtension · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_hypotheses_rn⟧. The paracompactness of $|X|$ and the goodness of $V(x)$ are not used. Variants with global sc⁺-sections on a smaller $V'$ with $\operatorname{cl}V' \subset V(x)$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_LocalExtension · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4_of_closure⟧, and on a good $V'(x)$ from Lemma 14.2.1 ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_LocalExtension · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_4⟧. The text calls the $\bar s_i$ "sc⁺-multisections"; presumably sc⁺-sections are meant.

### XIV.4 Definition 14.1.7 (2017: 14.4) and Proposition 14.1.8 (2017: 14.1): structured sc⁺-multisections over $\partial X$

**Decorations and their correspondences** ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryDecoration⟧: a good system for $\partial X$ with a boundary symmetric structure on each of its neighbourhoods. Correspondences for it ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryDecoration.Tau⟧ are maps $\tau_{x,x'} : \mathcal U(x, x') \to J(x, x')$, locally constant in $\mathcal U(x, x')$ with finitely many values, with (a) $\tau_{x',x}(\varphi^{-1}) = \tau_{x,x'}(\varphi)^\sharp$, (b) $\tau_{x,x}(\Gamma(g, z)) = [I_x \leftarrow I_x \to I_x]_{(\mathrm{Id}, g)}$, (c) compatibility with the bi-action, and (4) $s^{x'}_{b(k)}(t(\varphi)) = \mu(\varphi, s^x_{a(k)}(s(\varphi)))$ pointwise on $\mathcal U(x, x')$, as printed. A structured tuple is $\Lambda$ with a decoration and correspondences ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple⟧.

**Definition 14.1.7** (restated). *Equivalence* ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.Equiv⟧, the text's "similar to the $X$-case": the same $\Lambda$ over $\partial X$, and open $O(x) \ni x$ with $O(x) \cap \partial X$ inside both $U(x)$, on which the index sets and the correspondences agree. It is an equivalence relation ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.equivalence⟧; for tame $X$ it agrees with the literal analogue of Definition 13.3.8, with a common good system inside both ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.equiv_iff_goodSystem⟧, and the open-set form gives transitivity without tameness. Structured sc⁺-multisections over $\partial X$ are the classes ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredMultisection⟧, with the underlying functor ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredMultisection.forget⟧; $\Lambda$ is structurable over $\partial X$ if a class lies over it ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.IsBoundaryStructurable⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.isBoundaryStructurable_iff⟧. Witness: the zero multisection, with the unit correspondences ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryDecoration.zeroTau⟧, for tame $X$ with $|X|$ paracompact ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.isBoundaryStructurable_zero⟧.

**Proposition 14.1.8**, the interior case (as printed). The proof is "similar to" Theorems 13.4.1 and 13.4.3. For sc⁺-multisections of the whole bundle, the push-forward and the pull-back along a generalized strong bundle isomorphism preserve structurability (Part XIII, §XIII.24) ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.isStructurable_pushMult⟧ ⟦Chapter13/P3W4FN_Pushforward · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.isStructurable_pullMult⟧. *The boundary case*, for boundary symmetric structures, boundary correspondences and good systems for $\partial X$, is proved in wave 5 for a representative with tame middle, with two hypotheses on the transport of face-wise sc⁺ sections (§XIV.18).

### XIV.5 Theorem 14.1.9 (2017: 14.2): the ∂-extension theorem, from the extension

**The statement** ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_statement⟧, as printed: let $X$ be tame with $|X|$ paracompact and sc-smooth partitions of unity on its objects, $\Lambda$ structurable over $\partial X$, $N$ an auxiliary norm, $\tilde U$ an open saturated set containing the boundary domain support of $\Lambda$, and $f \ge 0$ a continuous functor with support in $\tilde U$ and $N(\Lambda) < f$ on the boundary domain support. Then there is a structurable $\Lambda' : W \to \mathbb Q^+$ with $N(\Lambda') \le f$, domain support in $\tilde U$, and $\Lambda' = \Lambda$ over $\partial X$. The boundary domain support ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.boundaryDomSupp⟧ is the closure of the set of $x \in \partial X$ with some $w \ne 0_x$ over $x$ and $\Lambda(w) > 0$; that of the zero multisection is empty ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.boundaryDomSupp_zero⟧. "Supported in $\tilde U$" is read as: the closure of $\{f \ne 0\}$ lies in $\tilde U$. The hypotheses are satisfiable together ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_BoundaryStructured · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_statement_hyp_witness⟧: $\Lambda = 0$, $\tilde U = \emptyset$, $f = 0$.

**The extension** ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_NormControl · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_extension_statement⟧, the output of §§14.3–14.5: for every structurable $\Lambda$ over $\partial X$ and every open saturated $\tilde U'$ containing its boundary domain support, there is a structurable $\Lambda''$ on $W$ with domain support in $\tilde U'$ and $\Lambda'' = \Lambda$ over $\partial X$. Its witness covers only $\partial X = \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_NormControl · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_extension_statement_of_boundary_eq_empty⟧, with $\Lambda'' = 0$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_NormControl · SBLocalization.domSupp_zeroMultisection_gl⟧. That it holds when $\partial X \ne \emptyset$ is the content of §§14.3–14.5; wave 5 proves it from the data of that construction (§XIV.22)." and, in the third paragraph, "*Narrower*: the extension is a hypothesis, with a witness only for $\partial X = \emptyset$." → "*Narrower*: the extension is a hypothesis here; wave 5 derives it from the data of §§14.3–14.5, a hypothesis that is still witnessed only for $\partial X = \emptyset$ (§XIV.22).

**Theorem 14.1.9** (narrower) ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_NormControl · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_hyp⟧: the extension implies the statement. This is the size control at the end of the text's proof (p. 677). *Step 1.* Apply the extension with $\tilde U' = \{f > 0\}$: it is open and saturated, since $f$ is a continuous functor, it lies in $\tilde U$, and it contains the boundary domain support, where $f > N(\Lambda) \ge 0$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_NormControl · SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm_nonneg⟧. *Step 2.* Let $G = \{N(\Lambda'') < f\} \cup (X \setminus \operatorname{dom-supp}\Lambda'')$. It is open, because $N(\Lambda'')$ is continuous where $\Lambda''$ has local structures ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_NormControl · SBLocalization.isOpen_pointwiseNorm_lt⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_NormControl · SBLocalization.IsScPlusSectionOn.continuousOn_normW⟧; saturated, because $N(\Lambda'')$ is a functor ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_NormControl · SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm_tgt⟧ and closures and unions of saturated sets are saturated ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_NormControl · SBLocalization.isSaturated_closure_gl⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_NormControl · SBLocalization.isSaturated_union_gl⟧; and it contains $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_NormControl · SBLocalization.isSaturated_boundary_gl⟧: on the boundary domain support $N(\Lambda'') = N(\Lambda) < f$, and at the other boundary points either $\Lambda''$ is trivial nearby, by the choice of $\tilde U'$, or $f > 0 = N(\Lambda'')$. *Step 3.* An sc-smooth Urysohn functor $\sigma$ with $\sigma = 1$ on $\partial X$ and $\sigma = 0$ off $G$, from Part VII's sc-smooth Urysohn functions on $|X|$ ⟦Chapter7/PartitionsOfUnity · EpGroupoid.exists_isScSmoothMap_orbit_urysohn⟧, and $\Lambda' = \sigma \odot \Lambda''$, which is structurable by Lemma 13.3.14 (Part XIII, §XIII.17). Then $N(\Lambda') \le |\sigma| N(\Lambda'')$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_NormControl · SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm_smulFun_le⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_NormControl · SBLocalization.normW_le_of_multisectionSmul_pos⟧, which is below $f$ on $G$ and $0$ off it; $\Lambda' = \Lambda''$ where $\sigma = 1$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_NormControl · SBLocalization.multisectionSmulFun_of_eq_one⟧, in particular over $\partial X$; and the domain support only shrinks. *Narrower*: the extension is a hypothesis, with a witness only for $\partial X = \emptyset$. *A reading*: the text writes $N(\Lambda)(x) < f(x)$ for $x \in \partial X$; the hypothesis gives it on the boundary domain support, and it is read there.

### XIV.6 Lemmas 14.2.1, 14.2.2 and Proposition 14.2.3 (2017: the text before Lemma 14.1, Lemma 14.1, Proposition 14.2): a good structured representative

**Lemma 14.2.1** (as printed) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodStructured · EpGroupoid.lemma_14_2_1⟧: a good $V_0(x)$ contains a good $V(x)$ with the restricted action and $\operatorname{cl}V(x) \subset V_0(x)$, $\operatorname{cl}(V(x) \cap \partial X) \subset V_0(x) \cap \partial X$ and $\operatorname{cl}|V(x) \cap \partial X| \subset |V_0(x) \cap \partial X|$ (14.15). The orbit closure comes from Proposition 7.1.10 and the properness of $V_0(x)$; since $|\partial X|$ is closed in $|X|$, closures are taken in $|X|$. For a whole good system ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodStructured · EpGroupoid.lemma_14_2_1_system⟧.

**Lemma 14.2.2** (as printed) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodStructured · SBLocalization.lemma_14_2_2⟧: for good systems $\mathcal U \le \mathcal U^0$ with $\operatorname{cl}_X U(x) \subset U^0(x)$, and $\tau$ locally constant on $\mathcal U^0(x, x')$, the closures of the sets $\tau^{-1}(d) \cap \mathcal U(x, x')$ for different values $d$ are disjoint. $\operatorname{cl}\mathcal U(x, x')$ lies in $\mathcal U^0(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodStructured · SBLocalization.closure_mor_subset⟧, where $\tau$ is locally constant, so a common limit point would have both values. The text defines $\mathcal U(x, x')$ with $t(\varphi) \in U(x)$; presumably $U(x')$ is meant, as in (P3).

**Proposition 14.2.3** (as printed) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.proposition_14_2_3⟧: for tame $X$, every structured tuple has an equivalent one with the same $\Lambda$, restricted actions, and (P4): for $[d] \ne [d']$ the closures of $\tau^{-1}([d])$ and $\tau^{-1}([d'])$ are disjoint ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.HasP4⟧. Restrict the tuple to the good system of Lemma 14.2.1 ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.restrict⟧, which is equivalent ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.equiv_restrict⟧; Lemma 14.2.2 gives (P4). (P4) persists under shrinking ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.HasP4.restrict⟧, and every class has a representative with it ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B1_GoodStructured · SBLocalization.BoundaryStructuredTuple.proposition_14_2_3_class⟧. (P1)–(P3) are the fields of a tuple; the assumptions of Theorem 14.1.9 enter only as tameness.

### XIV.7 Lemma 14.3.1, Definition 14.3.2, Lemma 14.3.3, Proposition 14.3.4 and Remark 14.3.5 (2017: Lemma 14.2, the text before Lemma 14.3, Lemma 14.3, Proposition 14.3, Remark 14.4): extension of the correspondences

**(P5)** ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds⟧: for a tuple $T$ with (P1)–(P4), neighbourhoods $\tilde U'(x)$ with the natural action, $x \in \partial X$, with the same natural representation as the good system of $T$, the properness property, and $\tilde U'(x) \cap \partial X = U^0(x)$. "Admits the natural $G_x$-action" is read as the action of $\mathcal U^0$, so that the bi-action on $\tilde U'(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.biact⟧ is that of Definition 14.1.7 (c) ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.biact_eq⟧. Witness: the good system's own $V(x)$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.ofGood⟧. The morphisms of $\tilde U'(x, x')$ that lie in $\partial X$ are those of $U^0(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.mor_inter_boundaryMor⟧.

**Lemma 14.3.1** (stronger) ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.lemma_14_3_1⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension⟧: under (P1)–(P5), every value $[d]$ has an open $\tilde O_{x,x',[d]} \supseteq \tau^{0-1}([d])$ with (1) $\tilde O_{[d]} \subset \tilde U'(x, x')$, (2) disjoint closures for $[d] \ne [d']$, (3) $h * \tilde O_{[d]} * g = \tilde O_{h*[d]*g}$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.image_biact⟧, (4) $\tilde O_{x,x'} \cap \partial X = U^0(x, x')$ for the union ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.iUnion_inter_boundaryMor⟧, and in addition $\varphi^{-1} \in \tilde O_{x',x,[d]^\sharp}$ exactly when $\varphi \in \tilde O_{x,x',[d]}$. *Proof*, the text's with one step added. Separate the closures given by (P4) by open sets in the metrizable, hence normal, morphism space ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · P3W4S3.exists_open_disjoint_closure⟧ and intersect with $\tilde U'(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrPre.exists_of_hasP4⟧; intersect over the bi-action, $\bigcap_{h,g}(h * \cdot * g)^{-1}(\tilde O'_{h*[d]*g})$, the text's $\bigcap h * \tilde O'_{[d']} * g$ over $h * [d'] * g = [d]$; and, added, intersect with the inverted sets for $(x', x)$. Each step keeps (1)–(4). Only finitely many $[d]$ occur; the others get the empty set. The inversion symmetry is what makes the extended correspondences satisfy Definition 14.1.7 (a), which §14.4 uses. The printed form ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.lemma_14_3_1_book⟧.

**Definition 14.3.2** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.Ohat⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat⟧: $\hat O_{x,x'}$ is the union of the components of $\tilde O_{x,x'}$ that meet $\partial X$, and $\hat\tau(\varphi)$ is the $[d]$ with $\varphi \in \tilde O_{[d]}$. The text defines $[d]_\varphi$ as $\tau^0(\psi)$ for a boundary morphism $\psi$ in the component of $\varphi$. The two agree: the $\tilde O_{[d]}$ are a decomposition of $\tilde O_{x,x'}$ into open sets with disjoint closures, so a component lies in one of them ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.component_subset⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · P3W4S3.connectedComponentIn_iUnion_subset⟧, and $\tilde O_{[d]} \cap \partial X = \tau^{0-1}([d])$. (14.23): $\hat O$ is open ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.isOpen_Ohat⟧, contains $U^0(x, x')$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.mor_subset_Ohat⟧ and meets $\partial X$ exactly there ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.Ohat_inter_boundaryMor⟧; $\hat O_{[d]} = \hat O \cap \tilde O_{[d]}$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.OhatD_eq⟧.

**Lemma 14.3.3** (as printed) ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.lemma_14_3_3⟧: two boundary morphisms in one component of $\hat O_{x,x'}$ have the same $\tau^0$, since the component lies in one $\tilde O_{[d]}$; so $\hat\tau(\varphi) = \tau^0(\psi)$ for every such $\psi$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_eq_tau_of_mem_component⟧.

**Proposition 14.3.4** (as printed) ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.proposition_14_3_4⟧: $\hat O_{x,x'}$ is open, $U^0(x, x') \subset \hat O \subset \tilde U'(x, x')$ with $\hat O \cap \partial X = U^0(x, x')$, invariant under the bi-action; $\hat\tau$ is locally constant ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_locallyConstant⟧, equals $\tau^0$ on $U^0(x, x')$, is the unique such extension ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_unique⟧, is equivariant ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_biact⟧, takes finitely many values ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.finite_tauHat⟧, and on the diagonal $\hat\tau_{x,x}(\Gamma(g, y)) = [I_x \leftarrow I_x \xrightarrow{g} I_x]$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_Γ⟧. *Uniqueness*: every component of $\hat O$ meets $\partial X$, and a locally constant function is constant on components ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · P3W4S3.eq_of_mem_connectedComponentIn⟧. *The diagonal property*, for which the text gives no argument: the component of $\Gamma(g, y)$ in $\tilde O_{x,x}$ stays in the sheet $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$, because the label of the sheet through a morphism is locally constant, $s$ being a local homeomorphism on sheets ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · EpGroupoid.sheetLabel_locallyConstant_p3w4⟧; this component meets $\partial X$ in some $\Gamma(g, z')$, $z' \in U^0(x)$, where Definition 14.1.7 (b) gives the value. *Added:* $\hat O$ and $\hat\tau$ are symmetric under inversion, $\hat\tau_{x',x}(\varphi^{-1}) = \hat\tau_{x,x'}(\varphi)^\sharp$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.inv_mem_Ohat⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_ExtendCorrespondences · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_inv⟧. **Remark 14.3.5** comments on the construction ($\hat O$ is not of the form $\tilde U(x, x')$) and states nothing to prove.

### XIV.8 Lemmas 14.3.6, 14.3.7 and Proposition 14.3.8 (2017: Lemmas 14.4, 14.5, Proposition 14.4): the cover by the sets $\hat V_a$

**Lemma 14.3.6** (explicit) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_Cover · EpGroupoid.lemma_14_3_6⟧: for $|X|$ paracompact, a set $B$ of objects with $|B|$ closed, and neighbourhoods $\tilde U(x)$ with the natural action, there are $A \subset B$ and nonempty open $\tilde V_a \subset \tilde U(a)$, invariant under $G_a$, with $|\tilde V_a|$ open, $\operatorname{cl}|\tilde V_a| \subset |\tilde U(a)|$, and $(|\tilde V_a|)_{a \in A}$ a locally finite cover of $|B|$. The proof is the text's: add $|X \setminus B|$ to the cover by the $|\tilde U(x)|$, take a locally finite refinement and shrink it with closures inside (normality of the paracompact Hausdorff $|X|$, Lemma 7.3.4), set $\tilde V_a = \tilde U(a) \cap \pi^{-1}(W_a)$ and keep the $a$ with $W_a \ne \emptyset$. *Explicit:* the text's step uses that $|\partial X|$ is closed in $|X|$; for $B = \partial X$ it holds because $\partial X$ is closed and saturated ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_Cover · EpGroupoid.isClosed_π_image_of_isSaturated⟧.

**Lemma 14.3.7** (stronger) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_Cover · EpGroupoid.lemma_14_3_7⟧: fix $a \in A$; every $y \in \tilde U'(a) \cap \partial X$ has a finite $o(y) \subset A$ and an open $\tilde O(y) \ni y$ in $\tilde U'(a)$ with (1) $|\tilde O(y)|$ meets $|\tilde V_b|$ only for $b \in o(y)$, (2) $g * \tilde O(y) = \tilde O(g * y)$ and $o(g * y) = o(y)$, and (3) every $\varphi$ with $s(\varphi) \in \tilde O(y)$ and $t(\varphi) \in \tilde U(b)$, $b \in o(y)$, lies in $\hat O_{a,b}$, without the text's "$\cap\,\tilde U(a)$". *Construction.* $o(y)$ is the set of $b$ whose $|\tilde V_b|$ meets a neighbourhood of $|y|$, finite by local finiteness and depending only on $|y|$, which gives $o(g * y) = o(y)$. For (3), the property holds at $y$ and hence near $y$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_Cover · EpGroupoid.exists_nhds_of_isProperSubset⟧: if morphisms $\varphi_k$ with sources $\to y$ and targets in $\operatorname{cl}\tilde U(b)$ avoided the open $\hat O_{a,b}$, properness of $t$ on $s^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}\tilde U(b))$, applied to the inverses, would give a limit outside $\hat O_{a,b}$ with source $y$, but such morphisms lie in $U'(a, b) \subset \hat O_{a,b}$. This gives an open $O_0(y)$; $\tilde O(y) = \bigcap_{g \in G_a}\tilde U'(a) \cap \Phi_g^{-1}(O_0(g * y))$ gives (2). The stabilizer of $y$ in $G_a$ leaves $\tilde O(y)$ invariant ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_Cover · EpGroupoid.lemma_14_3_7_stab⟧; "$G_y$-invariant" is read so, since every morphism between points of $\tilde U'(a)$ is a $\Gamma(g, \cdot)$. The hypotheses the proof uses are named: $\operatorname{cl}\tilde U(b) \subset \tilde U'(b)$, properness, $\hat O_{a,b}$ open and containing $U'(a, b)$, $\partial X$ saturated ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_Cover · EpGroupoid.IsSaturated.tgt_mem⟧, and local finiteness.

**(P6)** ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_CoverVHat · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.P6Nbhds⟧: neighbourhoods $\tilde U(x) \subset \tilde U'(x)$ with the restricted action, the properness property and $\operatorname{cl}|\tilde U(x)| \subset |\tilde U'(x)|$. The text's "obvious ramification" $\operatorname{cl}_X\tilde U(x) \subset \tilde U'(x)$ follows by Lemma 13.1.1 and the properness of $\tilde U'(x)$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_CoverVHat · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.P6Nbhds.closure_subset⟧; it needs $\tilde U(x) \subset \tilde U'(x)$ with the same action, which is how (P6) is read. They exist for all (P5) data, without tameness ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_CoverVHat · SBLocalization.P5Nbhds.P6Nbhds.exists_⟧.

**Proposition 14.3.8** (explicit). *Abstract form* ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_CoverVHat · EpGroupoid.proposition_14_3_8⟧: with $\hat V_a = (\bigcup_y \tilde O(y)) \cap \tilde V_a$ (14.32), (1) $\hat V_a$ is open, $G_a$-invariant and $\hat V_a \subset \tilde V_a \subset \tilde U(a)$; (2) $\hat V_a \cap \partial X = \tilde V_a \cap \partial X$; (3) $(|\hat V_a|)$ is a locally finite cover of $|\partial X|$ by open sets; (4) $\hat V_{a,a'} \subset \hat O_{a,a'}$, so $\hat\tau_{a,a'}$ restricts to it. (1) and (2) follow from the $\tilde O(y)$ containing $y$ and being invariant; (3) from Lemma 14.3.6; (4) from Lemma 14.3.7 (1), (3) and $\pi(t\varphi) = \pi(s\varphi)$, as in the text. The hypotheses the proof uses are named: $\partial X$ saturated ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_CoverVHat · EpGroupoid.isSaturated_boundary_p3w4⟧, the same action on $\tilde U(a) \subset \tilde U'(a)$, and $U'(a, b) \subset \hat O_{a,b}$ (Proposition 14.3.4 (1)). *Instantiated* ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_CoverVHat · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.proposition_14_3_8⟧: for the extension of Lemma 14.3.1, (P6) and $|X|$ paracompact, all of them are discharged, with $\hat O_{a,a'}$ the set of Definition 14.3.2 ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_CoverVHat · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.OhatObj⟧. The summary (14.33)–(14.38) is contained in it. On $\hat V_a$ the extended correspondences satisfy Definition 14.1.7 (b) ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_CoverVHat · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_Γ_of_VHat⟧ and (a) ⟦Chapter14/P3W4S3_CoverVHat · SBLocalization.CorrExtension.tauHat_inv_of_VHat⟧, the two properties §14.4 needs. *Nonvacuity* of the whole chain, for tame $X$ with $|X|$ paracompact: the zero multisection is structurable over $\partial X$ (§XIV.4), Proposition 14.2.3 gives (P4), the good system gives (P5), Lemma 14.3.1 the extension, (P6) exists, and the instantiated proposition the cover.

### XIV.9 Remark 14.4.1, Definitions 14.4.2–14.4.4, Lemmas 14.4.5 and 14.4.7 (2017: Remark 14.5, Definitions 14.5–14.7, Lemmas 14.6, 14.7): z-loops

**The setting** ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup⟧: the index set $A$; for $a \in A$ the neighbourhood $\tilde U(a)$ with the natural action, an invariant $\hat V_a \subset \tilde U(a)$, a finite index set $I_a$ with a $G_a$-action; and maps $\hat\tau_{a,a'}$ from morphisms to $J(a, a')$ with two properties on $\hat V$: *diag*, $\hat\tau_{a,a}(\Gamma(g, w)) = [\mathrm{id}, g]$ for $w \in \hat V_a$, and *swap*, $\hat\tau_{a',a}(\varphi^{-1}) = \hat\tau_{a,a'}(\varphi)^\sharp$. These are Definition 13.3.6 (1), (2) for the extended $\hat\tau$, which the text uses in the proof of Lemma 14.4.5; for the $\hat\tau$ of §14.3 they are §XIV.8's last two properties. Witness: every ep-groupoid, with $A = X$ and one-point index sets ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.trivialSetup⟧. Remark 14.4.1 explains the construction and is prose.

**Definitions 14.4.2 and 14.4.3** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.Arc⟧. A z-loop is a chain $a = a_0, \dots, a_n = a$ in $A$ with morphisms $\varphi_j$ from $\hat V_{a_j}$ to $\hat V_{a_{j+1}}$ composing to $1_z$; a z-arc along it is a sequence of indices $i_j \in I_{a_j}$ with each pair $(i_j, i_{j+1})$ a pair of the correspondence $\hat\tau_{a_j,a_{j+1}}(\varphi_j)$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.Pairs⟧. Loop and arc are encoded together as one inductive predicate, built from a start at $z \in \hat V_a$ by appending one morphism and one index step, with composite $\varphi$. Arcs concatenate ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.Arc.trans⟧ and reverse ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.Arc.symm⟧, the reversal through *swap* ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.pairs_swap⟧. Length $0$ is allowed and adds nothing: the one-step loop $1_z = \Gamma(1, z)$ relates the same indices, by *diag* ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.zRel_iff_unit_step⟧.

**Definition 14.4.4** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.ZRel⟧: $i \sim_z i'$ if there is a z-arc from $i$ to $i'$ along a z-loop, and $[i]_{\sim_z}$ is the class ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.zClass⟧. The text calls $\sim_z$ an equivalence relation; this is proved ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.zRel_equivalence⟧: reflexivity by the empty loop, symmetry by reversal, transitivity by concatenation. $i \sim_z i'$ forces $z \in \hat V_a$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.ZRel.mem_V⟧.

**Lemma 14.4.5** (explicit) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.lemma_14_4_5⟧: $i \sim_z i'$ if and only if $g(i) \sim_{g*z} g(i')$, hence $[g(i)]_{\sim_{g*z}} = g([i]_{\sim_z})$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.lemma_14_4_5_class⟧. The text's proof: prepend $\Gamma(g^{-1}, g * z)$ and append $\Gamma(g, z)$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_ZLoops · EpGroupoid.ZSetup.zRel_smul⟧; their correspondences are $[\mathrm{id}, g^{\mp 1}]$, which is *diag*, made explicit as a hypothesis of the setting; the composite is $\Gamma(g, z) \circ \Gamma(g^{-1}, g * z) = 1_{g*z}$. The converse applies this to $g^{-1}$.

**Lemma 14.4.7** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_FiniteRep · EpGroupoid.lemma_14_4_7⟧. It restates Part II's Proposition 7.1.15 and Corollary 7.1.17 for finitely many isomorphic objects $Y$ with open $Q(x) \ni x$: open, connected, disjoint $O(x) \subset Q(x)$ with a natural representation of the full subcategory on $O = \bigcup O(x)$ by sc-diffeomorphisms, (1)–(3) as fields, (4) $f(g) = g * \cdot$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_FiniteRep · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.F_isotropy⟧, (5) the equivariance through $\gamma_\varphi$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_FiniteRep · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.F_equivariant⟧, (6) the multiplication $\mathbf O(\psi) \times_{s,t} \mathbf O(\varphi) \to \mathbf O(\psi \circ \varphi)$ a bijection ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_FiniteRep · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.bijOn_comp⟧ and an sc-diffeomorphism in the parametrization by the second factor ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_FiniteRep · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.comp_srcInv_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_FiniteRep · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.isScDiffeoOn_comp⟧, and (7) the properness property ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_FiniteRep · EpGroupoid.exists_naturalRepFinite_subset⟧. Part II takes one open set around $Y$; the per-object $Q(x)$ and (7) come from applying it inside pairwise disjoint neighbourhoods with the properness property, and connectedness puts each $O(x)$ inside its own. The key identity of (6) is proved by connectedness: the image of $\mathbf O(\varphi)$ is connected and contains $\psi \circ \varphi$, so it lies in the component $\mathbf O(\psi \circ \varphi)$.

**The setting with topology** ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Deform · EpGroupoid.ZData⟧: the setting of §XIV.9 with $\hat V_a$ open, $\operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a \subset \tilde U(a)$ (14.33), and $\hat\tau_{a,a'}$ locally constant at every morphism from $\hat V_a$ to $\hat V_{a'}$ (Proposition 14.3.4 with Proposition 14.3.8 (4)). **Proposition 14.4.6 (1)** (as printed) ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Deform · EpGroupoid.ZData.proposition_14_4_6_1⟧: if $i \sim_{z_0} i'$, then $i \sim_z i'$ for all $z$ near $z_0$; in open-set form ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Deform · EpGroupoid.ZData.proposition_14_4_6_1_open⟧, and $[i]_{\sim_{z_0}} \subset [i]_{\sim_z}$ near $z_0$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Deform · EpGroupoid.ZData.eventually_zClass_subset⟧. *Key step* ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Deform · EpGroupoid.ZData.Arc.eventually_srcInv⟧: a chain with an arc through a morphism $\varphi$ deforms along any sheet $\mathbf U \ni \varphi$; for $z$ near $s(\varphi)$, the morphism $(s|\mathbf U)^{-1}(z)$ carries a chain with the same arc. By induction on the chain: each morphism is moved along its own sheet, using that $(s|\mathbf U)^{-1}$ is continuous ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Deform · EpGroupoid.Sheet.tendsto_srcInv⟧, that composition is continuous ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Deform · EpGroupoid.tendsto_comp_of_eventually⟧, that the moved morphisms stay between the open sets $\hat V$, and that $\hat\tau$ is locally constant, so the index steps survive. At the end the composite is a morphism near $1_{z_0}$ with source $z$ and in the sheet of the unit, hence $1_z$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Deform · EpGroupoid.Sheet.eventually_srcInv_eq_unit⟧. The text invokes Lemma 14.4.7 here; the deformation along sheets does not need it.

### XIV.11 Proposition 14.4.10, Definition 14.4.11, Remark 14.4.12 and Lemma 14.4.13 (2017: Proposition 14.6, Definition 14.9, Remark 14.6, Lemma 14.9): coherent neighbourhood systems

**Equivariant neighbourhoods** ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Theta · EpGroupoid.NatNbhd.exists_equivariant_nbhds⟧: for a property of open neighbourhoods preserved by shrinking and by the natural action, every point of an invariant set has neighbourhoods with it that satisfy $\tilde O(g * z) = g * \tilde O(z)$ and are disjoint from their translates when $g * z \ne z$: choose on orbit representatives, intersect over the stabilizer, separate from the finitely many other translates, and transport. The action maps open sets to open sets ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Theta · EpGroupoid.NatNbhd.isOpen_image_Φ⟧ and composes ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Theta · EpGroupoid.NatNbhd.image_Φ_mul⟧, and preserves $\partial X$ and $\operatorname{cl}\hat V_b$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Coherent · SBLocalization.Φ_mem_boundary_z4⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Coherent · SBLocalization.mapsTo_Φ_closure_z4⟧.

**Proposition 14.4.10** (as printed; §XIV.20)"; "Conditional on Proposition 14.4.6 (2) only through (4)." → "The hypothesis on Proposition 14.4.6 (2), used only through (4), is discharged in wave 5 (§XIV.20). ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Coherent · SBLocalization.proposition_14_4_10_hyp⟧: every $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$ has an open $\tilde O(z) \ni z$ with (1) $\tilde O(z) \subset \tilde U(a)$, (2) $\tilde O(g * z) = g * \tilde O(z)$, disjoint from $\tilde O(z)$ when $g * z \ne z$, (3) $[i]_{\sim_y} \subset [i]_{\approx_z}$ for $y \in \tilde O(z) \cap \hat V_a$, and (4) for $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$, $s^{0a}_i = s^{0a}_{i'}$ on $\tilde O(z) \cap U(a)$ when $i \approx_z i'$. The text's "immediate": (3) is Lemma 14.4.9 (4), (4) is Lemma 14.4.9 (3), and (2) is the equivariant choice above, which the text leaves implicit. Conditional on Proposition 14.4.6 (2) only through (4).

**Definition 14.4.11** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Coherent · SBLocalization.ZCoherentNbhdSystem⟧: a coherent neighbourhood system for $\operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \subset \tilde U(a)$ is a family of open $\tilde O(z) \ni z$ with (1)–(4), (3) as printed for $z \in \hat V_a$. Existence follows from Proposition 14.4.10 ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Coherent · SBLocalization.exists_zCoherentNbhdSystem_hyp⟧, with (3) for all $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X\hat V_a$; for zero data unconditionally ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Coherent · SBLocalization.exists_zCoherentNbhdSystem_zero⟧, since Proposition 14.4.6 (2) holds for them ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Coherent · SBLocalization.hasThetaLocalEq_zero⟧. The abstract form that Proposition 14.4.14 consumes ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.CoherentNbhdSystem⟧ is over data ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.LocalExtensionBase⟧ consisting of $\tilde U(a)$, an open invariant $\hat V_a$, the index set, face-wise sc⁺ boundary sections with (14.45), and relations $\sim_y$, $\approx_z$ as parameters, of which only Lemma 14.4.5 for $\sim$ is required; it asks (1), (3) for $z \in \operatorname{cl}\hat V_a$ and (4), and (2) is a separate predicate ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.CoherentNbhdSystem.IsEquivariant⟧. The data come from the setting of §XIV.9 ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.LocalExtensionBase.ofZSetup⟧ and from the boundary sections ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Instantiate · SBLocalization.ZSections.toLocalExtensionBase⟧, and the system from Proposition 14.4.10 ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Instantiate · SBLocalization.coherentNbhdSystem_hyp⟧. Witness of the abstract form at every boundary point of a tame $X$, with $a \in \hat V_a$: zero sections and trivial relations ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.exists_coherentNbhdSystem_zero⟧. The text first calls it a good neighbourhood system; **Remark 14.4.12** explains its meaning and is prose.

**Lemma 14.4.13** (narrower in (2)), for any coherent neighbourhood system and $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$, with $\tilde O([z]) = \bigsqcup_{z' \in [z]}\tilde O(z')$ a disjoint union ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Coherent · SBLocalization.ZCoherentNbhdSystem.disjoint_orbit⟧ over the orbit of $z$ under $G_a$. *(1)* ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Coherent · SBLocalization.lemma_14_4_13_1⟧: the stabilizer of $z'$ permutes the $\approx_{z'}$-classes, which are equal or disjoint ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Coherent · SBLocalization.approxClass_eq_or_disjoint⟧, by Lemma 14.4.9 (2). *(2)* ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Coherent · SBLocalization.lemma_14_4_13_2⟧: if $g$ fixes the class $[i_j]$, then $s^{0a}_{i_j}(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g, y), s^{0a}_{i_j}(y))$ on $\tilde O(z') \cap \partial X$, with the recalled identity that the sections of one class agree there ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Coherent · SBLocalization.lemma_14_4_13_classSection⟧; both for $z' \in \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$, since they are Definition 14.4.11 (4), which covers only those points. A point of $\operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$ need not lie in $\operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$; presumably $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$ is meant, which is what Proposition 14.4.14 uses. *(3)* ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Coherent · SBLocalization.lemma_14_4_13_3⟧: if $g$ moves the class, $s^{0a}_{g(i_j)}(g * y) = \mu(\Gamma(g, y), s^{0a}_{i_j}(y))$, by (14.45). *(4)* ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Coherent · SBLocalization.lemma_14_4_13_4⟧: the sections on $\tilde O(g * z') \cap \partial X$ are determined by those on $\tilde O(z') \cap \partial X$.

### XIV.12 Proposition 14.4.14 (2017: 14.7): the local extension near $\hat V_a$

**Proposition 14.4.14** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.proposition_14_4_14⟧: under the hypotheses of Proposition 14.1.4 (tame strong bundle charts, sc-smooth partitions of unity on the objects), for data with a coherent neighbourhood system there are sc⁺-sections $\hat s^a_i$ on $\hat V_a$, equivariant, with (1) $\hat s^a_i = s^{0a}_i$ on $\hat V_a \cap \partial X$ and (2) $\hat s^a_i(z) = \hat s^a_{i'}(z)$ when $i \sim_z i'$. "Symmetric section structure" is read as Definition 13.2.5 (1); the weights and $\hat\Lambda_a$ come in §14.5. *Proof*, different from the text's. *Local pieces* ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.CoherentNbhdSystem.exists_local_piece⟧: for $z \in \operatorname{cl}(V_a)$, take an open $G_z$ with $\operatorname{cl}G_z \subset \tilde O(z)$, choose a representative of each class of the equivalence relation generated by $\approx_z$, extend its boundary section from $G_z \cap \partial X$ (§XIV.3), and give every index the extension of its class's representative; the boundary sections of one class agree on $\tilde O(z) \cap U(a)$ by (4) ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.CoherentNbhdSystem.eqvGen_s0⟧, so each index still extends its own section. For $z \in \operatorname{cl}(\hat V_a) \setminus \operatorname{cl}(V_a)$, zero sections on a neighbourhood that misses $\operatorname{cl}(V_a)$. In both cases the pieces are constant on the classes of $\approx_z$, hence, by (3), on the classes of $\sim_y$ near $z$. *Gluing* by an ordinary partition of unity, not an invariant one; a glued section has the property (2) wherever every piece has it ⟦Chapter14/P3W4LX_CoherentExtension · SBLocalization.glueSection_congr_at⟧. *Averaging* over $G_a$ (§XIV.3): the average is equivariant, still extends $s^0$, which is equivariant, and stays compatible with $\sim$, because $\sim$ is, by Lemma 14.4.5. The text builds the sections class by class and orbit by orbit on the sets $\tilde O([z])$ and glues with a $G_a$-invariant partition of unity; the average replaces both, so Definition 14.4.11 (2) is not needed, and $\approx_z$ need not be an equivalence relation. For the data of §§XIV.10–XIV.11 ⟦Chapter14/P3W4Z4_Instantiate · SBLocalization.proposition_14_4_14_of_hyp⟧; the condition is discharged in wave 5, and for the objects of §14.3 the proposition needs only the hypotheses of Proposition 14.1.4 (§XIV.20).

### XIV.13 Lemma 14.5.1, Proposition 14.5.4 and Theorem 14.5.5 (2017: Lemma 14.10, Proposition 14.8, Theorem 14.3): transport and the structurability criterion

**Lemma 14.5.1** (stronger) ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_Cover · EpGroupoid.lemma_14_5_1⟧: if $X$ admits sc-smooth partitions of unity, $B$ is closed and saturated, and the saturations of open sets $\hat V_a$, $a \in A \subset B$, cover $B$, there are sc-smooth functors $\beta_a : X \to [0, 1]$ with support in $\pi^{-1}(\pi(\hat V_a))$, locally finite on saturated open sets, and $\sum_a \beta_a = 1$ on $B$. The proof is the text's: a partition of unity indexed by objects, subordinate to the cover by the sets $\pi^{-1}\pi(\hat V_x)$ for $x \in A$ and $X \setminus B$ for the other objects, whose members for $x \in A$ sum to $1$ on $B$. The saturation of an open set is open ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_Cover · EpGroupoid.isOpen_saturation⟧ and complements and preimages under $\pi$ of saturated sets are saturated ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_Cover · EpGroupoid.isSaturated_compl⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W3B2_Cover · EpGroupoid.isSaturated_preimage_π⟧. Tameness, assumed by the text through Theorem 14.1.9, is not used; the covering property (Proposition 14.3.8 (3)) and the closedness and saturation of $\partial X$ are named. (14.53) is not part of the lemma.

**Proposition 14.5.4**, the statement (proved in §XIV.21)"; "The proof, the transport along morphisms with well-definedness from z-arcs, is a new gap (§XIV.15)." → "The proof, the transport along morphisms with well-definedness from z-arcs, is §XIV.21. ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_Transport · SBLocalization.proposition_14_5_4_statement⟧. Its input ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_Transport · SBLocalization.TransportInput⟧ is the setting of §XIV.9 with the topology of §XIV.10, the functors $\beta_a$ with (14.53), the boundary sections with Definition 14.1.7 (4), and the local extensions $\hat s^a$ of Proposition 14.4.14 with their properties. The claim: for every $b \in A$ an equivariant family of sc⁺-sections $\tilde s^a_{b,j}$ on $\hat V_b$ with (1) $\tilde s^a_{a,i} = \beta_a\hat s^a_i$ on $\hat V_a$, (2) support closed in $X$ and inside $\hat V_a$, read as vanishing off a closed subset of $\hat V_a$, (3) $\tilde s^a_{b,j} = \beta_a s^{0b}_j$ on $V_b$, and (4) compatibility with the representatives of $\hat\tau_{b,b'}(\varphi)$. Consistency witness: zero data ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_Transport · SBLocalization.proposition_14_5_4_statement_of_zero⟧, since multiples of zero sections are zero ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_Transport · SBLocalization.sectionSmul_fiberZero_gl⟧. The proof, the transport along morphisms with well-definedness from z-arcs, is a new gap (§XIV.15).

**Theorem 14.5.5** (stronger) ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_Criterion · SBLocalization.theorem_14_5_5⟧: for $|X|$ paracompact and an sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda$ with criterion data ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_Criterion · SBLocalization.CriterionData⟧ (points $a$ with neighbourhoods $U(a)$ with the natural action, invariant open $V_a \subset U(a)$ whose orbits cover $|X|$ (c), symmetric sc⁺-structures on the $V_a$ representing $\Lambda$ (d), and correspondences $\tau_{a,a'}$ on $V(a, a')$, locally constant with finitely many values (e)), $\Lambda$ is structurable. With a good system in place of paracompactness ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_Criterion · SBLocalization.theorem_14_5_5_of_goodSystem⟧. *Proof*, along local transports rather than through Theorem 13.4.3 as the text does. For each $y$, a morphism into some $V_a$ and the sc-smooth local inverse of $t$ on its sheet give a local transport $\tau_y$ on an open set around $y$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_Criterion · SBLocalization.CriterionData.exists_transport⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_Criterion · SBLocalization.CriterionData.nonempty_transport⟧. As in Theorem 13.5.3 (Part XIII, §XIII.22), a morphism between transported points becomes, after conjugation by the transports, a morphism between points of the $V_a$; the correspondence there pulls back, through the conjugation homomorphisms ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_Criterion · SBLocalization.IndexCorr.biact_compHom_gl⟧, to a correspondence between the transported structures, locally constant because the conjugation is continuous. The structured data on a good system inside the transport domains are structurable ⟦Chapter14/P3W4GL_Criterion · SBLocalization.CriterionData.Transport.isStructurable⟧. *Stronger*: the properness of $t$ in (a) and the closure condition $\operatorname{cl}|V_a| \subset |U(a)|$ in (b) are not used, so not assumed. *A reading*: "correspondence" in (e) is read as Definition 13.3.4 (2) with Definition 13.3.6 (1)–(2), the bi-action, the compatibility with the sections, the diagonal and the swap.

### XIV.14 Witnesses and the hypotheses of waves 3 and 4

**Hypotheses taken.** *§XIV.2.* Theorem 14.1.6: tameness of $X$ and paracompactness of $|X|$ in place of the paracompactness of $|\partial X|$; not derived from the statement, but used by the text's proof; witness `trivial_quadrant_witness` with `hasParacompactOrbitSpace_trivial`. *§XIV.3, §XIV.12.* Proposition 14.1.4 and Proposition 14.4.14: every object lies in a tame strong bundle chart, and the objects admit sc-smooth partitions of unity; readings of the text's standing assumptions; witness `proposition_14_1_4_hypotheses_rn`. *§XIV.5.* Theorem 14.1.9: the extension statement of §§14.3–14.5, not derived from the text here, and derived in wave 5 from the data of §§14.3–14.5 (§XIV.22);"; "Proposition 14.4.6 (2) in the form with $z_k \in \hat V_a$, not derived;" → "Proposition 14.4.6 (2) in the form with $z_k \in \hat V_a$, proved in wave 5 (§XIV.20); witness `theorem_14_1_9_extension_statement_of_boundary_eq_empty`, **only for $\partial X = \emptyset$**. *§§XIV.10–XIV.12.* Lemma 14.4.9 (3), Proposition 14.4.10, the existence of coherent systems and Proposition 14.4.14 for the concrete data: Proposition 14.4.6 (2) in the form with $z_k \in \hat V_a$, not derived; witness `hasThetaLocalEq_zero` (zero data; it holds whenever the index sets have at most one element). *§XIV.9.* The properties *diag* and *swap* of the setting are Definition 13.3.6 (1), (2) for $\hat\tau$, which the text uses; they hold for §14.3's $\hat\tau$ on $\hat V$ (`tauHat_Γ_of_VHat`, `tauHat_inv_of_VHat`); witness `ZSetup.trivialSetup`. *§XIV.13.* Lemma 14.5.1 names the covering property and the closedness and saturation of $\partial X$, all facts of §14.3. *Kept and unused.* Paracompactness of $|X|$ and the goodness of $V(x)$ in Proposition 14.1.4; tameness in Lemma 14.5.1; properness (a) and the closure condition (b) in Theorem 14.5.5. No hypothesis quantifies over all charts.

**Every definition has a witness.** Good boundary neighbourhoods: every boundary point of a tame $X$ (§XIV.1). Sc⁺-multisections and structurable ones over $\partial X$: the zero multisection (§§XIV.2, XIV.4). Good systems for $\partial X$: Theorem 14.1.6. (P5), (P6) and the extended correspondences: the chain at the end of §XIV.8. The z-loop setting, with topology: the trivial setting on every ep-groupoid. Boundary sections: zero sections. Coherent neighbourhood systems: zero data, at every boundary point of a tame $X$. Criterion data: those of any structurable multisection with a good system. The input of Proposition 14.5.4: zero data.

### XIV.16 What the formalization taught us

Chapter 14 is the longest construction of the book, and its formal content splits into two kinds. The first is local topology of the morphism space: shrinking good neighbourhoods so that closures stay inside (Lemma 14.2.1), separating the values of a locally constant correspondence by open sets (Lemma 14.3.1), extending it by components (Proposition 14.3.4), and choosing neighbourhoods compatible with the action and with local finiteness (Lemmas 14.3.6, 14.3.7, Proposition 14.4.10). All of it rests on three facts used again and again: $t$ is proper on $s^{-1}$ of the closure of a good neighbourhood, so a property of the morphisms from a point persists near it; $s$ and $t$ are local homeomorphisms on sheets, so the sheet through a morphism is locally constant; and a locally constant function on an open set is constant on components. The diagonal property of Proposition 14.3.4, for which the text gives no argument, is the second fact: the component of $\Gamma(g, y)$ stays in the sheet of $g$ and reaches the boundary there. The inversion symmetry of the extended correspondences, which the text does not state, costs one more intersection in Lemma 14.3.1 and is what §14.4's z-loops need to be reversible. The second kind is combinatorics of index sets along chains of morphisms. Encoding a z-loop together with its arc as one inductive predicate made the equivalence-relation properties, which the text asserts, and Lemma 14.4.5 short, and made Proposition 14.4.6 (1) a deformation of the chain along sheets, one morphism at a time, without Lemma 14.4.7. The same encoding carried the limit argument of Proposition 14.4.6 (2): with Lemma 14.4.7 around the finitely many isomorphs of the limit point, each step of a nearby loop moves along its own sheet to the boundary, so the text's limit loop need not be built, and the result holds for loops at points of $\hat V_a$, which is the form Lemma 14.4.9 (3) uses. It also carried Proposition 14.5.4: defining the transported section through chains rather than single morphisms gives its equivariance and its compatibility with $\hat\tau$ directly, and its well-definedness is the text's closing of two chains into a loop.

Several steps needed less than printed, or more. The local extension of Proposition 14.1.4 cannot be glued with one partition of unity of $X$, because the boundary data on an open $V(x)$ may be unbounded at its frontier; an exhaustion of $V(x)$ by the sets at distance $> 1/n$ from its complement, glued by sc-smooth cut-offs, does it. Averaging over all of $G_x$ replaces the text's average over a stabilizer with orbit transport, both in Proposition 14.1.4 and in Proposition 14.4.14, where it also replaces the class-by-class, orbit-by-orbit construction and makes Definition 14.4.11 (2) unnecessary. The structurability criterion, Theorem 14.5.5, needs neither its properness nor its closure condition: local transports into the sets $V_a$ and the conjugation homomorphisms of Theorem 13.5.3 carry the structure. The final size control of Theorem 14.1.9 hides one choice: the extension must be taken with support in $\{f > 0\}$, not in $\tilde U$, or the cut-off cannot reach the boundary points where $f = 0$. Proposition 14.5.4 needs one property of the cut-offs that its statement does not list, that $\beta_a$ vanishes off the saturation of $\hat V_a$; Lemma 14.5.1 (1) gives it. Lemma 14.5.2 enters the proof only through its sum identity for sections, so the commensurable family over $\partial X$ is not needed. The index sets of §14.1 live on boundary points and those of §14.4 on all objects; a map to boundary points that is the identity on $\partial X$, with the identity on morphisms as a homomorphism of isotropy groups, joins them without casts. Over $\partial X$, Proposition 14.1.8 carries everything along except Definition 14.1.3 (1), which is read in every tame strong bundle chart; its transport needs that tame charts compose with local strong bundle isomorphisms, a fact of Part I's kind that is not yet formalized. In §14.6 the step from compatible classes to agreeing representatives is where the text is shortest: the equivalence of structured multisections does not compare sections. What remains is the instance of the construction's data, with the shrinking behind (14.53), that transport of face-wise sc⁺ sections, and §14.6 at the level of classes; about 1,750–2,750 lines, and nothing found so far suggests that they do not hold as we read them.

### XIV.17 The remark after Definition 14.1.2 (2017: after Definition 14.1): the faces $\bar\theta_j$ are tame M-polyfolds

**The faces of the open set $V$.** For $X$ tame, $V$ open and faces $\theta_1, \dots, \theta_{d_X(x)}$ at $x$ in $V$ (§XIV.1), the faces of $V$ in the sense of Part I's Definition 2.7.6 are exactly the sets $\bar\theta_i = V \cap \operatorname{cl}\theta_i$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceTame · EpGroupoid.HasBoundaryFaces.isFaceIn_iff⟧, pairwise distinct ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceTame · EpGroupoid.HasBoundaryFaces.injective_closure⟧, and the faces through a point are those of §XIV.1 ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceTame · EpGroupoid.HasBoundaryFaces.facesThrough_eq⟧. So $V$ is a face-structured open set ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceTame · EpGroupoid.HasBoundaryFaces.isFaceStructuredOpen⟧; as an M-polyfold (Part I's restriction to an open set) it is tame and face-structured ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceTame · EpGroupoid.HasBoundaryFaces.isFaceStructured_restrictOpen⟧, and each $\bar\theta_i$ is one of its faces ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceTame · EpGroupoid.HasBoundaryFaces.isFace_restrictOpen⟧. Two bridge lemmas identify Definition 2.5.10 with Definition 2.7.6 on the whole space ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceTame · MPolyfold.isFace_iff_isFaceIn_univ⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceTame · MPolyfold.isFaceStructured_iff_univ⟧.

**The remark** (as printed) ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceTame · EpGroupoid.HasBoundaryFaces.face_isTame⟧: with its sub-M-polyfold structure from Part I's Theorem 2.5.17, each $\bar\theta_i$ is a tame M-polyfold, and $d_X = d_{\bar\theta_i} + 1$ on it. *Proof*: Theorem 2.5.17 applied to the face $\bar\theta_i$ of the tame face-structured M-polyfold $V$. Each $\bar\theta_i$ is also a sub-M-polyfold of $X$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceTame · EpGroupoid.HasBoundaryFaces.isSubMPolyfold⟧, restated for good neighbourhoods ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceTame · EpGroupoid.IsGoodBoundaryNbhd.faces_isSubMPolyfold⟧; that this structure agrees with the one as a face of $V$ is not stated, though both come from the same local face charts. Only tameness of $X$ is assumed. Nothing in §§14.1–14.5 uses the remark; §14.6 reads sc⁺ on a face through the charts of $X$ (§XIV.23).

### XIV.18 Proposition 14.1.8 (2017: 14.1) over $\partial X$

**The statement** (narrower) ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_8_hyp⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_8_pullMult_hyp⟧: for a representative $W \leftarrow V \rightarrow W'$ of a generalized strong bundle isomorphism, by strong bundle equivalences, with the middle tame and the target tame, the push-forward of a $\Lambda$ structurable over $\partial X$ is structurable over $\partial X'$; and the pull-back of a $\Lambda'$ structurable over $\partial X'$ is structurable over $\partial X$. The text proves it "as in" Theorems 13.4.1 and 13.4.3 for a representative with tame middle; the two steps are those of Part XIII, §XIII.24, over the boundary.

**Pull** ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.isBoundaryStructurable_pull_hyp⟧, for any pull map of Part XIII (equivalences ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.proposition_14_1_8_pull_hyp⟧, proper coverings): the map pulls the boundary back to the boundary, $F^{-1}(\partial X') = \partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.mem_boundary_iff⟧; a good system for $\partial X'$ pulls back to one for $\partial X$, each neighbourhood shrunk to a good one by Proposition 14.1.1 ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.exists_bdryPullData⟧; the boundary symmetric structures and correspondences pull back ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.bdryPullStructure⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.bdryPullTau⟧ to a structured tuple ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.bdryPullTuple⟧. **Push** ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.isBoundaryStructurable_pushMult_hyp⟧: the push-forward is a functor over $\partial X'$, Lemma 11.5.2 over the boundary ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.isBoundaryWFunctor_pushMult_fm⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.pushMult_eq_bdry_fm⟧; good systems for $\partial X'$ inside the push charts ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.bdryPushGood⟧, the pushed structures ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.bdryPushStructure⟧ and the pushed correspondences ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.bdryPushTau⟧. *A congruence* used throughout: Definition 14.1.3 (1) on $U$ depends only on the values on $\partial X$ near $U$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.IsFaceScPlusSectionOn.congr_fm⟧, because a local face of a tame chart lies in $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.symm_mem_boundary_fm⟧.

*Narrower*: two hypotheses, not derived from the text, both the transport of Definition 14.1.3 (1), which is read in every tame strong bundle chart (§XIV.2). `PullMap.FacePull_hyp` ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.FacePull_hyp⟧: for open $O$, $O'$ with $F(O) \subset O'$, a section face-wise sc⁺ on $O' \cap \partial X'$ pulls back to one face-wise sc⁺ on $O \cap \partial X$. Witnesses: the identity of every strong bundle, a nonvacuous one, proved through the congruence ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.facePull_hyp_id⟧, and $\partial X = \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPull · SBLocalization.PullMap.facePull_hyp_of_boundary_eq_empty⟧. `FacePush_hyp` ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.FacePush_hyp⟧: for every transport chart and push neighbourhoods, the pushed section of a face-wise sc⁺ one is face-wise sc⁺. Witness only for $\partial X' = \emptyset$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5FM_BoundaryPush · SBLocalization.facePush_hyp_of_boundary_eq_empty⟧; it quantifies over all transport charts, so that witness shows it can be satisfied, and a nonvacuous one needs the composition of tame charts with local strong bundle isomorphisms (§XIV.15). Everything else, good systems for $\partial X$, structures, correspondences and the functor property over $\partial X$, is proved. The paracompactness of the orbit spaces is not used.

At $z_0$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_LimitExists · SBLocalization.ZLimitSetting.exists_limitRep⟧: local finiteness gives a finite set $o \subset A$ of the $b$ with $|\hat V_b|$ near $|z_0|$; $K = \bigcup_{b \in o}\operatorname{cl}\hat V_b$ is proper, so the objects of $K$ isomorphic to $z_0$ form a finite set $Y$ (Lemma 7.1.11); Lemma 14.4.7 on $Y$ gives connected $O(y)$ inside $\tilde U(b)$ and away from the $\operatorname{cl}\hat V_b$ that do not contain $y$, with sheets inside the sets $M_{b,c}$, by properness ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_LimitExists · SBLocalization.ZLimitSetting.exists_nbhd_near⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_LimitExists · SBLocalization.ZLimitSetting.exists_nbhd_yb⟧; and a neighbourhood $W$ of $z_0$ whose morphisms into any $\hat V_c$ lie in these sheets ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_LimitLoops · SBLocalization.ZLimitRep.mem_o_of_mem_W⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_LimitLoops · SBLocalization.ZLimitRep.sheet_subset_M⟧. By induction on a z-arc starting in $W$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_LimitLoops · SBLocalization.ZLimitRep.arc_transport⟧: the composite lies in the sheet of some $\psi : z_0 \to y$, and along the chain moved by $(s|\mathbf O(\psi))^{-1}$ to any $y' \in O(z_0) \cap \partial X$ the sections are transported, $\hat\tau$ being constant on the connected sheets ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_LimitLoops · SBLocalization.ZLimitRep.tau_eq⟧. For a loop the composite is a unit, so its sheet is that of $1_{z_0}$, the sheets being disjoint ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_LimitLoops · EpGroupoid.NaturalRepFinite.eq_of_mem_sheet_z5⟧; hence $s^{0a}_i = s^{0a}_{i'}$ on $O(z_0) \cap \partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_LimitLoops · SBLocalization.ZLimitRep.sections_eq⟧. The text builds the limit $z_0$-loop and deforms it along $\partial X$; here each step of the $z_k$-loop is moved directly, and the identity of the composite is Lemma 14.4.7 (6). *Stronger* in two ways: $z_k \in \hat V_a$ instead of $z_k \in V_a$, the form Lemma 14.4.9 (3) uses, which settles the reading of §XIV.10; and every $z_0 \in \operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$, not only $z_0 \in \operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$. Gap G.168 is closed.

**Lemma 14.4.9 (3)** (as printed; stronger) ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_LimitExists · SBLocalization.lemma_14_4_9_3_of_limit⟧: for every $z \in \operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$, $i \approx_z i'$ implies $s^{0a}_i = s^{0a}_{i'}$ on $\partial X$ near $z$, by the stronger statement above chained along $\Theta_z$. **Proposition 14.4.10** (as printed) ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_LimitExists · SBLocalization.proposition_14_4_10_of_limit⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_Instance · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.proposition_14_4_10⟧: the construction of §XIV.11 with its hypothesis discharged. **Definition 14.4.11**, the existence of coherent neighbourhood systems ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_LimitExists · SBLocalization.exists_zCoherentNbhdSystem_of_limit⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_Instance · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.exists_zCoherentNbhdSystem⟧, and of equivariant ones in the abstract form of §XIV.11 ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_LimitExists · SBLocalization.coherentNbhdSystem_of_limit⟧.

**Proposition 14.4.14** (restated, as in §XIV.12) ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_Instance · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.proposition_14_4_14⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_LimitExists · SBLocalization.proposition_14_4_14_of_limit⟧: for the concrete $\hat V_a$ and $\hat\tau$ and the sections of the tuple, sc⁺-sections $\hat s^a_i$ on $\hat V_a$, equivariant for the natural action of $\tilde U(a)$, equal to the sections of the tuple on $\hat V_a \cap \partial X$, and with $\hat s^a_i(y) = \hat s^a_{i'}(y)$ when $i \sim_y i'$; under the hypotheses of Proposition 14.1.4 only (tame strong bundle charts, sc-smooth partitions of unity on the objects; §XIV.3). The face-wise sc⁺ condition on $U(a)$ is Definition 14.1.3 (1) restricted ⟦Chapter14/P3W5Z5_Instance · SBLocalization.ZConcrete.isFaceScPlus⟧. *Lemma 14.4.13 (2)*: the reading of §XIV.11 stays. Definition 14.4.11 (4) covers only points of $\operatorname{cl}_X(V_a)$, so the printed (2) at the other points of $\operatorname{cl}_X(\hat V_a) \cap \partial X$ needs a system with (4) there; the stronger Lemma 14.4.9 (3) allows such a choice (about 90 lines, not done; Proposition 14.4.14 does not use it).

### XIV.21 Proposition 14.5.4 (2017: 14.8): the transport, proved

**The statement** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.proposition_14_5_4⟧: the statement of §XIV.13, exactly, for every input with one more property of the cut-offs ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.SuppInSat⟧: $\beta_a(y) \ne 0$ only where $y$ is the target of a morphism with source in $\hat V_a$, that is, on the saturation of $\hat V_a$. This is Lemma 14.5.1 (1), part of the text's data, which the input of §XIV.13 records only through (14.53); Lemma 14.5.1 produces it (§XIV.13). It is needed for (3): a point of $\hat V_b \cap \partial X$ outside the saturation of $\hat V_a$ must have $\beta_a = 0$.

**The section** ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec⟧: $\tilde s^a_{b,j}(t\varphi) = \mu(\varphi, \beta_a\hat s^a_i(s\varphi))$ for every z-arc (§XIV.9) from the index $i$ at a point of $\hat V_a$ to the index $j$ at $t\varphi \in \hat V_b$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec_of_arc⟧, and $0$ where there is none ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec_of_not⟧. A pair of $\hat\tau_{a,b}(\varphi)$ is an arc of length one ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.arc_of_pairs⟧, so this agrees with the text's definition along single morphisms ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec_of_pairs⟧. *Well defined* ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.fibAct_bsec_eq⟧, the text's z-loop argument: two arcs to the same index at the same point close, with a morphism $\Gamma(g^{-1}, \cdot)$, into a z-loop at a point of $\hat V_a$, and Proposition 14.4.14 (2) with the equivariance of $\hat s^a$ gives the same value. *Sc⁺ on $\hat V_b$* ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.isScPlusSectionOn_tsec⟧: near the target of an arc, a local inverse of $t$ on the sheet and the local constancy of $\hat\tau$ write the section as the transport of an sc⁺-section ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.isScPlusSectionOn_bsec⟧; at a point reached by no arc it vanishes nearby ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec_of_not_reach⟧, since it vanishes off $t(s^{-1}K)$ with $K = \operatorname{cl}\{y \in \tilde U(a) : \beta_a(y) \ne 0\} \subset \hat V_a$, which is closed by the properness of $\operatorname{cl}\tilde U(a)$ and (14.53). *Equivariance and (4)* follow from the arcs ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec_equivariant⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec_compat⟧. *(3)* ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.tsec_boundary⟧: at a boundary point reached from $\hat V_a$, Definition 14.1.7 (4) transports $s^{0a}$ to $s^{0b}$; at one not reached, $\beta_a = 0$. Witness of the added property: $\beta \equiv 0$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_TransportProof · SBLocalization.TransportInput.suppInSat_of_zero⟧. Gap G.170 is closed.

### XIV.22 The sum over $a$, Lemma 14.5.2 (2017: 14.11) and Theorem 14.1.9 (2017: 14.2): the assembly

**The data of §§14.3–14.5** ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_SumSections · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput⟧, for $\Lambda$ structurable over $\partial X$: an input of Proposition 14.5.4 with the property of §XIV.21, the $\beta_a$ locally finite on saturated open sets with $\sum_a \beta_a = 1$ on $\partial X$, nonempty index sets, the correspondences $\hat\tau$ with finitely many values and the bi-action, the representation of $\Lambda$ by the boundary sections, and the functor property of $\Lambda$.

**The sum** ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_SumSections · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.usec⟧: $\tilde s^b_j = \sum_{a \in A}\tilde s^a_{b,j}$ on $\hat V_b$, locally a finite sum ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_SumSections · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.exists_finite_tsec⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_SumSections · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.usec_eq_sectionSum⟧, hence sc⁺ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_SumSections · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.isScPlusSectionOn_usec⟧, equivariant ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_SumSections · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.usec_equivariant⟧ and compatible with $\hat\tau$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_SumSections · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.usec_compat⟧. A closed saturated set $C$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_SumSections · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.C⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_SumSections · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.isClosed_C⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_SumSections · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.isSaturated_C⟧, off which every transported section vanishes ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_SumSections · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.tsec_eq_zero_of_not_mem_C⟧, gives the points outside $\bigcup_b|\hat V_b|$ a neighbourhood on which all sections are $0$; the text says this in words. **Lemma 14.5.2**, its sum identity: $\tilde s^b_j = s^{0b}_j$ on $\hat V_b \cap \partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_SumSections · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.usec_boundary⟧, by (3) of Proposition 14.5.4 and $\sum_a\beta_a = 1$ there. This is the use the proof of Theorem 14.1.9 makes of Lemma 14.5.2; the commensurable family $(\beta_a|\partial X) \odot \Lambda$ over $\partial X$ is not built (gap G.172, §XIV.15).

**The extension** ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_Assembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.extension⟧. A cut-off $\sigma$ is folded into the sections ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_SumSections · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.ssec⟧, and $\Lambda'$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_Assembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.mult⟧ counts the indices whose section passes through $w$; the count is the same in every chart, by the compatibility with $\hat\tau$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_Assembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.mult_eq⟧, and $\Lambda'$ is a functor ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_Assembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.isWFunctor_mult⟧. *Criterion data* for Theorem 14.5.5 ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_Assembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.crit⟧, over the index set $A \sqcup X$: the sets $\hat V_a$ with the sections $\sigma\tilde s^a$, and for each object $x$ the invariant core of $X \setminus C$ in a natural neighbourhood of $x$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_Assembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.critV⟧, with one index and the zero section; the correspondences are the text's, $[I_b \leftarrow I_b \to \{1\}]$, its reverse, and the identity of $\{1\}$. Criterion data with a functor give local section structures ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_Assembly · SBLocalization.CriterionData.hasLocalSectionStructure_t9⟧, and Theorem 14.5.5 (§XIV.13) makes $\Lambda'$ structurable ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_Assembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.isStructurable_mult⟧. $\Lambda' = \Lambda$ over $\partial X$ when $\sigma = 1$ on the boundary domain support ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_Assembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.mult_boundary⟧, the domain support of $\Lambda'$ lies in the support of $\sigma$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_Assembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.domSupp_mult_subset⟧, and $\sigma$ is an Urysohn functor on the normal space $|X|$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_Assembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyInput.exists_cutoff⟧. *The difference* from the text: the cut-off is folded into the sections before Theorem 14.5.5 is applied, where the text multiplies $\Lambda'$ afterwards, and the points away from $C$ are covered by invariant cores of natural neighbourhoods of all objects, where the text uses the $x$ with $|x| \notin \bigcup|\hat V_b|$. Everything else is the text's construction.

**Theorem 14.1.9** (narrower) ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_Assembly · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_of_assembly⟧: the extension statement of §XIV.5 follows from the data ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_Assembly · SBLocalization.theorem_14_1_9_extension_statement_of_assembly⟧, and the size control of §XIV.5 gives the theorem as printed. *The hypothesis* ⟦Chapter14/P3W5T9_Assembly · SBLocalization.AssemblyHyp⟧: for $X$ tame with $|X|$ paracompact and sc-smooth partitions of unity on its objects, every $\Lambda$ structurable over $\partial X$ has the data of §§14.3–14.5.
