Remark 14.5.3 is explanatory.

### XIV.23 Definitions 14.6.1, 14.6.2 and Theorem 14.6.3 (2017: Definitions 14.10, 14.11, Theorem 14.4): assembling the faces

**Faces.** The faces of §14.6 are Part XI's ep-faces $X_\theta$ (Definition 11.1.3). They lie in $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceGerm · EpGroupoid.IsEpFace.subset_boundary⟧; every boundary point lies in one ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceGerm · EpGroupoid.exists_isEpFace_mem⟧ and in finitely many ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceGerm · EpGroupoid.finite_isEpFace_mem⟧; near $x$, every face through a point contains $x$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceGerm · EpGroupoid.eventually_mem_of_isEpFace⟧; they are saturated ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_Theorem1463 · EpGroupoid.IsEpFace.tgt_mem_iff⟧ and invariant under the natural action ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_Theorem1463 · EpGroupoid.IsEpFace.Φ_mem⟧; and in a tame chart, a local face near $y$ lies in one face of $X$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceGerm · EpGroupoid.exists_isEpFace_germ⟧. **Sc⁺ relative to a face** ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceGerm · SBLocalization.IsFaceRelScPlusSectionOn⟧: in every tame strong bundle chart, on every local face germ of the model that lies in $F$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceGerm · SBLocalization.FaceGermIn⟧, the local representative is sc⁺. This reads the text's sc⁺-sections of $W|F$ through the charts of $X$, whose local face germs in $F$ are the local models of $F$ (Theorem 2.5.17), in the style of §XIV.2. A gluing criterion ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceGerm · SBLocalization.isFaceScPlusSectionOn_of_local⟧: a section that near each point agrees, on each face through it, with a section sc⁺ relative to that face satisfies Definition 14.1.3 (1).

**Definition 14.6.1** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceStructured · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredTuple.restrictFace⟧. Structured data over a set $K$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelTuple⟧: a functor $\Lambda$ on $W|K$, natural neighbourhoods $U(x)$ with $t$ proper on $s^{-1}(\operatorname{cl}(U(x) \cap K))$, equivariant sections representing $\Lambda$ on $U(x) \cap K$, and correspondences, locally constant with finitely many values, with (a)–(c) and (4); with the equivalence of Definition 13.3.8 ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceStructured · SBLocalization.RelTuple.Equiv⟧. A face-structured tuple adds sc⁺ relative to $F$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceStructured · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredTuple⟧. The restriction to $F \cap F'$ restricts all data and keeps sc⁺ relative to $F$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceStructured · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredTuple.restrictFace_isFaceRelScPlus⟧; it is well defined on classes ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceStructured · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredMultisection.restrictFace⟧. "Good $U_F(x) \subset F$" is read as $U(x) \cap F$ for a natural neighbourhood of $X$ with the properness of Definition 13.1.4 (1); condition (2) of a good system is not part of the data, and §14.6 does not use it (§XIV.15).

**Definition 14.6.2** (restated) ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceStructured · SBLocalization.IsCompatibleAssignment⟧: $\tilde\Lambda_F|F' = \tilde\Lambda_{F'}|F$ for all faces $F$, $F'$. Then $I^F_x = I^{F'}_x$ for $x \in F \cap F'$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceStructured · SBLocalization.IsCompatibleAssignment.index_eq⟧ and $\Lambda_F = \Lambda_{F'}$ on $W|(F \cap F')$ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceStructured · SBLocalization.IsCompatibleAssignment.Λ_eq⟧. Witness: the zero multisection on every face ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceStructured · SBLocalization.isCompatibleAssignment_zero⟧.

**Theorem 14.6.3** (narrower) ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_Theorem1463 · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.theorem_14_6_3_hyp⟧: for $X$ tame and face-structured with $|X|$ paracompact, and face data with agreeing representatives ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_Theorem1463 · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData⟧ (one family of index sets, a face-structured tuple on each face, and agreement of $\Lambda$ on $W|(F \cap F')$, of the sections on $U_F(x) \cap U_{F'}(x) \cap F \cap F'$ and of the correspondences between such sets), which form a compatible assignment ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_Theorem1463 · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.isCompatibleAssignment⟧, the glued $\Lambda$ is structurable over $\partial X$ and equals $\Lambda_F$ over each face. *Proof*, the text's. A good system for $\partial X$ adapted to the faces ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_Theorem1463 · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.exists_adapted⟧, from Theorem 14.1.6 and refinements: the faces through points of $V(x)$ contain $x$, $V(x) \subset V_F(x)$ for $F \ni x$, and the natural actions agree. On it $s^x_i = s^x_{F,i}$ on $F$, face-wise sc⁺ by the gluing criterion, and $\tau_{x,x'}(\varphi) = \tau_{F,x,x'}(\varphi)$ for $s(\varphi) \in F$; the glued tuple ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_Theorem1463 · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.glue⟧ restricts to the face data ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_Theorem1463 · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.glue_s⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_Theorem1463 · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.glue_τ⟧. *The extension part* ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_Theorem1463 · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.theorem_14_6_3_extension_hyp⟧: with Theorem 14.1.9 as a hypothesis (proved from the data of §§14.3–14.5, §XIV.22) and its other hypotheses, $\Lambda$ extends to a structurable $\Lambda'$ on $W$ with $N(\Lambda') \le f$, domain support in $\tilde U$, and $\Lambda' = \Lambda_F$ over every face. *Narrower*: the input is representatives that agree, not a class-level compatible assignment. The text derives $s^x_{F,i} = s^x_{F',i}$ on $U_F(x) \cap U_{F'}(x)$ from compatibility; the equivalence of Definition 14.6.2, like that of Definition 13.3.8, compares $\Lambda$, the index sets and the correspondences on smaller neighbourhoods, not the sections. Presumably the text means that representatives can be chosen to agree; no counterexample is claimed (§XIV.15). The standing assumptions, tame and face-structured $X$ and paracompact $|X|$, are explicit. Witness: zero data on every face ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_Theorem1463 · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.zero⟧ ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_Theorem1463 · SBLocalization.CompatibleFaceData.zero_Λg⟧. Gap G.173 is formalized in part.

### XIV.24 Witnesses and the hypotheses of wave 5

**Hypotheses taken.** *§XIV.18.* Proposition 14.1.8 over $\partial X$: `PullMap.FacePull_hyp` and `FacePush_hyp`, the transport of Definition 14.1.3 (1) along the pull and the push; not derived from the text. Witnesses: `facePull_hyp_id` (the identity of every strong bundle, nonvacuous) and `facePull_hyp_of_boundary_eq_empty`; for `FacePush_hyp` **only `facePush_hyp_of_boundary_eq_empty` ($\partial X' = \emptyset$)**, which shows that this hypothesis over all transport charts can be satisfied, not that it holds for a map with nonempty boundary. The tameness of the middle of the representative is the text's choice of representative. *§XIV.20.* Proposition 14.4.14 for the objects of §14.3: tame strong bundle charts and sc-smooth partitions of unity, the readings of §XIV.3; witness `proposition_14_1_4_hypotheses_rn`. The facts of §14.3 in the abstract form (`ZLimitSetting`, `ZSections.CompatNbhd`) are no hypotheses of the text, and are discharged for the objects of §14.3 (`ZConcrete.toLimit`, `ZConcrete.compatNbhd`). *§XIV.21.* Proposition 14.5.4: `SuppInSat`, Lemma 14.5.1 (1), part of the text's data; witness `suppInSat_of_zero`, and Lemma 14.5.1 produces it. *§XIV.22.* Theorem 14.1.9: `AssemblyHyp`, the data of §§14.3–14.5 for every structurable $\Lambda$; not derived; witness `assemblyHyp_of_boundary_eq_empty`, **only for $\partial X = \emptyset$**. *§XIV.23.* Theorem 14.6.3: `CompatibleFaceData`, representatives that agree on the overlaps of faces, a reading of the text's step from compatibility; witness `CompatibleFaceData.zero`. Tameness, face structure and paracompactness of $|X|$ are standing assumptions of the chapter, with witnesses from Part XI (`isEpFaceStructured_trivial_restrictOpen`) and §XIV.2; the extension part takes Theorem 14.1.9, whose other hypotheses are jointly satisfiable (`theorem_14_1_9_statement_hyp_witness`, §XIV.5).

**Discharged.** Proposition 14.4.6 (2) in the form with $z_k \in \hat V_a$, the hypothesis of Lemma 14.4.9 (3), Proposition 14.4.10, the existence in Definition 14.4.11 and Proposition 14.4.14 in §§XIV.10–XIV.12, is proved (§XIV.20). The extension statement, the hypothesis of Theorem 14.1.9 in §XIV.5, is proved from `AssemblyHyp` (§XIV.22). No hypothesis of wave 5 quantifies over all charts of an atlas; `FacePush_hyp` quantifies over the transport charts of one map and has the satisfiability witness above.

**Every definition has a witness.** The objects of §14.3 with the setting of §14.4: every tame $X$ with $|X|$ paracompact and $\partial X \ne \emptyset$ (`exists_zConcrete_of_tame`). The data of §§14.3–14.5: `emptyAssemblyInput` ($\partial X = \emptyset$). Sc⁺ relative to a face: the zero section ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceGerm · SBLocalization.isFaceRelScPlusSectionOn_fiberZero⟧. Face-structured tuples: the zero tuple ⟦Chapter14/P3W5F6_FaceStructured · SBLocalization.FaceStructuredTuple.zero⟧. Compatible assignments and face data with agreeing representatives: the zero multisection on every face. No statement of Chapter 14 was found not to hold as we read it.

## Part XV. Transversality and invariants (HWZ Chapter 15, §§15.1–15.4)

Chapter 15 (Springer 2021, pp. 683–703; 2017 numbers in parentheses) is the perturbation theory of sc-Fredholm section functors by sc⁺-multisections. §15.1 defines the linearization $T(f, \Lambda)$ of $\Lambda \circ f$, a section of the formal sums $\mathrm{GrF}$ of sc-Fredholm operators (Theorem 15.1.1, Remark 15.1.2, Proposition 15.1.3, Lemmas 15.1.4, 15.1.5, Remark 15.1.6, Definition 15.1.7 (2017: Theorem 15.1, Remark 15.1, Proposition 15.1, Lemmas 15.1, 15.2, Definition 15.1; Remark 15.1.6 is new in the 2021 edition)). §15.2 treats transversality and local solution sets, §15.3 perturbations (general position, Theorem 15.3.7, and the transversal extension, Theorem 15.3.9), §15.4 orientations and invariants. This Part retells §15.1: the separation lemmas (§§XV.1–XV.2), the core of the proof of Theorem 15.1.1 (§XV.3), Theorem 15.1.1 on a strong bundle model and in a chart (§XV.4) and with intrinsic operators, with Definition 15.1.7 (§XV.5); then the witnesses (§XV.6), what is not formalized (§XV.7) and what the formalization taught us (§XV.8), then the sections $f - s_i$ on $W|_O$ (§XV.9), the sc-Fredholm summands (§XV.10), §15.2 (§§XV.11–XV.12), products and $[0, 1]^n \times X$ (§XV.13), the definitions of §15.3 (§XV.14), Corollary 15.3.10 (2) (§XV.15) and the wave-2 witnesses (§XV.16), then, in waves 3 and 4, the functor property of Theorem 15.1.1 (§XV.17), Theorem 15.2.5 under general position (§XV.18), the rest of Remark 15.3.6 (§XV.19), Theorem 15.3.7 (§XV.20), Theorem 15.3.9 and Corollary 15.3.10 (1), (3) (§XV.21), §15.4 (§XV.22) and the witnesses of waves 3 and 4 (§XV.23), then, in wave 5, tame solution sets, tame branched ep⁺-subgroupoids and the ep-groupoid $U(x)$ (§XV.24), the local constructions of Theorem 15.3.7 (§XV.25), its global transversality and the theorem from (15.1) at single points (§XV.26), step (a) of Theorem 15.3.9 and Corollary 15.3.10 (1) (§XV.27), Corollary 15.3.10 (3) and the last paragraph of its proof (§XV.28) and the witnesses of wave 5 (§XV.29).

**What is proved, and what is not.** Waves 1–5 of Part III (2026-11-13) formalize §§15.1–15.2 and the definitions of §15.3, and reduce the existence theorems of §§15.3–15.4 to facts that are open: for Theorem 15.3.7, (15.1) at single points of $S_f$, which are Part I facts behind a bridge; for the rest, the relative general position, the boundary data on the cylinder, and Theorem 15.4.1. *Theorem 15.1.1* is proved in what is its substance, the independence of $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$ from the local sc⁺-section structure and from the chart, in a stronger form: at all level-$1$ points, for any sc-smooth $f$, and on the model for any weights (§§XV.4–XV.5). The sc-Fredholm property of its summands is proved in wave 2, read in a chart, for $f$ with Part I's tame germ data (§XV.10); gap G.145 is closed. The functor property $T(f, \Lambda)(t(\varphi)) = \varphi_*T(f, \Lambda)(s(\varphi))$, which makes $T(f, \Lambda)$ a section functor, is proved in wave 3 at all level-$1$ points, a stronger form than the text's smooth points (§XV.17); gap G.144 is closed. *Remark 15.1.2* and *Definition 15.1.7* are formalized (§§XV.4–XV.5). *Lemmas 15.1.4 and 15.1.5* are proved in a stronger, topological form (§XV.1), and *Remark 15.1.6* in an explicit form (§XV.2). *Proposition 15.1.3* is proved with the added hypothesis that the base point is not isolated. At an isolated point, for instance when the local model is a single point, Proposition 15.1.3 does not hold as we read it: there is no sequence $x_k \ne 0$ with $x_k \to 0$. This is a degenerate case, and Theorem 15.1.1 is unaffected, because the formal proof does not need the sequence (§XV.2). The proof of Theorem 15.1.1 is read in two places: the separation and the limit run in the level-$1$ topology, with the "weak topology" read as pointwise convergence of operators; and the final sum is presumably over the $i$ with $f(0) = s_i(0)$ (§XV.4). *§15.2.* Definitions 15.2.1 and 15.2.4 are formalized, the first with "nonzero" and "sc-Fredholm" proved automatic (§§XV.11–XV.12). Theorems 15.2.2 and 15.2.5 and Remark 15.2.3 are proved with Part I's tame germ data for $f$, inherited from Theorem 3.6.8, on which they rest (§§XV.11–XV.12); in wave 5 their tame submanifolds and tame branched ep⁺-subgroupoids (Definition 9.3.6) are proved, and Remark 15.2.3 and Theorem 15.2.5 also on the ep-groupoid $U(x)$, read as the translation groupoid $G_x \ltimes U(x)$, where the paracompactness of the support is proved; the global forms on $X$ need a paracompact support (§XV.24); gaps G.150 and G.152 are closed. Theorem 15.2.5 under general position, its closing sentence, is proved for tame $X$ (§XV.18); gap G.151 is closed. Remark 15.2.6 is prose. *§15.3.* The paragraph before Definition 15.3.1, Definitions 15.3.1, 15.3.3, 15.3.5, the example after Definition 15.3.3 and the first sentence of Remark 15.3.6 are formalized and proved (§XV.14); the rest of Remark 15.3.6 is proved with the inherited tame germ data, at every point of the support, and with a paracompact support for the branched ep⁺-subgroupoid, which is tame (§§XV.19, XV.24); gap G.161 is closed. Theorem 15.3.7 is stated, and its "in particular" is proved, with "tame" (§§XV.20, XV.24). Its existence part is proved from a good system and two facts about (15.1) at single points of $S_f$, small vectors that satisfy it and its openness along $S_f$ (§§XV.25–XV.26): the two analytic steps of the text's proof, the local families and the parametric transversality, are proved from them and from the theorem's hypotheses. The two facts are Part I facts behind a bridge that is not formalized. Theorem 15.3.9 is stated and proved from tame strong bundle charts, the extension of Theorem 14.1.9 (Part XIV, §XIV.22) and the relative general position of steps (c)–(d) of its proof; its step (a) is proved (§§XV.21, XV.27); gap G.177 is closed with the tame bundle charts. Corollary 15.3.10 (1) is reduced to Theorem 15.3.7, with the tameness of $X$ derived from $d_X \equiv 0$ (§XV.27); gap G.183 is closed. Corollary 15.3.10 (3) is reduced to Theorem 15.3.9 on $[0, 1] \times X$, whose paracompactness is proved, with the partitions of unity of the cylinder and the structurability and face condition of the glued boundary data as hypotheses, jointly satisfiable (§XV.28). Corollary 15.3.10 (2) is proved, with explicit $\widetilde N$, $\widetilde U$, over a tame ep-groupoid $[0, 1]^n \times X$ built for it, whose section $\tilde f$ is sc-Fredholm under the tame germ data of $f$ (§§XV.13, XV.15), and the last paragraph of the proof of the corollary is proved (§XV.28). Product ep-groupoids exist (§XV.13); product strong bundles and $\Lambda \times \Lambda'$ (the products remark and Remark 15.3.4) do not. Remarks 15.3.2, 15.3.8 and 15.3.11 are prose. *§15.4.* Theorem 15.4.1 and Definition 15.4.2 are not formalized (G.159). Theorem 15.4.3 is proved with the orientation of $\Lambda \circ f$ taken as data, by Part IX's Stokes theorem (§XV.22). Corollary 15.4.4 is proved from the existence of oriented cobordisms between regular perturbations, which is open; the cobordism argument itself, with Stokes and $dF^* = F^*d$, is proved (§XV.22). Remark 15.4.5 is prose. *Open:* G.159, G.160, G.162, G.178–G.182, as listed in §XV.7. No statement of §§15.2–15.4 was found not to hold as we read it.

**Three structural choices.** (1) *Formal sums are finitely supported functions.* $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$ is the set of finitely supported functions from operators $T_xX \to W_x$ to $\mathbb Q^+$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.GrF⟧, defined at every level-$1$ point; that the operators are sc-Fredholm is not part of the type. On a strong bundle model the operators are $T_zO \to F$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationModel · Linearization15.GrFModel⟧. (2) *The separation argument is pure topology.* Propositions and lemmas about finitely many continuous maps $s_i$ are proved in topological or (pseudo-)metric spaces, with values in a Hausdorff space, and applied on the level-$1$ subspace $U_1 \subset E_1$ of the model, where the sections and their derivatives are continuous. (3) *Pairs, not operators.* The proof compares formal sums of pairs $(s_i(y), (f - s_i)'(y))$, over all $i$; the sum of Theorem 15.1.1 is then the part with first entry $f(y)$. A finite formal sum of points is $\mathrm{wsum}(a, \sigma)(q) = \sum_{i : a_i = q}\sigma_i$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.wsum⟧, and the mass of a set is the sum over the $i$ with $a_i$ in it ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.mass⟧ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.mass_eq_of_wsum_eq⟧.

Throughout, $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ is a strong bundle over an ep-groupoid, $f$ an sc-Fredholm section functor and $\Lambda$ an sc⁺-multisection with local sc⁺-section structures $(s_i, \sigma_i)$ in Chapter 11's sense ⟦Chapter11/MultisectionLocalStructure2021 · SBLocalization.IsLocalRepOn⟧ (Part XIII, §XIII.6).

### XV.1 Lemmas 15.1.4 and 15.1.5 (2017: 15.1 and 15.2): separating finitely many maps

**Lemma 15.1.4** (stronger) ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.lemma_15_1_4⟧: if a ball $B_\varepsilon(y)$ of a pseudo-metric space is the union of finitely many sets closed in it, one of them has nonempty interior. The text works in $\mathcal O$ with the metric of $E_0$ and moves a point step by step; the formal proof is an induction over the index set: a finite union of closed sets with empty interiors has empty interior ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.interior_biUnion_eq_empty⟧, so a nonempty open set covered by finitely many closed sets meets the interior of one ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.exists_nonempty_interior_of_finite_closed_cover⟧. No Baire property is needed for a finite union.

**Lemma 15.1.5** (stronger) ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.lemma_15_1_5⟧: for finitely many maps continuous on $B_\varepsilon(y)$ into a Hausdorff space there are $z$ with $d(z, y) < \varepsilon$, $\delta > 0$ and a partition $I = I_1 \sqcup \dots \sqcup I_p$ with (1) $B_\delta(z) \subset B_\varepsilon(y)$, (2) $s_i = s_{i'}$ on $B_\delta(z)$ within a piece, and (3) $s_i(u) \ne s_j(u)$ for $u \in B_\delta(z)$ across pieces. The maps need only be continuous; they need not be sc⁺-sections. *Topological form* ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.exists_isOpen_dichotomy⟧: inside any nonempty open set there is a nonempty open $W$ on which each pair of maps either coincides or differs at every point. The proof goes through the pairs one at a time. For a pair, the set where $s_i \ne s_j$ is open in $W$ (Hausdorff values); if it is empty the two maps coincide on $W$, and otherwise $W$ is shrunk to it. This route does not need Lemma 15.1.4. The pieces are the classes of "coincide on $W$" ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.exists_fin_partition⟧. A point is *locally dichotomous* when every pair coincides near it or differs at it ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.IsLocDich⟧, and such points lie in every nonempty open set ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.exists_isLocDich_mem⟧.

### XV.2 Proposition 15.1.3 (2017: 15.1) and Remark 15.1.6

**The separation property** at a point $z$ for a partition $e : I \to \{1, \dots, p\}$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.IsSeparatedAt⟧: (1) $s_i(z) = s_{i'}(z)$ iff $e(i) = e(i')$; (2) then $s_i = s_{i'}$ near $z$.

**Proposition 15.1.3** (narrower) ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.proposition_15_1_3_hyp⟧. Let $Z$ be a first countable $T_1$ space, $s_i$ finitely many maps continuous on an open $V \ni x_0$ with values in a Hausdorff space, and $x_0$ not isolated. Then there are $x_k \in V$, $x_k \ne x_0$, $x_k \to x_0$, and one partition $e$ with the separation property at every $x_k$. The text states it on the local model $\mathcal O$ with $x_0 = 0$. *Step 1.* For a countable decreasing basis $(B_k)$ of neighbourhoods of $x_0$ inside $V$, each $B_k \setminus \{x_0\}$ is open and nonempty, because $x_0$ is not isolated and $Z$ is $T_1$; it contains a locally dichotomous point $z_k$ (§XV.1), and $z_k \to x_0$. *Step 2, the subsequence.* There are finitely many patterns of coincidence; along a subsequence the pattern is constant, and it defines $e$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.exists_isSeparatedAt_subseq⟧.

**The added hypothesis**, that $x_0$ is not isolated, is not derived from the text; its witness is two maps on $\mathbb R$ at $0$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.proposition_15_1_3_hyp_witness⟧. **At an isolated point, Proposition 15.1.3 does not hold as we read it.** If $\{x_0\}$ is open there is no sequence $x_k \ne x_0$ with $x_k \to x_0$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.not_proposition_15_1_3_of_isolated⟧; this happens for the one-point local model $\mathcal O = \{0\}$ of a zero-dimensional $X$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.not_proposition_15_1_3_point⟧. The case is degenerate: there the statement of Theorem 15.1.1 holds directly, and the formal proof of Theorem 15.1.1 does not use Proposition 15.1.3 (§XV.3).

**Remark 15.1.6** (explicit). *First part* ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.remark_15_1_6⟧: in a metric space, from any $x'_k \to x_0$ in $V$ there are $x''_k \in V$ with $d(x'_k, x''_k) < 1/(k+1)$ and a subsequence of $(x''_k)$ with the properties of Proposition 15.1.3; "slightly" is the bound $1/(k+1)$. *Second part* ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.IsSeparatedAt.eventually⟧: the separation property at $z$ holds at all $z'$ near $z$, for maps continuous at $z$; so small moves of the points keep it.

### XV.3 The core of Theorem 15.1.1: two families with the same counts

**The limit step** ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.wsum_eq_of_frequently⟧: two finite formal sums of points $a_i(z)$, $b_j(z)$ of a Hausdorff space, continuous at $x_0$, which agree for $z$ frequently near $x_0$, agree at $x_0$. Near $x_0$ the points $a_i(z)$ lie close to the finitely many $a_i(x_0)$; separating these by disjoint neighbourhoods, the weight of each neighbourhood is the weight of the corresponding point at $x_0$.

**At a locally dichotomous point** ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.wsum_pair_eq_at_of_isLocDich⟧. Let $c_\alpha$, $\alpha \in I \sqcup K$, be the branches of two families with weights $\sigma$, $\tau$ and equal weighted counts of every value at $u$, and let $D_\alpha(u)$ depend only on the germ of $c_\alpha$ at $u$. If $u$ is locally dichotomous for the combined family, all branches through a value $v$ coincide near $u$, so they have one $D$, say $L_v$. Hence the formal sum of pairs gives $(v, L)$ the weight of $v$ if $L = L_v$ and $0$ otherwise ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.wsum_pair_of_const⟧, the same for both families.

**The core lemma** ⟦Chapter15/P3T_SeparationLemmas · Linearization15.wsum_pair_eq_of_isLocal⟧. Let both families be continuous on an open $V$, with equal weighted counts of every value at every point of $V$, and let the "derivatives" $D_\alpha$ be continuous on $V$ and depend only on germs. Then at every $x_0 \in V$ the formal sums $\sum\sigma_i \cdot (c_i, D_i)$ and $\sum\tau_j \cdot (c_j, D_j)$ agree. *Proof.* Locally dichotomous points of the combined family lie in every neighbourhood of $x_0$ (§XV.1); the sums agree there, and the limit step carries the equality to $x_0$. The text separates the two structures by forming their union and halving the weights; here Lemma 15.1.5 is applied to the combined family $I \sqcup K$ at once. The points used may include $x_0$ itself, so no sequence $x_k \ne x_0$ is needed, and isolated points are covered.

### XV.4 Theorem 15.1.1 (2017: 15.1) and Remark 15.1.2 (2017: 15.1) on a strong bundle model and in a chart

**The model.** $U \triangleleft F$ is a strong bundle model with retraction $R$, $O = r(U)$, and principal parts $\hat f$, $\hat s_i$ with $\hat f \circ r$, $\hat s_i \circ r$ sc-smooth on $U$. At a level-$1$ point $z$, $(\hat f - \hat s_i)'(z)$ is $D((\hat f - \hat s_i) \circ r)(z)$ restricted to $T_zO$, Part I's linearization in a chart, and $\sum_{i : \hat s_i(z) = \hat f(z)}\sigma_i \cdot (\hat f - \hat s_i)'(z)$ is the formal sum ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationModel · Linearization15.linSumModel⟧.

**Two readings of the proof.** (a) The text takes the points $x_k$ of Proposition 15.1.3 in the metric of $E_0$ and passes to the limit of $T(f - s_i)(x_k)$ "in the weak topology". The derivative of an sc¹ map is continuous only on level $1$, and there pointwise as an operator $E_0 \to F_0$ (Definition 1.1.15 (3)). Presumably the limit is meant in this sense: the separation runs on the level-$1$ subspace, where the sections are continuous, and the derivatives are continuous into the topology of pointwise convergence ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationModel · Linearization15.continuousOn_scDeriv_coe⟧. The derivative at a level-$1$ point depends only on the values near it in the level-$1$ topology ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationModel · Linearization15.scDeriv_eq_of_eventuallyEq_lvl⟧. (b) The last display sums $\sigma_iT(f - s_i)(0)$ over all $i$ and uses $f(0) = s_i(0)$; this holds only for some $i$, and the sum is presumably over $\{i : f(0) = s_i(0)\}$. The formal proof compares the formal sums of the pairs $(\hat s_i(z), (\hat f - \hat s_i)'(z))$ over all $i$ and then selects those with first entry $\hat f(z)$.

**On the model** ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationModel · Linearization15.wsum_model_eq⟧: if two structures $(\hat s_i, \sigma_i)$, $(\hat t_j, \tau_j)$ give the same weighted count of every value at every point of $O \cap N$, $N$ open, then the formal sums of pairs agree at every level-$1$ point over $O \cap N$. This is the core lemma on $U_1$ with $c_\alpha = \hat s_\alpha \circ r$ and $D_\alpha$ the derivative of $(\hat f - \hat s_\alpha) \circ r$; the germ condition holds by locality of the derivative. **Theorem 15.1.1 on the model** ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationModel · Linearization15.theorem_15_1_1_model⟧: the formal sums $\sum_{i : \hat s_i = \hat f}\sigma_i(\hat f - \hat s_i)'$ agree at every level-$1$ point of $O \cap N$ (selection of the pairs with first entry $\hat f(z)$), also after pushing forward by any map of operators ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationModel · Linearization15.theorem_15_1_1_model_map⟧. Neither $\Lambda$ being a functor nor positivity of the weights is used.

**Remark 15.1.2** (restated) ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationModel · Linearization15.remark_15_1_2_model⟧. In the formalization $(f - s_i)'$ is defined for every $i$, and the sum is filtered by $s_i(y) = f(y)$, which is the text's point that only defined terms are counted. With positive weights the formal sum is $0$ where the weighted count of $\hat f(y)$ is $0$, so (1) follows from (2); and the operators with nonzero coefficient are those $(\hat f - \hat s_i)'(z)$ with $\hat s_i = \hat f$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationModel · Linearization15.mem_support_linSumModel_iff⟧.

**In a strong bundle chart.** A local sc⁺-section on $O$ has an sc-smooth principal part $\hat s \circ r$ in every chart with domain in $O$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_Linearization · SBLocalization.IsScPlusSectionOn.isScSmooth_principal_comp_r⟧, and in the chart the weighted count of $v$ at $y$ is $\Lambda(\Phi^{-1}(y, v))$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_Linearization · SBLocalization.IsLocalRepOn.count_eq⟧. So two structures of the same $\Lambda$ have the same counts, and the model applies: **Theorem 15.1.1 in a chart** ⟦Chapter15/P3T_Linearization · SBLocalization.theorem_15_1_1⟧ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_Linearization · SBLocalization.linSumChart⟧: for two structures of $\Lambda$ on open $O$, $O'$, the formal sums agree at every level-$1$ point of a chart with domain in $O \cap O'$, for any sc-smooth $f$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_Linearization · SBLocalization.linSumChart_eq⟧. Every object lies in such a chart ⟦Chapter15/P3T_Linearization · SBLocalization.exists_chart_isLocalRepOn⟧. *Definition 15.1.7 in a chart* ⟦Chapter15/P3T_Linearization · SBLocalization.linearizationIn⟧ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_Linearization · SBLocalization.linearizationIn_eq⟧, with Remark 15.1.2 ⟦Chapter15/P3T_Linearization · SBLocalization.remark_15_1_2⟧.

### XV.5 Theorem 15.1.1 with intrinsic operators, and Definition 15.1.7 (2017: 15.1)

**Intrinsic operators.** From an operator $L$ of a chart $c$, $\Phi_x^{-1} \circ L \circ T\varphi : T_xX \to W_x$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.toIntr⟧, read through the chart operators ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.chartOp⟧. The formal sum through $c$ is $\sum_{i : f(x) = s_i(x)}\sigma_i \cdot (f - s_i)'(x) \in \mathrm{GrF}(x)$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.linSumIntr⟧. *The reduction "without loss of generality $X = O$"* is a change of chart. A global section equal to $f - s$ on $O$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.sectionSubOn⟧ has an sc-smooth principal part in every chart with domain in $O$, and at a zero of $f - s$ the intrinsic operator $(f - s)'(x)$ is the same through any two such charts ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.toIntr_chart_independent⟧, by Part I's chain rule for linearizations. So the formal sum does not depend on the chart ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.linSumIntr_chart_independent⟧.

**Theorem 15.1.1** (narrower) ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.theorem_15_1_1_intrinsic⟧: for an sc-Fredholm section functor $f$ and two local structures of $\Lambda$ on open $O$, $O'$, the formal sums in $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$ agree, through any two charts with domains in $O$ and $O'$, at every $x \in X_1$ in both domains. The two structures are compared through a common restricted chart (§XV.4), and each through the change of chart. The theorem is stated for sc-Fredholm $f$, as in the text, and uses only that $f$ is sc-smooth.

**Definition 15.1.7** (restated) ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.linearization⟧. *Local data* at $x$ are a local structure of $\Lambda$ on an open $O$ and a chart around $x$ with domain in $O$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.LocalLinData⟧, with their formal sum ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.LocalLinData.sum⟧. $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$ is the sum of some local data, and $0$ if there are none. Data exist for an sc⁺-multisection ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.nonempty_localLinData⟧, and any data give the value ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.linearization_eq⟧; this is Theorem 15.1.1 (2). Theorem 15.1.1 (1) and Remark 15.1.2: $T(f, \Lambda)(x) = 0$ where $\Lambda(f(x)) = 0$, that is, off $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$ ⟦Chapter15/P3T_LinearizationIntrinsic · SBLocalization.linearization_eq_zero⟧. The definition is made at every level-$1$ point; it is not yet shown to be a section functor (§XV.7).

### XV.6 Witnesses and the hypotheses

**Hypotheses taken.** One: in Proposition 15.1.3, that $x_0$ is not isolated, not derived from the text, with witness `proposition_15_1_3_hyp_witness` (two maps on $\mathbb R$ at $0$); without it the proposition does not hold as we read it (§XV.2). Theorem 15.1.1 takes no added hypothesis and holds at isolated points as well. It takes sc-Fredholm $f$ as the text does and uses only sc-smoothness.

**Every definition has a witness.** $\mathrm{GrF}(x)$ and $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$ exist at every level-$1$ point of a strong bundle with an sc⁺-multisection (`nonempty_localLinData`); sc⁺-multisections exist, for instance the zero multisection (Part XIII, §XIII.6). The separation property: the witness of Proposition 15.1.3.

### XV.8 What the formalization taught us

The proof of Theorem 15.1.1 is a statement about finitely many continuous maps and their germs, and it holds in that generality: two finite families of branches with the same weighted count of every value at every point have the same formal sums of (value, germ-invariant) pairs, at every point, as soon as the germ invariants vary continuously. Lemmas 15.1.4 and 15.1.5, Proposition 15.1.3 and Remark 15.1.6 are pure topology. Written this way two places of the text needed a reading. The derivative of an sc¹ map is continuous only on level $1$, and there pointwise; so the argument runs in the level-$1$ topology, where it holds equally, and the text's "weak topology" is pointwise convergence. And the final sum of the text runs over all branches, as if every $s_i(0)$ equalled $f(0)$; comparing pairs (value, derivative) for all branches and then selecting the value $f(0)$ avoids this. Applying the separation to the two families together, rather than to their union with halved weights, gives the comparison in one step. Proposition 15.1.3 asks for a sequence $x_k \ne 0$ converging to $0$, which a one-point local model does not have; at an isolated point the proposition does not hold as we read it. Nothing depends on it: the core lemma needs locally dichotomous points in every neighbourhood of $x_0$, and $x_0$ may be one of them. The step "without loss of generality $X = O$" is, formally, the independence of the intrinsic operator $(f - s)'(x)$ from the chart, which Part I's chain rule supplies at a zero of $f - s$. The functor property, for which the text gives no argument, is the same chain rule once more: a local section structure near $s(\varphi)$ is carried to one near $t(\varphi)$ by the local strong bundle isomorphism of the sheet of $\varphi$, and in the carried chart $T\varphi$ is the identity on chart vectors, so the intrinsic operators are conjugate by $\mu(\varphi, \cdot)$.

§15.2 is Part I's implicit function theorem applied branch by branch, and its formal content is the passage from a local sc⁺-section $s_i$ on $O$ to a global section problem: $s_i$ is a global sc⁺-section of the restricted bundle $W|_O$, and $(f - s_i)|_O$ is an sc-Fredholm section there, so Part I's Theorems 3.1.18 and 3.6.8 apply. This also gives the sc-Fredholm property of the summands of $T(f, \Lambda)$, which wave 1 left open; the operators $T_xX \to W_x$ carry no sc-structure of their own, so the property is read in a chart. The price is the hypothesis of Part I's Theorem 3.6.8: tame germ data, without which that theorem does not hold as we read it (Part III, §III.65). It is inherited, not new, and it is the same hypothesis that §12.5 and the cylinder $[0, 1] \times X$ carry. Definition 15.2.1 asks for less than it says: "nonzero" and "sc-Fredholm" are automatic, so transversality is the surjectivity of every summand; and the proof of Theorem 15.2.2, which writes $f(x) = s_i(x)$ for all $i$, presumably means the branches through $f(x)$, the others having empty solution sets near $x$. General position reduces to Part I branch by branch: on $T^R_xX$ the intrinsic operator of a branch is the derivative of the branch in a transported chart of $W|_O$, so surjectivity there is Part I's general position of $(f - s_i)|_O$, which gives good position by Part I's Lemma 5.26 and persists near $x$; this is why Remark 15.3.6 holds at every point of the support, not only at the boundary, and needs no $d_X = 0$. The tameness of the local solution sets is Part I's Theorem 3.1.26 on $W|_O$ in the same way. In §15.3 the cylinder needed more than the text says: the product with $[0, 1]$ is built as the product with Part I's cube $[0, 1]^n$, whose parametrized Fredholm theory is available, and the auxiliary norm of Corollary 15.3.10 (2), which the text does not give, is an explicit interpolation $\max(\alpha(t)N^0, \beta(t)N^1)$.

The existence theorems of §§15.3–15.4 separate cleanly into an assembly and analysis, and wave 5 moved most of the analysis to Part I. The assembly of Theorem 15.3.7 (finite covers of $|S_f|$, sums of linear families of structurable multisections, norm and support bounds, a small parameter off a null set) was proved first. Parametric transversality is Part I's Sard step branch by branch: in a tame chart a branch of $\Lambda_t$ is the slice at $t$ of Part I's parametrized section, (15.1) for the branch is Part I's general position of that section at $(0, x)$, and a local form of Part I's Theorem 5.3.10, without compactness, together with the compactness (15.2) and the invariance of general position along morphisms, which the text uses silently when it passes to saturations, gives the null set. The local families are Part XIII's atomic multisections built from seeds, linear in the parameter and carried along morphisms. What is left is (15.1) itself at one point and its openness along $S_f$, Part I facts once (15.1), which uses $T^R_xX$, is matched with Part I's conditions (i)–(ii), which use the full tangent space; the two are equivalent by two lines of linear algebra in each direction, and the text presumably relies on this when it cites the implicit function theorem for the openness. "Structurable" contains a good system, so Theorem 15.3.7 needs one, which Remark 15.3.8's dropping of paracompactness leaves unaccounted for. Theorem 15.3.9 is Theorem 14.1.9 followed by Theorem 15.3.7 relative to the boundary; its first step, the cut-off $h_0$, uses the upper semicontinuity of $N(\Lambda)$ along $\partial X$, which holds when the bundle has tame charts at every object and which the text uses without comment. The corollaries are those theorems on the cylinder: $d_X \equiv 0$ makes $X$ tame, the orbit space of the cylinder is the product of $[0, 1]$ with $|X|$, and the boundary data glued from $\Lambda^0$ and $\Lambda^1$ have the right values, support and norm, so what remains there is their structurability and face condition and the partitions of unity of $[0, 1] \times X$. "The ep-groupoid $U(x)$" of Remark 15.2.3 is the translation groupoid $G_x \ltimes U(x)$; on it the paracompactness of the support, a hypothesis on $X$, is automatic, its orbit map being closed with finite fibres. In §15.4 the cobordism argument for the invariants is Stokes' theorem with $dF^* = F^*d$ and a few lines, once a cobordism between perturbations exists; the existence is the hard part, and it needs the canonical orientation of Theorem 15.4.1 and the sign bookkeeping of the boundary orientation.

### XV.9 Local sc⁺-sections and the sections $f - s_i$ on $W|_O$ (prerequisite for §15.2)

The proofs of Theorems 15.2.2 and 15.2.5 apply the implicit function theorem to $f - s_i$ near $x$, where $s_i$ is a section of a local structure, defined only on an open $O$. The formalization makes $f - s_i$ a section problem of Part I.

**Restriction to $O$.** A local sc⁺-section on an open $O$ is a global sc⁺-section of the restricted strong bundle $W|_O$ ⟦Chapter15/P3L_LocalScPlus · SBLocalization.IsScPlusSectionOn.restrictOpen⟧; in every chart with domain in $O$ its principal part is sc-smooth after the retraction ⟦Chapter15/P3L_LocalScPlus · SBLocalization.IsScPlusSectionOn.isScSmoothRetractMap_localRepOne_of_isChart⟧. The section $f + (-1)s$, with $s$ extended by $0$ off $O$ ⟦Chapter15/P3L_LocalScPlus · SBLocalization.subSec⟧, restricts to a section of $W|_O$ ⟦Chapter15/P3L_LocalScPlus · SBLocalization.subRestrict⟧, and it is a tame sc-Fredholm section there when $f$ has Part I's tame germ data ⟦Chapter15/P3L_LocalScPlus · SBLocalization.isScFredholmSectionTame_subRestrict⟧: restriction to an open set keeps tame germ data, and an sc⁺-perturbation of a tame sc-Fredholm section is one, by Part I's Theorem 3.1.18 ⟦Chapter3/TameGermsAddG · theorem_3_1_18_tame⟧. Its zeros are the points with $f(y) = s(y)$ ⟦Chapter15/P3L_LocalScPlus · SBLocalization.isZeroAt_subSec_iff⟧.

**The linearization in a chart.** At a level-$1$ point $z$ of a chart with domain in $O$, $D((\hat f - \hat s) \circ r)(z)$ ⟦Chapter15/P3L_LocalIFT · SBLocalization.subDeriv⟧; "onto" means onto $K_z$ from $T_zO$ ⟦Chapter15/P3L_LocalIFT · SBLocalization.ChartOnto⟧. The intrinsic operator $(f - s)'(x)$ of §XV.5 is onto $W_x$ iff the chart operator is onto in this sense ⟦Chapter15/P3L_LocalIFT · SBLocalization.surjective_toIntr_subDeriv_iff⟧, and this is Part I's surjectivity of the linearization of $(f - s)|_O$ ⟦Chapter15/P3L_LocalIFT · SBLocalization.isLinSurjAt_subRestrict⟧ ⟦Chapter15/P3L_LocalIFT · SBLocalization.chartOnto_of_isLinSurjAt_subRestrict⟧, since the restricted chart has the same principal parts ⟦Chapter15/P3L_LocalIFT · SBLocalization.scDeriv_restrictTo_subRestrict⟧.

**Local solution sets.** At an interior point $x$ ($d_X(x) = 0$) with $f(x) = s(x)$ and $(f - s)'(x)$ onto ⟦Chapter15/P3L_LocalIFT · SBLocalization.exists_solutionSet_interior⟧, and at a point where $(f - s)|_O$ is in good position (Part I's Definition 3.6.6) ⟦Chapter15/P3L_LocalIFT · SBLocalization.exists_solutionSet_of_isGoodPosition⟧, there is an open $V \ni x$ such that $\{y \in V : f(y) = s(y)\}$ is a smooth submanifold (Definition 4.2.1) of smooth points, at whose points the linearization is onto, and in the second case in good position. Both come from Part I's Theorem 3.6.8 for $(f - s)|_O$ ⟦Chapter3/GlobalIFTNearbyOntoG · theorem_3_6_8'⟧, read back in $X$.

### XV.10 Theorem 15.1.1 (2017: 15.1): the summands are sc-Fredholm

**The chart operator is sc-Fredholm** ⟦Chapter15/P3L_FredholmSummands · SBLocalization.subDeriv_isScFredholm⟧. Let $f$ have tame germ data, $s$ be sc⁺ on an open $O$ containing the domain of the chart, $f(x) = s(x)$, and $z$ the chart point over $x$. Then $D((\hat f - \hat s) \circ r)(z)$ is an sc-operator, $T_zO$ and $K_z$ are sc-subspaces, and its restriction $T_zO \to K_z$ is sc-Fredholm, Fredholm on every level with the index of level $0$. The proof is Part I's statement that the linearization of an sc-Fredholm section at a zero is sc-Fredholm ⟦Chapter3/LinearizationChartsScG · StrongBundle.linAt_isScFredholm⟧, applied to $(f - s)|_O$ (§XV.9).

**Theorem 15.1.1 (2), the summands** (restated) ⟦Chapter15/P3L_FredholmSummands · SBLocalization.linearization_summand_isScFredholm⟧: for $x \in X_1$ and any local data (a local structure and a chart, §XV.5), every operator in the support of $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$ is $(f - s_i)'(x)$ for some $i$ with $f(x) = s_i(x)$, and its chart operator is sc-Fredholm as above. *Reading.* $T_xX$ and $W_x$ carry no sc-structure in the project; "sc-Fredholm $T_xX \to W_x$" is read through the identifications $T_xX \cong T_zO$ and $W_x \cong K_z$ that define the intrinsic operators. $\mathrm{GrF}$ is not cut down to a subtype; the lemma says what lies in the support. The tame germ data are Part I's (below, §XV.16).

### XV.11 Definition 15.2.1, Theorem 15.2.2 and Remark 15.2.3 (2017: Definition 15.2, Theorem 15.2, Remark 15.2): transversality and interior local perturbation

**Definition 15.2.1** (restated). $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$ is onto at $x \in X_1$ if every operator in its support is surjective ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Transversality · SBLocalization.IsOntoAtLevel⟧ ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Transversality · SBLocalization.IsOntoAt⟧; $(f, \Lambda)$ is transversal at $x$ if $\Lambda(f(x)) > 0$ and $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$ is onto ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Transversality · SBLocalization.IsTransversalAt⟧, and transversal if it is so at every point of $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$ ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Transversality · SBLocalization.IsTransversal⟧. In the text's terms ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Transversality · SBLocalization.isOntoAtLevel_iff⟧: onto iff, for any local data, every $(f - s_i)'(x)$ with $s_i(x) = f(x)$ is surjective, because the support of the formal sum consists of exactly these operators ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Transversality · SBLocalization.mem_support_linSumIntr_iff⟧. *Reading.* The text asks for a nonzero combination of surjective sc-Fredholm operators. "Nonzero" is automatic where $\Lambda(f(x)) > 0$ ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Transversality · SBLocalization.linearization_ne_zero⟧, and "sc-Fredholm" by §XV.10; so the definition asks only for surjectivity. $T(f, \Lambda)$ lives on $X_1$, and under tame germ data the support of $\Lambda \circ f$ consists of smooth points ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Transversality · SBLocalization.mem_smoothSet_of_pos⟧, since $f - s_i$ is regularizing.

**Theorem 15.2.2** (narrower) ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Transversality · SBLocalization.theorem_15_2_2_hyp⟧. Let $f$ be an sc-Fredholm section functor with tame germ data, $\Lambda$ an sc⁺-multisection, $d_X(x) = 0$ and $(f, \Lambda)$ transversal at $x$. Then there are a natural representation of $G_x$ on $U(x)$, a local structure $(s_i, \sigma_i)$ on an open $O$ and a chart with $U(x) \subset \operatorname{dom} \subset O$ such that, with $M_i = \{y \in U(x) : f(y) = s_i(y)\}$: (1) $d_X = 0$ on $U(x)$; (2) $T(f, \Lambda)$ is onto at every $y \in U(x)$ with $\Lambda(f(y)) > 0$; (a) each $M_i$ is a smooth submanifold; (b) properly embedded, the inclusion being a proper map; (c) $\{y \in U(x) : \Lambda(f(y)) > 0\} = \bigcup_iM_i$; (d) $\Lambda(f(y)) = \sum_{i : f(y) = s_i(y)}\sigma_i$ on $U(x)$; (e) $T(f, \Lambda)(y) = \sum_{f(y) = s_i(y)}\sigma_i(f - s_i)'(y)$ in the chart; and only the branches with $s_i(x) = f(x)$ meet $f$ in $U(x)$. *Proof.* *Step 1.* A local structure on an open $O \ni x$ and a chart inside it (§XV.5). *Step 2, separating the branches.* The branches with $s_i(x) \ne f(x)$ differ from $f$ on an open neighbourhood of $x$ ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Transversality · SBLocalization.isOpen_sep_ne⟧, by continuity of local sc⁺-sections ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Transversality · SBLocalization.IsScPlusSectionOn.continuousOn⟧. *Step 3, each branch through $f(x)$.* By transversality $(f - s_i)'(x)$ is onto, and §XV.9 gives an open $V_i \ni x$ on which $\{f = s_i\}$ is a smooth submanifold with onto linearizations ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Transversality · SBLocalization.exists_branch_interior⟧. *Step 4.* $\{d_X = 0\}$ is open around $x$; a natural representation inside all these sets and inside $O$, with the properness property (Theorem 7.1.13), gives $U(x)$. (c) and (d) are the local structure; (e) is Definition 15.1.7 with these data (§XV.5); properness of the inclusions is closedness of $\{f = s_i\}$ in $U(x)$. *Readings.* The index set is that of the local structure; branches with $s_i(x) \ne f(x)$ give $M_i = \emptyset$ (the last clause), where the text's sentence "by assumption, $f(x) = s_i(x)$" presumably restricts to the branches through $f(x)$. "Natural smooth manifold structure" in (a) is Definition 4.2.1 inside $\{d_X = 0\}$, so (a)'s "$d_{M_i} \equiv 0$" is (1) with Definition 4.2.1. (e) is read in one chart, which is no restriction (§XV.5). The added hypothesis is tame germ data (§XV.16); witness of all hypotheses together ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Witness · SBLocalization.theorem_15_2_2_hyp_witness⟧.

**Remark 15.2.3** (narrower). *Locally* ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Transversality · SBLocalization.remark_15_2_3_hyp⟧: at $y$ with $d_X(y) = 0$ and $(f, \Lambda)$ transversal at $y$, $z \mapsto \Lambda(f(z))$ has a local branching structure in the sense of Definition 9.1.2 (2)–(4) (Part IX, §IX.1) at $y$, with the $M_j$ of Theorem 15.2.2 for the branches through $f(y)$ and the weights $\sigma_j$. By (2) of the theorem every support point in $U(x)$ satisfies these hypotheses. *Globally* ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Transversality · SBLocalization.remark_15_2_3_isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_hyp⟧: if $(f, \Lambda)$ is transversal, $d_X = 0$ on $\operatorname{supp}(\Lambda \circ f)$ and the orbit space of the support is paracompact, then $\Lambda \circ f$ is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid. The paracompactness is Definition 9.1.2 (1), new in the 2021 edition, which the remark does not address. Witness ⟦Chapter15/P3L_Witness · SBLocalization.remark_15_2_3_isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_hyp_witness⟧, with the paracompactness from Part IX ⟦Chapter9/Propositions · EpGroupoid.paracompactSpace_orbitSupp_trivial_rn⟧. The tame form, and the statement on the ep-groupoid $U(x)$, are proved in wave 5 (§XV.24).

### XV.12 Definition 15.2.4, Theorem 15.2.5 and Remark 15.2.6 (2017: Definition 15.3, Theorem 15.3, Remark 15.3): good position and boundary local perturbation

**Definition 15.2.4** (restated). For one branch ⟦Chapter15/P3L_BoundaryPerturbation · SBLocalization.IsBranchGoodPosition⟧: $(f - s)|_O$ is in good position at $x$ in the sense of Part I's Definition 3.6.6 on $W|_O$, which gives (1) tameness near $x$ in a tame chart and (3) a linearization onto with kernel in good position to the partial quadrant. $(f, \Lambda)$ is in good position at $x$ ⟦Chapter15/P3L_BoundaryPerturbation · SBLocalization.IsGoodPositionAt⟧ if $\Lambda(f(x)) > 0$, $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$ is onto, and for some local structure on an open $O \ni x$ every branch through $f(x)$ is in good position. The text calls this "a version of Definition 3.6.6"; it is read per branch, for one local structure (the text does not say whether it depends on the structure), and $x \in \partial X$ is not required.

**Theorem 15.2.5** (narrower) ⟦Chapter15/P3L_BoundaryPerturbation · SBLocalization.theorem_15_2_5_hyp⟧: for $f$ with tame germ data and $(f, \Lambda)$ in good position at $x$, the data of Theorem 15.2.2 exist with: the $M_i$ smooth submanifolds, (1) properly embedded, $\{y \in U(x) : \Lambda(f(y)) > 0\} = \bigcup_iM_i$, (2) $(f, \Lambda)$ in good position, with the same local structure, at every $y \in U(x)$ with $\Lambda(f(y)) > 0$, (3) $\Lambda(f(y)) = \sum_{y \in M_i}\sigma_i$, the formula for $T(f, \Lambda)$, and only branches through $f(x)$ meet. The proof is that of Theorem 15.2.2 with the second local solution lemma of §XV.9 per branch ⟦Chapter15/P3L_BoundaryPerturbation · SBLocalization.exists_branch_goodPosition⟧: good position is open along the solution set (Part I), so it persists at nearby solutions. "Tame submanifolds" and "tame branched" (Definition 9.3.6) are proved in wave 5 (§XV.24), and the closing variant with $T^R_yX$ in §XV.18. **Remark 15.2.6** is prose pointing to §15.4; the data it needs, the $M_i$ and the surjective $(f - s_i)'(y)$, are those of Theorems 15.2.2 and 15.2.5.

### XV.13 Product ep-groupoids, and $[0, 1]^n \times X$ (prerequisites for §15.3)

**Products** (extra) ⟦Chapter15/P3P_ProductEp · EpGroupoid.prod⟧. The product $X \times X'$ of ep-groupoids has componentwise structure maps ⟦Chapter15/P3P_ProductEp · GroupoidStr.prod⟧; the étale property comes from products of local sc-diffeomorphisms ⟦Chapter15/P3P_ProductEp · MPolyfold.IsLocalScDiffeo.prodMap⟧, properness from products of proper maps ⟦Chapter15/P3P_ProductEp · isProperMap_domRestrict_prod⟧, and sc-smooth composition is checked in its local sheet form ⟦Chapter15/P3P_ProductEp · EpGroupoid.prod_isScSmoothCompSheet⟧. The projections are functors ⟦Chapter15/P3P_ProductEp · EpGroupoid.prodFst⟧, tameness passes to products ⟦Chapter15/P3P_ProductEp · EpGroupoid.isTame_prod⟧, $d_{X \times X'} = d_X + d_{X'}$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_ProductEp · EpGroupoid.degIndex_prod⟧, and two objects are isomorphic iff their components are ⟦Chapter15/P3P_ProductEp · EpGroupoid.prod_π_eq_π_iff⟧.

**The cylinder** ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeEp · EpGroupoid.cubeProd⟧: $[0, 1]^n \times X$, the product of the trivial ep-groupoid of Part I's cube with $X$; the text's $[0, 1] \times X$ is $n = 1$. The cube is used because Part I's parametrized Fredholm theory is stated for it. The projection to $X$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeEp · EpGroupoid.cubeProj⟧ and the inclusions at $q \in [0, 1]^n$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeEp · EpGroupoid.cubeIncl⟧ are functors; the orbit space is $[0, 1]^n \times |X|$ in the sense that the orbit map is continuous ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeEp · EpGroupoid.continuous_cubeOrbitMap⟧ and compact sets of $|X|$ give compact sets ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeEp · EpGroupoid.isCompact_image_π_cubeProd⟧. It is tame ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeEp · EpGroupoid.isTame_cubeProd⟧; for $n = 1$ and $d_X \equiv 0$, $d(t, x) = 1$ iff $t \in \{0, 1\}$, so $\partial([0, 1] \times X) = \{0, 1\} \times X$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeEp · EpGroupoid.degIndex_cubeProd_one_of_degIndex_eq_zero⟧. Bump functions pass to it ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeEp · EpGroupoid.admitsBumpFunctionsPointwise_cubeProd⟧. **The bundle and the section.** $\widetilde W$ is the pull-back of $W$ along the projection ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeEp · SEP.cubeSEP⟧, and $\tilde f(q, x) = (q, f(x))$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeEp · SEP.cubeLiftEp⟧ is an sc-smooth section functor ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeEp · SEP.isScSmoothSectionFunctor_cubeLiftEp⟧, sc-Fredholm when $f$ has tame germ data ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeEp · SEP.isScFredholmSectionFunctor_cubeLiftEp⟧, by Part I's parametrized form for the cube (gap G.65 (a) of Part I concerns the untamed case), with $S_{\tilde f} = [0, 1]^n \times S_f$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeEp · SEP.solutionSet_cubeLiftEp⟧ and $|S_{\tilde f}|$ compact when $|S_f|$ is ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeEp · SEP.hasCompactSolutionSetEp_cubeLiftEp⟧.

### XV.14 The paragraph before Definition 15.3.1, Definitions 15.3.1, 15.3.3, 15.3.5 and Remark 15.3.6 (2017: Definitions 15.4, 15.5, 15.6, Remark 15.6)

**Definition 15.3.1** (restated) ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.ControlsCompactness⟧: $(N, U)$ controls the compactness of $f$ if $N$ is an auxiliary norm, $U$ a saturated open neighbourhood of $S_f$, and $\operatorname{cl}_{|X|}|\{x \in U : N(f(x)) \le 1\}|$ is compact. $N$ lives on $W_{0,1}$, and "$N(f(x)) \le 1$" is Part I's relation, which is the text's extension of $N$ by $+\infty$. Paracompactness of $|X|$ is not part of the definition; the statements that need it carry it. A smaller saturated open $U' \supset S_f$ also controls ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.ControlsCompactness.mono⟧. **The paragraph before the definition** ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.exists_controlsCompactness⟧: for an sc-Fredholm section functor with compact $|S_f|$ and any auxiliary norm $N$, some $U$ controls the compactness, by Theorem 12.4.2 (Part XII, §XII.9) ⟦Chapter12/P3S_CompactnessEp · EpStrongBundle.isProperLtInftyFunctor_of_hasCompactSolutionSetEp⟧.

**Definition 15.3.3** ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.IsAdmissible⟧: an $(N, U)$-admissible perturbation is an sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda$ with $N(\Lambda)(x) \le 1$ for all $x$ (Definition 13.2.3) and $\{x : \exists t \in [-1, 1],\ (t\Lambda)(f(x)) > 0\} \subset U$ ($t\Lambda$ of Definition 13.2.10). The text's standing data are hypotheses of the statements that use it. **The example after it** ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.isAdmissible_of_domSupp_subset⟧: if $S_f \subset U$, the domain support of $\Lambda$ lies in $U$ and $N(\Lambda) \le 1$, then $\Lambda$ is admissible. Off the domain support $\Lambda$ is trivial ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.eq_zero_of_not_mem_domSupp⟧, so $(t\Lambda)(w) > 0$ forces $w = 0$ for every real $t$, $t = 0$ included ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.eq_fiberZero_of_multisectionSmul_pos⟧; then $f(x) = 0$ and $x \in S_f \subset U$.

**Definition 15.3.5** (restated) ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.IsInGeneralPosition⟧: $(f, \Lambda)$ is in general position if for every $x \in X_1$ with $\Lambda(f(x)) > 0$ and every operator $L$ in the support of $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$, the restriction of $L$ to the reduced tangent space $T^R_xX$ is surjective, $T^R_xX$ read in every chart around $x$ and every presentation of its partial quadrant (Part I's reduced tangent fibre). Charts and presentations exist at every point ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.exists_chart_presentation⟧, and since $T^R_xX$ does not depend on them, one per point suffices ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.isInGeneralPosition_iff_exists⟧. The reduced linearization $T^R_{(f,\Lambda)}(x)$ is the formal sum of the restrictions ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.reducedLinearization⟧ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.isInGeneralPosition_iff_reducedLinearization⟧. The support of $\Lambda \circ f$ lies in $X_1$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.mem_levelSet_one_of_pos⟧ ($f(x)$ is then a value of an sc⁺-section, in $W_{0,1}$, and $f$ is regularizing), so restricting to $X_1$ loses nothing. The all-charts form is satisfiable with nonempty support ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.isInGeneralPosition_witness⟧: the zero section of $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^0 \to \mathbb R^n$ with the zero multisection. **Remark 15.3.6, first sentence** ⟦Chapter15/P3P_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.IsInGeneralPosition.surjective⟧: in general position every operator of $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$ is onto, since its restriction to a subspace is. The rest of the remark is §XV.19, its "tame" §XV.24.

### XV.15 Corollary 15.3.10 (2) (2017: Corollary 15.1 (2)): an auxiliary norm on $[0, 1] \times X$

**The pulled-back norm** ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · SEP.cubeAuxNorm⟧: $\widetilde N(q, x, h) = N(h)$, Part I's pull-back of an auxiliary norm, is an auxiliary norm of $(\widetilde W, \tilde\mu)$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · SEP.isAuxNorm_cubeAuxNorm⟧, invariant under $\tilde\mu$ because $\tilde\mu$ acts on the $W$-component by $\mu$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · SEP.cubeVal_μ⟧. **The step of the proof** ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · SEP.controlsCompactness_cube⟧: if $(N, U)$ controls the compactness of $f$, then $(\widetilde N, [0, 1]^n \times U)$ controls that of $\tilde f$; the sublevel set is $[0, 1]^n$ times that of $f$, and its orbit set has compact closure ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · SEP.isCompact_closure_image_π_cube⟧.

**Corollary 15.3.10 (2)** ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · SEP.corollary_15_3_10_2⟧: for $(N^0, U^0)$ and $(N^1, U^1)$ controlling the compactness of $f$, the norm $\widetilde N = \max(\alpha(t)N^0, \beta(t)N^1)$ with $\alpha(t) = \min(1, 3(1 - t))$, $\beta(t) = \min(1, 3t)$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · SEP.interpAuxNorm⟧ and the set $\widetilde U = ([0, \tfrac23) \times U^0) \cup ((\tfrac13, 1] \times U^1)$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · SEP.interpSet⟧ control the compactness of $\tilde f$ on $[0, 1] \times X$. *Step 1.* $\max(aN_0, bN_1)$ is an auxiliary norm for continuous $a, b \ge 0$ never both $0$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · StrongBundle.isAuxNorm_max_mul⟧: continuity and the seminorm property are clear, completeness passes to an equivalent fibre norm ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · StrongBundle.IsCompleteFiberNorm.congr⟧, and condition (2) holds for the larger of the two terms; so $\widetilde N$ is an auxiliary norm ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · SEP.isAuxNorm_interpAuxNorm⟧. *Step 2.* $\widetilde U$ is open, saturated and contains $S_{\tilde f} = [0, 1] \times S_f$. *Step 3.* On $[0, \tfrac23) \times U^0$, $\alpha = 1$ and $\widetilde N \ge N^0$, so the sublevel set lies in $[0, 1] \times$ the sublevel set of $(N^0, U^0)$; similarly on the other piece; the orbit set lies in the union of two sets with compact closure. *Restrictions.* Over $t = 0$, $\widetilde N = N^0$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · SEP.interpAuxNorm_of_cubeTime_eq_zero⟧ and $\widetilde U$ is $U^0$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · SEP.mem_interpSet_zero⟧; over $t = 1$ they are $N^1$ and $U^1$ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · SEP.interpAuxNorm_of_cubeTime_eq_one⟧ ⟦Chapter15/P3P_CubeAuxNorm · SEP.mem_interpSet_one⟧. The text does not give $\widetilde N$; its proof uses a single $N$, which is the step above. The perturbations $\Lambda^i$ of the corollary play no role in (2). With §XV.13 ($\tilde f$ sc-Fredholm with compact solution set) all of (2) is covered, $\tilde f$ carrying the tame germ data of $f$.

### XV.16 Witnesses and the hypotheses of wave 2

**Hypotheses taken.** *Tame germ data for $f$* (Part I's `IsScFredholmSectionTame`), in Theorems 15.2.2, 15.2.5, Remark 15.2.3, the summands of §XV.10 and the sc-Fredholm property of $\tilde f$ in §XV.13. It is not new: it is inherited from Part I's Theorems 3.1.18 and 3.6.8, which are proved for tame germ data and on which these statements rest; with the 2021 untamed notion Theorem 3.6.8 does not hold as we read it ⟦Chapter3/GapP1_UntamedBundleTheorem · UntamedCorner.theorem_3_6_8_untamed_not⟧ (Part III, §III.65). It is the hypothesis of gap G.140 in §12.5 as well. No ep-level counterexample for the untamed §15.2 was built. Witness for all hypotheses of Theorem 15.2.2 together (`theorem_15_2_2_hyp_witness`): over $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^0 \to \mathbb R^n$, the graph section of $0$, which has tame germ data by Part I ⟦Chapter3/NonVacuityG · isScFredholmSectionTame_graphSection⟧, with the zero multisection; it is transversal, $d_X \equiv 0$, and $\Lambda_0(f(x)) = 1$ everywhere. *The global form of Remark 15.2.3* has, besides, $d_X = 0$ on the support and a paracompact orbit space of the support, witnessed by the same example. *None added* in §§XV.13–XV.15 beyond the tame germ data of $\tilde f$.

**Every definition has a witness.** Transversality: the example above. Good position at a point: not witnessed separately (at interior points Part I's graph section would give one on $W|_O$). Controlling compactness: from any auxiliary norm when $|S_f|$ is compact (§XV.14). Admissible perturbations: the zero multisection, by the example after Definition 15.3.3. General position with nonempty support: `isInGeneralPosition_witness`. Product ep-groupoids and cylinders: of any ep-groupoid (§XV.13).

### XV.17 Theorem 15.1.1 (2017: 15.1): the functor property

**The action of a morphism on $\mathrm{GrF}$** ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.grfPush⟧: for $\varphi : x \to y$ at level $1$, $\varphi_*(\sum\sigma_LL) = \sum\sigma_L\,\mu(\varphi, \cdot) \circ L \circ (T\varphi)^{-1}$, the push-forward of formal sums along $L \mapsto \mu(\varphi, \cdot) \circ L \circ (T\varphi)^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.conjOp⟧ ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.conjOp_apply⟧. Here $\mu(\varphi, \cdot)$ is a linear map $W_x \to W_y$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.muLin⟧ and $T\varphi$ is Chapter 7's intrinsic tangent isomorphism of a morphism (Part VII). A morphism with source at level $1$ lies at level $1$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.mem_levelSet_one_of_src⟧.

**Carrying a local structure along a morphism.** Wave 1 attached to $\varphi$ a local strong bundle isomorphism built from its sheet (Part XII, §XII.10). Local sections near $s(\varphi)$ are carried to sections near $t(\varphi)$ by $\Psi \circ s \circ \phi$ on the image of the sheet ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.transSec⟧ ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.transSet⟧, an open set ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.isOpen_transSet⟧; sc⁺-sections stay sc⁺ ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.isScPlusSectionOn_transSec⟧, and a local section structure of $\Lambda$ is carried to one ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.isLocalRepOn_transSec⟧, because $\Lambda$ is a functor and the isomorphism acts by $\mu$ on fibres ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.isWFunctor_morIso_Φ⟧. A chart at $x$ is carried to the transported chart at $y$ (§XII.23), in which the principal parts of the carried sections are those of the given ones ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.principal_transportChart_transSec⟧.

**The chain rule in the carried chart.** In the transported chart, $T\varphi$ is the identity on chart vectors ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.chartVec_transport⟧, and the fibre part of the transported chart composed with $\mu(\varphi, \cdot)$ is that of the given chart ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.fiberLin_transport_muLin⟧. So the intrinsic operator of a carried branch in the carried chart is the conjugate of the given one ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.toIntr_transportChart⟧, and the formal sums of §XV.5 correspond under $\varphi_*$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.linSumIntr_transportChart⟧.

**The functor property** (stronger) ⟦Chapter15/P3W3K_LinearizationFunctor · SBLocalization.theorem_15_1_1_functor⟧: for an sc-Fredholm section functor $f$, an sc⁺-multisection $\Lambda$ and a morphism $\varphi$ between level-$1$ points $x$, $y$, $T(f, \Lambda)(y) = \varphi_*T(f, \Lambda)(x)$. By §XV.5, $T(f, \Lambda)(y)$ may be computed from any local section structure and any chart at $y$; take the carried ones. The text's smooth points become all level-$1$ points. That $\varphi \mapsto \varphi_*$ is itself functorial is not formalized and not needed (§XV.7).

### XV.18 Theorem 15.2.5 (2017: 15.3) under general position, and witnesses for §15.2

**General position at a point** ⟦Chapter15/P3W4SM_GeneralPositionLocal · SBLocalization.IsInGeneralPositionAt⟧: Definition 15.3.5 read at one point $x$ of the support, every operator of $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$ onto $W_x$ on $T^R_xX$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4SM_GeneralPositionLocal · SBLocalization.IsReducedOntoAtLevel⟧; general position is this at every point of the support ⟦Chapter15/P3W4SM_GeneralPositionLocal · SBLocalization.isInGeneralPosition_iff_forall_at⟧.

**From general position to good position** ⟦Chapter15/P3W4SM_GeneralPositionLocal · SBLocalization.isGoodPositionAt_of_isInGeneralPositionAt⟧: for $f$ with tame germ data, general position at $x$ gives good position at $x$ (Definition 15.2.4, §XV.12). For each branch, $\ker(f - s_i)'(x) + T^R_xX = T_xX$ when the operator is onto on $T^R_xX$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4SM_GeneralPositionLocal · StrongBundle.linKer_sup_reduced_eq_of_isGeneralPositionAt⟧, so $(f - s_i)|_O$ is in Part I's general position at $x$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4SM_GeneralPositionLocal · SBLocalization.isGeneralPositionGerm_branch_at⟧ and hence in good position (Part I's Lemma 5.26). *Conversely*, Part I's general position germs give surjectivity on $T^R_yX$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4SM_GeneralPositionLocal · SBLocalization.isReducedOntoAtLevel_of_isGeneralPositionGerm⟧ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4SM_GeneralPositionLocal · SBLocalization.surjective_reduced_toIntr_of_isGeneralPositionGerm⟧.

**Theorem 15.2.5, closing sentence** (narrower) ⟦Chapter15/P3W4SM_GeneralPositionLocal · SBLocalization.theorem_15_2_5_generalPosition_hyp⟧: the conclusion of Theorem 15.2.5 holds when its hypothesis (2), good position, is replaced by general position at $x$, and then general and good position hold at every support point of $U(x)$. *Proof.* General position at $x$ gives good position at $x$, so §XV.12's Theorem 15.2.5 applies at $x$. Part I's openness of general position on each branch, over the restricted M-polyfold $W|_O$, which is tame, gives general position at nearby points, and a shrinking of the natural representation keeps them inside. *Hypotheses*: tameness of $X$, the setting of Definition 15.3.5, which Part I's openness of general position needs; and the inherited tame germ data of $f$. Witness: the zero section of $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^0 \to \mathbb R^n$ with the zero multisection ⟦Chapter15/P3W4SM_GoodPositionWitness · SBLocalization.theorem_15_2_5_generalPosition_hyp_witness⟧.

**A witness for §XV.12** ⟦Chapter15/P3W4SM_GoodPositionWitness · SBLocalization.theorem_15_2_5_hyp_witness⟧: the hypotheses of Theorem 15.2.5 in good position are satisfiable together, on the same example, where good position holds at every point by §XV.19; the conclusion then holds there ⟦Chapter15/P3W4SM_GoodPositionWitness · SBLocalization.theorem_15_2_5_hyp_applies⟧. This replaces wave 2's remark that good position was not witnessed separately.

### XV.19 Remark 15.3.6 (2017: 15.6) after its first sentence: general position gives good position and a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid

**The chart step** ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GoodPosition · SBLocalization.isGeneralPositionGerm_subRestrict⟧: in a tame chart of $W$ centred at $x$ with domain in $O$, if the intrinsic operator $(f - s)'(x)$ is onto $W_x$ on $T^R_xX$, then $(f - s)|_O$ is in Part I's general position at $x$ (Definition 5.3.9). In the transported chart of $W|_O$ the operator is the derivative of the composite of the principal parts with the retraction (§XV.11); onto on $T^R_0O$ gives $\ker + T^R_0O = T_0O$, Part I's chart criterion. The chart reading of "onto on $T^R_xX$" ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GoodPosition · SBLocalization.exists_reduced_preimage⟧, and per branch ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GoodPosition · SBLocalization.isGeneralPositionGerm_branch⟧.

**Remark 15.3.6, second sentence** (narrower) ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GoodPosition · SBLocalization.remark_15_3_6_goodPosition_hyp⟧: if $(f, \Lambda)$ is in general position and $\Lambda(f(x)) > 0$, then $T(f, \Lambda)(x)$ is in good position, and every branch $(f - s_i)|_O$ through $f(x)$ is in Part I's general position at $x$, the reading of "even in general position" (Definition 15.3.5 is "a natural extension of Definition 5.3.9"). Good position from general position is Part I's Lemma 5.26. *Narrower* only by the inherited tame germ data, which provide the tame chart centred at $x$; *stronger* in that it holds at every point of the support, not only on $\partial X$.

**Remark 15.3.6, last sentence** (narrower). *Local branching* ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.remark_15_3_6_localBranching_hyp⟧: at every $y$ with $\Lambda(f(y)) > 0$, $z \mapsto \Lambda(f(z))$ has a local branching structure (Definition 9.1.2 (2)–(4)) with $M_j = \{z : f(z) = s_j(z)\}$ over the branches through $f(y)$, from Theorem 15.2.5 (§XV.12) at the point of good position just obtained. *Branched ep⁺-subgroupoid* ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.remark_15_3_6_isBranchedEpSubgroupoid_hyp⟧, given the paracompactness of the orbit space of the support, Definition 9.1.2 (1), which is new in 2021 and which the remark does not address; it is automatic when the support is compact, the situation of Theorem 15.3.7. $\Lambda \circ f$ is a functor ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.isFunctorial_comp⟧. Unlike Remark 15.2.3 (§XV.11), no $d_X = 0$ on the support is needed: boundary points are covered through good position. "Tame" (Definition 9.3.6) is proved in wave 5 (§XV.24).

### XV.20 Theorem 15.3.7 (2017: 15.4) and Remark 15.3.8: general position

**The statement** ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_statement⟧: for tame $X$ with sc-smooth bump functions (pointwise reading), $f$ an sc-Fredholm section functor with tame germ data and compact $|S_f|$, $(N, U)$ controlling compactness, and $h : X \to (0, 1]$ a continuous functor, there is a structurable $\Lambda$ with (1) $N(\Lambda) < h$, (2) domain support in $U$, (3) transversality, (4) general position. (3) and (4) are Definitions 15.2.1 and 15.3.5; $U$ is open and saturated, where the text says "a saturated subset"; there is no paracompactness, as Remark 15.3.8 says. It holds on $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^0 \to \mathbb R^n$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_statement_epSEP_zero⟧, where every pair is in general position ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.isInGeneralPosition_epSEP_zero⟧ and the zero multisection has all conclusions ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_of_isInGeneralPosition_zero⟧ ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm_zeroMultisection⟧.

**"In particular"** (narrower) ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_in_particular_hyp⟧: for $\Lambda$ with $N(\Lambda) \le 1$, domain support in $U$ and general position, $\Lambda \circ f$ is a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid with compact support. The support is closed, locally a finite union of the sets $\{f = s_i\}$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.isClosed_supp_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.pos_iff_exists_eq⟧, and its orbit set is closed, being saturated, since the orbit map is open (Proposition 7.1.8) ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.isClosed_orbitSupp_comp⟧. With $N(\Lambda) \le 1$ and domain support in $U \supseteq S_f$, the support lies in $\{x \in U : N(f(x)) \le 1\}$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.supp_comp_subset_controlled⟧, whose orbit set is compact because $(N, U)$ controls compactness ⟦Chapter15/P3W3G_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.isCompact_orbitSupp_comp⟧. Compactness gives the paracompactness of Definition 9.1.2 (1), and §XV.19 the local branching. Only (1) with $h \le 1$, (2) and (4) are used; (3) follows from (4) ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.isTransversal_of_isInGeneralPosition⟧. "Tame" is proved in wave 5 (§XV.24).

**Linear families** ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_ParamFamily · SBLocalization.IsLinearFamily⟧: families $t \mapsto \Lambda_t$, $t \in \mathbb R^\ell$, with local representations around every point by sections $\sum_j t_js_{ij}$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_ParamFamily · SBLocalization.paramSec⟧ with the same domain, sections $s_{ij}$ and weights for all $t$. (15.1) at $x$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_ParamFamily · SBLocalization.IsParamOntoAt⟧: for every branch $i$ and every operator $L$ of $T(f, \Lambda_0)(x)$, $(v, \tau) \mapsto Lv + \sum_j\tau_js_{ij}(x)$ is onto $W_x$ from $T^R_xX \times \mathbb R^\ell$; the $t$-derivative of $f - \sum_jt_js_{ij}$ is read as this map, the sign being immaterial. A family good on a saturated open $Q$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_ParamFamily · SBLocalization.GPFamily⟧ is linear, structurable, with $N(\Lambda_t) \le |t|_1h$ and domain support in $U$, and with (15.1) at the points of $S_f \cap Q$.

**The two hypotheses**, the two analytic steps of the text's proof, stated as propositions. *Local families* ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.HasLocalGPFamilies⟧, the "local constructions at $x \in S_f$", interior and boundary: every $x \in S_f$ lies in a saturated open $Q$ carrying a good family. *Parametric transversality* ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.HasParametricGeneralPosition⟧, "achieving global transversality": for every linear family with $N(\Lambda_t) \le |t|_1$, domain support in $U$ and (15.1) on $S_f$, there is $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $(f, \Lambda_t)$ is in general position for almost every $t$ with $\|t\| < \varepsilon$.

**Theorem 15.3.7** (narrower) ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_hyp⟧: given a good system, compact $|S_f|$, $(N, U)$ controlling compactness, $0 < h \le 1$, and the two hypotheses, there is a structurable $\Lambda$ with (1)–(4). *Proof*, the text's assembly. *Sums of families* ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_ParamFamily · SBLocalization.famAdd⟧: $\Lambda_t \oplus \Lambda'_{t'}$ over $\mathbb R^{\ell + \ell'}$ is linear, its local representations being the sections $\sum_jt_js_{ij} + \sum_kt'_ks'_{i'k}$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_ParamFamily · SBLocalization.isLocalRepOn_famAdd⟧ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_ParamFamily · SBLocalization.IsLinearFamily.famAdd⟧; it is structurable by Proposition 13.3.12; (15.1) for either summand gives it for the sum ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_ParamFamily · SBLocalization.IsParamOntoAt.famAdd_left⟧ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_ParamFamily · SBLocalization.IsParamOntoAt.famAdd_right⟧, at $t = 0$ the second summand being trivial; $N(\Lambda \oplus \Lambda') \le N(\Lambda) + N(\Lambda')$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_ParamFamily · SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm_multisectionAdd_le⟧ and the domain support of a sum lies in the union ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_ParamFamily · SBLocalization.domSupp_multisectionAdd_subset⟧, two facts the text uses silently. So good families on $Q$ and $Q'$ add to one on $Q \cup Q'$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_ParamFamily · SBLocalization.GPFamily.add⟧. *Finite cover*: finitely many $Q$ cover the compact $|S_f|$, by Proposition 7.1.8, giving one good family on a neighbourhood of $S_f$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.exists_gpFamily_of_compact⟧. *Choice of $t$*: parametric transversality gives a null set off which $(f, \Lambda_t)$ is in general position for $\|t\| < \varepsilon$; a ball has positive Lebesgue measure, so there is such a $t$ in the ball with $\|t\| < 1/(\ell + 1)$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.exists_norm_lt_of_ae⟧, hence $|t|_1 < 1$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.sum_abs_lt_one⟧ and $N(\Lambda_t) \le |t|_1h < h$ ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_ParamFamily · SBLocalization.pointwiseNorm_le_of_linear⟧. (3) follows from (4). *From the statement's hypotheses* ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_of_hyp⟧: if, under the hypotheses of the theorem, both analytic steps hold, then the statement of the theorem holds, given a good system. *The added hypotheses*: a good system, not derived from the text; it is necessary, since structurable multisections carry one, and holds for paracompact $|X|$ (Theorem 13.1.8); witness ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.nonempty_goodSystem_epSEP_zero⟧. The two analytic steps, not derived here; wave 5 proves the second and reduces the first to (15.1) at single points (§§XV.25–XV.26);". (7) §XV.21, Theorem 15.3.9: "The tame germ data are inherited; "tame" branched is not formalized." → "The tame germ data are inherited; step (a) is proved in wave 5 with tame strong bundle charts (§XV.27). witnesses ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.hasLocalGPFamilies_epSEP_zero⟧, for every $f$, $N$, $U$, $h$ with $\ell = 0$, and ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.hasParametricGeneralPosition_epSEP_zero⟧. Parametric transversality quantifies over all linear families; on $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^0$ it holds because every pair is in general position there, and jointly all three hypotheses give the statement there ⟦Chapter15/P3W4GP_GeneralPosition · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_7_statement_epSEP_zero_of_hyp⟧. The tame germ data, tameness, bump functions and the functor property of $h$ enter only through the two steps. **Remark 15.3.8** is prose: the theorem assumes no paracompactness of $|X|$; structurability still needs a good system.

### XV.21 Theorem 15.3.9 (2017: 15.5), Corollary 15.3.10 (1), (3) (2017: 15.1) and Remark 15.3.11 (2017: 15.7): the transversal extension

**The statement** ⟦Chapter15/P3W4TX_TransversalExtension · SBLocalization.theorem_15_3_9_statement⟧: $X$ tame with $|X|$ paracompact and sc-smooth partitions of unity, $f$ with tame germ data and compact $|S_f|$, $(N, U)$ controlling compactness, $\Lambda$ structurable over $\partial X$ with boundary domain support in $U$ and $N(\Lambda) \le 1$ on $\partial X$, a continuous functor $h : X \to (0, 1]$ with $N(\Lambda) < h$ on $\partial X$, and the face condition.
