A representative is $(\Theta, (X, \alpha))$ with $(X, \alpha) \in c$ and $\Theta$ a branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of $X$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedRep⟧; $(\Theta, (X, \alpha)) \sim (\Theta', (X', \alpha'))$ if a generalized isomorphism $f$ has $\alpha' \circ |f| = \alpha$ and $f^*\Theta' = \Theta$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedRep.Rel⟧, an equivalence relation ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedRep.Rel.trans⟧, reflexive because $1^*\Theta = \Theta$ for functorial $\Theta$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.pullTheta_id_of_isFunctorial⟧. A branched suborbifold is a class ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold⟧. **$\theta = |\Theta| \circ \alpha^{-1}$ is well defined** ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.toFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_1_wellDefined⟧: $\theta(\alpha(|x|)) = \Theta(x)$ for every representative and every $x$. The key step is $(f^*\Theta')(x) = \Theta'(y)$ whenever $|f|(|x|) = |y|$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.pullTheta_eq_of_orbitMap⟧, the text's $|f^*\Theta'| = |\Theta'| \circ |f|$.

**Definition 16.4.2.** A property holds for $\theta$ if it holds for some representative ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.HasRepProperty⟧; for a property stable under pull-backs by generalized isomorphisms, some representative has it iff all have ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.hasRepProperty_iff⟧. (1) closed, (2) compact, (3) of manifold-type, (4) of orbifold-type are such properties by Theorem 11.3.3 (3)–(5) (Part XI, §XI.7), so they hold for every representative iff for one ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_2_closed⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_2_compact⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_2_manifold⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_2_orbifold⟧, and so is the dimension, used in Theorem 16.4.6 ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_2_nDim⟧. (5) tame (narrower) ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.IsTame⟧: some representative is tame (Definition 9.3.6). The text says on p. 729 that tameness is preserved by $f_*$ and $f^*$; this is proved in wave 3 (§XVI.19).

**Proposition 16.4.3** (narrower). *The set* ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_supp⟧: $\operatorname{supp}\theta = \alpha(|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|)$ for every representative, and $\alpha$ restricts to a homeomorphism $|\operatorname{supp}\Theta| \cong \operatorname{supp}\theta$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_homeomorph⟧. *Manifold-type* ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_manifold⟧: with Proposition 9.1.9 (1), $|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|$ carries an M-polyfold structure for which $\operatorname{supp}\Theta \to |\operatorname{supp}\Theta|$ is a local sc-diffeomorphism. *Orbifold-type* ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_orbifold⟧: with Proposition 9.1.9 (2), $|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|$ is the orbit space of the ep-groupoid on $\operatorname{supp}\Theta$. This is done for every representative; that two representatives induce sc-diffeomorphic structures, the word "natural" of the text, is not formalized (§XVI.6).

### XVI.13 Definitions 16.4.4 and 16.4.5 (2017: Definitions 16.31, 16.34), and the integrals of p. 732

**Definition 16.4.4** (restated). A representative is $((\Theta, \hat T_\Theta), (X, \alpha))$ with $(\Theta, \hat T_\Theta)$ an oriented branched ep⁺-subgroupoid of $X$ (Chapter 11) and $\hat T_\Theta$ zero off $X_\infty$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep⟧; related by $f^*(\Theta', \hat T_{\Theta'}) = (\Theta, \hat T_\Theta)$ and $\alpha' \circ |f| = \alpha$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.Rel⟧. An oriented branched suborbifold is a class ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold⟧, with an underlying branched suborbifold ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.toBranched⟧. *Reading.* The text's $\hat T_\Theta$ lives over $X_\infty$, and $f^*$ only reads it there; the formalization makes it $0$ elsewhere, which reflexivity needs: $1^*\hat T = \hat T$ holds for such $\hat T$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.pullSection_id_of_mem⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.pull_id_of_mem⟧. Every pull-back of Chapter 11 has this property, so it is a normalization, not an added hypothesis.

**Definition 16.4.5** ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.definition_16_4_5_wellDefined⟧: if two representatives are related through $f$, then $f^*\partial\Theta' = \partial\Theta$ and $f^*\hat T_{\partial\Theta'} = \hat T_{\partial\Theta}$, by Theorem 11.3.9 ⟦Chapter11/BoundaryOrientationEquiv · theorem_11_3_9_pull_boundaryOrientation⟧ (Part XI, §XI.8); so $\partial\hat\theta = [\partial(\Theta, \hat T_\Theta), (X, \alpha)]$ does not depend on the representative. The boundary function $\partial\theta = |\partial\Theta| \circ \alpha^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryFun⟧ does not either ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryFun_eq_of_rel⟧. *Readings.* The compatibility holds without tameness, which the text assumes. $\partial(\Theta, \hat T_\Theta)$ is formalized componentwise, as in Chapter 11.

**The integrals (p. 732).** On a representative that is compact and tame of dimension $n$ in the sense of Chapter 9 (oriented tame structures describing $\hat T_\Theta$ at every point of $\operatorname{supp}\Theta$) ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.IsTameOriented⟧: $\int_{\hat\theta}\tau = \mu^{\hat\Theta}_\omega(|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|)$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.integral⟧ and $\oint_{\hat\theta}\tau$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.integralEff⟧, $\omega$ the representative of $\tau$ on $(X, \alpha)$; for the effective integral (ZHOU) gives the local uniqueness condition (LUC) by Proposition 7.4.10. The boundary integrals ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryIntegral⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryIntegralEff⟧ are the measures of Theorems 9.5.15 and 9.5.16 (Part IX, §IX.34), with separate forms for dimension $1$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryIntegralDim1⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryIntegralEffDim1⟧. **"The definition does not depend on the choice of the representatives"** (narrower), among tame compact representatives: $\int$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.integral_eq_of_rel⟧ and $\oint$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.integralEff_eq_of_rel⟧. *Proof.* The representative of $\tau$ on the first structure is $f^*$ of that on the second, and the tame integrals are invariant under pull-back, Theorems 11.4.1 and 11.4.2 (Part XI, §XI.9) ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.tameBranchedIntegral_pull⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.tameBranchedIntegralEff_pull⟧. For the boundary integrals the independence is obtained from Stokes' theorem, with sc-smooth partitions of unity ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryIntegral_eq_of_rel⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryIntegralEff_eq_of_rel⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.boundaryIntegralDim1_eq_of_rel⟧: both sides equal the integral of $d\tau$. The integrals are defined on tame representatives because tameness is not known to be invariant (§XVI.6).

### XVI.14 Theorem 16.4.6 (2017: Theorem 16.5): Stokes' theorem on polyfolds, with sc-smooth partitions of unity

**Theorem 16.4.6** (with sc-smooth partitions of unity) ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.theorem_16_4_6_hyp⟧: let $(Z, c)$ admit sc-smooth partitions of unity (Definition 16.1.5), $\hat\theta = [(\Theta, \hat T_\Theta), (X, \alpha)]$ oriented, compact and tame of dimension $n = m + 1 \ge 2$, and $\tau \in \Omega^m_{sc}(Z, c)$. Then $\int_{\hat\theta} d\tau = \int_{\partial\hat\theta}\tau$. The effective form ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.theorem_16_4_6_eff_hyp⟧: $\oint_{\hat\theta} d\tau = \oint_{\partial\hat\theta}\tau$; dimension $1$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.theorem_16_4_6_dim1_hyp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.theorem_16_4_6_eff_dim1_hyp⟧; both identities together ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.theorem_16_4_6_both_hyp⟧.

*Proof.* *Step 1, to the representative.* The representative of $d\tau$ on $(X, \alpha)$ is $d$ of the representative $\omega$ of $\tau$ ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.toStructure_d⟧ (§XVI.11), so both sides are integrals over $\Theta$ on $X$: $\mu^{\hat\Theta}_{d\omega}(|\operatorname{supp}\Theta|)$ and the boundary measure of $\omega$. *Step 2, the partitions of unity.* By Definition 16.1.5 (2) ⟦Chapter16/P3Z_PolyfoldPartitions · PolyfoldClass.definition_16_1_5_two⟧ (§XVI.3), $X$ admits sc-smooth partitions of unity. *Step 3, Stokes on $X$.* Theorem 9.5.17 ⟦Chapter9/GapP3_K1_Theorems · theorem_9_5_17⟧, and for the effective form Theorem 9.5.18 ⟦Chapter9/GapP3_K1_Theorems · theorem_9_5_18⟧ with (LUC) from (ZHOU) (Part IX, §IX.35), give the identity on $X$. By §XVI.13 the result does not depend on the representative.

*The added hypothesis.* Theorem 16.4.6 does not state that $(Z, c)$ admits sc-smooth partitions of unity, but its proof reduces to Theorem 9.5.17, which assumes them for $X$; the polyfold theorem is proved with the same hypothesis, as Definition 16.1.5. Witness ⟦Chapter16/P3H_BranchedSuborbifold · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.theorem_16_4_6_hyp_witness⟧: the polyfold $\mathbb R$ of §XVI.1 admits sc-smooth partitions of unity ⟦Chapter16/P3Z_PolyfoldExamples · PolyfoldStructure.z3Polyfold_admitsScPartitionsOfUnity⟧. Without it the theorem is a new gap (§XVI.6). *Reading.* "Tame" is Chapter 9's, on the representative used (§XVI.13).

### XVI.15 Witnesses and the hypotheses of wave 2

**Hypotheses taken.** *Sc-smooth partitions of unity* in Theorem 16.4.6 and in the independence of the boundary integrals (§§XVI.13–XVI.14), witnessed by the polyfold $\mathbb R$ of §XVI.1 (`theorem_16_4_6_hyp_witness`). *An effective target* in `lemma_16_2_1_of_isEffective`, witnessed by the point ep-groupoid; without it Lemma 16.2.1 does not hold as we read it (§XVI.9), and the orbit form needs no added hypothesis. *A tame compact representative* for the integrals: this is the text's "tame, compact", read on a representative because tameness is not known to be invariant. The normalization $\hat T_\Theta = 0$ off $X_\infty$ is not a hypothesis (§XVI.13).

**Witnesses of the definitions.** The tangent polyfold: $T$ of the polyfold $\mathbb R$ of §XVI.1 (§XVI.10). Forms: $\Omega^k_{sc}(Z, c)$ is a vector space isomorphic to $\Omega^k_{ep,\infty}(X)$ for every structure in $c$ (§XVI.11). Branched and oriented suborbifolds: a class exists as soon as a representative does; no separate example was built in wave 2, and the hemisphere of Part IX (§IX.35) is the nearest ep-level example of a compact tame oriented one.

### XVI.16 Definitions 16.1.6–16.1.11 (2017: 16.5–16.8) and Remark 16.1.9 (2017: 16.2): maps of polyfolds

**The category PS of polyfold structures** (p. 709): a morphism $(X, \alpha) \to (Y, \beta)$ is a pair $(f, \mathfrak f)$ of a continuous map $f$ and a generalized map $\mathfrak f$ (a morphism of Chapter 10's localization) with $f \circ \alpha = \beta \circ |\mathfrak f|$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom⟧; then $f = \beta \circ |\mathfrak f| \circ \alpha^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.f_eq⟧ is continuous ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.continuous_f⟧. Identities and composition are componentwise ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.id⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.comp_assoc⟧, and PS is a category ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSCat⟧. Its isomorphisms over the identity of $Z$ are the pairs $(h, \mathrm{Id}_Z)$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.IsIdIso⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.IsIdIso.inv⟧; one exists between any two equivalent structures ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.exists_isIdIso⟧.

**Definition 16.1.6** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.Equiv⟧: $(f, \mathfrak f) \sim (f', \mathfrak f')$ if $(f', \mathfrak f') \circ (h, \mathrm{Id}_Z) = (k, \mathrm{Id}_W) \circ (f, \mathfrak f)$ for isomorphisms $(h, \mathrm{Id}_Z)$, $(k, \mathrm{Id}_W)$, the square in PS. Then $f = f'$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.Equiv.f_eq⟧; it is an equivalence relation ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.Equiv.refl⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.Equiv.symm⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.Equiv.trans⟧ on representatives between structures of $c$ and $d$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.MapRep⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.MapRep.setoid⟧, and composing with isomorphisms over the identity stays in the class ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.equiv_comp_left⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.equiv_comp_right⟧.

**Definition 16.1.8 and Remark 16.1.9** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap⟧: an sc-smooth map $(Z, c) \to (W, d)$ is a class $[(f, \mathfrak f)]$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.mk⟧. Every class has a representative between any two given structures of $c$ and $d$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.exists_rep⟧. Its continuous map ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.toFun⟧ is $\beta \circ |\mathfrak f| \circ \alpha^{-1}$ for every representative ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.remark_16_1_9⟧, Remark 16.1.9. The identity is $[([1_X], \mathrm{Id}_Z)]$ for every $(X, \alpha) \in c$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.id⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.id_eq⟧.

**Definition 16.1.10.** The text defines $\hat g \circ \hat f = [(g \circ f, \mathfrak g \circ \mathfrak f)]$ for representatives with a common middle structure, and says that this does not depend on the choices. The claim in Lean ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.Definition_16_1_10⟧: equivalent pairs have equivalent composites.

**The claim of Definition 16.1.10 does not hold as we read it** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.not_definition_16_1_10⟧. *The example.* $Z = W = V = \mathbb R$; $(X, \alpha) = (U, \gamma)$ the polyfold structure $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$ with the trivial action (§XVI.1); $(Y, \beta)$ the structure $(\mathbb Z/3)^2 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$, again with the trivial action ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.k2Structure⟧, which satisfies (ZHOU) ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.isZhou_k2⟧ and has $|Y| \cong \mathbb R$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.k2OrbitHomeomorph⟧. All continuous maps are the identity. Let $\iota(g) = (g, 1)$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.ι⟧, $\sigma$ the swap of the two factors ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.σ⟧, an automorphism over the identity with $\sigma \circ \sigma = 1$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.σ_σ⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.kσ_isIdIso⟧, and $\mathrm{pr}_1$ the first projection ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.pr₁⟧. Then $\hat f$ has the equivalent representatives $(\mathrm{Id}, [\iota])$ and $(\mathrm{Id}, [\sigma \circ \iota])$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.a_equiv⟧, with $k = [\sigma]$. Composed with $(\mathrm{Id}, [\mathrm{pr}_1])$ they give $[1_X]$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.ι_pr₁⟧ and $[T]$ with $T(g) = 1$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.ι_σ_pr₁⟧. These are not equivalent ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.not_equiv_comp⟧: $[T]$ would then be a generalized isomorphism, and $T$ is not an equivalence, not being faithful ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.not_isEquivalence_T⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.not_isIso_T⟧. On classes, no composition agrees with the representatives ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.not_exists_comp⟧. The hypotheses are exactly the printed ones: polyfold structures and morphisms of PS. The mechanism is that of §XVI.2: $k$ is not determined by $\mathrm{Id}_W$. The middle structure is not effective ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_CompositionCounterexample · CompositionCounterexample.not_isEffective_k2⟧.

**The form that holds: an effective middle structure** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PSHom.Equiv.comp_of_isEffective⟧. Then Theorem 10.3.19 holds and $k$ is unique, and equivalent pairs have equivalent composites ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.MapRep.comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.MapRep.comp_equiv⟧. Effectiveness of a polyfold ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.IsEffective⟧ holds for one structure iff for all ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.isEffective_iff⟧, being invariant under equivalences ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · EpFunctor.IsEquivalence.isEffective_iff⟧ and generalized isomorphisms ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · EPLoc.isEffective_iff_of_isGeneralizedIso⟧ (Remark 10.1.12). For effective $d$ the composite of classes is defined ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.comp_mk⟧, with identities ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.id_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.comp_id⟧ and associativity ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.comp_assoc⟧.

**Definition 16.1.11** (narrower) ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · EffPolyfold⟧: the category of effective polyfolds and sc-smooth maps, with $1_{(Z,c)} = [([1_X], \mathrm{Id}_Z)]$. *Narrower* because, as we read Definition 16.1.10, the composition is not defined on all polyfolds. Witness: the point polyfold ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_PolyfoldMaps · EffPolyfold.point⟧.

### XVI.17 Theorem 16.2.4 (2017: 16.1) and Theorem 16.2.6 (2017: 16.2), the pull-back: functoriality

**The tangent functor on PS** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor · PSCat.tangentFunctor⟧: $(X, \alpha) \mapsto (TX, T\alpha)$ and $(f, \mathfrak f) \mapsto (|T\mathfrak f|, T\mathfrak f)$, a functor from PS to PS one universe up; a generalized map alone determines a morphism of PS ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor · PSHom.ofGen'⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor · PSHom.ofGen'_comp⟧, and $T(X, \alpha)$ is the structure of Definition 16.2.3 ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor · PolyfoldStructure.tangentSelf⟧, isomorphisms over the identity going to isomorphisms over the identity ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.tangent_isIdIso⟧.

**$T$ on sc-smooth maps** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.tangent⟧: $T\hat f = [(Tf, T\mathfrak f)]$, well defined because equivalent representatives have equivalent tangents ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.MapRep.tangent⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.MapRep.tangent_equiv⟧. $Tf$ is determined by $Tf \circ T\alpha = T\beta \circ |T\mathfrak f|$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.tangent_toFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.tangent_mk⟧; $T1 = 1$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.tangent_id⟧; the tangent of a composite of representatives is the composite of the tangents ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.tangent_mk_comp⟧.

**Theorem 16.2.4** (narrower) ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.theorem_16_2_4⟧: the facts above together; and $T(\hat g \circ \hat f) = T\hat g \circ T\hat f$ when the middle polyfold $d$ and its tangent are effective ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_TangentFunctor · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.tangent_comp⟧. *Narrower* because there is no category of all polyfolds (§XVI.16), so functoriality on classes is stated where composition is defined. *The hypothesis* that $Td$ is effective follows in wave 5 from the effectiveness of $d$, and the theorem becomes a functor on effective polyfolds (§XVI.26).

**Theorem 16.2.6, the pull-back** (as printed) ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.theorem_16_2_6_pullback⟧: an sc-smooth map pulls back forms, $\hat f^*[(\omega', (Y, \beta))] = [(\mathfrak f^*\omega', (X, \alpha))]$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.pullback⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.pullback_mk⟧, linearly ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.MapRep.pullback⟧ and with $d \circ \hat f^* = \hat f^* \circ d$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.d_comp_pullback⟧. It is well defined on every class, with no effectiveness ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.MapRep.pullback_eq_of_equiv⟧. $1^* = 1$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.pullback_id⟧; $(\hat g \circ \hat f)^* = \hat f^* \circ \hat g^*$ on representatives ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.pullback_mk_comp⟧, and on classes for an effective middle polyfold, where the composite is defined ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_FormsPullback · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.pullback_comp⟧. With §XVI.11 this is Theorem 16.2.6 in full.

### XVI.18 The raised polyfolds $(Z, c)^i$ (p. 715) and the tangent projection $\tau_Z$ (p. 717)

**Raising generalized maps.** The index raise $X \mapsto X^1$ of Chapter 7 is functorial ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · EpFunctor.liftOne_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · EpFunctor.liftOne_id⟧, passes to diagrams and their refinements ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.Diagram.liftOne⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.Diagram.Equiv.liftOne⟧, and so to generalized maps ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.liftOneHom⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.liftOneHom_id⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.liftOneHom_comp⟧, keeping generalized isomorphisms ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.isGeneralizedIso_liftOneHom⟧ and with $|\mathfrak f^1| = |\mathfrak f|$ on $|X^1| \subseteq |X|$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitIncl_orbitMap_liftOneHom⟧. $X^1$ has a paracompact orbit space and (ZHOU) ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldStructure.liftOne_paracompact⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldStructure.liftOne_isZhou⟧.

**The raised polyfold** (restated) ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raise⟧: $(Z, c)^1$ is the space $|X_0^1|$ for a structure $(X_0, \alpha_0)$ of $c$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.RaisedSpace⟧, with the structures $(X^1, \alpha^1)$ for $(X, \alpha) \in c$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseStructure⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseMap⟧, all equivalent ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseStructure_equiv⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raise_eq⟧; $\alpha^1$ is a homeomorphism ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.isHomeomorph_raiseMap⟧. The inclusion into $Z$ is injective and continuous ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseIncl⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseIncl_injective⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.continuous_raiseIncl⟧, with image $Z_1 = \beta(|X|_1)$ for every $(X, \beta) \in c$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.range_raiseIncl⟧. $(Z, c)^i$ is the $i$-fold raise ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseN⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseN_succ⟧. *Restated:* $(Z, c)^1$ is a space with an injection into $Z$, not the subspace $Z_1$: its topology is that of $|X^1|$. The index $mI$ is not introduced; $Z_i = \alpha(|X_i|)$.

**The tangent projection** (restated) ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.tangentProj⟧: $\tau_Z : T(Z, c) \to (Z, c)^1$, continuous ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.continuous_tangentProj⟧, with $\tau_Z \circ T\alpha = \alpha^1 \circ |\tau_X|$ for every $(X, \alpha) \in c$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.tangentProj_tangentMap⟧; composed with the inclusion it is the text's square into $Z$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · PolyfoldClass.raiseIncl_tangentProj_tangentMap⟧. It rests on the naturality of $\tau$ for generalized maps ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_RaisedPolyfold · EPLocalization.EPLoc.orbitMap_tangentProj_tangentHom⟧.

### XVI.19 Tameness of branched suborbifolds (p. 729, Definition 16.4.2 (5)), the integrals on classes, and Proposition 16.4.3

**Tameness moves along equivalences.** The tame branching structures of Definition 9.3.6 restrict to smaller natural representations ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · EpGroupoid.TameBranchingStructure.restrictRep⟧ and move along sc-diffeomorphisms ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · EpGroupoid.TameBranchingStructure.move⟧. So for an equivalence $\Phi$, $\Theta'$ is tame iff $\Phi^*\Theta'$ is ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · EpFunctor.isTameBranched_pullbackTheta⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · EpFunctor.isTameBranched_pullbackTheta_iff⟧, and push-forwards of tame ones are tame ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · EpFunctor.isTameBranched_pushforwardTheta⟧, along the transport charts of Theorem 11.4.1; the same holds along generalized isomorphisms ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · EPLocalization.EPLoc.isTameBranched_pullTheta⟧. **Definition 16.4.2 (5)** (as printed) ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.definition_16_4_2_tame⟧: $\theta$ is tame iff every representative is; gap G.154 is closed. *Oriented:* related oriented representatives are tame together ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.Rel.isTameOriented⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedRep.Rel.isTameOriented_iff⟧, so tameness of an oriented class ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.IsTameOriented⟧ holds in every representative ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.isTameOriented_iff⟧.

**The integrals of p. 732 on classes** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.integral⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.integralEff⟧: for a tame compact oriented class, $\int_{\hat\theta}\omega$ and $\oint_{\hat\theta}\omega$ equal the integrals on every representative ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.integral_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.integralEff_eq⟧; compactness is that of any representative ⟦Chapter16/P3W3Y_BranchedTame · PolyfoldClass.OrientedSuborbifold.isCompactBranched_of_mk⟧. The boundary integrals are not wrapped on classes (§XVI.6); Theorem 16.4.6 keeps its added partitions of unity (§XVI.14).

**Proposition 16.4.3, the comparison of two representatives** (partial). For two representatives $\Theta$, $\Theta'$ of $\theta$, the homeomorphism $|\operatorname{supp}\Theta| \to |\operatorname{supp}\Theta'|$ over $\operatorname{supp}\theta$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.suppTransition⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.β_suppTransition⟧ satisfies the cocycle identities ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.suppTransition_self⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.suppTransition_trans⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.suppTransition_symm⟧. The comparison is stated ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_naturality_statement⟧: for structures induced by Proposition 9.1.9 (1) ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.IsInducedSuppStructure⟧, suitably chosen, the transition is an sc-diffeomorphism. It is proved for one representative ⟦Chapter16/P3W4SM_SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_naturality_self⟧, and in general, for any induced structures, in wave 5 (§XVI.28).

### XVI.20 Definitions 16.3.1–16.3.8 (2017: 16.16–16.22) and Lemma 16.3.2: strong polyfold bundles

**Definition 16.3.1** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure⟧: a strong polyfold bundle structure for $p : Y \to Z$ is a strong bundle $(P : W \to X, \mu)$ over an ep-groupoid with (ZHOU), paracompact $|X|$ and the local regularity property (Definition 8.4.2), with homeomorphisms $\Gamma : |W| \to Y$ and $\gamma : |X| \to Z$, $p \circ \Gamma = \gamma \circ |P|$. Then $p = \gamma \circ |P| \circ \Gamma^{-1}$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.p_eq⟧ is continuous and surjective ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.continuous_p⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.surjective_p⟧, which the text assumes. **Lemma 16.3.2** (new in 2021) ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.lemma_16_3_2⟧: $Y$ and $Z$ are metrizable: $|X|$ by Theorem 7.3.1, and $|W|$ through the paracompactness of Proposition 8.4.1.

**Definition 16.3.3** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Equiv⟧: two structures are equivalent if a generalized strong bundle isomorphism $F$ covering $f$ has $\gamma' \circ |f| = \gamma$ and $\Gamma' \circ |F| = \Gamma$. It is an equivalence relation ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Equiv.refl⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Equiv.symm⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Equiv.trans⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.setoid⟧, by the strong bundle form of Proposition 10.3.11: orbit maps of generalized strong bundle maps compose ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.orbitMap_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · SBLocalization.SEPLoc.orbitMap_comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · SBLocalization.SEPLoc.orbitMap_inv_comp⟧. The condition on $\gamma$ follows from the one on $\Gamma$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Γ_base⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.equiv_iff_exists_Γ⟧.

**The uniqueness after Definition 16.3.3.** The text says that for equivalent structures $f$ and $F$ are uniquely determined, by $|f| = \gamma'^{-1} \circ \gamma$, (ZHOU), Theorem 10.3.19 and Proposition 10.4.7. The claim in Lean ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_UniquenessCheck · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Uniqueness_16_3_3⟧: any two generalized strong bundle isomorphisms satisfying both conditions agree, on the bases and on the bundles.

**The uniqueness after Definition 16.3.3 does not hold as we read it** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_UniquenessCheck · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.not_uniqueness_16_3_3⟧. *The example* ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_UniquenessCheck · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.z3Structure⟧: $\mathbb R \times \mathbb R^k \to \mathbb R$ over $\mathbb Z/3 \times \mathbb R \rightrightarrows \mathbb R$, with the trivial actions and $\Gamma = \gamma = \mathrm{id}$; it satisfies (ZHOU), has a paracompact orbit space and the local regularity property ⟦Chapter10/LocalizationLRCounterexample · LocalizationLRCounterexample.isLR_z3EpBundle⟧. The generalized strong bundle isomorphisms $[1_W]$ and $[W \xleftarrow{1} W \xrightarrow{\mathrm{Inv}} W]$ of Remark 10.5.5 induce the identity on both orbit spaces ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_UniquenessCheck · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.z3_orbitMap_id⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_UniquenessCheck · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.z3_baseOrbitMap_id⟧, so both satisfy the conditions, and they differ already on the bases ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_UniquenessCheck · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.uniqueness_16_3_3_counterexample⟧. The base is not effective ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_UniquenessCheck · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.not_isEffective_z3Structure⟧. This is the bundle form of §XVI.2, and the mechanism of Definition 16.1.10 (§XVI.16). **The form that holds** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_UniquenessCheck · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.uniqueness_16_3_3_of_isEffective⟧: for an effective target base, $f$ is unique by Theorem 10.3.19 for an effective target, and $F$ by Theorem 10.5.7 for an effective base. Nothing later in §16.3 uses the uniqueness.

**The induced polyfold** (p. 723) ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.toPolyfoldStructure⟧: the base of a structure is a polyfold structure on $Z$, equivalent structures giving equivalent ones ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.toPolyfoldStructure_equiv⟧. **Definition 16.3.4** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundle⟧: a strong polyfold bundle is $p$ with an equivalence class $\bar c$ of structures, a Lean quotient, with its polyfold $(Z, c)$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundle.polyfold⟧. **Definition 16.3.5** (restated) ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsTame⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsWeaklyFaceStructured⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsFaceStructured⟧: (1) tame, if $(Z, c)$ is (Definition 16.1.20), equivalently every representative's base ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · StrongPolyfoldBundle.isTame_iff⟧; (2), (3) through representatives ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · PolyfoldClass.IsWeaklyFaceStructured⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · PolyfoldClass.IsFaceStructured⟧, since Definition 16.1.21 is not formalized; face structure holds for one representative iff for all (Remark 11.1.7) ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_StrongPolyfoldBundle · PolyfoldClass.isFaceStructured_iff⟧, and for weak face structure "some representative" is the reading.

**Definition 16.3.6** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS⟧: the category $\mathcal{SPBS}$. A morphism ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.Hom⟧ is $(A, a, \mathfrak A, \mathfrak a)$ with continuous $A$, $a$, a generalized strong bundle map $\mathfrak A$ covering $\mathfrak a$, $\Gamma' \circ |\mathfrak A| = A \circ \Gamma$ and $\gamma' \circ |\mathfrak a| = a \circ \gamma$; $p' \circ A = a \circ p$ follows ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.Hom.p_comm⟧. Composition is componentwise ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.Hom.comp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.category⟧, and a morphism is invertible in the text's sense iff it is an isomorphism of the category ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.Hom.IsInvertible⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.isIso_iff_isInvertible⟧. *The text before Definition 16.3.7* ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.exists_isInvertible_iff_equiv⟧: $\bar c$ consists of the structures related by an invertible $(\mathfrak A, \mathrm{Id}_Y)$, and $A = \mathrm{id}$ forces $a = \mathrm{id}$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.Hom.f_eq_id⟧.

**Definition 16.3.7** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.MorEquiv⟧: $(\mathfrak A_0, A_0) \sim (\mathfrak A_1, A_1)$ if $(\mathfrak A_1, A_1) \circ (\mathfrak H, \mathrm{Id}_Y) = (\mathfrak H', \mathrm{Id}_{Y'}) \circ (\mathfrak A_0, A_0)$ for isomorphisms of the special form; then $A_1 = A_0$ and $a_1 = a_0$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.MorEquiv.F_eq⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.MorEquiv.f_eq⟧, and it is an equivalence relation ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.MorEquiv.trans⟧. **Definition 16.3.8** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.StrongPolyfoldBundleMap⟧: an sc-smooth strong polyfold bundle map is a class of morphisms between structures of $\bar c$ and $\bar c'$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.MorRep⟧, with its continuous maps ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.StrongPolyfoldBundleMap.toFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_BundleCategory · SPBS.StrongPolyfoldBundleMap.p_comm⟧. As for polyfolds, the composition of such maps on classes would meet the question of §XVI.16; the text does not define it, and it is not formalized.

### XVI.21 Definition 16.3.9 (2017: 16.23) to Theorem 16.3.17 (2017: 16.4): auxiliary norms

**Definition 16.3.9** (restated) ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsAuxNorm⟧: $n$ is an auxiliary norm if, for every structure of $\bar c$, $N(e) = n(\Gamma(|e|))$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.normOf⟧ is an auxiliary norm of $W$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.IsAuxNormFor⟧; one structure suffices ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.definition_16_3_9⟧, by Proposition 11.5.1 ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.isAuxNormFor_of_equiv⟧. (16.7), $N = [D]^*N'$, is the pull-back of norms ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.normOf_pull⟧, and $Y_{0,1} = \Gamma(|W_{0,1}|)$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Y01⟧ does not depend on the structure ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.Y01_eq_of_equiv⟧. *Restated:* $n$ is a function on $Y$ whose values on $Y_{0,1}$ matter; its continuity, in the topology of $|W[1]|$ carried by $\Gamma$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.continuous_normOrbit⟧, and its nonnegativity ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsAuxNorm.nonneg⟧ follow from those of $N$. An invariant $N$ descends to $Y$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.descend⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.isAuxNorm_descend⟧.

**Proposition 16.3.10** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.proposition_16_3_10⟧: an auxiliary norm exists: Theorem 12.2.2 in a representative, descended. The paracompactness it uses is part of Definition 16.3.1. **Remark 16.3.11** is prose.

**Definitions 16.3.12–16.3.14** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.HasReflexiveFibers⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsReflexiveAuxNorm⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.MixedTendsto⟧: reflexive $1$-fibres, reflexive auxiliary norms (Definition 12.2.10) and mixed convergence (Definition 12.2.8), each in some model of $\bar c$, as printed; mixed convergence in a given model ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.MixedTendstoIn⟧. That the model does not matter, the parenthetical of Definition 16.3.12, is proved in wave 5 for the reflexive fibres in the pull direction (§XVI.27); the rest is gap G.166 (§XVI.6).

**Theorem 16.3.15** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_3_15_one⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_3_15_two⟧: with reflexive $1$-fibres, (1) a reflexive auxiliary norm exists and (2) every auxiliary norm $n$ has reflexive $n_1 \le n \le n_2$ on $Y_{0,1}$, from Theorem 12.2.11 in the reflexive representative.

**Proposition 16.3.16 (1)** (stronger) ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.proposition_16_3_16_one⟧: $p(y_k) \to z$ and $n(y_k) \to 0$ imply $y_k \to 0_z$ in $|W[1]|$ of a representative, for every auxiliary norm; reflexivity is not used. It is the compactness property of Theorem 12.2.2. **Proposition 16.3.16 (2)** (narrower) ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.proposition_16_3_16_two_of_mem⟧: $n(y) \le \liminf n(y_k)$ for $y_k$ mixed convergent to $y$, the mixed convergence read in the model in which $n$ is represented by a reflexive norm. The text's form, with two models, needs the invariance gap.

**Theorem 16.3.17 (1)** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_3_17_one⟧: over a tame polyfold, an auxiliary norm of $Y_{0,1}|\partial Z$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsAuxNormBoundary⟧, read as in Definition 16.3.9 over $\partial X$ in all models, extends to an auxiliary norm: Theorem 12.2.7 in one structure. $p(\Gamma|e|) \in \partial Z$ iff $P(e) \in \partial X$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.mem_boundary_iff⟧. **Theorem 16.3.17 (2)** (narrower) ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_3_17_two_hyp⟧: if $n$ is reflexive, read as reflexive fibres and a reflexive norm over $\partial X$ in one model, the extension can be taken reflexive, from Theorem 12.2.13 with its reflexive local step as a hypothesis. *The hypothesis* is not derived from the text; witness ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldAuxNorm · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_3_17_two_hyp_witness⟧, on every bundle with reflexive $1$-fibres. For tame bases Part XII proves it ⟦Chapter12/P3W3K_ReflexiveLocalExtension · EpStrongBundle.hasReflexiveLocalExtensions_of_isTame⟧ (§XII.22), so the unconditional form is a one-line corollary, not stated. Tameness is not otherwise used.

### XVI.22 Definitions 16.3.18, 16.3.19 (2017: 16.27, 16.28): sections, and the zero of a fibre

**The relation before Definition 16.3.18** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.Rel⟧: a representative is $(f, \Gamma, W, F)$, $f$ a continuous section of $p$ and $F$ an sc-smooth section functor with $\Gamma \circ |F| = f \circ \gamma$; two are related if $f = f'$ and a generalized strong bundle isomorphism $\mathfrak A$ has $\Gamma' \circ |\mathfrak A| = \Gamma$ and $\mathfrak A_*F = F'$. The text's "this defines an equivalence relation" is proved ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.Rel.trans⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.setoid⟧. The condition $\mathfrak A_*F = F'$ follows from the others ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.pushforward_eq_of_Γ⟧, so two representatives are related iff $f = f'$ and their structures are equivalent ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.rel_iff⟧.

**Definition 16.3.18** ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection⟧: an sc-smooth section is a class, with its section $f$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.toFun⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.p_toFun⟧, which determines it ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.ext_toFun⟧. **Definition 16.3.19** (restated) ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.IsScPlus⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusSection⟧: an sc⁺-section is an sc-smooth section with an sc⁺ functor in one, equivalently every, representative ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_PolyfoldSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.isScPlus_iff⟧ (Theorem 10.5.4); the continuity of $f$ into $Y_{0,1}$ is that of $F$ into $W_{0,1}$.

**The zero of a fibre** (p. 728) ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.zeroAt⟧: $0_z = \Gamma(|0_x|)$ for any $x$ with $\gamma(|x|) = z$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.zeroAt_eq⟧, with $p(0_z) = z$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.p_zeroAt⟧. It does not depend on the structure ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundleStructure.zeroAt_eq_of_equiv⟧, because generalized strong bundle maps send orbits of zeros to orbits of zeros ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_ZeroSection · SBLocalization.GenSBMap.orbitMap_π_fiberZero⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_ZeroSection · SBLocalization.π_eq_fiberZero_iff⟧. An auxiliary norm extended by $0$ off $Y_{0,1}$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.normY⟧ has $n(\Gamma|w|) = N(w)$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_ZeroSection · StrongPolyfoldBundle.normY_Γ⟧. The zero section as an element of Definition 16.3.18 is a new gap (§XVI.6).

### XVI.23 §16.5 (2017: Definitions 16.35–16.39, Remark 16.5, Theorem 16.6): sc⁺-multisections

**Definition 16.5.1** ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection⟧: an sc⁺-multisection $\lambda : Y \to \mathbb Q^+$ is a class of $(\lambda, \Gamma, W, \Lambda)$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.MultisectionRep⟧, $\Lambda$ an sc⁺-multisection functor with $\lambda(\Gamma|w|) = \Lambda(w)$; two are related if $\lambda = \lambda'$ and $\Lambda = \bar f^*\Lambda'$ for a generalized strong bundle isomorphism $\bar f$ with $\Gamma' \circ |\bar f| = \Gamma$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.MultisectionRep.Rel⟧. *The relation does not depend on $\bar f$*, which by §XVI.20 need not be unique: for every such $\bar f$, $\bar f^*\Lambda'(w) = \lambda(\Gamma|w|)$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.pullMult_eq_of_Γ⟧, so two representatives are related iff their functions agree ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.MultisectionRep.rel_iff⟧, and it is an equivalence relation ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.MultisectionRep.setoid⟧. On the $\mathbb Z/3$ example of §XVI.20 both isomorphisms pull every functor back to the same functor ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Checks · StrongPolyfoldBundle.pullMult_z3_independent⟧. A multisection is its function ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.ext_toFun⟧; every structure of $\bar c$ carries a representative of every $\lambda$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.exists_rep_of_mem⟧ (Proposition 11.5.3), and a functor in one structure gives one ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ofFunctor⟧.

**Definition 16.5.2** (restated) ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.domSupp⟧: the domain support is the closure of the $z$ over which some $y \ne 0_z$ has $\lambda(y) > 0$, as in Definition 13.2.2. The printed set ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.domSuppText⟧, with $y = 0_z$ allowed, is all of $Z$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.domSuppText_eq_univ⟧, since the weights over a fibre sum to $1$; presumably $y \ne 0_z$ is meant. **Remark 16.5.3** ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.remark_16_5_3⟧: a representative gives $\gamma(|\operatorname{dom-supp}\Lambda|) = \operatorname{dom-supp}\lambda$; the text writes $\Gamma$, presumably $\gamma$, since both sets lie in $|X|$ and $Z$.

**(16.8)** (as printed; continuity in §XVI.29)"; "The text calls it continuous; that is a new gap (§XVI.6)." → "The text calls it continuous; that is proved in wave 5 (§XVI.29). ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.normLam⟧: $n(\lambda)(z) = \max\{n(y) : p(y) = z, \lambda(y) \ne 0\}$, with $n(\lambda)(\gamma|x|) = N(\Lambda)(x)$ in every representative ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.normLam_eq⟧. The text calls it continuous; that is a new gap (§XVI.6).

**Definition 16.5.4** ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.IsStructurable⟧: $\lambda$ is structurable if one representative is (Definition 13.3.6). *"And therefore all"* ⟦Chapter16/P3W4FN_StructurablePullback · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.definition_16_5_4⟧: every representative is then structurable. The step is the proposition that pull-backs of structurable multisections along generalized strong bundle isomorphisms are structurable ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StructurablePullback⟧, from which the class statement follows ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.definition_16_5_4_hyp⟧, and which holds by Theorems 13.4.1 and 13.4.3 for generalized isomorphisms (Part XIII, §XIII.24) ⟦Chapter16/P3W4FN_StructurablePullback · fnStructurablePullback⟧. The text's "$\lambda : Z \to \mathbb Q^+$" is presumably $Y \to \mathbb Q^+$. Witness: the zero multisection ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.zero⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.zero_isStructurable⟧.

**Definition 16.5.5** (restated) ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisection⟧: multisections of $Y|\partial Z$, classes of representatives with $\Lambda$ on $W|\partial X$ (Definition 14.1.3) ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisectionRep⟧; the pull-back over $\partial X$ is read in orbit form, $\Lambda(w) = \Lambda'(w')$ when $|\bar f||w| = |w'|$ over $\partial X$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisectionRep.Rel⟧, since the pull-back of multisections over the boundary is not yet defined, which is part of the gap of Proposition 14.1.8 over $\partial X$ (Part XIV, §XIV.15). As for Definition 16.5.1, the relation is that the functions agree over $p^{-1}(\partial Z)$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisectionRep.rel_iff⟧. **Definition 16.5.6** ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisection.IsStructurable⟧: structurable over $\partial Z$ if one representative is (Definition 14.1.7), with its domain support ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.BoundaryMultisection.domSupp⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.boundaryDomSupp_subset⟧.

**Theorem 16.5.7** (with an added hypothesis) ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_5_7_hyp⟧: for a tame strong polyfold bundle with sc-smooth partitions of unity, an auxiliary norm $n$, $\lambda$ structurable over $\partial Z$, an open $\tilde U$ containing its domain support, and a continuous $f \ge 0$ with support in $\tilde U$ and $n(\lambda) < f$ on the domain support, there is a structurable $\lambda'$ with $n(\lambda') \le f$, domain support in $\tilde U$ and $\lambda' = \lambda$ over $\partial Z$. *Proof*: Theorem 14.1.9 in one representative, with $f \circ \gamma \circ \pi$, read back by (16.8) and Remark 16.5.3. *The added hypothesis*: Theorem 14.1.9 in every representative of $\bar c$, not derived from the text; it is the statement of Part XIV, §XIV.5, proved there from the data of §§14.3–14.5 (§XIV.22), whose witness covers only $\partial X = \emptyset$. Partitions of unity are read on the objects of every representative, the form Theorem 14.1.9 uses, and "support" as the closed support. The other hypotheses are jointly satisfiable on every tame bundle ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_Multisections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_5_7_hyp_witness⟧, with the zero multisection, $\tilde U = \emptyset$ and $f = 0$.

### XVI.24 §16.6 (2017: Definitions 16.40–16.42, Theorems 16.7, 16.8): sc-Fredholm sections

**The claim before Definition 16.6.1** ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.isFredholm_iff⟧: if one representative of a section is sc-Fredholm, every other is, by Theorem 10.5.4; a section is sc-Fredholm if one is ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.IsFredholm⟧. **Definition 16.6.1** ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.FredholmSection⟧: the sc-Fredholm sections; every structure of $\bar c$ carries a representative ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.exists_rep_of_mem⟧.

**Definition 16.6.2** ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.HasCompactSolutionSet⟧: $\{z : f(z) = 0_z\}$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.solutionSet⟧ is compact. In a representative, $S_f = \gamma(|S_F|)$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.solutionSet_eq⟧, so it is Definition 12.4.1 (1) there ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.hasCompactSolutionSet_iff⟧. **Definition 16.6.3** (new in 2021) ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.IsProper⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.IsProperLtInfty⟧: proper and proper$<\infty$, through the sets $\{z \in U : n(f(z)) \le C\}$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.sublevel⟧, with "$n(f(z)) \le C$" read as $f(z) \in Y_{0,1}$ and $n(f(z)) \le C$; in every representative they are Definition 12.4.1 (2), (3) ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.isProper_iff⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.isProperLtInfty_iff⟧, and controlling compactness is Definition 15.3.1 ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScSection.ControlsCompactness⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.controlsCompactness_iff⟧. The translation uses that the projection $\gamma \circ \pi$ is open and that saturated sets are its preimages ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.isOpen_g_image⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.preimage_g_image⟧, and that "every auxiliary norm" may be read in any representative ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.SectionRep.forall_auxNorm_iff⟧.

**Theorem 16.6.4** (as printed) ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_4⟧: for an sc-Fredholm section, a compact solution set, proper and proper$<\infty$ are equivalent: Theorem 12.4.2 in a representative.

**Definition 16.6.5** (narrower) ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.OrientationRep⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.FredholmSection.IsOrientable⟧: an orientation is the choice of an orientation of a representative $(W, F)$: sc⁺-sections through every point, a topology on $O_F$ as in Theorem 12.5.3, and an orientation as in Definition 12.5.4. *Narrower*: its transport to the other representatives by Theorem 12.5.7, with continuity, and the independence of the transporting isomorphism are gap G.176 (§XVI.6), whose prerequisites in Part XII are now proved. On the $\mathbb Z/3$ example the two isomorphisms are the identity on objects and transport alike; no example was found where the choice matters.

**Theorem 16.6.6** (narrower). *Controlled multisections* ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.IsControlledBy⟧: $n(\lambda) \le 1$ and domain support in $U$. *The reduction* ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_6_6_reduction⟧: for $\partial Z = \emptyset$, $f$ sc-Fredholm with compact solution set, $(n, U)$ controlling compactness and $\lambda$ controlled by $(n, U)$, in every structure of $\bar c$ the representatives $F$, $\Lambda$ satisfy the hypotheses of the ep-groupoid statements of §§15.3–15.4: $\partial X = \emptyset$, compact $|S_F|$, $(N, \gamma\pi^{-1}U)$ controlling compactness, and $\Lambda$ admissible. *The choice of $\lambda$* ⟦Chapter16/P3W4PB_FredholmSections · StrongPolyfoldBundle.exists_generalPosition_hyp⟧: from the statement of Theorem 15.3.7 in a representative and its standing hypotheses (tameness, bump functions, tame germ data), there is a structurable $\lambda$ controlled by $(n, U)$ with $n(\lambda) < 1$ whose representative is transversal and in general position. *The added hypothesis*, Theorem 15.3.7 in the representative, is not derived from the text; Part XV reduces it to its two analytic steps (§XV.20), and its witness covers $\mathbb R^n \times \mathbb R^0$. *Not formalized*: the integrals $\Phi_{(f,o)}([\omega]) = \int_{(\lambda \circ f, o)}\omega$ and their independence of $\lambda$, a new gap (§XVI.6). The text's $Z_{0,1}$ for the domain of $n$ is presumably $Y_{0,1}$.

### XVI.25 Witnesses and the hypotheses of waves 3 and 4

**Hypotheses taken.** *§XVI.16.* An effective middle polyfold for the composition (`ScMap.comp` and its laws) and for Definition 16.1.11; not in the text, which claims the composition in general; witness `EffPolyfold.point`; without it the claim does not hold as we read it (`not_definition_16_1_10`). *§XVI.17.* For `tangent_comp`, an effective middle polyfold and an effective tangent of it (`hTd`); the second follows from the first in wave 5 (§XVI.26), so `hTd` holds whenever the composite is defined, with the witness `EffPolyfold.point`. `pullback_comp` needs only the effective middle polyfold. *§XVI.20.* `uniqueness_16_3_3_of_isEffective` takes an effective target base; satisfiable, since trivial ep-groupoids are effective (Chapter 7); without it the uniqueness does not hold as we read it (`not_uniqueness_16_3_3`). *§XVI.21.* Theorem 16.3.17 (2): the reflexive local step, with witness `theorem_16_3_17_two_hyp_witness` on every bundle with reflexive $1$-fibres, and proved for tame bases in Part XII; "$n$ reflexive" read in one model. Proposition 16.3.16 (2): the same-model reading, no added hypothesis. *§XVI.23.* Definition 16.5.4: `StructurablePullback`, discharged by `fnStructurablePullback`. Theorem 16.5.7: Theorem 14.1.9 in every representative, proved in Part XIV from the data of §§14.3–14.5, whose witness covers only $\partial X = \emptyset$, and partitions of unity in the object form, witnessed for the polyfold $\mathbb R$ by `z3Polyfold_admitsScPartitionsOfUnity`; the remaining hypotheses by `theorem_16_5_7_hyp_witness`. *§XVI.24.* `exists_generalPosition_hyp`: Theorem 15.3.7 in a representative, with its standing hypotheses, as in Part XV (§XV.20).

**Every definition has a witness.** Maps of polyfolds: the identity `ScMap.id`; the category PS: identities; effective polyfolds: `EffPolyfold.point`; the raised polyfold and $\tau_Z$: on every polyfold, for instance the polyfold $\mathbb R$ of §XVI.1. Strong polyfold bundle structures and bundles: `z3Structure`, `z3Bundle`, with nontrivial isotropy; tame ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_Examples · StrongPolyfoldBundle.z3Bundle_isTame⟧; an invertible morphism of $\mathcal{SPBS}$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_Examples · StrongPolyfoldBundle.z3_id_isInvertible⟧; reflexive $1$-fibres ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_Examples · StrongPolyfoldBundle.z3Bundle_hasReflexiveFibers⟧; an auxiliary norm ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_Examples · StrongPolyfoldBundle.z3Bundle_exists_auxNorm⟧ and a reflexive one ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_Examples · StrongPolyfoldBundle.z3Bundle_exists_reflexiveAuxNorm⟧; auxiliary norms over the boundary ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_Examples · StrongPolyfoldBundle.IsAuxNorm.isAuxNormBoundary⟧ ⟦Chapter16/P3W3V_Examples · StrongPolyfoldBundle.theorem_16_3_17_one_witness⟧. sc⁺-multisections: `zero`, structurable; over $\partial Z$, the zero multisection of `theorem_16_5_7_hyp_witness`. Sections, sc⁺-sections and sc-Fredholm sections: not separately witnessed in waves 3 and 4; the zero section of the bundle, which would witness them, is the new gap of §XVI.22. Orientations of sc-Fredholm sections: not separately witnessed. Branched suborbifolds on classes: as in wave 2 (§XVI.15).

### XVI.26 Theorem 16.2.4 (2017: 16.1): the tangent functor on effective polyfolds

**The tangent of an effective ep-groupoid is effective** ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_TangentEffective · EpGroupoid.isEffective_tangentEpGroupoid⟧: for $X$ effective with (ZHOU), the tangent ep-groupoid $TX$ (Theorem 8.1.1) is effective (Definition 7.2.1). *Proof.* If an isotropy element $g$ of $TX$ acted trivially near a tangent vector, it would act trivially on an open set of $TX$, which sees only level $1$; moving to a smooth point of $X$ below it ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_TangentEffective · EpGroupoid.levelVal_tangentProj_mem_smoothSet⟧, (ZHOU) and a linear map equal to the identity on an open set ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_TangentEffective · linearMap_eq_self_of_eqOn_isOpen⟧ make the underlying element of $G_x$ act trivially near $x$, so it is the identity by effectiveness of $X$, and so is $g$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_TangentEffective · EpGroupoid.tangent_isotropy_eq_one⟧. Effectiveness alone does not suffice for this argument, since it is a statement at level $0$. **For polyfolds** ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_TangentEffective · PolyfoldClass.IsEffective.tangent⟧: the tangent of an effective polyfold is effective; (ZHOU) is part of every polyfold structure (Definition 16.1.1 (2)), so no hypothesis is added.

**Theorem 16.2.4** (narrower) ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_TangentEffective · theorem_16_2_4_eff⟧: $T$ is a functor on the category of effective polyfolds ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_TangentEffective · EffPolyfold.tangentFunctor⟧, with $T$ of an effective polyfold its tangent ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_TangentEffective · EffPolyfold.tangent⟧, $T1 = 1$, and $T(\hat g \circ \hat f) = T\hat g \circ T\hat f$ whenever the middle polyfold is effective ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_TangentEffective · PolyfoldClass.ScMap.tangent_comp_of_isEffective⟧, without the effectiveness of its tangent that §XVI.17 assumed. *Narrower* only as in §XVI.17: there is no category of all polyfolds (§XVI.16), and on effective polyfolds, where Definition 16.1.10's composition is defined as we read it, it is the text's statement with no added hypothesis. Witness: the effective one-point polyfold and its tangent (`EffPolyfold.point`). With wave 3's formula $Tf \circ T\alpha = T\beta \circ |T\mathfrak f|$ (§XVI.17) this is Theorem 16.2.4. Gap G.157 is closed.

### XVI.27 Definition 16.3.12 (2017: 16.24), the parenthetical: reflexive $1$-fibres along equivalences, pull direction

**Charts** ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_ReflexivePull · StrongBundle.LocalIso.exists_reflexive_chart⟧: for a local strong bundle isomorphism $\Phi : Y|U \to Y'|U'$ over $\phi$ and $x \in U$, a compatible chart of $Y'$ at $\phi(x)$ whose fibre $F_1$ is reflexive gives one of $Y$ at $x$: restrict the chart to $U'$ and transport it along $\Phi$; the fibre model does not change. **Bundles** ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_ReflexivePull · StrongBundle.hasReflexiveFibers_of_isStrongBundleIsoOn⟧: if $X$ is covered by the domains of such isomorphisms, reflexive $(0, 1)$-fibres pull back. **Equivalences** (narrower) ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_ReflexivePull · EpStrongBundle.IsStrongBundleEquivalence.hasReflexiveFibers_of⟧: for a strong bundle equivalence $W \to W'$ (Definition 10.4.1), reflexive $1$-fibres of $W'$ give reflexive $1$-fibres of $W$; the local isomorphisms covering the objects are (2) of Definition 10.4.1, so no hypothesis is added. *Narrower*: for a generalized isomorphism $[W \leftarrow W'' \rightarrow W']$ this gives $W'$ reflexive $\Rightarrow$ $W''$ reflexive; from $W''$ to $W$ is the push direction, which is missing, as are mixed convergence and reflexive auxiliary norms (gap G.166, §XVI.6).

### XVI.28 Proposition 16.4.3 (2017: 16.6): the structure on $\operatorname{supp}\theta$ does not depend on the representative

**Proposition 16.4.3** (as printed) ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_naturality⟧: the comparison statement of §XVI.19 holds, for two representatives $\Theta$, $\Theta'$ of $\theta$ of manifold type. In a stronger form ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.proposition_16_4_3_naturality_all⟧: for any structures induced by Proposition 9.1.9 (1) on the two supports, and $\Theta$, $\Theta'$ of orbifold type, which manifold type implies, the transition homeomorphism of §XVI.19 is an sc-diffeomorphism; so the choice of the induced structures does not matter. *Proof.* For a generalized isomorphism $X \xleftarrow{F} A \xrightarrow{\Phi} X'$ between the representatives, the transition sends $|Fb|$ to $|\Phi b|$ for $b$ in the support of the pulled-back functor ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.suppTransition_orbitSuppProj⟧. Near $|Fb|$ it is therefore $p' \circ \Phi|_{\operatorname{supp}} \circ (F|_{\operatorname{supp}})^{-1} \circ p^{-1}$, where the legs restrict to equivalences of the sub-ep-groupoids on the supports and $p$, $p'$ are the local sc-diffeomorphisms $a \mapsto |a|$ of the induced structures; so it is sc-smooth ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_SuppNaturality · PolyfoldClass.BranchedSuborbifold.isScSmoothOn_suppTransition⟧, and so is its inverse. Gap G.155 is closed.

### XVI.29 (16.8) (2017: after Definition 16.36): the continuity of $n(\lambda)$

**$N(\Lambda)$ on $X$** ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_NormLamContinuous · SBLocalization.IsScPlusMultisection.continuous_pointwiseNorm⟧: for an sc⁺-multisection functor $\Lambda$ and a continuous $N$ on $W_{0,1}$, the function $N(\Lambda)$ of Definition 13.2.3 is continuous on $X$: in a local section structure it is the maximum of the continuous functions $N \circ s_i$ ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_NormLamContinuous · SBLocalization.IsLocalRepOn.pointwiseNorm_eq⟧, over a nonempty index set ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_NormLamContinuous · SBLocalization.IsLocalRepOn.univ_nonempty⟧. **(16.8)** (as printed) ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_NormLamContinuous · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.continuous_normLam⟧: for an auxiliary norm $n$, $n(\lambda) : Z \to [0, \infty)$ is continuous; it equals $N(\Lambda)$ on orbits in a representative (§XVI.23), and the map $X \to Z$ is a quotient map ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_NormLamContinuous · StrongPolyfoldBundle.isQuotientMap_γπ⟧. The maximum is attained ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_NormLamContinuous · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.isGreatest_normLam⟧ and the values are nonnegative ⟦Chapter16/P3W5PC_NormLamContinuous · StrongPolyfoldBundle.ScPlusMultisection.normLam_nonneg⟧. Gap G.174 is closed.

### XVI.30 Witnesses and the hypotheses of wave 5

**Hypotheses taken.** None. *§XVI.26.* `isEffective_tangentEpGroupoid` takes (ZHOU) at the level of ep-groupoids; for polyfolds it is part of the structure, and `IsEffective.tangent` takes only effectiveness; witness `EffPolyfold.point`. *§XVI.27.* The local isomorphisms covering $X$ in `hasReflexiveFibers_of_isStrongBundleIsoOn` are (2) of Definition 10.4.1 in the equivalence form, which has no extra hypothesis. *§XVI.28.* Orbifold type of both representatives, which manifold type, the text's case, gives. *§XVI.29.* An auxiliary norm, as printed.

**Discharged.** The hypothesis `hTd` of `tangent_comp` (§XVI.17), that the tangent of the middle polyfold is effective, follows from the effectiveness of the middle polyfold (§XVI.26), so `tangent_comp` now has a witness. The comparison statement of Proposition 16.4.3 (§XVI.19) is proved (§XVI.28). The hypothesis of Theorem 16.5.7, Theorem 14.1.9 in every representative, is proved in Part XIV from the data of §§14.3–14.5, whose witness covers only $\partial X = \emptyset$ (Part XIV, §XIV.22). No hypothesis of wave 5 quantifies over all charts. No new statement was found not to hold as we read it.
